generated_text: Honestly, I’m still recovering from Saturday night. That Prosecco was deceptively strong, wasn’t it? Tell me about it! I thought I was being sensible with just two glasses, but I woke up feeling like I’d run a marathon. Poor you. Little Leo's been surprisingly good today though, hasn't he? Sleeping fairly well which is a blessing. You’ve got your hands full with Elsie though, haven’t you? She's a little whirlwind! She is! Absolutely loves climbing on everything. I’m convinced she’s going to scale the curtains one day. We're thinking about getting that baby gate for the living room. Good idea. Remember when Mark used to try and climb the bookshelves? Total chaos. Oh god, yes! He was a menace. Elsie's got the same mischievous glint in her eyes, I swear. Speaking of Mark, are we still on for visiting Mum and Dad next weekend? Yes, definitely. I booked the train tickets yesterday. Saturday’s probably best, so we can catch the afternoon train home and I can get some proofreading done Sunday. Work's been a bit manic this week. That’s good you’re getting it in. How's that advertising campaign going for the bakery? It’s going really well actually! They're really pleased with the social media reach. It’s nice to see that little bit extra coming in. Thinking about Elsie’s birthday… have you got any ideas? She'll be two in February, won't believe it. I know! Where did the time go. I was thinking maybe a little party at home? Nothing too extravagant. Just a few friends, cake, balloons… That sounds perfect. We could do a little teddy bear theme? Elsie's obsessed with teddy bears at the moment. That’s a brilliant idea! I’ll start looking at decorations online. What about a cake? I'm terrible at making cakes. I’ll do the cake! I’ve been practicing my Victoria sponge. It’s actually quite good now, surprisingly. You can get away with a lot when you're baking for a two-year-old. True. It doesn’t have to be perfect! Speaking of friends, have you heard from Sarah lately? Not for a while, no. I'll give her a text. Things have been quiet haven't they. Yeah. Oh look, Leo's awake. Ready for a feed?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from how easy it was to hop over to Berlin last month. It really highlights how much we took for granted, doesn't it? Absolutely. Remember back in the day, the mountains of paperwork just to get a visa for, like, Poland? It felt like a military operation. Book a flight, deal with the consulate, make sure your passport photo was  exactly  the right size… Oh god, the passport photos! You'd spend longer stressing about the photo than you did actually planning the holiday. I remember Mum nearly having a breakdown trying to get Dad’s to look "official" enough. And the queuing! I went to Prague in ’03, and the queue at passport control snaked halfway down the airport corridor. You practically needed a survival kit. Now, you just stroll through. It’s just… liberating. I was chatting to this girl in a cafe in Prenzlauer Berg, and she was from Spain. We were just instantly connecting, you know? No language barriers or complicated visa stuff to navigate first. We ended up sharing recommendations for hidden gem bars. That’s brilliant. I’ve been looking at flights to Lisbon. Been wanting to go for years, but the hassle always put me off. Now, it’s just... a Tuesday afternoon impulse purchase. Proper easy. Exactly! I was thinking of doing a few days in Amsterdam at the end of the summer. Research purposes, obviously.    Research? Into what? The best stroopwafels?    Let's just say my work involves understanding consumer behaviour and cultural trends. It's all very valid. Anyway, did you ever manage to figure out that awful French bureaucracy when you were doing your Erasmus in Lyon? Don't even  start  me on French bureaucracy. It was a masterclass in inefficiency. I swear, they deliberately designed the system to frustrate you. Remember trying to register as a resident? I spent three weeks chasing my tail, got sent from office to office, and eventually just gave up. Oh, I’ve heard horror stories. Did you at least get to see the sights? Eventually, yes. It was worth it, honestly. Lyon's amazing. But that registration process... I still have nightmares about it. Paperwork piled up to the ceiling, long queues, people shouting in rapid French... Honestly, it was a test of my sanity. See, that's what I'm worried about now. Post-Brexit, I’m expecting things to get a bit more complicated again.

Right, who wants dessert? I was thinking crumble tonight. Apple or rhubarb? Apple! With custard! Lots of custard! Rhubarb! Rhubarb is better! It’s pink! Oh, you two. Alright, alright, we’ll have apple crumble with custard. And a little bit of rhubarb too, just for you, Oscar. Are you two tired of Monopoly yet? No! Let's play again! I need to win! I'm gonna buy Park Place this time! That’s my strategy! Park Place and Boardwalk! That's a very ambitious strategy, Charlie. But those are the most expensive properties. You need some money to actually  buy  them, remember? I'll lend you some money, Charlie! Really, Elsie? Thanks! How much? Elsie, you're meant to be saving your money, not just giving it away! It’s Monopoly, you have to be ruthless! But it's more fun if everyone has money! And can buy houses! Yeah! Then we can all build hotels! And charge loads of money! Alright, alright. But after dessert. We’ll have a think about some rules. Maybe a five-pound penalty for landing on someone else’s property. What do you think? Five pounds is good! I like that! Six pounds! Six is better! Six pounds? You're getting greedy, aren't you? It's just a game. But, fine. Six pounds. But if you land on my Park Place with a hotel, you're paying the price! How about that, you two? Deal! Deal! Park Place is mine! Just you wait! I'm gonna be rich! You two and your dreams of being Monopoly millionaires. Now, who wants to help me peel the apples? Elsie, you can wash them. Charlie, you can pile them up! And please, try not to eat them all before they get into the crumble. I won't! Promise! Just one. Maybe two. Park place. Soon to be mine. All mine. Let's remember to sort the money out properly this time. Last game, Charlie kept sneaking extra ten pound notes out of his pocket! I didn’t! I just… found them! Behind the sofa! Right you did. No more 'finding' money behind the sofa. Understand? Fine. But Park Place is still mine! You can't find Park Place, Charlie! It's on the board! I'll find a way. I always do. That’s my boy. Now, apples! Let’s get peeling. And then... Monopoly domination!

Honestly, this traffic is brutal. I thought coming this way would be quicker, avoiding the A1. Clearly, I was wrong. You always think you’ve found a shortcut. Remember that time we tried to get to Gran's in Newcastle via that tiny country lane? Ended up on a farm track. Don’t remind me! Sheep everywhere. I was convinced we were going to be stuck there forever. Though, to be fair, your navigation skills weren’t exactly stellar that day. Hey! The sat nav led me astray. It’s not entirely my fault. Besides, it was a good story. At least we got some sheep photos out of it. Yeah, photos that Mum still uses to tease you about your sense of direction. Alright, alright. But seriously, this is a nightmare. Think we'll make it to Fiona's by six? Assuming this standstill resolves itself. I’m starving. Did you at least get a pasty before we left? I did! It’s in the glove compartment. Freshly baked this morning. Best pork and onion you’ll ever taste. You are a lifesaver. Honestly, a pasty is all that's keeping me going right now. This commute is proper testing my patience, you know. Especially after that week I’ve had at work. Dealing with all those verbose linguistic ambiguities... Sounds stressful. Anything specific? Just… a researcher kept insisting “very” was a meaningful marker of emphasis. Like, just because someone uses "very" a lot, it’s somehow linguistically significant. It’s filler! Pure filler. It means nothing! Sounds like a proper headache. You and your language stuff. You know, engineering is significantly less philosophical. It’s all cables and stresses and load-bearing capacities. Pretty straightforward, really. See, that’s what I like about you. You deal in facts. I’m drowning in opinions and interpretations. It’s exhausting. Well, you're good at it! You’re a brilliant corpus administrator. And you're practically an expert on "very". Don’t push it. Now, is that pasty going to magically appear, or do I have to threaten you? Hold your horses. One pork and onion pasty, coming right up. And maybe a chocolate digestive? You look like you need it. Don't mind if I do! Thank you. Now, let’s hope this traffic eases up soon. I’m missing Fiona’s lasagna already. It will. We’ll get there.

Right then, tea’s on. I’ve put biscuits out this time, not just digestive ones. Got some shortbread and those chocolate things you like, Arthur. Splendid, Harold. Always good to have a bit of variety, eh? Though you can't beat a good digestive, of course. Good, solid biscuit. Oh, that smells lovely. Thank you, Harold. Did you see that article in the paper this morning? About the new bridge they’re building over the Broads? I did. Looks a bit ambitious, doesn't it? For that location. Lot of water involved. They’ll need to be careful with the foundations. And the wind, of course, those gales can be ferocious. They always say that, don’t they? “Careful with the foundations.” As if they won’t be! They’re engineers, Harold! Building bridges isn’t exactly a pastime. I’m not saying they won’t be careful, Arthur. Just that it’s a challenging site. The silt, the tides… they all add complications. Need a good geotechnical survey, that's what they need. I wonder if they'll disrupt the wildlife. All those birds nesting on the banks. It’s such a lovely spot, usually so peaceful. They will, unfortunately. There’s always a disruption. But they'll try and mitigate it, I’m sure. Nest boxes, relocation… the usual procedures. It wouldn't be right to just bulldoze everything. Still, a bridge! Right over the Broads! Seems a bit… unnecessary. I used to enjoy a good row myself. Lovely way to see the country. Oh, yes. Remember when young Emily used to come with us, Arthur? She'd stand in the bow, pretending to be a pirate. Aye, she did. Covered in reeds and mud, she was. Happy as Larry. Speaking of young Emily, has she mentioned anything about her plans for Christmas? Still thinking of coming down from London, I suppose? I haven’t heard anything definite yet. She did say she was rather busy with work. But she’ll let us know. She always does. She’s a good girl, Emily. Always was. Got her mother’s good sense, you know. That she does. Now, who wants another biscuit? I've got a fresh pot of tea brewing too. Oh, go on then. Just one more chocolate one for me, Harold. Thank you. Don’t mind if I do. Shortbread’s been lovely. A bit crumbly, mind you.

So, the sample sizes for the new lavender range are all ready to go. I’ve wrapped them up nicely, little ribbons and everything. Ready for the Instagram photos. Ooh, lovely! Ribbons are a  must . Makes it feel more… luxe, doesn’t it? Are you doing a giveaway, then? I was thinking about it. A giveaway would massively boost engagement. But I’m worried about the cost of postage. It’s bleeding me dry! Tell me about it. Shipping is the killer, isn’t it? I’m still wrestling with the best way to calculate it on the website. I keep messing up the dimensions. People are expecting free shipping like it’s going out of fashion, the cheek of it! Honestly! I accidentally put the wrong weight on the last batch of orders. Ended up having to refund nearly a dozen people because I’d overcharged them. Nightmare. Oh gosh! That's awful. You need to triple-check everything, especially with skincare. People expect transparency. What did you use for measuring? Just a standard kitchen scale? Yeah, just my kitchen scale. I need to invest in something more accurate. Do you know a good brand? I was looking at those digital postal scales... I’ve heard good things about those Salter ones. Pretty reliable. And you can get ‘em cheap on Amazon. But, honestly, the customer service calls I had after those refunds… I needed a stiff drink. I can imagine! Have you considered offering tiered shipping? Like, free over a certain spend? I’ve been playing with the idea. It might encourage people to add a few extra things to their basket. But I worry it’ll eat into my profit margins. It’s a gamble, definitely. But building customer loyalty is key. Honesty Skincare is all about building that trust, isn't it? People appreciate knowing where their products are coming from, that they're ethically sourced… Exactly! That’s the whole point. That's why I’m trying to get the labels printed with the exact percentages of each ingredient. It’s a faff, but… It’s worth it. That’s what sets you apart! Beauty brands are often so vague. Speaking of separating out, Mum’s been nagging me to list some of her old earrings on Etsy. Apparently, they’re “vintage treasures.” I'm rolling my eyes, but it could be a bit of extra cash flow.

Honestly, David, the news is just relentless, isn’t it? One thing or another. It's hard to keep up. Did you see about that MP? Absolute disgrace. Aye, I did. Shocking, really. Thought they’d have learned by now, some of them. The public sees right through it. Though, does it really make a difference, does it? It feels like the same thing happened last month, and the month before. It’s just disheartening. Makes you wonder what the point of it all is, really. Though, I suppose it’s good to talk about, isn’t it? Better than bottling it all up. How are things with you? Still battling that leaky roof? Still battling, sadly. The rain's been awful lately. Got a few quotes in, but nobody seems keen to do the job properly. They all say the same thing – "it's a tricky one." Typical. Oh, I know exactly what you mean. They just want the easy money. You need to find someone with a bit of grit, someone who’s not afraid of a challenge. Did you try that firm, Henderson and Sons? They did a good job on Mrs. Peterson’s place down the road. Henderson and Sons? I’ll give them a ring, thanks. I'd forgotten about them. They may be a bit more expensive, but it's worth it if they do a proper job. Absolutely. And how’s Emily doing? Still enjoying her pottery? She is, actually. She's got a little exhibition planned for next month, down at the little gallery on the seafront. It's all very exciting. She’s nervous, of course, but mostly excited. Oh, that’s wonderful! I’ll definitely come. I'd love to see her work. I remember when she was little, she always had a creative streak. Making little sculptures out of playdough. Aye, she always was. And what about you? Keeping busy? Still volunteering at the library? Yes, still going strong. It keeps me active, you know. And I love being around the books. Got a lovely group of volunteers, we're like a little family. Though, I must admit, I miss teaching sometimes. Just seeing those young faces, their eagerness to learn... I understand. It’s a rewarding job, teaching. Though, I have to say, some days I wonder why I didn't follow your lead and choose something less stressful.

Right, so glad you all made it! The stew’s nearly ready, should be bubbling away in about ten. Smells fantastic, Sarah! Feels good to finally be here, bit of a trek from Newcastle. Snowed over a bit on the way, actually. Oh, you poor thing, Liam! Luckily Swindon was relatively calm. Though, it  is  freezing, isn’t it? I'm layered up like an onion. Aye, a bit nippy it is. Though, not as bad as up in Scotland. Had a right blizzard swirling around Carmarthen yesterday. Nearly lost a stack of timber I was trying to dry in the shed. I’m definitely cranking the thermostat up a notch. It's ridiculous how much energy everything uses these days, isn't it? Thinking about it, I should probably look into getting one of those smart thermostats. Retirement plans, I guess. Retirement? Sarah, you're barely thirty-five! I know, I know! Just daydreaming about a time when I can finally grow a proper mulberry tree without worrying about the research budget. Speaking of which, how’s the woodworking going, Rhys? Still churning out those gorgeous bowls? Aye, keeps me busy. Just finished a commission for a local gallery - a set of nesting bowls using reclaimed walnut. Had to sharpen the chisels something fierce for that one, though. My old set’s starting to go - thinking of investing in some proper Lie-Nielsen tools. Bit of a splurge, but worth it, I reckon. Lie-Nielsen? Fancy! I'm rather more basic in my recreation activities. I’ve been completely obsessed with Ticket to Ride lately. Have you guys played? Ticket to Ride? Yeah, I’ve played that a few times. It's a good one, easy to pick up. More my speed than, say, Settlers of Catan. Too much negotiating for me! I’m terrible at negotiating. I just tend to stress myself out trying to be fair. I'm more of a Scrabble girl, myself. Though my vocabulary hasn't improved much from my research. It's all technical terms and obscure Latin roots. Speaking of obscure things, did you hear about that new archaeological dig they've started down near Stonehenge? Apparently, they've found evidence of seasonal feasting – loads of pig bones and…mulberries! Mulberries! That's fascinating! Maybe I'm onto something with that garden plan of mine. Pig bones and mulberries... ancient Christmas dinner, perhaps? Could be!

This gravy is absolutely incredible, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, love, that's good to hear! It's just a bit of Bisto really, but I added a touch of Worcestershire sauce, you see. Makes all the difference. It’s amazing. Everything's lovely, honestly. Did you manage to find those dessert spoons, Dad? You were saying earlier...? Ah yes. Right mess, the cutlery drawer. Been meaning to sort it out for ages. Can’t find the dessert spoons anywhere. Seems to be a black hole in there. Used to have a whole set, nice silver ones. Belonged to me Granny… Aye, you did, Dad. Lovely silver spoons. Probably rolled under something years ago. It's such a classic problem, isn't it? Things just vanishing into drawers. I had that with my scissors at uni. Spent ages looking for them, then found them sticking out from under a pile of socks. Oh, you young people! Always losing things. Remember your Auntie Carol? She lost her glasses for three days once, and they were on top of her head the whole time! Classic Auntie Carol. She's good at that sort of thing. Are you seeing Sarah this week, Liam? She mentioned she’s got that new exhibition opening she’d love you to go. No, not yet, I've been swamped at work. And I need to get my flat redecorated... seriously considering a bold colour scheme. Oh, don't you dare! Keep it neutral, love. You can always add splashes of colour with cushions and pictures. Bold is a nightmare to live with. Your mother’s right, dear. I tried a lime green bedroom once, years ago. Biggest mistake of my life. Always felt like I was living in a giant lemon. Okay, okay, point taken. Neutral it is. Although… I was thinking a deep teal. Teal...like the sea. Nice. Used to sail, you know. When I was a lad. Remember that trip to the Lake District, Dad? You nearly capsized that little boat. Nearly did! Wind got right under me. Scared the bejesus out of your mother. Speaking of trips, is Uncle David still planning to come down next month? He's booked his train ticket, apparently. He’s ever so excited to see little Finn. He keeps asking if Finn’s started walking yet. He has! He took his first proper steps yesterday. It was so cute.

So, the meeting went okay then? Did they seem happy with the proposal? Mmmhmm. Happy. Really? That’s good. I was a little nervous, you know, putting myself forward for that project. It’s a big responsibility. Big. Like… like mountains, Mummy. Exactly like mountains, darling. Which reminds me… Are you excited about the skiing trip? Snow! Lots of snow! Lots of snow, hopefully. I’ve been looking at the weather reports. Austria looks promising. Can I build a snowman? A really, really big one? Of course, you can! The biggest snowman ever. We'll need to find the perfect spot. And snowball fights, naturally. Can I throw snowballs at Daddy? You absolutely can. But be gentle, okay? Daddy’s not as nimble as you are. No. Not gentle. Okay, okay! A little bit gentle. So, I need to confirm the ski hire with that website. And book the ski school for you, obviously. I want to go fast! Zoom! You’ll go as fast as you’re ready for, love. We’ll start you on the nursery slopes. Are you practicing your snowplow? Like this? Perfect! You’re a natural. Listen, I was thinking, should we get those special ski socks? The really thick ones? Keep your toes warm. Warm toes! Yes! Right. I'll add it to the list. It's getting quite long actually. Flights, ski hire, ski school, socks… oh, and we need to get your salopettes checked and adjusted. Are they still too long? Mmm-hmm. Long. Right. I’ll make an appointment at the outfitter's. They're usually pretty good with adjustments. And we need to pack loads of layers. It can get very cold up there. Cold! Like… like an ice cream! Exactly like an ice cream. But don't try to eat the snow, okay? It's not very tasty. No eat snow. Good girl. Now, finish your pasta. Tomorrow we can look at some pictures of the Austrian Alps, alright? Dream of snow! Dream snow! Snooooo! Zoom! Zoom! Zoom! Zoom, zoom, zoom. Rest your little legs. We’ve got a fun adventure coming up. Don't you worry, we’ll have a brilliant time. Even if I’m slightly stressed about all the logistics! Mummy silly. We go skiing! Happy! You are right, darling. We will. Very happy. Very happy indeed. Do you think I should email the project manager about a possible meeting next week?

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. Maths was brutal today. Mrs. Davies was on one. Tell me about it! I spent the whole lesson trying not to stare at the clock. Did you even understand anything she was saying about quadratic equations? Not a single bit. I think she's deliberately trying to confuse us. I swear, last year’s Maths class was way easier. Seriously! Remember Mr. Harrison? He actually made it...interesting. Yeah, he’d tell these crazy stories about his trips to Scotland while he was explaining Pythagoras’ theorem. It was bizarre, but it stuck in my head better than anything Mrs. Davies says. Definitely. Anyway, what did you think of Food Tech this afternoon? The veggie burgers were…interesting. "Interesting" is a very generous word. They tasted like sadness wrapped in a bun. I felt so bad for Mr. Peterson, he looked so proud of them. Poor Mr. Peterson! I think he’s trying too hard to be healthy. I miss the cheesy chips days. Me too! Speaking of jobs, did you hear about Tilly getting a Saturday job at the ice cream shop? No way! That’s so cool. Loads of free ice cream for her, I bet. Exactly! I’m still trying to decide what I want to do. Mum keeps suggesting something retail, but I’d rather not deal with grumpy customers all day. True. Have you thought about that tutoring thing? Mrs. Evans said you’re really good at English. Yeah, I’ve thought about it. But it’s kind of boring, isn’t it? Helping little kids with their spelling? It’s not  that  bad. And you’d be earning proper money. Plus, it'd look good on your uni application. True, true. What are you doing for Spanish homework? I’m dreading it. Señorita Rodriguez just keeps piling on the grammar. Oh god, me too. I'm stuck on the subjunctive. It's like, when  should  you use it? It’s so confusing. Right? I had a nightmare about it last night. I was trapped in a room full of verb charts! Oh no! Maybe we should have a study session? We could quiz each other. That’s a good idea. Maybe on Sunday? I'm already wishing it was Sunday. Definitely. And we could order pizza? YES! Perfect. Oh, speaking of Spanish, I was listening to that Rosalía song the other day.

Honestly darling, I’m still reeling from that new film, “Saltburn.” Have you seen it? I have! Just last week, actually. What did you think? It’s…a lot, isn’t it? A lot is putting it mildly! I mean, the cinematography was gorgeous, beautifully shot, absolutely. But the story…the  content … dear me. My stomach was churning for half of it. I know, right? It definitely lingers. Some of the scenes were just...intentionally shocking, I think. Shocking is one word for it! I felt rather… assaulted at times. Though, I must admit, Barry Keoghan was brilliant. He carried the whole thing. Absolutely. He was mesmerizing, wasn't he? So unsettling and captivating all at once. I kept trying to figure out what his endgame was. That's what I found so frustrating! It felt like the film just  wanted  to be shocking, without really having anything profound to say about class or desire or whatever it was trying to explore. I think it was trying to say a lot, maybe too much. And not always successfully. The class dynamics were definitely there, the desperation of Oliver... Yes, but the way they were portrayed felt almost cartoonish, didn’t it? They were caricatures, really. The aristocratic family, so carelessly destructive and oblivious. I agree. Though, I did appreciate the attention to detail with the period setting. The costumes, the music… it felt very meticulously crafted in that sense. Oh, the music was lovely, yes. Though, I scarcely noticed it over the feeling of wanting to cover my eyes. Remember “The Piano” with Holly Hunter? Now  that  was a film with unsettling moments, but it felt earned. This? It felt… gratuitous. That's a good comparison. “Saltburn” definitely feels a bit performative, like it wants to be remembered for its outrageousness rather than its artistry. Precisely! I'm not against a bit of daring cinema, mind you. But it needs to serve a purpose. I liked that bit when...oh, I won’t spoil it for anyone else. Good thinking! I think I'll avert my eyes if anyone mentions that scene again. Did you see the bits about the art history, with the museums? That was interesting. It was! They clearly did their research. Though again, it felt a bit like style over substance at times. Did you know that Francis Bacon lived in a very similar house to Saltburn? No, really?

This coffee's lovely, Mum. Thanks for bringing it. Don't mention it, love. Needed a good catch-up. How was the drive up? Traffic alright? Honestly, it was a nightmare. Sat behind a lorry for what felt like forever. Him and another one, just tootling along at 50. I swear, they do it on purpose. Oh, they do, don't they? Think they own the road. You need to overtake, love. Don’t let them rattle you. I know, but I really didn’t feel comfortable. It was a bit bendy in places. And that rain! Absolutely lashed down for a while. Aye, a bit miserable, wasn’t it? Could have done with some sunshine. So, what's been happening with you? Still enjoying teaching? Yeah, mostly. It's busy, as always. I've got that new class of A-Levels starting next week, so that’s a bit of a worry. They seem…unenthusiastic. Oh dear. Hard work with unenthusiastic students, isn't it? What are you teaching them? Advanced Spanish. It’s supposed to be exciting, but some of them just can’t be bothered to learn the grammar. Grammar’s important, though, isn’t it? Need a good grounding. Like with court cases, you know. Everything has to be precise. Exactly! It's frustrating. Anyway, how are things at court? Still the same old dramas? Pretty much. Bit of everything, really. Some nasty stuff going on, as always. Makes you think, doesn’t it? People are capable of such things. It does. It must be hard to see every day. Are you looking forward to retiring anytime soon? Well, I’m thinking about it. Five years yet, though. Trying to save up a bit more. Prices are ridiculous now, aren’t they? Even for a little cottage somewhere quiet. They are mad. I'm trying to save too, but it’s hard when rent in London is so extortionate. Bless you. Have you found that nice book I lent you? About the gardens? Oh! Yes, I have. It’s lovely. Honestly, it's made me want to start gardening. Though I've got no clue where to start. Well, we’ll have to sort that out then. We could come up and get you started. I know a few tricks. That would be amazing, Mum. Really. I’d love that. Good. And have you heard anything from Jamie?

Honestly, the marking pile is ridiculous this year. I swear, half the essays feel like they've been written by chatbots. Really? I thought mine were fairly decent, considering. A few interesting perspectives popping up, actually. That's what I was hoping for, but no. Just… generic. Repetitive. You know the type, vaguely referencing Foucault, but without actually  understanding  anything he said. The classic. Did you manage to get through any of the reading list for the new module? Not even close. I spent most of my lunch break trying to decipher the syllabus for the postgraduate seminar. It's dense, even for me. I think Professor Davies has deliberately made it obtuse. He does have a thing for those unnecessarily convoluted phrases. Remember that whole lecture on semiotics he gave last year? Don’t remind me! My brain felt like it was going to explode. Right, did you remember to pick up milk? Completely forgot. Of course. Is it vital for tonight? We're supposed to be having that lemon drizzle cake with custard, aren’t we? Pretty vital, yes. And ice cream. It’s a very sophisticated dessert, you know. Not just any old custard and cake. True, true. I'll head to the shop on the way home then. There’s that new Asian supermarket opened up, I should check it out. They supposedly have amazing mangoes. Ooh, yes! Let’s stock up. I'm craving a proper mango lassi. I saw some beautiful silk scarves in there last week too. Silk scarves? Are you planning a new look? Maybe. Just browsing, really. Although, I do need something to wear to that conference next month. It's frightfully formal. You always look impeccable, even in formal settings. Honestly, you should see me attempting to put on a tie. It’s a disaster. That's true. You look like you’re wrestling an octopus. Although, I did see a rather nice cashmere sweater on sale online the other day… could be a good option for you. Tempting. Very tempting. But first, milk and mangoes. And maybe a sneaky packet of prawn crackers. Definitely prawn crackers. Honestly, sometimes I think you’re more motivated by snacks than anything else. Hey, a man’s gotta have priorities! And sustaining my energy for all this intense lecturing is a serious business. Always the excuses. Come on, let's get home. It’s getting chilly.

“…and the little bear waved goodbye to his mama, and promised to be brave on his adventure!” Brave! Like me when I went to Mrs. Higgins' today? Absolutely brave! You were a superstar. Did you have fun playing with the dinosaurs? Yes! And I built a tall tower. A very tall tower! Tower… gotta be higher. You're becoming quite the architect, aren’t you? Okay, little builders. Dinner's nearly ready. How about we read a few more pages? Yes! Can we read about the grumpy badger? Of course. But first, a quick question. Liam, darling, do you remember what we talked about with Nana? Pictures? That’s right! We’re going to have a photoshoot this weekend, remember? So you need to pick out your favourite shirt. I want the sparkly one! The pink one with the butterflies! You look beautiful in that, sweetheart. Okay, photoshoot planned. Now, about Saturday night…I’m thinking of trying to see Sophie and Ben. Would you two like that? Sophie! Can I bring my dinosaur? We’ll see if Sophie approves of a dinosaur invasion. But it's definitely a possibility. Can I have cake? Always, my love. Always cake. I'm thinking of making that chocolate cake. Are you feeling brave enough to help me lick the bowl? Yes! Me too! Lick! Lick! Well, we need to finish this book first. And then plates need to be set for dinner. Liam, darling, can you help me count the forks? Count! Good boy. Sophie said she'd be free Saturday. I just need to text her now. And I need to get a haircut. Mine’s getting terribly long. It’s getting in my eyes when I'm trying to read with you both. Mommy needs a pretty haircut! Like a princess! You think so? Maybe. Maybe I’ll get a sparkly one too! Now, let’s finish our story and then it’s dinner time. Brave little bears, ready for adventure! Right? Speaker_2 & Right! Good. Now where were we… Ah yes! “And the little bear…” My turn to read! Just a little bit longer, my love. Just a little longer. Read about the badger! Please! Okay, okay. The grumpy badger it is. Let's see what he’s up to… Grumpy! Very grumpy… indeed. He needs a dinosaur! Maybe he does! Maybe he does… That's my boy.H.H..

Honestly, this soup is grim. Like, absolutely grim. Did you try it? Nah, I saw you eyeing it up like a hawk, thought I’d spare myself the disappointment. What is it even supposed to be? Apparently, butternut squash. Tastes like wallpaper paste mixed with sadness. I’m sticking with the chips. Sensible choice. They’re alright, aren't they? Not amazing, but better than potential wallpaper paste. So, big night tomorrow? Yeah! Maya’s finally managed to get into Venue. I’m really buzzing for it. You know how hard it is to get in there. Tell me about it! I think my best friend, Liam, might know someone who knows someone, hopefully. It’s always those connections that get you in. Exactly! I nearly cried when Maya texted me saying she’d secured us a table. Do you think we should pre-drink? Definitely. My flat just got a new bottle of prosecco, so we could start there. Or we could hit up The Ramble. Their cocktails are lethal. Ooh, The Ramble is always a good shout. But let's do my flat first. It’ll be more relaxed. And less crammed. Last time I was in The Ramble, I practically had someone's elbow digging into my ribs the entire night. Fair enough. Elbows are not a vibe. So, uni stuff… anything exciting happening? Besides the impending doom of deadlines, obviously. Ugh, don't remind me. I've got that presentation due on Friday. I’m properly stressing about it. My group's being useless. Oh, the classic uni group dynamic. Who's carrying the team? Definitely me. I swear, if I have to remind them one more time to read the assigned chapters... I’m going to scream. What about you? How's your coding project going? It's…progressing. Slowly. I keep getting these bizarre errors that I can't figure out. It’s like the computer is actively mocking me. I know that feeling. It's the worst. You should show me later. Two heads are better than one, right? Maybe. Or we'll just end up confusing each other even more. Honestly, sometimes I think I should just drop it and become a florist. A florist? You? You’d be terrifying the customers with your ruthless coding skills. "Those lilies aren't symmetrical enough! REBOOT!" Exactly! I'd be a floral overlord. Right, I'm going to grab another chip.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that weekend. You two were absolutely relentless with the quiz questions. Hey, we just wanted to test your obscure trivia knowledge, Liv! You’re the expert! It was good fun though, wasn’t it? Besides, you smashed most of them. Though that one about Georgian furniture nearly stumped us all. Nearly stumped  me ! I was just making educated guesses. Seriously, did you two plan those questions? It felt suspiciously organised. We did a little research. I’m still buzzing from finding that fact about Yorkshire puddings being traditionally served with gravy  and  meat pies. Mind blowing. Don't even start. I had a meat pie last night and now I’m convinced everything’s going to taste like gravy. So, holiday plans still on for Italy then? You were talking about that trip to Tuscany. Yeah, definitely. I’ve been looking at flights again. Problem is, everyone else is having the same idea. Prices are insane. Well, you could always come with us to Cornwall. We’re thinking of heading down there for a long weekend in August. Bit of surfing, bit of hiking… less Renaissance art, more pasties. Cornwall’s lovely, but Tuscany... it’s a dream, you know? And I need some sunshine and pasta after this dreary weather. Did you see that new series on Netflix, ‘Slow Horses’? I’ve heard good things! Gary Oldman, isn't it? I'm trying to avoid spoilers. I’m currently obsessed with ‘Succession’ though, anyone else? Absolutely! The writing is just phenomenal. And the characters are so brilliantly awful. I’m actually feeling emotional about it ending. Me too! I’m going to be devastated. Right, speaking of food, I’m starving. I made a massive batch of chilli last night. Fancy some? Chilli sounds amazing! I'm in. Cheers, Liv. Always good to have a proper home cooked meal. Did you manage to grab that new cookbook you were mentioning? The one about regional British dishes? I did! It's fascinating. Apparently, there's a very specific way to make a proper Cornish pasty – a crimped pastry edge to prevent the miners' fingers from getting burned when they held it during their lunch break. Who knew? See? You  are  the trivia expert. It’s a curse, really. I can't walk past a historical fact without absorbing it. You know what? I saw a terrible pun online the other day…

Right then, so the telly’s on, kettle’s boiled… what’s everyone fancy? Another cup of that Earl Grey, Brenda? Please, Arthur. And you, David? You've been staring at the news like it's going to bite you. Just catching up, Mum. This election stuff's a right mess, innit? Seems like nobody knows what they're doing. Never do, do they? Politics. Always been a load of hooey. Remember when they said they were building a new bypass around Costessey? Still waiting for that one, I am. Arthur, darling, don’t start reminiscing about road schemes. We were talking about the trip to London. David, have you made any progress on the tickets yet? Nearly there, Mum. Just looking at some options for the theatre. Thinking of seeing "Wicked," Bethany loves that one. "Wicked," eh? All that singing and dancing. Not my cup of tea, that. Give me a good old Western any day. John Wayne, now that's entertainment. Arthur, you and your Westerns! Honestly. Remember that trip to Cornwall we took? The youth hostel was lovely. Though I do wish they hadn’t had quite so many horses. Horses! Loved the horses. Always fancied myself as a bit of a jockey, I did. Never had the opportunity, mind. Family commitments and all that. Speaking of commitments, Dad, did you manage to get that car listed on eBay? You were talking about selling it last week. Aye, listed it. Not much interest so far. People looking for a bargain, they are. Don’t appreciate a decent Vauxhall, do they? Been a reliable motor, that one. It's got to go, Arthur. You can't keep it just sitting there. It's costing you money in road tax. Mum's right, Dad. You could put more pictures on. Show off the interior. And maybe lower the price a bit. Lower the price? It's worth every penny! I’m not just giving it away. Besides, someone offered me a fiver for it the other day. Said they'd do it up as a garden ornament. A garden ornament! Arthur, really! Honestly, Dad. Anyway, I was thinking about buying that little cottage near Lichfield. The one Mrs. Peterson was selling. Oh, that’s lovely, David. But is it a good investment? You know how the housing market is. It seems reasonable, Mum. And it’s got a nice little garden.

So, how's Leo been? Last time I spoke to Mum, she said he was teething terribly. Oh, don’t even get me started on the teething! It’s been…intense. He basically hasn't slept properly in two weeks. Just tiny little bursts of sleep and then screaming. I’m running on fumes. Poor you! I remember Mum saying it was rough with Harry, but this sounds next level. Are you managing to get any help? Dad's been amazing, honestly. He’s been taking Leo for a couple of hours in the morning so I can at least shower and drink a hot cup of tea. It’s the little things, you know? But the nights are still… the nights are something else. I can imagine. Is he still refusing the bottle? Completely. Solidly. He gives me the most dramatic look of betrayal if I even  try  to offer it to him. It’s a battle of wills every single feed. I'm pretty sure he thinks I’m trying to poison him. That's classic! Mum told me Harry was exactly the same. She felt like she was constantly being judged by this tiny human. Exactly! And it’s exhausting. I feel like I’m failing him, you know? Like I should be able to feed him perfectly. Everyone keeps saying, "Oh, babies are so precious, enjoy every moment!" But some moments are just… survival mode. They are. It's okay to feel that way. And honestly, breast feeding is hard work even  without  a stubborn little man. I remember reading about it at uni, but the reality is... so different. Tell me about it. I remember being all idealistic about the whole thing, imagining these lovely moments of bonding and… well, it’s mostly just me hunched over in a darkened room, leaking everywhere. Right? Don’t let anyone romanticize it. Did you hear from Auntie Carol today? She was asking about coming over next weekend. Yeah, I told her maybe. I'm not sure I'm up for having visitors right now, honestly. I need a solid eight hours of sleep before I can face anyone. I understand completely. Maybe just a quick coffee and a peek at Leo? She does adore him. Yeah, okay. Maybe. I’ll have a think. But no holding him for too long! My arms are already feeling like lead. Deal!

Right, so toast and eggs everyone? I’ve got the bacon on. Sounds amazing, thanks! What’s all the fuss about in the news this morning? I just saw the headlines about those cuts to the NHS. Usual story, isn't it? More of the same. They promise the world then quietly chip away. It’s dreadful, isn’t it? I’m seeing it firsthand in my training. Resources are stretched so thin already. It makes you wonder. Don’t we all. Right, eggs are almost done. Anyone want brown or white? Brown, please. Did you see Brenda’s garden looking the other day, Mum? Absolutely bursting with roses. I did! She's got the magic touch, that woman. I swear, my roses look like they’re constantly apologising for existing. You need to use some proper fertilizer, love. Not that supermarket stuff. Got to get the right balance. I know, I know! It's on the list. Alongside sorting out the guttering, and finally tackling that overgrown patch by the shed. You should ask Richard about the guttering. He’s surprisingly good at that sort of thing. He fixed mine last year, no bother. Proper DIY skills, that man. Honestly, I'm exhausted just thinking about housework. I’m trying to convince my flatmate to take on more responsibility, but… it's a lost cause. Young people these days, eh? No appreciation for a good scrub. Remember when your Aunt Maureen… Oh, please, Dad. Spare us the Maureen anecdotes before breakfast! Alright, alright. Just saying. She used to polish the silver until you could see your reflection. Speaking of silver, I need to take my grandmother’s teapot to the silversmith. It’s gotten terribly tarnished. Oh, that’s lovely. It’s such a beautiful piece. It is. Listen, I need to run through some patient notes before my shift. Looks like a busy one. Are you working the oncology ward again? Yeah, I am. It's... challenging. But rewarding if you know what I mean. Just be careful, Sarah. Don’t let it get to you. These things… they can wear you down. I know, Dad. I’ve got my coping strategies. And Brenda’s roses to look forward to! Absolutely. You deserve a beautiful garden to escape to. Right, well I need to hit the gym before my freelance deadlines hit. Wish me luck! Good luck, darling! And don't forget to eat something proper afterwards.

Ugh, I’m so stressed about the Chemistry test next week. Mrs. Davies is being  brutal  this year. Tell me about it! I spent, like, three hours last night just trying to memorise the periodic table. It’s ridiculous. Why do we even need to know all that stuff? Because apparently it's "fundamental," according to her. Fundamental to what, I don’t know! I'd rather be painting. Ms. Riley let us do watercolour landscape studies today and it was  amazing . You're so lucky. We had Maths. Mr. Finch just drones on and on about quadratic equations. It’s mind-numbing. Did you see the dress Ruby was wearing today? The sparkly one? It was a bit much, wasn’t it? Especially for a Tuesday. Did she get in trouble? I don't think so. Head of year didn’t say anything. Maybe she just doesn’t care. Speaking of, have you seen the new stamps that just came out? The ones with the wildflowers? Oh yeah! My grandad has loads. He’s obsessed with stamps. He keeps trying to show me different varieties, but honestly… they all look the same to me. They're actually really cool, if you look closely. There’s one with a bee orchid. They’re so rare, you know. It’s kind of like a bit of science and art all combined. True. I wouldn’t have thought of it that way. Anyway, back to the stress. Is anyone else doing extra revision sessions for Chemistry? I’m thinking about it. But I’d rather watch Ed Sheeran’s concert film. Have you seen it? I’ve got the DVD! It's so good. His mum plays the violin, remember? That was a really lovely moment. It was! Okay, quick change of subject - Christmas. Are you getting a real tree this year? Definitely. Mum's already started decorating the house. It’s a bit chaotic, but festive. What about you? Yeah, my dad’s ordering one from that farm shop on the edge of town. He's always on about supporting local businesses. Smart. Are you getting any new plants for the garden? Mum wants me to help with the winter bedding. I’m not sure I’m very good at it. I keep accidentally squashing things. My grandma's got the greenest fingers you've ever seen. She can make anything grow.

That rat puppet, eh? Still got it, you know. Down in the shed somewhere. Oh really, Arthur? The one your mum made? I’d almost forgotten about that! It was rather… lifelike, wasn't it? A bit creepy, if I'm honest. Lifelike's the word! Your mum thought she was being clever with the whiskers. Gave it a right mischievous look. Used to terrify the grandkids, you remember. Little Emily used to scream blue murder if it came near her. I do recall that rat, Arthur. A rather striking piece of needlework, actually. Though, as Brenda says, perhaps a bit unsettling for the very young. It had a certain presence, didn't it? Presence is right! Used to sit on the mantelpiece and stare. Makes you wonder what she was thinking. Mum, I mean. Not the rat. Oh, Arthur. Always going off on one. Speaking of which, are you still managing alright on the buses, dear? Getting about as easily as you used to? Well, it’s alright. A bit of a faff, waiting around, you know. And some of the young drivers… don’t have the patience they used to. Grumbling about every stop. But it’s better than nothing. Need to keep moving, that's what they tell you. I was thinking about getting your eyes tested, Arthur. It's been a while. Perhaps that would make a difference with the bus journeys. See the signs clearer. Aye, might be a good idea, Robert. The numbers on the bus stops are getting smaller by the day, I swear. Always squinting. Might as well be trying to read ants' writing. We could book you in with Dr. Davies, remember? She’s very good. Always lets you look at the pictures with the animals. Animals, eh? Bit childish, isn’t it? But I suppose it's a good test. Remember me saying the 'E' looked like a wonky gate? You always did. And that time you thought the 'W' was a pair of swans! It did! Looked just like two swans swimming on a pond. Don’t argue with me! Oh, Arthur. Now, about that handbell ringing… Are you still practicing? The church is looking for a few more ringers, you know. Aye, trying to keep my fingers nimble. It's tricky, these days. My hand isn’t what it was. But it’s a good way to pass the time.

Right, so I was thinking, after coffee, we could potter around those little shops by the canal? Maybe get a little souvenir – you know, something cheesy. Cheesy is exactly what Venice does best, isn't it? Though you won't find much that's genuinely authentic anymore, love. Used to be, you'd find little workshops, glassblowers, lace makers...My grandma used to bring back the most beautiful lace collars from here. Really? I didn't know. It feels pretty touristy now, doesn't it? Still lovely though. It is. But it's changed a lot. Remember that little ice cream parlour, Gelateria Valentino? Right near the Rialto Bridge? The one with the queue stretching halfway down the street? That's the one. Used to be a tiny, proper local place. The gelato was incredible. Pistachio, especially. They don't make it like that anymore. Everything’s just become so…commercial. Sad, innit? Still, ice cream’s ice cream. What are you thinking about for lunch? I’m starving already. Want to try some cicchetti? Cicchetti? You’re learning my ways! Yes, absolutely. Those little Venetian tapas. Some fried zucchini flowers, a little plate of meatballs...and a glass of prosecco, of course. Can't have cicchetti without prosecco. Of course not! I was thinking we could wander and just see what catches our eye. There’s always something delicious looking tempting you from those doorways. I saw a place earlier with a board advertising "fritto misto" – sounded amazing. Fritto misto is always a good choice. Fresh seafood, lightly battered… Heavenly. You know, they used to have a proper fish market here, proper hustle and bustle. You'd see these huge crates of eels, octopus... Now it’s all a bit sanitized, a bit controlled. I can imagine. Still, even with the tourists, there's something magical about it, isn’t there? The canals, the gondolas... It is. And the history! Everywhere you look, there's a story. I once spent an afternoon just following a little side canal, and I stumbled upon this tiny, ancient church...completely deserted. Felt like I was stepping back in time. Sounds incredible. Maybe we should do that today, get lost a little bit. Forget the guidebooks and just see where we end up. I like that idea. After lunch, we could head towards St. Mark’s Square. But don't linger too long. It's a pigeon feeding frenzy these days!

Seriously though, I need to get back to the gym. I’m feeling it. All this peri-peri chicken is delicious, don’t get me wrong, but I’m definitely regretting skipping leg day. Tell me about it! I was so disciplined last week, managed five sessions, and then this weekend…boom, all bets are off. Too much prosecco, not enough squats. Prosecco is the downfall of us all. Did you hear from Chloe and Ben? Are they still in Bali? Oh, I saw their stories. Looks absolutely idyllic. Ben’s really getting into surfing, apparently. I’m so jealous, I just spent my holiday stressing about finding a decent SPF. Classic you. I’m trying to be more adventurous. Thinking about that climbing trip to Portugal next year. Ooh, adventurous! You? I’d be terrified! Although… a bit of sun, a bit of climbing… sounds better than another week in Brighton. Did you ever hear back from that Portuguese climbing instructor you were chatting to? Yeah, he sent through some itineraries. It’s expensive though. So, work's been manic, as always. The Johnson project is eating into all my time. Tell me about it. Bupa’s going crazy with new initiatives. We practically live in Zoom meetings now. Honestly, I need a holiday just to recover from work. I’m thinking Spain, sometime in November. Somewhere warm, where I can just… relax. Sounds heavenly! We should go together. You, me, Chloe, Ben... I'd love that! Although, you'd probably want to find hiking trails. I’d be content with finding a decent tapas bar and a sunbed. Compromise is key! Hey, did you ever hear from… you know… Liam? Oh, Liam. He messaged actually, a couple of weeks ago. Said he was ‘thinking about things.’ Super cryptic, as usual. I just ignored him. Honestly, he was a drama magnet. Good for you! You deserve better than constant drama. I’m glad you cut ties. Speaking of which, Alex is no longer speaking to Sarah… apparently over a boy. No! Alex? Seriously? That’s ridiculous. What’s he like, a teenage heartthrob? Apparently quite charming. Anyway, don't get me started. It's ridiculous. So, about that climbing trip… I was thinking of doing a beginner’s course here first. Anyone fancy joining? I think I’ll stick to my Zumba classes for now. But definitely count me in for Spain!

It’s absolutely wonderful news, darling. A little girl! Seven pounds, they said. Absolutely perfect. A girl! Splendid. Splendid indeed. Quite a weight, though, isn't she? They don't make ‘em small anymore. And abroad, you say? Where was she born? Paris. They decided to have her in Paris. Apparently, the healthcare is… well, much better than here, and they felt more comfortable. France. Always a complicated relationship, France. Property, you know, dreadful to acquire. Bureaucrats and anarchists, really a swirling stew. I remember trying to buy a small patch of land near Dijon once… an absolute nightmare. Oh, I can imagine! Though, I’ve always found the French to be rather charming when they’re not trying to sell you something or refuse you permission. We had a lovely couple visit from Lyon last year. Spent a week here, absolutely fell in love with Richmond Park. Richmond Park. Good choice. Though, have you heard about that Chichester Cathedral spire? Collapsed, you know. Terrible shame. The architect, Porden, a brilliant man, though his designs weren’t always universally admired. Oh, no! I saw something about that online. Dreadful. They’re having an open day and a photo exhibition soon, apparently, documenting the repairs. And there's an art competition linked to it, inspired by the history of the cathedral. Art competition, eh? Nowadays, you can hang anything on the wall and call it art. I saw a sculpture in Trafalgar Square once… looked like a crumpled-up crisp packet. You’re terrible! But it’s true, standards have slipped. Speaking of things that irritate, have you noticed the new bollards they’ve put on Streatham High Road? Appalling placement. Completely block the view and make it impossible to reverse. I had a near miss last week. Bollards! A constant source of irritation. Utterly thoughtless planning. Now, locally, things are even worse. This new housing management company… truly appalling. They’re neglecting the building, ignoring complaints… total shambles. Oh, I'm so sorry to hear that. It's the same everywhere, isn't it? No one cares anymore. It reminds me somewhat of my experiences in the Spanish archives. Trying to trace the lineage of a distant relative… Philip of Spain, during Mary Tudor’s reign. The paperwork was horrific. Mountains of it. They didn’t throw anything away! Good heavens! What a project. It was fascinating, though. I nearly got lost in the details.

This sweet and sour chicken is actually pretty good, yeah? Way better than last time. Yeah, it is. I think they got a new chef. This crispy beef is banging too. Nah, the noodles are rubbish. Seriously, so soggy. I asked for them dry. My parents always say Chinese food is bad for you, all the salt and stuff. My mum’s the same. She’s always on about my diet. Like, I’m sixteen, let me live. I ate a whole bag of crisps on the bus here. You are a menace! My dad’s the same, though. He keeps telling me I need to eat more vegetables. At least you have a dad who cares. My mum just says, “Eat what you want, you’ll be thin like me eventually.” Which isn’t reassuring considering she’s practically a stick insect. Haha! My mum’s obsessed with fitness. She drags me to Zumba on Saturday mornings. It’s so embarrassing. Zumba? Seriously? That's brutal. Did you see Liam yesterday? He was having a complete meltdown in maths. What happened this time? Apparently, Mr. Davies drilled him on quadratic equations for an hour straight. Liam was practically crying. Poor Liam. Davies is a monster. I think he gets kicks out of torturing us. Remember last year when he made us write an essay on why Pythagoras’ theorem is important? Oh my god, yeah! I spent the entire weekend researching it and my essay was still terrible. It’s a miracle any of us pass. Did you hear about Sarah and Jake? No! What? They're officially a thing. Apparently, they went to the cinema last night. No way! Sarah? I thought she was still hung up on Ben. Ben’s with Chloe now, remember? That was a whole drama. Yeah, I blocked that from my memory. So, Jake? He's… decent. Not exactly my type. He's alright. He’s got that awkward charm thing going on. You know? I saw a new comic book yesterday. Oh yeah? What is it? It's the latest issue of ‘Galactic Defenders’. The artwork is insane. I’m more into ‘Shadow Runners’ myself. ‘Shadow Runners’? Sounds depressing. Nah, it's brilliant! It's all about cyberpunk and hacking. You guys are weird. I’m sticking with superheroes. They’re way more fun. So, who's doing homework tonight? Definitely not me. I'm going to play Fortnite.

Well, isn't this lovely? Jonathan’s birthday, everyone together. It's been far too long since we've all been in one place like this. Aye, it has. Feels good to be back in Kendal, though. The air’s different, you know? More… bracing. It’s alright. Wi-fi's a bit dodgy though. Classic Kendal. Though I've upgraded the router, lad. Should be better. Aye, it’s good to be ‘ere. Though I’m not sure my legs are up to all the standing about. Now, now, Elsie. You sit and rest. We'll bring everything to you. So, we're thinking about clearing out the attic, aren't we, David? It's overflowing. It is. It's horrifying, actually. Decades of stuff. I was thinking about having a proper clear-out, maybe a car boot sale. Tidying up for Jonathan’s sake, too. Bit less clutter for his birthday celebration. Car boot sale! Brilliant! I’ve got loads of stuff I could get rid of. Some pottery, some old bits and bobs...though some of that stuff might be worth something now. Branding, you know. Nostalgia’s a powerful thing these days. You wouldn’t get much for old pottery, Auntie Brenda. It's all landfill-bound, realistically. Don't be so pessimistic, lad! Elsie here is rather the expert on antiques. Isn’t that right, Elsie? Well, I knew a thing or two. Though mostly it was just knowing what my mother wouldn’t let me touch! Speaking of forgetting things, I’ve been trying to sort out those plans for the holiday. We were thinking of the Lake District, weren’t we? A nice walking holiday. Aye, sounds lovely. Although, I'm not sure my knees are up to fell walking anymore. Might be easier somewhere flatter. Like Norfolk. Norfolk? Seriously? It's just...flat. We can compromise, Liam. Maybe somewhere with gentle hills. We’ll have a proper look at some options. Have you been to that new restaurant in Penrith, David? 'The Hearth'? I went last week, actually! The food was simply divine. A bit pricey, mind you, but worth it for a special occasion. Jonathan would love it. Right, well, that's settled then! The Hearth it is. Are we booking a table for the lot of us? I'll do it. Anything else we need to sort out for Jonathan? Gifts?

Ugh, I’m so stressed about GCSE options already. Like, it’s only October! Tell me about it! My parents are being all pushy about science, but I really want to do Art and Drama. Seriously? My mum’s obsessed with me doing triple science. Says it’s the only way I'll get a good job. What do  you  want to do? I don't know, honestly. Maybe film making? Or something creative. I saw this amazing youtuber the other day, she’s got like millions of subscribers. Oh yeah? Who? I’m mostly on TikTok, you know? Bogs and bloggers are my thing. Her name’s LunaBloom. She does these really aesthetic travel vlogs. It's so inspiring! You should check her out. Maybe later. I'm more interested in school stuff, right now. What about jobs? Are you thinking about that yet? My dad just keeps going on about needing to ‘secure our futures’. Future's terrifying! I keep picturing myself working in a grey office, staring at a computer all day. Dreadful. Exactly! Though I did consider being a clarinet player, but then I realised you have to be, like,  really  famous to make a living from it. And I'm not exactly a prodigy. Haha, true. I saw this thing about how hard it is to be a professional athlete too. All the injuries and pressure! It’s so weird how everyone is suddenly famous, isn't it? Like, last week I was obsessed with that actor, Liam something... Liam Hemsworth? Yeah, that’s the one! Everyone was going wild over him but then I realised he's, like, totally ordinary. He lives in Malibu. People are obsessed! My PE teacher thinks he’s a god. It’s so embarrassing. Speaking of PE… I’m dreading the fitness test next week. I'm going to fail the bleep test for sure. Me too! I’m hopeless at running. I’d rather do perfect duty in the library than run a mile. I hate perfect duty! Miss Henderson is so strict. Gets right up your nose. Seriously! She’s watching everyone like a hawk. I accidentally dropped my pen last week and she gave me the stink-eye. Ugh! I wish school wouldn't be so intense all the time. Maybe we should just watch LunaBloom’s travel vlogs and pretend we’re somewhere amazing. Like, Bali or something.

So, the bluebell woods were absolutely glorious today, weren't they, Margaret? Proper carpet of them. Oh, they were lovely, Arthur. Absolutely lovely. Though I did nearly trip over a badger sett. Nearly sent me sprawling! Badgers, eh? Used to know a fella, worked at the Vauxhall dealership, saw a badger rooting about in the engine bay of a Viva once. Didn't like it much. You wouldn't, would you? Imagine the paperwork. Yes, well, they're getting bolder, aren’t they? Heard tell of foxes rummaging through bins in the village now. Times are changing. Reminds me of that article I read about the software updates on cars – apparently, they can now track your driving habits and adjust the engine settings. Bit spooky, isn't it? Oh, don't start me on that technology, Arthur. It's all frightfully complicated. I can barely work the telly, let alone a car that’s spying on you. Aye, spying’s the word. Remember when cars were just… cars? You put petrol in, you turned the key, and off you went. No computer telling you how to drive. Simpler times. Though the rust was a right bother. True, Dad. But the fuel economy is so much better now. And the safety features – airbags, ABS, lane assist… it's all pretty impressive. I agree, it's come a long way. Though I do miss the days of a good old British Leyland. Solid vehicles, they were. Even with the… eccentricities. I had a Triumph Toledo once. Lovely car, but the steering wheel locked itself at random intervals. Nearly ended up in a ditch a few times. Oh dear! That sounds terrifying. Anything’s better than ending up in a ditch. I used to tell the children, 'Always look both ways, girls!’ You never know what’s lurking. Always a good lesson, Nan. I was reading about the Roman history of Norfolk the other day – apparently, they built some pretty impressive roads around here. Must have been quite the undertaking. Romans, eh? Built the roads, alright. And a bloody fort near Wymondham! Still bits of it left, you know. Can't believe they came all the way here. That’s right! Boudicca’s revolt, wasn’t it? Terrible business that. They say the Romans had left their demijohns of wine behind after the battle...locals plundered them for years afterward. Really? Wine! Imagine that.

Well, I never! Did you see that delivery man yesterday? Tripped right over the gnome. Nearly broke his ankle, poor fellow. Oh, heavens! Gertrude’s gnomes are a menace, aren't they? Always strategically placed to trip someone up. She thinks it’s a laugh, the old girl. Sounds like her. Gertrude always did have a… unique sense of humour. So, how’s the school front going, ANON? Still wrestling with those Year 7s? Wrestling is the word! Honestly, the amount of TikToks they're watching in class… it’s astonishing. Trying to teach Shakespeare when their brains are full of dance routines. Oh, TikTok! I’ve heard tales. My granddaughter’s obsessed. Sends me videos of cats doing silly things. I don't understand it. It's a rabbit hole, that's what it is. One minute you're watching a cat, the next you're learning how to make sourdough bread. And then you're wondering where the last three hours went. Exactly! Speaking of rabbit holes, my daughter keeps badgering me to get on Twitter. "It’s a great way to connect, Dad!" she says. Twitter? Oh, I tried that once. Nearly gave myself a heart attack reading all the arguments. Deleted it within an hour. Fair enough. It’s a battlefield out there. Though, I confess, I do enjoy a good rant on Twitter now and then. Keeps me feeling young, somehow. You? A Twitter warrior? I’d never have guessed. Don’t tell anyone. It’s my guilty pleasure. Right, so what's on the telly these evenings? Anything worth watching? Oh,  Bake Off  is back! I’m so looking forward to that. Always a bit of comfort viewing, isn't it?  Bake Off  is lovely. Though I'm not sure about these new complicated recipes. Remember when it was just Victoria sponges and lemon drizzle? Much simpler. Simpler times. I’m more of a  Line of Duty  man, myself. Keeps you on the edge of your seat. Though, all that tension does give me a headache. Speaking of headaches, my knees have been playing up again. Doctor says it’s just age, you know. Age is a cruel mistress. I’ve got a dodgy hip myself. The doctor keeps suggesting exercises. But who has time for exercises when there's cleaning to be done? Cleaning! Don’t even get me started. My wife’s got this obsession with spotless floors.

Honestly, this is mad! I didn't think it would snow this much in Cambridge! It's like being back home - remember all those snow days in Sunderland? Aye, I do. Though I reckon it’s a bit milder than what you'd get up north, isn't it? Still, it’s pretty. Fancy a cuppa? I'm just making some. Please! And maybe something cakey? This cold is sucking the life out of me. Sorted. So, have you been looking at any of those spring bulbs for the garden? The snowdrops are already poking through in a few places. I have! I was thinking tulips, definitely. And maybe some daffodils, to brighten the place up. It all looks so grey at the moment. It’s a bit depressing, to be honest. We could use some colour. Right, tea’s on. Did you catch the latest Come Dine With Me? The one with the dodgy risotto? Oh god, yes! The host was horrendous. So smug about his ‘culinary skills’ while serving absolute slop. And didn’t even clear the table between courses! Awful, wasn’t it? It was glorious train-wreck viewing. Speaking of plans… Have you made any progress on booking those flights to Greece for us? Almost! I’m just trying to find a decent deal. I wanted to go in mid-June, before it gets too sweltering. I was thinking Rhodes, or maybe somewhere on the islands? Rhodes sounds lovely. Relaxing. We need that. And what about Mark’s stag do? Any idea what they’re planning? It’s only a few months away now. He’s being deliberately vague, which is probably a good thing. Apparently, there’s a paintballing session planned, confirmed by his best man. I'm worried it'll be a mess and I'm hoping to keep my distance. Paintballing – sounds… energetic. And what about Sarah's hen do? Are you involved in any of the organising? A little bit. She’s keeping the main details hush-hush, but I’m helping with decorations. It's going to be a murder mystery theme at The Cambridge Arms, pretty classy stuff. That sounds brilliant! Far better than some of those wild hen dos you see. Less chance of anyone ending up in the wrong pub. Exactly! I'm more of a sophisticated criminal vibe. Speaking of, I need to pop to the garden centre later.

This roast potatoes are absolutely spot on, Dad. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Well, practice makes perfect, doesn't it? Though I still think I used to do them better back in the day. Don’t be silly, Arthur. They're lovely. Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside. Just how they should be. Though, a little more rosemary wouldn’t have gone amiss. They’re great, honestly. Better than any roast potatoes I’ve made, and I’ve had a fair few goes. I've been trying to replicate this roast potato for years! It’s the secret to the fat, isn't it? Goose fat, rather than sunflower. Aye, goose fat’s the ticket. Sunflower just doesn’t have the same…oomph. Though goose fat is getting a bit pricey these days. Everything's pricey these days. Remember when you could get a whole chicken for a shilling, Arthur? Don't I just. And a loaf of bread. A proper loaf, not one of these airy things you get now. It's crazy, isn't it? The prices of everything are ridiculous. Though, you can’t deny these roast potatoes are worth every penny. You’re buttering him up, Tom! He’ll be charging us next time. Wouldn’t be the first time. Now, are you going to finish that Yorkshire pudding, dear? Don't want to waste it. Almost done, Mum. It was lovely. So Sarah, how’s that new course going? The one on, what was it, existentialism? Sounds wild to me. It is a bit head-scratching, yeah. But fascinating. It’s all about finding meaning, apparently. Meaning in life? What's wrong with a good cup of tea and a biscuit, eh? That's meaning enough for me. You’re incorrigible, Arthur. I'm trying to get through a module on Baudrillard. It's… intense. He argues that our experience of reality is increasingly mediated through signs and symbols, so we’re living in a simulacrum. Basically, nothing is real. Ah, that's the one. Bit depressing, isn’t it? It is, a little. But intriguing. It makes you wonder what’s truly authentic anymore. Authentic? We had authentic. In my day, bread was bread, milk was milk. You knew where it came from. Now everything’s got fancy labels and hidden ingredients. You're right, Arthur. It's all so complicated these days.

This gravy is absolutely incredible, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Aye, well, it’s just a bit o’ gravy love. Nothin’ fancy. Got a secret ingredient though… Oh really? What is it? More stock? Hmph, if I told you that, I’d have to… never you mind. It’s a family secret. Your Dad here doesn’t even know. That’s right. Been eating it for fifty years, still no clue. You're both terrible. Seriously, though, this roast is perfect. And Dad, the Yorkshire puddings were brilliant! Glad you liked ‘em, love. Took me a while to get the oven temperature right. Remember your Nana always said… Oh god, here we go. ...Hot enough to burn the devil, but not enough to scorch the angels, aye. Classic Grandpa. Still passing on those baking lessons. He’s been saying that for as long as I can remember. Though his Yorkshire’s always been a bit flat. Flat! They were lovely. They were lovely, Grandpa. Everything's lovely. So, Mum, how’s the garden doing? Did you manage to get those roses planted? Aye, they’re in. Though the slugs are having a field day with them. I’ve put down some slug pellets, but it’s a constant battle. You should try beer traps, Mum. They’re surprisingly effective. Beer traps? Don’t be daft. Waste of good beer. Actually, they do work quite well. Got a few for the grandkids when they came over. Reminds me, I saw this amazing little house for sale in Bristol. Three bedrooms, garden… really cute. Bristol? Bit far from here, isn’t it? Yeah, I know. But the prices are insane out here. And I’m thinking about a change, you know? Somewhere a bit… vibrant. Vibrant? Where have you been love, Bishop Auckland! Mum! It used to be quite vibrant, you know. Before the mill shut. Grandpa’s got a point. It’s just different now. Different opportunities. I’ve been wanting to explore a bit. Well, you should do what makes you happy, love. You only live once. Just don’t forget to come home for Christmas. Never. You know I'd never miss Christmas with you all. Speaking of Christmas… remember that time when your Uncle Kevin tried to dress up as Santa? Oh, don’t start! Oh, it was a sight to behold! The beard was all crooked and… Oh god, yes!

Honestly, the heat is something else here, isn't it? Even this morning, walking the dog. It’s relentless. It is, but the light! Have you noticed the light? It's just incredible. Makes everything look…painterly. And it’s perfect for those drone shots I was talking about for the app. Right, the app. Still massively ambitious, isn't it? Trying to gamify university study with augmented reality. Are you  sure  it's not going to just be a massive headache? I’m aware it’s a challenge, but I genuinely think it’s needed. Students learn differently now. Lectures are... well, let's just say they're a dwindling resource. They need something interactive, engaging, a way to tailor their learning. Remember that social story-telling project you did a few years ago? Vaguely. It was hellishly time-consuming, but the kids loved it. They built characters, created narratives... the learning happened organically. That’s the model I'm thinking about, but scaled up for higher education. Exactly! And think about it – instead of dry textbooks, students build virtual realities around the course material. They collaborate, they problem-solve  within  the simulation. It’s about creating a sense of agency. But the technical hurdles are enormous. Getting the AR to be genuinely useful, not just a gimmick... and the developmental cost! You need a stellar development team. I know. I’ve been talking to a couple of guys in Melbourne. Ex-gaming developers, clever fellas. They've got a knack for making things "go viral." Remember that crazy cat video that showed up on everyone’s feed last month? How could I forget? My students were analysing its marketing strategy for a whole week. What’s that got to do with anything? They understand how to hook people, how to make something shareable. I want that spark for the app. Something that makes students  want  to learn. It's not just about the technology, it’s about the psychology of it all. I've even been looking at behavioural economics models for incentivization... Behavioural economics. Right. You’re thinking rewards, points systems, leaderboards... Simplistically, yes. But also about shaping the learning environment to encourage certain behaviours, nudge them towards curiosity. I was reading about this entrepreneur in Singapore… he built an entire platform around problem-solving challenges, focused specifically on developing resilience. Resilience. That's a key skill for university.

Right, so I made far too much lasagne. You want a portion for later? Oh, definitely! You’re a lifesaver. I’m absolutely starving after that shift. Had a really tough one today. Oh no, what happened? Don't tell me, you don’t want to relive it. No, it’s alright. Just a bit much to unpack right now. Mostly it was just… intense. Ms. Davies was having a particularly bad day. You know how she gets. Yeah, the whole crashing-waves-of-emotion thing. Poor thing. How was your weekend, then? Did you manage to get out of London at all? Not really, no. I was supposed to go to Cornwall with Liam's family, but his mum came down with something. Gutted. Cornwall's been on my list forever. You ever been? Once, ages ago. Holiday with my parents when I was a kid. Beautiful, but so touristy now, isn’t it? I’d rather go somewhere a bit… quieter. Like Norfolk, maybe? Norfolk? Really? Why Norfolk? Bit flat, isn't it? I don’t know! Just feels… peaceful. And the Broads are lovely, I've seen some gorgeous photos. What about you? Any five-year plan dreams kicking around? Beyond keeping Ms. Davies from throwing chairs, obviously. Right. Good point. Hmm… five years… I'd really like to be a senior mental health nurse, leading a team. Maybe specialising in something, like addiction or trauma. And definitely want to own a rescue dog. A big, fluffy one. What about you, Miss Project Coordinator? World domination? Don't be silly. Mostly just hoping to be slightly less stressed! Ideally, I’d love to be running my own project management consultancy. Freelance, so I can work from anywhere. Maybe… Devon? Devon! That's lovely. You'd love it. Rolling hills, cream teas... Exactly! Ooh, speaking of things I love... Halloween parties! Have you started planning anything? I saw this amazing costume idea online – a giant avocado. Please don't. My eyes! But seriously, I might just do a low-key thing with Liam’s friends. We talked about doing a murder mystery night. Ooh, that's good! We could join! I’ve got some killer one-liners for a dramatic reveal. You always do. Okay, murder mystery, it is! It’s just… I’m so tired. I need a huge plate of lasagne and a lie-down. Coming right up!

Honestly, darling, the traffic getting here was absolutely ghastly. Took me nearly two hours, and I usually do it in about ninety minutes. Oh, Mum! That’s awful. I’m so sorry. I didn't realise it would be so bad. Everything's usually pretty smooth around here on a Sunday. Well, not today, love. Apparently, there was an accident on the A14. Something about a lorry and a caravan. Dreadful. The whole road was backed up. Had to listen to that awful radio show the whole way. Oh, really? Which one? One of those… well, I can't remember the name. All blather about celebrities and what they had for lunch. Honestly! I switched it off as soon as I could. Sounds like you. I bet. Did you at least have a nice cup of tea when you got home? I did, thank you. A good strong one. Settled me right down. Although, the cat was being a right terror, demanding attention and rubbing against my legs. Honestly, that animal thinks he owns the place. He’s just affectionate. You love him really. Speaking of things owning places, Daniel’s been on at me about getting a dog. A dog! Oh, goodness. Where would you put a dog? This flat isn't exactly spacious. I know, I know. But he says we could take it for walks in the park, and it would be good for us to get out more. It would be a lot of responsibility though. I don't know. It certainly would. They’re not like having a goldfish, you know. They need a lot of time and attention, and they can be expensive. Think carefully, darling. Don’t get caught up in the moment. I’m trying to. He keeps showing me pictures of golden retriever puppies on Instagram. It’s relentless. Men and their puppies. It’s a classic. So, are you seeing Liam tomorrow? Actually, yes. We're going to that new Italian place in the centre. Heard good things. It's called "Bella Notte," I think. Oh, lovely! I do hope it’s good. Do let me know what it’s like. I might fancy trying it myself. Will do. And we're thinking of going ice skating next weekend. Fancy joining us? Ice skating! Oh, my knees wouldn’t thank me for that. But it sounds like fun. Perhaps I’ll just wave from the sidelines and offer moral support.

Honestly, I can’t believe Leeds lost yesterday. Absolutely gutted. Oh, really? I didn’t even realise they were playing. I've been so buried in French grammar, my head’s a mess. It was a nail-biter though, right up until the last minute. Just a silly mistake cost them the game. Proper heartbreaking. How’s your translation work going, then? Still wrestling with those tricky subjunctive clauses? Don't even get me started! This Professor is obsessed with the subjunctive. It’s like, if you get it wrong, the whole essay is marked down. I'm half tempted to just switch to a completely different field of study. Astrophysics, maybe. Less grammar. Astrophysics, eh? Bit of a jump from French, isn't it? Well, anything’s better than endless subjunctive, to be honest! What about you? Still enjoying your uni course? Loads of fieldwork this term? Yeah, it's good, dead good.
