Next week we’re off to look at some erosion patterns in the Peak District. Proper outdoorsy stuff, which is brilliant. Although, the lectures are getting a bit… intense. Loads of stats and different scientific methods we need to remember. My brain’s practically fried. Sounds intense! That's always the way, isn’t it? They cram everything in right at the end. Are you still seeing that lad, Ben? Ben? Oh, yeah, he’s alright. He's been really busy with the band rehearsals, though. They’re trying to get some gigs lined up around Christmas. Oh, that’s exciting! What kind of music do they play? Kinda indie-rock, you know? A bit like The Strokes, maybe. They’re pretty good, actually. You’d probably like them. I’ll have to check them out! Have you been keeping up with anything interesting on the French music scene? I'm trying to broaden my horizons. Not really, to be honest. I mainly just listen to Spotify playlists. What about work? Are you still at that cafe near the university? Yeah, still slinging coffees and pretending to care about latte art. Pays the bills, though! It’s actually not too bad sometimes. Just gets a bit manic during exam season. It’s crazy how many students need caffeine to function! Tell me about it! I've been there. Right, I'm gonna get another pain au chocolat. Fancy one? Absolutely! You know, this trip is actually turning out to be quite nice, despite the grammar struggles.

Honestly, I nearly screamed this morning. Biggest spider I’ve ever seen, right there on the bathroom mirror. Proper hairy legs and everything. Oh, no! Whereabouts? Just sort of staring back at me, you know? Like it owned the place. I had to grab a tissue and flick it out the window. You’re brave! I would’ve run. I’m not good with spiders. We’ve had a bit of a mouse problem this year, haven't we? Can’t seem to get rid of 'em. Oh really? I’ve not noticed anything. We've got a cat though, Jasper, he’s pretty good at keeping things in check. See, I wish I had a cat! I've got traps out, but they only catch the odd one. Little blighters are clever. Nibbled through the cereal box the other day, the cheeky things. Oh, that’s awful. They just seem to pop up out of nowhere, don't they? They do. And the birds are getting bolder too. They’re pecking at the windows, making an awful racket. They do that sometimes! I think it’s because they see their reflection and think it’s another bird, trying to chase it away. That’s what my dad said, years ago. Used to wrap shiny foil around the windows to stop them. Did the trick, apparently. That's a clever idea! I might try that. I've been trying to put up those plastic owls, but I reckon they've worked out it's a fake. They just sit on top of them. They’re on to you, are they? Right little devils, those birds. Everything’s getting bolder these days. You’re telling me! I swear, my garden's turning into a wildlife sanctuary. I almost tripped over a hedgehog the other night. Oh, how lovely! See, you're doing a good job then. Giving them somewhere safe. I'm just trying to keep my house mouse-free! Well, no harm in trying, is there? Though I’d rather not spend my life battling spiders and mice. It's tiring! Tell me about it. It's never ending, isn’t it? But you do what you have to do. Absolutely. So, are you alright for a cuppa? I made some fresh biscuits. Oh, that would be lovely, thank you! A biscuit sounds just what I need after all that talk of creepy crawlies.

It’s lovely to finally meet you, Gwen. I’ve heard so much about you from my mum. Oh, it's wonderful to meet you too, Eleanor. Your mother has spoken about you endlessly, you know. A teacher, just like her! Such a lovely profession. Yes, it is. Though it has its challenges, of course. Did you teach long, Gwen? My mum never properly explained what you taught. Just that you were wonderful. Oh, yes, a good many years. Started in 1973, finished just before I turned sixty. Mostly Welsh, near Cardiff. Bit of a change from Bristol, where I grew up, but I settled in beautifully. Loved the language, loved the kids. That’s brilliant. I’m teaching Year 5 at the moment. It's… energetic. Lots of questions, lots of energy! Oh, I remember those days! Always good to have a bit of life in the classroom, though. So, you’re researching your family history too, then? Your mum mentioned you’d been digging into the past. I am! It’s become a bit of an obsession, actually. I wanted to understand where I came from, you know? Mum always talked about our Welsh roots, said we had some interesting characters in our family tree. Indeed you do! The Rhys family were quite the adventurers. My grandfather, Rhys ap Gwyn, he went to America in the 1880s. Tried his hand at farming, but it didn’t take. Came back a few years later, a bit hardened, but with some stories to tell! Wow! That’s incredible. I wish Mum had told me more. She always seemed to gloss over the details, or forget things. Especially towards the end… I know. It’s a cruel disease, Alzheimer's. Such a slow fading. I remember when your mother had that fall last year. Awful. It was. And the way it progressed so quickly after that... It was just relentless. It’s strange, isn’t it? Knowing she's gone but feeling like a part of her is still here, somewhere. It is. And the guilt, too. You feel guilty for the times you weren’t there, for the things you didn't say. Exactly! I kept thinking, I should have visited more. I should have asked her more about the family. She always had such wonderful stories. You can’t beat yourself up about it, Eleanor. She knew you loved her.

Honestly, look at that sky! It’s just… vast. Makes you feel quite small, doesn't it? It does. And look – is that a hot air balloon? It is! Over there, drifting towards the coast. Proper Norfolk scene, isn't it? Remember when we talked about going up in one? Vaguely. It seemed… expensive. A bit of a frivolous expense, really. Maybe. But imagine the view! Though, I still worry about the landing. Seems a bit haphazard. Well, at least the dog seems happy. Look at Willow bounding around. She’s loving this walk. She is. She's got more energy than me after a day of marking essays. I swear, those students think grammar rules just disappear when they’re writing. Tell me about it. I had one call me out on my use of semi-colons yesterday. A semi-colon! As if that’s a personal attack. Oh, bless. Did you win the argument? Eventually. After about twenty minutes of explaining its purpose. It’s draining. You know, sometimes I wonder if we’re teaching them anything at all. Don't be so bleak. We’re molding young minds. Shaping the future. Shaping the future by arguing about punctuation. Right. Anyway, look - deer! Over by those power lines. Oh, beautiful! They’re so graceful. I love seeing wildlife like this. It’s so different from the grey concrete of the university. It is. Reminds me of that camping trip we did last summer. That was… an experience. The leaky tent, the midges… Don't remind me. I’m still finding pine needles in my hair. And we had to buy a new tent after that, didn't we? We did. Which… brought up a slightly awkward conversation about the budget, didn't it? It did. I know, I know. It's just… it feels like everything costs so much these days. Even a bit of peace and quiet in the countryside. Agreed. Retirement feels a very long way off when you're constantly budgeting for tent repairs and dog food. Don’t even mention retirement. We'll be working until we're eighty, just to afford the postcode lottery of healthcare. Come on, let’s not get into that now. Let’s just enjoy the view, the fresh air, and a well-behaved dog. You're right. You’re always right. Even when you’re subtly reminding me about our financial shortcomings.

Phew! That was a good session. My legs are definitely feeling it this evening. Aye, well done lass! You’ve got some grit. Didn't think I'd see you keeping up with my serves. I'm usually a bit of a beast on the court, you know. You’re not wrong! I’m still relatively new to this, but I’m enjoying it. The weather's been lovely lately, hasn’t it? Unusual for September, really. Aye, really strange. Feels more like July than September. Makes you wonder what the winter’s gonna be like, doesn’t it? I'm bracing myself for a harsh one, honestly. The last few years have been a bit mild, which is nice, but... I'm trying to enjoy the sunshine while it lasts. So, how's everything going at the gyms? Still running around the country? Aye, still doing the rounds. Thankfully things are steady, though our new corporate wellness packages are finally starting to pay off. Head office’s been right on my back about it though, pushing for increased sales. You know how it is. Absolutely. I’m used to deadlines and targets. Teaching languages, it’s always about those exam results, isn’t it? Speaking of, I was just reading this fascinating article about the polyglot effect – how learning multiple languages can actually improve your cognitive function generally. Really? That's a grand thing to know. My granddaughter’s trying to learn Spanish, the clever little thing. I keep telling her to stick with it, but she’s got a million and one distractions these days. That’s so true. It’s tough keeping children engaged. Do you think the education system is moving fast enough to keep up with changes? We're seeing huge shifts in how people learn, especially with online resources. Well, I’m no expert, mind. Finished school back in '82, and things were a fair bit different then. Felt like a lot of rote learning back then. My brother, he said they're bringing coaching techniques into schools now, teaching kids how to learn  how  to learn. That’s exactly what we’re aiming for in my classes. It’s less about memorizing vocabulary lists and more about empowering students to become autonomous learners, you know? Finding their own tools and strategies. Sounds smart to me. They didn't do that where I went.

Right then, so the bins need taking out on Wednesday, definitely. And I’ve got that dentist appointment in the afternoon, so I’ll need a lift. Wednesday’s fine for the bins, Mum. I'll do it before I head out. What time’s your dentist? Two o'clock. It's that hygienist appointment I’ve been putting off for ages. You know how I am. Hygienist! That’s a posh word, that is. In my day we just called 'em teeth cleaners. Aye, teeth cleaners! That's right, Elsie. Fancy words these days. Well, times change, Dad. Anyway, easy lift, not far. Just down to Dr. Harrison's. No problem. I can drop you off and then grab a coffee before heading back. Oh, lovely. And did you manage to sort that thing with the boiler, love? Still making that awful racket, it is. Yeah, I phoned them yesterday. They said they’ll send someone out Thursday morning. Should be alright. Thursday morning! That’s a long wait for a racket like that. Sounded like a herd of elephants stampeding about in there last night. Aye, a proper din. Woke me right up. It's driving me mad, it really is. They say it’s just the pressure building up, but I don't believe it. They’ll sort it, Mum, don’t worry. Are you needing anything from the shops while I’m out? Milk, bread… Actually, yes, please. Could you get a loaf of that sourdough? The one from the baker's on the High Street? And a pint of milk. And could you pop into that little card shop for a birthday card for Auntie Mary? It's her birthday next week. Sourdough, milk, and a card for Auntie Mary. Got it. Don’t forget a packet of those chocolate digestives. They’re the best, you know. Elsie, you and your chocolate digestives! We’ll get you some, love, don’t you worry. Always have been partial to a good digestive. Anything else while I'm out? I’m heading into town anyway. Hmm, let me think… Oh! Could you check if they've got any of those lavender bath salts at Boots? The ones I like? Alright, lavender bath salts too. Right, I’ll make a list. Just let me scribble it down. You're runnin’ about like a busy bee, aren't you? Well, someone has to keep things running, doesn’t it, Elsie?

Right, so the satnav's being absolutely baffling again. It’s sent us down another lane that’s barely wider than the car! Are you sure it's right, love? I’m starting to think this thing has a personal vendetta against us. According to Google Maps, we’re still on track for the gig, though. Just a slightly… scenic route. Scenic? It’s a track fit only for sheep! Honestly, I swear satnavs get more clever at misleading you. Remember that time it told us to drive into the river in Cornwall? How could I forget? That was a highlight! Though, I think we should be grateful for seemingly random detours. We spotted that kestrel earlier, didn't we? Wouldn't have seen that on the motorway. True, true. A bit of wildlife is always a bonus. Still, I'm desperate for a cup of tea. Are we anywhere near a decent cafe? Not that I’ve noticed, pet. We’re slap-bang in the middle of nowhere. Though, I did see a sign for a farm shop about a mile back. Might be worth a shout after the gig. A farm shop, now you’re talking. Think they’ll have good scones? They probably will. Expect the cream to be thick and the jam to be homemade. It’s Yorkshire, after all - they take their baked goods  very  seriously. I’m looking forward to it. Speaking of things I'm looking forward to, have you finalised the seating plan for your cousin's wedding yet? I’m dreading that. Don’t remind me! It’s a nightmare. Auntie Maureen’s demanding to be next to the buffet table, and Uncle Derek’s convinced he needs to be within earshot of the speeches – even though he’ll probably fall asleep halfway through. Sound about right. You need to be ruthless. Tell them what’s what. Easier said than done when it’s family! But I'm trying to channel my inner wedding planner. Actually, I saw this amazing poem the other day about weddings. It was by… let me think… Don't start reciting poetry now, love. I'm trying to concentrate on not driving into a ditch. Just thinking out loud. It reminded me we really should organise another ceilidh. Haven’t been to one in ages. Oh, that would be lovely! Remember that one in Newcastle? The caller was brilliant, and the music was infectious.

Right, so, massive oat latte for me, please. And a bacon roll. Extra sauce. Sounds good. I'll have a full English and a black coffee, strong. Still buzzing from that site visit, I need the caffeine. Honestly, that Victorian terrace was a nightmare. The client’s brief seems impossible. "Modern elegance, sympathetic to the original architecture, massively bigger kitchen... on a budget." It's not going to happen, is it? It’s ambitious, definitely. But not impossible. We just need to be clever about it. I think the key is focusing on the natural light. Maximise the existing windows, maybe skylights in the kitchen? That could give the illusion of more space. Yeah, but they’re so precious about the original cornicing and mouldings. Every time I suggest anything remotely modern, they recoil in horror. Clients. Right? Remember Sarah's project with the modernist extension on that Georgian manor? She nearly lost her mind. Oh god, yeah. Poor Sarah. How's she doing, by the way? Still struggling with that deadline? Worse, actually. She rang me last night, sounded properly stressed. Apparently, her team is completely demoralised and the lead contractor keeps missing deadlines. That's awful. She needs to tell her manager. She can’t just grind herself into the ground. I know it’s tough when you’re trying to prove yourself, but… I told her the same thing. I just feel bad for her. She's so talented, and this project's just… a disaster. It's so frustrating to see talented people held back by terrible management. Speaking of which, did you read that article about those experimental communal living spaces they're building in Amsterdam? The ones with the modular apartments? Yeah, I saw something about it. Seemed interesting, but a bit sterile from the pictures. I know, right? But the concept – flexible living spaces that can adapt to changing needs – I find it fascinating. It could be a real solution for young professionals in cities like London. It’s a nice idea in principle. But I wonder if people would actually  want  to live in that kind of setup. I mean, who wants to share a kitchen with complete strangers? Well, maybe not  share  completely. But have flexible communal spaces - a shared workshop, a rooftop garden… that kind of thing. It's about fostering a sense of community, isn’t it? True. I guess it depends on the design.

Right, so Earl Grey or Yorkshire for you, love? Kettle’s just boiled. And what about biscuits? Rich tea, digestives, or something a bit more exciting? Yorkshire, definitely. And… digestives, please. Thanks, Mum. This is nice. Just what I needed after that nightmare drive. Nightmare? What happened? The A1 always seems to be causing chaos these days. It was awful. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe it. Some bloke in a lorry decided to merge lanes about five yards in front of me. Completely unexpected. Oh, the cheek of it! People have no spatial awareness, do they? Honestly, it’s a miracle we all get anywhere safely. Exactly! And then, he just slowed down, like nothing happened. I nearly had to brake really hard. Ugh, those types of drivers. They just assume everyone will adjust to  them . You’ve got to be so vigilant. Did you manage to get past him? Eventually, yeah. After about ten minutes of tailgating. It was so stressful. I swear, driving in Lincolnshire sometimes feels like a competitive sport. You're not wrong. Everyone’s in a hurry to get nowhere. So, what about Sarah and Liam? Still going strong? Yeah, they’re really good. Liam's got a new job, actually. At the council. Oh, really? That's brilliant for him. What’s he doing? Something in IT, apparently. He seemed pretty chuffed. We're all going to that new tapas place next Saturday, fancy coming? Oh, I’d love to! That sounds lovely. Been ages since we’ve all had a proper catch-up. Don’t want to impose, though. Don't be silly! It wouldn't be the same without you. You always know the best stories. Well, I've lived a little longer, haven't I? Here you go. So, anything exciting happening at work? Still enjoying it? It's… fine. Mostly paperwork, to be honest. It's not exactly thrilling, but it's steady. Just need to try and stay out of the lorry drivers’ way on the commute! Absolutely. Right, digestives then. And tell me more about this new job Liam’s got... I'm already wishing I had his ability to navigate IT systems. I struggle with the TV remote sometimes! He’s finding it a bit much at times, but yeah… It's good. He likes the people, at least. They're all pretty friendly. So, did you ever get around to re-organising the garage?

Right, so let’s have another look at this draft. Honestly, it’s looking pretty good, but I still think we can sharpen it up a bit, especially for a production role. Aye, it’s good, really. Just needs a bit of… punch, maybe? It’s a bit… polite. Radio production needs a bit of sass, doesn't it? You’re wrangling presenters and sound engineers all day! Exactly. I think you’re right. It reads a little too much like a teaching application, doesn’t it? Less “facilitating language acquisition” and more… “managing creative chaos.” There you go! Nailed it. How about we swap out the bit about 'student-centric learning' for something about collaborating with diverse teams under pressure? Ooh, that's good. Definitely more aligned. What about this paragraph about transferable skills? It feels a bit generic. Everyone claims to have 'excellent communication skills' these days. Yeah, scrap that. Tell them  how  you communicate. Give them an example! You once calmed down a presenter who had a full-blown meltdown over a misplaced microphone, didn’t you? Oh god, yes! The Mike incident. Right, okay. So, something like, “Successfully de-escalated a stressful situation during a live broadcast, demonstrating strong communication and problem-solving skills…” Perfect. See? Concrete, shows them you can handle the heat. And don’t be afraid to brag about the podcast you produced! That's directly relevant. I know, I know. I was worried it seemed a bit… much. I didn’t want to sound like I was just listing things. Nah, you’re selling yourself! This is a job where they  want  enthusiastic people. Highlight your achievements. What was the peak listener count for that podcast? Throw that in! It got up to nearly 3,000 downloads an episode. That’s pretty good for independent, isn’t it? That's brilliant! Put it in! And what about that music editing software you're good with? Mention that too. I’ve added it. I’m a little worried about the interview stage though. I haven't been in a proper interview for ages. It's predominantly been teaching since uni. Don’t you worry your head about that. You’re sharp, you’re capable. Practice the STAR method – Situation, Task, Action, Result. Structure your answers. Right, STAR. I always forget that. It's a game changer, honestly. Think of a few key experiences – maybe that time you had to drastically re-edit a piece to meet a deadline, or when you had to work with a particularly difficult guest.

Right, so let’s actually drill down on this little pottery thing. I mean, it's not going to replace your entrepreneurial success, but it could be a nice little side hustle, wouldn’t it? And something genuinely  you . Exactly. Something I enjoy, not something I'm selling into. More of a, you know, offering workshops, maybe selling pieces online, but really just for the joy of it. The Wellington clay is just incredible, you know? I know, you’ve talked about it forever. So, realistically, if you were to set up a small online shop – Etsy? Shopify? Etsy feels a bit crowded. Shopify gives me more control, I think. I'd need a decent photographer, though. Those pieces need to  look  good. And a good website, obviously. You could learn to take the photos yourself, actually. There are loads of tutorials. And a simple Shopify site isn't massively difficult. I've had a look at a few. The tricky bit is the marketing, isn’t it? Yeah, that’s where I'll need some help. Maybe someone freelance, just to get me started, handle social media, that sort of thing. We could set a budget for that each month? £500? Seems reasonable to begin. We should factor in materials, studio time… are we going to use the shed when we get back, or should we look at a proper studio space? The shed's fine to start. It’s isolated enough, and having everything in one place is convenient. We can upgrade later if it grows. I rather like the idea of having a bigger kiln though… somewhere that isn't in the garden. Okay, so priorities then. Website, photography, marketing support. And maybe looking at kiln options further down the line. What about the actual training? Any pottery courses lined up? I’ve been looking. There's a really good weekend workshop in Margaret River. Pretty stunning scenery, apparently. And the potter teaching is supposed to be brilliant. Could we do that? Maybe in October? October sounds lovely. We're free then, aren’t we? Let's book it. And while we’re at it, can you start sketching out a business plan? Even a rough one. Just to have some targets and expectations. Will do. I was thinking, you know, initially just selling smaller pieces, mugs, bowls, that sort of thing. Then, once I've got more experience, perhaps I could do some commissioned work.

Honestly, the state of schools these days! It’s a disgrace, isn't it, Arthur? A complete disgrace. It is, Margaret. Housing, schools… the whole system seems to be creaking under the strain. Absolutely ludicrous, the shortage in Cambridge. You'd think a university town would have… well,  something  organised. It’s terrifying, isn’t it? I was reading about it. They’re talking about mobile classrooms being the only option for some new developments. Mobile classrooms! When I was a kid… Mobile classrooms… the things we’ve seen in education. Back in my day, we patched things up with enthusiasm and a whole lot of cardboard. But this is… different. This is a systemic failure. Finn, darling, just one bite of your carrots. I heard they’re trying to build on some of the green spaces now. It’s awful. The council’s always been short-sighted, haven’t they? Always chasing the quick win, the easy money. Remember that fiasco with the planning permission around the river? Oh, don’t remind me! It was a battle. A proper battle for the soul of Cambridge. It's just... It feels like the city is changing so quickly. All these new people coming in... Well, there’s been a significant influx, that’s undeniable. The Polish community, for instance, has done wonders for the local economy. Brilliant bakers, those Polish ladies. You ever tried a Polish babka, Margaret? I used to have a Polish student, years ago. Lovely girl. Always brought in plates of pierogi for the class. Delicious. Finn doesn't like anything other than bread. It's a constant battle. I'm trying to get him into vegetables, but it's like pulling teeth. I’ve started ordering HelloFresh, though. It’s a lifesaver when I can’t be bothered cooking. HelloFresh? Is that the one that sends you boxes of chopped ingredients? Yeah, exactly. Honestly, it's made a huge difference to my sanity. And at least he's trying  something  vaguely healthy. He looks like your grandfather, that boy. Same mischievous glint in his eye. Oh don’t say that! He’s been getting into everything lately. Found my old eyeliner yesterday. You know, speaking of appearances… I read an article this morning about the resurgence of the beard. Apparently, it’s all the rage again. Beards? Really? After all these years. Apparently. They say it’s a sign of rugged masculinity.

So, how was the school run this morning? Absolute carnage, I bet. You have no idea! The new parking restrictions they've put in around the school – utter chaos. I swear, people were practically dueling for spaces. Honestly, they need to issue proper car park passes. It’s a nightmare. Tell me about it! They’re always messing with parking. Remember when they tried to put double yellows on the High Street? Nearly bankrupted the little bakery. Oh, yes! Mrs. Higgins nearly had a breakdown. She was reliant on the passing trade. It’s just… inconsiderate. Anyway, the lunchtime supervisor role’s been keeping me busy enough, thankfully. Kids are a handful now, even more than when I was in Sixth Form. Sixth Form… goodness, feels like a lifetime ago. You were brilliant at English Lit, weren’t you? Always analysing everything to death. Probably! I did enjoy a good dissection of a poem. Did you ever go back and reread those texts we studied? Occasionally. Mostly when I'm trying to distract myself from looming deadlines! Marketing and proofreading… it’s all consuming at the moment. But good to be self-employed, you know? Flexible. Absolutely. Though I always said I'd hate the responsibility of being your own boss. Far too stressful. Speaking of stressful, how's your mum doing? Still feeling a bit under the weather? Yeah, she had another bad day on Tuesday. Just can't seem to shake that persistent cough. It's worrying, really. The doctor's keeping an eye on her, but you know… I do. My dad’s been complaining about his knee lately, creaking like an old gate. He's trying to get back into tennis, bless him. Says it’s the only exercise he gets. Good for him! We need to be a bit better at that, don’t we? Trying to squeeze in a walk most days, but it’s hard. The referendum… still can’t believe the outcome. It’s divided families, hasn’t it? It certainly has. Awful, really. I try not to dwell on it too much. Gets you down. Have you heard anything about the village fete this year? They're trying to get a brass band again. I saw a poster for it in the village shop. Sounds lovely. Are you going? Definitely. Little Sarah loves the bouncy castle. And I’m hoping to get some of those homemade jam doughnuts.

So, you’re actually using Twitter for your student support now, huh? That’s quite a shift. Aye, it is. Seems a bit daft at first, doesn’t it? But honestly, it’s been brilliant. Far more efficient than email for quick announcements. Like, a snow day, a change in the library opening hours… boom, out it goes to everyone. Right, that’s smart. I can see the benefit there. Saves you trawling through a whole mailing list. We use Slack a bit at work for internal stuff, but external… nah, never really ventured there. Slack’s good for internal, definitely. But Twitter’s public face is…well it has its advantages. Students are already on it, you know? It's where they are. And they’ve started replying with questions - simple stuff, mostly, but it's engaging them. Engagement is the key, isn't it? We’re constantly battling that at the comms team. Everyone's got short attention spans these days. What sort of tone are you adopting? Don’t want to be one of those overly corporate accounts, do you? Nah, not at all. Kept it pretty informal. Using emojis a bit, you know? Not too much mind you, don't want to look like I'm trying too hard. But it works. Got a wee hashtag going – #StudySmart_Edin – and students are using it when they’ve got a particularly good study tip or found a useful resource. Clever! That’s really clever. Leveraging the student body to create content for you. I should suggest that to the marketing team. Though I suspect they'd have a spreadsheet and a brand style guide for emojis before even considering it. Aye, they probably would. It’s a constant battle to keep things fresh and approachable. I was reading something the other day about authentic voices being vital on social media. Oh, you and me both. We're trying to build a reputation for transparency and genuine engagement. Difficult when every tweet feels like a potential PR disaster waiting to happen. Tell me about it! I nearly had a meltdown last week when a student complained about the coffee in the canteen. I spent half an hour crafting a reply, trying to be empathetic and resolution-focused... And? And another student piped up saying the coffee was brilliant and the best thing about the canteen! Suddenly, I looked like a right eejit trying to apologise for something that wasn't even a problem.

Finally! What a weekend. Seriously, I feel like I ran a marathon made of spreadsheets and small talk. Tell me about it. I feel like I've spent the last 48 hours mediating arguments and offering lukewarm tea. At least  your  small talk probably involved slightly posher canapés. Only marginally. Mostly it was networking events full of people who kept saying things like, “Synergy is key, don’t you think?” I swear, if I hear "synergy" one more time... You should have told them it was a type of chilli. See if they notice. Ooh, that’s brilliant! I should have. Anyway, what did you get up to? Anything less…intense? Relatively. A couple of admissions, a family dispute that required a surprising amount of tissues, the usual. Mrs. Davies insisted on telling me the entire history of her prize-winning begonias for twenty minutes. Oh, bless. Want some dinner? I grabbed a load of stuff from the supermarket – not a gourmet feast, but it’s food. Starving! What did you get? Please tell me it’s not more ‘mystery meat’ scenarios. Nope, no mystery meat tonight. I got that pasta you like, pesto, cherry tomatoes… it’s ridiculously simple but it does the job. Perfect! You are an angel. Seriously, I needed comfort food after dealing with David’s family drama. Apparently, he and his sister are no longer speaking because of a misplaced heirloom teapot. A teapot! That’s a new level of pettiness, even for family squabbles. I know, right? He’s being completely unreasonable, apparently it was  his  grandmother's favourite. I tried to mediate, but he just kept muttering about ‘respect for family history’. Men. Honestly. Has he said anything about seeing you this week? We were thinking of hitting up that new cocktail bar on Friday. He mentioned it, but he’s got a work thing on Thursday. He said maybe Friday or Saturday? The usual vague promises. I’m starting to think I’m just a convenient “maybe” in his life. Don't say that. He's probably just busy. Although… you’re right to be cautious. Remember what happened with Liam? Don't remind me. The guy who promised me the moon and then disappeared to Peru with a yoga instructor? Exactly. Learn from your mistakes! Seriously though, Friday’s still on with me, whether David shows up or not. You deserve a night out.

This risotto's lovely, really. You’ve outdone yourself, Sarah. Thanks, Dad. I tried a new recipe actually. Found it online. Quite fiddly though, I'll admit. Fiddly, you say? Everything seems fiddly these days. Remember when a simple Shepherd's Pie was all we needed? Yes, Mum. Simpler times. But this is much better than a Shepherd’s Pie, don't you think? Agreed. Though a bit of a pie wouldn’t go amiss some time. So, has Emma called about Uncle David’s visit? Yes, I spoke to her earlier. He's confirmed he’ll be here on Saturday. She's booked him a taxi from the station, and she's arranging for someone to help him with his meals, as you know. That's good, good. He needs support. Poor man. He doesn’t always… well, you know. It’s tough, isn’t it? Hearing things… or thinking you hear things... He needs to be kept busy. Something to occupy his mind. David always enjoyed that little puzzle book we bought him. I’ll bring it down from Wellington then. Should be there somewhere. Did you tell him about your new car, Anon? Not yet. Save it for dessert, perhaps? Ooh, dramatic reveal! What is it? Something sporty? Sporty? No. Something sensible. And economical. A hybrid. The EV9. Blue. Oh, a sensible blue! Very you, dear. The EV9, is it? Fancy name. It is, isn't it? Always loved Kia, used to have a Sorento. This is much better on fuel. Took it out for a spin this morning. Lovely. Sensible  and  lovely. That’s the best combination. You've been driving a twenty-year-old Ford Fiesta for years! I have! It did me proud. But it was time. Speaking of cars, do you think David will want to go for a drive while he's here? Even a short one? Possibly. We’ll have to see how he is. It might be too much for him. Emma said he's been struggling with the anxiety again. We'll take it easy. Just gentle conversation, good food, and keep him company. Exactly. No pressure. And I’ll make sure I bring some of those biscuits he likes. The ones with the currants. Perfect. Mum, you’re a lifesaver. And Sarah, this risotto is truly superb. You should consider opening a restaurant! Don't be silly, Dad! I'm perfectly happy teaching.

Honestly, love, it's just baffling, isn’t it? This Spanish. I've been at it for six months now and I still feel like I'm banging my head against a brick wall. I know, I know. It’s a proper challenge. More so than I anticipated, to be fair. I thought with my memory, I'd pick it up quicker. Memory’s not the problem, is it? It’s the genders of the words! Why is a table masculine and a chair feminine? Makes no sense, does it? Well, it doesn’t to us, does it? But that's just how the language evolved. You just have to learn it. That's what the app keeps telling me. The app! Don't even get me started on that. Duolingo. Chiming at me every five minutes. "Practice your Spanish!" I swear, I'm going to throw the phone out of the window. It’s a bit relentless, isn’t it? I tried that once. Nearly drove me mad. Remember that Pimsleur method my cousin recommended? Oh, yeah! The one where you just listen and repeat? I did that for a couple of weeks. Found it terribly dull, to be honest. Felt like I was hypnotised half the time. No engagement, you know? Fair enough. I gave that one a whirl too - too repetitive. I think I prefer the more immersive methods. Like that Learn Spanish with Stories one. Aye, I've heard good things about those. But I'm terrible at following storylines when I’m simultaneously trying to decode every single word. My brain can only handle so much at once! See, you’re putting too much pressure on yourself. Just try to absorb the sounds, the rhythm of the language. Don’t worry about understanding everything straight away. Easier said than done, love! Especially when you're trying to order a coffee and they just look at you like you’re speaking Martian. Well, you are, a little bit! But seriously, it’s the exposure, isn't it? You need to immerse yourself. Have you looked into those language exchange programs? I have, but the thought of speaking to a complete stranger in a language I barely know fills me with dread. What if I completely butcher everything? You’ll be alright. Everyone makes mistakes. That’s how you learn. Think about Catalonia, for example. People fluent in both Catalan and Castillian.

Right, so I reckon this is all the banking stuff then? Statements, bills… a proper mountain. Aye, it's built up, hasn't it? You’ve been having a right clear-out down here. Found a fair few things you'd forgotten about, I reckon. Definitely. Luckily, a lot of it is relatively recent, so I’ve been able to scan it and shred the paper. Saves space, you know? Smart lad, you are. Saves me lugging boxes of this lot about, too. Speaking of which, where’s that scanner? I’ve got a few documents I need to get onto the computer. It’s on the desk over there, the one I borrowed from the uni. It's pretty quick once you get going. Be careful with the settings though, it can be a bit fiddly. You want high resolution for the important stuff. Right, high resolution. Good tip. You know, I was reading about corpus linguistics the other day. Oh yeah? Where did you hear about that? In a magazine about language, can you believe it? All about how they analyse huge amounts of text to see how people actually use words. Fascinating stuff, really. It  is  fascinating. That’s essentially what I do, albeit on a slightly smaller scale. Using databases to track language trends. Helps with the teaching. Blimey. You English Language Instructors learn a lot, don’t you? More than I ever did at school. It does require a bit of digging. Anyway, found a folder full of flight confirmations. Remember that trip to Alicante? Oh, aye! Lovely holiday that was. Kelly Brook was on the flight. Right across the aisle from us. You and your celebrity spotting! I was more interested in the sangria, to be honest. So, scanning these, then… what needs to go where? Best put the flights and holiday receipts into their own folder. Makes it easier to find them later on. I've got some old insurance documents here too. Think it’s time to sort those out properly. Good shout. Speaking of sorting things out, I’m thinking of ordering in some proper shredders. The one I've got now is a bit pathetic. A good investment. Keeps your identity safe. Now, this is a treasurer document to scan. Actually, I'm starving. Fancy we get some of that lasagna you made the other day? Oh man, that was good.

Right, so, like, I’m absolutely gutted we’re stopping at this one. Why? What’s wrong with it? Seems fine. It’s just… the petrol’s always a couple of pence more here than at the Shell down the road. And you know they always try and upsell ya. "Would you like a windscreen wash, love?" Like I haven't already checked it! They’re just doing their job. Aye, but I’m doing mine, which is to save a few quid where I can, especially with the price of petrol these days! It’s scandalous, isn’t it? It is, yeah. Though I did fill up a bit last night. Thought I’d beat the rush. Didn't work. Did it not? Loads of cars queuing even then. Reckon it's all the bikers going up to the Lake District. Possibly. There were quite a few bikes around this morning. All rumbling along. Love bikers, though. Proper freedom, innit? Not stuck in a boring hatchback like us. Not everyone finds hatchbacks boring. They're practical. Aye, practical. I’ll give you that. Though practically boring, maybe. Fancy a sports car for a bit, though? A little red number? I'm thinking more of an electric SUV, to be honest. Less noise, better for the environment… and still practical. Oh, you and your ethics! I just want to hear an engine roar. Well, we’re not going to be stopping for a roar anytime soon. Just need to fill up and let's get going, yeah? Fine, fine. But I'm keeping a close eye on the price display. And I’m definitely  not  getting windscreen wash. Deal. You driving? Nah, you take over. My arm's a bit tired after wrestling with that shopping bag. Right you are. Just gotta make sure I remember to turn the heating down. You were practically boiling in there before. It was a bit chilly, I'll admit. And definitely didn't need the fan on full blast. Honestly, sometimes I think you're trying to freeze me. Never! Just trying to regulate the temperature. You're a human furnace. I am not! Just properly warm. Get on with it, then, will you. Let's go. Do you think we'll see any more bikers today? It's been interesting watching them. You can tell they love it. Probably. Weekends are always busy for them.

Right, so the coach said you were getting a bit sloppy with your backhand today. Just rushing it a bit. Yeah, I know. It felt weird. Were you thinking too much about where you wanted it to go, rather than just letting it flow? Maybe. I was trying to hit a winner every time, I think. That's what they said. Trying to force it. Remember what we talked about? Consistency over flashy shots. I know, Mum. I just… I want to beat Liam next week. Liam’s good, no question. But you don’t need to play hero tennis to beat him. Solid groundstrokes, get him moving. Use your head. Exactly. And focus on that footwork. He was saying you weren’t getting in position quick enough. It was hot! It was like, roasting out there. It was a bit warm, but everyone was feeling it. Still, you can’t let the weather excuse sloppy technique. Now, do you want me to chuck some more peppers in this stir-fry? Yeah, please. Loads of peppers. You’re getting quite good at serving, you know. Remember when you used to slice it into the net every time? Ugh, don't remind me. It was brutal! You looked like you were trying to hit a fly. I was! Literally. Trying to be all clever, and it didn't work. Well, you've come a long way. You’re hitting with decent pace now, and your placement is improving. Have you been practicing the topspin serve? Yeah, a bit. It's hard to get the angle right. It takes practice. And watch videos of Federer. His serve is a masterclass. How he generates power and spin… it’s incredible. Federer or Djokovic. Both phenomenal servers. You could learn a lot from both. Have you seen much of the matches recently? I watched a bit of Wimbledon last year. It was good. Mostly I watch YouTube highlights, though. Saves time. YouTube's great, but watching the full matches helps you understand the strategy, the patterns. It's not just about hitting the ball, it's about outsmarting your opponent. Okay, okay, I get it. Less YouTube, more actual matches. Exactly. And don't get discouraged if you have a bad session. Everyone does. It’s how you bounce back that matters. You've got the potential, just need to keep working at it. Are the noodles nearly ready?

This is good, Nan. Really good. Better than last year. Glad you think so, love. I did put a bit more sage in this year. Your dad kept saying it needed more sage. He does, doesn’t he? Always wanting more sage. And look at these napkins! Honestly, they look like tiny underpants! They do! They’re a bit much, aren’t they? I mean, Christmas is festive enough without underwear-shaped napkins. They’re fun, though. Lighten the mood a bit. It’s Christmas day, after all. So, are we doing the wishbone this year? Of course, we are! You always win, though. It’s ridiculous. Just lucky, I reckon. I’m still trying to figure out what my uni friends are going to do for Christmas. Liam’s going to spend Christmas Eve in a fancy ski lodge, apparently. He’s calling it a ‘Pre-Festive Detox’. A detox? On Christmas Eve! He’s mad. Young people, eh? Always doing things differently. Last year, Sarah and her fella ended up playing charades dressed as reindeer. That's brilliant! I wish I was there for that. Speaking of brilliant, remember when you went to Florida, love? You said the airport was crazy. Don’t remind me! The queues! And the sheer number of people. Honestly, it was like being herded. The security was a nightmare too. I’m not sure I’m ready for another transatlantic flight anytime soon. You have to go again, though. You loved it. And your nickname there was 'Sunshine,' wasn't it? Your friends thought it suited you. Yeah, they did. It was… nice. It's just… I hope they treat people better than some of the staff did at the airport. It seemed like a lot of people were getting unfairly hassled. It's the world, isn't it? Can't always be right. Have to just remember to be kind to each other, especially around Christmas. That’s right, love. That's exactly it. It’s a time for kindness. And forgiving. I'm putting on Downton Abbey afterwards. Everyone wants to watch it. Yes! I love Downton Abbey. The soundtrack is amazing. And the dancing! I always try to copy the dances, but I’m not very good. You're a better dancer than you think, actually. Liam’s always joking about your ‘dad moves’ but you liven up the party. Dad moves, eh?

This roast potatoes are brilliant, Mum! Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, you’re sweet, love. Just a bit of extra rosemary this year, I think. It makes all the difference. Did you manage to get away from work this afternoon? I know you were saying it was a bit hectic. Yeah, managed to wriggle out of most things. Sarah was covering for me on that presentation, so that was a relief. Actually, speaking of Sarah, she's being a right drama queen over Mark again. Mark, eh? Still going strong, is he? Thought they were on the rocks a few months back. That’s what everyone thought! But now apparently he’s forgotten her birthday,  again . The level of angst is astonishing. She's ranting on WhatsApp to everyone. Oh, dear. Poor girl. Men, eh? Can't remember a thing. Your dad, bless him, used to forget what day it was sometimes. Your mother used to have to write it on his hand! Nearly every Sunday. Sounds familiar! Anyway, she's threatening to call off the wedding. Again. I’m trying to tell her to breathe, but it’s like talking to a brick wall. Well, you know Sarah. She needs to sort herself out. Sometimes you’ve just got to let people make their own mistakes and learn from them. She'll come round. She always does. Women are a bit like that, aren’t they? Got to have a good cry and a moan. That’s what I keep saying! But she’s got everyone else feeding into it. Now Emily’s convinced he’s lying about the whole thing. Emily’s always been a bit of a stirrer, hasn’t she? Remember that fiasco with David and Lisa at the summer fete? Oh god, don’t remind me. The whole village was gossiping for weeks. Lisa was mortified. Poor woman. Still, David learned his lesson. Didn't he? Didn't he, Margaret? He did, yes. Though he claimed it was all a misunderstanding. Bless him. Anyway, how's the farm doing, Dad? Harvest been good? Aye, not bad at all. Bit of a scare with the blight on the potatoes, but managed to salvage most of them. Prices are still a nightmare though. Can’t make a decent living these days without government subsidies. Tell me about it. Everything’s expensive. Have you looked at the price of electricity lately?

Right, so I’m thinking pizzas tonight. Easy supper. Do you fancy a Margherita or something with a bit more going on? Something with a bit more going on, definitely. Remember that Black Olive and Chorizo one we had from Marks and Spencer last week? That was amazing. Oh yes! They've really upped their game haven't they? Their food section is just brilliant now. I was in there earlier, just browsing. Honestly, makes you want to chuck out your freezer full of ready meals. Absolutely. I saw their new range of Mediterranean antipasti plates. Tempted to grab one for later. We should. Right, pizza base is proving a bit… stubborn. Need to get the blender out to smooth it a bit more. Or should I just roll it out properly? Roll it. Blenders always make a right mess, don’t they? I had a disaster with the smoothie last week. Cat, of course, was straight on it. Oh, she’s always interested in anything remotely edible. Speaking of, has she been bothering you this afternoon? Not too bad. Just the usual persistent meowing routine. I’m trying to ignore her. Actually, I’m a bit stressed already about tomorrow. Oh? Your appraisal? How are you feeling about that? Honestly, not great. I think the new manager’s a bit… prickly. Doesn't seem to appreciate anyone’s effort. Just nit-picking and rearranging things for the sake of it. That's awful. You've always been a hard worker. Don’t let him get you down. Just focus on what you’ve achieved. Remember that project you spearheaded last year? Yeah, but he barely acknowledged it. Just kept going on about the quarterly report being delayed by fifteen minutes. Fifteen minutes? Honestly, some people. Right, base is looking a bit better now. What about toppings? Pepperoni? Mushrooms? Mushrooms would be good. And some red onion. I'm trying to pretend I’m being healthy. Speaking of healthy, I saw something about the appalling conditions some racehorses are kept in. Makes you sick. It does. It’s so easy to forget how much suffering goes on behind the scenes. It's just awful. Hey, did you manage to finish that crossword? Nearly! Got stuck on that clue about the Icelandic detective programme. What  is  it called? Not ‘Trapped,’ is it? No, ‘Trapped’ is the Welsh one, isn’t it? ‘Trapped’ is excellent though, by the way.

Right, so, who's actually  wearing  something decent tonight then? Because I'm feeling a bit rubbish about my outfit. Don't be daft, Rach. You always look good. What's wrong with it? It's just…plain. Black jeans, black top. It's like, every other night out. Need a bit of sparkle, don't I? I reckon you look fine! I'm rocking my flares and this sparkly top from New Look. Bit tacky, but hey, it’s a Tuesday. Tacky is good, Beth! Embrace the tack! I'm going for a more… subtle vibe. Black dress, but with a little side split. Scandalous, I know. Oh, you're all looking good. I'm in my new skirt – the one from Depop. Took ages to find one that fit right. Depop? You’re brave, Maisie! I’m always scared of buying clothing online. It's alright, you just have to check the seller's reviews. This one's really good. It’s proper vintage too. Okay, you've convinced me. Need to have a mooch about Depop. I'm desperate for a new pair of heels too. Anyone see anything good lately? H&M had some killer platforms last week - barely wore them. They’re comfy, surprisingly. I hit up Schuh yesterday and saw some really cute block heels. Like, a proper 90s vibe. I’m thinking of getting them. Ooh, block heels are back? Wicked! I’m all about a good block heel for dancing. Easier on the ankles, you know? My feet thank me later. Are we all getting ready at yours, Chloe? Yep! Got a bottle of Prosecco chilling already. Need to get a massive bowl of nachos sorted. Churros would be amazing too! Oh my god, YES! Let's get churros! We  are  planning on actually going  out  or are we just gonna stay here and eat and drink? We're going out! Eventually... after Prosecco and churros, obviously. It's a Tuesday, we deserve a treat. What's the plan though? The Reflex? Reflex is always reliable. Gets busy, but it’s always a laugh. Let's hit up that new cocktail bar first, the one down near the station? We haven’t tried it yet. Sounds good. Fancy a pre-drinks before we hit Reflex? Then we can properly make a show of ourselves. Absolutely. Just need to find some actual sparkle for my outfit first… right, Depop, here I come!

This coffee's really good, actually. Much better than that instant stuff I made yesterday. It is. I think I finally cracked the recipe for a decent pour-over. Needed more bloom time, apparently. Bloom time? Seriously? You're getting  really  into this coffee thing. Well, gotta have a hobby, right? Less stressful than troubleshooting network outages. Speaking of which… Did you see that article about the rise in AI predicting personality traits from social media? Oh, the one that said you’re apparently 87% introverted? Exactly! Eighty-seven percent! They've clearly never seen me organising a work conference. True, you do shine when you're bossing people around. It’s your spiritual journey, isn’t it? Feeling in control. Don’t be cheeky! It's about efficiency, darling. But seriously, it got me thinking about soulmates. Do you ever wonder if there's some algorithm that could find our perfect match, beyond just shared interests? Probably a formula for optimal division of labor and argument avoidance. Not terribly romantic. But you know, I read something interesting the other day. A historian arguing that the Victorian era was essentially one long, protracted imaginary party. A party? Yes! Think about it – all those elaborate social rituals, the obsession with appearances, the endless balls and galas… They were constructing an entire reality, a performance. That’s… remarkably pessimistic. Maybe, or maybe it's a rather elegant explanation for why they were so obsessed with propriety. It’s a comforting thought, actually - that all these tedious social obligations are a legacy of some vast, historical charade. Imagine if we threw a proper Victorian-style party now. Oh,  please  don't. The sheer effort involved in corsets and top hats... No, thank you. Besides, people would just be on their phones. That's the irony, isn't it? We'd have all the outward trappings of Victorian grandeur, but everyone would be secretly scrolling Instagram. Utter chaos. Although… no, you’re right, it  would  be quite something. We could have a strict no-phones policy. Guests would have to write their impressions of the evening in quill and ink. Now  that  I'd pay to see. Though frankly, I'm more worried about the shepherds pie. Did I remember to defrost it? I think so. I put it in the fridge last night, didn’t I? Sorry, I meant to remind you. Didn’t want you slaving over a hot stove all day.

This coffee is lovely, isn't it? You’ve really nailed the oat milk this time, Sarah. Thanks, Fiona! It’s all about finding the right brand, isn't it? Took me ages to figure it out. So, you were telling me you’re finally considering selling your little knitting business? I am, yes. It’s… massively overwhelming. I love the knitting, absolutely adore it, but the business side is just relentless. All the admin and marketing and… oh, the form-filling. It’s a nightmare. Tell me about it! Head of Admin and HR, darling, it’s all forms, all the time. You’re brave trying to run a business on top of everything. Is Mark helping? He’s trying, bless him. He’s brilliant at the practical stuff, setting up the website and stuff like that, but the finances... he just gets glazed eyes. He’s far better at engineering. He always was! Remember when he tried to ‘help’ you sort out the stocktake one Christmas and nearly had a breakdown? Oh god, don't remind me! I spent the next two days calming him down and re-doing the whole thing. He said it was like advanced algebra. Men and numbers, eh? They're a special breed. Anyway, what's stopping you selling? Is it just the workload? Part of it. And the thought of someone else selling my creations, you know? They’re so personal. But honestly, the level of online hate I've started getting... it's ridiculous. Someone left a scathing review saying my scarves were “cultural appropriation” because I used a cable stitch traditionally found in Ireland! Oh my god, seriously? People are insane! Absolutely. It's galling though, isn't it? Like, can’t people just enjoy something without trying to find something to complain about? I had a woman complain to me last week that the font on our HR policy was “too aggressive.” It's mad. I'm seriously considering just shutting it all down completely. No, don’t! Your knitting is gorgeous. You need to focus on the people who appreciate it. Maybe scale back the online shop, sell at craft fairs instead? Definitely. That way you control the environment. Plus, you'll get that lovely direct interaction with customers. They can appreciate the craftsmanship. That's a thought. I did a market in Stamford last year, and it was lovely.

Speaker_1 : Right, so, listen to this, yeah? Liam proper bottled it at the union last night. Speaker_2 : Bottled it? What happened? Did he actually try and do the karaoke? Anyone up for exploring the city? I found this little vintage shop the other day, apparently.

This bread is unreal, isn’t it? Like, seriously good. Yeah, it's boss. This Bolognese is proper good too. Better than Mum's. Don’t you say that! You'll be in the doghouse. It’s just…different. A Croatian Bolognese is a bit richer, I think. It’s decent. Though I’m missing a decent Pret sandwich, to be honest. Proper bread, you know? Not this…rustic stuff. Dad, always the Pret man, aren’t you? Honestly, he’d be lost without his Pret. Remember that time in Paris, he nearly had a meltdown because they didn’t have a tuna and cucumber sandwich? It was a cultural emergency! It was a horrifying morning without caffeine and a tuna and cucumber. Anyway, I've got this history essay due on Monday. It’s about the Romans and, like, all they built. Super boring. Ugh, history. I’m so glad I chose English Lit. At least Shakespeare’s a bit more interesting. How’s uni going, Liam? It's alright. The buses are a nightmare though. Always late. I nearly missed a lecture last week thanks to the number 1. They haven't improved at all, have they? Still the same shambles as when I was your age. Speaking of which, are you still thinking about that tattoo, Liam? The one on your arm? Yeah, probably. It'll be a little wolf howling at the moon. A wolf? Seriously? That’s a bit…dark, isn’t it? It's cool, though. All my mates have got tattoos. Look, Liam, I understand you want to express yourself, but think about it carefully. Tattoos are permanent. Your dad’s right, love. It’s a big decision. And think about your future job, you never know. She's right. Just don’t get anything on your face, yeah? That’s my only rule. Yeah, yeah, I know. Your Nan keeps posting about that awful cat on Facebook. Did you see? Knitting a little jumper for it. Oh, bless her. She’s obsessed! I don’t think she’s actually remembered who’s in the photo half the time. You’ve got to understand, your Nan’s in her eighties. Facebook is her window to the world. She’s communicating! Rest of the family wants to go to that park this afternoon? Yes, it’s a lovely park. And they have a little moped track that you youngsters can use.

Right then, settle in, settle in. Cup of tea anyone? I’ve made a fresh pot. Cornwall was lovely, wasn’t it? Bit blowy, mind you - bracing! It really was lovely, Arthur. Absolutely smashing. Though my knees are aching something fierce from all that walking. The coastal path, you know. Aye, it was alright. A bit… exposed, maybe. Bit much wind for me. Glad to be back on solid ground, so I am. This tea smells good, though, Betty. Aye, well, we did get some proper storms going on. But that lighthouse at Land’s End… magnificent. I’ve never seen anything like it. Standing there, watching the waves crash… made you feel very small, didn't it? It did. And the little village we stayed in – Port Isaac? Absolutely charming. All those little winding streets and the fishing boats. Reminded me of Mousehole. Port Isaac? That’s where they film Doc Martin, innit? That's the one. Didn’t manage to spot Martin Clunes, though. Bit disappointed about that, actually. We didn’t either. Though I did manage to get some lovely photos. Look, here’s one of the lighthouse. Proper dramatic sky behind it. Nice one. You’ve caught it well, Doris. Speaks volumes that even with that wind it was a proper view. Did you manage to see any crabs? Crabs? Oh yes! Down on the beach at Porthcurno. Loads of ‘em scuttling about. Little blighters. I didn't, I just kept a look out for puddles and tried not to trip - knees, you know. Anything exciting happening at school, Mark? Been a while since we’ve had a proper chat. Aye, things are ticking over. Year sevens are being a handful, as per usual. We're doing a project on coastal erosion - a bit ironic, really, given where we’ve just been! And there's this one boy, Liam... a bit of a handful but loads of potential. Reminds me of myself at school. Always getting into scrapes. Oh, Arthur! Don’t start! Speaking of potential, did you hear about that cycle race they're doing? The 'Yorkshire in a Day' thing? Apparently it's supposed to be brutal. Brutal is right! Blimey. Anyone brave enough to do that? No. No, thank you very much. I'll stick to gentle walks, I think. How was the YHA, Arthur? Are they still needing volunteers down there? They were chuffed to see us, actually.

This bread is boss, isn't it? Proper good. Yeah, it's alright. Your Nan makes a fantastic sourdough, though. Remember that time she tried to teach me? Oh god, yes! Still moaning about you going out with your workmates? Don't even. Seriously, he's like a teenager. Says I'm "leading him on" by having friends. Blimey. That's mental. Is it though? My cousin Sarah's fella got like that. Started saying she needed to “prioritise”  him . She ended up dumping him. Exactly! Like, I love spending time with him, but I’m not about to give up my entire social life. I practically live at work some weeks. He needs to chill out, properly. There’s a difference between wanting to spend quality time together and trying to control someone. I know! But explaining that to him is like talking to a brick wall. He just purses his lips and says, “I just miss you.” The classic guilt trip. Honestly, some lads... I told him last night, I said, “I need my own space, Ben. It's not a massive ask.” He went silent and just stared at his soup for like five minutes. Awful. Did he say anything then? Just mumbled something about being tired. Then he went to bed. Classic avoidant behaviour. You need to have a proper sit down with him. Lay it all out. No more hinting, no more vague complaints. Just straight up tell him what you need. Easy for  you  to say, Miss Independent Conference Coordinator. You're practically running the world. Don’t get me wrong, it's stressful, but I have boundaries. And I'm not afraid to use them. You need to do the same. Yeah, seriously. Don't let him walk all over you. You're right, you're right. It’s just… I like him, you know? I don’t want it all to go tits up. I get it. But you deserve someone who supports your happiness, not someone who tries to dim your sparkle.

Oh my god, you're back! Barcelona looked incredible in your Insta stories. Seriously, I’m so jealous. How was it? It was amazing! Honestly, even better than I anticipated. Fancy a quick takeaway? I was thinking Thai. Ooh yes please! That sounds brilliant. I’m starving. What about next weekend? Are we thinking Paris still? Definitely still on for Paris! It’s so ridiculous but I can't stop watching. Have you finished it yet? Almost. Just a couple of episodes to go. Listen, I was thinking – Liam texted me asking if I was free on Friday night. He wants to try that new Italian place downtown. Oh? And...? And I said yes! Thought you might want to join us? It would be nice to have a proper catch-up. That would be lovely! Let me just check with Dad first - he said he might be heading to a rugby match.

This coffee's surprisingly good, isn’t it? Didn’t expect much from a place right on the seafront. It is rather good, yes. Much better than the hotel’s, that's for sure. Insisted we all had to talk in Received Pronunciation, even when answering the phone. Right, proper posh. That sounds wild. I once worked as a games tester for a computer company. I can imagine! It's the attention to detail that gets you, isn’t it? That’s why I find marking essays so tedious. Spotting the perfectly placed comma error that reveals the student hasn't actually read the text... Exactly! So, you ever thought about moving away from teaching? Somewhere like this, perhaps? North Cyprus is lovely. Tempting, very tempting. But who would I teach? There aren't exactly hordes of eager students clamoring for Shakespeare lessons here. Though… maybe a creative writing class. A bit of a change. You should do it!

Honestly, I'm starting to think living with three other people was a mistake. Really? You’re saying that now? Everything was fine last week when we were ordering pizza and moaning about coursework. Thanks. Just needed to vent, really. It's just… stressful. Tell me about it. Living with anyone is stressful sometimes. But at least you've got a good story to tell. Right then, that’s the lot in. Bit of a carry, wasn’t it? My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. You were moaning about your knees before we even left the house, Arthur! I'm going to have a little rest first.

Nan’s got a big mug of tea, hasn’t she, Mum? Looks like she’s gonna sink in it. Aye, lad, I do like a good brew. Keeps me warm, dosn't it? This room's a bit chilly, innit? It is a bit draughty, Gran. Needed me concentration, I did. World was changing too fast, needed to keep up. What were you reading about then, Grandad? Something exciting? Oh, nothing exciting. Just the price of parsnips. Always going up, they are. Used to be able to get a sack of ‘em for tuppence. Tuppence! That’s unbelievable. Things were so different then. Aye, they were. Now you can't even buy a sweet for that. Speaking of sweets, Mum, are you going to do some baking? Nan loves your lemon drizzle cake. I was thinking about it. I've got some lemons, but I'm low on sugar. I might need to pop to the shops later. Oh, do get some jam too, love. I'm running short. Good for a slice of toast with me tea. Toast? Waste of bread, that is. Should be eating proper food. Oh, here we go. Are you saying you're eating proper food, then? Those biscuits you had earlier didn't look very "proper" to me. They were digestives. Healthy and wholesome. Not like that sugary rubbish you kids eat these days. Alright, Grandad. We get it. You're the healthiest of us all. You’re going to the shops later? Could you get me a packet of those shortbread fingers from Sainsbury’s? The ones with the chocolate on top. Of course, Gran. Anything else? Just make sure you don’t fall for any of those fancy new fangled sweets. Stick to the classics, lass. A proper bag of humbugs is all you need. You and your humbugs, Nan! Humbugs are good. Reliable. Unlike everything else these days. I’ll get the heating turned up a bit higher then.

Right, so anyone else try that new supplement, Peak Performance? Saw it advertised everywhere. Promised you’d be benching your own weight within a week. Yeah, saw that. Felt like I was being targeted, honestly. All my Instagram ads are suddenly about muscle gain and protein shakes. Bit much, innit? Nah, I tried it. Honestly, tasted like chalk mixed with pineapple. Didn’t feel a thing. Waste of money. Typical. Marketing hype. You’d be better off just, like, lifting weights properly. And eating. I’m with Finn on this one. Peak Performance? Sounds like something you'd find in a garden centre. I know! But I was tempted. Been feeling a bit sluggish lately, you know? Uni's been intense. Thought maybe a little boost… I get it. I've been thinking about getting a new smartwatch too. One of those that tracks everything – sleep, heart rate, steps… proper obsessive stuff. I’ve got one. Pretty cool, actually. Though I’m starting to get anxious about beating my step count every day. It’s ridiculous. Fitness is one thing, but you guys are taking it to the extreme. Remember when we were kids and just ran around the park and were happy? No tracking, no targets. True. Simpler times. Speaking of which, did you see Aunt Carol’s Facebook post? The one with her and that cat she rescued? Oh god, yeah. It was like a professional photoshoot. The cat looked incredibly unimpressed. She’s got that filter on, hasn’t she? Makes everything look… plastic. She does, doesn’t she? You can tell it’s a filter. Like, her eyes are glowing. Honestly, she's convinced she's a social media influencer now. It's hilarious. How's your Nan doing, by the way? Haven’t heard anything. She's alright. A bit confused about TikTok, as always. Keeps sending me videos of squirrels. Classic Nan. She's got to find something to entertain herself, I guess. Remember when she tried to start a YouTube channel? The quality was… something else. Oh yeah! All shaky and blurry. And she kept accidentally turning the camera on herself. And she was wearing that floral dressing gown the entire time. Good times. So, are we expecting a long wait for this appointment, then? Anyone fancy a quick browse online? I’m dying to see what’s new in the student clothing sales.

Right, so we need milk, definitely. And bread. And eggs. Oh, and tomatoes for the pasta. Dad, are you getting anything from the shop tomorrow? I might, yeah. Depends how busy I am with that Johnson account. What exactly are you lot needing? Just the basics, love. We're running low on everything, aren't we? And some washing-up liquid. That's essential! Can we get those curly crisps? The ones in the blue bag? You only ever want crisps, don’t you, Liam? Okay, write them on the list then. Blue bag crisps. Honestly, the amount of insects we’ve had this week…Have you seen that big spider in the bathroom, Sarah? Gave me a right fright! Oh, God, yeah! Massive. I sprayed it, thankfully. Did you find any more, Mum? Not yet, but I reckon there's more lurking. That’s why I’m thinking of getting one of those electric fly swatters. Honestly, love. They're a bit gimmicky, aren’t they? A bit of insect repellent spray does the trick. Though even that doesn’t seem to be working this year. They’re probably coming ‘cause it’s warmer, innit? Probably, yeah. Liam, stop poking your brother! Anyway, speaking of bites, I got bitten by a midge last night. It’s itching like mad. Ooh, wretched things. I've got some cream in the cupboard somewhere that might help. An antihistamine cream. Sarah, have a look if you can find it. Cheers, Mum. Right, let’s finish this list. Anything else? What’s on the telly tomorrow? Manchester United are playing! Spurs, I think. Really? Is that on a Saturday? Yeah, it is. I'll have to remind you, Dad. Oh, I hope they win! I’m putting a little wager on them actually. You and your football betting, Margaret. You'll bankrupt yourself one day. Never! Gets me out of the house for a while, cheering them on. Keeps me young, it does. Now, is there anything else to add to that shopping list? Anything you've forgotten? Hmmm…let me think... Oh! We need some fresh herbs. Basil for the pasta? Can we get those chocolate cookies, too? The ones with the caramel in? Liam! You’re relentless. Fine. Chocolate cookies, added to the list. Okay, I think that’s pretty much it. Who’s doing the actual shopping then? I can do it.

Ugh, P.E. was brutal today. Mr. Davies made us do suicides for, like, forever. Seriously? He’s been doing that a  lot  lately. I swear he's trying to kill us. I know, right? And then I tripped over my own feet during the basketball drill. Everyone was laughing. Don’t worry about it, happened to the best of us. Did you see Chloe’s Instagram story? She was doing parkour! No! Seriously? Where? Let me see… Wow! She’s actually really good. I wish I had her coordination. I know! And she’s got, like, loads of followers now. Everyone’s obsessed. It’s kind of annoying, isn't it? It’s like, she's trying too hard. Maybe. But she's doing cool stuff, I guess. Did you see that science experiment Mr. Henderson did? Oh my god, the baking soda volcano exploded  everywhere . It got in Emily's hair! No way! That’s hilarious! She looked like a yeti. It was so funny but she was proper annoyed. She went straight to the office. Poor Emily. Henderson does that on purpose, doesn’t he? To get a reaction. Totally! He's weird. And Miss Davies is being so extra about the coursework deadlines. Like, posting reminders every five minutes. Ugh, tell me about it. I'm still stuck on the history essay. I can't find any good sources. What’s your topic again? It’s about the impact of the Industrial Revolution on Cambridge. So boring. Maybe you could focus on the canal building? That’s pretty interesting. Good idea, thanks. I'll have a look. Have you been watching that new Youtuber, “StudyWithLiam”? Yeah! He’s actually really helpful for revising. Especially his videos on quadratic equations. Right? I used to get so confused by those, but his explanations make sense. Definitely better than trying to understand Mr. Jones. He just drones on and on. Seriously, you need subtitles to understand him. Hey, did you hear about what happened to Olivia and Jamie? No! What? Apparently they were caught sneaking out of the library after curfew last night. No way! Detention, right? Do you think they'll get suspended? I heard Mrs. Peterson was pretty angry. It depends on how she feels when she finds out the whole story. Let’s hope not! It's going to be a long week. Absolutely. Right, I'm going to upload a TikTok of that volcano explosion.

Honestly, I feel like I've been run over by a bus. This cold is absolutely brutal. Yeah, you sound rough. It's a proper one, isn’t it? Worse than last month’s dodgy curry. Definitely worse than the curry! That was just a fleeting moment of gastro distress. This is… persistent. I’m still convinced I’ve got something lurking deeper. A properly nasty virus, maybe. Are you thinking hospital? It's probably just a cold. You get these ones that cling on forever. Remember that awful flu I had a couple of years ago? I was convinced I was dying. That was terrifying! You were like a zombie. But no, not hospital yet. Though, I am wondering about getting the flu jab this year. I usually skip it, but… Smart move. Especially with what you do. Constant travel, being around loads of people… it’s like you’re baiting the germs. Exactly! I just wish I'd had it earlier. I've been cancelling things left and right. I even had to postpone that meeting with Professor Davies. Oh, that’s a shame. He was looking forward to hearing your findings. Did you let him know you were ill? Yeah, sent him a very apologetic email. Made it sound like I was on my deathbed. I think he bought it. I’m half tempted to send over a photo of me looking completely miserable with a box of tissues. Tempting, but probably overkill. You’ll be fine. Just rest up, drink plenty of fluids… and avoid any questionable takeaway food. You're preaching to the choir! I've been living on honey and lemon and watching old Lloyd Grossman shows. It’s the only thing that’s remotely cheering me up. Lloyd Grossman! You’re a woman after my own heart. That show was brilliant. All those spices, all that colour… brought a bit of vibrancy to a wet Tuesday night. I know, right? It’s pure comfort viewing. Speaking of vibrancy, I saw a documentary the other day about body language recognition. It was fascinating. Oh really? What about it? They were using AI to analyze micro-expressions. Apparently, you can tell so much about a person just from the subtle movements in their face. It's a bit scary, to be honest. It is a bit. Makes you wonder about all the cameras that are silently recording us, doesn't it?

"Double word score! 'Quixotic' – feeling good about that one." “Quixotic! Rather grand for a Tuesday evening, isn't it, love? I was aiming for 'rat'.” "My goodness, that’s a bold play, Eleanor. Quite theatrical." "The young ones do love their extravagant words. When I was teaching, vocabulary was a simpler affair. ‘Good’ and ‘bad’ were often sufficient." "Well, Dad, it's a Scrabble board. Theatre is the point! Besides, David was edging me out with all his 'dog' and 'cat' combinations.” "Hey, they're legitimate words! And reliable point-getters. You can't beat a good 'dog'." "Speaking of reliable, did you manage to navigate that gridlock at the Trafford Centre today, Eleanor?" “Oh, don't even mention it, Mum. It was absolute chaos. Seriously considered leaving without the Christmas decorations. I swear, half the cars were just parked haphazardly, people running in and out. The butcher's queue was a nightmare too - stretched halfway across the shop.” “The consumer frenzy. It’s gotten worse, hasn't it? Back in my day, you'd pop into the local butcher and a friendly chat was part of the service.” "Right? It was a community thing rather than a competition to see who could grab the last gammon steak." "I remember. There was a sense of civility. Though I did find myself rather flustered this afternoon trying to post a picture of Angus on Facebook – he’s finally mastered the art of sitting still for five seconds." "Let me guess, the photo was blurry and everyone commented on his ears?" "Precisely! Though Margaret did say he looked 'remarkably regal'. That was a plus." "Speaking of regal, did you ever get around to reading that article in 'Harmony' magazine about the rediscovered Bach recording?" "Not yet. It's buried under a pile of transcription work, I'm afraid. The client wants this legal document typed by tomorrow - the drama! It’s fascinating stuff, though, some court case about a stolen antique teapot." “A stolen teapot? Goodness. Some people are peculiar, aren't they." "Right, your turn, David. Don't expect me to be merciful just because you complain about my vocabulary.” "Merciful? You? Eleanor, you're a Scrabble shark." "Hmm, 'Zeal'. A rather fitting word for this game, I think. You’re full of zeal, Eleanor.” "Well, someone does need to keep you youngsters on your toes. Now, let's see… what can I do with these rather unfortunate letters…" "Just don't try 'quixotic' again, dear.

Lovely light this afternoon, isn't it? Rather warm for October, though. It is indeed. Bit unusual for this time of year. Good thing we're inside, at least. This TME working party is proving rather… thorough. Thorough seems a polite way to put it, Bernard. It’s relentless! Still, important work, preserving this heritage, of course. You seem to be quite enjoying it though. I saw you dismantling that printing press earlier. Well, I do enjoy a bit of tinkering. Spent my career doing it, after all. Though, admittedly, my tinkering involved rather more advanced machinery. Oh, really? I know you’re retired, naturally, but I didn't realise you’d been… what exactly did you do? Apart from occasionally correcting my grammar at village fetes, of course. . A bit more than that, I fancy. I invented and marketed printing systems. Quite a niche area, really, but it took off. Automated typesetting, mostly. Did very well for a while. Goodness! Really? How fascinating. All those clever gadgets… printing! I always felt it was a rather magical process, transferring thoughts to paper. I mostly painted landscapes, you know, although I did some antique dealing too, for a bit of variety. A very different world, I’d imagine, from yours. Different, yes, but there’s a creative element to it, you see. Finding the right combination of technology and application, the clever marketing… It's rather like composing a piece of music. You’re arranging all the elements to create something harmonious. That’s a lovely way to put it. Where did all this… ingenuity… stem from? Mostly Germany, actually. We had a lot of exhibitions there – Düsseldorf, Frankfurt… They were always at the forefront of technological innovation. I spent a great deal of time over there, demonstrating our systems. Spent six months living in Munich at one point. Learned rather a lot of German, needless to say. Munich! That sounds delightful. Must have been quite a cultural revelation. It was.
