Though the business trips weren’t always glamorous. Lots of long hours, trying to convince sceptical printers that automated typesetting was the future. One particularly frosty meeting in Berlin… the man nearly threw his coffee at me! Said it would ruin the art of the compositor. Oh dear! People can be so resistant to change. They certainly can. But eventually, they came around. The efficiency was undeniable. It certainly simplified things.

Dad, are you  sure  you’re taking the right way? This satnav is being weird. Aye, love, trust me. Been driving for nigh on fifty years, I have. Satnavs just give you a suggestion, you know. Gotta use your own judgement. Besides, I know these roads like the back of me hand. But it keeps trying to take us through little villages. Like, really,  really  little villages. Well, that’s the scenic route, isn’t it? Can’t rush a holiday. Besides, you’re studying English Language, aren’t you? You can pick up some interesting dialects in those villages. Not really what I was thinking when I chose it as a subject. It's mostly about etymology and grammar, not listening to mumbled accents. Professor Davies is obsessed with the history of words. Did you know "quinoa" comes from the Quechua language? Quinoa? Sounds like something you’d use to clean a drain. Quechua… is that Latin? Nope, it's from South America. It’s a really old language too. Bit like Latin, I guess, in the sense that people don't really speak it as everyday language anymore. Cor, isn’t that bleak? All those words and stories disappearing. Like that cobbled path back in Bolton we used to walk, remember? Gone now. Replaced with tarmac. Yeah, it’s sad. Makes you think about how much language changes, doesn't it? Like, are we even speaking the same English as Shakespeare? Doubtful, lass. Doubtful. Listen, there’s a service station up ahead. Need to stretch your legs, grab a coffee? Actually, yeah, please. My legs are killing me. And I'm craving a proper Cornish pasty. Do you think we can find a farmer’s market somewhere? We’ll keep an eye out. Plymouth's a decent sized city and should have something. Right, turn left at the roundabout. Okay… and… according to this signage, Cornwall is just… over there… somewhere. You and your no-satnav policy. You know, I was reading about the philosophical implications of directions the other week. It's about agency and free will. Honestly, lass, you’ll be arguing with a pigeon next! Philosophy in a car. What's next, debating the ethics of chip butties? They  are  ethically questionable, aren't they? All that white bread... Now you’re just being deliberately difficult! Fancy some bread and bacon later? Maybe. Although, I bet the Cornish have some really interesting baking traditions.

Right, so I reckon this needs a bit more seasoning, doesn’t it? Bit bland, this. Nah, it’s alright, just needs a bit of time to settle. You’re always adding loads of salt, Liv, you'll give us all heart attacks. Don't be daft, a bit of salt never hurt anyone. It’s flavour, Liam. My nan always says… Oh, here we go. Nan this, nan that. Everything’s thanks to your nan, isn't it? She knows best, George. She’s been cooking for seventy years. What do you know about cooking, Liam? You sling concrete all day. Hey! I can cook! I made a banging fry-up last Sunday, didn't I? A fry-up doesn't count. That’s just heating up pre-cooked stuff. It was better than that curry you tried to make last month. Remember that? We practically had to order pizza. That was one time! And you were being picky because you were hungover. Speaking of families... did you hear from your mum about the wedding? Not yet, no. I texted her earlier, she said she'd call. I’m starting to worry she's forgotten. It’s only six months away. She’ll be fine, Liv. Your mum’s always stressed about everything. Remember when she panicked about the RSPCA coming to check on Daisy? Don't remind me. It was a neighbour being nosy, but Mum was convinced Daisy was going to be taken away. She spent a week hiding her under the duvet. Goodness me. People do get worked up over the silliest things, don’t they? My Doris used to worry about the postman judging her flower arrangements. See! It’s a family thing. The worrying. I inherited it, clearly. So, what are you thinking for the wedding? I mean, food-wise? Your mum’s notorious for her dodgy buffet spreads. That's what I'm panicking about! She'll have vol-au-vents filled with something questionable and a mountain of prawn cocktail. I'm trying to convince her to go with a hog roast. Hog roast's always a winner. Easy, tasty, everyone loves a bit of pork. Yeah, and you can get it catered now, no need for your mum to be slaving away in the kitchen for days. Exactly! But she's being stubborn. She says it’s tradition to do a buffet.

Hey! Didn't expect to see you here. Thought you’d be teaching French or something. Hi! Yeah, it's my day off. Needed a swim and thought I'd grab a coffee. You're working, right? Still slinging drinks? Still am. Keeps me busy, you know? Though, some days, it feels like I’m just an expensive jukebox. What are you up to today, besides the swim? Just relaxing, really. My partner's away on a business trip – a blessed few hours of peace and quiet. How's the bar scene? Still full of stag dos and hen nights? On the weekends, definitely. It's a bit… chaotic. Weekdays are a bit calmer, though. I’m actually thinking about doing some online courses in the evenings. Maybe something in marketing. Oh, that’s smart. Always good to have something else going, isn't it? You always were a clever one. What about the dating scene? Still avoiding commitment like the plague? Something like that. Had a few dates, nothing serious. Dating apps are a nightmare, honestly. Everyone’s got the same three photos – gym selfies and hiking in the Lake District. Tell me about it! It's awful. I met my partner online, but it took weeks of sifting through the horrible profiles. Are you still driving that little Fiesta? Yeah, the Fiesta's still going strong. Just had it serviced, thankfully. It's seen better days, but it gets me around. You know, I nearly crashed it last week. Oh no! What happened? Total idiot pulled out in front of me. I slammed on the brakes, narrowly avoided him. Gave him a proper earful, too. Felt a bit bad afterwards, but he deserved it. Drivers around here are insane. I’ve been thinking about getting a dashcam, actually. For peace of mind. Do you think it's worth it? Definitely. They're not that expensive and it could save you a fortune in insurance claims. Plus, it’s good evidence if someone tries to blame you for something. Good point. You always have some practical advice. You should be a motivational speaker. Wouldn't suit me at all. So, you teaching any interesting books at the moment? Anything I should be reading? We're doing 'Madame Bovary' this term. A bit depressing, but a classic, of course. You ever read Flaubert? Not really, no. I tend to stick to thrillers.

Right then, break time's looming! Fancy a bit more coffee, Patricia? Oh, yes please, Derek. Just a little top-up. This is lovely, by the way. Much better than that instant stuff I'm forced to drink at home. Well, relax, both of you. You've been buzzing about all morning. I’ve just been enjoying the peace and quiet. Well, we’ve got a lot on our minds, haven’t we? This little fundraiser’s got to be properly organized. It will be, Derek. We're getting there. The donation box is almost finished, isn’t it? And I've managed to find some nice ribbon. It looks very good, Patricia. Though, I still think a banner would raise more awareness. Something bright and obvious. Absolutely. Something eye-catching. I was thinking maybe a picture of the bell ringing team? They’re always so enthusiastic. They are, aren’t they? It’s a shame Peter’s not able to be involved this time. He’s really missed it too. Yes, a shame. He sends his regards, you know. Though his mobility isn’t what it was. Remember that time he said he'd walked all the way from Norwich? Complete fabrication. Oh, he always had a story, didn't he? A bit like that doctor, you remember, from that documentary we watched? The one with Munchausen’s? Oh, don't remind me. Absolutely dreadful. And to think, deliberately inventing illnesses… it’s beyond comprehension. It is quite disturbing, isn't it? But a powerful reminder about the importance of listening to people, even when their stories seem… improbable. Speaking of improbable, I’m still amazed you drove all the way from Middlesex this morning, Edward. That’s quite a journey. Well, I wouldn’t miss it. And the traffic wasn’t too bad, actually. Though I did get rather lost following the sat-nav. Ended up on a farm track for a bit! Oh, you didn’t! I did! Sheep everywhere. Had to reverse all the way back to the main road. You’re a brave man, Edward. We're going to have to have a think about where to put the plants too. Patricia, you were saying you'd got some nice geraniums? Yes, I did. Just a few to brighten the place up. We should put them near the entrance so people can see them as they come in.

Speaker_1 : Right, okay, so TikTok’s algorithm  finally  understood I’m obsessed with cottagecore. My feed is just fields and flowy dresses now. It’s a little intense. Speaker_2 : Sounds about right. Mine’s still stuck on gaming montages, thanks to my brother. He keeps stealing my phone. Speaker_3 : Ugh, classic. My feed’s a mess because I got obsessed with true crime for like, a week. Now I get recommended murder documentaries. Terrifying. Speaker_4 : You should try the 'Coastal Grandmother' aesthetic instead. It’s way more calming than true crime. Think Diane Keaton in something linen and breezy. Elara: Ooh, I like the sound of that! Definitely adding it to my search history. Speaking of scary, did you guys see  Smile ? Liam: No way. I heard it was awful! Like, genuinely disturbing. My girlfriend refused to watch it with me. Chloe: It  was  pretty rough. I had nightmares for two nights straight. Maisie, what did you think? Maisie: I didn’t hate it, but it wasn’t as scary as everyone made out. I think I'm more into psychological thrillers now. Like, the ones that mess with your head, rather than jump scares. Elara: Fair enough. Anyone heard from Ben lately? I haven’t seen him at the gym. Liam: Nah, he went to that festival in Bristol last weekend. Sent a bunch of blurry Instagram stories. Said it was ‘epic.’ Chloe: I saw him liking all my hiking photos. Is he trying to get my attention? Maisie: Maybe! Don’t encourage him too much, Chloe. Remember what happened last time you let him buy you a drink? Chloe: Don’t remind me! Ended up singing karaoke and spilling red wine on my favorite top. It was mortifying. Liam: Speaking of drinks, this dinner is amazing, Anya. Seriously, you outdid yourself. Speaker_1 : Thanks! I wanted to try that new pasta recipe I found online. What do you all think? Elara: It’s incredible! The sauce is so rich. Maisie: Definitely the best thing I’ve eaten all week. Chloe: Agree! Though I’m still craving pizza. Liam: Always craving pizza. Anya: You guys are impossible! Okay, so, holiday plans. Anyone booked anything yet? Maisie: My parents are dragging us to Tenerife again. It’s fine, I guess, but I’d love to go somewhere different. Like… Italy. Or Greece. Elara: Ooh, Greece! I’ve always wanted to go. Imagine all the sunshine and the ouzo.

Right then, well that was lovely to see you, Margaret. Always a pleasure. You too, John. It’s been ages! How are you both keeping? We’re alright, Margaret. Just plodding along as usual. The weather hasn't been kind, you know. More rain than sunshine seems to be the order of the day. Aye, you're right, Arthur. Damp and dreary. At least it’s not freezing like last winter. Remember that? Couldn't feel our toes for a week. Oh goodness, yes! I was worried about the little ones I minded. Keeping them warm enough was a challenge. And trying to get the bus in those conditions! Dreadful. So, Margaret, how's your daughter doing? Still working in London? She is, yes. Doing very well, actually. She was just saying how the cost of living is soaring. Absolutely ridiculous. Tell me about it. Petrol prices, for a start. Highway robbery, that is. I’m trying to cycle more, you know, but it's not ideal with this weather. I'm glad you're trying, Arthur. Cycling's good for you. I'm thinking about getting one of them electric bikes. Less of a strain. Oh, that’s a good idea, John. My nephew got one and he loves it. Practically glides along! I saw one that looked a bit like a vintage Raleigh the other day. Bit posh, though. Probably cost a small fortune. Everything does these days. Thinking about it, how are you getting home, Margaret? It’s getting on a bit. Oh, I was just thinking about that. I’m a bit worried, actually. The number 28 isn’t running very often these days. The 28, eh? Always a problem with that route. It’s down to one bus an hour sometimes. I could give you a lift, Margaret. No bother at all. It’s on my way back anyway. Oh, John, would you? That would be so lovely! I really appreciate it. Good man, John. Always looking out for people. She lives down near the Co-op, doesn’t she Margaret? Yes, just around the corner from there. It's a bit of a walk otherwise. Right then. Let me just finish this cup of tea, and we'll be ready to go whenever you are. Wouldn't want to keep you waiting. Now, where did I put that biscuit tin ... Ah, here we are. Have a custard cream, Margaret!

Right, so the removals company are definitely confirmed for next Tuesday then? Everything’s booked? Yes, dear, all sorted. They rang this morning just to double check, and I’ve cleared out the last of the Christmas decorations. Honestly, the amount of tinsel I collected over the years… you’d think I was decorating Buckingham Palace! You always went overboard with the decorations, Mary. Remember that year you put lights on every single branch of the Christmas tree? It looked like a disco ball. Oh, don’t remind me! Your dad nearly had a heart attack trying to untangle them all. Speaking of Dad... how are his legs feeling today? He didn’t seem too mobile last time I called. A bit stiff, you know, the usual. These weather changes don't do him any favours. I’ve got him a heat pad for his feet – seems to help. And the physio is still going well, he says, slowly but surely. Good, good. We’ll need to make sure he's settled in properly when we get back to the new place. Bit of a change for him, going from a sprawling house to something a little more manageable. It’s a lovely place, though, isn't it? Much more manageable for everyone. And that garden! He’ll be in his element there, pottering about. It will be nice to have him closer, too. Easier to pop over for a cup of tea and a biscuit. Precisely! Although I might need to hide the biscuit tin from him… he has a fondness for those ginger nuts, doesn’t he? Oh, definitely. So, the car… are you still happy with the Volvo for the move? It’s a good size, isn’t it? It’ll do the job, I think. Although, I wouldn’t trust it for a long journey. I swear it rattles more with every mile we drive. It's getting on a bit, isn’t it? But reliable, mostly. I’m thinking we’ll need to look at a new one after this… something smaller, something a bit more economical. Have you looked at Hyundais? They seem to have good reviews for reliability and fuel efficiency. Possibly. Although I'm not a fan of the styling. I like something with a bit of…character. Like our Volvo, then? Full of character and questionable noises. Exactly. Hey, does anyone else find the M6  terrible  for traffic?

Right, so you won't believe this, love. Remember how upset you were about your bike being stolen? Yeah! Like, really upset. I needed it for college. Well, guess what? The police found it! No way! Seriously? Where was it? Apparently, it was dumped in a field down near Ore. Bit of a mess, but they managed to get it back. Bit muddy, but mostly okay. Oh my god! Really? Are you sure it’s  my  bike? Not some other poor person’s? Positive. They checked the serial number. They said some kids had probably nicked it just to mess around, you know how they are. Ugh, typical. Can I go and see it? They’ve got it at the station at the moment. I went down this morning to identify it. We can go down later this afternoon, if you like. Pick you up from college? Yes, please! That would be amazing! Do you think the brakes still work? They said they looked okay, but we’ll definitely check them before you ride it again. They didn’t do a full service or anything. Good. I was going to post about it on Insta, about the bike being found. Should I put a picture of it covered in mud? Haha, you could! Though it might not look very appealing! Maybe wait until it's all cleaned up? Yeah, you're right. Maybe a clever caption though, like "Justice prevails " Something like that! So, about food tonight… I was thinking of making that pasta bake you like. Ooh, yes please! That sounds amazing. I'm starving. All this excitement has made me hungry! Well, I’m glad to see some good news finally. It's been a stressful few days. Speaking of stressful, how's college going? That history essay due soon, isn’t it? Yeah, I'm… it’s going. I still need to do a ton of research. It's so boring though, all about Victorian factories. I know, it can be. Remember, if you need any help, just ask. Maybe we can grab some cycling gear from the shops tomorrow too, as a little reward for getting your bike back? That would be so cool! New gloves, maybe? And definitely a way better lock this time! No more of that flimsy thing. Absolutely. We’ll get the best lock they have. And no more leaving it outside unattended!

Honestly, this game is more stressful than marking years 10’s essays. Rhys, are you  sure  you’re not deliberately blocking me? Blocking you? Shwmae, Bethan, don’t be daft! I'm just… strategically expanding my network. Besides, look at Huw, he's got the entire American Midwest cornered.  He’s  the one to worry about. Just need to get to Seattle. Seattle's key. Utterly key. Back in my day, we didn’t have all this fancy railway building. We just had the trains. Used to travel all over the world on them. Singapore to Cardiff, you know. A long journey that, let me tell you. Oh, don't start with your stories again, Dad. We’ll be here all night. And Huw, are you even looking at the map? You’re about to run into Rhys's route in Denver! Exactly! It’s ridiculous. I need to connect London to Edinburgh, it’s vital! But everyone keeps hoarding the red trains. Honestly, it's like trying to get a decent avocado in November. It's called strategy, Bethan. You can't just waltz in and claim all the prime routes. Competishion, girl! Remember that time we were in the Brecon Beacons and you nearly fell off that cliff trying to take a selfie? That’s what happens when you rush things. That was a  completely  separate incident and involved an excessively enthusiastic sheep. And it was scenic, thank you very much. Anyone got any green trains? I need… I need to reinforce the Canadian Rockies and I'm running desperately low. Green trains, eh? Reminds me of a trip I took on the Orient Express, years ago. Everything was green velvet and polished brass. The chef made a wonderful lemon tart. Oh, here we go. Another one of Dad’s extravagant travel tales. Honestly, he'll probably tell us he wrestled a bear on his way to Singapore next. Don’t give him ideas, Mum. Bethan, you need to focus. I'm consolidating my position here. Watch. There. Control of the Mediterranean. It’s practically mine. You are unbelievably smug. And I’m pretty sure you’re spending all your points on cities with ridiculously low scores. Guys! Can we  please  focus? I’m about to lose everything! The entire Pacific Northwest. Gone! Speaking of journeys, remember when the trains were always delayed? Used to be the bane of my life.

Right, your turn. Are you going to try and monopolize Baltic again, or are you feeling generous? Generous? Where would that be coming from? It’s clearly my strategic advantage. Everyone knows the colour monopoly builds the strongest foundations. It’s repetitive and a bit boring, honestly. You just build a wall of brown and orange and then everyone else is doomed. It’s not nuanced! Nuance isn’t always the goal, darling. Sometimes, you just want to crush your opponents with the sheer power of financial dominance. It’s… satisfying. You’re such a capitalist pig. I’m going to build a hotel on Light Blue. Just to spite you. Don't you dare! That's financially irresponsible. Think about the return on investment! Light Blue is a terrible investment. Exactly! That’s why it’ll work. You’ll be so busy worrying about your brown hotels you won't notice me draining your resources. You’re going to regret that. Actually, speaking of resources... did you see that article about the rise in craft beer consumption in the UK? The one about how it’s basically replaced pubs for a lot of younger people? Yeah, I did. Quite sad, really. Sad, or just evolution? Pub culture has been on the decline for a while. It’s just… different now. People want bespoke, artisanal beers they can Instagram and a quieter atmosphere. Less yelling, less questionable karaoke. I do miss the yelling and questionable karaoke, though. There was something comforting about it, that sense of shared, slightly chaotic community. Comforting chaos. You’re a romantic. But I get it. I miss pubs too, sometimes. It’s just…a bit harder to find a decent pint these days, isn’t it? Everything feels a bit… curated. Totally. It's like genuine socialising is becoming a performance. Remember when we used to go to The Dog and Duck in Norwich and just end up chatting to absolute strangers for hours? Oh god, yes. That was a proper pub. Sticky floors, dodgy lighting, and a landlord who'd tell you his life story if you bought him a pint. And you ended up playing darts with someone you’d never met before. That’s what I miss. That spontaneity. Well, you can't recreate that. It's changed. Speaking of games... you know, I was thinking about Settlers of Catan the other day.

This lentil shepherd’s pie is surprisingly good, isn’t it? Better than I thought it would be. Yeah, it’s really tasty, Kerrie. You’ve outdone yourself. Much better than that dodgy lasagne last time. That lasagne was a disaster, wasn't it? I still think I tasted burnt cheese for a week afterwards. But this is lovely, really hearty. Well, I’m trying to eat less meat, and this seemed like a decent option. Less faff than a veggie stew too. So, how are the packing preparations going? Still a mountain of boxes? Don’t even get me started! It’s a nightmare. We’ve got the kitchen almost cleared, but the living room is another story. It's like a storage unit exploded in there. Moving is never easy, is it? I remember when your dad and I moved to this house, we had to cram everything into a tiny van. Nearly killed us all. You’ve got a bigger place though, right? More room for furniture? Yes, thankfully. But we’re having to buy a new washing machine and fridge freezer. The old ones are on their last legs. That's always a hefty expense, isn’t it? Have you looked at those energy-efficient models? They can save you a fortune on your bills in the long run. We've had a look. Thinking about a Bosch, but they’re pricey. Trying to balance quality with what we can actually afford. I'm definitely feeling the crunch of having to replace those things, that’s for sure. What about asking your brother if he has any recommendations? He’s good with that kind of stuff. Good point. I’ll give him a ring tomorrow. Speaking of recommendations, did you manage to get that appointment with Mr. Davies, Rhian? Yes, thankfully. Took weeks, but I finally got through. Turns out I've got a minor thing, nothing to worry about, just needs monitoring. Those Welsh NHS waiting lists… it’s ridiculous. Tell me about it. My aunt’s been waiting months for a scan. It's appalling. Anyway... moving on to something slightly more cheerful. Have you seen anything good on crafty YouTube lately? I'm trying to find a new project to keep me occupied while we're packing. Oh, I saw a really lovely macrame wall hanging tutorial. You’re good with your hands, Kerrie, you’d be brilliant at it.

This traffic is mental, isn't it? I swear it gets worse every time. It is dreadful. Should have left earlier. Though, what's the point, really? Would have just been stuck somewhere else. True. At least we can listen to some music. Fancy some Radiohead? Oh, please, no. Something a bit…gentler. My head's been pounding all day. Alright, alright. Classic FM it is then. Though I can’t stand the adverts. You're becoming just like your grandfather, complaining about everything. Hey! I just appreciate a decent music stream without breaks for insurance. Anyway, how was the TLS meeting today? Did you manage to get through that manuscript about the French existentialists? Don't even ask. It was…dense. Seriously dense. The kind of dense where you start to question your entire life choices, and whether you should have become a literary editor. Rough day at the office then? Let’s just say I'm considering early retirement and moving to a vineyard in Provence. Provence sounds good. With lots of sunshine and good wine. Speaking of things I’d like, are we still on for getting me that new driving gloves for my birthday? Of course, darling. You’ve been hinting about them for months. Though, I hope you’re being a bit safer behind the wheel. I saw you weave a little bit back there. Nearly gave me a heart attack! I was just avoiding that maniac in the black van. Seriously, the road rage in London is something else. It's like people forget how to be civilized. Exactly! It's frightening. And the noise! All that honking… I’m glad we’re going north. It’s quieter up there. Yeah, a bit. Still, I’m looking forward to seeing Grandma and Grandpa. Are we getting them anything special? I was thinking of that puzzle they like. The one with the Impressionist paintings. Remember how they were so pleased with the last one? Yeah, they loved it. Good shout. They're always saying they need more mental stimulation. They do, don't they? It keeps them going. Speaking of keeping people going, did you ever hear back about that internship with Penguin? I had an interview yesterday! Really! Oh, that's fantastic! How did it go? I think it went pretty well. They seemed really interested in my ideas for their social media strategy. It’s a digital focused role.

Right, so then the monkey nicked my sunglasses! Honestly, you wouldn’t believe it. Just snatched them right off my face! A monkey? Where were you, Tarzan? Thailand, you goof! We were at this sanctuary, feeding them and everything, and this little cheeky thing just…  snatch ! Gone. Worth a fortune too, they were. Did you chase after it? Honestly, what was I going to do? Wrestle a monkey for my Ray-Bans? The whole group were cracking up. My dad nearly choked on his beer. That's brilliant! I had something similar happen in Barcelona. A pigeon dive-bombed me and stole a chip right out of my hand. You always attract the wildlife, don’t you? Very funny, Liam. It was a particularly aggressive pigeon, I’ll have you know. Tried to take my whole bag. You’re just a pigeon magnet, Amy. Remember that time in London with the seagulls? Don’t remind me! I swear, one of them nearly took my ice cream. It was a rocky road flavour, too. Cruel. Speaking of cruel, remember old Mr. Henderson trying to teach his parrot to say ‘hello’? It only ever learned to shout ‘Fire!’ at random times. Oh god, yes! It gave the neighbours a right fright. He kept apologizing. Remember that holiday to Bournemouth, though? When Dad decided he was going to learn to surf? Oh my god, yes! He lasted all of five seconds before wiping out. And then he blamed the board. Said it was faulty. He gave the poor instructor a right earful, didn’t he? He did! Said it was clearly designed to throw people. The instructor just stood there, speechless. It’s still one of my favourite family stories. It’s the little things, isn’t it? Those awkward holiday moments. Totally. My grandad once tried to buy a camel in Morocco. No way! Did he succeed? Nope! The shop owner just laughed and said, ‘Where would you keep it, love?’. Grandad didn't have an answer for that. See? Everyone’s got a ridiculous holiday story. Makes them worth it, doesn't it? Even with the sunglasses-stealing monkeys. Cheers to ridiculous holiday stories! Cheers! Anyone fancy another round? I'm feeling brave enough for a pitcher of something fruity. I’m in, anything to top this one! Lead the way! I'll get this round, I think. Although… does anyone want to hear about the time I accidentally ordered a plate of fried insects in Vietnam…?

So, you’re actually seriously considering it, Fiona? Wild winter camping? In Scotland? It sounds utterly… bracing. Bracing is one word for it, David. Challenging is another. But aye, I've been reading up on it, and the photography potential alone is incredible. Imagine, snow-dusted landscapes, the Northern Lights… It's not just photography, Mum. There's something really primal about it. Stripping back to the basics, being completely reliant on your own skills and the environment. I’ve been looking into it too, actually. You are? Hamish, I didn't realise you had the inclination for such a... rugged pursuit. You always struck me as the literary type, buried in books. Well, I appreciate a good book, but I've been feeling the need to reconnect with nature lately. All this data and strategy and curriculum development... it gets a bit detached, doesn't it? And a lot of younger people are embracing these sorts of experiences. Exactly. It’s about resilience, and appreciating the simple things. It's a very different kind of therapy than what I offer in the office, you know? A really deep, visceral kind. I can appreciate that. Though the thought of being exposed to the elements like that... It sounds terribly uncomfortable. What about hypothermia? What about the midges, even in winter? Midge season is over, Dad. Mid-December onwards they're practically non-existent. And hypothermia is manageable with proper gear and preparation. It's about understanding the risks and mitigating them. I’m thinking a four-season tent, good layering system, thermal sleeping bag… I’ve been looking at Exped tents - they're surprisingly spacious for their weight. And I’m taking a wilderness first aid course in January, just in case. No need to be reckless, David. Wilderness first aid, eh? Sounds like you’re planning for the worst. What about food? Are you going to be foraging or...? Dehydrated meals mostly, Dad. Lightweight and easy to prepare. And I'm learning some basic wild edibles - there are still some berries and mushrooms that can be found even in winter, though you have to be  extremely  careful. I have a friend who’s a botanist. I’ll ask her for a list of safe and reliable ones. It’s fantastic getting to learn that side of things too - acknowledging what nature provides and learning to respect it. I still maintain it sounds freezing.

Honestly, I’m still buzzing from that film. "Everything Everywhere All At Once," right? It's just… a lot. It was intense, yeah. Visually stunning, though. And the acting was phenomenal. Michelle Yeoh was incredible. Incredible doesn't even cover it. The sheer range she had to display, jumping between universes, different personalities… It was mental. I kept thinking about that bagel scene, though. Just… wow. The bagel scene was… something else. Really drove home the nihilistic thing, didn't it? That it all ultimately meant nothing? Exactly! But then it completely flips on its head, doesn’t it? And you're left thinking, well, even if it  does  all mean nothing, the little connections, those moments of kindness and understanding… that's what matters. Yeah, that's the takeaway. It felt almost like a commentary on the modern world, with all the information overload and constant pressure. Trying to just… breathe and appreciate what you’ve got. Definitely. Speaking of appreciating things… I had this absolutely unbelievable curry last night. A little place down the road, “Spice King,” you’ve never heard of it. No, haven’t. Is it good? I need something new to try. I’m practically living on meal deals at the moment. Good? It was life-altering. Rogan Josh, but like, seriously next level. Loads of coriander, a creamy sauce… I wanted to marry it. You're being dramatic. I am, but it was that good. Proper comfort food. Makes you forget about all the universes collapsing around you. Sounds tempting. Maybe we should grab something from there next week? After work? Oh, absolutely! You wouldn't regret it. Although, fair warning, the décor is… well, let's just say it wouldn't win any design awards. As long as the food is good, I'm not bothered about the décor. I’ve been reading this fascinating essay about the use of language in… it’s a bit dense to be honest. Oh yeah? What’s it about? I always fancy a good read. I finally got around to "Frankenstein" last month. It’s about the semiotics of online communication. Basically, how emojis and GIFs and all that stuff have become a form of language in themselves. Right. I can see that. We communicate so much through visuals now, don't we? It's like a whole other layer of meaning. Do you think it blurs the lines between genuine emotion and just… performance?

Right, story time! Are you both snuggled in? Yes, Mummy! Can we have the one about the very hungry caterpillar? No! The one with the dragon! The sparkly one! Okay, okay, compromise. We’ll do the caterpillar first, and then we'll see if I can remember the dragon one. It’s got a much more complicated name, you know. Which reminds me, did Ms. Davies mention anything about Excel in class today, Leo? Excel? Is that a game? No, silly. It's… well, it's a computer thing. Grown-ups use it for numbers and charts. It looks a bit boring, but it’s actually quite clever. Like a really organised typewriter, almost. Remember when Grandma showed us her old typewriter? The clicky one! With the letters that pop out! Exactly! Excel is like that, but on a computer. It helps grown-ups keep track of things. Now, back to the hungry caterpillar… He started with one apple… …and then he ate a pear! And then… And then he ate a chocolate cake! You remember! Yes, he ate a chocolate cake. And then… He got a really big tummy! He did! And then what happened? He made a cocoon! And he went sleepy! Absolutely! And he came out as a beautiful butterfly! And what did you both learn from that story? Caterpillars like to eat lots! And then they fly! Can I play PlayStation now? Please, Mummy? Please, please, please???? Not yet, darling. It’s almost bedtime. Remember your Brownie Promise evening tomorrow? You were so excited. I’m gonna say the words really good! I’m gonna help other people! Like rescuing cats from trees! That’s the spirit! And you know what else? I was thinking… When you’re a bit older, you can learn about Excel. Maybe even build your own games with it. Really? Games?! Like on the PlayStation? Not quite like on the PlayStation, but you can create your own little worlds and problem-solving challenges. It's surprisingly fun. And you can use it to keep track of all your Lego pieces! Really?! So, like, a chart of all the red ones and the blue ones? Exactly! And the green ones, and the yellow ones! You could be Lego master organisers! That would be cool! Can we do that tomorrow then? After the Brownies? Maybe. We'll see. Now, let's remember our sparkly dragon story, shall we?

Right, more toast then, Robert? You were eyeing it up. Honestly, this marmalade is a bit thick today, isn't it? Bit too much pectin, I think. It is rather, isn’t it? Good strong stuff though. More’s the better, I always say. And yes, please, I’m famished. These roadworks on the M62 this morning added a good half hour to the journey. Absolute chaos. Tell me about it! I saw them on the news. Seemed like a right mess. Fruit farms all backed up, apparently. Heard they're having trouble getting the produce to market. That's what the radio said. Poor farmers. Speaking of farms, I was reading an interesting article the other day – about deserted medieval villages. Remarkable, really. Apparently, there are quite a few around these parts. Just swallowed up by the land. Really? I never knew. It's just fields now, isn't it? All ordinary countryside. It’s strange to think people lived and worked there. Yes, it is. Makes you reflect, doesn’t it? How quickly things change. Just like… well, like selling your house. Don’t remind me. It’s a big upheaval. The solicitor's been on the phone again, needing more paperwork. Honestly, these forms… it’s enough to drive you mad. And the junk mail! It’s tripled since we put the ‘For Sale’ sign up. Typical. They smell opportunity. I had similar when we sold the house in Windsor. I know! And then there’s the estate agents ringing constantly. Do you realize I’ve had three calls already this morning? I swear, they think I’m just sitting around waiting for an offer. Well, you are. Eventually. What about your herbs? Are they doing well? I remember promising to bring you some rosemary. They are actually! The thyme's gone a bit leggy but the rosemary’s thriving. I’m hoping to make some infused oil. Speaking of which, you really must try this coffee – it’s a new blend. It's lovely. Strong, just as I like it. Makes me think of those old adverts on the radio. "Nescafé, it's the thing!" Oh, I remember those! My dad used to buy tins and tins of it. You know, I keep thinking about downsizing, but then I realize how much stuff I have. It's ridiculous. All these little knick-knacks, mementos… You’re not alone.

Right, so I’ve ordered the salmon, and I’m thinking a lemon and dill sauce? What do you reckon, Dave? Sounds lovely, love. Salmon’s always a winner. You getting any veg with it? Yes, broccoli and some of those little new potatoes. And I’ve got that new cider from Waitrose, the one you liked. Ooh, exciting! Can I have extra potatoes, please? I’m starving. Of course, darling. Are you still on that ridiculous detox thing? It’s not ridiculous! It's just… well, I’m trying to be a bit better. Less Deliveroo, more… actual cooking. Good for you, sweetheart. Better than spending all your time glued to that mobile phone. Facebook’s a rabbit hole, you know. Tell me about it! I spent like, an hour yesterday just looking at pictures of cats. It's horrifying, really. You and half the population. Anyway, I finally got the prescription sorted for Mum. She was moaning non-stop about it. Did you remember to ask about the cream this time? The eczema’s been playing up. Yes, I did! The pharmacist said it was a new formulation, should be stronger. She’s already complaining it's not working, though. Honestly. Mothers, eh? They’re a force of nature. Did you tell her about that new body scrub you bought? The one with the sea salt? I did! She said it would be ‘far too abrasive’ for her delicate skin. As if she’s not 83! She just likes to moan, doesn't she? Remember last Christmas when she said the turkey was too dry, and then devoured three helpings? Classic Mum. So, any plans for New Year’s then? We were thinking of just staying in, really. Order some Chinese, watch a film. Low key. Sounds alright to me. Less stressful than going out. Remember that New Year’s Eve a few years ago at that awful pub in Kemsing? Don't remind me! The karaoke was horrendous, and the bar staff were awful. Oh, God, I'd forgotten about that. What happened to poor old Barry who tried to sing Bohemian Rhapsody? He gave up after the 'Mama Mia, Mama Mia' bit. Mortified. Good riddance, I say! You looked like you were trying  not  to laugh. I couldn’t help it! It was truly awful. I need a proper dram of something to wash that memory away.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that documentary on the energy crisis. It’s just… relentless. Everything’s going up, isn't it? Tell me about it. My parents were moaning about their gas bill the other day. Seriously eye-watering numbers. And I'm only living on student loans and sporadic survey work! It's mad. I'm trying to cut back everywhere I can, but it feels like you’re just chipping away at the edges of your life. Like, I’m almost ashamed to stream anything now. I get that. I’ve cancelled like three subscriptions this month. Do you still watch “Severance”? Absolutely obsessed. Finished it last night. The ending… I need a whole week to process it. What did you think? It was brilliant! Twisted, unsettling, but brilliant. Though I did kind of see the twist with the wife coming in. Did you? I was completely blindsided. Though, in retrospect, it was pretty obvious, wasn't it? Maybe a little. Still, the atmosphere was incredible. Anyway, enough about dystopian office dramas. How's the copywriting going? Still churning out snappy slogans for toilet cleaner? Pretty much. It pays the bills, though. I actually landed a decent project this week, writing the copy for a sustainable clothing brand. Which feels a bit ironic, considering I’m simultaneously trying to avoid spending any money. That’s great though! Sounds really interesting. Way better than toilet cleaner. Got any big plans after uni? Aside from, you know, saving the planet via copy? It’s terrifying. Honestly, I’m just trying to take it one step at a time. I’d love to move out of my mum’s eventually, get my own flat… but London rent is insane. Seriously. I’m thinking about moving back to Oxford, actually. It’s cheaper, and Mum and Dad would be thrilled. Part of me wants to just disappear into the countryside though. I understand that. It's hard to imagine leaving London, but it's also… exhausting. How's your mum doing? Still going on about you getting a "proper" job? Constantly. She keeps suggesting I become a solicitor. Like, seriously? After I spent four years studying philosophy? Oh God, mums. Mine's still trying to convince me to join the police force. Says it’s got “pension stability.” Pension stability! That's the metric for a fulfilling career now? Apparently. So, are you seeing anyone?

Honestly, I’m feeling it today. My back is protesting every single step I take. You’ve been doing too much Pilates, haven't you? Trying to be a twenty-year-old again. Don't you start. I need to stay active, you know. Otherwise, I'll just be a lump on the sofa, watching documentaries about obscure fungi. You’d enjoy the fungi documentaries. You always did have a fascination with the unusual. Remember that time you tried to grow your own glow-in-the-dark mushrooms? Oh, God, don't remind me. That was a disaster. The flat smelled like damp earth for weeks. And your attempts to make sourdough bread were legendary. Rock hard doorstops, every single one. Okay, okay, I'm not a domestic goddess. But at least I'm trying! What have you two been up to? I’ve just finished the first draft of a new chapter. It’s about a woman who inherits a haunted tea shop… rather cliché, I know, but it’s selling well. A haunted tea shop? That sounds right up your alley. You’ll be giving it a spooky name already, won’t you? "The Spectral Scones"? Something like that. Honestly, the publishers are demanding more gothic romance. It’s all everyone wants these days. Speaking of demands, have you seen the price of houses around here lately? Utter madness. I was looking at a flat the other day, two bedrooms, needed a complete renovation… and it was almost half a million. It’s scandalous, isn’t it? How can anyone afford to buy a home these days? We were talking about it at work – apparently, there’s a bidding war on for a semi-detached house three streets away. They're offering over a hundred grand above the asking price! It’s all driven by the investors, isn't it? They're buying up everything. First-time buyers haven’t got a chance. I’m seriously considering just renting indefinitely. It’s easier, less stressful… and I could move further out and actually get some space. You'd have to commute further. It's not as easy as it used to be. True, but I’d rather commute than spend all my savings on a tiny box with peeling wallpaper. Have you been trying out any new recipes lately? Something to take your mind off the housing crisis? I did make a rather lovely lemon and thyme chicken the other day.

Honestly, the new corpus interface is driving me absolutely mental. They’ve completely changed the search functionality. Oh, really? Still wrestling with that, then? I remember you were pretty stressed about the changes last time we spoke. Stressed is an understatement. It’s like they’ve actively tried to make it more difficult for users. I spent three hours yesterday just trying to pull a simple set of data. Three hours! That’s brutal. What’s the issue exactly? Is it the filtering? It's everything, really. The filtering's awful, the tagging system's clunky... it's just a mess. I keep having to contact support, and they're not exactly the most helpful, either. Sounds infuriating. You'd think with all the money they're throwing around, they could afford a decent UI designer. What was the Budget announcement like the other day? Did that affect your funding at all? It was… horrifying, to be honest. Thankfully, we’re mostly ring-fenced, so our funding wasn’t directly impacted. But the general mood is pretty down. So many research projects are facing cuts. It feels like the government doesn't really value things like language analysis anymore. It’s a shame. It's important work, you know? Trying to understand how language changes and evolves... Tell me about it. Anyway, enough about my work woes. Did you manage to finish that complex structural design you were on about? The bridge one? Nearly. Got the final stress calculations done yesterday. It was a nightmare, honestly. So many variables to account for. It's finally going to be presented to the council next week. Fingers crossed! Brilliant! That’s fantastic news. You must be relieved. So, anything exciting happening outside of bridges and stress calculations? I know you were talking about seeing a musical? Yeah! I managed to get tickets for  Wicked  next month. You free? Fancy coming with?  Wicked ! Oh, I’d love to! I’ve heard it's amazing. Been ages since I’ve seen a good musical. Me too. It’ll be a nice change from blueprints and concrete! Definitely. When are you thinking? It's just so lovely here today; it's nice to be around greenery for once. Let me check my calendar… Actually, how about the evening of the 17th? Should be a Saturday. The 17th sounds perfect. Let me just double-check my diary, but I think I'm clear.

Right, so I’m thinking a kind of muted grey for this section of the fence, blends in a bit more, don't you think? Less jarring against the brick. Mmm, grey's alright. Bit dull though, innit? Shoulda gone for a brighter colour, like. Give it a bit of character. Character, yes, but I’m trying for something a bit more… subtle. Something that doesn't shout. It’s a back garden, after all. Not a carnival. You and your subtlety. Always been like that, haven’t you? Remember that time you tried to direct that play at the Everyman? Don't remind me! The director's cut was three hours long. It cleared the theatre faster than you can say "Shakespeare." It wasn't subtle, granted. No, it were a bleedin' epic! Still, you’ve always fancied yourself an actor, haven’t ya? Ever acting again? Rarely. My acting days are best left in the distant past. I'm more comfortable behind the scenes these days, you know, with the language, the literature... analyzing it. Speaking of things behind the scenes, they’re starting to tear down them old warehouses down by the docks, aren't they? Yes, another block of flats, I suppose. More luxury apartments for people who don’t need ‘em. It’s depressing, really. What are they doing to Liverpool? Progress, they call it. Got yer politicians spinning stories, don't they? Used to be a lot of character down there. Proper artists, craftspeople. Now it’s all chain shops. Exactly. It’s a shame. I picked up a lovely old watercolour down at a car boot sale last week – landscape of the docks, from the 50s, it must be. Ooh, show me that sometime. I’m always looking for a bargain. Speaking of bargains, you still need that ladder to get up to the gutters? Yes, actually. Those gutters are a nightmare. Keeps leaking. I’ve been meaning to sort them out for weeks. I’ve got one in the garage. A bit wobbly, mind, but it’ll do the job. You can borrow it. Just give it back when you’re done. Brilliant! Thank you, Dave. Really appreciate that. I'll bring you a couple of beers as a thank you. Cheers, that’s grand. I'm always needing a reason to crack open a cold one. You know, I was thinking of getting myself a little easel and trying to learn to paint myself.

Oh, look, more fields. Just...fields. It's quite monotonous, isn’t it? Though the light is rather lovely on them this afternoon. All golden-y. Yeah, it is a bit. Still, beats staring at a classroom wall, eh? At least we’re  seeing  something. And it's miles better than Bury, honestly. Not that I'm knocking Bury, it's just... this is different. Absolutely. Though, I am starting to miss having a proper cuppa. That instant stuff just isn't the same. Did you manage to track down any decent Polish biscuits? I got some yesterday in Zakopane, the kind with the poppy seeds. They were actually all right. We should stop at a shop soon, I’m starting to feel peckish. Are we still on track for Tarnów by, like, seven? I think so. Google Maps is being fairly cooperative. Although, honestly, driving through Poland is just...it’s a palate cleanser after years of just saving up and then sorting through boxes. You know? Yeah, I get it. So much stuff. You're really making progress clearing out the flat, aren't you? Mum seemed really pleased when I spoke to her. It's liberating, actually. I’m selling bits online. Someone bought that ridiculous ceramic frog I'd had since university! Can you believe it? Seriously? That thing was hideous! Good riddance. You should’ve been posting those pictures of everything you’re selling, I’d have bought a few things for my flat. I will, I promise. Right now I’m just focused on getting rid. It’s quite a strange feeling, letting go of things you've held onto for decades. It is. I think that’s why I'm finding this trip so good. A total reset. Remember that time we tried to hitchhike to Whitby? Oh god, yes! That was a disaster. We ended up stranded in some tiny village and had to beg a farmer for a lift. And he smelled strongly of sheep! Still, it's a good story. Makes you appreciate having a campervan with a working toilet, doesn't it? It certainly does! Have you heard from Liam recently? I’ve been meaning to message him. Yeah, he's in Berlin, apparently. Said he's loving it. Properly living the expat life. Bit jealous, not gonna lie. So are you still planning on going to that festival in Manchester when you get back?

Are we nearly there yet? My legs are aching. Almost, love. Just another ten minutes or so. You alright? You seem a bit tired. Yeah, I stayed up late reading. I’m halfway through ‘The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida’ – it’s brilliant, Dad, you should read it! Ah, I’ve heard of that. Sheku recommended it, didn’t he? Bit heavy going though, isn’t it? All that political stuff. It’s intense, yeah, but the writing’s really clever. And it's got this really weird afterlife storyline, which is quite morbid but fascinating. You know like… people just hanging out waiting to be reborn. Sounds a bit grim for a car journey, doesn’t it? Not really, it makes you think. Remember when you wanted me to go to the Hay Festival? Yes! And you didn't want to. I still think you should go. All those authors... Hay Festival’s brilliant. Shame I missed it last year, completely wiped out with that chest infection. Thought I was going to end up in hospital. Speaking of things wiping you out, how are gran and grandad? Did you call them today? I did ring them. Gran’s saying she's feeling a bit better, but still struggling to sleep. Doctor thinks it might be those new pills they gave her. Those pills they give people these days! They never tell ya the side effects. It's a racket, it is. I remember my mum took something off the telly once for her arthritis... ended up with blisters all over her feet! Seriously, Dad? I'm serious! Right as rain one minute, walking around like she’d been through a furnace the next! Should've stuck to Epsom salts, that's what my grandma always used to say. What are we getting from Preston today, anyway? Besides cheering you up. We need milk, bread and some chocolate. And I wanted to go into Boots to get… oh, I can’t remember! Something for exams. Exams already? You’re flying through school. It's only just started. Yeah, but they’re looming, aren’t they? Plus, you know, that move is stressing me out. I need to de-stress somehow. Actually, I think I'll check online for some relaxation spotify playlists. Don't forget we need some new towels for the bathroom. The ones we have are looking a bit threadbare.

Nan! What are you doing here? This is brilliant! Didn’t expect to see you for ages. Well, I thought I’d surprise you all. Your son – my grandson – said you were all here, in Thirsk. And I thought, "Right, I’ll pop up!" Nan! You're here! Wow. You look…well, you look like Nan! And you’ve grown another inch, haven’t you, lad? Last time I saw you, you were still struggling to reach the biscuit tin. He’s well over that height now, Nan. He’s towering over me! So, what brings you all this way? Everything alright? Perfectly alright, dear. Just felt a bit restless. Needed a bit of a change. And I wanted to see your face, love. It's been too long since I've seen you properly. Besides, I was sorting through some old boxes back home and found a hilarious sketch from that comedy club we went to years ago. Reminded me of you. Oh, you haven’t! The one with the pigeon? Seriously? I’d forgotten all about that. And you were nearly choking with laughter! You sprayed your drink everywhere, didn’t you? A pigeon sketch? Was it good? It was brilliant, love. Really silly. Nan's got a good eye for funny. She used to drag us to all sorts of open mic nights. Well, you children need a bit of silly in your lives! Though I must say, all this technology you youngsters have now… it’s baffling. I tried to send an email the other day, and I ended up ordering five gardening gnomes online. Oh, Nan! Don't tell me! It’s true! I was trying to find Susan’s address, and I got completely lost. These icons… and the drop-down menus… utterly confusing. It’s easy once you get used to it, Nan. I can show you. Actually, I've been learning loads about coding. It's pretty cool. Coding? What's that? Sounds like something you do in a spy movie. He’s learning to write computer programs, Nan. Basically, telling the computer what to do. Fancy that. Well, you’re a clever lad. I'm proud of you. But tell me, are you two clearing out that garage like you said? It’s been months now. We’re trying! It’s a monumental task. It’s full of… well, everything. Your old china cabinet is in there, remember?

Right, so, initial impressions? What do you reckon of the new machine? It’s… surprisingly nippy, isn’t it? Loads better than yours was, for sure. The screen’s nice and bright too. What spec is it, exactly? It’s got a Ryzen 7, 16 gigs of RAM, 512 gig SSD. Not exactly top of the line, but should do the trick for the work I do. Figured it was time to retire that dinosaur. Looks respectable. Hardware-wise, pretty solid. I’m more interested in how it runs those complicated video editing things you’re always doing. That's where the real test is. Yeah, that's what I was thinking. I've got a 4K video I've been wanting to chop up for ages, a mate sent it over. Let's see if it can handle it without melting down. Right, let's fire it up. Got Premiere Pro installed, yeah? Yep, all sorted. Tried a quick render earlier, seemed pretty promising. What about you, Alex? Still beating people up at the gym? Nah, not this week. Got a dodgy knee. Trying to be a bit kinder to myself, you know? Maybe take up line dancing instead. Line dancing? Seriously? Don't knock it till you’ve tried it! All those repetitive movements are good for the core, apparently. Plus, the ladies seem to enjoy it. You’re a menace, Alex. Anyway, this video's loading… yeah, it’s actually surprisingly quick. Considering it’s 4K. That’s a relief. The old one would have taken forever. Remember that project I did for that wedding? Took a whole weekend just to render. Oh god, the one with the disastrous cake cutting? Still makes me laugh. Speaking of disasters, did you see that article in the Bedfordshire Gazette about Mrs. Higgins' cat getting stuck in a tree again? No, what? Really? That's the third time this year! Poor kitty. Someone really needs to get that cat a harness. You're right. Where have you been getting your groceries from latel. The new Korean place. They have amazing kimchi. Seriously, best I’ve had outside of Seoul. Korean food, eh? I've not really ventured past the usual. You gotta tell me what to order. Yeah, recommend something, man. I’m trying to eat a bit healthier, you know? Less beige food. Get the Bibimbap. Loads of veg, good protein, and it's got that lovely spicy kick.

This place is lovely, isn't it? I mean, Tarnów wasn’t exactly overflowing with trendy bistros last time I was here. It’s really good! The decor's so… Scandi-chic. And their coffee's proper good. I wasn’t expecting that in Tarnów, to be honest. No, me neither. I’m impressed. Though, the prices are a bit steep, aren't they? More London prices than anything I'd expect here. Yeah, a little pricey, but hey, it’s nice to treat yourself sometimes. Speaking of treating yourself, have you been to the new Primark that opened up? Not yet! Been a bit too busy trying to sort out my TEFL students. It’s a minefield, honestly. One wants to learn only about football, one is obsessed with American sitcoms... Tell me about it! Trying to keep them engaged when their English isn’t exactly fluent is… challenging. But rewarding, you know? Seeing them progress is brilliant. Absolutely. Reminds me of why I did it in the first place. Though, I do miss having a bit more… control over my own time, if I'm honest. This freelance thing is exhausting. It’s always going to be. It’s hard being your own boss. But the flexibility is awesome. Remember when we were younger and dreamt of being completely independent? Oh, God, yes. We were so idealistic. Do you ever think about that stuff now? Like, are we even close to what we thought we'd be? Sometimes. I mean, I have a job I enjoy, I’m living abroad… That’s a pretty big tick in the ‘life goals’ box, isn't it? Though, I do sometimes wonder about settling down and having a family. It's a big decision. And a scary one. You know, it’s funny, my sister was saying how she’s struggling with… well, it's a bit of a long story, but it involves a bit of an addiction problem with her partner. Wow, that’s awful. Is she okay? She’s trying. It's tough. You know, I always thought I'd have it all sorted by now, but life threw a few curveballs, didn’t it? Keeps you wondering who you really are, doesn’t it? Like, are you defined by your choices, or by your circumstances? Deep thoughts over coffee! I know what you mean. It's like you can spend ages trying to craft the perfect identity.

Right, so I was looking at the Dorset Steam Fair website, and it looks amazing! All those vintage engines and stuff. Have you guys got tickets yet? Haven't got around to it yet, love. Been a bit busy sorting out the garden. Should I get them online, or is it alright to pay at the gate? Online is definitely best, Dad. It’s always packed, and if you queue at the gate, you’ll miss most of it. Plus, it's slightly cheaper. I booked ours yesterday. Yeah, Mum's right. And they’ve got a discount for students, which is handy. I’m thinking of going on Saturday, is that the busiest? Saturday’s always the big day. Lots of people. Expect a crush everywhere. Are they still doing that shuttle bus from Bournemouth town centre? My knees aren’t what they used to be. They are, Dad, but it gets  very  crowded. They have a designated area for disabled visitors, though, closer to the entrance, with accessible toilets and parking. We'll definitely make sure you know where that is when we get there. Good shout, Mum. They’ve got a map online too, highlighting all the accessible routes. Speaking of which, it looks like most of the arena’s on fairly level ground, which is good. That’s good news. Being stuck on a slope is a nightmare. You know, property prices around there are absolutely ridiculous these days, aren't they? Saw a little cottage the other day, barely big enough for a cat, going for nearly half a million! Don’t even start, Dad! It’s insane. I was chatting to one of the nurses at work, and she said she’s thinking of moving out of Essex altogether just to get somewhere affordable. It is crazy. I'm lucky enough to be living in halls for uni, so I’m not thinking about buying yet, but it’s worrying for the future. What about Willow? Are we bringing her along to the fair? Oh, Willow’s coming! She adores all the steam engines. Reminds her of me, she says! She’s got you there, Dad. Just be careful she doesn't get trampled. She tends to wander off after butterflies. True. We’ll have to keep a close eye on her. Thinking about moving furniture to make space for Willow's cat tower. It's proving more difficult than I thought.

It’s lovely to see you, Mum! Thirsk looks beautiful in this light. Proper autumnal. It is, isn’t it? Better than that dreadful drizzle we had last week. Honestly, you could barely see across the garden. Thought the roses were going to drown. Roses need a good soak, Gran. Keeps 'em perky. Leave your grandmother alone, Finn. She’s earned the right to complain about the weather. How are you feeling, Mum? Much better, thank you, dear. That little knee niggle has subsided, mostly. Just a bit stiff after that walk this morning. Beautiful it was too, the colours are incredible. Saw a robin, bright as a button. We thought we’d take you out for a nice dinner tonight. Somewhere a bit special, as a treat. I was thinking The Black Swan in Sowerby. Have you been? Oh, ages ago. Lovely place, I remember. They do a smashing rhubarb crumble, don’t they? Although, goodness, I don't think I could manage a full crumble these days. Just a spoonful, perhaps. Rhubarb crumble? Seriously? That’s ancient. I’d rather have pizza. Loads of pepperoni. Finn, show some respect! Your grandmother has impeccable taste. Your dad’s been on about this new artisan cheese shop he found in Northallerton. Apparently, they have a Stilton that will blow your socks off. We could pop in there before dinner. Oh, cheese! Now you're talking. I do love a good Stilton, properly ripe. Though, I heard on Twitter the other day something about a shortage, due to the weather affecting the milk production. Dreadful, isn’t it? Twitter? What even is Twitter? It's just people moaning about stuff, right? It’s…a complicated platform, Finn. Think of it as a digital town square, and also a place to complain about cheese shortages. It’s how your grandmother knows about the important things, Finn. Like the ethical sourcing of our Stilton. Don’t you start, Sarah. It’s just a bit of a giggle, really. Though, I was reading an article about the rise of cottage industries… quite fascinating, you know. All these small businesses popping up, making artisan breads and jams and things. Actually, reminds me of when I was a student and we'd try to make our own jam on a Sunday. Absolute disaster, it was. So sticky. Can we at least watch the football after dinner? There’s a derby match on.

Right, so, the dentist appointment is booked for you two. Next Tuesday, alright? And Irma, you need to remember to keep opening wide! The hygienist gets a bit grumpy if you don’t. But I don't want to! I know, darling, but it's important. And Aaron, you've got your hearing test on Wednesday. Don’t wriggle too much, okay? They need to get a good reading. Will it hurt? No, silly. It won’t hurt. You just have to listen to some sounds. Like when we play those games with the beeps. Can we have Easter chocolate now? Not yet! We’ll have some after dinner. And then maybe a little bit before bed. Don't tell your dad. I want the bunny one! With the caramel inside. You can have the bunny. Irma, are you doing your times tables practice? We need to whip through a few before we go out later. Maths is boring! I know it can be, but it's important for school. Remember we talked about Ashaad and his maths test? Ashaad’s birthday’s next week, isn’t it? Yes, it is. His and Amy's. Birthdays on the same day. It’s quite a coincidence, really. Amy’s getting a scooter! She is! Very lucky girl. You two are getting... well, we'll see. I'm thinking about something Monet-related. You both like his paintings, don’t you? Yes! The water lilies were pretty. And the bridges! Exactly. Right. Okay, dinner time. Any requests? We've got radishes, do you want some? No! Radishes are yucky. Alright, alright, no radishes. I’m making pasta. Do you want tomato or cheese sauce? Cheese! Cheese! Tomato! Oh, for goodness sake! I’ll make both, then. And we need to look at that form for the school trip to the museum... Friday's the deadline, so we need to get it done tonight. It's about the Tudors. Tudors? Were they pirates? Not exactly pirates, darling. They were kings and queens. Think Henry VIII and all his wives! Did they have chocolate? I think  some  of them might have had chocolate, but not the Easter kind. It wasn’t as common back then. Come on, let’s wash our hands, pasta’s almost ready! And then maybe a little bit of Easter chocolate – shhh, don't tell your dad! Oh! And Aaron, remember you wanted to draw Monet’s bridge for your art project?

Oh my god, you're actually here! I can't believe it. It feels like forever. I know! The train was a nightmare, seriously delayed. But I made it! And look at this place, you've actually decorated! Last time I saw you, it was just…beige. Yeah, well, adulthood, right? I tried to add some colour. What do you think? And look at Finn! He’s grown a foot since I last saw him. Finn! Oh, you scruffy sausage! He’s gorgeous. You’ve been spoiling him rotten, haven’t you? He’s practically the size of a small pony. Maybe a little. He does get away with everything. Right, come in, come in. I made pasta carbonara, thought you’d be starving after that train journey. Carbonara? You know me too well. Although, knowing you, it’ll probably be healthier than it looks. All wholewheat pasta and lean bacon, isn't it? Oh, I'm hurt! This is  authentic  carbonara. Cream, egg yolks, guanciale...the works. Though, I did sneak in some extra parmesan. For good measure. You’re terrible. Honestly, though, it smells amazing. How’s everything been, really? You seem...calm. Usually, you're buzzing with stress about deadlines and clients. Work’s been alright, pretty steady. The freelance life, you know? Feast or famine. Finances are...well, they're finances. I’m trying to save for a little holiday, maybe somewhere warm. What about you? How’s the speech and language therapy going? It’s…intense. Really rewarding, but incredibly draining. Adult acute, so you see some pretty serious stuff. But I love it, genuinely. I’m learning so much. And my flatmate, Chloe, is a lifesaver. She actually did the washing up last night – a genuine miracle. Washing up! That’s a victory. I’ve been avoiding it like the plague. It’s piled up so high it's practically a monument to my laziness. Sounds about right. So, are you seeing anyone? Don’t tell me you’re still on that disastrous dating app. Please don't remind me. Bumble is a wasteland of people who only want one thing. No, nothing serious. Just…a lot of coffee dates that go nowhere. What about you? Anyone special? There’s this guy, Ben. From my placement actually. He’s…a nice guy. Really into photography. Photography, huh? Is he one of those guys who only posts black and white landscapes on Instagram?

Honestly, the planning meeting last night was just… baffling. Didn’t stand a chance, did they? Those flats on the green. Absolute eyesore. Dreadful, absolutely dreadful. They said it blended in. Blends in with what? A pile of rubble? The chaps on the panel know nothing. It’s all gone, hasn’t it? That sense of… character. Used to be you knew everyone in town. Now, it’s just… transient. Aye, it’s true. Used to be Manchester had a soul. Now it’s just another financial hub, all glass and steel. No warmth. You remember when we could just pop into the theatre, even if it was sold out? A friendly face at the box office, a couple of returns… Now it's all automated. You need a computer degree just to get a ticket! Precisely! And the NHS... don't even get me started. Back in my teaching days, you practically got the whole of the seaside for free. Sailing, you know. Used to have lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon. Wonderful, eccentric chaps back then. So many perks. Oh, I remember those days! A young dentist, just starting out… you could get a bargain trip to the med - Prague, was it? - for next to nothing. Look at the prices now! Prague's lovely. We went last year. Beautiful. But the beer...heavy! Speaking of things that are lovely, have you heard about Cecilia's plans for the jive night? The barn? Wonderful idea! A converted barn… feels right doesn’t it? Away from all the noise. That barn's been lying empty for ages, hasn’t it? What were they planning to do with it initially? A wine bar? Something like that, I think. Never really took off. This jive night sounds much better. Cecilia is a force of nature. She is! And she's hoping to get some local musicians involved. Trying to 'rebrand' the town, she says. Bring a bit of… buzz. Rebranding… could work. This town has seen better days, you know. Used to be vibrant. The market… thriving. The architecture… proper Victorian. Now, it's just tumbleweed and empty shops. Honestly, it was ruined by the bypass. Drove all the trade straight through. Nobody stops anymore. It needed a bit of attention, that’s true. A few decent shops, a nice café… Some investment in the square. But not those monstrous flats.

Right, so let’s run through this again. We’re looking at leveraging social media, but not in the way everyone else is doing it, right? No endless promotion of our own stuff. Exactly. Less ‘look at me, look at my course,’ more ‘look what’s happening in education, let’s discuss it.’ Building a community. Precisely. A hub. Think of it as a digital staff room for teachers. Somewhere they can share ideas, resources, and frustrations. I like that. A digital staff room. Safer than a real one, probably. Less passive-aggressive post-lunch gossip. True enough. But it’s gotta offer something tangible, beyond just platitudes and vague encouragement. The case studies are key, surely? Absolutely. The moving image stuff is the differentiator. So many people are stuck on static PDFs and worksheets. Short, impactful videos demonstrating effective teaching strategies, analysis of student behaviour…that’s sticky content. And accessible. That’s crucial. We don’t want to design something that only works on the latest Macbook Pro. Simple editing, shareable formats... We need to think about the different devices teachers will be using. Phones, tablets, laptops… they’re often on the move, isn’t it? During breaks, on the train... They may not have the bandwidth for huge files. So, short clips, optimised for mobile. Got it. But the platforms... LinkedIn seems a bit too formal. Instagram feels a bit… frivolous. Facebook groups are busy, but the signal-to-noise ratio can be dreadful. It’s just a constant stream of memes and venting. Not conducive to focused discussion. What about Twitter? Micro-blogging, quick updates, sharing articles… It's a possibility, but it’s so easy to get lost in the noise. And the character limit can be a pain when trying to explain nuanced teaching concepts. Perhaps a combination? Twitter for quick snippets and links to longer discussions on a dedicated forum? That could work. The forum gives us control over the conversation, the moderation… We can build a sense of community in a more deliberate way. Right. And who curates the content initially? I can do some initial research and sharing of case studies, but we need a plan for ongoing content creation. I can start pulling together some resources. I have a ridiculous number of clips and newspaper articles collected over the years. Plus, I know some brilliant teachers I could ask to contribute short videos focusing on specific areas.

The light was incredible on the sea today, wasn't it? That sort of hazy, golden feeling. It was beautiful. Proper postcard stuff. Felt like we should have been taking photos every five steps. I know! But I was too busy just… breathing it in, you know? Felt good to get away from everything for a bit. It did. Needed that. Reminded me of that trip we took to Cornwall, years ago. Remember St Ives? Vaguely. Feels like a lifetime ago, doesn't it? That tiny little café right on the harbour… The one that served the best pasties ever? Absolutely. I think I’m still dreaming of those pasties. Speaking of people we haven’t seen in ages, have you heard anything from Liam and Chloe? Not recently, no. I messaged Chloe a couple of weeks back about that photography exhibition and she said they’re both flat out with work. Liam’s been doing a lot of stuff down in Brighton, apparently. Oh, really? What sort of stuff? Something to do with marine biology, as I understand it. Some kind of research project. Bit above my head, to be honest. Wow, that’s brilliant for him. He always did love the sea. Remember that obsession he had with collecting seashells when we were kids? How could I forget? He'd spend hours on the beach, meticulously sorting them. Thought he was going to discover a new species. He was a character. I wonder if they're thinking about having kids. I’ve no idea. They always seemed quite... independent. Happy with their own company, you know? Yeah, I suppose. It's funny how people change, isn't it? Remember when we were all convinced we’d all be living in a commune by now, brewing our own beer and growing our own vegetables? Oh god, yes! We were so idealistic. I’m glad we didn’t actually go through with that. Imagine us, covered in mud, battling slugs in the garden. Horrifying. Although, a fresh vegetable every now and then does sound appealing. Especially with this weather... reminds me how much I miss being near the beach. Me too. Shall we plan another trip? Somewhere a bit different this time? Maybe Scotland? Scotland sounds amazing. We could go hiking, see some castles... And eat some truly terrible Scottish cuisine. You always find the worst food, don’t you? But it's worth it for the scenery.

Oh my god, that dress! Seriously, who dresses like that in real life? What, the sequined monstrosity? Don’t even get me started. It's so… much. I actually think it’s kind of fun, in a totally over-the-top way. Like, if you were going to a themed party, it could work. A themed party for "What if a disco ball threw up on someone?" Maybe. But daytime? No way. It’s giving me major Yorkshire market stall vibes. True. It’s a bit… trying too hard, isn't it? I mean, the stylist clearly wanted to make a statement, but it's not a good one. It's just… loud. I think it’s a reflection of the wider trends, though, isn't it? Everything’s so maximalist now. Think about the runways – feathers, clashing colours… Yeah, but the runways are supposed to be experimental. This is supposed to be normal people showcasing a look. Bit of a disconnect, innit? I’d rather be in my jeans and a nice jumper, honestly. Reliable. I’ve been eyeing up some tailored trousers at Arket. They look so good, like proper smart but also comfy for working from home. Have you seen them, Liv? Arket, yeah, I’ve had a look. They are good, aren’t they? A bit pricey though, eh? I might have to wait for a sale. Speaking of pricey, I saw a Shearling jacket on ASOS. Tempted but… £200?! Ooh, Shearling! Lovely. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a trench coat. Classic, right? But I'm struggling to find one that fits properly. Everything’s either too long or too boxy. A trench coat is always a good shout. London weather demands it. Have you looked at Warehouse? They often do some decent ones. Warehouse? I'll have a browse. I’m thinking a lighter colour, though. Something I can wear over practically anything. Not the usual beige. I saw some really nice olive green ones online. Quite stylish, don't you think? Practical and chic. Olive green’s fantastic. Goes with everything. And it’s more interesting than beige. Speaking of which, I need to decide what to wear to Sarah’s leaving do next week. It’s at that swanky bar in Shoreditch. Swanky, eh? So, no jeans and a jumper then! Dressy-dressy or dressy-casual? I’m leaning towards dressy-casual.

Look, this is the one I took in Brighton last week. I quite like it, don't you? Oh, that's lovely, darling. Really good composition. You’ve got the light just right. You’re getting really good at photography, you know. Thanks, Mum. It’s just… I get nervous sometimes. Like, what if people hate it? What if it’s rubbish? Oh, sweetheart. Everyone feels like that sometimes, especially when you’re creating something. It’s a vulnerability, isn't it? But you can’t let that stop you. Remember when I started my degree? I was terrified of presenting, absolutely petrified. You were? I can't imagine you being scared of anything. Oh, I was! I used to have nightmares about it. Ended up doing a whole presentation on overcoming stage fright! Irony, isn't it? But I just kept practicing, and eventually, it got a little easier. It’s the same with photography. Keep taking pictures, keep experimenting, and don’t worry about what other people think. Easy for you to say! You didn’t have to show them to everyone on Instagram. You’ve got a point there. But social media is the worst for that. Remember, darling, those people scrolling through, they’re mostly just distracting themselves. They’re not really  seeing  your work. True. So, how was work today? Did Mr. Henderson finally fix the printer? Don’t even mention it! He says he’s ordered the part, but it’s been “on order” for two weeks now. I swear, if I have to manually print another document… Anyway, it’s been a busy day otherwise. Got a new temp starting next week, apparently. Fingers crossed she’s better than the last one. Last one was awful. Kept asking me how to use the stapler. Exactly! This college application stuff stressing you out? A little. I’m thinking about applying for that photography course at Goldsmiths. It’s really competitive though. It is, darling, but you're a brilliant photographer. You should definitely go for it. It’s just like you’ve always wanted to do. Have you been reading that book I gave you, the one on Ansel Adams? Yeah, I've started it. It’s really good, actually. Did you see that comedian, Mitchell, on the telly last night? He was hilarious. I did! I love him. So observational. Makes me laugh so much.

Right then, settle in, settle in. Lovely to see you both. Brought a tin of biscuits, your favourite, Margaret. Oh, Arthur, you shouldn't have! They’re lovely. How are your joints today? Achey. The damp’s got right into ‘em, you know. Luckily the match wasn't rained off though, eh Paul? Not a chance! Beautiful day for it. Norwich played brilliantly, Arthur. Should have scored more, though.
