Should have, should have. Young Sargent’s got a bit of a temper, hasn’t he? Giving away silly fouls. Still, they’ll learn. Did you finish that application form, Arthur? For the garden club? Nearly there, Margaret. Just struggling with the section on ‘Hobbies and Interests.’ What do I put? ‘Watching football and complaining about the damp?’ Doesn't sound very impressive, does it? Put ‘observant of local wildlife.’ You’re always going on about the birds in your garden. That's true. See that nest in the apple tree? Got a pair of robins in there. Little blighters are working hard. Oh, that’s lovely. And the cockerel? Is he still keeping you up all night? Don’t remind me! Sometimes I think he's got a personal vendetta. Wakes me up at four o'clock every morning. Clucking his head off. Drives you bonkers, it does. Can't sleep a wink. Reminds me of a couple of my class last year. Absolute terrors. Couldn’t keep still for a second. Constantly disrupting the others. Oh, children! You get all sorts. Remember little Timmy, Arthur? Used to hide under the sofa every playtime. He did, didn’t he? Such a sweet little lad. Anyway, Paul, how’s the 3D printing going? Did you ever get that model of the cathedral finished? Nearly there. Just needs some final polishing. Thinking of printing one for you, Arthur. A little one for your windowsill. That would be smashing, Paul. Really smashing. Reminds me, I saw that new build over in Willow Road. Dreadful workmanship, it is. Windows don’t line up, brickwork’s all wonky. Honestly, you wonder how they get away with it. It is a disgrace. Developers these days. No pride in their work. Speaking of houses... I was thinking, maybe we should look at downsizing. Downsizing? Margaret, don’t you start! This house has been in my family for generations. I know, I know. But it’s just too much for you now, love.

It’s just…it’s a big change, isn’t it? A huge one. Bringing Elspeth all this way…from New Zealand. It is, love. It is. But it’s wonderful too. After all these years you'll have her close. You’ll see her properly, not just on a screen. I know, I know. It’s just…she’s built a life there. A good one, from what she tells me. A career, friends...a flat she adores. Uprooting all that… People do it, Moira. People move countries all the time. And she’s coming to  you . To find some stability, some family. That's worth a lot. She’ll figure out something new, a fresh start, perhaps? Brighton's not exactly New Zealand, weather-wise, but… No, it isn't, is it? She’ll need a very good coat. And a whole new idea of a summer. We can help with that. We'll show her the best places to walk along the seafront, introduce her to our friends, help her find somewhere to live… I worry about putting too much pressure on her. About it all being…too much. It's easy for you, your pension streams in and you are busy with your students. I've got…well, I’ve got a bit of savings, but it doesn’t stretch as far as it used to. Don’t worry about that. We'll manage. I have some contacts, I can help her look for part-time work. Something to tide her over until she finds something she truly enjoys. And we’ll visit her often, once she’s settled, won’t we? Yes, of course. But what if she misses it? What if she regrets it? Moira, darling, she's a grown woman. She’s made this decision. She wants to be closer to her family and I'm sure she'll settle in well. Brighton's a lovely place. Good theatres, music…the sea… It’s just…I haven't had her close like this since she was a little girl, you know? It's… overwhelming. Exciting, yes, but overwhelming. It's just so different than our weekly video calls. I understand. But think of the Christmases! And birthdays! Actually sharing those moments together, instead of watching grainy videos on a laptop. You’re right. You’re always right. It just feels like…a new chapter.

So, what did you think of the Scottish referendum debate last night? Felt a bit predictable, didn’t it? Predictable is a good word for it. Lots of fireworks, but not much new ground covered. I felt rather sorry for Salmond, you know. Pinned down on those currency questions. Absolutely. Though, I did feel a bit for the ‘Yes’ side generally. The weight of history…it must be something. Anyway, completely different topic – how did the interview go this morning? With Helen? Oh, it was…interesting. She seemed very keen on the modern literary theory stuff, which is encouraging. But she also kept probing about my experience with postgraduate supervision. I’m not entirely sure I convinced her I’m not a complete disaster. You're anything but! You've got years of experience. Did she ask about your methods? Yes, she did. Lots of questions about pastoral care and support. Apparently, the last supervisor they had…well, let's just say their students weren’t exactly showering them with praise. Oh dear. Sounds like a tough legacy to inherit. You’ll be brilliant though, genuinely. You always have the students’ best interests at heart. Thanks, James. Needed to hear that. It’s just… applying for jobs these days feels like an endurance test. All the ‘experience’ boxes you need to tick. Tell me about it. It's terrifying. How's Amelia doing anyway? Still enjoying her pottery classes? She is. Absolutely loves it. She’s actually entered a piece for the local arts fair next month. Can you believe it? A proper pottery exhibition. That’s brilliant! I must pop along and take a look. Is she thinking of doing it professionally? No, no. Not yet. She says it’s just a hobby, but I see the spark in her eyes. Same as her grandfather, always making things. It's wonderful, isn't it? Finding something you're passionate about. I wish I’d stuck with the guitar more. You always said you were going to join a band! Still could, you know. Highly unlikely. My guitar playing is an embarrassment to all who have to listen. Things are a bit hectic here at the moment; the department’s in a bit of a state. Budget cuts looming, you know the story. Yes, sadly. It's the same everywhere, isn’t it? It’s a shame, really. We used to have so much more freedom to…to actually teach.

Right, so, the mousetrap game. I’ve got all the bits. We need to decide on the layout. Do we want it really complicated, or relatively straightforward for the younger ones? Relatively straightforward. Leo will just knock the whole thing over if it’s too fiendish. Remember that time he built a tower of blocks so high, it collapsed and took out the cat? It was a good collapse! The cat was fine. Just grumpy. Though, to be fair, Dad’s towers were always more structurally unsound. Remember that Lego castle you tried to build, Dad? It looked like it was melting. It was an artistic interpretation of a fairytale ruin! Besides, you were the one who bumped the table. Oh, you two. Always at it. Anyway, back to the mousetrap. I think we should keep it simple. A few obstacles, maybe a spinning wheel, definitely a ramp. Good ideas. I was reading about a version they play in America, it’s called "Operation Mouse Trap," but it's much more elaborate. Like, you have to navigate a miniature rollercoaster to reach the cheese. Seriously. A rollercoaster? That’s mad! It sounds amazing though. I’d play that. They do love their elaborate games over there. Remember when we were in New York, and we saw that candy store with over 30 different kinds of gummy bears? Don’t remind me! Leo spent half an hour agonizing over which one to choose, then ate the entire bag. Leo loves candy. It’s just different over there. The scale of everything is different, isn't it? And the children. They seem so…confident. That’s just because they’re used to having everything immediately available, I reckon. They don’t have the same…restraint, perhaps. Like, when I was in New Hampshire, and I asked a kid what his favourite animal was, he just said "horses." No explanation, no context, just "horses" with this air of absolute certainty. That’s brilliant! I remember trying to order a simple cup of tea in a diner, and the waitress looked at me like I was asking for the moon. It had to be Earl Grey, with lemon, and have “just the right amount of milk.” It was ridiculous. American portions are ridiculous too. Remember the pancakes, Mum? The size of dinner plates! They were enormous, yes. But the kids cleared their plates, every single one.

Right, you will not  believe  what I’ve managed to find! Let me guess, another silk scarf? You're going to run out of room in the wardrobe soon. Oh, hush. It's not a scarf. Though, I did see a rather lovely jade green one… No, no, this is better. Look! Okay, you have my attention. What’s the haul? Okay, first, this dress. I know we’ve talked about needing something a bit more… versatile for these conferences, and this is it. It’s breathable, it’s elegant, and I can dress it up or down. That's actually really nice. The colour suits you. Is it the linen you were looking for? It is! Exactly. And the price was… incredible. I swear, the sales here are just insane. Then, I found this. Trousers? You normally shy away from trousers. I know, right? But they're  amazing . They're so comfortable, and they actually flatter my figure - weirdly. They’re made of this really soft cotton blend. I can wear them with a simple tee, or with the dress. It gives me options! You're on a roll then. What else have you got? Just a few little things. This - for layering. And... …a pair of sandals. Sandals? We're in China. It's practically a sauna. I know, I know! But they’re really stylish. They’re leather, very understated, and I’ve been meaning to get some decent sandals for ages. They'll be perfect for the hotter days. They sound palatable no. And, I had to get this. It's just so  me . It’s silk, with this beautiful bird design. It’s not practical, obviously, but it's pretty. You and your little trinkets. It’s lovely, though. So, a dress, trousers, a shirt, sandals, and a ridiculously pretty purse. Not a bad afternoon's shopping. Not bad at all! I’m feeling rather pleased with myself, actually. Now, help me try this dress on, will you? I want your expert opinion. And then… maybe we should go for some dumplings? Reward shopping, you know. Lead the way. Though, be warned, I'm a tough critic when it comes to dresses. Dumplings sound amazing though. Of course you are! The entertainment value for me alone is worth the effort. Come on! Let's go! Hopefully, that captures the conversation style and context well! Let me know if you’d like any adjustments. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

Well, that was a feed, wasn’t it? Absolutely demolished that chicken. It was lovely, Mark. Thanks for cooking. Though I think I might be comatose for the rest of the evening. Och, it was grand, dear. Absolutely scrumptious, it was. Better than anything I managed to cobble together in my day. Though I did make a mean crumble once… It was brilliant, Dad. The best dinner ever. Did you see that tackle in the first half though? Oh, are we going back to the rugby already, Oisin? You were glued to the screen. It was amazing! Ireland played so well. Did you see Kearney’s run? I did, I did. A bit scrappy in the second half, though. A few missed passes. But overall, a solid performance. Definitely. Though I didn't fully understand all the offside rules. Still, plenty of excitement. I've never been much of a rugby fan myself. All that running about… So much shouting. But it seems to be important to the boys, doesn’t it? It’s practically a religion in this country, Nana. Can I go and sign the birthday cards now, Dad? Auntie Sarah's and Uncle Tom's. Of course, son. They're on the table by the window. Nearly Oisin’s birthday tomorrow, isn’t it? It's flying past. It is! And we need to get that cake ordered, don’t we. Are you doing one this year, Mark? Yeah, I was thinking about ordering one from that bakery down the road. The one with all the fancy decorations. Can it have dinosaurs on it? Please, Dad? We’ll see. Dinosaurs are always a possibility. Now, go on and sign the cards. Oisin, dear, are you tired? You've been very energetic today. A little bit. Maybe a bath and then off to bed? Yeah. Right then. When you're finished signing those, maybe we can go out and have a look at the stars. Clear sky tonight. Really? Can we, Dad? Absolutely. Nana, are you up for a quick star-gazing expedition? Oh, I haven’t done that in years! My wee eyes aren’t what they used to be, but I’d love to. As long as it’s not too chilly. I'll get Oisin settled in and then join you both. What are we arranging for later this evening, Mark? Rest of it? Well, Sarah and Tom are coming over around eight, so we just need to tidy up a bit and make sure there’s enough wine.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from seeing your sister’s baby shower photos. She looks so tiny next to that giant pram! Isn't it mad? And she’s already having second thoughts about the pastel blue theme. Apparently, little Leo is apparently destined for a life of pink sequins and tutus. Right, rebel already! It’s massively overwhelming isn’t it? I’m still not sure if I ever want to have kids. The sheer amount of stuff… Tell me about it. My mum's already offering me her old baby monitor. It’s…vintage. I think it still uses cassette tapes. Oh god! And are you moving next month then, the flat in Norwich? Yeah, the contract's signed. It's so much bigger than my current place, a proper kitchen, you know? Though I’m terrified of the whole unpacking and decorating thing. I can help with that, definitely. We just need to coordinate. And you know, if you’re short on furniture, I've got that armchair I was saying about, the velvet one? You can have it. Seriously? That would be amazing! I didn’t want to ask, it’s so gorgeous. It’ll fit perfectly in the living room. No worries! And are you going to need any clothes for the baby? I’ve got loads of nearly-new stuff from when my niece was smaller. Loads that never got used. That's so thoughtful! Leo will be too small for most of it at the moment, but it would be brilliant to put away for when he’s bigger. Saves on buying everything new, doesn't it? Absolutely. Speaking of saving, my brother's trying to learn Spanish again - he's convinced he'll be fluent within six months. It's hilarious. Oh, bless him. He's been saying that since he was twelve. What's he using? Duolingo again? Yep. And he's complaining about the owl being patronising. Apparently, it said his pronunciation of “Hola” was "an insult to the Spanish language”. Oh, that’s rich! My sister's trying to learn Italian. She keeps getting frustrated with the genders of the nouns. The genders! Don’t even get me started. It's completely arbitrary, isn't it? Why is ‘tavolo’ masculine and ‘sedia’ feminine? Exactly! Makes absolutely no sense. She’s already given up on memorising them, just guessing. I don’t blame her.

Right, so, who's got the good tobacco tonight? Anyone smuggled any in? Nah, man, customs would have a field day with me. Got a pouch of Blackwoods though, decent stuff. You want a roll? Yeah, cheers. You know, I was thinking about that documentary we watched about accents. It’s mad how much regional variation there still is, even around here. Tell me about it. My nan still sounds like she fell off the back of a lorry from Cyprus. Proper old-school. Cyprus accent's pretty unique, isn’t it? Difficult to pin down. My students always ask me if I have an accent. I try to tell them, "I've lived in Bedford my whole life mate, this  is  my accent!" You sound pretty standard to me. Though, admit it, you’ve picked up a few phrases teaching English to foreigners. Guilty. I’ve started saying things like "Essentially, what I'm trying to convey is..." which sounds ridiculously pompous. You sound like a politician. Speaking of which, did you see that article about Lord Ashworth trying to buy up all the farmland around here? Seriously? What’s he planning, a giant pheasant farm? Probably some sort of luxury eco-village. Honestly, the amount of land these guys own... makes you wonder how they even got it in the first place. It's a bit scary, isn't it? You hear stories about people being squeezed off their land. You've got to look after yourself. That’s why I started that self-defence class. Good on you! Keeps you sharp. Speaking of sharp, anyone fancy a game of Settlers of Catan? I brought my expansion pack. Ooh, Catan! I'm in. But you’re going down, Tom. I’ve been practicing. We’ll see about that! I’ve got strategies you wouldn't believe. By the way, did you manage to sell that old acoustic guitar on eBay? Nearly! Had a couple of bids, but they disappeared. Think someone was messing me about. Shame. You could have used the money for some new gardening tools. How’s the weeding going? A nightmare. Mrs. Higgins’ roses are taking over everything. She keeps complaining, but she won't let me use any proper weed killer. Says it's cruel to the bees. Fair enough. You’ve got to be mindful. Speaking of mindful... you wouldn’t believe the amount of kale someone tried to sell me at the market today.

Right, so I’m thinking chicken and veg tonight. Simple, easy, and we need something relatively quick. This whole situation with the car is stressing me out. Tell me about it. The commute's already bad enough without the added anxiety of… you know. What did the mechanic say exactly? Basically, the exhaust system is shot, and it needs a proper overhaul. Not just a patch-up job. He quoted me something ridiculous. Like, nearly eight hundred pounds. Eight hundred! Seriously? That's insane. Are you sure he wasn't trying to rip you off? Did you get a second opinion? I thought about it, but honestly, I don't have the time. Work's a nightmare as it is, and spending another day off getting quotes… I just can't. Plus, I trust Liam – he seems straight. Liam is a good mechanic, yeah. Though he does like to use slightly... fancy parts. Have you considered just getting a used exhaust? It’d be significantly cheaper, wouldn't it? I looked into it. Some places online have used ones for around 250, but the shipping is a pain, and I’m worried about the quality. You know, it might fail again in six months. That's fair. True, then you're back to square one. But eight hundred… Ugh. We need to seriously factor this into our savings plan. Are we still on track for that weekend in Brighton? I don’t know. Brighton is looking increasingly unlikely. It would be a shame – I was really looking forward to it. And finding a replacement car doesn’t seem likely either. I’d rather fix what I’ve got unless something awful happens. We could cut back on eating out for a few months, right? And maybe dial back the subscription boxes? Remember how much we were moaning about how much we were spending on those. You’re right. It's just… it feels like everything costs so much lately. Every time I turn around, there's another bill. Insurance, petrol, now this… I know, me too. But we're good at managing, aren't we? We’ll figure it out. Maybe I’ll do a bit of freelance work on the side to boost our savings. Gets a bit dull, but needs must. Honestly, that would be amazing, love. You’re a lifesaver. Okay, so chicken and veg it is. While I'm chopping these peppers, can you get the olive oil out for me?

Right then, everyone settled in? Tea’s on in a bit, but thought I'd check if anyone wanted anything first. Yorkshire pudding's in the oven, should be ready after tea. Could I have a fizzy drink, Mum? Please? And what are you watching later? Lemonade, coming right up. And we were thinking of watching that nature programme about badgers. You still interested, Finn? Yeah, alright. Badgers are alright. Badgers, eh? Reminds me of when your grandfather – Arthur – chased one into the kitchen once. Thought it was a fox! Nearly had a heart attack. Aye, he did! A right commotion it were. Cats all scatterin', Arthur yelling... absolute mayhem. Oh, Dad, you always did exaggerate. It was just a little badger, and he didn't yell, he gently asked it to leave. Gently asked it to leave? I’m hearing things now, lass. He was waving a rolled-up newspaper! Nearly hit the cat. Grandad, you’re making things up! I am not! Your mother knows I’m right. She had to mend poor Mittens’ ear after that. True, Mittens did have a slightly wonky ear for a bit. But honestly, Dad, the newspaper story’s a bit far-fetched. Anyway, are you two alright? You seem a bit quiet. We're fine, dear. Just reminiscing. It does wonders for the memory, you know. Keeps the cobwebs off. Aye. Though sometimes I wish the cobwebs stayed put. Less to remember! Mum, can you show me where the router is? My internet’s been playing up all morning and I need to send off an essay for college. It’s in the cupboard under the stairs, love. Just be careful you don’t trip over the vacuum cleaner. I need to move it later. Okay, ta. That young man’s got his nose stuck in a computer all day long. Fresh air’s what he needs. Not staring at a screen. He’s working his way through A-levels, Mum. It's part of it, isn’t it? Aye, but back in my day… we played outside! Climbing trees, building dens… didn’t need computers. You could swear a tree had more character than that screen he’s always glued to. Right, well, don’t let’s turn this into a lecture. How about I put the kettle on? Are you both alright for sugar and milk with your tea? Just a splash of milk for me, love.

Right, so, pirates! Who wants to tell me what pirates  do ? They say "Arrr!" and find treasure! They… they fight! That’s right! They fight, and they sail the seas on big, scary ships looking for treasure. We're reading  Treasure Island  this week at school, remember? Do you want to draw some pirate ships, you two? Yes! With lots of gold! And a parrot! Can I draw a cannon? Absolutely! Big cannons. Now, are you two hungry? I’m making cheese sandwiches. Cheese! Yes, please! Can I have cucumber too? Of course, darling. Now, we’ve got a lot happening this month, haven't we? Shakespeare week at school next week, and then, remember, we're going to Stratford! Stratford! To see a play! Exactly! We’ll see  A Midsummer Night’s Dream . It’s all about fairies and magic. Bit like pirates, really – full of adventure. Will there be swords? Maybe! It’s Shakespeare, so there might be battles. And then, the circus workshop! Remember? In a  real  circus ring! With clowns! And acrobats! Yes! We're learning to juggle and balance and do some simple magic tricks. Speaking of which, I think we need to practice our "abracadabra!" before we go. Abracadabra! Abracadabra! Make a carrot disappear! Right, let’s not try  that  one just yet! We're also getting those Easter pictures back from school tomorrow, aren't we? I wonder what you drew, you two. I drew a bunny! With lots and lots of chocolate eggs! I drew a dragon breathing fire! A dragon! That's brilliant. We might even try some stop-motion animation with Lego over the weekend. You could make a little pirate movie! A pirate Lego movie? With cannons and treasure? Absolutely! It’s just like making a flipbook, but with Lego. We take a picture, move the Lego a little bit, take another picture. Then when we play them back quickly, it looks like the Lego is moving on its own. Magic! Can we make the bunny hop? We can definitely make your bunny hop! It’s going to be a very busy month. Now, eat your sandwiches, pirates and dragons! Then we can draw some treasure maps. Sound good? Yes! Yes! Arrr! Excellent! Arrr indeed! . . . . .. . . . . .. . . .. .. . . .. .. .. .. .. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .. . . .. .. . . .. . .. .. . .. . . ..H.HH.H.

Right, everyone’s got a glass, I hope? It's a nice little Pinot Grigio – not too fussy. Lovely, thanks, Penelope. Always appreciate a good pour. So, you were saying, Richard, about Saudi Arabia… it sounds quite the experience. It was, in its own peculiar way. I’ve told you snippets, of course, but the culture shock was monumental initially. The rules, the restrictions… Aye, the alcohol situation, particularly. Though I’m sure you’ve all heard my stories about attempting to smuggle some brandy into Cyprus… disaster. Oh, do tell that again, Bernard! It was hilarious. The poor constable! Right, right. It was back in the seventies. I was attempting to sail – very ambitiously, mind you – from Jeddah to Cyprus. A small craft, let's say... not built for such a journey. Anyway, Customs caught wind of my little scheme, and I ended up being held. Accused of… well, breaching numerous maritime laws, I think. And the brandy, of course. The brandy! Hidden in a false bottom of a watertight compartment. Clever, I thought at the time. Turns out, not so clever when you're being interrogated by a very stern officer. Eventually, they let me go, but it wasn't a pleasant experience. Gave up sailing after that, really. Extraordinary! And what was it like teaching out there, Richard? Dealing with cultural differences in the classroom? It was a challenge, definitely. And a privilege, in a way. The students were eager to learn, but you had to be incredibly sensitive to their traditions and beliefs. The most frustrating thing was the lack of discussion sometimes. They’d just memorize and repeat. No questioning, no debate. It was like teaching to a very sophisticated recording device. I can imagine. You had to tread very carefully. Did you find it difficult not having… well, the usual freedoms? It was a trade-off. You got access to a fascinating culture, a generous salary… but you definitely missed certain things. A glass of wine with friends, for example. It was all rather… dry. I remember holidaying in France once. Took a suitcase full of wine. Needed it for the conversation, you see! Now  that  is a story I’d like to hear. Though, speaking of magazines, I once had a peculiar situation with a dental journal and a particularly strong gin and tonic. Bernard, not another one! Well, I was at a conference in Barcelona, networking, you know.

Honestly, the bathroom renovation is driving me mad. I thought it would be a straightforward job, but it's been a saga. The tilers were three days late, and the plumber apparently doesn’t believe in level surfaces. Oh, you've had that then, haven’t you? It’s always like that, isn't it? You think, “A new bathroom, how nice!”, and then it’s weeks of chaos and dust. At least you’re getting it done. Remember when I tried to re-tile the downstairs toilet? Don't remind me. What was that, Liam? Nothing. Just saying, it was a disaster. You had tiles everywhere. It was! I gave up after about an hour and ended up putting up a floral wallpaper. It was… an aesthetic choice. Right. Well, at least it's livable. Speaking of horrors, how's school going, Liam? Still avoiding eye contact with your maths teacher? He's got a weird face. A weird face? That's a valid reason to struggle with algebra, apparently. Have you thought about work experience? It's coming up already. I said I don’t want to do any. They said I have to. Now, now, don't be like that, love. It's a good chance to see what you  don’t  want to do when you leave school. I did a week at a solicitors when I was your age, and I knew instantly I’d rather stack shelves. Exactly! It’s about exploring opportunities. Maybe something with computers? You're always on that phone. Ugh, Mum. People are always on their phones. It’s normal. Well, it's not normal to ignore your auntie when she’s trying to tell you about her cruise! You were practically glued to that screen when I was showing you the photos. Sorry, Auntie Val. The internet was buffering. Buffering. Right. That’s a perfectly legitimate excuse. Anyway, I was thinking of booking something for next summer, you two. Somewhere warm. Somewhere with a beach. Where have you two been dreaming of going? Somewhere with Wi-Fi. Cheeky. I've been looking at some places in Cornwall. Haven't been there for years. Beautiful coastline, nice beaches... Oh, Cornwall sounds lovely. It'd be good to get away, wouldn’t it? And then I could rope someone into babysitting – maybe Emily? She's getting pretty good at refereeing those football matches your cousin plays.

This scenery’s unreal, isn’t it? Like, something out of a film. It is lovely, pet. Absolutely lovely. Could get used to this sort of thing. Peaceful. Peaceful until Dad starts ranting about the sat nav again. I’m not ranting! It’s just…unreliable. It told me to go down a one-track lane. A one-track lane in Istria! You were ever so dramatic, John. It’s a holiday. Relax a bit. Speaking of dramatic, did you see that chef on that cooking show last night? The one with the truffles? Ugh, those truffle programmes are so staged. All that faffing about with the dogs, and then he’s pretending he found it himself. He’s a professional, son. It's entertainment. And those truffles… apparently they're insane money. Better than gold, practically. Reminds me of the caviar situation when I was working over in New York. New York? Did you ever fancy living over there, Mum? Oh, I did for a bit. Thought about it when John was doing that big project, but then…well, this is home, isn't it? Close to everyone. Speaking of home, did you see Man U lost yesterday? Don’t remind me. Absolutely dreadful. They need a new manager. And maybe a few new players. Honestly, at this rate… Right, let’s not discuss football. I’m starving. Are we stopping for lunch soon? I’m craving that pasta with wild mushrooms we had in that little place last year. We are, love. John's been researching some amazing restaurants. Apparently, there’s one near Rovinj that does incredible seafood. And they have a rather impressive wine list. Though I do wish some people in this car wouldn't constantly blow bubbles. What? It’s just a bit of chewing gum, Dad. It helps with travelling. Gets the ears popping. Don’t fuss, John. It's just a bit of gum. Honestly, you’re like my grandad. Grandad used to smoke like a chimney. Remember that? Always had a fag hanging out his mouth. Don't talk about your grandfather's habits, please. It's bad enough that the younger generation is addicted to... well, this . Oh, come on. It’s just a bit of fun. And anyway... did you read that article about stem cell research? Apparently, it’s getting really promising. Oh, I saw something about that. Incredible, isn't it?

So, has anyone else noticed how ridiculously quiet it is in here today? Usually there's a proper buzz. Yeah, it is strangely peaceful. Must be a slow day for the press. Good for our lunch break, though, right? No battling for space. Definitely. I was dreading it would be packed. Did you hear anything back about that proposal I put in for the student engagement project? No, haven’t heard a peep. Fingers crossed, though. It sounds really worthwhile. The learning analytics side is particularly interesting. Yeah, the tech integration side would be a real win for them. I’m still trying to wrap my head around all the platform options. What did you think about that webinar on AI language modelling? Found it a bit heavy-going, to be honest. Loads of jargon, very little practical application. Felt a little too focused on the theoretical and not enough on… well, on how we can actually  use  it for our research. I thought the speaker was brilliant, actually. Pretty inspiring to think about how we can be harnessing these tools. It felt like a proper step into the future. Though I admit, I may have dozed off for about five minutes. Fair enough. All those algorithms can be pretty soporific! Speaking of the future… did you see that article in the Guardian about the new generative AI writing tool? The one that can write academic papers? It’s terrifying and fascinating in equal measure. I can’t imagine the implications for plagiarism detection. Yeah, and what about job security for researchers and editors? Pretty scary if it gets good enough to replace us all. I don’t think it’ll replace anyone, just change the game. It’ll require a whole new set of skills. Adapt or become obsolete, I guess. Digital marketing's the same, constantly evolving. It’s exhausting keeping up, to be honest. I can imagine! My role is a bit more stable, thankfully. Though I do worry about the ethics of using these AI tools – the potential for bias and misinformation is huge. We need to be really careful about how we train them. Totally. It’s a responsibility, isn't it? I was chatting to Sarah from HR the other day, and she was saying they're thinking about bringing in mandatory ethics training for everyone. That’s a good idea, actually. Should be compulsory for all AI developers, too.

Right then, just a couple of hours to Magda’s, should be alright. Traffic's surprisingly light for a Sunday afternoon, isn't it? Yeah, it is. I was expecting a complete gridlock closer to the border. Are you sure about this route though? It looks like a bit of a back road on the map. Perfectly safe, darling. Magda insisted. Said it’s much prettier than the motorway, and she knows the area like the back of her hand. Plus, it avoids all those awful toll booths. Less hassle. Fair enough. Less hassle is always welcome. Though I do like seeing a bit of the landscape. Did you manage to sort out the insurance for the campervan properly, then? Yes, dear, all sorted. Had a bit of a palaver with them, trying to convince them I wasn't planning a round-the-world trip. They kept asking about mileage and destinations. Eventually, I told them I was only driving to Tarnow and back. Seemed to satisfy them. Good, good. Wouldn’t want any unexpected bills landing on our doorsteps. So, has Magda said anything about what she’s got planned for us? Is she cooking? She’s promised pierogi. Loads and loads of pierogi. Apparently, she's been practicing a new recipe all week. And she said she's got some homemade nalewka – plum brandy. Strong stuff, that. Oh lovely! I’m looking forward to that. I’m starting to miss Polish cooking, you know? Being away from it for so long. I know, isn't it? Proper comfort food. She was saying she’s got a few other Polish friends coming over too, so it should be a lively evening. Should we stop for petrol before we get into Tarnow? Yeah, let’s do. I’m not sure how much we’ve got left. Don’t fancy running out miles from Magda's. Where did you fill up last? Was that in Krakow, before we crossed the border? Seems like ages ago now. Probably was. Right, just keep an eye out for a signpost. I'll keep navigating. Are you sure you're comfortable with this campervan? I know you're not used to driving these things. Honestly, it’s not so bad. A bit bigger than a car, that’s all. And it’s got a lovely view from the driver's seat. Just need to remember not to take corners too quickly!

Honestly, the kit’s a disaster. Like,  really  a disaster. What were they thinking? Yeah, saw it on Twitter earlier. Pretty grim. Though, I reckon you're always gonna complain about a new strip, aren't you? Aye, but this is a special level of grim. It looks like something a five-year-old designed using felt tips. Are they even trying? It's like they've just thrown a load of colours at a wall. Seems like it. Did you see that article about Puma pulling out of that sponsorship deal with the German team? Apparently, the designs weren't hitting the mark. No! Really? That's mad. You'd think with the money they've got, they could employ, I don't know, a  designer ? It's not that hard, is it? Just make it look…respectable. This thing…it just looks cheap. Well, it's a marketing game, isn't it? Got to be edgy, got to be different...though aiming for edgy and landing on “a toddler’s drawing” is a bit of a miss. Exactly! And the sponsor’s logo… it’s massive! It's practically taking over the whole shirt. You can barely see the team colours. Fair point. All those sports companies fighting over that space, trying to get maximum visibility. It's just everything’s oversized and garish these days, isn't it? Remember when the strips were… well, simpler? Proper classic designs that have stood the test of time. Deffo. Less is often more, yeah. Speaking of oversized and garish... fancy a McDonald's after this? I'm feeling a Big Mac. You and your McDonald’s. It’s all those processed ingredients swimming in grease. But... Alright, alright. But you're getting the fries. And maybe a McFlurry. Deal. Gotta fuel the football despair somehow, right? And I want to see your reaction to the new kit plastered all over Instagram. You’re terrible. But yeah, fine. Let's go. Just need to grab my coat. And maybe some indigestion tablets, just in case. Smart thinking. Let’s get going. And I'm getting extra salt on those fries. Don’t judge me. You always do. Always. It's my weakness! It’s the one thing I love the most. You know that! Yes, I’m very aware. Let’s go then! Enjoy your Big Mac and potatoey goodness!

Honestly, it’s just… relentless. Every single day. What's up, love? Another issue with the housing benefit? It's not just the housing benefit. It’s  everything . The gas bill came through today, it’s ludicrous! Like, £280! How am I supposed to afford that on Jobseeker's Allowance? It’s ridiculous. Yeah, it's tough all round. Are you putting the heating on much? I try not to. I’m practically living in a cardigan and hat. But the kids are freezing! And they need to study. Little Leo’s got that history test next week. It’s just…unfair. They grow up quick, don't they? Remember when you were worrying about what breakfast cereal to buy, now you're calculating whether you can afford a hot shower. Exactly! And the others... you know, moaning about needing a new telly. They’re going to spend their inheritance, aren’t they? While I’m rationing electricity and praying the bailiffs don't knock. Don’t let it wind you up too much. They'll always find something to complain about. Remember that argument we had about the telly back in '98. True, but it’s hard not to feel completely resentful. And then there was the other day at the supermarket… some bloke gave me such a look. What happened? I was queuing and he just stared at me. Then he said, “You know, you shouldn't be claiming benefits when you’re clearly capable.” It was awful. I had to walk out. Absolute cheek. Who does he think he is? Probably spending all his money on takeaways and lottery tickets. Don’t listen to him. You’re working your butt off. I know, but it just piles on the pressure. And then you’ve got trying to entertain the kids with nothing. I was thinking of taking them to Margate one weekend, but the train fares are extortionate. Margate? That's ages. Remember those day trips Mum used to take us in the summer? That little cafe overlooking the sea… Exactly! Now it costs a fortune. And parking! It's madness. Speaking of money, I actually placed a bid on eBay last night. For a George Foreman grill. A George Foreman? What for? It's supposed to be really economical for cooking. Less electricity than the oven. And the kids like their grilled chicken. It’s a win-win, right?

Honestly, the traffic getting in was horrendous. Sat nav took me completely the wrong way. Ended up on a single-track road, dodging tractors. Oh, bless. That’s Peterborough for you. Everything's got one lane these days. More houses than roads seems to be. Used to be able to drive anywhere, you know. Proper roads. Not this nonsense. The council...never did anything right. I know, right? It added on nearly half an hour to my journey. And then there was that awful news report about that plane crash. Makes you think, doesn't it? Awful, isn't it? Terrible. Such a shock. I saw it on the news while I was hoovering. Can’t escape it, can you? Plane crash... Reminds me of when young Michael, your brother, went to Spain. Nearly didn't come back. Terrible storm, flight delayed for hours. Oh, I remember. Mum was frantic. Did you get much done here today, Sarah? Just the basics really. Kitchen’s gleaming though! Had a bit of a clear-out in the pantry. Found some ancient tins of beans. Don’t think they’re fit for consumption anymore. Oh, good find. I’ll bin them for you. I need to pop to that convenience store down the road later, pick up some milk and biscuits. They've got really good deals on the chocolate digestives, you know. Convenience stores these days. Everything’s so processed. Remember when we used to get our groceries from Farmer Giles’ shop? Proper butter, proper cheese… Oh, Gran, you and your Farmer Giles! He probably sold more dodgy sausages than good ones, if I remember correctly. Nonsense. He was a good man. He knew his produce. Unlike these supermarkets, everything looks the same and tastes the same. True. Supermarkets are just… convenient. Sometimes you need that convenience. I’ve been feeling run ragged at work this week. Dealing with Johnson and his ridiculous targets… I swear, he’s trying to wear me down. You're a tough cookie, you are. You'll outlast him. Did you see my hands today? Dreadful. Got a new wart on my thumb. Absolutely blooming awful. Wart? Oh dear. Do you know what causes them? It’s dreadful, isn’t it? Nobody knows! They just appear! It’s awful. Might have to try some of that freeze spray, I suppose. Never quite works, though. My doctor said to soak it in warm water and file it down gently.

Honestly, I’m so stressed about the biology test on Friday. Mrs. Davies is being brutal this year. Tell me about it! I spent all of lunchtime today just trying to memorise the different types of cells. It's not sticking. I know! And she’s obsessed with genotypes and phenotypes. Like, who even  uses  that in real life? Exactly! It’s so abstract. Did you see Chloe crying in the toilets today? She's panicking about it too. Yeah, I saw her. Poor thing. Honestly, the whole year group is stressing. I was chatting to Liam in art and he said he's barely touched his English homework because he's so focused on bio. Art's been a lifesaver, actually. Mrs. Peterson is brilliant. She just lets you experiment and it’s a proper chill-out. I'm really enjoying the portrait project. Yeah, she’s good. I’m trying to do a charcoal drawing of my cat, but it keeps looking like a grumpy badger. Oh no! Send me a picture. Maybe I can give you some tips. I’m doing a watercolour of the river in Linton. It’s really relaxing. I’ll do that. What do you think about the trainee teachers? They’re kind of…weird, aren’t they? So weird! Miss Davies seems nice enough, but Mr. Harrison just stares. Like, really stares. It’s unsettling. I know! And he keeps calling me 'Miss'. Even when I tell him my name's Emily, he still says 'Miss'. It's so bizarre. It is! And remember when he tried to explain photosynthesis using a banana? Oh my god! He was so serious! It was the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever seen. Honestly, the school is just a constant stream of oddness. Speaking of odd…have you heard about what happened in English? No, what? Apparently, James threw a paper aeroplane during Mr. Thompson’s lecture. And it landed  right  in his coffee. No way! I can’t believe it! James is such a troublemaker. I know, right? Mr. Thompson was furious. He just stood there, dripping coffee everywhere, and didn't say a word. Oh, stop! I’m picturing it! That’s brilliant. But also, I kind of feel sorry for Mr. Thompson. He looked so tired today. Yeah, he does. Maybe he needs a holiday. Or a shield to protect him from flying paper aeroplanes.

So, Mum, you were saying about your friend’s daughter joining Scientology? What’s that even like? Is it like The Matrix, but, you know, real? It's… complicated, Liam. It’s not really like The Matrix, though I can see why you'd draw that comparison, in a way. It’s a belief system, a self-help thing, but it’s got some… unusual practices. And a lot of money involved. Money? Like how much? A  lot . Courses, auditing… it’s very expensive. Apparently, it’s all about learning about your ‘thetan’ – it’s a spiritual being, they say, that’s trapped in your body. And through their methods, you can supposedly unlock it. It sounds a bit bonkers, doesn't it? Yes, darling, you’re right, it is a bit mad! Your Auntie Grainne used to work at a convent, remember? She said the nuns there were very strict, but at least they didn’t believe in spiritual beings trapped in bodies. It was all about prayer and service. True, but they didn't have cool stuff like unlocking spiritual beings, did they? Doesn't it seem a bit… weird to be paying people to tell you about your soul? That's what I thought! And the recruitment tactics... Grainne says they can be quite intense. They get you in, make you feel special, and then slowly start asking for money. It’s like they've got you hooked before you realize what's happening. So, is it like a cult then? Like, are they brainwashing people? That's a strong word, Liam. I don’t think brainwashing is fair. It’s more… persuasive. They try to isolate you from your friends and family who might express concerns. They focus on the positives, the potential for ‘clear’ – that's what they call people who've completed their courses. So, your friend's daughter... is she okay? She seems happy enough, I suppose. She's very enthusiastic about it all. But her mum is worried. She says her friends are dropping off, and she's spending all her free time – and a lot of her money – on Scientology. Maybe she just really likes it. Maybe. But her mum is worried about how much control they have over her. It's something to keep an eye on, I think. It’s just… I worry about people getting taken advantage of. Especially when it’s something as important as their beliefs.

Right, so are you sure this is the quickest way? I swear we’ve been driving for ages. Pretty sure. The sat nav says so. Although, you know how these things are… sometimes they get a bit confused. It's trying to be clever. Clever isn’t always best when you’re trying to get somewhere, is it? Remember that time it sent us down that tiny lane to get to Grandma’s? Oh god, yes! We nearly got stuck. She was furious – said we were showing off. Exactly! And she was right. Anyway, so, dancing lessons. How did they go? Did you finally master the waltz? Don’t remind me. It was a disaster. I’m utterly hopeless. Apparently, I have "two left feet." The instructor actually said that. Typical. You’re brilliant with engines, but a dancing disaster. It's just the universe’s way of balancing things. Tell me about it. I’m half tempted to just stick to engineering. Speaking of which, I’ve got this absolute nightmare of an assignment due next week. Old English… honestly! Who even uses it anymore? It's fascinating though, isn’t it? The roots of so much of our language. Think about it – "wendan" meaning "to turn," and it’s at the root of “window”... See? That's the kind of thing I have to analyse for hours. It's mind-numbing. I'd rather be calculating stress tolerances on a bridge. You’ll get through it. And speaking of tedious things, did you see what happened with that celebrity on  LoveFilm ? The one who…? Oh, you mean Bethany Bloom? The scandal! Apparently, she’s being ageist in her interviews. Getting all the criticism on social media. It’s a bit sad, isn't it? It is. I think people are quicker to judge now. It’s all so performative online. Remember how much simpler things were before Instagram? Absolutely. I miss Myspace, in a weird way. You could actually customise your page and pick your favourite song to autoplay. Oh god, the auto-playing music! Still, at least it was a bit more… personal. Right, are we near the junction yet? I swear I saw a sign for Little Puddleton a while back. Nearly. Just another couple of miles. So, how's your friend, Chloe? Heard she's doing something with that charity for animal rescue? Yeah, she’s really passionate about it.

Honestly, I’m starting to think Centre Parcs is just a glorified campsite. Now, don’t be daft, love. It's more than that! Heated pools, restaurants… it's a bit of luxury. Remember that one in Woburn? The kids loved it. Yeah, but the queues for the Aqua Sana were mental. You’re all having a go at Center Parcs. It’s a well-oiled machine, provides a reliable family break. Though I’d argue a proper Italian vineyard offers a more authentic experience. Authentic experiences are great, Dad, but I’m ready for a bit of pampering after exams. Plus, Ben wants to go canoeing again. And the pool! And the rapids! You two just want to splash around. He’s got the swimming thing in his blood, hasn't he? Like his granddad. Speaking of blood, did anyone fancy that olive oil we bought at that little market in Rovinj yesterday? That stuff was incredible. Oh my god, yes! We need to get more. Want to stop at another market this afternoon? Let’s see where we are first. I’ve got that little book, haven't I? Says there’s a good one in Porec. Can we get some wine too? Of course, you can get some wine, you cheeky monkey. Just don't drink it all before dinner! There's a lovely restaurant in Porec too. Remember that one we went to years ago? Little terrace overlooking the harbour… fantastic seafood. Honestly, this whole area is stunning. I saw the most gorgeous succulents in a nursery earlier. All these spiky little plants. It’s inspiring for my botanical art project. Art, eh? Still at it, are you? You’ll be painting truffles next. Maybe! I'm thinking of doing a series on Croatian flora. Can we watch Sons of Anarchy tonight? I missed the last episode. Must we? It's a bit violent, isn't it? Let him watch it, John. He's nearly a man now. Besides, it’s a good way to kill time while your mum’s painting her succulents. Hey! It's important artistic expression. Whatever you say. So, are we sticking to the main roads or tackling some of these smaller, more scenic routes? My GPS is suggesting a detour through some vineyards… Scenic sounds good. As long as it’s not too twisty. My nerves can only take so much, you know.

Right so, are we actually gonna play something or are we just gonna sit here staring at each other? Alright, alright, give us a minute. I’m still buffering. Honestly, this internet in Doncaster is a joke. Tell me about it! Took me twenty minutes just to load TikTok earlier. You'd think Yorkshire broadband would be better. My connection’s fine, actually. Though, honestly, I’m not even sure what we're playing anymore. What was it, Liam’s weird game suggestion again? Don't remind me. Something about being a… a sentient banana in space. Oh god, not that. No way. Absolutely not. Liam  really  thinks it's going to be the next big thing. He's been recording gameplay for weeks, promises us it’s going to be “groundbreakingly hilarious”. Groundbreakingly bizarre, more like. Remember his last gaming obsession? The one with the sentient broccoli? Oh my god, I've blocked that out completely. The broccoli was horrifying. So, what else is anyone been up to? Besides suffering through Liam's gaming endeavors? Not much. Mum’s been on about me applying for jobs again. Like, I told her, I’m taking a gap year. Tell me about it. My mum keeps asking when I’m going to start thinking about internships. She’s convinced I’m going to end up living under her roof forever. I have an interview next week for a part-time job in town. It's just shelf-stacking at Boots, but needs must, yeah? Oh, good for you! That’s brilliant. You'll be brilliant at it. Are you nervous? A tiny bit. I mean, it's Boots. How hard can it be? Although, I did see someone yell at a poor girl for putting the wrong shampoo on the shelf the other day. It was mortifying. People are scary. Anyway, about this banana game... Has anyone even seen it? Like,  really  seen any of Liam’s recordings? He sent me a link. I watched about three minutes. It mostly involved the banana rolling into walls. It wasn’t as groundbreaking as he claimed. Honestly, I think he’s just getting bored of his usual games and trying to find something new. He's got way too much time on his hands. Maybe we should suggest something else. Like, a proper co-op game? Something we can actually all play at the same time?

Right, I'm absolutely starving. This morning's brew wasn't enough to keep me going. Tell me about it! Had a rough commute, so skipped breakfast entirely. Thinking about grabbing something from the café down the hall. I packed a sandwich, thankfully. Turns out, dealing with those new trainees all morning burns a  lot  of energy. A sandwich, eh? What sort? Something decent or just a soggy cheese one? Surprisingly decent. Chicken and pesto. They’ve actually upped their game a bit. Ooh, that sounds good. I'm torn between a jacket potato and a panini. Decisions, decisions… You can't go wrong with a jacket potato. Can’t beat a good cheese and beans. Classic. It is. Though I did see they've got a pulled pork panini on the menu. Tempting. Pulled pork? Right, that’s settled then. Pulled pork for me! You’re tempting me now! I might have to abandon the jacket potato after all. They do a pretty decent chilli too, if you're feeling something a bit warmer. Bit spicy though. Spicy isn’t really my thing. I’ll stick with the savory, smoky goodness of pulled pork. Honestly, I'm craving something with a bit of spice. Maybe I'll risk it. Just a warning, it's not a gentle warmth. It’s a proper kick. We should probably get a move on before the queue gets too long. It’s always madness around lunchtime. You’re right. Let's head down then. Pulled pork or chilli, here I come! After you two. I’ll just finish this last bit of research for the presentation. Gotta keep earning my chicken and pesto. Fair enough! See you back up here then. Foot race to the counter? You're on! Don't hurt yourselves! And bring me back a menu just in case. Would be a shame to miss out. :D. Will do! Come on! Let's go. Honestly! You two. Always with the drama. :P. It's a serious matter - pulled pork !. It is! And not to be trifled with! Okay okay. Go, go. I will keep the presentation safe. Last one buys the coffee! Yep! Go! Go! Go! Hmph. Those youngsters. . At least there are decent sandwiches here. Thank goodness for that. :D. ::End::. Hopefully, that is satisfactory. Any follow-up requirements? . . . Would you like me to continue the conversation or perhaps generate a different scene?

Right, so, the big question – are we actually going to  use  this social media stuff for the library, or is this just another initiative that'll fizzle out? Good question, Dave. I think it's inevitable, really. The students are all on it, the public expect it. It seems a bit daft  not  to be present. But… using it  well  is the trick, isn’t it? Not just posting random book covers. Exactly! I’ve seen so many libraries floundering with it. All very earnest, tagging things like "Read this book! It’s good for you!" Nobody wants a lecture from the library, do they? No, and I’m not kidding, I saw one yesterday that was seriously pushing a book on Victorian botany. With emojis. It was… grim. Oh, bless. Emojis and Victorian botany. A recipe for disaster. I was thinking maybe short, fun videos? Like, a little tour of a particularly interesting section, or a quick “shelfie” showcasing new arrivals. I like that! Something lighthearted. We could do a series – "Shelfie of the Week." See what students are actually reading. Not just what the curriculum dictates. I’ve got some surprising stuff popping up on the returns trolley lately. Like what? Don’t tell me someone’s returning a manual on extreme ferret grooming again. Worse, Dave. Historical romance. Very popular, apparently. See! Useful information for our social media strategy right there. Gotta give the people what they want. And humor, definitely. Sarah’s got some amazing memes, doesn’t she? Sarah does, she’s a menace. Though, I’m still wary. I saw a joke go viral – something about librarians being secretly ninjas hiding behind bookshelves. Mortifying. Well, it got people talking, didn’t it? That’s the point, surely? Building a brand, getting attention. Though, maybe let's steer clear of the ninja angle. Unless we start offering self-defense classes alongside book recommendations. That would be a selling point. I tell you what, have you seen that meme where the librarian is arguing with a patron about the Dewey Decimal System in a completely dramatic way? Oh god, yes! The passive-aggressive sighing. Absolutely brilliant. I'll send you the link. It's glorious. So, what platform are we thinking? TikTok seemed like a disaster, but something a bit quicker than Facebook… Instagram’s good for visuals, aye. Quick, easy to post, reaches a broad demographic.

Right then, Sarah, thanks for coming down. Bit of a trek for you, I know, from Stratford. Hope the M25 wasn't a nightmare? It was surprisingly alright, actually. A little slow around Heathrow, but nothing major. Thanks for having me, David. This is all very exciting. Aye, exciting and a bit daunting, to be honest. So, let’s get down to it. The tape – the initial presentation to the Trust – is looming. We need to nail this. I’ve had a good look over your draft business case, solid stuff, but I really want to refine our rationale for Tunbridge Wells. Absolutely. I agree. The demographics are obviously favourable, the need is demonstrable, but we need to really hammer home  why  here, beyond just ticking those boxes. We've got that report from the CCG, highlighting the gaps in local palliative care... Right. And we need to really lean into that. The consultation process too. I’ve been having a few conversations with local councillors, and there’s a definite nervousness about increased traffic, and some concerns about impact on the green belt. Need to address those head-on, don't we? Definitely. We need a very proactive communication strategy. Maybe some open forums, site visits? And importantly, showcasing the benefits – the jobs it will create, the support it will offer the community… Good, good. What about the aesthetics of the building itself? I've been looking at some renderings, but I'm not entirely sold. It can't look like a hospital, you know? Has to be welcoming, peaceful… I agree completely. We need to incorporate natural light, create tranquil gardens. I was thinking something reminiscent of a country house, really, to alleviate any institutional feeling. We could involve some landscape architects who specialise in therapeutic gardens. That’s a powerful image. We could also mention the need for close collaboration with existing local health services. St. Augustine's, for example. Building on what they do, rather than competing. And obviously, the relationship with the hospices too - ensuring we complement their services and don’t overlap unnecessarily. Absolutely crucial. We need to emphasize a joined-up approach. I’ve been doing some preliminary research into the use of estate agents - do you think it would be more appropriate to look for land independently of them? The fees can be quite steep. That’s a fair point. Let’s look into that.

Right, where were we? Oh, this photo of Chloe at Ascot. Remember how excited she was? Absolutely. She was practically vibrating with excitement. That hat was… something else, wasn't it? A bit much, even for Ascot. A bit much is an understatement, Dad. It looked like a bird had built a nest on her head. But she loved it, and that’s what mattered. She did. And look at Uncle Arthur trying to look dignified in that ridiculous waistcoat. He always did try to dress the part. Never quite managed it though, did he? Honestly, he looks like he's going to a fancy dress party. So, Mum, how’s the risotto coming along? Smells amazing. Nearly ready. Just need to add the parmesan. Did you hear back from that agency about the interview, darling? Yeah, finally! I have an interview next Tuesday for the senior copywriter role at Bloom Creative. Oh, that’s brilliant! That’s a really good company. Well done, love. Sounds like a proper step up. Are you worried? A little bit. It’s a big responsibility. But the pay is better and the location is great too. It’s only a short commute. You’ll be fantastic. You’re so talented. Just be yourself, talk them through your process, and highlight your work on the Greenleaf campaign. That was amazing, that campaign. Thanks, Mum. Feeling a bit more confident now. Speaking of campaigns, did you see that ridiculous phone accessory Sarah’s got? The one with the little duck that pops out? Oh, that! Yes, I saw it. Absolute madness. She’s obsessed with those things. Remember when she had the one with the little flashing lights. Oh, goodness! It was epilepsy-inducing! Honestly, some people. I’m thinking about getting a case with a little bulldog on it. Just to annoy everyone. You’d be perfect for that. Right, risotto’s ready! Everyone, dig in. That smells wonderful, love. Say, have you been looking into that family history thing you mentioned recently? Did you find anything interesting? I did actually! I traced one branch back to a sailor who served on a clipper ship in the 1880s. Apparently, he ended up in Australia and started a sheep farm. It's incredible. Wow! That’s amazing! You should frame it and make a little family tree. I might just do that. It’s so fascinating to think about where we all came from, isn’t it?

Right, so we’re actually doing this then? You’re not going to chicken out and watch something tame like a rom-com? No, no, I'm game. You promised me a good scare, didn't you? Just... please, nothing  too  jumpy. My heart can only take so much. Aye, I’ll try and be considerate. But you asked for scary, didn't you? Are you thinking anything in particular? I was looking at ‘The Babadook’ actually. ‘The Babadook’? Oh, I’ve heard of that! Isn’t it supposed to be really psychological? Like, disturbing more than jumpy? Yeah, it is. It’s proper creepy, innit? Gets under your skin. There's jump scares, but mostly it's just… unsettling. That sounds a bit more my speed, actually, than something with hordes of zombies. I had a nightmare after ‘28 Days Later’ for a week. A whole week. Ooh, that was relentless. Didn’t like that one much myself. So, 'Babadook' then? Or shall I look at something else? I was also thinking about 'Hereditary'. ‘Hereditary’... I've seen snippets online. That looked…intense. Like,  really  intense. Is it properly bleak? Aye, it is proper bleak. Loads of disturbing imagery. It’s got good reviews, though, if you’re into that kind of thing. Trust me, it'll stick with you. Hmm. I’m not sure. I think ‘The Babadook’ is the safer bet, for now. Less chance of needing therapy afterwards. Fair enough. Right, let me find it then. Fancy some popcorn? I’ve got loads of those weird caramel ones you like. Oh, yes please! Those are brilliant. And do you want me to dim the lights? Proper scary cinema vibe. Aye, dim the lights and get the blankets. It’s gonna get proper chilly in here, I reckon. And hopefully a bit spooky too. Just promise me you won't scream too much. I'll try my best. But no promises. Prepare to comfort me if the Babadook gets me. Deal. Right, let's do this. Prepare to be spooked! I'm not sure I am ready for this... Rubbish get over it. Ready? Let's do it! It is starting! Ooh, it already looks creepy. Tell me when you want to skip it, aye? I don't think I will. Right, here we go.  quietly  Lots of stress going on. . . . Okay now I am freaked out.

Right, that’s the washing finished. Are you all settled for bed, Dad? Nearly, love. Just finishing up my crossword. Seems a bit lighter than usual tonight. Could be. I got that new iPad set up for you today. Did you manage to turn it on? Oh yes, lovely thing. A bit fiddly, I’ll admit. All these little buttons… But I managed to look at the BBC news. Are you sure it’s not going to run out of battery? It’ll last ages, Dad. It charges really quickly too. I set up a few email addresses for you, remember? So you can reply to your cousins. Yes, yes. Evelyn’s been sending lovely pictures of the roses in her garden. Though, I still don't understand why she uses that WhatsApp thing. So impersonal. I know, right? It's all the younger generation use. Anyway, I was thinking, we should look at that armchair again for the living room. The one we saw online. The grey one? The one that looked a little like my old Chesterfield? Yes! It’s on Airbnb too, apparently. They do a delivery service. It’d make a real difference to the room. Delivery... Are you worried about them scratching the floor? I'll be here to supervise. I’ll put down some blankets. It's a good deal online, you know. Cheaper than going to that furniture place in Plymouth. Well, we do need to do something about that chair. The springs are poking through again. It's like sitting on a bed of nails sometimes. Exactly! Speaking of which, fancy a takeaway pizza on Saturday? Amy and Tom could join us if they're free. Pizza sounds delightful. Their tomato soup is lovely too. Though, I still think that ordering online is a bit risky, you never quite know what you're getting. It's convenient though, isn't it? And they're always spot on with the delivery time. Right, well, I'm just going to quickly tidy up downstairs. Don't want to be tripping over things in the dark. Good girl. You take care. And don't stay up too late yourself, love. I won't. Night, Dad. Sleep well. Good night, dear. And thank you for the iPad. It’s a real treat. Just wishing I knew how to order a new crossword online now. We'll sort it out tomorrow, Dad.

So, have you got through “The Scottish Isles” yet then, Hamish? I was thinking about it last night, that map alone is worth the price of the book. Nearly, Alistair. Nearly. I got bogged down a bit in the Orkney section, honestly. All those standing stones, all those ancient sites, it's just… a lot to absorb. Takes me right back to that trip we had back in ’09, doesn't it? Does it ever! Remember trying to find the Ring of Brodgar in that torrential rain? I’m still convinced we were following the wrong directions and ended up in somebody's sheep field. Absolutely. And the wind! It was trying to blow us clean off the cliff at Skara Brae. I've never had to wrestle with a guidebook so hard in my life. But worth it, wasn’t it? Absolutely. Though, I'd argue Skye still holds the top spot for me. That Cuillin range, just breathtaking. Have you ever been hiking up there? A few years back, with Fiona. It was brutal, honestly. We thought we were prepared, all the right gear and everything, but the terrain… ferocious. I remember slipping on some scree and nearly taking Fiona out with me. Thankfully, I managed to grab onto a heather bush. You always were a graceful one. I can picture it now – you, flailing like a startled heron, clinging to the heather. Very funny. But seriously, it reinforced my respect for the Highlands. It’s not somewhere you can just wander around in flip-flops and expect to be fine. It demands a certain level of reverence and preparation. Absolutely. Speaking of travel, have you started planning anything for next year? I was thinking about getting down to Cornwall, to see the Eden Project and maybe do some coastal walking. Cornwall, eh? Tempting. I've been flicking through some travel magazines lately, and Iceland keeps popping up. The landscapes look absolutely otherworldly. All that volcanic activity, the glaciers… Iceland! That’s ambitious. A bit colder than Cornwall, perhaps. But the Northern Lights… you can’t argue with that. It's been on my list for years. Have you read that travelogue by Paul Murton? "Land of Fire and Ice"? I have! Brilliant, wasn't it? Really captured the raw, almost alien feel of the place. Makes you want to just pack a bag and go. Though, I'd need to do a lot more research on the best time to go to maximise the chances of seeing the aurora.

So, have you sent off the application then, love? For that architectural firm? Yeah, Mum, just this morning. Felt a bit rushed, honestly. Rushed? Why? You’ve had ages to work on it, haven't you? I know, but I spent all last week finishing up that freelance project, and then I’ve been trying to sort out this whole… flat situation. Right, right. The one near Shoreditch? How's that going? It’s…complicated. The landlord's being a nightmare, wants to double the rent. I'm trying to see if I can find a guarantor. Oh, darling, that’s awful. Don’t let him pressure you. There are plenty of lovely flats in London. You just need to find a good one. Anyway, back to the application. Did you get the portfolio sorted? Yeah, I think so. I spent hours last night just going through it, tweaking things. I just worry it's not... wow enough, you know? Everyone's portfolios are so amazing these days. Don’t be silly. You’re an incredibly talented architect. Remember that award you won at uni? That was brilliant! Yeah, but that was uni. This is… different. This is a proper job. Being good at university doesn’t mean you can’t be brilliant in the real world, love. And you  are  brilliant. Did you include the community centre design? That was your best work, in my opinion. I did, yes. I was a bit nervous about it, though. It’s quite different from the other stuff they showcase, a bit more… practical. Practical is good! They’re a company that prides itself on social responsibility, aren’t they? Their website mentioned sustainable designs and community engagement. Exactly! That’s why I thought it would fit, but… I don’t know. Maybe I should have included more of the sleek, modern stuff. Nonsense. They want someone who can be creative and who can think about the impact their designs have on people. Your community centre design showed that. Did you tailor your cover letter to them specifically? Mention their recent work on the eco-housing project? Yeah, I did. I read quite a lot about them. Tried to show I’d done my research. Good, good. That’s important. Now, about that interview… are you anticipating anything tricky? I’m terrified they’ll ask me about… about something technical I haven't prepared for.

Lovely to see you, Patricia. It's been far too long. How's young David getting on? He’s good, Arthur, very good. Just finished his apprenticeship, actually. A carpenter now, you know. Solid, reliable lad. Though, he's got his head full of these youngsters' ideas about politics these days… Politics! Don't get me started. Bunch of lot they are, the lot of ‘em. All promises and no substance. Just like they always have been. You’re telling me, George. Been saying that for fifty years, haven’t you? Still haven't convinced anyone otherwise, though. George, dear, play nice. Arthur’s just saying hello. Hello indeed. Just saying, you know. Things were better back in my day. Stronger communities, people looked after each other. That’s always the way, isn't it? Easier to remember the good bits, naturally. Though I do miss the days when you could buy a decent cup of tea for a tuppence. Oh, don’t remind me about prices! Everything's gone up, hasn’t it? And these houses... ridiculous. David’s been looking, you know, for a little place of his own. Can't find anything he can afford that isn’t falling apart. Aye, that’s the trouble. It's a disgrace, really. All these foreign investors buying up property and leaving young families nowhere to go. Should have a law. Foreigners! That’s the root of it all, you know. Should put a stop to it. George, honestly! You and your... views. Now, George, Patricia’s right. Can't blame everyone, can we? Though, I do think a cap on foreign ownership wouldn’t go amiss. Remember when they built that new estate out on the ring road? All those overpriced boxes, nobody could afford ‘em. Remember when a Morris Minor was a decent car? That’s what I remember. Reliable. You knew where you stood with a Morris Minor. These modern things… all computers and gadgets. Can’t fix a flat tyre! You’d have us all back in the Stone Age, George. Though, I must admit, I do miss the simpler times. Less noise, less… everything. Not everything. Wouldn't trade my mobile phone for a carrier pigeon, not a chance. Keeps me in touch with the grandkids. Though they’re all glued to those screens, same as the rest of ‘em. They are, aren’t they? Little William just turned eight.

Right, so I was thinking about the old boiler room conversion… it’s still looking pretty bleak in there. We really need to get that sorted, don’t we? It's just empty space at the moment. Could be a really good little art studio or something. Yeah, definitely. I walked past it earlier, and it's just…echoing. We need to think about how we can market that space too, though. Who would be interested in renting it? Are we targeting artists, yoga instructors, something else? I was thinking artists initially. Brixton's got a good creative scene. But yoga… that could work too. We’d need to look at the flooring though, wouldn’t we? Bit cold and hard as it is. Yeah, definitely. And what about storage? Are we going to offer storage alongside renting the space? Lots of people in Brixton are desperate for it. Good point. We could, absolutely. That'll generate extra income. Speaking of income, have you chased up Mrs. Davies about that outstanding payment for the community hall hire? It's been overdue for weeks. I’ll do that first thing tomorrow, yeah. Bit tricky to get hold of her, isn't she? Always seems to be flitting about. Right, speaking of flitting, did you see those pigeons nesting on the fire escape again? Don’t remind me! I nearly tripped over a pigeon feather yesterday. Maintenance needs to have a word about that. It’s a fire hazard, isn't it? Absolutely. Health and safety first, eh? We need to get that sorted before someone gets hurt. Also, I've noticed the seating area outside is getting a bit tired. The cushions are fading, and some of the chairs are wobbly. Should we start looking at new furniture? Perhaps something a bit more weatherproof? We should. It's the first impression people get when they come here. I’ve got a contact at ‘Urban Outdoors’ - they do lovely sustainable furniture. A bit pricey, though. Worth looking into, I reckon. It’ll improve the overall vibe. What about holiday cover for next month? I’m thinking of taking a week off in mid-July. Oh, brilliant! Need to do that! I can cover some of it. Sarah's offered to help too, so we should be fine. Just need to confirm with her. Great. And is Mark still reliable to cover the evening shifts?

Right, who wants seconds? This beef stew’s genuinely incredible, I’m chuffed with how it turned out. Oh, absolutely! It’s proper comfort food. Could eat this every day. Sounds about right coming from you, Sarah. You’d eat your weight in anything remotely resembling a casserole. Hey! There's a certain refined taste to a well-made stew, Rhys. It’s not just about stuffing my face. Leave her be, Rhys. It’s delicious. Did you use that red wine I brought, Tom? You did! Best decision you’ve made all weekend. Really deepened the flavour. Thanks, Gwion. Lovely, lovely. Though I do wonder, Tom, did you put any… shallots? I can’t abide a stew with too many shallots, they overpower everything. A couple, Dai. Just for a bit of sweetness. Nothing too aggressive, I promise. You know me, subtlety is key. Subtle for a chef, maybe! Mine were practically swimming in them last time! You’re exaggerating, Mum. It was fine. No, I'm not! Remember, everyone kept picking them out! I think there were a few. But honestly, this is fantastic, Tom. Seriously good. Glad you all like it. I was experimenting with some new herbs. Little bit of rosemary, a hint of thyme… See? Subtle! Trying to be. What about dessert? I managed to grab some gorgeous local apples at the market this morning. Thinking apple crumble maybe? Ooh, yes please! With proper custard? Custard’s a must. And maybe a scoop of that vanilla ice cream Sarah picked up? Good shout! Though I might fight Gareth for the last of it. You and your ice cream, Sarah! You're like a kid. Hey! It's a grown-up dessert. Don’t knock it till you’ve tried it. Especially when it’s served with Tom's amazing crumble. Well, you’re all keeping me amused. It's good to have a laugh, isn't it? Being together. Especially after… well, after everything. It is. It really is. A lovely few days. Thank you all for a chance to get away. No problem, Nan. Glad you could make it. So, apple crumble it is? Who wants to help me peel the apples? I'll do it. Anything to escape Gareth's relentless teasing. He’s just jealous you'll be getting the best apple bits. Okay, okay, settle down you two! Let’s just eat dessert and enjoy the peace.

Honestly, I'm still buzzing from that weekend in Manchester. Did you see the Northern Quarter? It's just…  vibrant . Yeah, it was pretty good. Bit too… alternative for my usual taste, maybe? But definitely interesting. All those murals. See! And the music scene. We need to get Liam up there, he'd absolutely thrive. He would, wouldn't he? He needs to get out of his comfort zone a bit. Speaking of which, have you heard from Chloe and Ben? Are they still planning on doing that road trip to Edinburgh? Last I heard, yeah. Ben’s been obsessively planning every pit stop like it’s the Dakar Rally. Apparently, he's found the perfect chip shop in Matlock.  Laughs  Classic Ben. Can’t leave a holiday without comprehensive research on regional delicacies. I saw an advert the other day for that new Italian place on Streatham High Road. They’re doing a two-for-one deal on Tuesdays. Streatham? You’re finally branching out from your Hampstead haunts, are you? Hey, a man needs variety! Besides, my mum’s been badgering me to try it. She swears the pasta is as good as her Nonna used to make. Your mum’s Italian, isn’t she? Honestly, your childhood sounded amazing – all those Sunday roasts and homemade pasta. It was pretty good, yeah. Though I wouldn't say my driving skills are owing to that. Trying to parallel park in London is a whole other skill set. Speaking of cars, did you see that new electric SUV ad? The one with the ridiculously posh couple driving through the countryside? Oh my god, yeah! The one where they’re pretending to be farmers? It was so cringey. Felt completely disconnected from reality. Totally. Like, who actually lives like that? Who drives a £60,000 car down a muddy track? Exactly. It just felt… patronising. I saw a much better ad the other day, that one for the streaming service. With the families arguing over the remote? Oh yeah, the relatable one! I can see why they ran with that. You know what I've been obsessed with lately? That film soundtrack – the one from  Everything Everywhere All at Once . It's completely bonkers, but brilliant. Oh my god, yes! That film was incredible. Michelle Yeoh was on fire. I’ve got it on repeat, honestly. Keeps me sane on the bus.

This is lovely, actually. Thank you for offering. It's just nice to sit down for a minute. Harston is so peaceful, isn’t it? It is, isn't it? Much quieter than Cambridge these days. So, you mentioned on the phone, you’ve been having a bit of a time with your mum? A bit of a time is an understatement. She’s…well, she’s not doing well. They’ve scheduled her for another scan next week. I’m dreading it. Oh, I’m so sorry to hear that. It’s awful when it drags on like this. My Uncle Arthur… he passed away last month. Sudden heart attack. Knocked the whole family sideways. Oh, goodness, I’m so incredibly sorry. That’s just…awful. So unexpected. I can barely imagine. How are your dad and sisters coping? Dad’s trying to be strong, you know how he is. Keeps saying, "He lived a good life, a full life." But I can see it’s taking its toll. My youngest sister, Chloe, she’s a mess. Just…a complete and utter mess. Crying all the time, barely eating. Typical Chloe, really. Always so outwardly emotional. It’s different with everyone, isn’t it? My brother, David, he's the stoic one. Puts on this brave face, but I know he’s hurting terribly. It’s the quiet ones, I find, who are the hardest to know how they’re really feeling. Absolutely.
