It’s just… the funeral, that’s looming. We’re trying to organise it, but it’s proving difficult. So many opinions, you know? Aunt Margaret wants a gospel choir - Arthur  hated  gospel choirs! And Cousin Kevin insists on a slideshow of embarrassing childhood photos. Oh, dear. It sounds… chaotic. It always is, isn’t it? Trying to please everyone. My mum's always wanted a small, intimate affair, but my brother insists on inviting every distant relative he's ever met. It’s the same here. It’s just… exhausting. And the food! Everyone keeps asking what we’re serving. I said I didn't want anything too fancy. Just simple things, sandwiches, cake, you know? Keeps costs down. Practical. That's sensible. These days, everything is so expensive. I’ve been trying to cut down on things, on my food even. Trying that new juice cleanse everyone’s talking about - the one with the green algae.

Right, that was a lovely meal. Thanks, love. Didn’t realise you were feeling quite so ambitious tonight. Wanted to impress. And test out the new oven. Seems to work a treat! It was really good, Dad. Thanks! Yeah, brilliant, Mr. Lee. So, operation work experience - how did everyone get on this week? Alex, you were at the garage, weren’t you? Yeah, it was alright. Colin, the mechanic, showed me how to change a tyre. Pretty straightforward once you get the hang of it. Nearly cross-threaded the bolts though. Nearly broke the car. Nearly broke the car! Sounds like a promising career. Nah, Colin spotted it. He's alright. Did some oil checks too, learned a bit about engines. Good, good. Practical skills are brilliant. And Sam, what about you? How was the office? It was… okay. Filing. Lots of filing. And answering the phone. Really boring. Oh, I'm sorry, love. Not the most exciting start. No, it wasn't. Mrs. Higgins kept telling me off for breathing too loudly. Breathing too loudly? Seriously? Yeah! Apparently, it was distracting her. Oh, that's ridiculous! It wouldn't be my cup of tea. Maybe you need to talk to your mentor about shadowing someone more interesting. I might do that. I’d rather be doing something with computers, like Alex. Speaking of shadowing, I had a rather interesting meeting today. Big discussion about project restructuring. Lots of moving parts, lots of opinions. Sounds stressful. It is, occasionally. But I managed to get my point across, which is always a win. Got a verbal agreement for the team to get extra training. That's brilliant! Well done, love. You're always so good at navigating those situations. It's a knack, I suppose. Speaking of navigating, anyone thinking about a ski trip this year? Yeah! Where are we going? I was looking at Austria. Good pistes, decent value. Can we go to France instead? They've got better slopes. We’ll see. Depends on the budget. We need to start saving. So, Did you manage to get that vintage Bordeaux you were after? Yes! Found a bottle at that little wine merchant in Kenilworth. A 1982. Oh, you spoil us! That’s a dinner for a special occasion. It is. Rest of it is for me. Can I have a sip? Only if you help with the dishes. Deal! I'll load the dishwasher!

Right, have a look at this one. Found it rummaging through the old boxes. Remember this trip to Norfolk Wildlife Trust? Oh my goodness! Yes! Remember how determined you were to get a good badger photo? Determined is one word for it. Obsessed is probably more accurate. I must have spent five hours crouched in that hide. Five hours! My knees were killing me. And all you got was that blurry bit of a backside disappearing into a bush. Hey! It  was  a badger! Technically. And it's proof I was there. Artistic blur, I like to call it. Captures the essence of the badger’s retreat. You and your artistic licenses. Honestly, you were like a wildlife ninja, creeping around with your camera. Did you ever find out why they kept running off just as you pressed the shutter? I think, and this is just a theory, they could sense my desperation. Badgers are psychic, you know. Or maybe it was that ridiculous camouflage jacket I was wearing. It was supposed to be woodland, but it mostly just looked like a lime green explosion. It clashed terribly with the reeds. You looked like you belonged in a particularly vibrant field of lettuce. Very funny. Anyway, look at this one. From that photography workshop in Japan. Remember Kyoto? The bamboo forest? Oh, Kyoto! Absolutely stunning. That was an incredible trip. The light filtering through the bamboo... it was magical. Did you finally manage to master your aperture settings? Let’s not talk about aperture settings. It was a learning curve. A very steep learning curve. I think I took more blurry pictures of ramen than anything else. You did! Every bowl of noodles was a masterpiece of unintentional motion blur. But this one... this one's actually pretty good. The symmetry is lovely. You captured the stillness of the forest perfectly. Yeah, I was happy with that one. I was trying to channel some ancient Japanese Zen photographer. Probably just got lucky, to be honest. Maybe. Or maybe you were just concentrating on not tripping over a root. Remember that near-disaster with the koi carp pond? Don't remind me. I almost ended up swimming with the koi. Luckily, you grabbed my arm just in time. You were a real-life life guard that day. Someone had to be. You'd have become a legend – “The Man Who Almost Drowned in a Koi Pond in Kyoto.”

Seriously though, Ireland was mental. Like, absolutely mental. Didn’t realize how much green there  actually  was. Tell me about it! I’m still sifting sand out of my swimsuit. Sand? What happened? Skinny dipping. Don't judge. Oh, you did! That's classic. Reminds me of the time we went to Byron Bay... Right? And the landscape was just... overwhelming. Lush. I feel like I need to write a poem about it. Oh god, not another one. Last time it was about a pigeon. Hey! That was a profound meditation on urban wildlife. It was three lines, Liam. Artistic license! Anyway, what about you, Jess? How’s the café? Absolutely rammed, I bet. It’s okay. Busy. Trying to figure out how to deal with these suppliers, they’re ripping me off. It’s exhausting. You know, sometimes I just think… zombie apocalypse. Then at least I wouldn’t have to worry about invoices. Good attitude. I hear ya though. Dealing with tourists who don’t know how to use a coffee machine… it’s a special kind of torture. Speaking of torture, Harry's snoring last night... woof. Truly biblical. He was exhausted, you lot. Blame the Guinness. It was like a freight train. Honestly, I was debating moving into the spare room. You should. I’ve got that amazing Claudia Roden cookbook with all the Jewish food recipes. I could cook a feast for you there. Jewish food? I’m in. Always happy to broaden the palate. You wouldn't be convinced to come for a week in Australia, right? Tropical climate. Tropical plates. Australia sounds lovely. But… I'm kinda on a baking kick at the moment. Trying to perfect my babka. A babka! Seriously? Those are so tricky. That’s what makes them exciting. Got some amazing tips from a chef I spoke to the other day. Turns out the secret is... Don't tell us! We want to be surprised. Hold on, speaking of amazing recipes, have you guys ever had chopped liver? Seriously delicious. My grandma used to make it. She had this  amazing  recipe. It started with... So, Jewish jokes? Anyone got any good Jewish jokes? Okay, don’t laugh… Why did the Jewish baker break up with the bagel? I don’t know, why? Because he was feeling crumby! Oh, mate. That was terrible. You're trying, though! I've been trying to find a good photo app.

Honestly, the amount of peanuts they give you here is ridiculous. I’ve already eaten a small mountain. It’s a Cambridge pub tradition, isn't it? Free peanuts. Can’t complain. Though I am starting to feel a bit…silenty. Silently? Is that even a word? I’m making it up. It’s the peanut-induced state of being. You know, full of shells and a vague sense of impending doom. Very poetic. So, are you still obsessed with that new strategy game? You were going on about it last week. Massively. "Empires of Aethelgard." It's brilliantly complicated. You're building a kingdom, managing resources, negotiating treaties… the AI is brutal. I lost a major battle last night because I underestimated the Ork reinforcements. Orks? Sounds a bit Warcraft, doesn’t it? It does, loosely. But the historical elements are surprisingly well-integrated. It’s got this whole feudal setting inspired by the Norman Conquest, but with fantastical creatures. That’s a weird combination. So, no exciting theme park trips planned then, given your obsession? Sadly no. My thesis demands all my waking hours. Though I did see they’re building a new roller coaster at Alton Towers. The “Leviathan's Fury.” Apparently, it's got a backwards loop and drops you from like, 80 metres. Ooh, that does sound thrilling. Maybe once I’ve finished this research project, we can actually do something fun. I’m drowning in data analysis at the moment. Border security, can you believe? Looking at patterns of crossings - it's fascinating, but also exhausting. That sounds incredibly intense. Border security? Bit far removed from empires and orks, isn't it? You’d be surprised. There’s surprisingly complex modelling involved. Trying to predict patterns, assessing risk… it’s all about data driven insights to create policy. Wow. That’s… actually really interesting. Far more palatable than splitting hairs over thesis methodology, anyway. I’ve been arguing over the correct interpretation of post-structuralist readings of medieval romances for the last three hours. Sounds… delightful. Did you see that new Wes Anderson film? “The Astounding Adventures of Archibald Abernathy”? I did! Absolutely gorgeous visuals, as always. But the plot was a bit… meandering, wasn't it? Beautiful, but meandering. Exactly! It felt like he was more interested in the aesthetic than the actual story. Still, I enjoyed it. Needed a bit of whimsical escapism after dealing with… well, border crossings.

Mmm, this is lovely, isn’t it? Proper chippy chips. You can’t beat it. It is! Much better than the soggy ones we get back home. Though, to be fair, takeaways have declined everywhere, haven’t they? They have. So, you're actually going to give rowing a proper go then? I thought it was just a fleeting fancy. Well, I’m determined! It seemed like a good way to enjoy the river, get some exercise…and frankly, I’m tired of being on my bum all day marking essays and teaching grammar. Understandable! You’ll need some serious waterproofs though, won’t you? Cambridge in November… not exactly balmy. That's what I've been looking at. Proper cagoules, decent waterproof trousers... I was horrified at the price, though! Apparently, you need specialist gear. Did you ever kayak much? A little, ages ago. A holiday in Scotland. It was brilliant, but freezing! Reminded me of that time I tried to go camping in the Lake District and ended up soaked to the bone within an hour. Never again! Oh, I know that feeling. Speaking of family holidays, I finally met my cousin, Emily. Remember I told you about her? Of course! The one your dad barely spoke about? Yes! It was… strange, actually. We looked so much alike, but we come from such different worlds. She’s in the army, stationed in Germany. We had a lovely afternoon though. A bit awkward at first, but we found a lot to talk about. It was lovely to bridge that gap. That's wonderful! It’s never too late to connect. I’m glad it went well. Anything else happening? You seem a little subdued. Well… it's Uncle George. He's been poorly, you know. Oh, no. Poor George. What's wrong? They think it's pneumonia, but it’s complicated. He’s got underlying…issues. It's worrying the whole family. Mum is beside herself. It's just… a reminder, isn't it? How fragile everything is. It is. It really is. I'm so sorry to hear that, Caroline. Honestly, it's hard, isn't it? Losing people, even when you're expecting it. My Nan passed last year. Still feel it, you know? Oh, I remember. So sorry. It's never easy. And now this. My niece, Sophie, she’s been diagnosed with something too. It's a minor thing, thankfully, but it just all piled up, you know?

Dad, did you ever learn Morse code? Aye, a bit at school. Dot dash, dot dot – that’s S, isn't it? Haven't used it in years though. Why d’you ask? Just wondered. I was watching this thing online, and they were sending messages, and it was kinda cool. It’d be a good way to be sneaky with messages, wouldn't it? Sneaky indeed. Much better than texting, eh? Though I can barely work out these emojis you lot send. What’s that swirling face supposed to mean? That’s feeling good! Or like a party. You know? You’ll be needing it next week – results day! Are you nervous? A bit, to be honest. Just want you to be happy with whatever you get. You done alright in your A-Levels? I think so. Fingers crossed for Manchester Uni. I've been looking at the campus online, it's massive! It is, isn’t it? We'll have to go for a wander around when we get there. Oh, and Amazon finally delivered that new phone case for you. Orange one, right? Yeah! Thanks, Dad. It’s got a little pocket for my card, so I don’t have to carry my purse around. Speaking of which, got any cash on you? A bit. Barely enough for a packet of crisps, mind. Need to do a proper food shop when we get back. All you eat is pizza and pasta these days, lass! That’s not true! I had a salad the other day. Well, most of a salad. A salad with chips on the side, more like. We’ll need to get you to eat some proper vegetables. Remember Mrs. Harrison's soup? The one with the parsnips? Ugh, don't remind me! It tasted like dirt. It weren’t dirt! That was parsnip. Proper good for you. Anyway, about that uni… student finance sorted? Mostly. Still waiting for them to confirm a few bits. It’s a nightmare, isn't it? This much money… I can’t believe it. Aye, it is. Just be careful with it, eh? Remember that glass water bottle you wanted? Might be cheaper to buy it on eBay than on Amazon. Good point. And I need new shoes. These ones are falling apart. Right, well, let's not go spending it all in one place. And speaking of places, are we almost there?

Man, this sofa is proper comfy. Feels good to be back in a real living room, you know? Uni accommodation was… a choice. Tell me about it! This is way better than that tiny box you were in. Still can't believe you managed to squeeze all those textbooks in there. Haha, it was a Tetris game, honestly. How’s things with you? Long time no see, yeah? Feels like ages since we properly chilled. Yeah, man. Things are… busy. Exams were brutal, you wouldn’t believe. Still recovering, to be honest. How did yours go? Pretty rough, to be fair. One went okay, the other... let's just say I'm praying for a miracle. The AI essay monitor almost caught me out too, that was a close one. No way! Seriously? They’re getting scary clever with those things. Glad you dodged a bullet, though. So, Japan still on the cards then? You were buzzing about that trip ages ago. Still the dream, yeah. I’m trying to sort out the visa and stuff, but it’s a nightmare. Tokyo’s top of the list, obviously. Been watching loads of travel vlogs to get hyped. Have you ever looked at going? Nah, never really considered it. Always wanted to go to South America, though. Like, backpacking through Colombia or something. Proper adventure. That sounds wild! You’d love that. I’m just drawn to the whole Japanese culture thing, you know? The food, the temples, the anime… True, true. Speaking of food, we need to order something. I’m starving. Any recommendations? That Korean place down the road still good? Yeah, they’re banging! Or we could try that new ramen place in Shoreditch. Heard it’s proper authentic. Ramen sounds amazing. Let's do that. So, future plans then? What are you thinking after uni? Another degree? Massive career move? Honestly? I haven't got a clue. I'm feeling a bit lost at the moment. Everyone else seems to have their lives figured out. You? Don’t let them fool you. Half of them are winging it just like the rest of us. I was thinking about maybe working abroad for a bit. Get some experience, see the world. Might be a good escape. That’s a cool idea. Where would you go? Probably somewhere in Europe. Maybe Germany, or the Netherlands. Heard the tech scene is buzzing there.

Right, look at this! Remember this holiday to Cornwall? Dad’s got the most ridiculous tan. Oh, bless him. Remember he insisted on wearing that straw hat for the entire week? Looked like a scarecrow! A scarecrow, you say? Well, I wasn’t going to let a bit of sun spoil my complexion, was I? Need to protect the skin, you know. Nowadays, they worry about everything. Absolutely, Dad. Speaking of worries, have you seen anything on Facebook about that cruise Emma’s been looking at? The Mediterranean one? I had a little browse yesterday. It looks lovely, doesn't it? Bit pricey, though. Must look into travel insurance, that’s for sure. It’s all so confusing these days. Absolutely. And have you seen what David Cameron’s been up to? Apparently, avoiding taxes through offshore accounts. Honestly, the cheek of it! Politicians! Bunch of rogues, the lot of ‘em. Always lining their pockets. Back in my day, things were much simpler. You paid your taxes, and you kept your head down. That’s the way it should be. I’ve just been reading about this gentleman who ate an entire pineapple. Ended up in hospital. Apparently, he was allergic and didn't realise. Good heavens! You hear the strangest things. Reminds me of Mrs. Higgins at school, she once tried to eat a pencil because she thought it would help her concentration. A pencil! That's a good one. My sister Mabel once insisted she could hear voices in her fillings. Ended up with a whole new set. Said they were telling her to buy lottery tickets. Oh, Mabel! Always a character. Speaking of tickets, did you manage to register to vote, Dad? The local elections are coming up. Of course, my dear. Wouldn’t miss it. It's your civic duty. Got my postal vote application in weeks ago. Can't let those youngsters think they're the only ones who matter! Good man! We should all be making our voices heard. Have you thought any more about those suggestions for trips this year? We were talking about going to Buckfast Abbey last week; it was lovely, wasn’t it? It was, very peaceful. The grounds are beautiful. Maybe Cornwall again? Or we could try somewhere new… perhaps the Lake District? Lake District? Bit damp for me, isn’t it? I prefer somewhere with a bit of sunshine.

So, tell me everything! Belgium sounded amazing in your texts. Did you have a good time? Oh, love, it was lovely. Really lovely. Just what we needed. Needed to get out. Absolutely. A bit of sunshine, y'know? And good food. Honestly, the food! You kept sending pictures of waffles… Were they as good as they looked? Better! Honestly, the best waffles I’ve ever tasted. Cream, chocolate, fruit… layered high. And the frites! Don't even get me started on the frites. With the mayonnaise, of course. Proper mayonnaise, not that watery stuff you get here. Sounds incredible! So, cycling everywhere, as you planned? That's what we tried to do. Mostly. The sat nav was a nightmare, mind you. Oh no, really? What happened? Took us down roads that just weren't suitable for cycling! Narrow little lanes, cobblestones… nearly ended up in a ditch a couple of times. And the traffic! They drive completely differently there. Close, very close. I kept having to shout "Oi! Watch where you're going!" Sounds stressful. Did you manage to see all the markets you wanted to? Oh, the markets were brilliant. Bruges especially. So many little stalls selling everything. Chocolate, cheese, antiques… I bought a little Delft pottery bird. Lovely little thing. Got a few chocolates myself, naturally. And some beer. A lot of beer, actually. I can imagine! How was the driving, Dad? You were a bit apprehensive about taking the car, weren't you? Apprehensive is putting it mildly! The roundabouts… dear me. They’re like a battleground over there. And the signs… completely different to what we’re used to. And the parking! Trying to find a space was a nightmare. We ended up leaving it miles away sometimes. Did you get a new phone while you were out then? I saw a picture of you with a shiny new thing. Yes, sorted that out! My old one finally gave up the ghost. This one’s got a better camera, and hopefully a more reliable sat nav – though I'm not holding my breath! It's got a really big screen too. You can see everything on it. Good! So, are you both recovered now? Ready to face the UK again? We're definitely recovered, though I don’t think I’ll ever get over the frites. I’m still dreaming of those waffles, to be honest. Should have brought back more chocolate.

Right, so I was thinking butternut squash risotto for tonight. Do you fancy that? Or too much effort after the day we’ve both had? Butternut squash risotto sounds lovely, actually. Bit more exciting than just beans on toast, eh? Let’s do it. What about starters? Hmm. I saw a recipe for baked camembert with fig jam and walnuts… fairly easy, I think. Would that work? Perfect. And a simple salad on the side? Keeps it all relatively healthy. Absolutely. I'll get the squash prepped while you find the camembert? I've been meaning to try a new perfume too, though - might have to pop into Jo Malone later in the week, the amber and sandalwood ones all smell amazing. Ooh, nice. You've got such a good nose for that sort of thing. You always pick interesting scents. Remember that one you bought that smelled exactly like freshly cut hay? Oh god, yes! That was a disaster. My colleague nearly fainted. I think I was trying to channel some rural idyll. It completely missed the mark. It did. Reminded me of my grandfather’s farm. Speaking of accents, I was listening to that documentary on the radio earlier about regional dialects. It's fascinating how much they've changed. Isn’t it? I was reading something about the Scottish accent and how it's undergoing a resurgence in younger generations. It’s a shame so many people feel pressured to sound "neutral" these days. Totally. Although sometimes I do wish I hadn't tried to completely copy the "received pronunciation" they taught us at university. My Edinburgh accent comes out when I’m stressed – it's infuriating! It’s a lovely accent when it does! Right, squash is peeling nicely. Should I order some flowers for the table? I saw some gorgeous peony bouquets on Bloom & Wild. Yes, please! Something colourful. And have you seen Sarah’s photos on Facebook? She's finally gone on that trip to Italy she's been planning for ages. I did! Looks absolutely stunning. She seems so relaxed. It makes you want to book a holiday, doesn't it? It does. Maybe we should look at something for next year. It would be good to get away. Definitely. We need to start thinking about it. Before it's too late. Oh, and I think I’ll get some logs for the fireplace too.

It’s lovely to finally meet you both, isn’t it? I’ve heard so much. Do make yourselves comfortable. More tea? Thank you, yes, please. This is lovely, really. Your home is… quite charming. It is, yes. Very welcoming. And relax, Allan, don't be analyzing the décor! Just admiring, Margaret! Admiring. I spent a lot of time in Queensland, you know. Years back. Business trips. Oh, really? Queensland. I've only seen pictures really. Did you enjoy it? Immensely. The climate is fantastic, of course. The people are very friendly. Bit laid back, you know, for business. The suits were a problem, though. Trying to sell financial software to fellas in shorts and Hawaiian shirts… a challenge. I can imagine. Trying to maintain that corporate image. Exactly. You'd go into a meeting, and the bloke’s got his flip-flops on. Hard to take him seriously. Still, the money was good. I was teaching in Bristol for many years, and one of my students was from Brisbane. She kept trying to teach me about the accent. It’s quite distinct, isn’t it? Oh, I love different accents. Growing up in Sheffield, you hear everything. It's a melting pot. Though nothing quite compares to a good Sheffield dialect, mind. Sheffield? Now that's a strong accent! Very distinctive. My accountant in Manchester, he was from Sheffield. Couldn't understand half of what he said sometimes. Well, that’s the beauty of it, isn’t it? “Ey up!” And a whole conversation can be had without a single word understood outside of South Yorkshire. I was used to a bit more standard English, I suppose, teaching EFL. Getting students to understand Southern accents could be tricky enough. Trying to explain 'quite' and 'right'… and the nuances of 'that' versus 'this'… it's a minefield. I can imagine. I once had a disastrous attempt at a bank loan in Australia. Tried to explain my business plan to a chap in Sydney, who had a speech impediment. Couldn't understand a word I was saying. Ended up borrowing the money from a bloke who ran a horse racing stable – he was much easier to deal with, surprisingly. That’s a story! A racing stable beating a bank! Oh, goodness. Well, I’m glad you both had such interesting experiences. It's been lovely hearing about them. It has been very enjoyable.

This lentil shepherd’s pie is surprisingly good, isn’t it? I wasn't sure what to expect from a vegan place in Rzeszow. It’s brilliant, actually. Much better than anything I’ve had back home. Seriously, I'm obsessed with this place now. We  have  to come back before we leave. Absolutely. It’s so nice to have somewhere decent to eat, especially something a bit different. So, what’ve you been up to? Still battling the hordes of teenagers with their Polish grammar? Pretty much! They’re…enthusiastic, let’s say. It’s been a challenge this week. One girl was convinced "I am go" was perfectly acceptable. Oh, bless her. The classic error. Did you send her some extra resources? Yeah, I did. I linked her to a couple of YouTube channels. She seems to prefer visual learning. You know, like everyone these days. Completely. Speaking of which, have you been on TikTok lately? I’m trying to understand what all the fuss is about. Oh, it's a rabbit hole. I occasionally dip in. Mostly just for a laugh. I follow a few linguistics accounts - you’d probably like them. Lots of grammar and pronunciation breakdowns. Oh, really? Send me their names! I’m always looking for new content. I've been thinking about starting a little account myself, just doing short explanations of common English mistakes. That’s a brilliant idea! You’d be great at it. Seriously, your explanations are always so clear. I used to tell all my students to come to you for clarification. That’s kind of you to say. I've just been putting stuff on Facebook - a bit of a laughing stock for my nieces and nephews, obviously. But it’s something to do, I suppose. You should branch out! TikTok is huge. It’s how my students learn now, and I've picked up some useful ESL strategies there. I'll consider it. Actually, I've been listening to podcasts lately. Have you heard of 'Stuff You Should Know'? It's fascinating. They cover everything, from squids to the history of mayonnaise. Oh, I've seen that! I’ve mostly been listening to true crime podcasts. Keeps me entertained on the bus. That’s a bit intense for me. I prefer something a bit lighter. Speaking of entertainment, have you seen anything good on TV recently? Anything worth streaming?

Right, Pippy, Leo, are you two listening? Big weekend plans! What do you reckon? Swimming! Swim! Swimming! Splash! Yes, swimming on Saturday! Pippy's been so keen, hasn't she? And Leo, you loved it last time. We need to pack your towels and goggles, though, don’t we? Goggles! Shiny! Big splash! Exactly! And then on Sunday... remember we talked about seeing Mr. Bumble’s Travelling Circus? Circus! Horses! Clown! Funny! Yes! It’s just down the road in Grantchester. We can pack a picnic. But before that... I need to sort out something important. Remember you're working for your Blue Peter badges? Blue Peter! Badge! Silver badge! Well, Pippy, you’ve nearly collected all your things for the photograph - the badges, the drawings… We just need a really good photo, and then we can send it off for your badge. Want photograph! Smile! We’ll have a lovely photo. Maybe we can take it at the circus? It'll be bright and cheerful. Leo, you practically take photos all the time. You’re the photographer of the family, aren't you? Click! Click! See? And then...but we need to renew our passports first! Remember how you were asking about going to France? France! Eiffel Tower! Little boat! Yes, but we need passports. So, I need to book an appointment. It's a bit of a faff, isn’t it? Online forms... everything’s online these days. Mummy’s computer! Exactly. But then we could go to France! Or Italy! Anywhere you like. Though Pippy, you’re nearly seven now, aren't you? Seven! Almost! Pippy big! You are! That’s amazing. Do you feel big? Yes! You are a big girl now. And Leo... you're five! So close to six! Five and a half, isn’t it? Five! Almost six! Yes. Listen, there's a funny story I heard from Auntie Carol today. You won’t believe it. She was talking to Mrs. Peng down the street, and Mrs. Peng was telling her about a trip to China. Apparently, they eat these… old eggs. Old eggs? Yucky! No want old eggs! Apparently, they’re preserved in a special way, and they’re supposed to taste amazing, but Auntie Carol said she couldn’t even look at them! Gross! No like! Blue! They look blue! Anyway. That's a silly story for another time. We need to focus on swimming, the circus, and getting those passports sorted.

Honestly, I'm having a right mental block about this essay. It's just… so much. Tell me about it. Sociology’s chewing me up and spitting me out, isn't it? What's the block specifically? It's this section on… well, it’s on sexual health, obviously. But then they wanted us to look at specific conditions. Right. Like? Erm… things like erectile dysfunction. And Premature ejaculation. And I just... I don't know. It feels weird talking about it, even in an academic setting. Like, it's… personal, innit? I get that. It’s a bit clinical, isn't it? When you're analyzing something that's so tied to… you know. Relationships. Intimacy. Exactly! And I'm just thinking about Liam, and… well, I know he had some issues a while back, and it just brings all that stuff up. Oh, reet. Sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it? Not really, no. It was a while ago, and we sorted it, but... it’s just triggering, you know? I’m trying to write about these conditions objectively, but my brain keeps going to… feelings. It’s totally understandable. Maybe you need to take a break from that section for a bit? Come back to it with fresh eyes? Yeah, maybe. I was reading about the psychological side of it, though, and it's actually really complex, isn’t it? How stress and anxiety can just… mess everything up. Absolutely. It's not just a physical thing, is it? There’s a huge emotional component. It’s all linked. Yeah. And the shame and stigma around it. It's gotta be horrible for people. It must be. I think that's why it’s important to talk about it, though, right? To destigmatize it. Even if it's uncomfortable. Yeah, you're right. Just... still feels a bit awkward, you know? Like, I’m a student writing about men’s… well, you know. It’s alright. You're not analysing  men , you're analysing a medical condition. Try to keep it separate. And if it’s really stressing you out, maybe chat to the lecturer? Explain what's going on? That's a thought. I just didn’t want to seem daft. You wouldn't. They’re used to students struggling with this stuff. They’d rather you asked than suffered in silence.

Right, so I’m thinking cauliflower cheese with a roast. Proper Sunday dinner vibes. Ooh, that sounds amazing! Are we doing Quorn or…? I was thinking Quorn. They've really upped their game at Sainsbury's, haven't they? The new range is actually, like, genuinely good. Definitely! I’ve noticed. I reckon it’s worth the extra couple of quid. Did you get your veg box this week? Yeah, it arrived. Loads of courgettes. What am I going to do with all these? Grate them into pasta sauces, courgetti… the possibilities are endless! I’m trying to be really strict, you know? Slimming World’s been going alright. Yeah, you've been smashing it. I'm a bit all over the place at the moment. These scales are useless, honestly. I swear they’re plotting against me. Tell me about it! Mine decided to add a stone just last week. I just ignored it and went and measured myself with a measuring tape instead. Smart. So, about this cauliflower cheese…how are we going to ‘Syn’ it? I hate how everything is just ‘syn’ this and ‘syn’ that. Loads of Healthy Extras! We can use loads of onion soup for flavour, and it's HEB, isn't it? Plus, a bit of Frylight to stop it sticking, that's practically zero. Good shout! And I’ve got that 0 calorie syrup, so we can add a little drizzle on top as a ‘treat’ but it won't have any Syns. Tasty. That stuff always tastes a bit artificial, though, doesn’t it? Like fake sweetness. Yeah, but it’s a tiny bit of fake sweetness for zero Syns! Gotta prioritise. Speaking of priorities, what's the plan for Treat Day Saturday? I was thinking that big chocolate cake from the bakery. The one with the salted caramel. YES! But we have to split it between us. I’m seriously trying to avoid a massive blow-out. Remember last month…? Don't remind me! I felt awful for days. Right, so, tea? We need a cuppa while we chop all this veg. Mint or English Breakfast? Mint, definitely. Something refreshing. This cooking is thirsty work. I'll put the kettle on. Also, I’m planning on doing a proper workout on Sunday. Like, an hour. No excuses. Go you! You know what’s the best thing about it? We can have double peas in the freezer.

Right, so I was looking at flights to Iceland again. Just daydreaming, obviously. Iceland, eh? Still dreaming of chasing the Northern Lights? Absolutely. Remember how we talked about maybe doing it for our tenth anniversary? Well, that's... looming. Looms it does. We should make it happen. It would be incredible. What did the flights look like? A bit pricey, as always. But I found some good deals on accommodation too. Little cabins, you know, with hot tubs. Hot tubs under the Northern Lights… that's a pretty perfect day right there. Exactly! It’s the benchmark now. Everything else has to measure up to a hot tub under the Northern Lights. Speaking of perfect days, if you could design your ideal day, what would it look like? Apart from the obvious Iceland trip. Right, let me think. No emails. Absolutely no emails. A leisurely breakfast… poached eggs, avocado, you know the drill. Then maybe some tinkering in the garage, sorting out that ridiculous collection of vintage circuit boards. So, tinkering and poached eggs. Romantic. Hey, it’s a blissful combination! Then we’d go for a long walk in the countryside, somewhere with a proper pub at the end. Real ale, a roaring fire... Sounds lovely. Mine would probably involve a quiet morning with a cup of coffee and a good book, followed by a wander through a local market and a ridiculously long lunch with friends. Nice. Less technological, more people-focused. Which is probably why you’re better at socialising than me. Don't be silly. Although, sometimes I do wonder if we should both get more involved in local politics. I’ve been thinking a lot about the state of things lately. Oh, don't start. I’d rather discuss tattoos. Have you been looking at any new designs? You and your tattoos. No, not really. Though, I was thinking… a tiny constellation on my wrist? Something subtle? See, that’s a good idea. Something celestial. I'm still toying with a phoenix. Rising from the ashes, that sort of thing. Symbolism, you know. You and your symbolism. What happens if you get a phoenix on your shoulder and then completely fail at something? Does that mean the phoenix falls over? No, no! Even if it fails, it rises again. That’s the point. It's about resilience. Speaking of failures... remember that time I tried to build a birdhouse?

So, about this weekend. Are you still on for Saturday? We said we’d try and get that table at The Fig Tree. Aye, still on. Saturday’s good. Did you manage to book it? They're usually rammed. I managed to snag one for seven-thirty. Said it was a “prime time” slot, apparently. Seemed a bit much, but I didn’t want to risk not getting in. Seven-thirty eh? Right. Aye, that’ll be decent. Fancy a pint beforehand, maybe? The Old Crown’s just around the corner. That could be nice. Let me see… seven-thirty at The Fig Tree, pint beforehand. Sounds lovely. Should I ring Jill and let her know? Definitely. She’ll be wanting to know. She was asking about it earlier in the week, wasn't she? She was. Something about wanting to try that sea bass. Good choice, that sea bass is lovely there. Speaking of recent holidays… did you ever send me that postcard from Cornwall? Oh, bother. I completely forgot! It’s somewhere around here, I think. Let me have a look… Found it! Here you go. Lovely picture. Porthleven, wasn't it? You were saying it was a bit blustery. Blustery is putting it mildly. Nearly lost my hat in the sea. But the food was wonderful, and the walks were spectacular. Really bracing. Glad you enjoyed it. Say, have you been following the latest stuff with Scottish independence? Of course. It’s hard to avoid. Bit messy, isn't it? All this back and forth. Aye, it is. Seems like there's no real consensus. Brings up a lot of old feelings, doesn’t it? About the union and all that. It does. Difficult to see how they’re going to resolve it in a way that satisfies everyone. Although, I suppose that's always the case with these situations. True enough. It's a bit of a headache, that's for sure. Anyway, back to Saturday. Should we tell Jill to meet us at The Old Crown at six, then? For that pint? Yes, let's do that. I'll give her a ring now and confirm it all. And I'll try to remember to send you postcards in the future! Good lad. That'll be grand. Now, where's that wine? It’s been a good dinner. It has. Shall I pour you some more?

Right, so I was thinking, you know, with all that’s happening with the Syrian refugees… it feels really helpless, doesn’t it? Helpless? What’s that? Well, like… we can’t all go over there and help, can we? It’s massively complicated. But maybe we could do  something  small. Like what? I had an idea. We could draw chairs. Chairs? Why chairs? Well, people who are displaced, they need somewhere to sit, don't they? Comfort. A sense of… home. It's symbolic, really. And we can send the drawings off to charities that are helping, a little bit of kindness. Can I draw a bouncy chair? A bouncy chair? That would be lovely, wouldn’t it? But maybe we should think about what  sort  of chair people would need… like, if they were waiting for help, or in a camp… A big chair! A really big chair so lots of people can sit on it! Good thinking, sweetheart! That's a brilliant idea, actually. A communal chair. Like the ones in the library. Like the ones at school? The ones with the sticky bits? Yes, like those! Though hopefully a bit cleaner! What about chair types? Have you learnt about different kinds of chairs at school, love? We did! We learned about… thrones! And stools. And… those swivel chairs! Swivel chairs! Great! Perfect for a waiting room, maybe. Right, let’s get some paper. We’ll need lots. And think about what colours you want to use. Maybe warm colours, to make people feel cosy? Can I use blue? Of course, darling. Blue’s a lovely colour. You know, it's a bit like when you were worried about that maths test last week… it felt big and scary, didn't it? It was really hard! But you studied, and you did your best, and that’s what matters. Drawing these chairs is a bit like that. It’s a small thing, but it shows that we care. Can I draw a chair for a princess? Absolutely! A princess deserves a beautiful chair. A throne, even! And can you draw a chair for a superhero too? Yes! A very bright red one! With wings! Wonderful. Let’s get started, then. And maybe we can research some charities later, to find out where to send them. It will make a difference, however small. Just showing that we’re thinking of them.

Right, so I was chatting to Chloe after my seminar today. She said Liam’s finally booked in for that hip replacement. Really? About time. He's been moaning about it for ages. How’s he feeling about it? Apparently, apprehensive, obviously. But mostly relieved, to be honest. He was saying how much his walking has deteriorated, and he’s just fed up with the pain. Said it’s going to be a real game-changer for him and Sarah. That’s good. Less strain on her. You know how much she does for him. Did she mention anything about the kids? Briefly. Imogen’s apparently got into that drama school she wanted. She’s ecstatic, obviously. Little Oliver’s just… well, Oliver. Still obsessed with dinosaurs and demanding chicken nuggets at every meal. Classic Oliver. Should we text them and congratulate Imogen? Definitely. I was thinking of sending flowers too, actually. A proper bouquet, not just a little something from the supermarket. That's a nice touch. Speaking of kids... did you hear anything about Mark and Emily? Just a rumour swirling around the department. Something about Emily trying for another baby. Apparently, she’s been a bit quiet in meetings, lots of tea breaks... Really? That would be their third. They’re going to be run ragged. I know, right? It’s amazing, isn't it? How quickly things change. It feels like only yesterday we were stressing about our first lectures. And now we’re gossiping about friends’ babies and hip replacements. Getting old. Don’t say that! Anyway, I’m marking essays until about nine tonight. Fancy making a cup of tea and bringing it up? Absolutely. And maybe we can have a proper chat about that consultancy proposal afterwards? It’s been on the back burner for too long. Deal. And I'll send a text to Chloe and Liam. It's about time someone got a bit of good news. Cheers. That’s the plan. I’ll get the kettle on. And, you know, if Emily does end up pregnant, we'll have to start practicing our ‘encouraging aunt and uncle’ faces. Oh God, please don’t remind me. Let’s just focus on the academic world for now, shall we? And not the impending baby boom. You got it. Tea's coming up! Is there anything else I can help you with? I would add that the dialect descriptions in the context did not add much information, so I did not attempt to incorporate any specifics, and set the tone with more natural flow of conversation.

Honestly, the way that man tripped over that gate post...it was slapstick gold. Like something out of a Benny Hill sketch. You mean the policeman? He looked mortified. Poor bloke. I hope he wasn't hurt. He seemed alright, just a bit red-faced. But the way his hat flew off! Pure comedy timing. It almost feels…superstitious, doesn’t it? Like a sign of things to come. Superstitious? Don’t go all rural on me now. It was just gravity and a slightly overgrown path. I know, I know. It’s ridiculous. But I always feel a bit…off when something like that happens, especially in a place like this. The air feels thicker somehow. You and your superstitions. You know, Professor Davies was telling me about his research on folklore and belief systems just the other day. Apparently, it's a surprisingly robust field. See! Even academics are interested in it. Anyway, speaking of robust, have you seen the publicity surrounding the new creative writing course at the uni? They're really pushing it. Yeah, plastered all over the website. A bit over the top, if you ask me. Seems they're desperate for numbers. Exactly. It’s almost…aggressive. Like they're trying to convince  us  it's a worthwhile course. Perhaps they are. You know, remember that disastrous open day we had a few years ago? Nearly empty. Don’t remind me! The catering was a disaster too. And that student who kept asking about writing sitcoms for toddlers. Oh, God, yes. The one who wanted to call it "Tiny Laughs." It’s still haunts me. Anyhow, back to the positive – at least they’re trying. It’s good for the department. It might even put Norfolk on the literary map a bit more. It would. Speaking of maps, are we still on for that holiday to Scotland in October? Absolutely! I’ve started looking at potential walking routes. The Isle of Skye looks amazing. That would be incredible. Though I'm slightly nervous about midges. We'll bring the repellent. Lots of it. Plus, you know, the scenery will be worth the bites. It’ll be a good change of pace from grading essays about Victorian poetry. A very good change. It’s just… sometimes I wonder if we're doing the right thing, with everything. The university workload, trying to get the publicity right, keeping up with… well, everything.

Dad, have you seen my phone anywhere? I swear I had it a minute ago. Nope, haven't touched it, love. Probably left it in your room, like always. You know you really should get one of those tile trackers. I know, I know. I keep meaning to, but then I forget. It's ridiculous, isn't it? All this technology. My grandma wouldn't understand half of it. Your grandma wouldn’t understand a telephone, let alone this. Remember when she used to complain about the wireless set crackling? Seems a lifetime ago. It does. So, about the move… have you started thinking about what you’re going to take with you when we’re sorting out the house? Not really, no. It's all a bit overwhelming. So many years of… stuff. You know, the fishing rods, those old radios, that ridiculous collection of teacups your mother adored. We'll go through it together, Dad. Don’t worry. We’ll decide what to keep, what to donate, what to chuck. Need to get a van booked, too. Something big enough for everything. A van… right. Should we get a quote? I don’t want to get ripped off. Some of these companies are daylight robbers. I can look online. There's loads of options now. I’ll compare prices, check reviews. Good girl. I saw something on the telly the other day, about that Great Dorset Steam Fair. It looked like a right knees-up. Oh yeah! I remember seeing adverts for that. Massive steam engines and all sorts. Fancy a trip down there sometime? Might be a good day out. Maybe! After we’ve got everything sorted with the move. We should try and get the rest of the family together too, before we go. You know, Mum, Sarah, little Tom… Yes, that would be nice. Difficult to get everyone in the same place these days. They’re all scattered about, aren't they? It is. Maybe a Zoom call could work. Everyone's always on their phones anyway. Hmph. Zoom. I still can't get my head around those computer games young people play. All shooting and shouting. It's not all like that, Dad! Some of them are pretty clever. Have you ever thought about trying your luck with the lottery? Lottery? No. Waste of money, I reckon. Buy a raffle ticket maybe, something a bit more… tangible.

Honestly, I'm fuming about the library. Demolishing it for another block of flats? It's just… short-sighted. I know, isn’t it? I saw the planning application online. They're claiming it's structurally unsound. Structurally unsound? It’s been standing there for eighty years! It’s Victorian brick. It’s solid. I bet it's just easier to knock it down and build something profitable. Exactly. And that art deco facade? It’s one of the few examples we have left in the area. It’s part of the character of the place. It really is. I used to spend hours in there as a kid. My mum would drop me off after school, and I’d just lose myself in the children's section. You can’t replace that. They’re saying they'll build a smaller library, but it won't be the same. It won't have the same atmosphere, the same history. Have you signed the petition? I’ve been sharing it on Facebook, trying to get as many signatures as possible. Of course! I signed it as soon as I heard. The local council is just… hopeless. They’re only interested in lining their own pockets. Tell me about it. Speaking of lining pockets, have you had a chance to look at those upholstery samples I ordered for the living room sofa? I did a quick glance. That deep teal one looked promising, but I’m not sure it's quite right for the room. I was thinking the same. I’m leaning towards something a bit lighter, perhaps a linen-look in a neutral tone. Something that will brighten the place up a bit. Yeah, that's probably a better choice. What about that textured cream one? I thought that was a little… bland. But I’ll have another look. I was reading an article online about how different weave patterns can affect the way a fabric looks in different lighting. You and your research! It’s a sofa, love. Not a PhD thesis. I know, I know. Just trying to make the right decision. It's a big investment. Speaking of things online, have you caught up on the news today? It's pretty grim. Typical. I haven't really. Avoiding it, actually. Too depressing. I was trying to find some interesting articles about preserving old buildings, actually. There’s a fascinating case in Cornwall about a council trying to force a resident to replace the original stonework on his cottage.

Right, so, who's got the aux? Anyone got a playlist sorted? I’ve got a few banging tunes, Dad. Loads of 90s stuff. Spice Girls, Blur… you know the drill. The drill, yes. Let’s stick to the classics then, shall we? Nothing too…experimental. I’m happy with anything, honestly. As long as it’s not country. Please, no country. Agreed. Country’s a non-starter. Right, let's hear what you've got, [Speaker 2’s Name]. Okay, here we go... Ooh, that takes me back! Remember trying to learn all the dance routines to this? You did! You were terrible, Uncle [Speaker 4’s Name]! I was enthusiastic! There’s a difference. So, right, presents! We've got to sort out who's getting what for [Speaker 3’s Name]’s birthday next week. Any bright ideas? Honestly, I don't need anything. Just seeing you lot is present enough. Don’t be daft. Everyone deserves a present. [Speaker 2’s Name], any suggestions? You’re good at this sort of thing. Hmm… she's been really into pottery lately, hasn’t she? Maybe a voucher for a class? That's actually a really good idea. I’ve been looking at those classes. That’s brilliant! I can chip in towards that. And I’ve got a little something already, a set of brushes for when she’s painting. Excellent. I’ll get her a nice book. Something a bit…intellectual. You know, to challenge her. Oh, wonderful. More dense European literature. Just what I always wanted. It'll broaden your horizons. Now, thinking about broadening horizons... did you all catch that new documentary on BBC Two about… Oh, not another wildlife documentary, Dad! Can we please just listen to music for a bit? She’s got a point. Let’s have a rest from the serious stuff. What are you both watching at the moment? Anything good? I’m hooked on that Korean drama, "Kingdom." It's like, Game of Thrones but with zombies. Absolutely brilliant. Oh my god, I’ve heard about that! Is it scary? A little bit! But in a really good way. The costumes are amazing, the plot's gripping... Zombies? Really? I’m not sure I can get on board with that. Don't knock it 'til you've tried it, [Speaker 1’s Name]. You might be surprised. Speaking of trying things... have you started clearing out the shed yet?

Right then, so let's have a proper look at these insurance quotes for you, love. It's a nightmare, isn’t it? Aye, it is. It’s gone up loads since last year. Well, that's cars in general, isn’t it? Everything’s going up. But we need to find something reasonable for you, especially as you’re only just starting out. Have you had a look at comparison websites? Yeah, but they all come back with like, ridiculous prices. And loads of exclusions. Aye, that’s the way of it. They’ll offer you a bargain price, then load it up with extras you don’t need, or things you can’t do. Did you try adding a black box? Black box? What’s that? It’s a little thing you plug into the car that monitors your driving – speed, braking, that sort of thing. If you drive sensibly, you get cheaper insurance. They’re incentivising good behaviour, see. Sounds a bit like Big Brother, doesn't it? Well, everything’s Big Brother these days, isn't it? But it can work out cheaper, especially for young drivers. Have you considered adding me and your dad as named drivers? Yeah, we looked at that. Apparently, it doesn’t really make much difference anymore. Insurance companies can see right through it, can't they? They know it's you driving most of the time. They do, aye. They're getting cleverer. Right, let's see… this one from Admiral, that’s a bit better, but it’s restricted to 50 miles a day. That's no good for you, is it? With getting to college? Nah, that's useless. I sometimes need to go into York, that's like a 40-mile round trip. Okay, okay. And this one from Direct Line… it's slightly higher, but it's fully comp and there aren't as many restrictions. It's worth paying a bit extra for fully comp, isn’t it? Especially as you’re only just learning. I suppose so. What about the excess? That's the amount you'd have to pay towards a claim if you had an accident. This one’s £300 excess. Can you manage that if something were to happen? I think so. Dad might help out if needed. Right, well, let's just go through the key points again. Fully comp, £300 excess, Direct Line… what do you reckon?

Jaysus, this week has been something else. The project deadline’s breathing down my neck, and the system keeps throwing up errors. Honestly, I’m starting to see blinking cursors in my sleep. Sounds rough, Dad. Like, really rough. Is it, like, the worst ever? No, not the worst ever. But it's edging close. The worst was when the database corrupted on Christmas Eve. Doesn’t bear thinking about. Stress levels? Through the bloody roof. I’m honestly wondering if I should start doing those wrist temperature things people talk about. Apparently, chronically elevated temperatures are a sign. You shouldn’t obsess over that, Liam. You look exhausted. Have you been getting enough sleep? And honestly, less time staring at screens and more time… well, anything else. Did you see that the equality vote passed? Aye, brilliant news isn’t it, Sarah? Absolutely brilliant. A long time coming. It’s just…it feels like a palate cleanser after the week I've had. A bit of good news, something hopeful. I voted for it! Does that make me a good person? Makes you a sensible one, Jamie. And already a step ahead most of the world, I'd say. Right…Chinese takeaway tonight? I’m starving. Sounds perfect. I'm not in the mood for cooking. Jamie, are you alright? You’ve been staring at your plate for a minute. I thought I heard a clicking sound. Is someone recording us? Don't be daft. Why would anyone record us? Though…I did start listening to a podcast about eavesdropping the other day. It's a bit creepy, actually. Don’t tell me, true crime again, Sarah? You’re obsessed. You know, my sister keeps telling me I should start a podcast. Something about IT security, or maybe just…ranting about work. Oh, please no. Nobody wants to hear about your server issues. Although…that awful chicken they used in the curry last week.  That  might get some listens. It was like chewing rubber. It tasted like cardboard! Honestly, Sarah, cardboard would have been a step up. I don't know how they mess it up so badly. It’s just… not chicken. You're analysing chicken now? You’re losing it, Liam. Do you even  use  words properly these days? You’re all jargon and stress. I’m trying! It’s just… when you’re explaining logical operators to a room full of people who think a boolean is a type of bubble bath… your vocabulary gets a bit… strained.

Honestly, Dad, you're taking us the scenic route again, aren’t you? I’m going to miss half my lecture. Now, don't start, love. It’s a lovely drive, look at the countryside! Proper Lancashire, isn’t it? Better than staring at a motorway. I’m bored. Are we nearly there yet? Nearly, Leo. Just enjoying the landscape. It's quite pleasant. Besides, you’ll appreciate the quiet after the school gates. Pleasant for  you , maybe. You're not the one trying to cram in a chapter on contract law before my seminar. Is that a goshawk? It is! Lovely bird. Always used to see them nesting near Moor Park when I was little. Proper aerial acrobatics, they are. Can we get some chips when we stop? Please? We’ll see, son. First, let’s focus on the journey. Did you hear about that dispute over the parking charges at Aldi? Apparently, they’ve tripled them. Seriously? What for? Everyone avoids parking at Aldi now anyway. It’s always rammed. It’s about the EU referendum, apparently. Council trying to recoup some losses. Always something. Is that why Mum’s been moaning on about it? Aye, that's right, lad. Just the usual red tape. Speaking of which, are you doing alright with your physics, Leo? That conversion from kilometers to miles last week gave you a funny look. It’s hard. Why do we need to know kilometers anyway? It’s a global world, Leo. You need to understand different measurement systems. Think of it – travelling to Europe. And for my law conversion, I need to understand weights and measures too! Scales vs. kilograms vs. grams. It's a nightmare. You'll get the hang of it, love. Just practice. Like when I was training to be a midwife – calculating dosages, keeping track of weights… you learn to do it instinctively in the end. Instinctive calculation, that’s a good phrase. I often have to look at the finer points of contracts – the minutiae of weight and liability. It’s all numbers, really. I was reading about Shakespeare the other day - apparently he used weight and measures loads in his plays. Made it much more relatable for the audience. Shakespeare’s boring. Can we listen to some music? Fine, but no boy bands. Remember Terry Wogan used to say "good evening" every night, used to listen to him coming home from the hospital.

This lentil shepherd’s pie is actually banging, isn’t it? Better than last time. Definitely! You've cracked it, Freya. It doesn’t taste like sadness anymore. Remember that first attempt? Oh god, yes. Like you were actively punishing yourself for being vegetarian. It was…rustic. Let’s just say that. Though, I respect the attempt. It takes courage to try lentil shepherd’s pie. Courage and a strong stomach. Seriously, though, I was reading about cultured meat the other day. Shmeats, they’re calling it. Shmeats? That’s a terrible name. It is. Sounds like a disease. But think about it! Lab-grown meat. No animals involved, a fraction of the environmental impact... It sounds terrifying, honestly. Like something out of Black Mirror. I’m cautiously optimistic, I think. Still a long way to go, though. Is it  actually  ethical if it's fuelled by unsustainable energy sources? And what about the people who  do  the lab work? Are  they  being exploited? It’s a whole can of worms. Exactly! It isn't automatically ethical just because it avoids one form of cruelty. And are we just going to replace one horrible industry with another? Like, factory farms and now lab farms… True. But you have to admit, the potential to massively reduce animal suffering is huge. Even if it’s just a stepping stone to something better. I saw a documentary about abattoirs the other day. Absolutely brutal. Honestly, I had to turn it off. Yeah, I can’t even watch those. Hunting seems… more respectable, somehow, when it’s done respectfully. Like, for sustenance, not for sport. That’s a weird distinction, isn’t it? Both end up with an animal being killed. It’s just the optics of it. I think it’s about the relationship. The hunting idea conjures a connection to the animal. Respect for it’s life. Abattoirs are just…churning. Utterly detached. You're right. It's the lack of agency. It's just a faceless process. Speaking of faceless things, has anyone been taking their B12 supplements? I've been trying. Forgot this morning. I’m just… not built for dietary discipline. I’m alright. I’ve got a good system. Plant-based iron supplements with my coffee, B12 with my dinner… It’s a ritual. See, that's the key, isn’t it? Routine. I’m always forgetting. I need to be like you, Systems-Man.

This is mental, isn’t it? The special effects in this film are just… bonkers. Aye, they’re alright. Could be better, mind. Remember that Marvel film we saw last year? That was proper good. I thought it was a bit much, to be honest. All that CGI. Just gives me a headache. Plus, the plot was a bit ropey. Nah, I loved it! The fight scenes were epic. You know, I was thinking about getting a new gaming headset. Mine's on its last legs. You always need a new headset. What’s wrong with the one you’ve got? It only works on one ear now! It’s a nightmare trying to hear voices. I was looking at ones online, like, proper fancy ones with RGB lights and everything. RGB lights? Seriously? You’re gonna look like a Christmas tree. What’s wrong with that? It’ll be festive. Want to go to town tomorrow and have a look? Nah, I’m sorted. Besides, I’m trying to save for a new phone. This one practically has a crack in every square inch. You need to be more careful. You drop it every five minutes. Remember last week when you cracked the screen while you were trying to catch it? It was a tricky catch! It slipped out of my hand. And anyway, I ordered summat ridiculous off Amazon last night. Proper needed somewhere to keep it. What did you buy? Don't tell me another one of those weird gadgets. It’s a mini projector. So we can watch films on the wall. A projector? That's actually a good idea! We could even have movie nights. Yeah, that would be class. But you’ve probably bought one that only projects blurry images and shuts down after ten minutes. Hey! It's got five-star reviews! And it was a bargain. Did you order Christmas presents yet? My mum’s already started nagging me about it. Nah, not yet. I was thinking of just getting everyone gift vouchers this year. Less stress. Easier, aye. My mum wants a new slow cooker. Says she’s going to become a gourmet chef. Your mum? Gourmet chef? She burns toast. Exactly. My grandma’s after a new tablet. Said hers is too slow. They all want technology. Can’t beat a good book, that’s all I’m saying. Easy for you to say, Mr. Never-Leaves-The-House.

Honestly, the keynote speaker was a bit of a snooze, wasn’t he? All talk about legal precedent and very little about – well, anything exciting. Tell me about it! I was practically fighting the urge to check my emails. Though, seeing all the familiar faces from uni did make it a bit nicer. Did you see Eleanor? Briefly, yeah. She looked… stressed. Still ploughing away at corporate law, I presume? Seems so. She said the hours are brutal, but the money’s decent. Though she’s seriously considering a career change. Something about wanting to do something that felt… impactful, she said. That's always a tricky one, isn't it? The impact versus the pay-check debate. I’m lucky, I genuinely enjoy what I do, even when the data’s a nightmare. You are! Coordinating language research sounds fascinating. How's that project you were telling me about – the one with the Cornish dialects? It’s going really well, actually! We've got some incredible recordings and transcriptions coming in. It's unbelievable how much has been lost, even in the last few decades. Reminds you how important our work is, really. What about you? Still loving the admin side of things? It's... stable. Pays the rent, you know? I’m thinking about doing some volunteering, maybe with a refugee charity. Something that uses my skills but feels a bit more… meaningful. That's brilliant! You’d be amazing at it. You’re so organized and good at communicating. Speaking of volunteering, my mum’s badgering me to go on that archaeological dig in Cyprus with her again this summer. Seriously? Still? That looked absolutely miserable the last time. Dust, heat, and digging up ancient pottery? Exactly! But she insists it's a 'cultural experience' and that I need to 'connect with my roots'. Apparently, a distant relative was a pirate.  Laughs  A pirate! That’s amazing. You'd be obligated to dress the part. I'm going to Greece this year, though. With my sister. Just a relaxing beach holiday in Crete. Needed a serious break after the thesis. Crete sounds divine. Sun, sea, and no pirates. Jealous! Where else are you hoping to travel this year? I’m dreaming of Iceland. Iceland! That is on my list. The Northern Lights, right? I’d love to see them. My grandma's been trying to convince me to go to Scotland for years to see them, but Iceland just sounds… wilder.

Honestly, I’m proper beat. This essay on Wordsworth is killing me. Still battling with it, then? Thought you’d cracked it yesterday. Cracked it? Nah. I wrote like, three paragraphs and then stared at the screen for an hour. Felt like my brain was full of treacle. Treacle, eh? Sounds awful. You need a massage. Properly loosen those knots. Ugh, you’re right. I could definitely do with one. Maybe we could try that place down the street? The one with the aromatherapy oils? Yeah, that's a good shout. I’ll book something for later tonight, sound good? That'd be amazing, thank you! Seriously, I'm starting to think those lecturers deliberately set the essays to make us suffer. They probably do, a bit. Want to test our dedication, I reckon. Though, Professor Davies' lecture on Romantic poetry yesterday was actually pretty good. Was it now? I missed it, I was drowning in daffodils and hopeless. He brought in some really interesting points about the influence of nature on Wordsworth's writing. Seriously made me rethink a couple of things I was planning to write about. See, that's exactly what I need. A rethink! I just feel like I’m saying the same things everyone else is saying, you know? It’s all “nature is important, Wordsworth loved nature, bla bla bla.” You'll find something unique to say. You always do. Just need to dig a bit deeper. Maybe try looking at some of his lesser-known poems. True. I’ll try that. And maybe I’ll have a breakthrough after a nice relaxing massage, courtesy of you. Just doing my boyfriend duties. Anything else I can do to help? Fancy a cup of tea? Ooh, yes please! And maybe a biscuit? A proper Yorkshire biscuit, none of that flimsy stuff. Sorted. Coming right up. So, Wordsworth or massage first? Massage first, definitely. Wordsworth can wait. He’s got all the time in the world, hasn’t he? That’s the spirit. Now, what kind of tea are we thinking? Earl Grey please. With a digestive! Thanks love. You're the best. Only for you, pet. Now let's get that essay sorted...after the massage, of course. Of course! Alright. Let me check booking slots then. Perfect. Thanks. No worries. Do you want me to get the tea on while you have a look at it again?

This lentil soup is actually quite good, wouldn't you say, Sarah? A bit more pepper next time, maybe. It is lovely, Dad. Really hearty. Thanks for making it. Much better than anything I could've thrown together on a weekday. It's delicious, Robert. You've really nailed it. I always struggle with lentils – they either end up mushy or rock hard. It's all about the simmering time, Carol. And a good stock. Though, I do wish I’d remembered to add a bay leaf. I’m really losing my touch, I think. Don’t say that! It’s perfect. Did you see the news this morning, though? About Calais? It’s just heartbreaking. Absolutely dreadful. The situation is just getting worse and worse. Those poor people… It’s just devastating to see. It is. And what are we doing about it? Pointless hand-wringing on the news doesn’t solve anything. Of course, you know the usual political arguments. Always blaming someone else. It’s so complicated, isn't it? So many factors at play. I’m trying to do a little something – donating to some charities helping with food and shelter. It feels like a drop in the ocean, though. Every little bit helps. And raising awareness, talking about it, that's important too. Do you think the children are understanding what’s going on, Sarah? They are, but I’m trying to be mindful of how much I talk about it. It's rather upsetting to them, Leo feels upset but I don't have to do. Children are remarkably resilient, though, aren't they? They absorb more than you realize. Still, it’s a tough world to grow up in these days. It is. Moving on to less depressing topics… Has anyone given any thought to Christmas yet? It’s only… what… November? Mum, really? It’s barely Halloween! Though, I suppose we should start thinking about travel plans. I was thinking maybe we could go to Cornwall again this year? Cornwall’s lovely. Though it’s getting terribly crowded, isn’t it? It is. But it's still beautiful. And we haven’t seen Aunt Margaret in ages – she’d love it. True. Though getting there… all that driving. I may be too old for that kind of journey now. I was thinking about possibly doing a cruise next year. Something around the Mediterranean.

Honestly, Bryn, this bathroom renovation… it’s been a saga. A complete and utter saga. Tell me about it! I’ve been looking at kitchens myself. Though thankfully, I’m dealing with a brother-in-law who, bless him, thinks he’s Bob the Builder. That’s… something at least. Mine, on the other hand, claims to be a ‘handyman.’ Turns out, that translates to ‘occasionally hits something with a hammer.’ The tiling is… questionable, to put it mildly. Oh, the tradespeople! You get a mixed bag, don't you? Remember old Dai Jones who used to do gardening for my sister? Solid as a rock, that man. Knew his onions. These days, they all seem to vanish halfway through the job. Precisely! This fellow, Omar, he’s disappeared. Vanished. Last I heard from him was a message saying he’d ‘got a better offer.’ Leaving me with half-tiled walls and a leaking pipe. That’s rotten luck. Did you get a contract? A handshake agreement, naturally. Typical. Should have known better, really. Should have documented everything. My late wife, Eleanor, would have had the contract drafted and notarized. She ran a tight ship, that woman. Aye, Eleanor was a force of nature, wasn’t she? Remember her lecturing Dr. Evans on the proper way to prune roses at the garden club? He didn't know what hit him. He was speechless. Utterly speechless. She always did have a way with words, my Eleanor. It’s not just the tiling, you know. It’s the grout. The grout is a disaster. It’s uneven, it’s patchy… You’re catastrophizing a little, aren’t you? A bit of extra grout won’t bring the house down. It’s the principle, Bryn! The utter lack of professionalism! I’m seriously contemplating just hiring someone else to redo the whole thing. Someone reputable. Now, that’s sensible. My niece, Seren, she’s got a lovely bathroom. Small, but lovely. All done by a bloke called Gareth – he’s highly recommended. I’ll give you his number if you like. Actually, he did my daughter's kitchen last year. Top notch. That would be wonderful, Bryn. Absolutely wonderful. So, you’re thinking kitchen renovation then, are you? How’s that progressing? Slowly. Very slowly. My brother-in-law’s convinced he can handle the cabinet installation himself. I’m trying to steer him towards a professional, but… stubborn Welshman, you know.

Ah, that was a grand curry. Bit too much chili for me though, even for a man from Belfast! It  was  lovely, Liam. Though I think you enjoyed the heat a little  too  much, you were practically sweating! You looked like a dragon, Dad. All red and breathing fire. Well, a wee bit o’ fire never hurt anyone, did it? Reminds you of your Granny Moira, she could put down a curry like nobody’s business. You’d be feeling it for days after! Don't remind me. Nearly lost a night’s sleep trying to cool down after her Vindaloo. Remember when Finn tried to eat a metal spoon last week? Yeah! He was determined. Thought it was a biscuit or something. Nearly gave Mum a heart attack. Tiny mites are at it again. He’s going to be eating a car next, mark my words. It reminds me of me and my cousin, we'd eat anything we could get our hands on. Reminds me of the time we tried to eat a bar of soap! Honestly. And you’re supposed to be the responsible adult. Trying to be, trying to be. Speaking of responsible, are we still on for the park event on Saturday for Finn's birthday? Yes, definitely. I've booked the bouncy castle and ordered the cake. Trying to keep it simple, you know, with the toddler mayhem. Can I bring my mates? Well, let’s see how many they are. Don't want to overwhelm the poor boy. And make sure they behave themselves! No eating metal spoons. Speaking of behaving... I was reading that awful history book Finn's school gave him. It’s all grim battles and horrible kings. How are kids supposed to learn about history with that stuff? It’s boring! I'd rather read about superheroes. I wish I had superpowers, like flying or invisibility. You could use invisibility to sneak extra biscuits. Funny dad. I could use super strength to... to beat up bullies! Oh, someone's got a hero complex. Don’t go getting any ideas now. Remember, being kind is more powerful than any super strength. True that. Speaking of powerful, I was thinking about setting up a night deposit box at the bank down the street. Just for easy access you know, for… well, for important things. Important things like…? Just important things! Financial management, right?

So, Halloween's coming up then, eh? Always quite liked a good fright. Used to scare the wits out of the little ones down the road. You always were a character, Arthur. Remember that year you dressed as a giant pumpkin? Oh, yes. Absolutely ludicrous, wasn't it? Rolled down the hill, I did. Nearly ended up in Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning petunias. Right laugh that must've been. My little 'uns are already planning their costumes. Maisie wants to be a unicorn, bless her. A sparkly unicorn! I've got the glitter glue already, Dad. It's going to be epic. The school's doing a Halloween disco too, which is brilliant. Ooh, a disco! That’s lovely, dear. Are they letting you dress up at school? Yeah, costumes are allowed, but no masks. Apparently, safety reasons. Sensible, I suppose. Masks can hide a multitude of sins. Speaking of schools, how’s school going, love? Getting much homework these days? Loads! Especially in maths. Mr. Davies is being really tough this term. I’m having to go to after-school tutoring. Oh dear. That's a shame, isn't it? Still, good that you're getting the help you need. What are you enjoying the most? Art, definitely. We’re doing a project on mixed media – sticking fabric and things onto canvas. It’s really messy but fun. I’ve been drawing horses a lot as well. Horses, eh? Always been a fondness for horses. Remember old Bess, down at Farmer Giles'? Used to ride her bareback, I did. Oh, Arthur! You and your horses. Getting into all sorts of scrapes, you always did. Speaking of getting into scrapes, did you ever manage to get that leaky tap fixed, Margaret? Not yet, sadly. Nigel's been promising to come round for weeks, but he's a busy man, you know. Always teaching. Nigel's a good lad, though. Proper teacher. Remember when he used to bring us little quizzes after Sunday lunch? Don’t remind me! He used to quiz us on everything. From the capitals of countries to the types of birds in the garden. Can we go to that new riding stables near Wymondham this weekend? Please, Dad? I saw they have lessons for beginners. Wymondham, you say? That's not too far. We could make a day of it, couldn't we? That sounds lovely, dear. A change of scenery would be nice.

Honestly, this traffic is dreadful! I thought getting here early would beat it, but no such luck. You never beat it to the Steam Fair, love. It’s a rite of passage. Part of the experience, you know. Tell me about it. I’ve seen worse, but this is definitely testing my patience. And trying to navigate with these narrow lanes... nightmare. It's worse than the M25, it really is. At least on the M25 you can zone out a bit. Here, you're constantly swerving to avoid tractors and… is that a vintage motorbike? It is! Splendid, isn’t it? Look at that chrome, the gleam. Proper classic. Nice to look at, perhaps, but not so nice when it’s crawling in front of you at twenty miles an hour. I worry about my mum, you know. She'd absolutely hate this. What’s up with your mum? Well, she's been on the council housing list for ages. Needs a ground floor flat, something with easy access. Her stairs are killing her. But these council houses… absolute nightmare to get. They’re putting people in places that are completely unsuitable. It’s a disgrace. Absolute disgrace, the way they treat our older generation. No thought for anyone. Back in my day, the council cared. Now… It’s all about targets and budgets, isn’t it? Doesn’t matter if it’s the right thing to do. Exactly! I applied for her to go into one of those supported living things, assisted living. But the waiting list is like a decade long. And the prices! Ridiculous for what you get. Supported living... sounds a bit fancy to me. My sister tried to get my dear old friend Maggie into one of those. She needed somewhere to be looked after, a bit of help with her medication. But they didn't grant her one, kept saying she wasn't “dependent enough.” That’s ridiculous! Dependent enough to wander off and get lost but not dependent enough for care. It's all so complicated. And then there’s the parking, I bet. This fair has got to be a nightmare for disabled parking. Oh, it always is! Last time, I spent half an hour just circling. Ended up parking a mile away and lugging my little Doris around. She wasn't best pleased, let me tell you. We'll need to scope that out first thing.

So, I was thinking about the allotment… it's properly exciting, isn’t it? Having somewhere to actually  grow  things. I’ve always wanted one. It is! I’m so glad you got a plot, honestly. It’s brilliant. So, what are you picturing? More veg than flowers, I presume? Definitely more veg. Though a few sunflowers would be nice, just to brighten the place up. I’ve been looking at some guides online, and it seems like tomatoes and courgettes are pretty easy to start with. Good choices. Courgettes are prolific, though! You’ll be swimming in them. You might want to limit yourself to just a couple of plants. Yeah, I suppose so. And what about potatoes? Are those tricky? Not terribly, but you do need to ‘earth them up’ as they grow. It’s a bit of a faff, but not rocket science. Early potatoes are easier than main crop, apparently. Have you got any idea about soil conditions there? It’s worth checking before you commit to anything. Not really, to be honest. I was going to pop down and have a look tomorrow, maybe take a little sample to that garden centre near the station. They’ve got that soil testing thing, don't they? They do. Definitely a good shout. Knowing your soil pH will make a huge difference. You don’t want to be planting acid-loving plants in alkaline soil, or vice versa. Right. Okay, soil testing. Got it. What about fencing? Do you think we need to put some up to keep out the rabbits? Oh, absolutely. 100%. There are rabbits everywhere! Unless you fancy sharing your lettuces with them. You could go for something simple - chicken wire would be cheapest, but proper wooden fencing looks much nicer. I was thinking wooden fence actually. Maybe something reclaimed? It feels a bit more… sustainable. Good idea! There’s that reclamation yard just off the High Street, isn't there? They often have loads of old fencing panels. We could have a look. We could!
