That could be a weekend project. So, fence, soil testing… what about tools? I've only got a rusty trowel and a pair of secateurs. Well, you’ll need more than that! A good spade is essential, a fork, maybe a hoe. I've got loads of bits and bobs you can borrow to start with. Don't go buying everything brand new straight away.

Honestly, I'm proper chuffed you came up, Lizzie. Been ages! It’s lovely to be here, Maisie! Doncaster looks… well, like Doncaster. Nice to see you though. Ha! That’s fair. So, what’s been happening with you? Still moaning about the lack of decent coffee in Cambridge? Don’t even get me started! They have this new place, “The Bean Scene,” but it’s all foam and no flavour. It’s a crime, I tell you. What about you? Studying hard? Trying to. History’s alright, but Modern Languages is killing me. Trying to learn Spanish is like wrestling a badger. I can imagine. Remember when you tried to learn French? "Le chat est sur la table," you’d say, but with a Yorkshire accent. Don't remind me! Anyway, speaking of wrestling badgers, have you heard anything from Liam? Liam? No, not for ages. He just… disappeared after that gig, didn't he? Did something happen? Nah, nothing bad. He just said he needed some space. Apparently, his mum’s been giving him a right earful about getting his life together. Oh, Liam and his mum. Always a recipe for disaster. He does need to sort himself out, though. Still playing gigs? A few, yeah. He’s playing at The Black Bull next Saturday. Fancy coming up and having a listen? Saturday? Let me check my diary. I think I'm free! That would be good, actually. It’s been ages since I’ve seen him play properly. Perfect! We can grab some chips afterwards, proper Doncaster chips. You know, the ones dripping in vinegar? Oh, you’re tempting me. And what about Chloe and Amelia? Are they still going out with those… what were their names? The rugby lads? Chloe is, yeah. Seems happy enough. Amelia dumped Tom last month. Apparently, he kept borrowing her jumpers without asking. Honestly! Men! That’s the worst offense. It's like, borrow my jumpers and you've gone past the point of no return. Exactly! So, listen, I was thinking… we should all try and plan something soon. Like a proper girls' weekend away. Somewhere sunny. Ooh, I like the sound of that! Where were you thinking? I don't know. Maybe Cornwall? Or even Spain if we're feeling ambitious? Cornwall would be amazing! We could go surfing, eat cream teas… Exactly! Let’s look into it, yeah? See if we can find some decent deals.

Right, I’m going for it. Full throttle. Come on, come on… Don’t crash, Liam! You know you'll hate redoing that section. I know, I know, but if I don't risk it, I'll never get past. It's gotta be the quickest route. You’re obsessed with speedrunning. Honestly, just enjoy the game. Easy for you to say, Mateo. You’re not trying to beat your personal best. Anyone else feel like a proper feed after all this gaming? I'm starving. Always, Finn. You’re always hungry. What are we thinking? Pizza? I was craving a pepperoni. Pizza’s always a winner. Or we could try that Korean place near campus? Remember how good that Bulgogi was? Bulgogi sounds amazing. But I'm not pausing my run for food, okay? Just shout if anything important happens. Very dedicated. You’re missing out, though. I saw on Insta that they have a new dessert - matcha cheesecake. Proper drool-worthy. Matcha cheesecake… okay, you’re tempting me. But I’m still voting for pizza. Less effort. I’m easy either way. Just need something substantial. Speaking of food, did anyone manage to get into the final night of the food festival on campus? I tried! Absolutely rammed. Couldn’t even get near. Everyone and their mum was there. Right, nearly through. Don’t talk to me, please! Dude, relax. It's just a game. Remember that time you spent three hours trying to find that hidden item in Zelda? That was different! This is crucial. Okay, okay… I’m in! Yes! Told you you could do it! See? Risking it paid off. Massive congrats, Liam! Now, about that pizza... I saw a video of some crafter making miniature clay animals. It was so oddly satisfying to watch. Like, seriously, tiny foxes and hedgehogs. Oh yeah? Send me the link. I’m always on the lookout for things to distract me from studying. Okay, right. So, now I've cleared that, maybe I’ll take a break for  some  food. But I’m still aiming for the speedrun record this weekend. You’re relentless. Anyone seen that new Baz Luhrmann film? The Elvis one? Yeah, I went last week. It was… a lot. Very Baz Luhrmann, you know? All flash and style. I've been meaning to see it. Is it worth a watch? I’m a sucker for musicals.

So, darling, how was work today? Did you manage to sort out that… what was it? The widget situation? The widget situation is still a situation, Mum. Honestly, it’s a nightmare. Everything’s got delayed, and I'm chasing my tail trying to keep things on track. Oh, love, that sounds stressful. You shouldn’t be working yourself to the bone. You need to take breaks. Remember what Dr. Patel said about your blood pressure? I know, I know. It’s just… it’s really important to get this done. The new client is relying on us. Well, get it done, but don't let it consume you. Speaking of which, have you heard from Chloe and Liam? They were supposed to call about the film night. Not yet. I’ll text them. I was thinking maybe we could watch "Everything Everywhere All at Once"? I’ve heard it’s brilliant. Oh, that sounds intriguing. What’s it about? I struggle to keep up with these new films. Everything's so… fast-paced these days. Used to be you could sit and enjoy a nice, straightforward drama. It’s a bit hard to explain, actually. It’s sci-fi, comedy, action… all mixed together. About a Chinese-American immigrant who has to save the multiverse. It’s wild. A multiverse? Heavens to Betsy! Sounds complicated. Is it any good? Really good! Seriously, Mum, you’d like it. It's got heart, even with all the craziness. And Michelle Yeoh is fantastic. Michelle Yeoh… yes, I remember her from “Tomorrow Never Dies”. Very elegant woman. Exactly! Right, texting Chloe now... Nope, no reply yet. Maybe they’re still stuck in traffic. They probably are. London traffic is always a nightmare. Remember that time you and your brother were late for your dance recital because of a lorry breakdown on the A40? Oh God, yes! I was so stressed. I thought I'd missed my whole solo. You had to practically drag us out of the car. Well, you weren’t going to miss it! All that hard work and choreography. That’s why I insisted. Sometimes, you need to be pushed along a little bit, darling. True. Okay, Chloe just replied! They’re running a bit late, but they’ll be here around seven. They said they’re bringing popcorn. Oh, lovely. Popcorn is essential for a good film night. I’ll make some chocolate brownies.

Right, so spill! How was the interview? You were so stressed about it last week. Honestly? A bit…weird. They kept asking about my experience with obscure Welsh folklore. Like, seriously. What does that have to do with editing a glossy lifestyle magazine? Maybe they're aiming for a very niche audience. "Welsh Myth and Marina Life." Catchy, right? Right. Catchy and slightly terrifying. I tried to play it cool, said I’d always been fascinated by cultural narratives and storytelling. Which, technically, isn’t a lie. See, you’re clever! You spun it. And did they offer you anything? Not yet. They said they'd be in touch next week. Gutted though, because I really wanted the stylist role. The staff benefits are insane - free spa days, cinema tickets… A spa day! That's exactly what you need. You've been working yourself ragged. Fancy a joint one next month? My treat. We can finally try that aromatherapy place we talked about. Oh my god, yes! That would be amazing. I could seriously use some serious relaxation. Speaking of things to relax me, did you finish 'The Undateables' last night? Oh, practically inhaled it. Absolutely brilliant. That couple with the dogs… just adorable. Broke my heart a little too. It’s so lovely, isn't it? It makes you realize that love and happiness come in all shapes and sizes. It's a proper antidote to all the manufactured reality TV nonsense. Totally. It's so refreshing. And speaking of media, Sarah sent me this article in "Bloom" magazine - apparently, the colour magenta is going to be  the  colour of next season. Seriously? Magenta? That's bold. I always thought burnt orange was having a moment. It still is, but magenta's rising. Apparently, it's all about embracing bold self-expression. I might have to revamp my wardrobe. Good idea! Actually, I saw this DVD at the charity shop - "Amelie." Have you seen it? Oh, "Amelie"! Classic. Absolutely adore it. So whimsical and charming. It's wonderful. Such a feel-good film. Perfect for a cozy night in with tea and cake. Definitely. Actually, remember how we were saying we should play board games more? I found this really cute one at a car boot sale last weekend. It's called “Creature Caravan” – it's all about building a travelling circus for mythical creatures. Seriously?! That sounds amazing! We have to play it.

Right, so I’ve officially lost the will to live thanks to this washing machine. Oh no, what’s it done now? Last week it was eating socks, wasn't it? Worse. It's decided to leak. Proper waterfall situation in the laundry room. I mopped it up, but I’m genuinely terrified it’s going to happen again. Blimey. Have you contacted the company then? Yeah, ages ago. They sent someone out who said it was “a minor issue” and charged me a fortune for a temporary fix that clearly hasn't worked. I'm half tempted to just chuck the whole thing out the window. Don't do that! You'll have to pay for the window too. Maybe it's worth another call, just to be a pain. Threaten them with a strongly worded letter? I’m surprisingly good at those. You are. I might take you up on that. I just feel like every time something goes wrong in this house, it's a drama. We've got ancient plumbing, a washing machine from the depths of despair, and I'm pretty sure the oven is plotting against me. Well, at least the cat's happy. Extra moisture in the air, I suppose. He practically has his own little rainforest going on down there. Speaking of, I did a massive shop today. Feeling domestic. Did you now? What’d you get? Anything exciting? Loads of pasta, some proper chorizo - the good stuff, not the cheap supermarket version – and I impulse bought a jar of pickled onions. Don’t ask. Pickled onions? That’s a choice! What are you planning on making? Probably a massive pile of pasta carbonara. Easy, comforting, and requires minimal effort. Which is exactly what I need after battling the washing machine. Sounds perfect. My mum keeps sending me recipes for casseroles. I swear, she thinks I'm incapable of feeding myself. She's just looking out for you! It's the mum thing. Mine’s obsessed with Yorkshire puddings. Like, no matter what I’m doing, she'll try and get me to eat a Yorkshire pudding. My nan was like that with trifle. Always had a bowl of trifle handy. It's a generational thing, isn't it? Comfort food. Anyway, I was thinking we could watch something tonight? I downloaded "Everything Everywhere All at Once" - heard it's amazing. Oh yeah, I’ve heard good things!

Honestly, the sheer gall of them. I’ve been reading about this Volkswagen thing. It's unbelievable. Saying it’s a scandal doesn’t even begin to cover it. It is pretty shocking, isn't it? The scale of it is what gets you. All those vehicles... deliberately programmed to cheat emissions tests. Corporate greed, plain and simple. Always has been, always will be. They think they’re being clever, hiding their negligence, and lining their own pockets. Exactly, Michael. It’s the deception that’s the worst part. Imagine trusting a car, thinking you’re doing your bit for the environment, only to find out you've been duped. I suppose the technology's moved on so much, it’s easier to pull off things like that now. It wasn't as simple to cheat back then. Well, it's not like this is the first time a big company has done something underhand, is it? Remember Rover? All those promises about safeguarding jobs, then suddenly,  poof . Gone. Yes, but this feels different somehow. It's not just about jobs, is it? It's about knowingly polluting the environment, actively deceiving consumers. And all for what? A few extra pounds in profit? They said it was to meet emissions regulations. Apparently, American standards were so strict, it was tough to get the engines to perform well  and  comply. So they…found a loophole. A loophole? That’s a polite way of putting it, isn't it? It's blatant dishonesty. They should be made to pay, properly. Not just a few fines that will barely scratch the surface of their profits. Agreed. And all this talk about house prices… it's all connected to it, somehow. Why is it so ridiculously expensive down south? Everything's inflated. Well, there’s the demand, isn’t there? More people wanting to live in London and the surrounding areas. That drives up prices. It’s ridiculous. You could buy a decent-sized house here in Cumbria for what you’d pay for a tiny flat in Birkenhead. It's no wonder people are moving up north. I know! Imagine the money you'd save! We’re so lucky to have found this place. It's peaceful, it's beautiful, and the community is wonderful. Absolutely. And you can actually afford a garden! I'm already planning to plant some lavender. Don't forget the rhododendrons.

Honestly, Doreen, I don’t know why I bothered. He was just being deliberately difficult. About the double glazing, you know. Men, eh? Always having to have the last word. Remember your Uncle Arthur? Similar sort. Stubborn as a mule. Oh, don't remind me about Uncle Arthur! He used to complain about the price of everything, even when he was getting it free! Well, this wasn’t about the price. This was about him insisting the surveyor was wrong about the window sizes. He'd measured them himself, supposedly! Said I was being "fussy". Fussy! You’re a sensible woman, Margaret. Good sense, you’ve always had. Probably wondering when he's going to get his pension sorted. Speaking of pensions, have you seen that new thing online about claiming back overpaid National Insurance? Apparently, loads of people are entitled. Really? Where did you hear that, Christine? I’m hopeless with those computers. My granddaughter tried to show me, but it was just… numbers and flashing things. Gave me a headache. Computers! A waste of time, I say. All this technology… remember when a phone was just a phone? You picked it up and talked. Simple. Well, they do connect you to people, George. Otherwise, we'd be stuck here talking about double glazing and grumpy relatives all day. Though, to be fair... . It’s just… having to deal with these endless forms. It’s exhausting. And then worrying about whether you’ve put the right figures in. It's all so overwhelming. Remember when they were talking about building all those houses on the old airfield? Said it’d be ‘affordable housing’. Don’t make you laugh, does it? They’re all overpriced boxes, aren’t they? And the traffic… it’s dreadful already. Trying to get into Norwich is a nightmare. It is. I'm considering moving, actually. Somewhere smaller, maybe. Somewhere with a bit more peace and quiet. I’m just not sure where to go. Everything's so expensive. You’d be mad to leave this house, Margaret. Been here fifty years. It's got memories. He’s right. It’s your home. Unless… you’re thinking about that bed and breakfast you mentioned last week? The one in Cromer? It was just a thought. A little break. Somewhere by the sea. Just to escape it all, for a bit. But the cost… and being someone else’s guest… Better than being at the mercy of that surveyor, eh?

Honestly, Mr. Davies is just relentless with the evolution stuff. Like, we get it, Darwin. Tell me about it. He spent twenty minutes today explaining how a beetle’s shell developed. A BEETLE’S SHELL, Liam. Seriously? It's only interesting if you’re, like, a paleontologist. Which none of us are. I’m pretty sure I'm failing that test next week. You could just memorise the key processes. Natural selection, mutation... Easier said than done, Finn. I’m still trying to wrap my head around genetic drift. It’s just random. Why learn random stuff? It's seemingly important, Sam. Mrs. Patel says it’s fundamental to understanding biology. And biology is fundamental to everything. Everything? Like what? Baking a cake? No, not like  baking a cake . But understanding how living things work. Speaking of things working... did you see that video of the guy trying to grow a plant out of his ear? Oh god, yeah! That went viral, didn't it? Absolutely bonkers. It’s probably fake. Some clever editing. People will believe anything they see online. But what if it wasn't? What if it wasn't fake and he actually had a plant growing out of his ear because of some weird genetic mutation? Then we'd be in a sci-fi film. Exactly. Although, thinking about mutations… it makes you wonder about, you know, gender stuff. Like, why is it so binary? That’s a bit deep for a Tuesday, Liam. I’m down to hear this. Well, I was reading an article – it was about intersex people, and how a lot of times, even doctors get it wrong. It's not just male or female, there’s a whole spectrum. Yeah, I saw some stuff about that too. It made me think about how much pressure people feel to conform to those labels. It's no joke. My cousin, remember Sarah? She had a really rough time growing up because she didn't fit into either box. The bullying was awful. People are so stupid sometimes. Like, why does it matter what gender someone is? It doesn't. It truly doesn’t. And sexism in general... It's still a thing, isn't it? Even now? Absolutely. You see it everywhere, even in school. Teachers expecting girls to be more organised, boys to be better at maths… the stereotypes are just ridiculous. It's ingrained, isn't it?

Right, so the consultant finally called. About the operation. Oh really? What did they say? Are we any closer to a date? They want me to do some more blood tests, apparently they're a little concerned about a potential infection. Nothing major, they said, just want to be absolutely sure. Infections are awful, dear. Always were. Used to get them all the time when I was a girl, scrubbing floors all day. No proper gloves, you know. You and your floors, Margaret. Always a drama. Well, that’s just brilliant, isn't it? More blood tests. More waiting. I know! It’s incredibly frustrating. And I’m still trying to sort the tablets out. The pharmacy keeps messing up my repeat prescription. It’s like pulling teeth. You should complain, love. Always complain! Gets results. I know, I know. I'm trying to be patient, but it's hard. Still, at least I'm seeing David on Saturday for lunch. Oh, good! You deserve a nice lunch. How’s David? Still playing rugby? He is, although he’s said his knee’s playing up a bit. They may have to get him to retire. Can you imagine, David, without rugby? Can’t imagine it myself. He’s like a fish out of water without a ball under his arm. Remember when he broke his collarbone? Oh, I remember! The whole village was talking about it. Poor boy. Sarah, have you ever tried acupuncture? Brenda at the gym swears by it for all sorts of aches and pains. I’ve considered it, but I’m a bit wary, to be honest. Seems a bit… New Age. Brenda says it’s amazing for back pain, and you've been complaining about yours. I suppose. I'll look into it. Anyway, how's your MOT coming along, John? You were worried about the tyres last time. Got it booked for next week. They said the tyres are on their last legs, need replacing. That’s not good! It’s getting colder, isn’t it? You need to be safe. Definitely. And how's your sister doing? I didn’t see her last time I was over. She's okay. Still complaining about the council not fixing the pothole outside her house. Typical. Council! Don't even mention them. They took away my bench last year. Said it was a hazard. A hazard! You were feeding the pigeons, Margaret!

Right, so we've been talking about how things weren't always fair, haven't we? Was it like when the dinosaurs fought? Not quite, sweetie. This is about people. A long, long time ago, some people thought they could own other people. Own them like a pet? Can we have a pet dinosaur? No, love. It was much worse than a pet. It meant forcing people to work without paying them, and taking them away from their families. It’s called slavery. Why would people do that? That's not fair! Well, people can be really unkind sometimes, even when it's wrong. They wanted to make money and get richer, so they made people work on farms and build things for them. They brought people from Africa, across the sea, and forced them to work. Did the dinosaurs help? No dinosaurs this time, darling. But many people did fight back. Brave people both who were enslaved and the people who helped them. They said it wasn’t right, and they tried to stop it. Like in a superhero movie? A bit like that, yes. But real life is often more complicated. There were wars about it too, you know. People fighting over whether slavery should be allowed or not. Wars are bad! They are, darling, very bad. Lots of people get hurt. And sometimes, even though people fight, things don’t change straight away. It took a very long time for slavery to be stopped. Why did they stop it? Because lots and lots of people kept fighting for what was right. They kept telling everyone that all people are equal and deserve to be treated with respect and kindness. They held protests and wrote letters, and eventually, the laws changed. It's important to remember it though, so we don't make the same mistakes again. Can I have a biscuit now? Fighting is hungry work. Absolutely. Let's go get some biscuits. And then maybe we can read a story about brave people who stood up for what’s right. How does that sound? Yes! A story! With a princess! And a superhero! We’ll see what we can find, darling. Let's go. Remember, even though things have gotten better, we still need to be kind to each other, okay? Always be kind. It’s the most important thing. Okay, Mummy. Biscuits! Biscuits! Biscuits! . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ....

Right, has everyone managed to snag a biscuit before they’re all gone? Dad, you’ve already cleared half the plate! Can't help myself, love. Best ginger snaps I've had in ages. You've outdone yourself, Fiona. Speaking of outdoing, have you seen what's happening with the energy prices again? Honestly, it’s getting ridiculous. I saw that, Dad. It’s terrifying. I’m hoping my freelance work will cover it, but things are tight already. Well, at least the weather's been decent. Makes a change from the endless rain we've had. Did you see that otter down by the river yesterday, Fiona? Huge thing! No way! Really? I didn't see it. I was rushing back from the hospital, you know how it is. I saw a squirrel bury a nut in the garden this morning. Felt very autumnal. Reminds me of that documentary about squirrels we watched. The intelligence of those little creatures is astonishing! They are clever little things. Remember Millie used to hide her toys under the sofa cushions? Nearly gave me a heart attack the first time I found them. Millie was a handful, wasn't she? Always getting into mischief. She was a happy little thing, though. Always smiling. It's lovely to see the grandkids growing up so well. Speaking of growing up, did anyone see that Bridgerton series? Oh, don't even start! I can’t stand those costumes. So fussy! I enjoyed it, actually. A bit of frivolous fun. Although, the historical inaccuracies are a bit much. You know, it reminds me a little of that Upstairs, Downstairs. Remember that? Oh yes, lovely series that. Elizabeth Bennet was my favourite character. It’s just… it’s all so heightened, you know? It’s not exactly a realistic portrayal of life. Though, that's the appeal, I suppose. You and your realism. Sometimes you need an escape! What have you been reading, Emily? Anything good? I just finished "Daisy Jones & The Six". It's told like an oral history, it was brilliant! So gripping. Sounds interesting. Is it any good? I’m looking for something to read on my holiday next month. Definitely recommend it! It's all about the music scene in the 70s. Holidays! We’re going to Cornwall again this year, aren’t we, dear? Yes, booked it last week. Same cottage we had last year.

Right, dishwasher’s done. Let’s get this unloaded, shall we? Thomas, you can grab the plates, Lily – cups, please. But Mummy, I want to talk about Harry Potter! I know you do, sweetheart, but we need to tidy up first, then we can. George Stephenson wants to talk too, apparently. George Stephenson built the trains! He did indeed! A very clever man. Thomas, plates, please? But Mummy! Draco Malfoy is being really mean in this chapter! I’m sure Harry will sort him out. Okay, Thomas, you're doing brilliantly. Now, Lily, cups? Remember to stack them neatly. My train goes  choo choo ! That’s right! George Stephenson’s trains went  choo choo . Did you know he had a really hard time getting people to believe that trains could  actually  work? Like, when people didn’t believe Harry Potter was a wizard? A bit like that, yes! People thought trains were too noisy and too smelly and that they’d frighten the horses and ruin the countryside. They worried about all sorts. Did the horses run away? Some of them did, at first! But George Stephenson kept building them, and making them better and better. He really believed in them. He built the first public railway, the Stockton and Darlington Railway – that was a huge thing! Was it like the Hogwarts Express? Sort of! It didn't take children to a school for magic, but it took people to work and to visit their families. It was a really important invention. George was a bit like a wizard, wasn't he? Making things that everyone thought were impossible, possible.  Choo choo ! He got the steam right! Exactly! He figured out how to use steam to make the wheels go round and round. Thomas, are you finished with the plates? Mummy, can we read another chapter now? Please? And can I tell you about the time Snape… Just let me put these glasses away and then, absolutely! George Stephenson’s trains can wait a few minutes. Right, silverware's next. Come on, little ones, team effort. And then – back to Hogwarts! Trains and wizards! Yay! That's the spirit! A brilliant combination. Now, where are those forks...? Snape was being very cross! Very, very cross! I'm sure he has a good reason, sweetheart. Now, forks…plates… cups…Let’s go!  Choo choo ! You and George Stephenson are just the best, you two!

Right, so I’m beat. This essay on post-structuralism is genuinely trying to break me. Tell me about it. I’m covered in flour and buttercream and still haven't figured out how to properly caramelize sugar. It's either burnt or a watery mess. You’d think with all that baking, you'd have it down by now, Liv! Caramel is tricky though, honestly. Low and slow. Seriously low. I know, I know! I watched, like, five different YouTube tutorials, and they all contradict each other. One says really high heat, one says barely a simmer… Argh! Sounds like trying to navigate the London Underground, hey? Everything’s a suggestion, not a rule. Seriously! Speaking of navigating, I’m losing at Words With Friends. Chloe’s just wiped the floor with me. She’s playing with, like, triple-word score strategy. Chloe always was ruthless. Remember that time she accused us of cheating at Monopoly? Oh god, yes! She was convinced we were switching money under the table. Classic Chloe. Anyway, dinner’s smelling good. What are we having? I was thinking pasta carbonara. I’ve got some really nice pancetta. Ooh, good choice! I'm starving. Running the cafe all day… God, I’m dreading the council turning up again about that patio space. They won't leave you alone, will they? These councils, they are relentless. I had trouble with my coffee shop in Melbourne. Little things escalating into massive paperwork nightmares. Yeah, bureaucracy’s a special kind of hell. My mate, Finn, is getting into it deep with some legal stuff over a rental agreement. Apparently, the landlord’s been dodgy. Ugh, that’s awful. Sounds stressful. You should tell him to look at Shelter's website. They’re really good for advice. Yeah, Shelter's brilliant. I’ve directed a few of my regulars there over the years. Anyone having rental dramas needs to know about them. I learned a lot about Aussie tenant’s rights from a website called Tenants Victoria. Similar vibe, I reckon. Good to know. Finn’s just really worried. It’s affecting his studying, too. He needs to prioritize that. These things take time, but his education is important. Right, pancetta’s sizzling! Anyone want a glass of wine while I get the pasta going? Always! I’m trying to get my hands on some proper Pecorino Romano. The supermarket stuff just isn’t the same.

Right, lunchtime at last! This morning has been  mad . Little Thomas decided he needed a full-blown dinosaur excavation in the play corner. Tell me about it! I've been battling printer issues all morning. Seriously, these things have a mind of their own. How was Thomas, though? Still obsessed with the T-Rex? Absolutely. He was roaring at the poor teaching assistants. It's a phase, I hope. What about Anya? Has she started ballet yet? She had her first class last week! She was so excited, completely dressed up in her leotard and everything. It’s adorable, but also a huge expense! I’m considering taking up pottery again just to earn a bit of extra cash. Pottery! That's a lovely idea. You were always good at it. Remember that little ceramic hedgehog you made me for my birthday years ago? Oh, goodness, that thing! It was… rustic, to say the least. But it was the thought that counted. I miss having a creative outlet, though. Between Anya and work, there’s not much time for anything else. I know exactly what you mean. It’s the same with me and gardening. I always plan to get out there and do loads, but the weeds win every time. I'm thinking of getting one of those robotic lawnmowers - extreme, I know! Extreme, but tempting! Have you seen those? They look like little tanks trundling around your garden. I saw one on YouTube the other day; it got stuck in a flowerbed. Oh dear! Well, perhaps not then. So, are you having much luck with the contract work alongside your reprographics role? Anything exciting on the horizon? It’s been steady, but nothing major. I’m looking at a few IT admin roles though, more permanent ones. I'd love something with a bit more responsibility. The admin stuff is good, but I miss the more technical challenges. Absolutely. It's good to keep your options open. Maybe you should talk to Mr. Henderson. He's always saying they’re looking for someone with solid IT skills. I can mention it to him if you like. Oh, that would be brilliant, thank you! Honestly, just having someone put in a good word makes a difference. This sandwich looks amazing by the way - what is it? Smoked salmon and cream cheese on granary. Treat yourself! It's been a stressful morning.

Dad, are we nearly there? I’m parched. Nearly love, just another turn. Keep your eyes peeled for Mothercare, it's on the left, right after the roundabout. Is the traffic bad? It was awful last time we came this way. No, surprisingly good actually. Must be a Friday, people either shopping or off for the weekend. Ugh, I need a fruity ice pop. They had amazing slushies at that shop in Manchester last week. Remember when you were little and you'd demand a grape ice lolly? You'd scream the place down! Don’t remind me! I was such a drama queen. You were a character, that's for sure. Anyway, did you manage to find the nappy bags you needed? Yeah, loads! And that little knitted blanket looked so soft. I almost bought it. Oh, the one with the little sheep on? It was cute. We should pick one up for little Leo, he'll need something snuggly for his cot. Right, good shout. Remember that disgusting blanket my mum had when I was a kid? Hideous Floral thing. Oh my god, you’ve told me about that before. Did she really use it for years? Years! And she swore it was lucky because it had been her mum’s. I swear it shed fibers everywhere. Gave me itchy eyes for weeks. My grandma was the same! Kept a moth-eaten shawl forever. Sentimental value, I guess. Speaking of sentimental things, have you heard back from the surveyor about the house yet? Just this morning, actually. He said the structural survey’s looking good. A few minor things, nothing major, but we need to get the damp checked out in the downstairs bathroom. Damp? That’s not ideal. How much will that be to fix? Hard to say until we get some quotes. But it’s not the end of the world. We were planning on redoing the bathroom anyway, so we can get it all sorted at once. That’s ages away though. I know. It all seems so overwhelming. The whole moving house process. It is, but we’ll get there. Don't worry. You'll be able to decorate your room exactly how you want. Remember how you wanted that pale pink wallpaper? I do! So girly. I might change my mind by then though. Do you think I’ll be able to do a degree in Media Studies?

Ugh, I’m so bored. I’ve been playing Stardew Valley for like, four hours straight. Stardew Valley, is that the farming one? It looks quite lovely. Are you doing well with your crops? Yeah, it’s addictive. I’ve got, like, the best blueberry farm in Pelican Town, apparently. But I’m just… I don't know. My mood is really low. Low mood, eh? What’s up? Everything okay? It's just… school stuff mostly. And everyone’s already planning Christmas trips and I feel like I'm just stuck here. Well, Christmas feels a long way off yet, love. Don’t get caught up in everyone else’s excitement. What are you studying at school now, anyway? Still doing the science stuff? Yeah, biology. It's actually really interesting when you're not being tested on it. We were talking about the psychology of gaming today, which was weirdly relevant to Stardew. Like, how it’s designed to trigger reward systems in your brain. See? Even playing games can be educational! Although, I bet mom would disagree. Don’t you start, Alex. It's important to have a balance. Stardew Valley is lovely, but staring at a screen for four hours can’t be good for your eyes. I know, I know. I just… It’s an escape. What about that science thing you mentioned? Is there any news on your internship at the university? It's still pending. They haven’t replied to my email yet. I sent it ages ago. It would be an amazing opportunity, working in the genetics lab - I'm really hoping I’ll get it. They’re probably just busy, sweetheart. Universities are always busy. Don’t worry yourself sick about it. What are you hoping to research? Tissue regeneration. It's mind-blowing, honestly. Imagine being able to grow back limbs, heal injuries completely… Wow, that  is  amazing. Sounds like something out of a sci-fi film. Exactly! But it’s actually happening. There have been some breakthroughs. It's just so complicated. It always is with science. Speaking of complicated, Alex, is your work situation sorted then? Still looking for something stable? Yeah, still searching. It’s tough out there. Lots of applications, lots of rejections. I'm thinking about a course in data analysis, would that be useful? Definitely! Everyone needs data analysts these days. It’s a good idea.

Right, so, diamonds are the best, obviously, in Minecraft. Everyone knows that. But I like amethyst! It's purple! Amethyst is pretty, sweetie, but it's not as useful. It's mostly for decoration, isn’t it? You need it for the spyglass. Spyglass! I want to see faraway things! Like dragons! There aren’t dragons in Minecraft, love. That’s a different game. Though, we  could  invent some! What would your dragons be like? They’d be sparkly! Like diamonds! And they’d breathe purple fire! Mine would be big! And strong! They'd have iron scales! And they’d sleep on piles of gold! Iron scales, good idea! Strong and shiny. Gold for a comfy bed – very luxurious. So, dragons guarding gold…that’s a good legend. We could tell that story! Can we draw it? Absolutely, we can. Mummy’s got some lovely paper. Now, what about materials for making armour? What’s the strongest? Diamond! Correct! And what’s a bit easier to get, but still pretty good? Netherite! Excellent! You both know your stuff. Now, Netherite is like… really tough metal, even better than diamond. It’s found deep in the Nether, which is a very dangerous place. Is it harder than iron? Much harder than iron. Iron is good for starting out, but it doesn't last very long against creepers. Speaking of which, how are you both doing on your vitamins? I took mine! The chewy ones! I don't like the yucky ones. I know, love, but they're good for you. Like the iron in iron armour! They make you strong. So, back to materials... what about fabric? What’s the most luxurious fabric you can imagine? Silk! Like a princess dress! Very posh. And what’s a strong fabric? You know, something a knight would wear. Wool! Sheep! Good! Wool is pretty warm, too. Though, not as strong as, say, leather. Leather's tough, but needs to be tanned properly. It's not just  any  animal skin, is it? No! You have to… make it soft! Exactly! It’s a whole process. It's like smelting iron ore into ingots - you have to work with the raw material to make it useful. Can we build a dragon nest outside? Maybe we can, sweetheart. But first, let’s finish our vitamins, okay? Then we can draw the dragons! And maybe we’ll even invent a whole history for them.

Honestly, I’m proper chuffed you lot managed to get a table this early. It's rammed tonight. Aye, we were lucky. Liam’s mum knows the bloke who runs this place. Always pulls strings for us. Reckon she’d pull strings for a drink if we needed it, eh? Probably! Speaking of Liam, where  is  he? Said he'd meet us here. He texted, said he was stuck tuning his guitar. Apparently, the E string’s being a right pain. Typical Liam. Always fiddling with that thing. You still play yours, then, Josh? Sometimes. Haven't had much chance, really. Uni’s been manic. You still gigging? A bit. We did a set at the Uni pub last week. It was a right laugh, even if only about fifteen people turned up. Mostly just sixth formers looking for a cheap pint. Still, fifteen’s fifteen, isn’t it? Better than playing to a room of empty chairs. What band were you covering? Arctic Monkeys, as always. Gotta keep the classics in the setlist, haven’t you? Then we did an original, which went down alright. Good on you. You should record some of your stuff. Put it on Spotify. I know, I know. Just haven’t got round to it. Too busy stressing over essays, I reckon. What about you? Still sketching? Trying to. Got a blank sketchbook mocking me from inside my cupboard. Used to be proper obsessed, now… just don’t have the time. It’s a shame, really. It is. You were brilliant, though. Remember that portrait you did of Mrs. Henderson from down the street? She was proper chuffed with it. Aye, she was. Still has it up on her mantelpiece, apparently. Wonder if she still remembers me. She'll not forget you, love. You gave her a proper work of art. Hey, listen, I saw something online the other day that proper worried me. Oh? What’s that? It was about those people…you know…online. Grooming kids. Proper sick. Makes you want to just… Aye, it is. It's awful. My mum's always banging on about online safety. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It does. It's just… scary how easy it is for people to hide behind a screen and be… well, just awful. Definitely. We gotta look out for each other, don’t we? Tell someone if you see somethin’ dodgy.

So, have you guys looked at any of the uni courses properly yet? I’m still kind of stuck. A bit. I’m thinking about that astrophysics course at Manchester, but it looks insane. Like, mountains of maths. Astrophysics? Seriously, Ben? Where do you even start with that? I don't know, Chloe! That’s why I’m panicking! My EPQ's given me a taste of how much work it is, you know? I'm doing a presentation on black holes, and honestly, it's swallowing  me  whole. Yeah, EPQs are brutal. Mine’s on the socio-economic impact of gentrification in London. It's bleak. Really bleak. I’m interviewing people who’ve been priced out of their own neighbourhoods. Oh, that sounds heavy, Liam. But important. I'm doing mine on the portrayal of women in modern feminist literature. Less depressing, hopefully. Though, sometimes, it just makes you angry. My dad keeps saying I should just do something sensible, like engineering. Something with a guaranteed job. Mine too. Want to be a "proper" professional. What even is that? My mum’s already planning my gap year. Humanitarian work in Nepal, she says. Like I’m some kind of do-gooder saviour. Classic. My grandma wants me to be a doctor. Apparently, that's the height of respectability. Remember when Mrs. Davies tried to make us all join the debating club? Ugh, don’t remind me. The most boring thing ever. All those rules and procedures. I’d rather juggle flaming torches. Actually, Liam, you’re pretty good at juggling, aren’t you? You should teach me. Yeah, sure. We could do it in the park. You know, while contemplating global poverty. Sounds like a lovely afternoon. Anyone fancy grabbing some chips? I'm starving. Yes! And a veggie burger. Anyone else veggie? Nope, I’m back on meat. Sorry, Chloe. I'm trying to be less meat. It's… complicated. The ethics of it all, you know? Honestly, it's a minefield. I remember when I was little, I used to think chickens lived in farms where they just roamed around free all day. I thought pigs lived in mud puddles and had swimming lessons. That’s adorable. I thought Santa Claus lived in a giant gingerbread house. Remember when we all tried to build a fort in Mr. Henderson's garden? He nearly had a heart attack.

Honestly, this kitchen is grim. Like, seriously grim. I saw a spider the size of my hand in here earlier. Tell me about it! My radiator's been gurgling all day. Sounds like a dying whale. I've put in another complaint, but you know how that goes. You guys complain too much. It’s student accommodation. What did you expect, the Ritz? It’s freezing in my room, though. Like, genuinely freezing. I've got about five blankets on. Well, at least you’ve got blankets. Mine are paper-thin. Basically holes. And I’m running low on money again. Anyone else feeling the pinch? Massive pinch. Mum sent me a fiver yesterday. A fiver! To last me until next week. I’m thinking of selling my kidney. Don't be dramatic, Priya. You'll find something. I’m managing, just about. Nan’s been sending me parcels. Loads of Indian sweets and stuff. Keeps me going. My mum says my auntie Sarah’s having a baby! She didn’t even tell anyone she was pregnant. No way! Really? How far along was she? Apparently she's just had it. They’ve named it Alfie. Honestly, Alfie. Alfie? That's…a choice. What’s wrong with Alfie? It’s a classic. My cousin’s called Alfie. It's just... boring. Like, super safe. Not exactly pushing any boundaries, is it? My grandma thinks it's really traditional. She said it’s been in the family for generations. Generations???? Of people naming their kids Alfie? That's insane! My mum was telling me about a wedding she went to last weekend. Apparently, the bride was wearing a dress that was completely see-through. No! Seriously? Was it on purpose? Apparently, her mother-in-law thought it was  scandalous . There was a whole argument about it. Oh my god. This is gold. I need details. Was there cake? Yeah, lots of cake! My auntie’s a pretty good baker, apparently. But the rest of the wedding seemed to be overshadowed by the dress. Apparently, the groom didn’t even notice. My brother's got his driving test next week. So stressed. He keeps practicing with Mum, but she gets a bit frantic, apparently. Oh poor him! My dad's terrible at giving directions. I’m pretty sure he’s deliberately tried to get me lost several times. My dad’s the same! Once he took me to the wrong airport, like two hundred miles in the wrong direction.

Honestly, the kids were absolutely mental last Christmas. Finn nearly set the Christmas tree alight with a sparkler. A sparkler! At three years old. Oh, goodness! Little terrors, aren't they? Though, I remember my grandson, Rhys, once tried to feed the cat a Christmas pudding. Said he wanted to share. Oh, bless him. Finn just wanted fireworks everywhere. It took three of us to wrestle the sparkler away. And Leo, well, he just smeared mashed potato all over himself. It was… chaotic, but lovely. How was Christmas at yours, Mum? Quiet, dear. Very quiet. Your Auntie Carol didn’t make it this year, you know. The house felt awfully empty without her booming laugh. We still put her favourite carols on, though. "Silent Night" was a must. Oh, Mum, I’m so sorry. I know how much you both loved her. We should’ve popped round more last year. Things just got so hectic with work and everything. Don't you fret about that, petal. She knew you were busy. She was always saying, "That girl's making a difference halfway across the world, teaching those kids English!" She was very proud of you, you know. That's nice to hear. Teaching is rewarding, but tiring. I’m in Prague at the moment. It’s beautiful, but I miss home, obviously. Prague, eh? Always wanted to go. Such history there. Are you having a good time teaching? It's great, honestly. The kids are brilliant. Little sponges, they are. Keen to learn and they're so polite. But some days, the bureaucracy… it’s a nightmare. Paperwork, visa extensions, trying to navigate their system... Sounds familiar, dear. Dealing with paperwork is the bane of everyone’s existence, isn’t it? Remember when I was trying to get all my qualifications recognised after moving away from Cardiff? Footling bureaucracy! You always were a whiz at navigating red tape, though. You managed to pull off that training contract with British Telecom, didn’t you? Well, someone had to, didn't they! It was a bit of a whirlwind, all those training days and meetings, but it was good money, it was. I’ve been doing freelance consultancy ever since, which gives me the freedom to travel a bit. Just been to Cornwall last week. Cornwall! Lucky you. I haven’t been back in ages. Remember Mrs. Trethewey from school down in Torquay, the one with the prize-winning roses?

It’s… it's actually really good to see you, Dad. Two years, eh? Feels like longer. You too, son. Feels like five! Bit of a whirlwind having to pack up the flat like that. You're looking well, though. Still rocking the beard, I see. Yeah, it's a commitment, isn't it? So, how’s the new place? Is it settling in alright? It’s...different. The area's changed a lot. More flats being built, less green space. Not really my cup of tea, to be honest. Bit too…sterile. Understandable. You preferred Crayford. More character, right? Definitely. Though, the speed cameras around there were a menace. Nearly got caught twice. You still got your license clean, do you? Absolutely. Been a model driver since I learned, Dad. Speaking of which, how’s your work at the call centre going? Still dealing with Mrs. Higgins’ complaints about her broadband? Don’t remind me! Some days, I swear she has a personal vendetta against me. But hey, pays the bills. Been a bit rough this past week though, been feeling a bit under the weather. Just a cold, hopefully. Hope it clears up quickly. So, Brighton. Really going for it, aren't you? Big move. Yeah, needed a change of scenery. Plus, that little flat overlooking the beach… it’s tempting, isn't it? You should come down for a weekend, see for yourself. I would love to. I’ve got that conference in London in November, maybe I can swing a weekend after that. How's Mum? She’s good, mostly. A bit lonely, to be honest. We try to see her as much as we can, but it’s tricky. You know. Yeah, I know. Remember when we all went to Tanzania together? That was… incredible. Ah, the safari. You were fascinated with those giraffes. Tried to get one to eat out of your hand. I did! It didn’t work, obviously. You've put on a bit of weight, Dad. Don't you start! All this moving’s taken it out of me. Comfort eating, I suppose. It's been a bit tough. Don’t be too hard on yourself. Look, I know you’ve had your struggles, openly talking about it sometimes helps. Mental health is important, don’t forget. I know, I know. Appreciate it, son. You always were the sensible one. Speaking of which, have you seen that new show on HBO?

Honestly, the Sainsbury's was absolute chaos this evening. Didn’t you hear about the kerfuffle with the avocados? Apparently, someone tried to return a whole basket of them because they were “too ripe.” Seriously? People are unbelievable. Sounds like peak middle-class drama. Did they actually get a refund? Apparently, the manager ended up offering them a voucher. The whole thing was all over the local Facebook group. Someone filmed the whole thing. The comments were wild. Standard. People love a bit of supermarket drama. How was your day otherwise? Did the PR students manage to avoid melting down in the presentation prep? Surprisingly well, actually. They’re starting to get the hang of anticipating potential pitfalls. We did a mock crisis scenario—a totally fabricated Twitter storm about the university's catering—and they handled it reasonably calmly. Though one of them did suggest apologising with a free pizza. Classic. You can’t argue with pizza as a crisis management tool. Still, it’s good they're thinking on their feet. My own lectures were pretty standard. Tidied up my notes for the upcoming post-structuralism module. Dreadful, but someone has to do it. Speaking of things that are dreadful, did you hear about that new band, 'Static Bloom'? They’re the ones everyone’s been saying sound like a slightly more melancholic Arctic Monkeys, right? I’ve had a few recommendations. Yes, that's them. I gave them a listen in the car today. Honestly, I couldn't get past the first two songs. It's just... bland. Overproduced and lacking any originality. A real triumph of marketing over substance, I suspect. Sounds about right. The industry seems to churn out these perfectly engineered bands who are designed to be palatable. No rough edges, no surprises. Exactly. Anyway, I need to order some new sheet music. I'm thinking of trying Beethoven’s Moonlight Sonata. It’s been on my list for ages and I figured it was time to finally tackle it. Oh, that’s lovely! You’ll be brilliant. Fancy me accompanying you sometime? I'm embarrassingly rusty on the piano, but it could be a laugh. Definitely. We could have a very amateur recital. Just don’t expect Carnegie Hall. Perhaps this weekend? I need to grab that music online, so I’ll have a look and let you know. Sounds perfect. I should probably get started on that reading for the faculty meeting next week.

Right, so I was thinking, for the beanbag cover… do we go with a really chunky cable knit or something a bit finer? It's such a huge project, I'm a bit overwhelmed already. Chunky, definitely chunky. It’ll be warmer, comfier. And frankly, a finer knit would take forever. You’ve enough on your plate as it is. True. But I’m worried it'll look a bit… rustic. Too farmhouse chic, maybe? Nonsense. It’s  our  farmhouse chic. Besides, we need something to offset all that… minimalist bathroom décor you're obsessed with. Hey! It's modern! And the new shower curtain looks lovely. The grey really brightens the space. Brightens it? It’s the colour of a rainy Edinburgh afternoon. But yes, it  is  a good curtain. Much better than that floral monstrosity we had before. Don’t remind me! Okay, chunky knit it is then. I’ll start on the back panel tonight. What are we having for supper? I was thinking maybe a lentil shepherd’s pie? Sounds good. Bit of a hearty winter warmer. I’ll get the lentils on. Did you manage to find any decent thyme at the market? Yes, a whole bunch! And some rosemary, too. Should be fragrant enough. I’m trying to remember what Mum used to put in her shepherd’s pie… did she used to use Worcestershire sauce? I think so. A secret ingredient, apparently. She never told anyone. And if you asked her she’d just give you that look. Exactly! That knowing look. Right, Worcestershire sauce it is, then. Should I parboil the lentils or just add them straight to the pot? Straight to the pot, I think. They’ll soften up nicely. And I’ll peel the potatoes while you’re sorting out the lentils. Do you think we need more bath mats? The ones we've got are getting a bit threadbare. Hmm, good point. Maybe a plush grey one to match the shower curtain? It could tie the whole bathroom together. Now  that  is a good idea. Let's look online later. Just don’t spend all our money before the beanbag is even finished. That’ll be another huge project on top of everything else. Don't worry. I'm a master of multitasking. Now, lentils... on or off the heat first? On the heat, love. On the heat. We wouldn’t want a cold shepherd’s pie now, would we?

Right then, Doris, tea's brewed. Strong, as you like it. Oh, lovely, Arthur. Thank you. You’re a dear. It's just what I needed after that bus journey. Dreadful traffic today, simply dreadful. Morning, you two. Traffic was a nightmare even on the A1, I can confirm. Should have taken the old A10, slower but less stressful. You and your A10, George. Always preaching the virtues of the old ways. Arthur, don’t tease him. He’s got a point, you know. Sometimes the old routes  are  better. Remember when we used to drive to Norfolk, before the M11? Took all day, but it was a proper road trip. Aye, remember those. Stopping at little pubs in wayside villages, proper ale. Not like those fancy craft breweries now. Speaking of proper, did you see that article in  The Times  about the resurgence of traditional pubs? Apparently, people are craving authenticity again. Going back to the basics. Good for them! All these gastropubs with their tiny portions and ridiculous prices… utterly pointless. Give me a pint of bitter and a ploughman’s lunch any day. Hear, hear. Though, a ploughman’s lunch these days... they put things in it you wouldn't believe. Pickled beetroot and… gooseberries! Gooseberries! With cheese! The modern chef’s interpretation, I suppose. Trying to be ‘innovative’. Innovation isn't always a good thing, George. Not when it comes to a good, honest ploughman’s. What’s Doris been up to lately, Arthur? Still knitting those lovely scarves for the charity shop? She is, Doris is. Knits faster than she can buy wool, the woman. Got a whole pile ready for the autumn fair. And what about you, Arthur? Still keeping the garden tidy and battling the squirrels? The squirrels are winning, George. Absolutely winning. They raided the bird feeders again this morning. Little devils. I swear, they're organised. They probably have a squirrel union. Oh, Arthur, you and your squirrels! It's a documented phenomenon actually. Squirrels exhibit surprisingly complex social behaviours. Social behaviours, indeed. They're after my peanuts, that’s all. And I’m not letting them have them without a fight. Well, I’m glad you're keeping them on their toes, Arthur. It's good to have a little excitement in life. Now, tell me, George, how’s your daughter doing with that new business venture? I heard she started selling those artisan chocolates.

Honestly, the supermarket was chaos today. Absolute chaos. You’d think it was Christmas Eve already. Tell me about it. I tried to get in and out of Sainsbury’s in ten minutes. Failed miserably. Ended up spending nearly half an hour wrestling for a marrow. A marrow? Seriously? What are you even doing with a marrow? Soup, love. Winter warmer. You have to make the most of these things when they’re cheap. Keeps you going. I did well, actually. Got a whole chicken for a fiver. Bargain. Five quid?! Where?! Aldi. You have to be quick though, they snap those up. I managed to grab one just before the rush. I’m heading to that new vegan place in town tomorrow. Heard it’s really good. Want to come? Oh, that sounds lovely! I'll check if I can get out of my shift, but I’d really like to. What’s it called again? ‘Root & Bloom’. Apparently, their jackfruit burgers are amazing. Jackfruit? Sounds disgusting. Dad! It tastes exactly like pulled pork. Seriously! I’ll stick to my marrow soup then, thank you very much. Remember Brenda from work? She’s finally going on that trip to Italy she's been talking about for years! Oh, amazing! Whereabouts in Italy is she going? Tuscany, apparently. All vineyards and rolling hills. She's taking her daughter and granddaughter. Said she’s practically bursting with excitement. That’s so cool! Must be a massive culture shock for her, though. She’s never been abroad before, has she? No, not really. Just a couple of trips to France with school. But she’s been saving for ages. It's wonderful that she's getting to do it. I'm considering a trip myself next year, somewhere warm. Maybe Spain? Spain's alright. Bit too many tourists for me though. I prefer somewhere quieter. You’d hate Spain, Dad! Too much sunshine and sangria. There's something to be said for a good grey day, you know. Keeps you grounded. True enough. How's your mum doing, by the way? She's alright. A bit stiff this morning, but nothing major. She's been trying to do some gardening, bless her. We should go and see her next week. Maybe take her some of that chicken you got, Maggie? That’s a lovely idea. And I can bring over some of those shortbread cookies I made.

This coffee is lovely, isn't it? Much better than what I can get back home. It's really quite strong. It is, yes. They roast it themselves, apparently. Bit of a local pride thing. Northern Cyprus, you know, you find a lot of that. People clinging onto what makes them unique. Absolutely. It’s so different from what I expected. I mean, I knew it was Turkish, but it feels…distinct. Are you enjoying your time here, David? Oh, very much so. It's peaceful. That's the main thing for me, after…well, after things. Needed a change. A lot of sunshine helps too. I can imagine. It’s beautiful here. I’m still getting used to driving on the left though! Bit of a shock after all those years in England. Yes, that can be tricky at first. Though, to be honest, the driving here is a bit…relaxed, shall we say? Relaxed is one word for it! I nearly had a heart attack yesterday when someone pulled out right in front of me. So many scooters. Ah yes, the scooters. They rule the roads! But truthfully, it’s chaos everywhere you go. It's a bit like Corfu. Corfu? Really? I’ve never been. Yes, I used to go a lot when I was younger. Same sort of vibe, you know? Laid back. Lovely food. And ridiculously close calls on the roads. You’ll get used to it eventually. I hope so! What’s been your favourite thing to do so far? Aside from drinking excellent coffee, of course. That’s a tough one. I really enjoyed wandering around Girne - Kyrenia – beautiful harbour. Reminds me a bit of Dubrovnik, actually. And Karpaz Peninsula is stunning, so wild and unspoilt. Saw a wild donkey just wandering down the road. A wild donkey! That’s amazing. I’ve been meaning to go out that way. It’s a bit of a drive from here, isn't it? A bit, yes. About an hour and a half, I’d say. But worth it. You should definitely rent a car for a day and go explore. It's just so breathtakingly beautiful; it's like you’re on another planet. I think I will. I've been trying to avoid driving too much, but I'm missing having my own transport a bit. What about the food? Have you tried the halloumi?

Honestly, the marking pile is just… relentless this term. I swear they breed overnight. Tell me about it. My undergraduates seem to think Wikipedia is a valid primary source. I spent half an hour yesterday gently explaining the difference between scholarly articles and… well, you know. The eternal struggle. Did you manage to catch up with Ben and Chloe after your seminar? Briefly. They’re off to Shanghai next week for that conference. Sounds incredible, but also slightly terrifying. All that networking. Oh, I can imagine. I’m really glad I don’t have to travel for anything like that right now. Too much disruption. Though, I do wish I could see them. We should try and video call them. Shanghai time difference will be a bit tricky, but… Definitely. I need to hear about the conference from someone who isn't just spouting jargon. Speaking of, did you get that email from Carol about the departmental social? The one at that fancy tapas place? Yes. I’m trying to decide if I can stomach another evening of forced small talk with half the History department. I know exactly what you mean. Though, at least the tapas are usually decent. And you can’t deny, it's good to see everyone outside of the faculty room. True. But I feel like I’m going to lose a lung just walking down this street. What do you mean? The pollution. It’s getting worse, isn't it? I can practically taste it. I’m starting to miss clean English air. It’s definitely noticeable. Sarah was complaining about it too – her little one’s been coughing a lot. I’ve got a mask in my bag, do you want one? No, I'm alright for now. Just… makes you think, doesn't it? Living here, all this incredible history and culture… but at what cost? It does. Still, we're only here for a year. We’ll appreciate the clean air even more when we go back home. I suppose so. Let's just get back, put our feet up, and try to forget about essays and pollution for a few hours. Sounds like a plan. Are you thinking Chinese takeaway tonight? Now  that  is a good idea. Let's do it. I’ll order. And then maybe we can look at those flight options for visiting Ben and Chloe. Perfect. Let’s head back.

Right, nearly ready to start chopping the veg, then? Smells lovely already. Did you see those photos from our holiday last year, David? Sarah sent them over. I did, actually. Wonderful sunshine wasn’t it? Shame about the… incident with the seagulls, though. Still, good memories. Sarah always does pick good spots for photos. It was pretty hilarious, Dad! Mum’s face when that seagull nicked her chips! Should have framed that one. Don’t you dare! It was mortifying! Still, it’s a good story now. So, Sarah and Tom, are they enjoying the holiday? Photos look amazing. They are, seemingly. She sent me a picture of the beach – looks idyllic. Must be a welcome change from that grey weather we've been having. They’re having a blast. I pinged them a message earlier – they’re currently attempting to learn how to surf. Apparently, Tom’s a natural, Sarah’s a bit more…graceful. Oh, bless her. I'm glad they're having fun. So, what are we having for lunch tomorrow? I was thinking of doing a big salad, with that halloumi we got. Halloumi salad sounds lovely, dear. A bit lighter than roast dinner. Though, I wouldn’t say no to a roast, to be honest. I'm good with the salad, Dad. It's nice to have something refreshing after a day glued to a screen. What about you, Mum? Still enjoying  Bake Off ? Absolutely! It’s my comfort viewing. They’ve got some lovely bakers on this series. Though I still firmly believe Rahul could have won last year. He was very precise. A bit  too  precise, perhaps? Some of those creations were almost engineered, weren't they? You’re just jealous you can't make a perfect choux bun, Dad! Don't be cheeky! I’m perfectly capable of a choux bun. It's just… time-consuming. Right, onions need doing. David, can you get the pepper mill? Certainly. Pepper mill coming right up. Been a busy week have you, love? It has. Lots of new nurses, you know. Trying to get everyone up to speed. Always a challenge. And then there's Mrs. Peterson… she’s been having a particularly difficult time this week. That’s tough. It's so rewarding, though, isn't it? Helping people. It is, despite the challenges. Wouldn't swap it. You having a good week, Sarah? Anything exciting happening with work?

Honestly, this new bus route is a joke, isn’t it? I’ve been trying to get to the city centre for ages and it’s just looping around all these weird streets. Yeah, I noticed that too. It's a bit baffling, isn’t it? Where did they pull that route from? No idea! I think they’re trying to be clever with connecting all these little residential areas, but it’s making the journey longer, not shorter. I used to get into town in twenty minutes, now it’s pushing half an hour. It’s a classic Cambridge council decision, isn't it? Overcomplicating things. Did you go into the Cambridge University Press bookshop the other day? I was in there looking for a particular engineering textbook. I did! It was rammed, as usual. I was trying to find something on corpus linguistics, but they didn't seem to have much. It’s always a bit chaotic in there, isn't it? It is. They’ve got a decent selection of classics, but for more specialist stuff, you're better off ordering online. Oh, and did you see what happened with that student protester yesterday? No! What happened? I’ve been buried in data all week. Apparently, he chained himself to the railings outside Senate House. Something about the university's investment in fossil fuels. It caused a bit of a stir. Oh wow, that's intense. It wouldn't happen in Sunderland, would it? We’re a bit more… reserved, I think. Definitely. It’s just classic Cambridge, though. They take their activism pretty seriously. What’s the atmosphere like at your uni then, compared to here? Is it all studying and meritocracy, or more of a social scene? Well, it used to be a lot more studying, to be honest. Now there’s loads of protests, lots of diversity drives. But its still very academic, very focused on research. People are fiercely competitive. What's it like at your uni? It's a mix. There's definitely pressure to succeed, particularly in engineering. But everyone's surprisingly sociable. It's a bit posh, though, isn't it? Lots of people come from very privileged backgrounds. Do you ever feel that difference? Sometimes, yeah. Like, everyone's talking about their gap years in Patagonia or something, and I'm thinking about trying to save up for a train ticket home.

Honestly, the best thing about retiring is being able to just… relax. No more marking exams, thank heavens. Though, I do miss the kids, a bit. I can imagine. It must be a massive shift. How's Michael settling in with you in Cumbria? Is he enjoying the countryside? He seems to be, yes. A bit quiet, perhaps. He’s always been a bit of a homebody, you know? But he makes a decent cup of tea, which is a start! And he’s attempting to bake. The results are… variable. Oh, I love that! A retired maths teacher and a son attempting to bake – sounds like a recipe for chaos. Precisely! Yesterday he tried to make a Victoria sponge. It resembled… well, not a Victoria sponge. It was dense. Very, very dense. Oh no! Did you intervene? Of course! I gently suggested a few adjustments. A little more baking powder, perhaps? Less flour? He just looked at me with that ‘I’m a grown man’ look. Classic. Speaking of food, this lunch looks incredible! This little place in Cheshire is a gem. It really is. And so nice to get out and about, isn't it? I've barely left the house myself this week. Deadline madness. Editing a particularly tricky medical transcript. So much jargon. Jargon, eh? You English have such a knack for creating it. We do, don't we? Trying to explain the intricacies of a particular enzyme to a layperson… it’s a challenge, that’s for sure. So, Maive, has Liam confirmed his visit yet? For Christmas? He’s saying he's 'probably' going to make it. You know Liam. 'Probably' could mean anything. He’s a busy man with consultancy work, apparently. Poor thing. Always working. Has he said when he’s planning on coming? He said potentially the week before Christmas, but said he'd let me know. I just want him here! It wouldn't be Christmas without him. He'll be here. You know he loves a good roast dinner. And your mince pies! Those are legendary. Oh, I do make a decent mince pie. Always have. Michael is still trying to figure out the secret. They aren't too sweet. The perfect balance. Speaking of, did you manage to sort out Millie's school uniform? She needs new shoes, doesn't she? Yes, thankfully! I went into town yesterday and found some lovely ones.

Honestly, look at that sky. Absolutely glorious, isn’t it? Though it does threaten rain, doesn’t it? It does, a bit. But the light’s lovely on the water. You can just make out the O2 from here, can't you? It looks like a giant glass eyebrow. It really does! I still can't believe how big it is. We should have gone to a concert there when we had the chance. Remember that email? Vaguely. Something about Coldplay, wasn’t it? Seems a lifetime ago. Still, good thing we don’t own a car, imagine battling that traffic getting back. Exactly! A nightmare scenario. Walking along the river like this is much better. It’s peaceful. Though I do wish there weren't so many tourists taking selfies in front of every single landmark. Tell me about it. Trying to get a decent photo is impossible. You know, I was thinking about that holiday to Cornwall we’re planning with the kids… Oh, yes! Nearly forgot about that. Booking flights is a source of constant stress. So, are we sticking with that little cottage near St Ives then? That’s the plan. Though I’m worried about space. Three kids and two adults in a cottage... it’ll be like sardines. We'll manage. Remember that recipe I found for scones? I'm thinking of making them fresh every morning. Lovely! But please, no American cup measurements. Trying to convert cups to grams is a recipe for disaster. “One and a half cups of flour… that’s about… somewhere between 180 and 220 grams, give or take.” It's infuriating! You’re right. Metric all the way for me! Though, you know, it got me thinking... why do we even  need  measurements? Isn’t cooking just about feeling it? About intuition? Oh, here we go with the philosophical questions again. It’s just baking, love! But seriously! What's the point of striving for precision in everything? Doesn’t it take away some of the joy? What’s happiness itself, if not a kind of imprecise feeling? Right. Well, happy scones are definitely a precision-dependent thing. We’ll stick to the recipe. Woolwich Arsenal, there's a landmark. They're certainly making a play for the top six. Do you think they’ll make it? It's a long shot, but with a bit of luck… Do you know, even  that , "a bit of luck," is just another imprecise measurement.

Honestly, this rain is never ending. I’ve worn my raincoat every single day this week! It's depressing. Tell me about it, love. It's awful for the old bones. Makes everything feel damp and dreary. Still, at least the garden's getting a good watering. Speaking of dreary… how was Leo's sports day? Did he win anything? Oh my goodness, it was a total disaster. Well, not  disaster , but chaotic. The rain started halfway through the egg and spoon race, and everyone was slipping and sliding. He nearly dropped his egg three times! Bless him! They don’t make it easy, do they? All that competitive spirit when they're just little ones. He loves a good race though, doesn’t he? Remember when he used to race around the kitchen table, shouting "I'm the fastest!"? Oh, vividly. And he’d always trip over the rug! It’s a wonder he didn’t break a leg. Anyway, he didn’t win, but he did get a participation medal, which seemed to make him happy enough. Tilly was more interested in the bouncy castle, obviously. Bouncy castles are always a winner. Remember when little Emily used to be terrified of them? Cried every time! She was! Then she suddenly got the hang of it one day and wouldn’t come down. Stuck up there like a little monkey! She still has that little teddy she took with her that day, Mr. Floppy. Oh, Tilly has a whole army of teddies! It’s ridiculous. She’s got that Build-a-Bear she made last year, Bartholomew, that she takes  everywhere . Build-a-Bear… pricey things, those. My granddaughter’s got three. One’s got a little recording in it that says, "I love you, Grandma!" Nearly makes me cry every time. Leo insists on cuddling his dinosaur, Rexy, even though he's practically a teenager. I'm trying to gradually phase them out, but it’s a battle. I know! It’s the same with Tilly and her teddies. I’m thinking of trying to subtly donate a few when we clear out her toys... maybe to a charity shop. Good idea, love. That’s a kind thing to do. Now, is anyone else watching that show about swimming in English lakes? It's on tonight. Oh, no! I swear, everytime I think about swimming openly in water, I remember trying to teach Amy to flush the toilet, she would just cover her hands in poo and then pop it over the side.

Right, so I was thinking, beyond the usual "grow the business by X percent" kind of goals, what are we actually  wanting  to achieve in the next year or so? You know, personally. That's a good question. It's easy to get so bogged down in the entrepreneurial stuff, isn’t it? I think for me, it's about feeling… less frazzled. Less constantly ‘on’. I’d really like to find a decent balance. Maybe a yoga class? Something consistently, rather than just sporadically. Yoga sounds dreamy. I'm terrible at consistency though, you know me. I need something with a bit more...kick. I was thinking about finally getting that coding certification. There are a couple of decent online options, and it feels like it would be a really valuable skill, both professionally and just for keeping the brain ticking over. That’s brilliant, actually. Really practical. And you've been talking about wanting to explore that side of things for ages. It would be such a boost to your skillset. Exactly. What about you, career-wise? Still feeling content with teaching? Mostly, yeah. I do love the kids, genuinely. But I’m starting to think about a bit of professional development, perhaps. There’s a mentoring programme at school, which could be interesting, or maybe a short course on SEN. Just to refresh things. That sounds great. We could look into those together, maybe. Sharing ideas. That would be lovely. It’s always easier when you’ve got someone bouncing things around with you, isn't it? On a completely different tangent… did you hear from Liam and Chloe? About their plans. Just a quick text this morning, actually. They’re serious about trying for another one. Said they’re going to start properly in the new year. Oh, wow! That's exciting. And a little daunting, I imagine. Absolutely. But lovely for them. We should definitely make an effort to see them more. It feels like we haven't properly caught up in ages. Agreed. Maybe we could organise a weekend away with them? Somewhere relatively close, but still a change of scenery. That's a fantastic idea! Somewhere in the Margaret River region, perhaps? We could look at some of those lovely little beachside cottages. Yes! And we could rope in Amelia and Ben too. A proper catch-up. They've been pretty quiet lately. Excellent.

Honestly, I can’t beat this weather, can you? Proper summer vibes. It really is lovely – perfect for a pub garden. Did you see Amy's Insta story? She's camping. Aye, saw it! Looks freezing though, doesn't it? Like, proper misty. You'd need a full duvet and hot water bottle. Camping’s not for me. Too many creepy crawlies. I’d much rather be playing Pokémon Go. Speaking of, have you guys seen the new update? There's a special event going on. Oh yeah? I keep forgetting to play. I’m too busy stressing about work. Audit season is a nightmare. Tell me about it. You're working hard though, aren't you? Putting in the hours. I am. Trying to. It's just… like, the other day, I was explaining something to a client, and he just looked at me like I’d grown another head. It was so awkward. Oh, bless. Some people just don't get it, do they? Remember when Liam tried to explain blockchain to his grandma? Classic Liam. He was red-faced for a week after that. He was trying so hard to sound clever. Honestly, some people have no manners. I had this bloke on the bus last week, just coughing all over the place without even a tissue. It was disgusting. Oh god, the audacity. It's a fight-or-flight response every time, isn't it? Like, do you confront them, or do you just move as far away as possible? Definitely flight for me. Confrontation isn't my strong suit. I'd just stand there, panicking. I'd probably try to be polite, say “Excuse me, could you maybe cover your mouth?” And then they'd just glare at you. I'd just move. Escape. Find a new seat. This conversation is making me hungry. Fancy some chips? Yes please! Actually, can someone nip to the shop for After-Eights? I’m having a serious craving. I can do that. Anyone want anything else? I’ll have a Coke. Thanks, 5. Don't forget the mints! While you're there, could you grab some batteries for my Fitbit? It's died again. So, , you mentioned work being stressful. Have you looked at that new app everyone’s talking about? It’s supposed to help with managing your time. You mean the one with all the notifications? No way!

Well, I tell you what, that football match this afternoon…shocking! Absolutely shocking! Didn’t see that result coming at all. It was dreadful, wasn’t it? Absolutely dreadful. I was so hoping for a win, but they just didn’t seem to be at it today. Though, I am rather peckish now. This roast smells heavenly, dear. It is good, Mum. Dad, you were right to say we should get goose this year. It feels more festive. Absolutely. Much better than the usual chicken we have. Thanks for doing this, ANON. It's a lovely change from our flat. Nonsense, nonsense, it’s my pleasure. Always good to have the family round. Especially when someone’s cooked such a splendid meal. Though, I did see that new series on the telly last night…political drama. Bit depressing, really. Oh, don't talk to me about politics! It's all a load of tosh, isn't it? Never a good thing said, always arguing. Give me a nice baking show any day. So, are you all still planning that Christmas party? Yes, we are. We’ve booked the village hall, but we’re still figuring out the decorations. It’s hard to get everyone to agree on anything! I offered to do the music. I’ve put together a playlist of classic Christmas songs – nothing too cheesy, I promise. Oh, good man. Always good to have a bit of music. Though, I do rather like a good carol myself. "Silent Night," that’s a proper Christmas carol, that is. You and your carols, George! You’ll be leading the whole village in song. Anything exciting happening at work, Amelia? Not much, really. Just prepping lectures and marking essays. The students are getting stressed about their finals already. It’s a bit chaotic, but it’s all part of the job. Same here, Liam. Preparing for my seminars, trying to keep up with the research. It feels like there’s never enough time. Never is, lad. Never is. When I was a lad, we were always busy. Helping on the farm, you know. Never a dull moment. Oh, your farm stories, George! We've heard them all a hundred times. Though, I do enjoy them. Remember that time you chased that cow through the market square? Ah yes! That was a tricky one, that was. Old Bess, she was a rebel. Didn’t like being herded.

Honestly, I’m starting to seriously think about just...not finishing this year. Blimey, really? What's brought that on? Everything alright? I just... I can’t seem to get my head around any of it.
