Lectures feel pointless, the readings are overwhelming, and I’m just constantly exhausted. It feels like I'm wading through treacle. Yeah, uni IS a right slog sometimes. I get it. It’s not like the brochures make it sound. Remember when we were kids and we thought going to uni would be all library cafes and instant ramen? Oh god, yeah. And knowing everything instantly. I’m starting to think I was better off just… doing something else. Like, what was I even hoping to achieve? Don't say that! It's just a rough patch. What kind of something else were you thinking? I don’t know. Something practical, I guess. My nan used to say I was always fiddling with things, making stuff. Maybe something design-related, but… less academic. Hmm. Have you spoken to anyone about this? Student services? A lecturer? Not really. Feels a bit embarrassing, you know? Like I’m failing. Failing? Nah. Trying to figure out what’s right for you isn't failing. It’s mature. Look, my cousin Liam dropped out of uni after a year, and he’s doing alright. He’s a mechanic now and he loves it. A mechanic? Really? Yeah! Said he feels like he’s actually  doing  something. Anyway, did you see what state your shoes were in when you came in? Honestly, you could grow penicillin on them. Don't remind me. I was traipsing through that muddy field on the way back from the library. Worth it for the view, though. Worth it for the view and now my carpet is covered in mud. Seriously, you've got more dirt on your trainers than my dad does after a gardening weekend. Sorry! I'll clean them. Speaking of mud, do you remember when we were little and we built that huge fort in your garden? The one that collapsed the second my dad tried to walk past it? Oh my god, yeah. That was iconic. Building it took us like, three days. And then your mum made us have tea on a picnic blanket in the rain. Classic Mum move. She always said we had to "appreciate the outdoors."

Honestly, this risotto is  divine . I'm so glad we finally made this happen. It feels like ages since we properly caught up. Tell me about it! Life's been a whirlwind. This place is gorgeous too, Oxford is always so pretty. Proper treat after the week I've had. Seriously! You look exhausted, what's been going on at Pearson? Ugh, don't even get me started. New marketing campaign launch and it’s been absolute chaos. So much pressure to hit targets, and honestly, some of the ideas they’re pushing are just… ridiculous. Like, promoting paper textbooks in 2024? Seriously? Oh, the irony! At least you’re not dealing with spreadsheets all day like I am. My project's hit a snag with the budget, which means endless meetings trying to justify every single penny. Sounds stressful. Are you going to be able to pull it off? I think so. It’s just… tedious. I’m starting to dream in pivot tables, I swear. What about you? Any fun projects you’re actually excited about? Not really, no. They're talking about a student engagement campaign, which could be interesting, but it's still early days. I'm desperately trying to save up for a deposit, though. The property market is insane, isn't it? Don’t remind me! I'm trying to get on the ladder too. I’ve been looking at places in Richmond, but they're all tiny and ridiculously expensive. Richmond! Fancy! I was thinking maybe somewhere a bit further out. Manchester, perhaps? My cousin’s got a place there, and it’s a lot more affordable. Manchester? Hmm, not really my vibe, is it? Though, you’re right about affordability. I did see a listing in Reading that actually looked promising… Reading? Seriously? That sounds… bleak. It’s growing on me, actually. Good transport links, decent schools… you know, the whole nine yards. I’m thinking long term, you know? Eventually, kids, the works. Wow, ambitious! I’m not even thinking about kids yet. Though… remember Liam from university? He’s just got engaged. Oh, really? Liam with the questionable fashion sense? That’s surprising! I know! Apparently, she’s lovely. They're having the wedding in Cornwall next summer. I'm tempted to go, but it’s a long way. We should definitely go! It’d be good to see him, and the Cornish coast is beautiful.

Right then, have a look at this. I've been searching for a replacement handle for that old tea chest. You know, the one Great Aunt Mildred left us? Yeah, the one that’s falling apart? Is it any good? Well, according to this eBay listing, it's a genuine reproduction. Says it's from the same maker, too. Only £12.99 with free postage! Can you believe it? Twelve ninety-nine? That’s not bad. Amazon wanted how much for one? Don’t even start on Amazon. They wanted nearly twenty quid! And postage on top. It’s daylight robbery, isn’t it? Definitely. Amazon’s all about inflated prices, innit? Everything's got that Prime mark on it, trying to convince you to pay more. Exactly! I try and avoid it now unless it’s something I absolutely need. This eBay seller seems decent, good reviews. Got loads of them, proper reliable. Have you checked they’ll actually post it? Some of them on eBay, they list things but then you try to buy it and they say ‘Oh, sorry, we’ve run out’ or something. Good point, love. Just had a look, says ‘In Stock’ and ‘Ready for Immediate Dispatch’. See? Sorted. Right. So, should you bid on it? Or just buy it? It's marked as 'Buy it Now', thankfully. No need to get into a bidding war over a tea chest handle. Let's just get it done. Smart. It's always better to buy it now, especially when you know what you want. Less hassle. Exactly. I’ve got my card details saved, so it’ll be a matter of a few clicks. Just gotta double-check the address is correct. Don’t want it turning up at some random person’s house. No! That would be embarrassing. Remember when Nan ordered that bird feeder and it went to someone in Scarborough? She was fuming. Oh, I remember! Poor Nan! Had to trek all the way down there to get it back. Makes you think, doesn't it? It does. Technology's supposed to make things easier, but sometimes it just causes a right kerfuffle. That’s the truth. Right, address looks good. Clicking 'Confirm Payment' now… There we go. Paid. Sorted! When do you reckon it’ll arrive? They’ve said 3-5 working days, so hopefully by next week. I can’t wait to get the tea chest sorted.

So, the new flat's coming along okay, Dad? You said you were thinking of getting some new curtains. Oh, it is, it is. Quite alright, actually. Bit bare, still. Needs a bit of… softening, you know? The curtains are definitely on the list. Been looking online. Bit of a nightmare, all the choices. I can help with that if you like. I'm pretty good at interiors, you know. I could have a look with you, or at least send you some links to things I think you’d like. That'd be lovely, really. Don’t want to end up with something ghastly, do you? Last thing I need is to be stuck looking at the same floral monstrosity all day. No, absolutely not. So, what else have you been up to? Apart from battling curtain catalogues, that is. Oh, you know. The usual. Watching the telly, reading. Got that biography of Churchill you lent me. Quite a slog, that one. Dry as dust in places. Yeah, he wasn't exactly known for his brevity, was he? But fascinating nonetheless. How's the neighbourhood treating you? Making any new friends? A few. There's a gentleman across the street, Mr. Henderson. Quite the talker. Tells me all about his prize-winning roses. Apparently, the secret’s in the manure. Sounds like a character. It's good to have someone to chat to. It is, yes. It gets lonely otherwise. Though I do enjoy my own company. Had a bit of a scare the other day, actually. Oh no, what happened? Went to get a loaf of bread, you see, and when I came back, the door wouldn't open. Locked myself out! No! Dad, that's awful! How did you manage that? No idea! Must have bumped the lock or something. Anyway, young chap from number 12 came to the rescue. Had to call a locksmith, of course. Cost me a pretty penny, that did. I’m glad you’re alright. You should get a spare key hidden somewhere, just in case. Good idea, that. I’ll have a word with Mr. Henderson. He’s got a shed full of useful things, I’m sure he'll have a spare key box. Right you are. So, any plans for this weekend? Thinking of going into town. See a bit of the world, you know? It’s been a while.

Right, so flights are looking insane. Seriously, Christmas Day flights are like, three times the usual price. Anyone actually considering it? Me? Absolutely not. Remember last Christmas when Dad tried to convince us to fly to New York? Nearly bankrupted us. And for what? To spend six hours in various airports? Yeah, no thanks. I’m happy with a vaguely chaotic Christmas here. At least the chaos is familiar. Who’s cooking this year? I'm throwing in a Yule log, obviously. Yeah, Christmas Day flying is a nightmare. Tried it once, felt like I’d aged ten years. Stick to a nice relaxed stay-at-home Christmas, that’s my motto. I’m happy to throw together a pavlova, that’s my specialty. Pavlova sounds amazing! Maybe that’ll tempt me to actually leave the flat. What about the main roast? Are we doing turkey again? I reckon we should spice things up. My mum’s doing the turkey, bless her. It’ll be traditional. Probably sprouts as well, much to everyone’s dismay. Want stuffing? Stuffing is essential! I might do a vegetarian one, with chestnuts and cranberries. It’s surprisingly good. Proper stuffing, with sausage meat, that’s the way to go. Can’t go wrong with a bit of meaty goodness. Speaking of food, you guys see that poor deer on the A40 this morning? Hit by a car. Horrible sight. Oh gosh, really? That's awful. It's getting worse, isn't it? All the foxes around too, bolder than ever. It is. I saw a fox wandering around my café car park the other day, brazen as you like. Sniffing at the bins. We get ‘em all the time back home, too. They’re crafty little buggers. Always scavenging. I was thinking about it, and it’s just… sad. They’re struggling. The deer especially, with the cold. Definitely. Maybe we should donate to the wildlife rescue centre this year instead of, you know, another scented candle. Good idea! I’m in. We could even collect donations at the café. That’s a top idea. Always good to give back. Speaking of giving, anyone need help with Christmas presents? I can get you some killer deals from some Aussie suppliers. Actually, yes! I'm completely lost on what to get for my little brother. He's obsessed with… well, everything vintage at the moment. Vintage, huh?

Right, so I’m still convinced you’re doing that posh accent on purpose, Chloe. It's brilliant, though. I’m quite certain I’m not, Finn. It’s simply my natural timbre, darling. Must be all those years of editing highbrow literary journals. Oh, please. You’ve been watching too many period dramas. Your accent was perfectly normal when we left London. Nonsense, Matty. One’s elocution must adapt to one’s surroundings. Cambridge is frightfully… refined. Refined? It’s full of students in hoodies and cycling everywhere. Precisely. One must maintain a certain level of dignity. You’re killing me, Chloe. So, are we there yet, Finn? This sat-nav is being incredibly vague. “In 200 yards, proceed with caution.” Caution from  what  exactly? Should be any minute now. This countryside is gorgeous though, isn't it? I'm glad we took this route instead of the A10. Much nicer drive. It is rather pleasant. Though I do believe this car could benefit from a little… refinement. It’s rather…agricultural. Hey! There's nothing wrong with my Fiesta. It gets me from A to B. And it’s reliable, unlike some people's vintage Land Rovers. Ouch! Low blow, Finn. You know Amelia adores her Landy. It’s an investment piece, Matty. It's practically a classic. Right, well, here we are. Nearly there. See, I told you it’d be scenic. Just down this lane and we’re at ANON’s place. Finally! I’m starving. And my back’s killing me. Honestly, Matty, you’re always complaining. Blame the Fiesta’s springs. Just get out, okay? And be nice to Chloe. She’s trying to embrace the local culture. One must. It’s terribly important. Besides, I quite like being posh. You’re incorrigible. Right, let’s go find some cake. ANON promised cake, remember? Cake is the only reason I agreed to this trip. Lead on! One simply  must  indulge, darling. It's the civilized thing to do. And,  whispering  It’s very clever what you’re doing with the accent Finn! Much better than mine! Just enjoying the ride, Chloe. Just enjoying the ride. Now, let's get out of the car before you develop a monocle. Hopefully, that captures the tone and context of the conversation! Let me know if you’d like any adjustments. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .H.H..

Did you hear that new Arctic Monkeys track? The one they dropped yesterday? Yeah! It’s proper good, innit? Definitely a return to form. Much better than the last album. I thought it was alright. A bit… predictable, maybe? Predictable? No way! The guitar riffs are insane. And Alex’s lyrics are proper clever this time. Yeah, Alex is back! Remember when he was writing about… I don't know, lobster telephones and stuff? This actually  means  something. I guess. It just felt a bit… safe. Like they were trying too hard to be ‘cool’ again instead of just being themselves. Safe? Come on! It’s got that edgy vibe, like their early stuff. You're just being difficult. Nah, I’m with Liam on this one. It's got a classic sound but modern touches. Reminds me a bit of that early Strokes stuff, you know? Yeah, maybe a little. Speaking of music, did you guys see that doc about David Bowie on BBC iPlayer? No! Was it any good? Brilliant! Loads of unseen footage. Really showed how much he was always experimenting and pushing boundaries. I’ve got loads more respect for him now. I love Bowie. Need to watch that. So, physics test tomorrow – anyone actually revised?  groans  Don’t remind me. I’m completely lost on everything to do with quantum entanglement. It's mad, like, particles being linked together even if they're miles apart. Yeah, it’s pretty trippy. Mr. Davies just goes on and on about Schrodinger's cat. Like, who cares about a cat in a box? It’s meant to be an illustration, man! It demonstrates the concept of superposition. Well, it just confuses me. I wish we were studying film instead. Speaking of which, did you guys see Oppenheimer? Yeah! It was incredible. Three hours long, though. My bum went numb. Worth it though. Nolan is a genius. The way he showed the science, and the moral complexities… proper thought-provoking. The visuals were insane! The Trinity test scene was actually scary. Cillian Murphy’s acting was on another level. Def his best role. Proper haunting. Maybe I'll watch it again. I already have. Twice. It’s got me reading up on the Manhattan Project now. You're a geek, mate. Hey, knowledge is power! Besides, it connects to physics! See? It all comes together. Alright, alright, Professor. Let’s just promise each other we’ll actually try and understand quantum entanglement before tomorrow's test.

Right, so how was Balanceability today? Did you two manage to keep your feet on? Almost! I wobbled a lot. I did it! I went all the way around the track without falling off! Wow! That’s brilliant, mate! So proud of you! See, you're getting really good. It takes practice, doesn't it? It's not about being the best straightaway, it's about sticking at it and being able to say "I did that." Yeah! And I went really really fast! I bet you did! That’s fantastic. You know, it’s like trying to learn something new, any new skill. Sometimes you don’t get it right the first time – or the tenth! – but you just keep trying. Remember when I was trying to learn to make proper sourdough bread? Disasters. Absolute disasters. Mummy’s bread exploded! It did! It literally exploded! But now, I can make a pretty decent loaf. It's all about not giving up. Did you have any funny conversations at school today, sweetheart? Lily’s house is being fixed up! It’s got a swimming pool! And a fake waterfall! A whatfall? A waterfall, but it’s… not real! It's made. A manmade waterfall. Fancy that! Does that mean it’s safe to dive in? No! You can hurt yourself! Exactly! You know, my cousin once dived into a paddling pool thinking it was deep and he got a really bad bump on his head. Never dive into water you can’t see the bottom of. It’s not worth it. Miss told us about Japan today. Oh yeah? What did you learn? They celebrate National Cat Day! With lots of cat treats! I want cat treats. We don't have any cat treats here, I'm afraid. Although, you're kind of like a little kitten sometimes. Always wanting something! Now, about dinner. What are we all feeling? I was thinking pizza tonight. Pizza! Pepperoni and pineapple! Pineapple? Really? You know that’s a controversial pizza topping, don't you? I like pineapple on pizza! It's sweet and salty! You two have very different tastes. It's a bit like mushrooms, isn't it? Some people love them, some people hate them. How about we have half with pepperoni and pineapple, and half just with cheese? That way we all get something we like. Okay! And can we have chips too?

Honestly, I’m absolutely beat. This conference was a nightmare. Catering disasters, speakers dropping out… the lot. Oh, no way! That sounds horrendous. You’ve been working ridiculously long hours, haven’t you? You look knackered. Tell me about it. I think I’ve forgotten what a normal bedtime feels like. I need, like, a week-long spa retreat. Or just a solid twelve hours sleep. You absolutely do. Have you managed any exercise this week? You said you were trying to get back into running. Running? What’s running? I've barely left my desk! I did a few stretches at my desk during one of the particularly stressful moments, but that’s about it. My legs feel like lead. You need to prioritise it, honestly. Even just a twenty-minute walk can make a difference. It clears your head, you know? I've been hitting the gym most evenings, feeling loads better. I know, I know you're right. It's just… lacking the motivation. And the energy. So, what's the gossip then? Aside from the conference chaos. Anything exciting happening? Not really. Mark’s still being… Mark. Oh, spill. What's he doing now? Being mysteriously unavailable again? Essentially. He said he’s “really busy” this weekend. Again. It's always something. Ugh, that’s infuriating. Honestly, if he can't make time for you, what's the point? I keep telling myself that. But then he’ll do something sweet, and I’ll start questioning myself again. Classic. You’re way too good to him, you know? You deserve someone who puts you first. Seriously. I know, I know. It's just… hard. Been together so long. Long and unhappy isn’t better than short and happy, you know? I’m serious. Don't waste your time on someone who doesn’t appreciate you. Remember that awful date I had last month? That no-show? Oh god, yes! The one who cancelled an hour before. The very same. I was gutted at the time, but you know what? I'm glad it didn't work out. Avoided a whole load of nonsense. True. Okay, you’re right. I need to have a proper chat with him. Maybe next week, when I’m not completely brain-fried. Good. And in the meantime, maybe treat yourself to a nice bath and a face mask. Self-care is essential, especially when you’re dealing with Mark drama.

Right then, finished your pizza, lad? Don't want any left-overs lurking under the sofa. Aye, all gone, Auntie Maureen. That was champion, though. Pepperoni and mushroom – can’t beat it. Best Domino's we've had in ages. Aye, they've upped their game, haven't they? Used to be a bit soggy, but this was cracking. Worth the twenty quid, even with the extra dips. Twenty quid! Honestly, the price of things these days. Remember when you could get a pizza and a couple of drinks for a fiver, George? Aye, and a packet of crisps thrown in! Simpler times, lass. Simpler times. Speaking of times, how was the dominoes tonight? Did you win? Oh, a right shambles, George. Mrs. Henderson had a blinder. Cleared the board three times running. Beat me fair and square. Did you try that trick you were showing me, Auntie Maureen? With the double tap? I did, love, but it didn’t work as well as I’d hoped. Too many people watching. They were all laughing! They were probably just jealous of your skill, Maureen. You're a formidable opponent when you're on form. Did young Daniel get his Easter presents yet? Not yet, Uncle George. Mum's still shopping. She promised me a new football shirt. Good lad! And I got you that book you wanted, Daniel, the one about the history of football. Be having your nose stuck in that for weeks, I expect. Cheers, Auntie Maureen. I appreciate it. Right, I'm off home now. Just need to get this log back in the fireplace before it tries to escape again. It’s been sliding out all night! Nearly took a chunk out of the carpet. Be careful, George. You’d better get Brian to have a look at that hearth. It's getting worse, isn’t it? Aye, he says it’s the settling of the house. Everything settles eventually, doesn't it? Just like me! Starting to feel every one of my sixty-eight years. You’re not old, Uncle George! You’re just experienced. That's a good one, lad. Experienced! I’ll tell your mum that one. Say I'm experienced, not old. You should get your hair cut, George, love. It's getting a bit… wild. Looking like a scarecrow! Aye, you’re right. It’s a fright, isn’t it? Might pop down to Colin's on Tuesday.

Right, so I reckon we've got enough water boiling for a decent pot? It's freezing in here, isn’t it? Yeah, definitely enough. And you're right, it's a bit nippy. Should’ve put the heating on before you arrived. Sorry about that. Nah, don't worry about it. I’m used to a bit of chill. Sunderland winters are a different beast altogether. At least this isn’t rain and wind battering the windows. True. Fancy a digestive with your tea? I got some nice ones from the market yesterday. Ooh yes, please. Biscuits are essential during cold weather like this. Not the jammy ones, the plain ones, if you’ve got them. Got loads of the plain ones. I’m trying to eat a bit healthier, you see. Been experimenting with growing veg. Oh really? What have you got going on? You, a gardener? Never thought I'd see the day! It’s a struggle, honestly. I've got some tomatoes, a few courgettes… and some rocket that’s gone completely berserk. Taking over the entire patio. Typical. Rocket’s always a rogue. My nan used to say it grows like bindweed. Exactly! Honestly, I'm thinking of just letting it take over. Might as well be a rocket farm. You could be famous! Rocket man. Don't even go there. Anyway, I saw Taylor Swift was in Cambridge last week. Apparently she had a pint at The Eagle. No way! The Eagle? That's mental. It's a tourist trap, isn’t it? Apparently enjoyed it anyway. Always loved that place for a quick drink – good atmosphere. I’ve not been there in ages. Need to pop in when I’m next up. Speaking of drinks and food, what about that Thai place we tried last month? The one on Mill Road? Oh, yeah! That was brilliant. Best Pad See Ew I’ve had in ages. I’m thinking we should go again next week. Definitely. I’m craving something spicy. Although, maybe if the rocket's still rampant, we could have a salad straight from your garden? That's the spirit! Though bearing in mind the rocket situation, it might just be a rocket salad. I'm game for anything! Just as long as there are biscuits involved. Now, where's that milk? It’s proper chilly in here. It’s in the fridge.

Right, okay, my turn. "Duct Tape." Anyone? Hmm, tricky one! Is it allowed to be, like, a compound word, or does it have to be a single word? Rules, Rhys! The rules clearly state single words only. Remember last time, when you tried to get away with "Honeycomb?" Don't remind me! That was embarrassing. Okay, okay. "Duct Tape…" uh… Desk? No, that doesn’t work. Desert! Good one, Dad! Desert it is. Okay, Rhys, your turn to explain. Alright, alright. It was a tough one! I was thinking… Door, but that didn’t seem right. Then… Deep? No. I was panicking. You were definitely panicking. You went all red. Poor Rhys! You just need to think about words starting with "D" that aren’t common. Like, “Draft” – that would have worked too. Yeah, well, hindsight is a wonderful thing, isn’t it? Now it’s your go, Elin. Don't give us something impossible. Alright, alright. Let's see… "Palestine." Elin! Seriously?! That’s deliberately difficult! It’s a word! And the clever thing is, I know it’s going to be hard. Dad, you're up first. Prepare to be stumped. Palestine… hmm. That’s a proper head-scratcher. Fishing! Dad! How did you even…? Just a lucky guess. Been playing this game a long time, you see. Besides, I’m pretty good with geography. It’s true, your general knowledge is exceptional, Dai. I’m impressed. Okay, my turn to have a go. “Palestine…” Perhaps… Paint? No! Rhys, you have to be more creative! That’s so obvious. It is obvious. It’s almost insulting, Elin to give us ‘Palestine’ then accept Paint. Give us something truly challenging. Oh, alright, alright. Okay, next word… “Quizzical." Oh, Elin, you are wicked! That’s sneaky. Rhodes, you’re up. Quizzical… Quick? No... Quill? Oh, this is ridiculous! You're just trying to wind me up. You're moaning unfairly! I'm honestly impressed that you didn’t go with “Quiz” immediately. That would have been far too easy. Although... Don’t you dare think about it! You're next, Haf. Don’t you even try cheating us. Cheating? Me? Never! Let me see... “Quizzical…” quite… no... Queen! Queen it is! And so on… Haf...

Right, my turn! I'm going to lay down a seven of hearts. Anyone got anything to beat that? Let's see…let’s see… Ah! I’ve got a nine of diamonds, Gareth! Take that, Sarah! Always showing off, Gareth. You’re terrible at this game, you know. Now, now, Rhys. Don’t be unkind. He’s just having a bit of luck. Let’s see, I’ll play a Queen of spades then. Ooh, Queen of spades! Alright, that’s a decent play. I don’t have anything to beat that, so you win that round, Margaret. Blimey! You’re on a roll, Margaret. Should've known you'd have something up your sleeve! She always does! She’s got a poker face like you wouldn’t believe! You'd never know what she's holding. Years of playing against your grandfather, Rhys. He taught me a few tricks. He’d always say, “A smile and a bluff, boy, that’s the key!” Oh, I love hearing stories about your grandfather, Margaret. He sounds like a character. He was! A right character! Remember that time he tried to teach the cat to play whist? Oh, goodness! I’d completely forgotten about that! The cat just scratched him, didn’t it? Yes, a right indignant scratch it gave him! He blamed the cat’s Welsh blood, of course. Said it was too proud to follow the rules. He sounds absolutely wonderful. Right, my turn again. Let's see... I’ll play a Jack of clubs. Okay… I’ll play a six of diamonds. Trying to lay low this time. Hmm. I’ll play a four of hearts, just to keep things interesting. Let’s see... Let’s see… Oh, you’re all bluffing! I’ve got a king! A King of hearts! Rhys! You’ve ruined it! Rhys, you little sneak! You were saving that card, weren’t you? Well played, Rhys! You definitely pulled that one out of the bag! Now, who wants tea and biscuits? All this card playing has made me peckish. Definitely tea and biscuits. And maybe another round? Even if Rhys  does  have all the luck. I've been practicing, you know. It's a Welsh thing. We’re naturally good at bluffing. We all know it's just your mischievous nature, Rhys. Now, let's go get those biscuits! Exactly! Come on. You can try to beat me again later. .

Ugh, I'm so bored. Anyone seen anything good on Netflix recently? "Bridgerton" is still pretty good! They just released a new season. Oh yeah! I've been meaning to watch that. Is it as cheesy as everyone says? A little, but in a good way! It’s just fun, you know? Lighthearted. I’ve been rewatching "The Office" again. Classic. Never gets old. My mum’s obsessed with it. We've watched every episode at least five times. Seriously! Anyway, so Amelia, how’s the uni application process going? Still stressing? Loads! It's just a constant cycle of writing personal statements and researching different courses. I’m thinking of Warwick, but the competition is insane. Warwick's amazing, but you're right, tough to get in. Have you thought about just going for apprenticeships? My cousin’s doing an accounting apprenticeship and he’s loving it. Paid really well, too. Apprenticeships are brilliant. Proper learning while earning, you know? Beats racking up loads of student debt. Yeah, true. My brother’s doing that naval engineer thing - it's a really good apprenticeship. He says the training is intense, but it's worth it. My grandma's been feeling a bit poorly lately. Just a bad cold, but she's really not herself. Oh no, that's awful! Sending her lots of get-well wishes. Tell her to wrap up warm and drink plenty of tea. That’s always grandma’s cure-all. Speaking of getting ready for winter, are you guys thinking about Christmas yet? It feels so far away! I’ve already started buying presents! My mum’s turning 60 this year, so I want to get her something really special. I’m just hoping I can afford anything decent this year. Working at the shop doesn't exactly pay the bills. Don’t worry, you’ll manage. You always find the perfect gifts. What about you, Harry? Any plans yet? Just trying to figure out how to sneak away for a few days of leave from the Navy, that’s the tricky part. Probably just a family Christmas this year though. My family's all chaotic as usual. Aunt Carol's already threatening to bring her infamous fruitcake. Oh god, not the fruitcake. Last year, my little brother tried to bury it in the garden. Seriously! My grandad used it as a weapon once. Well, at least it’s entertaining!

Honestly, the traffic was dreadful coming up from Harlow. Absolutely dreadful. Took nearly two hours, and I usually do it in ninety minutes, tops. Oh no! That’s awful, Nan. Were there any accidents? No, not that I could see. Just…gridlock. Absolutely solid. So many lorries, you know. And people just dawdling. It’s appalling. Well, you could’ve got the train, Nan. Don’t be silly, Tom. The train’s expensive and then I'd have to get a bus from the station. This way, I just drive. Much easier. Although today... definitely not easier. Did you see that cyclist on the news earlier? The one who got doored? Oh, terribly sad. Really awful. You have to be so careful, don't you? When you're out cycling, I mean. Makes you think. Yeah, people just don’t look. They just open the doors without thinking. Exactly! I nearly got knocked off my bike last week, just by a car pulling out. It was so close. I shouted at them, obviously. You shouldn’t shout, love. It’s not worth it. Just report them, and move on. No good getting yourself all worked up. I know, I know. Just surprised me, you know? I always cycle defensively, but… I’m never driving again. Seriously. Too stressful. I think I’ll just stick to walking. And what about when you need to go somewhere that’s a bit further afield, Tom? Walking to Brighton isn’t an option, is it? No, Nan, not really. Maybe cycling then. Safer than driving, surely? Cycling is great, but it’s not practical for everything. I mean, I need my car for work sometimes. Getting around with shelves full of jumpers isn’t easy on public transport. Speaking of getting around, are you still thinking of going to Norfolk next month, love? Yeah, I booked the tickets last week. Hoping the weather’s decent. Fancy coming with us, Nan? Oh, lovely. But my knees aren't what they used to be. All that walking around Cromer… You could sit on the bench, Nan. They have plenty of benches. I know, I know. It’s just… tiring. But I’d like to see you both down there. It's been a while. Well, we’ll pace ourselves! We can do some nice, gentle walks along the coast. Maybe we should hire a mobility scooter for you, Nan?

Excuse me, do you happen to know where the seminar room for the Linguistics alumni panel is? Oh, absolutely! It's just down this corridor, third door on the right. I'm heading that way myself. Are you an alumna? Yes, I graduated last year. I'm Elara, by the way. Language Research Co-ordinator now, which is surprisingly useful for keeping up with all the changes. That’s fantastic! I’m Freya, Language Research Administrator. Graduated a couple of years ago. It's lovely to see so many people back for alumni day. Agreed. It's a bit overwhelming though, isn't it? So many faces. Forgive me for eavesdropping, ladies. Lovely to see such enthusiasm for the faculty. Wonderful to see young minds engaged with language again. Richard Davies, retired lecturer here, specializing in, well, a bit of everything really. Oh, Professor Davies! It’s a genuine pleasure to meet you. I remember your lectures on Basque – utterly fascinating. Basque, yes. So wonderfully isolated. The most challenging language I ever taught, undoubtedly. All those aggulutive cases. Do you work with anything comparable? In a way. My current role focuses a lot on language acquisition and computational linguistics, so we use large datasets. It touches on isolating languages, like Mandarin Chinese, which present their own set of complexities. China’s on my list for a trip, actually. I’ve been trying to brush up on my Mandarin – very slowly! I spent some time in Spain last year, though. Madrid is fantastic. Ah, Spain! Wonderful country. I spent a summer there years ago, studying the dialects of Andalucia. You realize how much more complicated languages truly are when you’re immersed in them like that. I completely agree. I’d love to visit the Basque Country someday, see it for myself. It seems…almost mythical. I was thinking about visiting Wales next year, actually. My friend’s family lives near Snowdonia, and said the scenery is incredible. Wales is beautiful. Utterly beautiful. Although… you’ll need to be prepared for the rugby. It’s a serious business. I know! My dad’s a massive rugby fan. He’d have a field day. He used to drag me to matches when I was a kid – didn’t appreciate it much at the time. My brother plays for a local team, actually. Quite competitive down our way. Sport, eh? A wonderful metaphor for language, in its own way.

It’s so good to see you both! Seriously, two years is way too long. Bedford hasn't really changed, has it? Oh, don't say that, you’ll give Mum a complex! It's had a bit of a facelift, actually. That new coffee shop on the high street is surprisingly decent. How's life in… where are you teaching now? Still in Milan. It's pretty hectic, but I love it. The students are great, although explaining British idioms is a constant battle. They keep asking me to “break a leg” at theatre performances, which is just… weird. Classic. You always were one for the dramatic. So, you still single? Any Italian beauties vying for your affections? Don't even go there, Chloe! There’s a lot of… competition. Let's just say navigating the dating scene is an experience. Mum’s been subtly trying to set me up with the daughter of Mrs. Henderson from the church, you know. Oh, goodness. I remember Mrs. Henderson. She has a very… strong opinion about everything, doesn’t she? How are the kids doing, Chloe? Last time I saw them they were knee-high! They’re shooting up! Liam’s obsessed with football, naturally. Spending all his pocket money on those ridiculous posters. And Lily's already planning her wedding. Honestly, thinking about them growing up makes me feel… old. Did you see all the posts about the ice bucket challenge? Liam wanted to do it, but I put my foot down. Too much water wasted, I said. Yeah, I saw a few. Felt a bit performative, didn’t it? Though it did raise a lot of money for MND. Speaking of which, Mum's always involved in some charity bake sale or other. Wonder what she's organising now? Probably something involving soggy bottoms and excessive icing. She’s obsessed. I overheard her on the phone earlier, coordinating the raffle prizes for the Women’s Refuge. You know she’s been a major supporter for years. It's wonderful. She's always been a champion for those sorts of causes. It's inspiring, really. Did you ever think about adopting, Ethan? I know you always said you wanted a big family. It crossed my mind, yeah. The paperwork alone seems terrifying, though. All those forms to fill in... And finding the right agency. It's a huge commitment. Not sure I'm quite ready for that level of responsibility right now.

This coffee machine is driving me mad. Honestly, I don't know why I bothered getting it. It’s more trouble than it’s worth. What's wrong with it now, Mum? It was working perfectly fine yesterday. It’s refusing to brew a decent cup. Keeps spitting out half-hearted espresso. I swear, it's sentient and mocking me. You’re exaggerating, love. Probably just needs descaling. You haven't done that in a while, have you? Don’t tell me I haven’t! I did it… well, I thought I did it last month. It’s all a blur now. Retirement is a strange thing. All this time and I can’t remember when I last descaled a coffee machine. I can have a look at it later. I’m reasonably good with these things. Though, honestly, a good French press is just as good and far less temperamental. Easier, certainly. But where’s the fun in that? It’s like, once you own something fancy, you  have  to try and make it work. Now, speaking of things that need working out… the removal quote came in. Oh? And? Is it extortionate? It's… substantial, yes. Storing everything for six months while we figure out what we're doing with the house. They said it’ll be over three thousand. Three thousand! Good heavens. That’s quite a sum. Have you looked at alternative storage options? Of course I have! But most of them are smaller units and we’d have to rent multiple. Honestly, the whole process is exhausting. I didn't realise moving house at my age would be so complicated. It's always a nightmare, Mum. But we'll find something manageable. We could always put some stuff in Dad’s shed initially, just until we get a better handle on things. He'd kill me. He’s just spent the last year organising that shed into some kind of industrial efficiency system. Every tool has its place. It  is  a thing of beauty, that shed. It's practically a museum of perfectly arranged power tools. Exactly! And now you're suggesting I fill it with dusty china cabinets and old school reports. The man would lose his mind. Speaking of minds, have you been following the Labour leadership race? A little bit. It’s all quite disheartening, isn’t it? Another round of infighting. It is.

This latte is lovely, Mum. Much better than that instant stuff you make at home. Well, you know I’m not a coffee connoisseur, darling. It's just a quick caffeine fix for me. Though, I must admit, it’s nice to be out and about on a drizzly Tuesday. It is, isn’t it? So, Christmas… have you thought about Uncle Dave and Aunt Fiona coming this year? I spoke to Fiona last week. They’re still wrestling with the idea. Dave’s got that charity gala he really wants to attend, you know how he is. Oh, the one for the wildlife sanctuary? He's always so passionate about those things. Is he still trying to convince everyone to only eat ethically sourced carrots? You know your uncle! He’s a force of nature. Fiona said he was lecturing the butcher about the carbon footprint of Brussels sprouts. Honestly. He hasn’t changed a bit. What about the little ones, Maisie and Finn? Going to inflict the Christmas chaos on us again this year? They're bouncing with excitement, apparently. Maisie keeps asking if Santa’s going to bring her a pony. A pony! In the back garden! Tell her Santa’s a very busy man and ponies are rather large. Speaking of chaos, I'm having the worst time trying to organize my students' end-of-year party. Oh dear. What’s the issue? Trying to get everyone’s parents involved. It's a nightmare! Coordinating schedules, dietary requirements... I’ve got a kid who’s allergic to everything under the sun, apparently. The joys of teaching, eh? It’s not all Shakespeare and grammar, is it? Exactly! I used to think I’d be whisked off to teach English in Tuscany, sipping wine and discussing Dante. Now I’m mediating conflicts over gluten-free cupcakes. Well, you’re doing a fabulous job, darling. You’re so dedicated. And you're good at it. It’s wonderful you’re still TEFL teaching. It suits you. Thanks, Mum. It has its moments. I'm thinking of maybe doing some freelance translation work alongside it, actually. Something a bit more… creative. That’s a lovely idea! You have such a good ear for languages. Perhaps you should look into it. It could be a nice change. I'm just worried about how it'll all fit with everything else, with the teaching and the flat… Don't overthink it.

Honestly, have you heard about Liam and Chloe? Apparently, he snores like a drain now. It's keeping her up all night. Liam, really? I didn't think he’d be the snorer. He was always so skinny. Maybe he's put a bit of weight on. Remember how much he used to complain about being too thin for rugby? Speaking of things you wouldn't expect... Did you see Waterfields' new custard tarts? They’re absolutely massive. I had one yesterday. Waterfields are getting a bit pricey, aren’t they? Used to be a bargain. True. But they're still the best in Warrington. Especially those Richmond sausages. Proper meaty. Oh my god, yes! My mum only buys Richmond sausages. She says nothing else compares. My nan's the same. Always going on about how much better they are. My grandma's obsessed with a good handkerchief, though. Still carries one everywhere, even though everyone has tissues now. Says it's more dignified. My mum’s like that too. She'll offer you a tissue and then pull out a floral handkerchief if you refuse. It's a classic! My auntie Joyce is exactly the same. Sometimes she’ll give you a tissue and then use the handkerchief to wipe her nose after! Oh god. That’s…a lot. I think it’s the whole "proper" thing. Like it's more refined than a disposable tissue. Definitely. My grandma will lecture me about wasting tissues if I use more than one. It’s funny how these little habits get passed down, isn’t it? Like, I used to hate Richmond sausages, but now I think they’re amazing. It’s all about nostalgia, isn’t it? Mum always got Richmond sausages when we had a special dinner. Speaking of nostalgia, did anyone go to that reunion thing for Penketh High? Oh yeah! I saw loads of people I hadn't seen in years. Sarah Miller looked completely different. I didn't go. Didn’t fancy reliving those awkward teenage years! I was tempted, but I had a mountain of coursework to do. Besides, I'm pretty sure I'd be the only one who still wore Doc Martens. Never! You always look effortlessly cool, even with the Doc Martens. Do you think Liam's snoring is getting worse because of the stress of his new job? Maybe. Or maybe he’s just finally reaching his full potential as a human foghorn.

Honestly, Dad, that pub quiz was brutal. I thought I knew a thing or two about 80s music, but apparently, I know nothing. Brutal, is it? You were doing alright until they asked about Duran Duran’s bass player. That tripped you up, didn't it? Totally! Who even  knows  that? It was just completely obscure trivia. And then Dave from accounts got it right. Seriously? Accounts? Dave’s a clever lad. He reads a lot, you know. Always has. Used to devour those encyclopedias at Grandma’s. I suppose. Still, the whole team was a disaster. We came last. Last! We lost to the group of retired ladies who knit hats for badgers. Badgers, eh? Well, at least someone benefited from your defeat. They probably needed the support. Did you at least enjoy the curry afterwards? The curry was amazing, actually. That's the only reason I'm not completely writing off the whole night. It was a proper vindaloo. Blistered my tongue a little, but worth it. Good. You need to treat yourself occasionally. All this coordinating projects and stressing about deadlines... you burn yourself out if you don’t. Tell me about it. This new client is a nightmare. Constantly changing their mind about things. Last week, they wanted blue, this week it’s green. It’s exhausting! Clients are like that, love. Always chasing something they can't quite define. You just need to be firm with them, that’s all. Show ‘em who’s boss. Easier said than done, Dad. Especially when they’re paying the bills. So, how was your weekend? Did you get any chance to get out to the farm? Aye, a bit of a wander. The barley is looking promising this year, touch wood. Though the pigeons are getting cheeky. Had to chase half a dozen of the blighters off the other day. Naughty pigeons! Did you manage to fix that fence yet? The one near the old apple tree? Nearly there. Just need to get around to that this week. Been a bit busy with the accounts, you know how it is. Paperwork never ends. Honestly, it never does. So, are you still on for that barbecue next weekend? Sarah and Mark are coming down. Barbecue? Absolutely. Wouldn’t miss it. Good to see Sarah. Always did like her, down-to-earth girl. Do you think she'll bring that apple crumble she makes?

Honestly, the marking alone is exhausting. I’m drowning in A-Level essays. And they’re getting  so  creative with their excuses for why they haven't done it. Tell me about it! I’ve got a Year 9 class who seem to think "google it" is a valid research method. It's a constant battle. At least your A-Levels have some level of...compilation. Year 9 is just chaos. Chaos is spot on. And the pressure! They're all so stressed about their futures, and it’s my job to somehow guide them. Isn’t it always? Remember when we were at the training centre? It felt like that pressure was aimed directly at  us . Oh god, yes! Mrs. Plumtree and her endless lesson observations. I still have nightmares about her feedback on that disastrous lesson about the subjunctive mood. Oh, don't remind me! I remember you trying to explain it with a poorly-acted mime. That was...memorable. It was mortifying! Anyway, what are you thinking about doing with your French teaching post? Are they offering any CPD? They are, actually. There’s a really interesting course on incorporating augmented reality into language lessons. I’m tempted, but it’s a lot of extra time. Augmented reality? Wow, that sounds amazing! I’d love to learn more about that. I’m trying to brush up my Spanish, but it's so hard to find the time. Duolingo is alright, but I really miss actually  speaking  it. I know, right? I’ve been trying to get back into French with Babbel, but it’s not the same. I miss being able to zip into Paris without feeling like a complete idiot. Me too! I was thinking of maybe finding a language exchange partner online. Do you think that’s a good idea? Could be! Just be careful. There are some dodgy characters out there. Maybe join a group first, a proper language learning forum? Good idea. Speaking of dodgy characters… how’s Liam doing? Still working at the garage? He is. He’s actually talking about leaving and trying his hand at something else. He keeps muttering about opening a food truck. A food truck? That’s…random. What would he even sell? He's been obsessed with those Korean bao buns. Apparently, he wants to do gourmet bao. It sounds bonkers, but knowing Liam, he'll make it work somehow.

Look at that, Elsie. They’re really busy today, aren’t they? The blue tits, especially. They are, Arthur. Chaps are right greedy, they are. Such a scrum. Did you put out the sunflower hearts this morning, then? I certainly did. Fresh batch. You know how they love those. A bit more expensive, of course, but worth it to see ‘em hopping about. Reminds me of the kids at school dinners, doesn't it? All shoving and elbows. Though they were after pudding, not birdseed. Oh, Harold, you always were a card. Remember Mrs. Davies’s treacle sponge? Now  that  was worth queuing for. Aye, those were the days. Elsie, have you got the Victoria sponge ready? Nearly. Just putting the last of the jam on. It's Mrs. Miggins’ recipe, you know. Best in Norfolk, I reckon. Don't you go getting too full now, Elsie. Want to leave some for the rest of us, eh? Speaking of full... that doctor’s appointment next week. Are you keeping an eye on your sugars, Margaret? Trying, Harold. Trying. It's these cakes, I reckon. Tempting, aren’t they? But I’m walking every day, you know that. Down to the shops and back. Keeps me ticking over. That's good, Elsie. Good for you. Remember what the doctor told you. I do, I do. Portion control. Easy for him to say, isn't it? He’s probably eating porridge all day. Probably building bridges, more like! Still a civil engineer at heart, eh, Arthur? It’s hard to shake off, Harold. A life spent building things sticks with you. Look at that nest in the clematis. Wonder who’s built that? Seems quite sturdy. Probably a robin. They’re clever builders, those robins. Remember those stick puppets you used to make with the children, Margaret? Oh, goodness yes. A fox, a badger, a little owl... Honestly, those children used to have such imaginations. You were always so patient. Little darlings, weren’t they? All demanding sugar lumps and stories. They were. But it kept me busy. And it's nice now to have a bit of peace and quiet. Though sometimes I do miss the chatter. Well, you've got us, Elsie. A good bit of chatter here. Just got to keep an eye on them sugars though. Easier said than done, Arthur. Easier said than done. But the tea is ready... and the cake.

This view is absolutely stunning, isn’t it? Just… incredible. It is, Celinda. Absolutely breathtaking. Worth every penny of the flight, I reckon. Though I’m having trouble hearing the waves properly with these blasted things. Oh, dear, still struggling with them then? We should make sure they're adjusted properly when we get back. I’ve been meaning to. It’s a fiddle, isn't it? Still, this place… Reminds me of that little taverna we went to in Greece, years ago? Remember that? Vaguely. My memory isn't what it used to be. Not like your niece, Amelia, though. She remembers everything. Even the colour of the curtains in Aunt Mildred's house. She certainly does. You know, I heard from Margaret – she’s doing alright, considering – she’s sending her best wishes. And worrying about poor Kevin, his back’s playing up again. Poor Kevin. He never seems to get a break. Anything he can do for it? He's seeing that osteopath he mentioned. Seems to be helping a bit. You know, it’s funny. He was talking about dowsing the other day - can you believe it? Michael, dowsing? Seriously? I know, I know! Said it helped him find a particularly good spot for his azaleas. Utter nonsense, of course, but you can’t argue with results, can you? He's gone rather spiritual in his old age, hasn't he? Talking about destiny and all that. Well, everyone needs something to believe in, don’t they? Though I think I’ll stick to a good glass of wine for now. What are you thinking of ordering? I fancy the grilled octopus. Sounds lovely. You? I'm tempted by the Kleftiko. Lamb and potatoes, sounds perfect. Are you going to try and learn any Turkish? Me? At my age? I can barely remember my own address sometimes. Though I did manage to master "Merhaba" and "Teşekkür ederim". That's a start! I'm attempting to count – "Bir, iki, üç…” It’s proving harder than I thought. These restaurants are always full of interesting characters, aren't they? Look at that gentleman over there – impeccably dressed, talking on the phone with such passion. I wonder what he does. He does look rather important. And look at that woman sketching in her notebook – so absorbed. I love watching people. Reminds me of that rather eccentric chap we met at Aunt Sheila’s funeral.

It’s so lovely to be here, honestly. Feels like ages since we last properly chatted. It does, darling! Work's been a whirlwind, hasn't it? How's the project coordination going? Still managing to keep everything on track? It's... busy. More or less, yes. We've got this huge deadline looming for the end of the month, so it’s all hands on deck. It's pretty intense, but I’m learning a lot. Though sometimes I just wish I could escape to Norfolk for a week. Always wanting to escape, aren’t you? Just like your grandfather. Remember him always moaning about the council? Oh god, don't remind me! Those stories could fill a book. How’s the farm business, Dad? Are the weather conditions being kind this year? It's a bit touch and go, apparently, with the rain. He’s been saying how the wheat isn’t doing as well as planned. It’s a struggle, that's all. Can't control the weather, can you? So, what's this about a future renovation? You mentioned it on the phone. Yes! So, Ben and I are thinking about finally doing the extension in the kitchen. Proper one, with an island and everything. Oh, that sounds wonderful, love. You deserve a nice kitchen! Where are you thinking about putting it? We're looking at going out the back, into the garden. There's ample space, fortunately. It'll be a massive project though, getting quotes and planning. It's daunting to think about. Don’t rush into it, mind. Get a few different builders in, check their references. My neighbour had a right nightmare with building work last year. Took forever, over budget, and the quality was appalling. We'll definitely do our research, Dad. Promise. What about you two? Any exciting news? Have you seen Barbara and David recently? We had them round for dinner last week. Barbara's still obsessed with her bridge club. Euchre, it is! They're both doing alright. David’s back's playing up again, poor bloke. He spends his days playing rugby on the telly, complaining. Honestly, some things never change, do they? Have you been to any matches recently, Dad? Watched the six nations, of course. England were a bit woeful, weren’t they? So disappointing. Absolutely dreadful. Do you think they'll recover next year? They'll need a new coach, that's for sure.

Honestly though, I still can't believe how many people fall for catfish. Like, seriously? Tell me about it! It's bonkers, innit? You see these stories on Catfish and you think, "how could you be so gullible?" It's the desperation, I reckon. People are lonely, looking for connection, and they latch onto anything that feels like it. Even if it’s clearly not real. Yeah, but the effort some of them put in! Like, fabricating these whole fake lives, details, photos… it’s just a really strange thing to do. Why go to all that trouble? Just to mess people about, obviously. Some people are just proper cruel, aren't they? I reckon a lot of 'em get a kick out of it. Like, a power thing. Definitely. Or a warped sense of humour. Imagine spending months chatting to someone, building a whole relationship, and then finding out it was all a lie. Gut-wrenching. My Nana nearly fell for one, you know. A supposed soldier stationed in Afghanistan. Kept sending her pictures and messages full of love and promises to come home. Oh, no! That’s awful. Did she suss it out? Eventually, yeah. My dad started poking holes in the story. Like, the pictures looked too good to be true, and the dates didn't add up. Turns out it was a guy in Nigeria. Blimey. My uncle once watched a whole episode of Jeremy Kyle and honestly, it just made him depressed for the rest of the day. Jeremy Kyle? Oh god, that show was something. I used to watch it with my nan but it felt a bit… exploitative, yeah? Right? Like, preying on people’s vulnerabilities for entertainment. It's easy to judge them for being so chaotic, but you've got to remember, a lot of those people are struggling. I know what you mean. Still, some of the situations were just mind-boggling. Like, who brings a lie detector test to a family reunion? Only on Jeremy Kyle, love! It's all a bit of a circus, isn't it? I always felt bad for whoever was trying to have a serious conversation amidst all that madness. It’s just… grim, innit? All that drama and confrontation, just laid bare for everyone to see. I'm glad it's not on anymore. Me too. I wouldn't want to be in that kind of spotlight, that's for sure.

This pasta's really good, Grandma. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Thank you, darling. It’s a recipe from my Nonna, you know, back in Italy. I haven't made it in ages. It's always nice to revisit those memories, isn't it? Definitely. So, you were saying you’re thinking about another trip to Paris? Yes, I was. I’ve been looking at flights. Just a short one, a week or so. I miss the Musée Rodin terribly. And the little cafes…oh, the little cafes! You have to try a proper café au lait in Paris, you know. Not like the ones here. I’ve never been, actually. Paris, I mean. Oh, you simply must go! Perhaps after you finish university? Though I imagine your Classics course keeps you pretty busy. Do they still teach Latin and Greek in that way? Yeah, pretty standard. Lots of translation, some reading original texts. It’s brilliant, honestly. Reminds me of when you used to talk about your lessons back in Vienna. Do you ever miss speaking German? Oh, terribly! I try to keep up, reading German newspapers online, but it’s not the same. My German isn't what it used to be. And the bee keeping articles... Honestly, those are getting increasingly technical. I struggle to understand half of them! You and your bees. Still buzzing away, then? Always. They are my little companions, you know? They're rather therapeutic. And last year's honey was exceptional, simply exceptional. Golden. That’s amazing! Speaking of things that are exceptional, I’m having the worst time with my laptop. It's constantly freezing. I think it might be a virus or something. Oh, that’s dreadful. Honestly, these computers! They’re all so complicated. I try to avoid them as much as possible and just stick to watercolour paints. At least you know where you stand with a brush and paper. Have you tried restarting it? Like ten times! I'm thinking about taking it to that shop in Camden, but I’m worried they’ll charge me a fortune. Yes, those places can be sharks. Let me see…my nephew, Marco, is quite good with computers. I’ll give him a call and see if he can offer some advice. He lives near you, doesn’t he? Yeah, not far from campus. That would be amazing, Grandma, thank you!

Honestly, Dad, that lorry driver was insane! He just cut us up on the A3. People driving these days, honestly. Never a blinker, never a thought. Back in my day… Oh, here we go. Back in your day, everything was perfect, wasn't it, John? Not perfect, but people had a certain respect, you know? A sense of responsibility. Not like these youngsters glued to their phones. I wasn’t on my phone, Dad! And it’s really stressful when people drive like that. I was trying to study Shakespeare on my tablet, that's all. Shakespeare! Good for you, love. Hopefully all that studying will get you somewhere nice. Better than Harlow, definitely. Harlow’s not that bad, Auntie Sue! Oh, don't even start with me about Harlow. Grey buildings, grey people, grey weather. Give me Dorset any day. Dorset’s alright. Bit quiet, but nice countryside. Still, this traffic’s dreadful. Should have left earlier. Holiday weekend, you know. The Sat Nav said it would be manageable. It’s lying. Typical. And the rain’s just starting again. Well, at least we’re going somewhere. Speaking of going somewhere, have you sorted the MOT out for the Fiesta, John? Not yet, dear. Been putting it off. Solicitor’s been taking all my available energy and attention. That bill is ridiculous, you know. Paying solicitors is a nightmare. It's costing me a fortune to sort out Grandma’s will. Tell me about it. Trying to get my daughter to move out is proving to be more complicated than I initially thought. Should’ve waited before you bought that new sofa, eh? Then she’d have moved out quick enough, thinking she’d have to carry all her stuff. Classic Dad. So, Auntie Sue, how are things at the care home? Anything exciting happening? Usual dramas, love. One patient insisted last week that he was William Shakespeare. Kept quoting sonnets and getting confused with Windows 8. Windows 8! That was a disaster. Never could get the hang of it. I remember. Everyone hated it. What about that antiques show, Mantiques, you were watching last week? Anything interesting? Oh, there was a lovely Victorian writing desk. Beautiful inlay. But far too expensive, of course. Do you think we’ll ever know more about Great Grandpa George? I did some family history research, but it just goes cold after him. George?

It’s a bit draughty in here, isn’t it, Margaret? I swear this old house just breathes out cold air. It is a little, dear. Perhaps I should light another fire. The logs are stacked up nicely, you know. Such a waste to let them go unused. Yes, please do. My bones are feeling it today, more than usual. Must be the damp. Everything's damp, isn't it? The rain hasn't stopped all week. It’s seeping in everywhere, I'm sure of it. I checked the gutters this morning, they are full to bursting. You’re a good woman, you are. Not many would bother with those gutters. I’d be up a ladder like a fool, risking a broken neck. Nonsense. Someone has to do it. And besides, I quite enjoy it. A bit of fresh air, even if it  is  drizzling. Fresh air. Ha! It’s a damp chill, that’s what it is. Did you hear about young Timothy next door? Timothy? No, what's he been up to now? Last I heard he was complaining about squirrels in his bird feeders. Worse than that. Broke his ankle, he has. Tripped over a rose bush, apparently. Can you believe it? A grown man, felled by a rose bush. Oh, dear! Poor man. Is he alright? They’ve set it, supposedly. He’s in a cast, looking miserable as sin. Says he'll never weed his garden again. Well, that  is  a tragedy for him. Though, honestly, his garden could do with a bit of neglect. It's always been rather… flamboyant. Flamboyant is putting it kindly. It's an explosion of colour, that’s what it is. Roses, lilies, petunias… all fighting for space. Like a jungle. Exactly! He fusses over it too much, if you ask me. A bit of wildness wouldn't hurt. You're right. Wildness suits a garden. Like life, really. A bit of chaos keeps things interesting. There you go. Now, are you going to let me light that fire, or are we going to discuss Timothy's horticultural shortcomings all afternoon? Oh, yes, please. The fire. My teeth are chattering. And perhaps a nice cup of tea as well? Something strong, if you please. Coming right up, love. Coming right up. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .H.H..

This risotto is absolutely gorgeous, honestly. You’ve really outdone yourself. Cheers! Glad you like it. It's a new recipe I tried. Needed something a bit lighter after that heavy curry last week. Definitely a good choice. Proper comfort food for this weather, though. Absolutely chucking it down out there, isn't it? It is. Forecast says it’s going to be like this all week. Shame about the garden, really. I was hoping to get those tomatoes planted properly. Yeah, a bit of a dampener. Still, we can always pot them up and keep them inside for a bit longer. Speaking of which, how are your little succulents doing? Still surviving the neglect? Surprisingly, yes! They're being remarkably resilient. I think they appreciate the neglect – less fuss for them, I suppose. That's the way to be, low maintenance. Reminds me a bit of Sarah, actually. Turns up, does what needs doing, then disappears. You mean Sarah and Mark? I haven't heard from them in ages. How are they doing with the flat renovation? Apparently, it's been a nightmare! The plasterer let them down at the last minute, so they're still waiting for the walls to be finished. They're booked in to come over next week, though, for a game night. Fancy that? Oh, brilliant! I'm looking forward to seeing them. We should get some proper music on, too. What have you been listening to lately? Anything good? I found this amazing playlist on Spotify - proper chilled indie stuff. Perfect for a rainy evening like this. It’s got a bit of everything, really. I can send you the link if you like. Definitely, send it over. Always looking for new stuff. I've been stuck on the same old Arctic Monkeys albums for about a month now. It’s a bit embarrassing. Don't be! Classic for a reason. But you gotta branch out a bit! This playlist is totally up your street, I reckon. It's… it’s got that sort of vibe, y'know? I do know that vibe, you’re right! I’ll have a listen tomorrow. It's been lovely catching up, as always. Cambridge feels so much more relaxed than the chaos of uni life. It is, isn't it? That's why I love coming here. Peaceful. And the food’s always fantastic. You truly are a domestic genius.

Honestly, I was reading this article about the rise in unemployment again, and it just made me think about your mam. You know, after all those years… it must be a right kick. Yeah, it is tough. She puts on a good face, you know? Says she’s enjoying the time, but I know she's worried about what comes next, about the bills and all that. Totally. It’s not something you just switch off from, is it? Especially when you’ve been contributing for so long. Makes you think about the whole system, doesn't it? It does. It makes you think about everything, really. Like, the way we fund universities...it's ridiculous now. The fees are just a barrier for so many. Tell me about it! I'm so glad I did my postgrad before the fees went absolutely mental. Remember when it was just a few grand a year? Feels like a lifetime ago. I’m regretting taking this PhD, to be honest. The stress is considerable, and the potential payoff… well, it's not exactly guaranteed. Don’t say that! You’re brilliant at what you do, Liam. You’ll publish something amazing. Besides, it’s about more than just the job at the end, isn't it? You’re genuinely passionate about it. That's what I keep telling myself. But still… sometimes I wonder if I should have just bitten the bullet and found a proper job. Something more stable. Nah. You’d be bored stiff. Plus, your research is important. Speaking of boring… did you catch "Wicked" last week? Oh, man! It was incredible! Elphaba was just phenomenal. I’d never seen it before, and I’m already planning a return trip. I know, right? The vocals were unreal. And the staging was so clever. I’ve been obsessed with the soundtrack since. I've been belting it out in the shower all week. Mortified the neighbours, probably. [Laughs] I can imagine! You're bringing a bit of Defying Gravity to Cambridge! Trying to! So, what are you working on at the moment with the PhD? Anything I can try and look into to show support. It’s mostly just sifting through data at the moment. tediously. It's to do with assessing government funding through rural communities. Quite dry when you say it out loud. Sounds interesting! Anything exciting on the horizon for you this week?

Nan, look! I've got it all sketched out. Och, let me see, love. What have you got there? It looks like a wee critter! It's a Rumblebug! He's a grumpy little beetle who can only be cheered up by singing silly songs. A Rumblebug? That’s brilliant, Liam. A very original idea! Is this for the book you’re thinking about? Aye! I want to do a whole series about him. He could have adventures! Maybe he goes to the moon! The moon, eh? A wee beetle on the moon! That’s quite the journey. Is he a colourful wee beetle? Yeah, lots of bright colours! Red and blue and green…and sparkly bits! Can you imagine him bouncing around in space? I can perfectly! It's lovely, Liam, really lovely. But the pictures are a bit rough, aren't they? Well, I'm not brilliant at drawing. Can you help me out, Mum? Of course, love. We can work on them together. Maybe we can find some colour pencils. Do you want to use watercolours? They're a bit messy, though. Watercolours would be cool! But maybe not today. I don’t want to get paint everywhere and Nan would have a fit. Don’t you worry about me, Liam. I’ve lived through worse than a bit of spilled paint. Though, I would appreciate it if you didn't get it on the rug! It's a very delicate Persian. Okay, okay! No paint on the Persian. What about the story, Nan? Should Rumblebug go to the moon or somewhere else? Well, a moon trip sounds grand, but perhaps something a bit closer to home first? Has he got any friends? Not yet. He’s quite grumpy, remember? He pushes everyone away. That's a good starting point, Liam. A grumpy little beetle who needs a friend. What’s stopping him from making friends? He's scared of being laughed at. He thinks his silly songs are rubbish. Och, the poor wee soul! Everyone’s got a song in their heart, Liam, you just have to have the courage to sing it. Reminds me of your Uncle Alistair. He always hid his poetry. Said it was too…flowery. Oh, Nan. Alistair's poetry was beautiful. It just took a bit of getting used to. So Rumblebug needs to be brave? And sing his songs even if people laugh?

Honestly, this essay deadline is killing me. I've barely slept this week. Tell me about it! Mine's on Friday and I'm still staring at a blank page half the time. What’s yours on? Victorian literature. So boring, but apparently vitally important for my English grade. You? Post-structuralism and feminist theory. Equally brilliant, equally draining. I’m seriously considering just writing a manifesto about the joys of naps. I wish. I feel like I’ve absorbed every Victorian novel ever written. I can practically recite Dickens in my sleep. You know what would cheer me up? A ridiculous debate. Like, which is the superior way to remove leg hair – shaving or waxing? Ooh, controversial! Waxing, definitely. Shaving always leaves those little prickly shadows. See, I love the smoothness of a fresh shave, but the regrowth is the absolute worst. Like tiny little needles. Exactly! Waxing is painful, don’t get me wrong, but the results last way longer. Plus, no prickly shadows. But the tearing! The redness! I swear, my legs look like they’ve been in a fight after a wax. Okay, fair point. It’s not exactly glamorous. Though, I think the pain is worth it. Are you even bothering with it at this point with all the essay stress? Honestly? No. I’ve accepted my fate. I'm embracing the natural look. My legs are a wilderness. Be honest, how much natural are we talking? Like, hiking through the Amazon natural? Okay, don't push it. It's more like…a lightly forested area. Just a gentle slope of hair. A slope! I'm loving this. My grandma would have a fit. She's a huge advocate for perfectly smooth everything. My mum’s the same. She'd be horrified. She once gave me a waxing voucher for Christmas. Oh no! That’s brutal. Did you use it? Eventually. Resentfully. It was a dark day. I feel you. Anyway, maybe after these essays are done, we should treat ourselves to a spa day, just to recover from the stress and the, uh, personal grooming decisions. That actually sounds amazing. Just a full day of pampering and escaping the world of footnotes. Deal! Deal. So, you still working on that manifesto about naps? It’s gaining traction. Seriously. It's very persuasive. You should read it. It might get you through your Dickens. I might just do that.

Honestly, I can’t beat you at the alphabet game. You’re ridiculously good. It's a honed skill, honestly. Years of trivia nights, you know? Plus, my brain is currently dedicated to memorising obscure historical facts for my PhD. Alphabetical order is practically second nature. You've got a serious advantage, then. I was using my brain for conference calls all day, trying to wrangle data and delegates. It’s exhausted. Fancy another pint? This cider's not bad. Yeah, alright. Another pint sounds good. Though, I’m starting to feel it a bit. I shouldn’t really be knocking back this much before hitting the books again tomorrow. You’re always saying that, though. Remember that stag do last year? You were still quoting Latin at three in the morning. Don't remind me! Though, to be fair, that was  considerably  more than a couple of pints. Speaking of things that alter perception… did you see that article about the increase in recreational drug use amongst students? Yeah, I skimmed it. A bit depressing, really. Peer pressure, I suppose. And the easy availability of things now. It’s a shame. Makes you wonder what’s going on, doesn't it? Proper escape route for some, maybe. Definitely. It's worrying. I hope people are aware of the risks, because it doesn’t take much to… well, to go down the wrong path. By the way, did you catch the boxing last night? Fury vs. Chisora. Briefly. It was brutal. Fury’s dominance was a bit… unsettling, actually. Yeah, he really took it to him. Though, I feel a bit bad for Chisora, you know? He’s always putting on a show, always giving it his all, but he’s just… he’s not at Fury’s level. It’s tough watching that. You feel for the guy. It's like you're watching someone’s dream get crushed. It made me think about that whole thing with the racist abuse towards those players the other week. Oh, don’t even get me started. It’s absolutely disgusting. I can’t believe we're still having this conversation in 2023. Football should be a celebration, not a platform for that kind of hatred. Agreed. And the way some people try to downplay it, saying "it's just a few bad apples…" it’s infuriating. It's systemic, isn't it?

So, the crux of it really is getting the funding through, isn’t it? And I’m just not sure about this new application process. It seems deliberately obtuse. It  is  obtuse, darling. They seem to enjoy making it so. But remember what I said about the Heritage Lottery Fund – you absolutely  must  emphasize the community benefit. They're not just interested in preserving bricks and mortar now, they want to see how it impacts the local people. I know, I know. I've been trying to weave that in, but it's tricky with St. Michael’s. It’s… well, it’s primarily a beautiful example of Elizabethan architecture. Less obvious community impact there. True, true. But think about the potential. Guided tours for local schools, workshops on traditional crafts, even renting out the space for community events. Things like that. Paint a picture for them. And don't be afraid to exaggerate  slightly . Exaggerate? Is that advisable? Of course! It's called ‘strategic presentation,’ dear. I've been doing this for decades. You need to sell the dream. Remember the debacle with the old mill in Marlow? Oh, don't remind me. The one where you promised a full-scale replica of the water wheel… Exactly! And the council was practically begging me to move it after they realised the ground couldn’t handle it! But I got them the funding, didn’t I? The point is, you need to show them ambition. Even if it’s a little… fanciful. I rather think I'll stick to demonstrable facts then. I’ve been looking at some estimates for pointing the exterior. It’s far more expensive than I initially thought. Pointing! Oh, dear. That's always the killer. Are you using lime mortar? Absolutely vital for a building of that age. Don’t even  think  about using modern cement. Of course not. I'm using a specialist supplier. The problem is, they’re quoting nearly double what other companies are offering. Specialist is key. It’s the only way to ensure longevity. And are you getting multiple quotes for everything else, of course? Certainly. Though I'm finding a lot of builders don’t seem to have experience with historic buildings. They just want to slap on whatever's cheapest. Precisely! And that’s where your expertise comes in. You need to find someone who understands the nuances, the sensitivity of the materials.

Right, kettle's on. Fancy a builder's brew or something a bit fancier? I've got some Earl Grey, that's a bit of a treat. Builder's is perfect, thanks. Always the most reliable. So, you were telling me about that paper you're reviewing on dialect shift? Sounds fascinating. It is, actually. It’s looking at how younger generations in certain rural areas of County Durham are losing some of the traditional vocabulary. You know, the specific words for things, the little nuances. Like what kind of words? Loads! Things like ‘sneck’ for the latch on a door, or ‘htoog’ for a slender pole. The kids are just… not using them anymore. They're opting for the standard English equivalents. That’s a shame, isn’t it? It’s kind of heartbreaking when you think about the history bound up in those words. The generations who used them, the communities they built. Exactly. It’s more than just words though, isn't it? It's a connection to a place, a heritage. The paper's interesting because it’s trying to tease out  why  this is happening. Is it purely social mobility, people wanting to sound less 'regional'? Or is it something deeper, a wider cultural shift? I suppose both, probably. It's the same with the way people speak generally, isn't it? Especially younger people. They’re constantly absorbing different accents and dialects from online. Absolutely. It's a double-edged sword, really. On the one hand, it means there's more exposure to different forms of language. But on the other, it potentially dilutes the strength of local dialects. It’s the same principle as studying language change over centuries, just compressed into a few decades. It does make you think, doesn’t it? About how quickly things change. Speaking of change, did you book anything for that holiday yet? You were saying you wanted to go somewhere completely different this year. I've been looking! I’m tempted to go to Iceland. I saw some incredible pictures of the landscapes. Vast, empty, volcanic… Iceland! That’s amazing. You'd love it there. It's so dramatically different from... well, from practically everywhere, isn't it? That’s what I like. Somewhere completely foreign. I need to decompress, you know? All this linguistics academic stuff can get a bit intense. I need to see something that throws all my linguistic frameworks out the window.

Mummy, Mummy! Did you pack me sausage and mash today? I thought I did, sweetheart. Did you have it? No! It was chips and beans. Chips and beans? Oh, dear. That’s not your favourite, is it? No! I wanted sausage and mash. And gravy! Oh, I’m so sorry darling. I must have mixed up the lunchboxes. Did you eat it all? Yes. It was okay. But I wanted sausage and mash. Granny makes the best sausage and mash. She does, doesn't she? That's true. We’ll definitely have to go see Granny soon. For sausage and mash. And Yorkshire puddings! And Yorkshire puddings. You remember, don't you? Granny always gives us extra Yorkshire puddings. Yes! Big ones! Right. So, William, did you have anything nice today? I had cheese and crackers and an apple. Good boy. And what about money for school tomorrow? Do you need any? Yes, please. For a cookie. A cookie? Just a cookie? Maybe a yoghurt too. Okay, okay. We'll pack some extra then. Beatrice, do you need any money? No, thanks. I want to save up for the tennis tournament. The tennis tournament! Are you excited? Yes! I’m going to win! You won’t. Yes, I will! I’ve been practicing! That’s the spirit! Just remember to have fun, okay? It’s not all about winning. But I want to win! Well, give it your best shot. Now, did anyone see that show on TV last night? About the circus? The one with the clowns? Yes! Didn't they look amazing? The clowns were silly! One fell over. He did! But he was a very funny clown. Imagine being in the circus! Flying through the air on a trapeze.
