Or riding an elephant! Or being a clown! Well, we can’t exactly join the circus, can we? But maybe we can go see one sometime. Would you like that? Yes! Please! Can I be the clown? We’ll see, William. We’ll see. Now, time for your bath, both of you. And then maybe we can read a book about…clowns! Yay! Okay. But I want a bath bomb. Of course, you do. Always a bath bomb. Let’s go! Mummy! Yes, darling? Sausage and mash! I promise, tomorrow you’ll have sausage and mash. And extra gravy! Yay! Can I have extra gravy too? Of course, you can, William.

Honestly, that film was dreadful, wasn’t it? Such a waste of two hours. Well, dear, not everything can be a masterpiece. Though I agree, it wasn’t exactly gripping. The plot seemed a bit…convoluted. I thought the visuals were stunning, actually. The CGI was really impressive, even if the story was a bit weak. Though I'm with you on the time waste, felt like it could have been tighter. The visuals were the only redeeming feature. And that debate at Cambridge the other day! I’m still buzzing from it. The panel on historical teaching methods... fascinating, but so divisive. I read about it online. Sounded pretty heated. What side were you on? Very much on the side of making it more relevant to modern students. Less rote learning dates and battles, more exploring the influence of historical events on contemporary issues. Back in my day, we just learned the dates. Got them all crammed in, and then promptly forgot them. Exactly! We need to engage students, make them  think  about history, not just regurgitate facts. The national curriculum is so outdated. How can we expect children to understand the complexities of today’s world if they don’t have a solid grounding in the past, but one presented in a way they can connect with? It's a tricky balance, isn't it? Striking that balance between demonstrable knowledge of dates and events, and making it relatable. It's the same in advertising, actually. You need to know your history – the evolution of campaigns, marketing strategies – but you also need to be able to apply that knowledge to create something fresh and engaging. That’s a brilliant analogy, actually. It’s the same principle. It’s not about just knowing the ‘what,’ it’s about understanding the ‘why’ and the ‘how.’ And how do you teach the ‘why,’ dear? Children these days… distracted. Always on those screens. That's part of the challenge. You have to use technology to your advantage. Incorporate film, music, even social media. I’m trying to get my school to integrate virtual reality experiences. Imagine walking through ancient Rome! That’s incredible! I’d be interested to see something like that implemented. It begs the question though, how do we ensure equitable access? Not all students have those opportunities. Absolutely. That's a critical point. It highlights the ongoing inequality in our education system.

Blimey, that wind's something, isn’t it? Blew a watering can right off the patio this morning. Nearly took me out! It is a bit fierce, dear. Reminds me of the rationing days, it does. Always a gale when they were handing out the butter. Speaking of the old days, did you hear what John’s found out about his grandfather? Apparently, he was with the Signals Corps during the war. Really? John didn't mention that. I thought he said his grandfather was a baker. Well, he was a baker after the war, of course. But before that, he was sending messages across the lines. Quite a perilous job, apparently. Perilous, aye. Every job was a risk back then. My old man, he was digging ditches for the ARP. Air Raid Precautions. Terrible work, that. All hours of the day and night. My father was a conductor on the Underground. Can you imagine, travelling through those tunnels while the bombs were dropping? Brave man, he was. Never complained, though. Just did his duty. Reminds me of what Clive was saying about his sister's husband. Apparently, he was a policeman during the Troubles in Northern Ireland. Quite a different sort of danger, wouldn't you say? Different yes. But danger's danger, whichever form it takes. Used to hear stories about the police then - over here, too, mind you, not just up north. Not all good ones, either. Some right rogues in the force. Oh, absolutely. I remember my cousin, Maureen, getting stopped for no reason at all. They wouldn’t let her go until she’d given them a right earful. Dreadful. You know, it’s funny thinking about those times. Everything seems so…simpler now, doesn't it? Even with all the bother we have today. Simpler in some ways, perhaps. But harder in others. The world’s gotten so much more complicated. All this technology… Don’t even start me on the technology! Give me a good old-fashioned armchair any day. Something solid you can sit in. Speaking of which, I'm thinking of getting rid of that awful floral thing in the living room. Oh, the one your sister gave you? That monstrosity? The very one. Don't think it's got any class, it hasn't. Just takes up space. Are you going to replace it with something nice then? Something comfortable? Well, I was thinking something a bit more modern, you know.

Right, so just to be clear – you’ve got the keys to Dad’s, you’ll let me in on Saturday after I'm done at the uni? Yep, all sorted. Dad’s got a key hidden under the gnome, you remember. The grumpy-looking one. Yeah, of course. Still gives me the creeps, that gnome. I still can’t believe this is it, really. Last time we’ll be driving this route to Mum’s. Bit weird, isn't it? It is. Bit emotional really. Mum seemed alright, though. A bit quiet, but alright. Yeah, I think she's putting on a brave face. She kept asking about the apartment, if it was 'cosy enough'. She'll miss you being around, that's for sure. Keeps saying she’ll have nobody to complain about the weather to now. That’s Mum all over. Did she mention anything about Uncle Barry being better? She did. Apparently he's out of hospital now, just back home. Still a bit weak, but thankfully not contagious anymore. She’s worried about his finances though, you know how he is with money. Yeah, he always has been. Hopefully, he’s got some savings. Did you tell him about me sorting out that student loan thing? The better rate? Did. He was dithering, as usual. Complaining about the paperwork. Honestly, sometimes I think he enjoys complaining. Sounds like him. Speaking of finances, how’s Dad’s mortgage looking? Still a bit tight? It’s okay. He’s been cutting back, hasn’t he? Less takeaways, more beans on toast. Though he won’t admit it. He was moaning about the price of petrol earlier, naturally. Classic Dad. I feel a bit bad, moving so far away when he’s getting on. He'll miss having me nearby. Don’t worry about it. He knows you need to be doing your own thing. Besides, you’ll be able to visit loads. And I’ll pop down regularly. You’ll still be connected. I know, I know. Just feels… final, somehow. Remember when we used to pile in this car for holidays? Blackpool, Skegness... seemed to take forever back then. Oh god, yes! And the smell of those travel sickness bags… glorious memories. Remember that time we got lost in the Lake District? Ended up driving down a farm track! Oh my god, the cows! Dad was fuming.

Right, so let’s nail down this seating plan for Nan’s birthday. It's proving trickier than a spreadsheet with a million rows, honestly. Tell me about it. Auntie Maureen has already sent three emails demanding to sit next to Uncle Barry, claiming they need to “monitor each other’s wine intake.” Oh, Maureen. Bless her. But you're right, it's a minefield. I was thinking Nan and Grandpa at the head, of course. Then your cousins, Emily and Liam, next to them. Seems sensible. Emily’s been going on about how she wants to quiz Nan on her childhood memories. Perfect! Distraction from Barry and Maureen’s…situation. We need to keep people entertained. What about your aunt, Carol? She's got that new hip, remember? Yeah, she’ll need a seat closer to the loo, definitely. Maybe next to Uncle David? They always seem to get along. Good call. David can navigate her to the ladies if need be. Now, the menu… I was thinking salmon en croute, but I’m having second thoughts. Nan’s been a bit off her fish lately. Oh really? Is she alright? Is it her dementia getting worse, do you think? I don’t know, love. Little bit. It's those little things, you know? Forgetting where she put her glasses, repeating stories... It’s heartbreaking. Maybe roast chicken then? Classic, always a winner. Definitely safer. And the veg? Roast potatoes, obviously, but what about… parsnips? She does love parsnips. Yes! Good idea. And I was thinking of getting one of those fancy butternut squash risottos as a starter - a bit posh for Nan, but I think she’ll appreciate it. Sounds lovely. And candles? I saw some gorgeous ones at the market last week – those scented ones with lavender and chamomile. Perfect! We need to create a nice, calm atmosphere. Speaking of calm, I've been dreading sorting out the hall cupboard… it’s a black hole of forgotten Christmas decorations and chipped teacups. Oh god, I remember that cupboard! Last time I opened it, a box of old photographs practically fell out. Exactly! We have to tackle it. I was wondering if you could help me on Saturday? Just to clear out all the junk. Yeah, I can do that. Anything for a bit of peace! What did you think of the Great British Bake Off last night? That chocolate orange cake was something else.

Honestly, I’m proper beat. This France thing has drained me. Tell me about it! My feet are killing me. All that cobblestone. Aye, it’s a killer. I’m getting a right ache in my jaw too, though. Reckon it’s all relaxin’ too much. Jaw ache? Oh no, not your wisdom tooth again, is it? Nah, not yet. Just a weird ache. Maybe it’s buildin’ up to it. Mum’s been on at me to get it out, you know? Said I’ll be lookin’ like a right cave troll if I don’t. She does have a point! She’s just worried. My mum’s obsessed with teeth, you know. Always looking in my mouth. Standard mum behaviour, innit? Mine's the same with me bro. 'Are you eatin’ enough? Are you gettin’ enough sleep? Are you SURE you’re lookin’ after yourself properly?' Like I'm some fragile ornament. Absolutely! My mum keeps asking if I’ve seen any “holes” while I'm here. Apparently, I need to report any suspicious-looking buildings. It’s ridiculous. Holes? She’s mental! I know! And she's been sending links to this property website. Saying she wants me to start thinking about moving closer to her once uni's done. Oh, goin' back to uni then? Got yer student loan sorted, have ya? Yeah, fingers crossed. It's all a bit daunting to be honest. Cambridge's lovely, but… I miss having a garden. A proper one, not just a tiny patch of grass. Aye, I get that. Always loved havin’ space. I’m thinkin’ about moving back to Doncaster actually, after I finish. Seriously? Why? I thought you were enjoying it there. I am, but… it’s just not home, is it? Plus, me mum keeps sendin’ me care packages full of gravy browning and Yorkshire puddings. Makes me feel guilty for bein’ so far away. Classic mum move. It is! And she keeps sendin’ photos of the dog lookin’ miserable without me. That’s the worst of it, really. Aw, poor little thing. Listen, about moving – are you thinking of renting or buyin’? Renting, defo. Buyin' in Doncaster's a nightmare. Everything's overpriced. I reckon I'll just find somethin' near the uni, somethin' small. Are you lookin’ at buyin’? Maybe. It's a long way off yet. Apartment near the city centre is the dream, but needs to be affordable, you know?

Right, so we were talking about things we could do for acts of kindness, weren’t we? Brainstorming. Like giving cookies! Can I give cookies to Mrs. Henderson? Absolutely, darling. That’s a brilliant idea. Bake some lactose-free ones, remember? She mentioned she was feeling a bit poorly, and those are much gentler on the tummy. Can we give them to the postman too? Yes, we definitely can! He works so hard, doesn’t he? Especially in this weather. Do you remember last year when he helped us find our lost parcel? Yes! He was a superhero! He smelled like rain. He did, didn't he? Well, we can give him cookies too. Maybe even draw him a picture. Can I draw him a superhero cape? You absolutely can! And maybe we could leave a little note too. Say thank you for being a superhero. Now, other ideas… What about sorting out some old toys to donate? Can we use the chess pieces? The chess pieces? What for? For money! We can pretend they’re money. Oh, you clever things. That's… an interesting idea. Chess pieces as money for charity! I like it. They  are  quite pretty, aren’t they? But a bit unconventional. Maybe just some toys then? Okay. Can we give the panda? Yes, you can give the panda. He looks like he needs a new home. What else? Oh! It's nearly Chinese New Year, isn't it? We could make some little red envelopes for neighbours. Put some little sweets inside? Ooh, can I pick the sweets? You can definitely pick the sweets. But maybe we try and find some that aren't too sugary, yeah? What about some of those little dried mangoes? Those are nice. I want the red ones! The red mangoes it is. And we could decorate the envelopes with gold stars and dragons. It’ll be fun. I saw some lovely temporary hair dye the other day too – sparkly purple and blue. Can I dye my hair purple? Maybe not quite purple  yet , darling. But maybe when you're a little bit older. It's quite a bold choice, you know. Can I be blue? We'll see. We'll have a little chat about it first. Right, cookie baking first. And then, superhero drawings and panda donations. Deal? Speaker_2 & Deal! Now, where did I put that lactose-free flour…?

Mum, did you ever finish “Alice in Wonderland”? I’m doing a project on it for English. Oh, really? I started it ages ago, actually. Got quite far, I think. Beautiful illustrations, wasn't it? What are you focusing on for your project? The symbolism, mostly. And how it reflects Victorian society, apparently. It’s a lot. Miss Davies is being really intense about it. Victorian society, right. Well, I remember being fascinated by the Mad Hatter’s tea party. Such a strange, nonsensical scene. Did you see that production of it at the De La Warr a few years ago? No, I was like, ten. I'd have probably just been bored. It was really inventive, actually. Loads of projections and weird costumes. It wasn't your typical panto version. Anyway, speaking of costumes… did you manage to finish your Medusa costume for Halloween? Almost. I still need to find some green fabric for the snakes. It’s being a nightmare. Everything’s either too bright or too… flowery. Hmm, maybe try that shop on the seafront? The one near the pier. They sometimes have good deals on remnants. Yeah, maybe. It’s just, I keep having this weird… memory of when I fell and scraped my knee really badly. Remember that, when I was little? By the beach? Oh gosh, yes! You were inconsolable. Huge tears. And you had that little scar under your knee for ages. I still remember putting that antiseptic on it. I know, right? It's still there, if you look. I always feel like that fall somehow… I don’t know… sealed my adventurous spirit or something. Don't be silly. You’re plenty adventurous! Just a bit more cautious, perhaps. Speaking of memories, did you hear about Mrs. Henderson’s car accident down by the Old Town? No! What happened? Apparently, a seagull flew into her windscreen. Total chaos, they said. Glass everywhere. Luckily, she’s okay, just a bit shaken up. Hastings seagulls are no joke. Seriously? A seagull! That’s insane. You see them every day, swaggering around, thinking they own the place. Exactly. They’re like feathered gangsters. Anyway, are you reading anything good at the moment, apart from academic stuff? I'm listening to a lot on audible right now. Trying to finish “The Silent Patient”. It's quite creepy. Oh, I’ve heard good things about that one.

Morning, everyone. Lovely to see you all again. Did you both manage to get through the traffic alright? Morning, Anne. Yes, managed just fine. A bit slow getting out of Ramsgate, as usual, but nothing too dramatic. How are you? Aye, managed alright myself. Bit of a crawl on the M6, but nothing I haven't dealt with before. Glorious morning, though, isn't it? It is. So, I wanted to chat about that meeting last night with the Friends of the Rural Landscape. They seemed to respond really well to what I was saying, after our chat yesterday. It felt like a breakthrough. That’s wonderful, Anne. Good on you, giving them a bit of strategic advice. It sounds like they’re facing a similar battle to what you and I dealt with regarding the solar farms in Little Puddleton. Aye. Reminds me of the fight we had with that developer trying to build a sprawling hotel on Marsden Moor. The sheer force of opposition eventually brought ‘em down, though it took years. Exactly. But these wind turbine proposals… they're more complicated. It’s not just about aesthetics, it’s about viability, environmental impact… the sheer number of them they want to cram into the valley. The local council's development control committee is notoriously weak, isn't it? Always seems to be swayed by the developers' promises. It's a classic case of the long game, isn’t it? These companies are well-funded, they’ve got legions of lawyers, and the council are desperately hoping for a boost to the local economy. Precisely. And the Planning Appeal process… that’s the real kicker if they get turned down at the local level. They'll just go straight to the national level. Absolutely. You really need to be prepared. Do you think we need to start looking at commissioning an independent environmental impact assessment? Essential. And noise pollution reports. The vibration alone can be disruptive. People need to understand that. But you've got to be well-informed. They'll tear you apart if you're not. I’ve started digging, but it’s overwhelming. The politics of it all… the local planners, the energy companies, the protest groups, the finance… it's a tangled web. They’re all connected, Anne. It’s about influence and money. That's why being technically sound is so important. Have you looked into the new battery technology?

So, how was the driving lesson today, love? Did you manage to parallel park? It was… eventful, Dad. Parallel parking is the bane of my existence. Managed to get halfway in, then bumped the kerb. Oh dear! Don't you worry, love. It takes practice. Remember when I first started? I put the car  into  a lamp post! Really, Mum? You did? Absolutely! On the A38, no less. Your Dad nearly had a heart attack. Said I’d never get behind a wheel again. Don’t exaggerate, Brenda. It was a minor scrape. A bit of a dent, really. She was just a bit flustered. See? Inherited the flustered gene, I guess. It’s just… I feel so self-conscious. Everyone’s watching, you know? They aren't, darling. Well, maybe Mrs. Higgins next door is, but she’s always watching. Don’t let it get to you. Just focus on what you’re doing. And breathe! Easier said than done. And the insurance is a killer! I got a quote and it’s ridiculous. Well, you’re a young driver, aren’t you? It’s always going to be expensive. Are you on your Dad’s policy? I was thinking about it, but it's expensive there too. They said it’s less if I take a Pass Plus course after I pass. That's a good idea. It shows insurance companies you're committed and safe. We’ll look into that if you pass, alright? Thanks, Dad. Right, speaking of commitments, have you booked anything for our holiday? We need to get a move on if we want decent flights. I've been looking at a couple of places. What about that villa in Portugal we talked about? Algarve, nice beaches. Algarve sounds lovely! Or maybe Greece? Somewhere with loads of sunshine. I desperately need a good dose of Vitamin D. Greece is a bit pricey this time of year, isn’t it? Algarve is more sensible. Let me have a look at some options tonight. We need to decide quickly. Okay. So, what’s everyone up to this week? Mum, are you working late any nights? Just Wednesday. Court’s particularly busy with the new housing cases. It's a bit grim, to be honest. So much unrest. You keep a good head on, Brenda. It can't be easy dealing with all that. Yeah, Mum. Take care of yourself.

This lentil soup is really good, Dad. Thanks for making it. You're welcome, love. It’s good for you, you know. All those vegetables. Needed to use them up before they went off. Definitely. I've been trying to eat better, especially with exams coming up. All that junk food just makes me feel awful. Exams, eh? Still at university then? How's it all going? Are you having to work late nights? It’s okay. The workload’s heavy, but I'm managing. It’s just… stressful. I was thinking about moving to Brighton after I finish though. Brighton? Bit far, isn't it? Away from all your friends and family. I know, but there are more opportunities there for what I want to do. And the sea! I need the sea. Gillingham's lovely, but… Brighton's a nightmare for parking, you know that. Absolute shambles. Remember when you used to come down here when you were little, we'd struggle to find a space for ages. Yeah! And Mum would always complain. Speaking of things to complain about, my phone’s been driving me mad. All these notifications going off every five minutes. I practically live on Facebook now, trying to keep in touch with everyone. Facebook. Waste of time, that is. Just people showing off. Nowadays, you have to be online all the time, don’t you? Back in my day, we didn't need the internet to know what was going on. We told stories over tea and biscuits. Well, it  is  good for keeping up with people who live far away. But I get distracted so easily. I tried turning off most notifications, but then I miss things. It’s a vicious cycle. You need to prioritise, love. And a good cup of tea always helps. Did you see what they're saying about that politician on Facebook? Blasted irresponsible. The way they go on, you wouldn’t think they cared about anyone. Don't even get me started on politicians! It's all just… noise. I saw something the other day about food banks being busier than ever. It's awful. It is. It wasn’t like that when I was a boy. We didn’t have much, mind you, but at least everyone managed. People helped each other out. These days… I know. And young people are struggling even more. Trying to get on the property ladder, paying off student loans… it’s almost impossible.

…and then Mr. Davies, right? The English Lit lecturer, he actually  stopped  mid-sentence to look at his watch after I made a sarcastic comment about Hamlet's existential angst. Just stopped, stared at me, and went, "Are you quite alright?" No way! Did you mean to be that cutting? Absolutely not! I just… slipped. It came out wrong. It was meant to be a playful thing about how everyone analyses Shakespeare to death, but it just landed like a personal attack on the Bard. Awful. Classic you. You’re a menace with sarcasm. Remember when you told my Aunt Brenda her new hat made her look like a startled pigeon? Okay, that was a low point. I was having a bad day. And honestly, the hat  did  resemble a startled pigeon. It was a floral fascinator! A perfectly respectable floral fascinator! Anyway, I've been trying to learn to golf. Utter disaster. Golf? Seriously? I thought you were all about parkour and urban exploration. I was! But my dad's obsessed, and he keeps trying to get me "into" it. I managed to slice the ball into a pond on my second attempt. Looked like I’d personally offended the wildlife. You’re terrible at everything that requires coordination. Remember that ceramics class you took? Don't remind me. My 'vase' ended up looking like a melted potato. Speaking of things I'm bad at, have you heard back from that internship at Ashland & Finch? Nope, nothing yet. I’m starting to think my surname - Featherstonehaugh, honestly - is working against me. It sounds like something a Victorian novelist invented for a character. It does! It’s ridiculous. Everyone calls you "Fez" though, doesn’t it? My mum gave you the nickname "Fitz" once and you nearly exploded. I did! It’s utterly absurd. Though, I suppose "Fez" is slightly more manageable. What about you? Still going by "Nodge?" Sadly, yes. My great-grandfather was a renowned Nodge, apparently. Though people do occasionally shorten it to 'Nodgey'. It's both endearing and mortifying. It’s probably why I’m so keen on golf, hoping to project an air of respectable… something. Respectable clumsiness, perhaps? Where are you working this summer, anyway? Back in Notts. Helping out at my uncle's firm, "Grimshaw & Sons," accountants. Exciting stuff. Living the dream. I’m hoping to land something remotely interesting, preferably not involving spreadsheets.

Honestly, the catering team were having a meltdown. Apparently, the keynote speaker has  serious  gluten intolerance, and one of the sandwiches had a rogue crouton. A  single  crouton. Caused a full-blown crisis. Oh my god, you’re kidding! That’s insane. So much stress over a crouton. Sounds about right for a conference. People get weirdly precious about their dietary needs. Tell me about it. I spent half the afternoon mediating between the speaker’s PA and the chef. It was a nightmare. Though, I did get a free cake as a peace offering. Chocolate orange, my fave. You're a saint, honestly. I’m so glad I don’t have to deal with that kind of pressure. Production control is mostly spreadsheets and occasionally shouting at the delivery drivers. Much calmer. Shouting at delivery drivers? That sounds… therapeutic. Sometimes it is! Though, I’m trying to be more zen about it. My new diet’s helping. Oh, you’re still on that juice cleanse thing? How’s that going? Surprisingly well, actually. I’m already feeling less bloated. Though, I’m eyeing up that chocolate orange cake with  serious  intent. Don't do it! You'll undo all your hard work! I'm with you on that one. I've been trying to cut back on bread. It’s the one thing I can't resist. I end up eating a loaf in a day. I know the feeling! Baguettes are my weakness. But I’ve started going to the gym a bit more. Just two or three times a week. It's making a difference. You’re so disciplined! I always start with the best intentions and then a Netflix binge happens, and the gym is forgotten. We’ve all been there! What are you doing this weekend then? Anything exciting? I'm going to see my brother in Brighton. He’s got a new girlfriend, apparently. Need to scope her out. Brighton’s nice. Got a good vibe. You'll have a laugh. Jealous! I'm stuck in Cambridge. Another conference, sadly. This one’s on sustainable tourism. Sounds… niche. Oof. Fun. I’m just chilling, probably. Might go for a walk along the river. Need to get out of this flat. It's starting to feel a bit claustrophobic. Have you thought about moving somewhere else? Maybe further out of the centre? I've been looking, but Cambridge is ridiculously expensive.

Right then, come and have a look at this bamboo. Didn’t think it’d actually take, did you? No, not at all, Arthur. Thought it’d be eaten by the slugs or something. It's grown a proper lot though, hasn't it? It has! It's wonderful, Bernard. Takes over, doesn't it? Like a jungle! Well, that’s the point, isn't it? A little bit of privacy from the neighbours. They’re still putting up that fence, you know. Apparently, they’ve ordered some fancy wrought iron. Wrought iron! Fancy indeed. What are they planning on keeping in, the lions? Oh, Bernard! Don’t be silly. Though I wouldn’t put it past them. They’re ever so particular, those Harpers. Particular, and nosey. I saw Mrs. Harper peering over the fence just the other day. Always watching, that one. Still, it’s better than nothing. At least we know someone’s about. Reminds me, did you ever manage to sort that TV licence out, Arthur? I’m still on it, Bernard. It’s a nightmare. They want to know if I use Skype. Apparently, that counts as watching television now. Can you believe it? Honestly, it's ridiculous. They’re just trying to get more money out of us. I had a similar problem with my benefits. They kept sending me forms asking about the most ridiculous things. And all that talk about being politically correct these days. It’s gone mad, it has. Can’t say anything anymore without someone getting offended. You’re telling me. I was reading about that eclipse the other day and even talking about how dark it got was apparently ‘insensitive’ to some people. Well, wouldn’t that be a sight? Everything going dark. Like the beginning of space, isn’t it? That documentary we watched about black holes… fascinating. Yes, absolutely gripping. All that stuff about how everything gets sucked in… Makes you wonder, doesn’t it? About the beginnings of everything. You know, I read an article the other day about that chap Stephen Hawking, about his theories on the universe. Oh, yes! Lovely man, such a clever person. Shame he's gone. They had that programme on the telly the other day, about painting. Do you remember, Arthur, you used to dabble a bit? A bit! A very long bit ago. Back when I was working, I used to sketch a bit in my lunch breaks.

Right, so, like, I’m absolutely starving. Didn’t eat much earlier, did I? No, you were busy cataloguing verbs all afternoon. Are we thinking Italian tonight? There’s that place near Southwark – ‘Bella Notte’ – remember? Bella Notte? Is that the one with the chips? I thought it was proper posh. No, no, it's not posh at all. Actually really decent pizzas and pasta. And surprisingly affordable. Though, to be fair, Southwark  is  a bit…rough around the edges, isn't it? Aye, it’s a bit of a mishmash, isn’t it? Not the loveliest part, but you get some good grub. Speaking of which, have you seen that new place that’s opened up in Shoreditch? ‘The Gilded Spoon’ or something ridiculous? I’ve seen the Instagram posts, yeah. Looks fancy. Tiny portions, probably. Costs an arm and a leg, I reckon. That’s what I thought. Reminds me of that cathedral we saw in Durham - huge, imposing, but you felt like you needed a mortgage just to walk inside. Durham Cathedral’s incredible, though. The architecture… you could get lost in there for hours. I'm worried about parking tonight, though. Southwark’s a nightmare. Maybe we should get the bus? The bus? Honestly, Daniel! In rush hour? I’d rather walk to Newcastle. Plus, driving’s easier than trying to navigate those bus routes. I still don't get why they call it ‘Elephant and Castle’ anyway. There’s no elephant! It’s a historical thing, apparently. Something about an old pub sign. You know, it’s funny – you’re from Sunderland, and you’re complaining about a place name in London! Well, Sunderland's got a proper name, hasn't it? Sunderland. No silly nicknames. And the houses there are…solid. Proper terraces. Not these flimsy Victorian things you get down here. They'd blow over in a strong breeze. They have their charm though, don’t they? Look at this street we’re on. Perfectly hideous, yet strangely… appealing. Like a badly painted postcard. Aye, I suppose. Still, I’d take a miner's cottage over a Chelsea townhouse any day. Speaking of houses, have you started looking at mortgages properly? A little. It’s…daunting, isn’t it? The prices are insane. I was looking at places near Canterbury, actually. Bit further out, but much more manageable. It’s got a lovely cathedral there, too.

Honestly, the robins have been quite vocal this morning. Absolutely belting out a tune. You’d think spring was already here. They are, aren’t they? It's astonishing, really. I can't identify half of them, though. Just a jumble of whistles and clicks. You’re always so good at knowing which is which. Years of practice, dear. My dad used to point them all out to me in the garden. He was a keen birdwatcher, you know. Though he'd wake everyone up at dawn with his alarm clock, just to catch the best of the singing. A menace, he was. Sounds familiar! My husband used to be like that. A five am riser for absolutely no reason. Drove me mad. You know, I’ve been trying to be a bit more proactive with the bird feeding. Put out fresh seed every morning, and they seem to appreciate it. Good for you! They do love a bit of sunflower heart. I’ve got a new feeder, one of those fancy ones that keeps the squirrels out. Although, they’re remarkably clever, those squirrels. They always find a way. Oh, I know all about clever squirrels! I had one once, it was hanging around every morning and pinching the seeds off the old feeder. I started putting out a bit of seed on the lawn, just for it. Now it ignores the feeder completely because it’s got an easier target. Oh dear. Well, at least you're keeping it well-fed! Speaking of things I rather don't enjoy… I’ve got the dentist next week. Dread. Absolute dread. Oh, don't remind me! I had a nosebleed last week. Right out of the blue. Horrendous. Nearly fainted. Oh, how awful! I had a bit of trouble with my throat recently too, a persistent tickle. Had to get it checked out, thankfully it was nothing serious. That's a relief. It’s scary, isn’t it? Those scares… my sister… it just highlights the importance of being vigilant. It really does. Speaking of vigilance, have you heard anything from Susan lately? I haven't seen her at the book club. No, not for a while. I heard through Margaret that she's been having some trouble with her gardening. The slugs have been horrific this year. Absolutely eaten everything. Oh, the slugs! It’s a war out there. I’ve been trying everything – beer traps, copper tape, the whole lot.

It’s so lovely to see you, honestly! It feels like ages. Last time we met was… what, Sarah’s wedding? It was! And goodness, that was nearly two years ago now, wasn't it? You look… really well. Proper relaxed. Thanks. Yoga’s been a lifesaver, seriously. I’m going three times a week now. Clears my head completely. You should try it. I keep meaning to, you know? But finding the time… with work and well, everything. It’s a constant juggle. I know exactly what you mean. Life's just a never-ending plate spin, isn’t it? How are the kids? Still keeping you on your toes? Oh, absolutely. Leo’s just entered that phase where he questions  everything . “Why is the sky blue? Why do birds fly? Why can't I have another biscuit?” It’s exhausting. And Maisie’s… well, Maisie’s a whirlwind of glitter and opinions. Sounds about right for that age! It's lovely though, isn’t it? Even when it’s utterly bonkers. How are you finding solo parenting? Still managing okay? It’s… challenging. Don’t get me wrong, I wouldn’t trade them for the world. But some days... Honestly, some days, I just lock myself in the bathroom for five minutes and breathe. It’s hard without another adult to share the load. I can imagine. I really can. I know we talked about the IVF years ago, after James… are you still… feeling okay about that decision? Not that there's anything wrong with it, of course. It’s a complex one, isn't it? At the time, it felt right, to give them both a sibling. But looking back… maybe it wasn’t. Maybe I should have just accepted that one was enough, for my own sanity. It's just… sometimes I wonder what it would have been like. It’s natural to wonder. It’s a big decision, and it’s okay to have those thoughts. Don’t beat yourself up about it. Thanks. What about you? Still teaching? Still enjoying it? It’s… different. It’s rewarding, of course. But the paperwork! It’s endless. And the social media, honestly. The pressure on teachers to be constantly online, sharing everything. It's ridiculous. Tell me about it! I swear, some people just use social media to show off. Like, "Look at my perfect child doing a perfect thing!"

This Earl Grey is lovely, really. Thanks for having me over, Robert. Oh, don’t mention it, Eleanor. Always a pleasure to see a friendly face. And you’re doing well, I hear? Still teaching languages? Yes, still plugging away! French and Spanish mostly. The kids are engaging this year, thankfully. A few real bright sparks. It’s rewarding, but exhausting too, you know? I can imagine. Teaching’s a tough gig. My Margaret used to say the same. Though she taught English Lit. Much more…intellectual, she’d insist. I’m sure it was. You must miss it though? Not really. Peace and quiet’s a wonderful thing. Though, occasionally, I do find myself correcting people's grammar. Old habits die hard, I suppose. Did you hear about that spate of burglaries on Oakwood Drive? Oh no, really? I hadn’t. That’s awful! Are they catching anyone? Seems not. Police don't seem to be doing much about it, if you ask me. Just more CCTV, more paperwork, less actual policing. Seems to be the way of things these days. It’s frightening, isn’t it? My brother's worried about his elderly mother; she lives on her own. That's the trouble. Folk are living longer, too, which is brilliant of course, but it puts extra pressure on families. My niece in Ashby just had twins! Can you imagine? Two babies! Goodness! That’s wonderful, but…a double handful! Are they doing alright? They say they are. Seems her and her husband are coping, though a bit sleep-deprived, naturally. He's a computer programmer, you know. Always glued to a screen. It’s funny how things change. My students are all so obsessed with their phones. Trying to get them to look up from the screen and actually  speak  to people…it's a challenge. They’re all attached to those things, aren't they? Margaret started a little knitting group down at the community centre. It's a good way to get people talking, do something with their hands. You ever fancied joining something like that? I haven’t really had the time, you know? Work’s pretty demanding, and I try to keep up with my French lessons. They're useful when interviewing candidates. Always good to keep learning, that is. Keeps the mind sharp. Speaking of sharp, have you seen that new Labour candidate?

Right, so pizza’s ordered then? I’m starving after that trek across town. Yeah, pepperoni and veggie for me. What about you lot? I'll have the pepperoni, please. Gotta fuel up for more FIFA later. Veggie for me too, trying to be vaguely healthy. Though, let's be honest, I’ll probably raid the biscuit tin afterwards. Classic Finn. Listen, did anyone manage to get tickets for The National next month? Ugh, I tried. Sold out instantly. Seems everyone and their dog wanted to see them. I had a look too, same story. Gutted. They're brilliant live. Yeah, I reckon you need to be on the website the second they go on sale. Those tickets disappear quicker than you can say “Matt Berninger.” Tell me about it! Well, at least we've got this. Anyone seen anything good at the cinema lately? Besides Matthew Vaughn’s new film which is dreary. I finally saw “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” Seriously blown away. Totally mad, but brilliant. Oh yeah, heard good things about that. Might have to check that one out. I’ve been re-watching a lot of old Studio Ghibli stuff lately. Ghibli's always a winner. Comfort viewing, isn't it? I saw "Oppenheimer" last week – pretty intense, but a proper cinematic experience. Yeah, heard it was good. I think I need something a bit lighter after all that. Any recommendations, Beth? Honestly, “Everything Everywhere…” It’s genuinely one of the best films I’ve seen in years. Just… prepare yourself for a lot. Right, pizza's here! Anyone want a drink? I brought some cider. Cider sounds perfect. Thanks, Dom. Although, I wouldn’t mind a cheeky lemonade too… Gotta pace myself. Lemonade for me, please. Thanks, mate. Okay, who’s up for FIFA first? I’m itching to beat you at it, Dom! Bring it on, Liam. You’re going down! Oh, here we go… Let the trash-talking commence. I’ll just be over here, quietly munching on pizza and hoping someone doesn't rage quit and throw the controller. Oh, should we get some popcorn too. Good plan! I'm in. Let's go! Do you guys want cheese or butter. Butter please! Butter! Cheese! Right coming right up! So anyone seen Dizzee Rascal live? I went to that gig once, it was good, so wild! Heard good things should check them out.

Right, so, who's got the aux? Anyone got a decent playlist? This Spotify's rubbish. I've got a few tracks. Bit of indie, bit of… well, you'll see. Is anyone else freezing? This weather is mental. One minute blazing sunshine, next minute, you could be in the Arctic. Tell me about it. I was practically sunburnt on Monday and now I need a blanket. It's ridiculous. Are we still on for that gym tomorrow? Yeah, definitely. I’m actually looking forward to it. Need to burn off some of that… stress. Game development is surprisingly sedentary. Sedentary and soul-destroying sometimes, let's be honest. But yeah, gym’s good. I’ve been trying to get back into it properly. That new place near the station seems alright, but the membership is extortionate. Right? Everything's so expensive these days. Speaking of expensive, Anon, how was that trip? You were gone for ages! It was brilliant! Barcelona was incredible. I wish I could just stay there forever. The architecture, the food… and the weather! Proper sunshine. Sounded amazing. Send some of that sunshine this way, please. Did you do any sketching while you were there? Loads! I've got a whole sketchbook full. I’ll show you when we get back. I even managed to squeeze in a couple of boat trips. Really needed that sea air. Good for you. I'm feeling a bit drained already, and I haven't even left Cambridge yet! Little Leo’s camp starts next week. I’m terrified. Camp? Seriously? He’s only, what, six? I know, right? But his school is doing this week-long outdoor adventure thing. Hiking, building shelters, all that stuff. He’s absolutely buzzing, but I’m picturing him covered in mud and missing me horribly. He'll have a blast. Kids are resilient. Remember when we were little and my parents sent me to that Scout jamboree? I came back with a million badges and a slightly disturbing obsession with knots. That’s true. Though I'd definitely pack him some extra snacks. And maybe a map? Just in case. A map’s a bit much, isn’t it? He’ll end up getting lost with the map. You’re probably right. I’m just… I’m worried about the bugs. He's terrified of spiders. They'll have staff to deal with bugs.

Oh, come  on ! Seriously? Another penalty shout turned down! They’re bottling it, aren't they? Absolutely bottling it. Ref’s having a mare. Bottling it is an understatement. They're practically handing the game to them. I can't believe they’re not pushing harder. All this possession, but where’s the killer instinct? It’s the Easter thing, innit. Everyone's a bit tired, a bit distracted. Family commitments and chocolate overload. Don’t remind me. My niece raided my chocolate stash within five minutes of arriving. It was carnage. Mine too. My little ones basically declared war on the Easter Bunny. It’s a battlefield in my house. Kids. Right. Back to the horrors on the screen. Did you catch any of that new sci-fi film,  Echoes of the Void ? Briefly. Sarah recommended it, didn’t she? I meant to watch it last night but got bogged down in reading. It looked pretty slick though, visually. Is it any good? Honestly? It's alright. Proper brain-tickler, lots of twists and turns. But it's a bit long. I felt like they were trying too hard to be clever. Right. So, not a massive recommendation then? Nah. Decent if you’re into clever sci-fi, but don’t go in expecting  Dune . It's more  Arrival  meets  Inception  with a dodgy plot twist at the end. You always give the best reviews. Always so detailed. Years of academic training, you know. It's a gift and a curse. Oh for goodness sake! Another wasted opportunity! Look, they’re just warming up. They've got time. It’s only the sixtieth minute. Easy for you to say. You’re not supporting them! I swear, every time I watch them, I feel ten years older. It's a spectator sport, love. Suffering is part of the deal. Want another cup of tea? I’ll put some biscuits on. Might ease the pain. Don’t mind if I do. Chocolate biscuits, please. I need something to distract me from this impending doom. And maybe a blanket. It's a bit chilly in here. Coming right up. Don't worry, something will turn around. They just need a little push. A spark of... something. A spark of sanity, more like. Now, now. Positivity, remember? Positivity. Even during Easter football disasters. End. Hope this helps! Let me know if you would like me to adjust or change aspects.

Look at this one, Grace. Remember when we took him to that fun fair in Weston-super-Mare? He was terrified of the waltzer. I was! I thought I was going to be sick. But then I loved it. I wanted to go on it again and again. He was so little then. You could have fit him into a rucksack. Almost! He was a whirlwind, wasn’t he? Always on the go. And look at this photo from Iceland. Remember that trip? Oh yeah! The glaciers! It was freezing, wasn’t it? But so cool, like in a film. Iceland, aye? Heard so much about it. Never been myself. Always wanted to see the Northern Lights, though. Such a beautiful sight, they say. We should take him again someday. He's just getting into photography now, you know. Iceland would be perfect. He definitely has your eye for a picture, Liam does. He’s got some really interesting stuff on Instagram. He's into filming things too. He says he wants to be a YouTuber. A YouTuber, is he? Well, he's certainly got the personality for it. Remember when he tried to build a rollercoaster in the garden? And it collapsed! It was hilarious. Dad nearly had a heart attack. Liam's always been a character. Still is. It's lovely to see. My wee grandson, Jamie, he’s quiet as a mouse. Keeps himself to himself. Every child’s different, aren't they? What’s his birthday coming up? Should we send something? He’s turning eight next month. He wants a Lego set. A big one. Maybe we should get him that new Star Wars set. He loves Star Wars. Good idea! We’ll look into it. Oh, this one! The London Marathon. Remember encouraging you to run that? I do. It was... chaotic. But amazing. Such a rush of adrenaline afterwards. You were incredible! I was so proud of you. Aye, a marathon! That takes dedication. My niece ran one once. Said it was the hardest thing she'd ever done. It was challenging, definitely. But worth it. You looked so happy in the photos. Liam was waving a flag along the route. He was! He’d made a big banner that said “Go Mum!” And it got all soggy in the rain. Oh, that’s classic Liam. Even then he could manage to be a bit of a disaster.

This lentil soup is really good, isn’t it? I’m glad you like it, Sarah. It's lovely, actually. Really warming - exactly what I needed on a day like today. You know, damp and grey. Remember those days in Peterborough when it just never stopped raining? Oh, dear, yes. Always damp. Remember those slate roofs, leaking everywhere? We used to have buckets all over the house. Mum, you always tell that story! It’s a classic. But seriously, Sarah, tell me about that new series you were reading. The Emma Donoghue one. 'Lessons in Lightning'? Yes! It’s utterly brilliant. A bit harrowing in places, obviously – it’s about a woman who accidentally kills her husband and raises their child in hiding - but the writing is just exquisite. I’m reading it on my Kindle, of course. So much easier to travel with, don't you think? Definitely. I've been trying to get into eBooks. My eyes aren’t what they used to be, but holding a physical book…it’s just a different feeling, isn’t it? It is, undeniably. Though I must admit, the convenience is hard to argue with. Remember those massive tomes we’d lug around as kids, Sarah? Trying to look intellectual. Oh, God, yes! Those Mills & Boon covers too, hidden under the homework books! We were scandalous. What was your favourite childhood game? Definitely skipping. Hours spent skipping in the street. Do you remember those long ropes? We'd challenge each other to do more rhymes. And Mum would get so cross if we were late home. Hopscotch was a good one too. And jacks. Remember jacks? Vaguely. We mostly played with dolls. My favourite was a little porcelain one called Beatrice. She had the most beautiful blue eyes. My sister had a doll called Penelope. She was covered in freckles! We used to have elaborate tea parties for them. Using my grandmother’s china, of course – which was a terrifying experience. Terrifying! My mum used to knit us little outfits for our dolls. Do you still knit, Mum? Not so much now. My fingers aren’t as nimble as they used to be. I used to make lovely scarves and jumpers. Wool was so much cheaper then. I've been trying to pick up crocheting again. I've got this pattern for a blanket, but it looks incredibly complicated. I think I might need a lesson!

Lovely sandwich, Maggie. Proper job you’ve done. Thank you, Arthur. Didn’t want you feeling peckish. Bit of pickle, just how you like it. Aye, that pickle makes all the difference. Remember old Mrs. Hawthorne down the street? She wouldn’t touch a sandwich without pickle. Said it gave it a bit of… zing. Mrs. Hawthorne! Goodness, that was years ago. She used to complain about the price of everything. Said the price of butter was scandalous. Scandalous it was. Everything’s scandalous now, isn’t it? Used to be able to get a loaf of bread for a few pennies. Not anymore. No, not anymore. The world’s changed, Arthur. Can’t remember the last time I bought a decent looking cabbage for a reasonable price. They don't grow 'em like they used to, that's for sure. My father had a little plot, just back of the house. Best cabbages you ever tasted. Firm, green, and crisp. Not like these things you get now. Watery and pale. Your father was a clever gardener. I always admired him. Remember that prize-winning marrow he grew one year? Aye, that was a whopper! Stood over three feet long, that did. Showed it off to everyone. Felt a bit silly, actually, standing over a marrow. Silly? It was impressive! Everyone was talking about it. Even the vicar came round to admire it. Funny, weren't it? The vicar wanting to look at a marrow. Still, he was a good man. Always had a kind word for everyone. He was. A lovely man. Do you think they'll have those summer fetes on this year? Hard to say, isn’t it? Everything’s so… uncertain these days. Still, I hope so. Always enjoyed a good fete. The coconut shy, the raffles… The homemade cakes were always the best. Mrs. Plumtree used to make a Victoria sponge that was simply divine. Aye, Mrs. Plumtree. Never could beat her sponge. You know, I wonder what became of those children from Costessey school. Remember young Timothy Bell? Always had his nose in a book. Timothy Bell… I think I remember. Always a quiet boy. Wonder what he's doing now. Probably a professor somewhere, I expect. Perhaps. Or maybe just living a quiet life. Wouldn't that be nice? A quiet life, with a bit of pickle on your sandwiches. It would indeed, Arthur.

Honestly, the amount of times I’ve had to correct Year 3 on ‘their’ versus ‘there’ is just… relentless. It's exhausting. Tell me about it! I saw a headline the other day - "Their going to fix the road" - I nearly spat out my coffee. The internet is a dark, dark place for grammar. It’s massively worse now though, isn’t it? Social media just encourages it. Everything’s rushed and sloppy. Remember when you had to actually  think  about your writing? Absolutely. It's not just the grammar either, it’s the vocabulary. They’re all speaking in slang now, and half the time I don't even know what they mean! Speaking of slang, have you heard from Chloe? I messaged her about that campaign I’m working on – need someone with a good ear for it – but she's been radio silent. No, I haven't. I hope everything's okay. She seemed a bit stressed last time we spoke about Mark. Still together? I think so, but she was hinting that things were rocky. Remember how she was obsessing over that tiny little detail about his job? Oh god, yes. The beige tie incident. He bought a beige tie and she nearly broke up with him. Seriously! It's like, let the man wear a beige tie! Anyway, what about you, Elsie? Still battling with your Year 2's over glitter glue? Don't even get me started on the glitter. I'm finding it  everywhere . In my hair, in my shoes, in my lunch… It’s a sparkly conspiracy. You need a glitter trap. Seriously. There are things online… Oh, speaking of online, I finally ordered that ridiculous sequin jumpsuit I was telling you about. No! Don’t tell me you actually did it? I did. It’s coming next week. I’m planning on wearing it to that Christmas party at work. You’re brave, girl. Very brave. You’ll blind everyone. That's the idea! Anyway, what are you all doing for Christmas? We're thinking of going to the Maldives. Maldives?! You’re kidding! Nope. Got a really good deal. My dad finally convinced me to check out those holiday comparison sites. Wow, lucky you! I'm stuck with Mum and Dad's annual Christmas drama. This year it’s apparently the perfect placement of the fairy lights. Oh, the Christmas Wars.

So, the planning permission came through then, for the extension? Aye, it did. Finally! Three years, can you believe it? Three years of forms and surveys and neighbours complaining. Seriously? What were they complaining about? Oh, the usual. "It'll block the light," "It'll devalue the property," "It’s an eyesore." Honestly, you’d think we were building a skyscraper. It’s just a little bump on the back, extra storage space. Can I have a room in the bump? Maybe, Liam. When you’re old enough to tidy your own room. He's got a point, though. We’re bursting at the seams in here. The kids are all grown up, but still hanging about. Tell me about it. I feel like I'm still living with my mum, even though I've got a flat. It's that Liverpool thing, isn’t it? We never really leave the nest. Aye, we don't. Where would we go? This neighbourhood's got everything you need. Close to the city centre, good schools… although, let’s be honest, the state of the roads is a disgrace. Seriously, they’re terrible. I was driving the other day and nearly lost a tyre on Smithdown Road. It’s getting worse, that's for sure. I read an article about the council cutting back on road maintenance. They're focusing on the tourist areas, apparently. Leaving us to fend for ourselves. Typical. They wouldn’t know a pothole if it bit 'em on the bum. Is Smithdown Road where Harry Potter films? That’s right, Liam. Parts of it were used for Diagon Alley. See? Even a pothole can be magical. I didn't even know that! He loves Harry Potter. Reads the books at least twice a year. Good lad. It's good to encourage reading. Although, sometimes I worry about the messages children get. All that talk of battling dark forces... Oh, here he goes with the serious talk. I’m just saying. There’s a lot in the news these days, isn’t there? ISIS, and all that… it's hard to protect them from it all. It’s scary, yeah. My boss was talking about it the other day, saying how much stricter security is going to be at the office. Well, you can’t afford to be ignorant. Need to be aware of what’s going on. But you can’t let it consume you, either.

Honestly, Nepal sounds like an adventure. I’ve never been anywhere quite like it, have you, Janet? Heavens, no. Though I did go backpacking through Europe when I was younger – seventies, you know! Very different then, of course. Much less…organized. Europe was a bit wild then, wasn’t it? I was busy trying to pass my O-levels. My parents never really believed in travel for us. Bit more sensible, I suppose. Sensible or just cautious? My mother always said travel broadened the mind. Though she hadn't travelled much herself! Made her own sausages though, bless her. Best in the village. I adore a good sausage! We get ours from the Farm Shop now – the pork ones are divine. And their coffee… far superior to anything you get in the supermarket. Are you stocking up for the weekend, Margaret? I might pop in later. I need some gluten-free biscuits. My grandson, bless him, is allergic to just about everything! The new school meal system is another nightmare, too. Honestly, trying to cater for every allergy and dietary requirement… Oh, don't get me started! When I was teaching, we had children with everything imaginable. Packed lunches were always a minefield. Though my husband, David, he’s a dab hand in the kitchen these days. Much better than I ever was. He does a mean risotto, gluten-free, naturally. Lucky you! My husband, John, is useless. Can’t boil an egg. At least he tackled that awful display at the school, though. I was the display co-ordinator for years, you know. Nightmare, it was. Oh, I can imagine. Sarah’s at it again – Iron Man training. She’s incredible, absolutely incredible. You should see her cycling down the lane now when the Tour of Britain went past... the tour itself was spectacular – right past our doorstep, can you believe it? It was lovely, wasn't it? I saw bits of it on the telly. All that effort… my daughter, Emily, she's trying to get into it, but she said it's too… intense. Intense is putting it mildly! My goodness, it takes dedication. Reminds me of my mother-in-law’s story, actually. Oh? Yes! During the war, you know. Fleeing Siberia – her family had to escape – all the way to Africa. They ended up in Kenya. Incredible journey. Makes Iron Man look like a walk in the park!

Right, so spill the tea. How’s the production control thing going, Chloe? You look knackered. Honestly, it's mental. Absolute chaos. We’re short-staffed, the supply chain is still a mess, and my boss is breathing down my neck about every little thing. It's like a constant fire drill. Oh, that sounds awful! Like proper stressful. Is there any way you can ask for some help? I have, like, three times. He just said, "It’s a busy time, Chloe, everyone's working hard." Which basically translates to, "Do more, don’t complain." Typical. Men. Honestly, the amount of times I've dealt with that in my job. It's infuriating, isn't it? Like, we're not robots. Seriously! And the worst thing is, I actually  like  the work itself, when it’s not a complete meltdown. I’m just drowning in detail right now. So, what  is  production control, actually? I've never really understood what you do. Well, basically, I make sure everything gets to where it needs to be, when it needs to be, and in the right quantities. Think about it, like if a shop needs a restock of, say, hairspray, I'm the one coordinating the order, the delivery, and making sure it actually arrives on time. It sounds simple, but with hundreds of different products and suppliers… it’s a nightmare. Blimey, that  is  a lot. I can see why you're feeling stressed. I’ve got a conference next month, and I'm already pulling my hair out thinking about all the logistics. Logistics are the bane of my existence. Right? It's always something. Last week, the caterer cancelled on me two days before a huge shipment arrived. Had to scramble to find a replacement. It was manic. Oh my god! That’s terrifying. Did you manage to find someone? Eventually! Thank goodness for Google and sheer luck. I practically begged a local restaurant to step in. They were absolute lifesavers. See, you're a superhero, Chloe. You're managing all that and still look like you haven't slept in a week. Thanks, I think. Keeps me busy, though, which I suppose is something. How's the conference planning going, Amy? Any disasters yet? Just the usual. Trying to corral suppliers, dealing with dietary requirements that are unnecessarily complicated, and figuring out the AV setup. You know, the fun stuff.

This Pad Thai is genuinely amazing, isn’t it? Much better than that last place we tried in Woolwich. Definitely. Needed a good noodle fix. Been a long day already, and it’s only half past six. Tell me about it. Double shift today. Honestly, dealing with those interview recordings… some people just mumble! It’s a nightmare transcribing them. I swear, my brain’s going to melt. You need to use some mnemonics, or something. Little tricks. I read an article about brain training exercises - apparently it helps with focus. Oh yeah? Like what? I’m all ears. Anything to stop me from wanting to chuck the laptop out the window. Well, this one suggested using rhymes to remember lists, or creating stories out of key words. Apparently, it engages a different part of the brain. Hmm, interesting. Though I think a large cup of tea and a lie-down might be more effective. Did you hear about the library, though? What, the Plumstead one? I saw something on the Borough Council website. They’re actually considering demolishing it to build flats. Can you believe it? Can you believe it? It’s the only decent library in this part of town! Where are kids supposed to go and read? They’re already cutting back on everything. Exactly. I had a look at the Council meeting notes. It’s all about ‘modernising’ the area and ‘increasing housing density’. They haven't really considered the community impact. It’s outrageous. I was thinking about starting a petition. Get people to sign it, maybe even stage a protest. That’s a brilliant idea. I’ll help you. I’ve got a bit more time, being a salaried administrator and all. You’re always running around. I know, right? It’s relentless. But someone needs to do something. It's always the same with these Borough decisions, isn't it? They don't listen to the people who actually live here. Never do. Remember when they tried to build that car park on the green space last year? Don’t remind me! That was a battle! Still, at least we managed to stop that. True. We’ll need to galvanize support this time around, though. It’s likely to be an uphill struggle. Let's start drafting the petition tonight. I can get it uploaded to Change.org. Perfect. And I’ll start advertising it on social media.

Well, Harold you’re looking peaky today. Bit pale, aren't you? Not enough sunshine, I reckon. Just a bit tired, Arthur. Not sleeping well. Been thinking, you know… about all this talk of the election. Oh, don't start on that again, Harold. You’ll give yourself an ulcer. And it’s all just noise anyway. None of them understand. Now, now, Margaret. Everyone’s entitled to an opinion. Though I must say, this year it’s particularly… convoluted. All that talk of taxes… frankly, it's a headache. It’s the principle of it, Arthur. Taking so much! We’ve paid in our dues, haven't we? Decades of it. And what do we get? Potholes, that’s what we get. Well, you can’t complain too much. You’ve had your pension, Harold. Better than some. Still, it’s dreary, isn’t it? Going through all the leaflets… half of them are from those Jehovah’s Witnesses again. Yes, they were round this morning. Quite persistent. Offering me tracts about the end times. As if I haven't got enough to worry about. They used to leave ‘em on the doorstep, you know. Now they knock. Bold as brass. They are, aren’t they? Speaking of bold… have you seen Elsie Perkins lately? She’s got a new hat. Bright orange, it was. Like a traffic cone. Elsie! She wouldn’t be caught dead in anything sensible. Remember that time she tried to park her Morris Minor right on top of the green at Mundesley? Oh, goodness, yes! Caused a right kerfuffle. The coast parking is a nightmare these days, isn't it? Used to be able to park anywhere. Now it’s all meters and restrictions. It's all greed, that’s what it is. Anyway, this Victoria sponge is lovely, Elsie. Did you use a lot of butter? Aye, I did. Never skimp on the butter, you know. Good for the soul. It certainly is. Though my joints are complaining a bit afterwards! Speaking of ailments, you’re still seeing that dentist on the Yarmouth Road, aren't you, Harold? They say it's the best in the county. Yes, yes, Dr. Finch. Not cheap, mind you. But he's thorough. Always talking about preventative care. Poking about with his little instruments. Well, you need to look after your teeth. They’re all we’ve got.

It’s so lovely to have you both here, really. Come in, come in. Let me take your coats. How was the journey? Perfectly fine, dear. Train was on time, and the taxi here was very pleasant. Though it's so much colder than Edinburgh, isn't it? Always is, Margaret. You never quite get used to English weather. Tea’s just brewing, darling. Are you having biscuits? I made fudge yesterday, you know, just like your mother used to. Oh, fudge! How wonderful, David. You know how I adore your fudge. Thank you. I’m trying to get the living room looking a bit more cosy, actually. I’m thinking of getting the armchair reupholstered. That old floral fabric is just dreadful. Upholstery is an art, you know. Used to know a chap, excellent work, but sadly he's retired. You need good quality materials, of course. Your neighbour, you mentioned him the other day, Peter, is that right? Something about a cat? Oh, Peter. Yes, he’s got this absolute menace of a Maine Coon. Keeps trying to get into the garden and terrorise the birds. It's a constant battle. I'm worried he might target the roses. Honestly, it's like having a small bear roaming about. Have you heard about that new Italian restaurant that's opened up on the high street? Apparently, it’s quite good. No, I haven't! We must try it. Everything seems to be getting so expensive though. It's all hitting the budget, isn't it? Electric bills are terrifying. That’s the story everywhere, isn't it? People are struggling. We were just talking about log burners this morning. Their efficiency is remarkable, but the cost of logs... Oh, a log burner is lovely. But so much soot! And the chopping! I remember your father used to spend hours chopping logs. It was good exercise, Margaret. Keeps you young. I liked the smell of woodsmoke. I've been interviewing for a new project, quite a big one. It's transcription work, mostly legal documents. They're talking about outsourcing some of it to India. Oh, really? That's a shame. But I suppose it's inevitable, isn't it? The world’s shrinking. I do worry about these things, David. Good jobs disappearing. Schools are struggling too, aren’t they? All these academies… a dreadful system, if you ask me.

Honestly, this business of buying a house is a nightmare. All these conveyancing fees and stamp duty… it’s enough to make a man tear his hair out. Tell me about it, Arthur. Remember when you bought that little bungalow in Wroxham? It was a doddle compared to this, apparently. All paperwork, eh? It was simpler times, Roger. A handshake and a bit of paper. Now it’s endless forms and solicitors breathing down your neck. Though, Brenda, you haven't said much. Are you finding it all a bit overwhelming? Just listening, Arthur. It’s all so complicated these days. Back when I was minding the children, things were straightforward, you know? A nappy change, a biscuit, a bit of playtime. No mortgages or conveyancers. You’re right, Brenda. Simpler times indeed. Though those youngsters today, they don’t know how good they’ve got it. All this discussion about Universal Credit and the like… it's a mess. Don’t even get me started on politics, Roger. The television’s been full of it lately. Makes you want to switch off completely. Speaking of which, did you find the remote, dear? I can’t seem to locate it. Is it under the cushion again, Arthur? Always under the cushion. No, not this time, Brenda. I’ve checked all over. Perhaps Roger’s moved it? I haven’t touched it! Honestly, everything disappears in this house. It’s like a Bermuda Triangle for remotes and spectacles. And what about that new recycling scheme they want us to do? Separating everything into seven different bins! It’s ridiculous! It’s for the environment, Roger. We have a responsibility. Though, I’ll admit, it’s a bit much. I’d rather just throw it all in one. It’s all down to politics isn’t it? Trying to make us feel guilty. I was just driving to Norwich the other day and the Sat Nav led me down this tiny country lane. Practically a cart track! Oh, Sat Navs! Don’t get me started. Mine once tried to send me through a farmer’s field. I told it exactly where to go after that. Old school, Arthur. Paper map and a good sense of direction – that’s what you need. I used to rely on the AA map, when I took the children out. So much more reliable than these new gadgets.

Right, so this thing is still playing up. It's driving me mad. What's it doing now, Dad? Still flashing that weird blue screen? Worse, actually. Now it's decided it doesn't want to recognise the hard drive at all. Just… clicks. A very ominous clicking sound. Oh dear. Is it the warranty still? That’s the rub, isn’t it? Apparently, they said it’s “user error” because I had a sudden power cut last month when fixing that dodgy cable. User error? You fixed the cable! That’s not your fault! Tell them that, son. They’re sticking to their guns. Said I should have used a UPS - a Uninterruptible Power Supply. Which, for a home user, is a bit much. Well, you use your computer every day for work, don't you? It might be worth getting a new one then. I know, but it's only been a year and a half. And it’s a decent machine. Just needs a little – or a lot – of fixing. Do you remember how to mend these? I could have a look. I've been watching a few YouTube videos about computer repair. Honestly, you'd be better at this than I am. You've got a knack for tech stuff. Just… be careful. Don't smash it any more than it already is. Little man’s letting us know he’s ready for dinner. Honestly, he’s got a timing system down to a science. Right, let’s get some food on the table then. Are we having those fajitas tonight? Yes, I’ve made the sauce. It’s a really good batch, I think. Lots of lime. Sounds good. Can I help set the table? Please do. And afterwards, if you're feeling brave, maybe you could take a look at this computer. No promises, mind you. Okay, I'll give it a shot. Though I'm not sure I'll be able to fix it before the rugby! Don’t worry about the computer, just enjoy the match. Are we going to head over to your uncle’s place after? Yes, we’re on for the Uncle Seamus’s. He said they're putting on a buffet. Alright, excellent. Although don’t be surprised if little Cian has been over-stimulated by that point. He’ll be grand. He just needs a good swim after all that excitement.

Right, pizza time! Who's hungry? Me! Me! Pizza! Pizza! Yummy! Okay, okay. Let's get these plates out. Now, who wants pepperoni, cheese, or veggie? Pepperoni! Cheese! Alright then. Two pepperonis, one cheese. Now, while we're eating, I was thinking…remember we were talking about how Mummy sometimes struggles to understand what you're saying, especially when you’re talking really fast? Yes… sometimes I say too fast. Exactly! It’s a bit like trying to catch bubbles – they just pop before you can grab them. So, sometimes you need to slow down and make sure I can hear every word. Like this: "I want more pizza, please." Can you say that slowly and clearly? I… want… more… pizza… please. Perfect! See? Much easier to understand. You’re brilliant at communicating! Communication… is… hard! It  can  be hard sometimes, little man. But you’re getting there. Okay, now, a quick game? Let’s do some adding. If I have five slices of pizza, and you have two, how many do we have altogether? Seven! You’re right! Super clever. One, two, three, four, five… six, seven! Excellent! Now, I had an idea...remember we talked about making a fairy garden? Maybe after we tidy up, we could look for some moss and little stones for it? Yes! A fairy house! With sparkly things! Can we put a Loch Ness monster in it? A Loch Ness monster in a fairy garden? That's a wonderful idea! He could be the guardian of the fairies. You know, I read a really interesting article about the Loch Ness Monster the other day. Apparently… What?! Tell me! Well, it said that some scientists think there might be a very large eel living in the loch. Eel? Like a slimy one?! A very, very big one! Maybe big enough to look like a monster from far away. But it's still a mystery, isn't it? Do you think it’s real, or just a big ol’ eel? I think it's real! A sparkly Loch Ness monster! A Loch Ness eel! With pointy teeth! Alright, alright. Now, who wants some juice with their pizza? And remember to use your words – “Please” and “Thank you” go a long way, you two! Please! Juice, please! Thank you! Pizza! Good! Perfect. You’re both doing brilliantly today! Now, have you two thought about what you want to wear to the party on Sunday?

This seafood pasta is unreal, isn’t it? Honestly, best I’ve had. It really is, love. And the wine’s lovely too. Much better than that stuff we had in Pula. Remember that, Liam? Bleugh! Yeah, it tasted like vinegar. This is proper nice, though. Can I have some more bread? Everything’s excellent, actually. The olive oil here… it’s on another level. Very well-sourced, I’d imagine. Dad’s always has to find the geographical origins of everything. Well, it’s a fascinating subject! Sustenance is tied to environment, you know. It's about the terroir. Terroir, is it? Liam, what's terroir? It's when the soil makes food taste better? Spot on, lad! See, you  do  listen in class sometimes. This risotto is brilliant too, Maisie. I'm proper full. I’m still working on mine. It’s huge. I’m trying to get a good shot for Instagram before it gets cold. Look at this light! Istria is stunning. You should have tried some of that truffle oil they sell in Rovinj. Fantastic stuff, though a bit pricey. Reminds me of those truffles we had in Florence, that little place… what was it called? Piccolo Fiore? You and your fancy restaurants, eh, John? Give me a greasy takeaway any day! Can we go swimming in the pool later? Definitely! It was freezing yesterday, but the sun’s out now. Don’t get too carried away, Liam. I hear they're finding more birds with avian flu. And there’s that new strain of Ebola floating around… John! Don't go bringing that into dinner! We’re supposed to be relaxing. Seriously, Dad. You're always finding something dreadful to talk about. Remember that time you told us about the computer virus that could wipe out the world? I was simply pointing out a potential threat! It's important to be informed. It's similar to the security issues at the border. I was chatting with one of the immigration officers at Zurich airport last year… fascinating insights into… Can we talk about something else? Like… are they ever going to invent flying cars? Good question, Liam. I reckon they will, eventually. You know, like Steve Jobs, thinking different. Oh, you and your tech hero worship, Maisie. Remember when you swore you’d never buy an iPhone? And now you’re glued to it! It was different then, Mum!

These letters from the debt collectors are getting quite relentless, aren’t they? Constant reminders. Reminds me of when they were trying to take our telly off us, years ago. Oh, don't remind me! That was awful. I was so cross. Remember Alan, on the phone, absolutely going for them? Typical Alan. Always stood up for what he believed in. Though it did get a bit heated, didn’t it? Had to calm him down. He’s always been a firebrand, that one. Good heart, though. So, what are you all watching these days? Anything good on the telly? Not much, to be honest. Too much of that Real Housewives rubbish. Give me a good detective show any day. Remember Bergerac? Now that was quality. Oh, yes! I loved Bergerac! And that lovely theme tune. We should have a party, a proper old-fashioned one. With a fancy dress theme! A party? Now there’s an idea. We’ve been a bit quiet lately. We could have it in the garden, weather permitting. Sounds rather nice. We could have a theme. Perhaps something to do with the telly? Bergerac, Columbo… I’ve got some lovely sunflower seeds, you know. Could plant them out, brighten up the garden. Always loved sunflowers, reminds me of Norfolk. Oh, that’s a lovely idea, Derek. Sunflowers are just so cheerful. I used to sing in church, you know, back when I was a girl. Really, Eileen? I didn’t know that. What kind of hymns? All sorts! And sometimes we’d go to the Abbey to sing. Beautiful acoustics, it was. Proper spine-tingling stuff. I did a bit of driving down to see my daughter in Surrey last week. Dreadful traffic. Absolutely horrendous. You need a good sat nav these days, otherwise you're completely lost. I’m hopeless with computers, you know. Always getting tangled in wires. Brebner tried to sort it out for me last week, but I no idea. I had a bit of a scare the other day. Thought I might be due some PPI compensation! Started filling out a form, but Brebner said it was probably a scam. PPI, eh? They're all over the place. Be careful with those, Eileen. They'll take your money if you let them. Speaking of money, you read that article in  The Spectator  last week, about the increasing debt levels among young people?

Dreadful weather this morning, wasn't it? Absolutely pouring down. I’m soaked through, despite the umbrella. Aye, it was a right deluge! Glad I brought my raincoat. Being inside all day does protect you from the worst of it, though. How was your day going, dear? Lots of interesting cases? A few, yes. Mostly petty theft, parking violations… you know the usual. It’s just… it feels heavier somehow, doesn’t it? All the negativity. This justice system, it feels more about punishing than rehabilitating. Aye, you’re not wrong there. It’s got stricter over the years. When I started as an usher, there seemed to be more emphasis on giving people a second chance, particularly the young ones. Now it's just… bang, straight into the system. Exactly! And the costs… the court fees, the legal aid cuts. It’s becoming a privilege to defend yourself properly. Makes you worry about fairness, doesn’t it? It does. My grandson, Liam, he’s trying to get into law himself. Says he wants to make a difference. I just hope he’s got the stomach for it. It's a rough world, the legal world. He sounds like a lovely boy. I teach languages, so I see a different side of things – communication, understanding. It feels like we need more of that in general, especially within this system. It’s true. Though, speaking of communication, the train delays were a nightmare this morning! Nearly missed my connection in Birmingham. They say it was down to signalling problems. Everything's connected, isn't it? The trains, the weather... the climate, generally. Oh, don't even get me started on the climate. It’s terrifying, isn’t it? The heatwaves, the floods… My sister lives in Australia, and she’s just sent me some photos of the wildfires. Heartbreaking. Terrible. Makes you think about your carbon footprint, doesn’t it? Though, what one person can do… it feels like a drop in the ocean. The price of everything’s going up too, isn’t it? Makes you wonder how people are managing. It does. Energy bills, food costs… it's a constant worry. I have to be so careful with my money these days. Savings are dwindling. Aye, it's tough all round. I’m lucky to have my bit of earnings from the court, and my pension helps. But I still worry about my daughter.

You know what, darlings? Mummy's feeling really, really happy today. Why, Mummy? Why are you happy? Because I built a big one! That’s lovely, sweetheart, but Mummy’s happy because…well, because we’re all together, having a nice time. And sometimes, just being happy feels...amazing, doesn't it? Like a bouncy castle! Exactly! Like a bouncy castle. Do you know a rhyme about being happy? Um…happy, happy, joy, joy! That’s a good start! Perhaps we can make one up together. Let’s see…Happy as… happy as a… Happy as a bumble bee! Buzz, buzz, buzz! Wonderful! Happy as a bumble bee, buzzing through the trees! Perfect. Now, do you know what else makes people happy sometimes?
