Ice cream! Ice cream definitely does! But sometimes, people think having lots and lots of money makes them happy. Lots and lots of money! Like a mountain of coins? Exactly! A huge, sparkly mountain. But do you think a mountain of coins would  really  make you happy? Hmm… if I could buy all the Lego in the world! Well, that  would  be a lot of Lego. But money doesn’t always buy happiness, does it? Sometimes, the best things – like playing with your brother, or a cuddle from Mummy – they don’t cost a thing. Cuddles are the best! They really are. You know, it’s much better than a mountain of coins. Wouldn't you agree, darling? Mmm-hmm. But I still want some Lego! We can talk about Lego later. Right now, let's finish building our bouncy castle, happy as bumble bees! Now, where did that red block go... ? Over here!    No, it's on the roof!    Little chatterboxes. Perfect. Makes me really happy to see you both. Me too! Happy happy! Bouncy castle! Buzz buzz!    That's wonderful! Now who's building the tower? Me! I am! No, me!   . Oh my goodness, settle down, both of you! Share the blocks, you two. Now. Don't we want a really good, tall, strong tower? Okay. Okay. That's my lovely children. And… if we had lots of money can we…can we buy the whole Lego shop? Perhaps one day! But for now, how about we save up for a little Lego set? That’ll be a very happy day! Yeah! A very happy bouncy castle day!H.,H........

So, what are you thinking about for careers, then? Like, realistically. Ugh, don’t even start. It’s terrifying, isn’t it? Everyone’s asking. My dad’s already got me looking at investment portfolios… apparently, it’s key. Investment portfolios? Seriously? Mine just keeps saying ‘something sensible.’ Sensible isn’t a career, Dad. Exactly! It's like, what  is  sensible? Being a lawyer? Accountant? So boring. I was looking at engineering. Structural, maybe. Designing bridges or something. Think about the impact, you know? Yeah, okay, that’s pretty cool. But what about the tech side? Like all the AI stuff. It's evolving so fast, it’s mental. True. I was reading about this guy who patented a self-healing concrete. Imagine that! No more potholes, ever. Wow! That’s actually amazing. It’s crazy to think about how many inventions could just… revolutionise things. Do you think we'll ever see flying cars? Probably not. Too much hassle, honestly. Too many rules and regulations. Speaking of things evolving, China’s getting huge. It’s kind of scary, isn’t it? Definitely. They’re investing so much in everything. My uncle, he works with a logistics company and he says it's all about them now. Everything’s being made there and shipped over. It’s weird, isn't it? Like the whole world’s shifting. I wonder if there’ll be any jobs left for us that aren't connected to China somehow. Maybe we should invent something  in  China, then. Joint venture or something. Get in on the ground floor. You're serious? Kind of. I mean, think about it - a market of a billion people! You could create anything. Okay, okay, you've got a point. But what about investment then? My dad was going on about diversifying and stocks… it just sounds complicated. Yeah, he does. It's overwhelming. He keeps talking about Bitcoin and crypto stuff that I don't even understand. It all seems so risky, doesn’t it? Plus, you need money to invest in the first place! Exactly! See, that's the catch. Maybe we should invent the self-healing concrete  and  a way to make money without working. Then we'll be set! Now you're talking! Although, I reckon the potholes will still be there before we get around to it. Probably. Still, it’s good to dream, right? Let’s just hope Sixth Form doesn’t kill all our dreams first.

This view is absolutely ridiculous isn't it? I mean, just look at it. Mountains for days. It is gorgeous. Definitely worth the early flight and the frankly terrifying transfer. Remember that driver? Don't remind me! He was driving like he was late for a rally. My knuckles were white gripping the seat. Did you manage to get any decent footage on your phone? I did, yeah. I'll send you some later. It was a bit shaky, but you can definitely hear me screaming. You should have filmed yourself! No way! I was too busy trying not to vomit. So, skiing then. How did you find it? You looked like you were having the time of your life on the slopes. It was brilliant! A little wobbly at first, obviously, but I got into it. Managed a couple of blue runs, even attempted a red. Didn't quite conquer it, but it was fun trying. Did you manage to stay upright? Last time we went, I’m pretty sure you ended up in a snowdrift. Oh, you're not wrong. I spent a good portion of the morning picking snow out of my gloves. But I’m improving! Definitely improving. I managed a few runs down the gentle slope without falling. Progress, right? Definitely progress. Though you looked slightly terrified the entire time. Strategically cautious. There’s a difference. Anyway, how are the kids coping? Have they managed to drag Mark up the mountain yet? They are loving it. Absolutely loving the snow. Mark… well, Mark’s having a ‘relaxed’ holiday. He’s mostly been found in the bar with a pint. The kids have managed to persuade him to take them tubing, though. Said he’s feeling brave. Good man! They need to wear him out a bit. It’s always good to get him out of his comfort zone. Have you heard from Mum and Dad? Did they manage to get through to Auntie Susan? Yes, I spoke to them last night. They’re both doing well, settling into their cruise. Apparently, Auntie Susan is complaining about the lack of tea bags in her cabin. Of course she is. You know she won't be happy unless she can brew a proper cuppa every few hours. It's her life’s purpose, isn't it? Anyway, have you looked at the menu yet? I'm starving. All that skiing really works up an appetite.

Right, so where were we? The string breaking, wasn't it? It's infuriating, absolutely infuriating. I’ve had so many rackets ruined that way. It is, isn't it? Proper waste of good money. I was thinking though, instead of that nylon string, what about using paracord? It’s much stronger, you see. Paracord? Really? Wouldn’t it be too thick? And rather… sticky? Not if you use the thinner stuff. And tie it properly, really tight. I’ve been experimenting with cable ties too, you know. A few strategically placed ones along the length of the string, almost invisible, and they’d stop it snapping. Cable ties… interesting. What sort of cable ties? And how would you secure them to the racket properly? Can’t have them pinging out mid-match! Small ones, the black ones. About an inch long. And you’d need a really strong adhesive. Something like epoxy. Dry fitting them first, of course, to get the spacing right. Need to factor in the weight gain too, doesn’t want to make it too heavy. Weight! Yes, absolutely. And the dimensions. We’d need to be able to adapt it to different racket sizes and string patterns. What do you think a repair like that would cost, realistically? Materials only, not including our labour, of course. Well, paracord’s not cheap, but a decent length would be under five pounds. Cable ties, a ten-pack, maybe two pounds. Adhesive… another three, four pounds. So, roughly ten pounds, all in. We could offer different tiers - basic cable tie version, full paracord replacement… Exactly. Tiered pricing. I like that. And a catchy name. Something memorable. "Fleet Strings"? No, that's silly. Fleet… as in, a fleet of rackets, all swiftly repaired. It's a bit clever, isn't it? A bit! More like convoluted. Anyway, where would we market this? Primary schools? Secondary schools? It’s a big difference, isn’t it? Primary kids are less likely to use full-string rackets. Definitely secondary schools. And maybe tennis clubs. We could even approach the local badminton association. Imagine, "Fleet Strings - your racket’s best friend!" Oh dear. Oh! Blast! Sorry, dear. I’ve just taken a bit too much off the side. Nearly clipped my ear lobe there! And look at that stripe, I’ve gone and chopped a stripe right in! Don't worry, it’ll grow back.

Lovely cuppa, that. Just right. Been a bit chilly this afternoon, hasn’t it? It has, dear. Bit of a nip in the air. Though Norfolk weather’s rarely ever predictable, is it? That’s the truth, Mum. Always a surprise. So, Dad, you were saying something about that exhibition you went to? Oh yes, the Turner exhibition at the Sainsbury Centre. Quite something, it were. Never much cared for landscape painting, truth be told, but Turner… well, Turner was different. Different how? What struck you about it? It were the light, lad. The way he captured the light. Almost like looking at the sky itself, rather than a picture of it. All those swirls and colours… like the sea boiling up, or a storm brewing. You’ve always been a bit of a grumpy old man when it comes to art, Harold. Always preferred a nice landscape painting with a sheep or two, haven’t you? Aye, that’s true enough. Something recognizable, something you can place. But Turner... he wasn't concerned with recognizability, was he? He was after something else entirely. Something deeper. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How art can evoke such different feelings in people. Some people might see chaos in Turner's work, and others might see a kind of sublime beauty. I completely agree. And it’s not just about the subject matter, but the technique too. The way he used oil paints, the layering, the brushstrokes... it’s all part of the message. I’ve been doing some research on his use of pigments lately. Apparently, he experimented with some really unusual materials. Pigments, eh? Never thought about that. Just saw the colours, you know. The way they danced. You’re getting cultured in your old age, Harold! It’s lovely to see. Don't go changing me now. Always preferred a nice bit of folk art myself. A pottery cat or a patchwork quilt, something like that. There's a wonderful exhibition of contemporary folk art at the Norwich Castle soon. I was thinking of going, might be something you'd enjoy, Dad. Folk art, eh? Now you're talking! Something with a bit of heart. A bit of charm. It's amazing how art can connect with people on such a different level. It's not always about technical mastery or deep intellectual concepts. Sometimes it's simply about finding something you can relate to.

Honestly, Chloe from marketing is just… something else, isn’t she? The passive aggression is  intense . Tell me about it. I overheard her complaining to Sarah about how ‘difficult’ you are to work with. Difficult?! I’m literally the one holding everything together on that project! She’s just massively insecure because I actually get things done. Classic. Girls like that. Thrive on drama and making themselves look like the victim. So, how’s the ward been? Still dealing with Derek and his… unique interpretations of reality? Don't even get me started. He insisted tonight that he was a talking pigeon. A  talking  pigeon. I spent a good twenty minutes trying to convince him he wasn't going to sprout feathers. Oh my god. Bless him. I had Mrs. Davies trying to teach me French again. Bless her. You’re a mental health nurse, not a linguist! I know! She keeps saying “Bonjour, comment allez-vous?” and expects me to reply flawlessly. My French is about as good as Derek’s pigeon skills. Right? It’s so frustrating. Like, why even bother? It's a waste of everyone’s time, and just makes me want to procrastinate more. Speaking of, I'm still avoiding doing the dishes. Join the club. They’re piling up like a miniature Mount Vesuvius in the sink. We need to tackle that tomorrow. Or Sunday. Definitely Sunday. I'm feeling exceptionally lazy tonight. I keep thinking about how that cleaning product I got smells like blueberries. Seriously? What brand is it? “SparkleClean”. Ridiculous name, but the smell is genuinely lovely. It’s almost hypnotic. You’re right! It does smell like berries. Maybe we should clean just for the aroma. Exactly! That's a truly brilliant idea. Although, I'm starting to think the English language itself is just one giant procrastination tool. What are you on about now? Think about it! All those unnecessary words, those complicated grammar rules… it's all designed to distract us from actually  doing  anything. You’re such a weirdo. But also, kind of right. Maybe. Okay, so less procrastinating about cleaning, more engaging in movie recommendations? I swear, if we don’t watch something tonight, I’m going to go crazy. Deal. But no rom-coms, please. I’m already overstimulated by Chloe’s melodrama. Something dark and twisty. You got it. Let’s get some popcorn going.

Honestly, another day, another spreadsheet. I’m starting to think I could dream in pivot tables. You always say that. It’s part of your daily ritual now, isn’t it? A lament about spreadsheets. Well, it's true! And then Mr. Henderson wants me to rearrange his schedule for the fifth time this week, because apparently a vital conference call moved by fifteen minutes. Fifteen minutes! He’s always been a bit… finicky, hasn’t he? You know, I bet if you offered him a cigarette, he’d take it. He looks like a man who’s fought hard for everything in his life, and now he’s just clinging to control. Don’t give him any ideas! I’m trying to wean him off the ones he already has. Honestly, the guy sneaks into the garden shed for a sneaky puff. It's ridiculous. It  is  ridiculous. Though, I have to admit, I wouldn’t say no to a dram of something decent tonight. This week has been… lacking. Don’t you start. You’re supposed to be cutting back! Remember what the doctor said? The doctor says lots of things. He also told me to do more yoga. I'm more of a ‘curl up with a good book and a whisky’ kind of man, apparently. Exactly. Which is why I'm reminding you. It’s common sense, darling. Not exactly rocket science. Now, now. Don't start the common sense vs. intelligence debate again. I told you, intelligence is inventing the rocket, common sense is knowing not to fly it into a wall. See, you  are  intelligent. You just like to pretend you're not. Speaking of which, I was reading an article this morning about cultural differences in parenting. Apparently, in some Asian cultures, children are taught explicitly how to behave in social situations from a very young age. Sounds… intense. A bit like Eton, but for everyone. It was explaining how it relates to feminism. How some argue it reinforces traditional gender roles, while others say it equips girls with the social skills to navigate a patriarchal system and negotiate fairer outcomes. That's a clever way of framing it. So, it's not just about social niceties – it’s about empowerment. Building a framework to operate within and subvert it when necessary. Exactly. It got me thinking about how much we explicitly teach Amelia about those things.

Right, so farm day done and dusted! What did you both think? Isla, you were practically glued to the sheep. They were fluffy! And they said baa! And I fed one a carrot. He ate it really fast. I liked the tractor ride! It was bumpy. And I saw a pig with a curly tail. You did! Both of you were excellent on the tractor ride, no complaining at all. Unlike some people I know who moan about everything! But it  was  a bit scary! And really fast! It wasn't that fast, sweetie. Just a gentle countryside ramble. So, the farm was a success then? Yeah! Can we go again? Yeah! Can we see the cows next time? We might have to save up a bit for that, but we’ll see. Now, how was school today? Any good reports from your teachers? Matthew, anything exciting to tell me? Mrs. Davies said I was good at sharing. That’s wonderful, love! Well done! Isla, how about you? Did you remember everything we talked about yesterday about listening and trying to take turns? Mostly. Mostly? What does that mean ‘mostly’? Finley kept looking at my drawing and I wanted to finish it first. Oh, I see. It’s tricky when someone’s being a bit nosy, isn't it? But it's important to take turns and let everyone have a go. I’ll have a chat with Mrs. Peterson about it. Can we watch a DVD now? You two always want to watch a DVD! After a long day out, maybe a bit of quiet time is good for everyone. Which one shall we choose? Horrid Henry or Moody Margaret? Horrid Henry! Moody Margaret! Okay, okay, let’s compromise. How about we watch half of each? We'll start with Horrid Henry, then Moody Margaret. That way you both get a bit of what you want. Okay! Okay! Can I have some carrot sticks first? The ones from the farm were really yummy. Of course, love. Carrot sticks it is. And then DVD time. Let's just wash our hands first, shall we? You're both covered in something... I don't even want to know what. Speaker_2 & 3:  sighs  It’s never a dull moment, is it? Now, hurry up and wash those hands! And no arguing over the soap! Okay? Okay! Okay! Right then wash, wash, wash! And that’s all for now.

Right, so, this crochet blanket. It's ambitious, isn’t it? I'm starting to think I bit off more than I can chew. It's supposed to be like a cityscape, you know? All different textures and colours. It looks brilliant, honestly. I’ve seen the squares you've done; the detail is incredible. Bit mad though, attempting something that big. Remember that time you tried to knit a life-sized badger? Don’t remind me! It ended up looking like a very misshapen sausage. I gave it to Auntie Elsie. She put it on the scarecrow in the garden. Said it scared off the pigeons. Typical Elsie. So, what inspired the cityscape? You were in London last month, weren’t you? Yeah, that’s where I got the idea. All those brutalist buildings, the graffiti, the sheer energy... I wanted to capture that. It's proving tricky to translate into wool though. Some of the colours are just impossible to find. I've ordered a couple from Etsy – variegated grey and "brick red" apparently. Fingers crossed. Sounds intense. Speaking of intense... did you see the closing ceremony of the Olympics? Honestly, that was something special. The tributes to Dame Olivia... heartbreaking. Awful, isn’t it? It's weird, seeing her everywhere now. Such a legend. And everything feels a bit… muted, like the world's taken a step back. Apparently, there’s a memorial in her hometown, that’s a rather lovely gesture. Definitely. Speaking of gestures, have you seen the Banksy piece that appeared in Weston-super-Mare? The girl with the aerosol can? Oh yes! I’ve been following that. Brilliant, as always. That council was predictably dithering about listing it. Thankfully, they came to their senses. It’s just so…  Banksy , isn’t it? Defiant and thought-provoking. Exactly. Captures the essence of the place, too. Weston-super-Mare's no stranger to artistic interventions, is it? No, I suppose not. Though usually of the donkey ride variety. We should go down and see it properly, you know, when we have time. It’s not far is it? Nope. Maybe when we've got Easter sorted. Are you thinking chocolate chickens again this year? Oh, please no. The supermarket ones are just pure sugar. I was thinking of making some hot cross buns instead. Trying a new recipe this year. Earl Grey infused. Earl Grey hot cross buns?

Right then, sorted the tea, you want a biscuit with that, love? Digestive or ginger? Digestive’s perfect, thanks, Maggie. Long day out, you know. Needed something a bit…substantial. Tell me about it! The Tube was a nightmare this morning. Absolutely rammed on the Northern Line, you wouldn’t believe. Felt like sardines in a tin. Oh, I know the feeling. I took the District Line, thought it’d be quieter, but no such luck. Packed like a clown car. Honestly, London Transport… Don't get me started! They’re charging a fortune and the service is still shocking. Remember when we used to be able to get a seat, even on a Saturday? Those were the days, weren't they? Everything's just gone up, hasn't it? Trains, buses, even a simple cup of coffee. Robbery! Absolutely. Anyway, the Science Museum was brilliant though. Wasn't it? That flight simulator... Oh, brilliant! I loved that. Nearly threw up, though. Felt like I was actually flying, you know, banking and all. A bit much for an old man, perhaps. You were clinging on for dear life, I could see it! I felt a bit queasy myself, but it was worth it. And the interactive exhibits, so clever. Yes, good stuff. Though I must say, the Impressionists exhibition at the Tate was a bit… disappointing. Really? I thought it was lovely. Monet's water lilies were gorgeous, as always. It was all a bit… blurry, wasn't it? Like looking through a steam-covered window. Needed a stronger cup of tea after that. You’re impossible! Then we went to that IMAX, for the 3D thing. That was something else, wasn't it? The sharks… practically swimming in my face. Felt a bit claustrophobic, though. I know! The experience is amazing, but I find it a bit overwhelming sometimes. All those flashing lights and the silly glasses… It's a bit much, yeah. My eyes felt strained afterwards. Though I did enjoy seeing those creatures up close. Reminded me of that documentary we watched ages ago. Honestly, it was a good day out overall though, wasn't it? Even with the transport chaos and the slightly blurry Impressionists. It was, yes. A good day out. Just need to promise myself I won't go on a flight simulator again. My stomach still hasn’t fully recovered! Fancy another biscuit? Go on then.

Right, so Christmas dinner. We need a plan, don't we? Otherwise, we’ll end up with turkey carnage all over again like last year. Remember that debacle? How could I forget? Carol was practically wrestling you for a bit of stuffing. Said it reminded her of Christmas with her Grandad. She does love her stuffing. Alright, so, turkey's a given. What about sides? I was thinking roast potatoes, obviously. Brussels sprouts – do we risk them again, or are we banishing them from the table for good? Brussels sprouts are essential! They’re a tradition. Although, I did find this recipe online – honey and balsamic glazed. Might actually make them palatable to some. Honey and balsamic? That's surprisingly adventurous for you. You usually stick to the classics. Well, I'm trying to broaden my horizons. Adapting to Chinese cuisine has certainly changed my perspective on food. Speaking of, we should probably incorporate something with a little more… flair. Good point. Maybe a stir-fry alongside the traditional stuff? A bit of sweet and sour to balance the richness? Exactly! And definitely spring rolls. Everyone loves spring rolls. We could even get them pre-made, save us some hassle. Solid plan. Right, so Turkey, roast potatoes, Brussels sprouts , and a Chinese stir-fry. What about dessert? Christmas pudding? Mandatory, surely? Though, I heard that Sarah and Mark are trying to do a sugar-free version this year. Can you imagine? The horror! I’d rather eat coal. Maybe we could just have a simple trifle instead? Less adventurous, but guaranteed to please. Trifle sounds lovely. Easy too. Speaking of Sarah and Mark, have you heard from them recently? They’re still stuck in Guangzhou, aren’t they? Yeah, still dealing with that visa nonsense. Apparently, the processing times are insane at the moment. They're hoping to be back for Christmas Eve, but I wouldn’t hold my breath. Shame. It won't be the same without them. Remember that time they brought that karaoke machine with them? Oh God, yes! We were belting out terrible renditions of 80s classics until three in the morning. My ears are still recovering. They were awful, but it was brilliant. Makes you think about getting one ourselves. Absolutely not. My eardrums have suffered enough. Right, let's just stick to a few beers then, shall we? It’s been good catching up. How are the students holding up?

Honestly, Twitter’s gone mad tonight. Some bloke’s arguing with a restaurant about their lobster thermidor. Saying it was “positively offensive.” Seriously? Lobster thermidor? What’s not to love? People are wild online, aren't they? It's just, seems like everyone's a critic now. I had someone leave a one-star review for the café this morning, just saying the coffee was "lukewarm." Lukewarm? Surely you can just send it back. You'd think, wouldn't you? But she just huffed and puffed and said, "It's the principle of the thing!" And then proceeded to take a selfie with the lukewarm coffee. The audacity. People are actively seeking out ways to complain. Especially online. It's almost a performance. It is! It's like, "Look at me, I’m a discerning customer!" It's just so tiring. I had a nightmare customer at uni the other day. Kept demanding I rewrite his entire essay. Like, I'm not a ghostwriter, mate. Oh god, the entitlement. What about you, have you had any baking disasters? Anything worthy of a scathing review? No, I'm worried about the new bakery opening up around the corner. The design is horrible, though. Like, aggressively beige. No personality whatsoever. All those exposed pipes… Exposed pipes are trendy. They're just… depressing. My place is all about colour and textures, you know? I want my customers to feel happy and excited when they walk in. Not like they’re in a dentist’s waiting room. Exactly! And the reviews they're getting already… mostly just about the décor. No one's mentioning the sourdough. Probably for good reason. Speaking of reviews, I’ve been meaning to ask, are you coming down to Margate next weekend? I’m finally opening the little shop I’ve been talking about forever. Margate! Oh my god, yes! I booked a train ages ago. Super excited. What kind of shop is it? It’s a little gift shop, mostly with stuff made by local artists. Prints, ceramics, little knitted things. It's tiny. I’m terrified it’s going to be a disaster. Don’t be! You've clearly put so much effort in. Plus, Margate is having a moment. The Turner Contemporary, the vintage shops… it's a vibe. Yeah, but what if it’s just… empty all day? Just me, sweeping up biscuit crumbs and wondering what I’ve done with my life?

Right, everyone, dinner's ready! Oisin, darling, come and sit down, please. Raspberries! Yes, you can have a few raspberries, sweetheart, but first, some vegetables. You need your greens, don’t you? Is there any chicken left? I’m starving. There’s plenty, darling. And broccoli, which I know you secretly love. Don’t tell anyone I love broccoli. It’s embarrassing. Exams are stressful enough. Well, eating well during exams is crucial. Fuel for the brain! Speaking of fuel, did you manage to go for a bike ride today, Liam? Briefly. Went around the park. Saw some bird eggs in a nest, which was kind of neat. Bird eggs! Lovely. I was thinking of getting some gerbils. Remember we used to have them when we were little, Sarah? Oh yes, Bartholomew and Penelope! They were absolute mischief-makers. Liam would probably be really good with them. Maybe. Depends if they chew my headphones. They might! Oisin, are you eating your carrots? They’re good for your eyes, you know. For seeing all the lovely things like…like ice cream! Ice cream! Chocolate! You are pushing it, Sarah! Don't fill her head with ice cream when she needs to be eating her peas. Just tempting her! A little bit. But honestly, she’s been so good about eating her vegetables lately. You’ve done a brilliant job, Chloe. She’s a good girl. Although, she does get a bit obsessed with raspberries. We’ve got them growing in the garden now. Trying to encourage her interest in gardening. Gardening’s pretty boring. It’s not! It’s amazing watching things grow. Remember how proud you were when you grew those sunflowers last summer? They were alright. Needed a lot of watering. I want chocolate ice cream! Not now, darling. We’ll have ice cream on the weekend. After your walk with Dad. Yes, you can go to the park with your dad this weekend. Can we go to the seaside after? Let's not get ahead of ourselves. Finish your dinner first. And Liam, put your phone away and enjoy the food. It's cooked with love. Absolutely. And Oisin, please try a bit of broccoli. It’s got little trees on it! Trees! Yummy! See? Told you you'd like it. Chloe, this roast chicken is lovely. Did you use rosemary again? Yes, I did. And a touch of lemon.

Right, so I was thinking, Thursday’s probably best for dinner, wasn’t it? It's the only day I’m not swamped at work. Thursday’s lovely. Does that work for your mum too? She was sounding a bit tired yesterday. Tired? I'm always tired, dear. Eighty-three doesn't come with a battery pack, you know. But Thursday’s fine. Anywhere that does a nice bit of fish and chips. Fish and chips it is then! I’ll book somewhere. There’s that new place in the market square, "Fry-Day's," have you heard of it? Fry-Day's? Can’t say I have. Is it alright? Apparently, it’s smashing. Proper thick-cut chips. I’ll ring them and see if they have a table for three, Thursday evening. Thick-cut chips, eh? Now you’re talking! These little ones they give you nowadays... like trying to eat matchsticks. Tell me about it! Speaking of which, I need to do a proper big shop tomorrow. Everything's gone in here. Oh, do you want me to come with you? I'm going anyway, and I need some bits for the cleaning cupboard. That would be amazing, actually. Two heads are better than one, especially when avoiding the impulse buy aisle. I swear they deliberately put the biscuits right at the end! Speaking of clever tricks, did you see Doreen Jenkins at the shops last week? She’d gotten herself a new pair of electric blue eyebrows. Honestly! Like a parrot. Oh, Doreen! She’s always experimenting. Though, I’ve been thinking about getting mine done too. They’re getting a bit sparse, aren’t they? They’re lovely, Sarah. You don't need anything done. But I've got a coupon for that salon on the High Street. They’re doing a deal on eyebrow tinting. Ooh, tinting! That’s probably a better idea than a full-on colour. Perhaps we could go next week? You look alright to me. All this messing about with your face… remember when we used to just draw them on with eyebrow pencil? That was simpler. Easier to clean off too, when you'd had a good cry. You’re a fountain of wisdom, Mum. Though I don't think eyebrow pencil will cut it these days, will it. No. And Margaret from down the road said she's finally getting her hair done.

Right, another coffee? You look like you need it. This weaning business is exhausting. Please! And you’re right, absolutely wiped. Honestly, pure chaos today. He threw mashed banana everywhere. Literally everywhere. Oh, they're good at that, aren't they? Little Picassos with purees. Did you manage to get any of it off the walls? Eventually. It took a good half an hour and a lot of wiping. I’m starting to feel like a human sponge. But he  did  eat some! A tiny bit, but a start is a start, right? Absolutely. Every bit counts. How’s the rice cereal gone down? Actually, surprisingly well. He seems to like the blandness, which is bizarre. Keeps wanting more, which is a little worrying, but… progress! Well done! So, what about next week, are you still managing to get round to seeing Sarah and Mark? They’re having us on Saturday. Said they’d clear out the garden for us. Honestly, I don’t know what they’re planning, it’s all a bit mysterious. They’re lovely. Their little girl will be so pleased to see him. He’s getting so big now, isn’t he? Practically crawling everywhere. He is! Being a toddler is exhausting. Anyway, I was thinking - are you free to come over on Wednesday? I need a bit of help, and a sanity break. Wednesday? Let me just check the diary … Yes, I’m free Wednesday! What did you have in mind? A couple of hours? That would be brilliant. Just to give me a chance to shower, maybe have a hot cup of tea without it getting cold, and catch up. You know, feel human again. Absolutely, I’d love to. And I've been thinking, are you still planning on trying those sign language classes? Yes! I’m signed up for the beginners one at the community centre on Thursday evenings. I'm a bit nervous, to be honest. I’m hopeless at anything practical. Nonsense! You’re a brilliant teacher, you’ll pick it up in no time. Imagine being able to communicate with him before he can even talk! It’ll be lovely. That's the idea, isn’t it? I've read it's really useful for reducing frustration, especially with babies. It is. My friend’s little boy used to throw huge tantrums until she started with him. Made a world of difference.

Honestly, I can’t believe how flat it is here. I keep waiting for a hill to appear. Well, you know Norfolk. It's famously…level. We’re practically walking on a giant pancake. I know, I know. I’m just used to a bit more…variation. All those hills in Norwich, even though they’re minimal, you still feel like you’re getting somewhere. It’s a different kind of landscape, isn't it? More about the big sky and the wide-open fields. Look, sheep! Oh, yes! They’re adorable. It’s nice to see them just…being sheep, you know? Not stressed or anything. Exactly. Peaceful. What did you think of that little village we passed through – Little Walsingham? Absolutely charming. Such a beautiful little church. And the tea room looked lovely. We should pop in there next time. Definitely. They probably do a wicked scone. I’m starved. Should we head back towards the car then? The light’s starting to change. Yes, good idea. It is getting a bit chilly. Do you think the students appreciate this kind of scenery? When we take them out on field trips, I mean. Some do. Others just want to know where the nearest coffee shop is. It’s tough, isn’t it? Trying to get them to engage with…the landscape. It is. I try to relate it to something they understand – a poem, a painting, a historical event. Something to make them see it in a different light. You're good at that. You always find a way to connect with them. It’s one of the things I admire about you. Oh, stop it. You’re just saying that. No, I’m not. Honestly. It's remarkable how you can make ancient field systems and drainage ditches… interesting. They’re not  that  interesting! But they  are  important. Part of a bigger picture. Exactly. And you help people see that bigger picture. Now, are we going to admire those cows, or are we going to head for scones? Scones, definitely scones. Let’s go. It's good to get out here, isn't it? It really is. A much needed break. I feel significantly less stressed already. Me too. Sometimes you just need a bit of wide-open space. And a lack of hills. It’s very restorative. Absolutely. Restoration via Norfolk flatness. Coming right up. Okay. Enjoy those cows.

Honestly, I’m still buzzing from seeing Oppenheimer. Didn’t realise it was going to be quite  that  intense. Three hours felt like three minutes, though. Yeah, it was pretty good, wasn't it? A bit long, maybe, but definitely worth seeing on the big screen. Did you catch the bit with… you know, the… The Trinity test? Yeah! Absolutely blew me away. All the visuals, the sound… incredible. I kept thinking about all those layered meanings too, you know? The moral implications. Definitely. It’s got you thinking about it days later, hasn’t it? Speaking of films, did you ever see that indie thing, 'Aftersun'? Oh yeah! Loved it. So heartbreaking. Proper emotional rollercoaster. It was. Liam – Sarah's new boyfriend – he recommended it. He's really getting into film analysis, which is, you know,  Liam . Yeah, that sounds like him. What's he doing now then? Still at that accountancy firm? Nah, he left a few months ago. He's working for that sustainability consultancy now, the one specialising in renewable energy. Apparently, it’s really interesting stuff. Loads of modelling and risk assessment. Wow, seriously? That’s brilliant for him. Sounds way more his thing than spreadsheets. I hope he’s happy. He seems to be. Says it’s properly challenging, and he gets to actually  see  the impact of his work. Good on him. Speaking of impact… did you see those cyclists causing chaos on the A1 this morning? Delayed me getting here by about twenty minutes! Seriously? What were they playing at? People are trying to get to work! I know! They were three or four of them, just weaving in and out of traffic, completely ignoring the speed limit. Honestly, it was like something out of a comedy sketch. They risk everything, don’t they? And they expect everyone else to watch out for them. It’s insane! I nearly had to brake suddenly. It's not a race track, you know. People need to use their common sense. Absolutely. It's just so frustrating. Sometimes I just want to grab them and say... I know! Let’s just forget about the cyclists and Oppenheimer for a bit. Fancy a coffee? I’m starving. Definitely. Lead the way. Hopefully, this fulfilled the prompt's requirements. Let me know if you'd like any modifications! I've tried to show their backgrounds through the language and topics of conversation.

This light is just incredible, isn’t it? Look at how it’s hitting those poppies. Like something out of a Turner painting. It is stunning. Though, I’m having to squint a bit. I should've brought my sunglasses. Nice to get out of the city, though. Needed a proper dose of countryside. Definitely. And it’s so quiet. You can almost hear the… well, not the silence exactly, but the lack of traffic noise is a revelation. It is. Reminds me of being a kid. Though even then it wasn’t quite this quiet, was it? There was always some tractor buzzing about. Probably. I’m starting to think about the economics of all this, actually. All these fields, mostly arable, right? What are the cash crops around here these days? Mostly rapeseed, I think. Definitely seeing a lot of yellow. And some barley, probably going into brewing. Norfolk's got a lot of breweries. Less wheat these days, I reckon. Prices are just… unpredictable. It's fascinating, isn't it, how much of our lives are dictated by these global commodity prices? It’s what my research is vaguely pointing towards, you know, the ripple effects of international trade on local communities. Sounds complicated. Though, I can appreciate the point. Global markets are the invisible hand guiding the farmer's decisions. Like with the football – international transfers completely distort the domestic league. Exactly! The same principles apply. Speaking of football, have you heard anything about that striker, Alvarez? Brighton seem to have got a steal. I have! Apparently, he’s got a nose for goal. My brother's going on about him incessantly. Keeps saying he's the next Haaland. Let’s hope he's not. We’ll be laughing if he starts playing for Man City. True. So, your research… are you still focusing on the impact on rural dialects? In part, yes. It’s interesting how economic shifts correlate with language attrition. Places that become highly reliant on agriculture, particularly monoculture, tend to… well, flatten out linguistically. Less diversity. It makes sense. Less need for specialized terminology, less cultural exchange. Precisely. It's a shame, really. So much richness lost. I was reading an article this morning about Basque, actually. Its isolation has maintained its unique linguistic structure for millennia. Basque! Incredible, isn’t it? Completely unrelated to anything else on the continent. Makes you wonder about the layers of history hidden in languages.

Right so, just to clarify, you’re picking me up from the station at like, half past four then? And we’re heading straight to your mam’s? Yep, half past four sharp. Straight to her's, she's making that proper Sunday dinner, you know, the one you always rave about. Aye, I know, I’ve been talking about it for weeks! You’re a saint for doing all this driving. Are you bothered about the fuel prices? Nah, not really. Less than bothered. Besides, it’s good to get out of London, bit of Yorkshire air in my lungs. Besides, I need something to do tonight - I’m trying not to think about the Arsenal game tomorrow. Oh, poor love. Don't tell me you're getting nervous again. A bit, yeah. They need to pull something special out of the bag, they do. You reckon they’ll win? Honestly? It's hard to say. They’ve been a bit patchy lately, haven't they? I'm hoping for a good game regardless, though. Not a thrashing. Want to catch some tennis while we're up North this weekend? There’s that tournament in Leeds. Ooh, tennis, good shout. We might, definitely might. But first, the Angel of the North. Need a photo, don't we? For the 'gram. Absolutely! It’s a must. It's still amazing, isn't it? Even after all these years. I still get a bit choked up every time I see it. I know, right? Massive piece of art. Speaking of things that are massive… have you seen the size of the flats your cousin’s got in Sheffield? Don’t even. It's ridiculous. He’s got a penthouse for three people! He’s never has anyone round. Seriously. How does he even afford it? And the parking! Apparently, he paid like, fifteen thousand for a parking space. Fifteen thousand! You're having a laugh! That's insane. We'll be circling the block for ages when we get to your mam’s, won’t we? Probably. She lives on a really tight street. You'll need to be patient. Although, I might have a trick up my sleeve. I know a bloke who's got his own little space near her, I could ask him. Seriously? You’re a lifesaver! That’d be brilliant. Fewer stress levels for me, then. No worries.

Honestly, have you seen what's going on with that trial? The one with the presenter, you know? It’s utterly ridiculous! Accusations flying left, right and centre. I can barely keep up. Oh, the telly one? No, I haven't really been watching much. Been a bit busy, you know. Though my mum, Margaret, she’s glued to it. Says it's better than Coronation Street! Corrie used to be something else, you know. Proper stories. Not this…this nonsense. Exactly! It’s all manufactured drama. Though, I do find the legal bits fascinating, in a morbid sort of way. It’s interesting to see the principles at play, even if it’s surrounded by absolute mayhem. Anyway, speaking of watching things, have you seen all the geese lately? There's a huge flock down by the river. Must be hundreds, easily. Oh yes! I noticed that just the other day. They’re already starting to gather, aren’t they? Getting ready for migration. Aye, they’re smart birds, geese. Know when to move on. Used to see them passing through Peterborough every year when I were a girl. Big V-shape in the sky, it was a sight to see. They’re so noisy though, aren’t they? Honking and squawking all the time. My neighbour complained because they were waking her up early every morning. Well, they are preparing! It’s a big journey for them. I read somewhere that some of them fly thousands of miles. It's amazing to think. All that way, just to find someplace warm. Keeps you humble, doesn’t it? Puts your troubles into perspective. Like this trial, eh? Absolutely. Speaking of nature, I put up a bird feeder in the garden this week. Hoping to attract some robins. Oh, that's lovely! I like the little finches. They’re so quick and cheeky. You get a lot of pigeons too, mind. Not the prettiest birds, but they’re hardy. They'll eat anything. I know! And they're fearless. I swear they have no sense of danger. The other day, one actually landed on the window ledge, stared straight at me, and then pecked at the glass. Cheeky! You should get a camera and film them. Put it on Facebook. That’s not a bad idea actually! I might just do that. It’s a bit of light entertainment after watching all that dreadful news.

This quiche is absolutely delicious, seriously. Thank you so much, Chloe. Oh, you’re so welcome, Maisie! Glad you like it. It's just something I whipped up. Needed to use up some eggs. Little one's been on a chicken nugget phase this week, you know. I completely get that. Leo’s obsessed with anything beige and fried at the moment. A battle every single mealtime. How's Elsie adjusting to nursery? Honestly? It's been a rollercoaster. Some days she's a little ray of sunshine, absolutely loving it, making friends… Yesterday she clung to my legs like a limpet for a full half hour. The poor little thing just looked heartbroken. Oh, sweetheart. That’s tough to see, isn't it? Remember when Leo did that? Practically had to peel him off the wall. Did they say what was upsetting her? Not really, just "a bit clingy." You know how they are. I'm trying not to worry too much. I think she just misses me, obviously. It's such a big change for her. Absolutely. It's a huge one for you too, though, isn’t it? Having that separation. How are you managing with the workload now you're back full-time? Trying! It’s busy, that’s for sure. Being a teacher and a mum...it’s a special kind of exhaustion. What about you? Still enjoying teaching French? Yes, mostly! The Year 10s are a bit of a handful this year, though. All angling for top marks and getting stressed about it. I had two nearly come to blows over a grammatical error last week. Absolute madness. Oh, goodness! Teenagers, eh? They’re a force to be reckoned with. I had a parent email me last week complaining that I hadn't marked their child's homework quickly enough. Seriously! You’re kidding! The entitlement! People just don’t realise the amount of work involved. Exactly! Anyway, so I have an interview next week… Oh, fantastic! Which school? St. Michael's. You know, the one just outside Sutton Coldfield? Heard good things about them. Headteacher seems lovely from what I’ve seen online. Oh! I know St. Michael's. It's got a good reputation. What role are you interviewing for? Head of Year 7. Massive responsibility, but if I got it… That would be incredible, Chloe! You’d be brilliant. You’ve always had a real knack with the younger ones.

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a little bit about the future. Like, properly. About what, specifically? The state of the world? Because that's fair enough, it's a bit terrifying at the moment. It's not  just  that, though. It’s, like… everything. Work, relationships, where I’ll be living in five years, whether I'll ever own a house… the whole shebang. Right, that’s a lot to unpack. You’re feeling a bit overwhelmed, I get it. Do you feel like your job is part of that? You seem pretty settled there. I  am  settled, I suppose. The work itself is fine, actually pretty interesting. It's just... Permanent contracts are becoming rarer and rarer, aren't they? And the company is always restructuring. You never really know if your role will exist a year down the line. Yeah, that's a legitimate worry. My admin job is pretty safe, I think, but it doesn't exactly set my soul on fire, you know? It's a means to an end. Exactly! It pays the bills. But is that all there is? Like, I’d love to do something that feels more… purposeful, I guess. Something that actually makes a difference. Have you looked into volunteering or anything like that? Something outside of work. I’ve thought about it. Loads of charities need help with admin and events, but I can barely find time to do my laundry, let alone volunteer! Fair point. What about relationships? Is Leo still driving you insane? Don’t even get me started. He's brilliant most of the time, but he’s got this… this unwavering optimism about everything. Like, he genuinely believes we'll be able to buy a three-bedroom house with a garden in Cambridge within the next two years. Bless him. Cambridge property prices are insane. Exactly! I keep trying to explain the reality of things – mortgages, deposits, the sheer competition – but he just smiles and says, "Positive thinking, darling!". It’s exhausting. You need to gently remind him that positive thinking doesn't magically manifest a house. Maybe suggest looking at slightly more realistic locations? I’ve tried. He’s got his heart set on Cambridge. It's sentimental to him, apparently. His nan lived there. Right, that makes sense. Family history is a powerful thing. But honestly, you need to look out for yourself, don't you?

Honestly, I can’t believe Liam’s still going on about Chloe. Like, it's been three weeks since his birthday! Get over it, yeah? Tell him! He's moaning about it to everyone. Even my uncle Derek who has absolutely no idea who Chloe is. Seriously? Your uncle Derek? He probably thinks Chloe is a type of French cheese. Exactly! I was trying to tell him about this lad at uni, Daniel, but all he could talk about was Chloe’s Instagram story from his birthday party. It's driving me mad! Daniel, eh? What's he like? You've barely mentioned him. He's alright. Funny, actually. Real proper laugh. And he’s into the same music as me. Which is a massive win. Sounds promising! Better than moping about a girl who clearly isn’t that bothered. Exactly! I reckon he's just fishing for compliments, that’s all. 'Oh, I'm still sad about Chloe, feel sorry for me.' Like, no one has time for that. Proper cringe. Remember when Ben did that? Took ages to get over Sarah. Oh god, don’t remind me. We had to listen to a month of heartbroken poetry and dramatic playlists. Ugh, the worst. I had a similar experience with Tom - kept going on about Olivia. It was exhausting. I almost didn't go to that concert with him! See, boys are weird, aren't they? I saw Mark with Bethany last night, and she was practically glued to his arm. And he was just… there. Like he couldn’t care less. Typical. It’s always the ones who aren't interested that girls pine for. It's infuriating! I mean, I’m happy for Amelia and Tom, honestly, but sometimes I get a bit jealous. They seem so… settled. You know? Settled? We're nineteen! Settled is not even in our vocabulary. We're supposed to be messy and making mistakes! Exactly! Living our best lives and not worrying about rings and mortgages. I know, I know. It's just... seeing them all couple-y makes me wonder if I’m missing out. Don't be daft. You've got us. And honestly, watching Liam fall apart over Chloe makes me feel way less pressured to find ‘the one.’ Plus, look at this sunshine! Who needs a boyfriend when you've got a baguette and a beautiful view? You’re right.

This chicken is lovely, isn’t it? Really tender. Yeah, it's good. Can I have some more peas? Of course, love. Plenty of everything. So, Jamie, how was hockey practice today? It was alright. Bit boring though. We were just doing drills. Drills, eh? Sounds a bit tedious after playing a proper match. Did you score any goals? Nah. I’m still rubbish at shooting. You’ll get there. Practice makes perfect, right? Remember when I used to try and teach you Korean? Oh, don’t start! I still can't remember "thank you." It’s “Kamsahamnida”! Easy to remember. You two are hopeless. Anyway, did you hear back from Mrs. Davies about that art exhibition you wanted to go to, Finn? Not yet. I messaged her yesterday, but nothing. I really want to go – Liam and Chloe are going, and it's got loads of Banksy stuff. Banksy's cool. Is he still doing stuff? Oh yeah, all the time. He's a bit of a legend. Though he’s probably causing chaos somewhere right now! Chaos is his brand. Thinking about it, we should actually go to London sometime soon. It's been ages. I’m in. We could tie it in with seeing that show about the space race, remember? Sarah mentioned it. That sounds good. And maybe a proper curry. We haven’t had a good curry in ages. Can we go to that place in Leicester Square? The one with the robot waiters? The one that always messes up your order? Perhaps we should try somewhere new. Let's just plan it all properly then. Once the mad rush of work calms down. I’ve got loads of freelance bits coming in this month, which is good, but it's full-on. I need some new hockey boots soon. These ones are falling apart. We’ll sort that out. No problem. Maybe after the half term? What's been going on with you at school, Finn? Apart from not scoring in hockey. Biology is really hard. Mr. Mitchell is explaining all this stuff about DNA, and I just can't get my head around it. DNA is tricky. Think of it like a complicated recipe. Are you doing alright in Maths? Maths is okay. It's Biology I’m struggling with. Maybe we can get a tutor for you? There are some decent ones online.

Wow, look at those trees! They’re absolutely enormous. I can’t even see the top. Incredible, right? It’s like being in a different world. It’s so green and… quiet. Surprisingly quiet for somewhere so vast. It is. You know, I was reading about how these Redwoods can live for, like, hundreds of years. It’s mind-blowing to think about all the history they’ve witnessed. Centuries! Imagine being around for that long. I wonder what they’d tell you if they could talk. Probably just complain about the tourists, I reckon. Probably. Do you remember Claire telling us about that time she tried to hike Yosemite? Oh my gosh, yes! She totally underestimated it, didn’t she? Went without water and got completely lost. Poor thing. I feel terrible for her now that I know how intense it can be. She was so dramatic about it too. Said she was going to sue the park rangers! Classic Claire. Remember when she tried to convince us she could speak fluent Italian after a week in Rome? Oh, don’t remind me! "Ciao! Sono... confused!" That was her opening gambit. It was awful! But you have to admire her confidence, even if completely misplaced. Honestly, though, it’s amazing she hasn’t gotten into more ridiculous scrapes. She’s always been one for a bit of chaos. Exactly! Remember that wedding in Scotland? The one where she accidentally set off the smoke alarm in the hotel room with the hairdryer? Oh god, yes! The entire floor had to be evacuated! She swore it was the fault of the ventilation system. And the look on the hotel manager’s face... priceless. He clearly knew she was the culprit. He suspected something anyway, I wouldn't put it past her. You know, my sister keeps asking when she's going to settle down. Oh really? Is she getting the pressure from your family? Tons of it. Aunty Brenda keeps suggesting eligible bachelors from her local bowling club. Like that’s the pinnacle of romantic achievement! Oh, bless her. Claire would probably find a way to make it wonderfully disastrous, wouldn’t she? Imagine her bowling with a bunch of retired men. Don’t even. I can just picture the chaos. Honestly, I just hope she’s happy. That’s all that really matters, isn't it? Absolutely. And clearly, she’s having a brilliant time living her life on her own terms, even if it does involve occasional smoke alarms and mispronounced Italian phrases.

These Chicken Kievs are actually not bad, are they? A lot better than that dodgy batch last week. They're alright, Dad. Bit greasy though. Everything's a bit greasy to you, darling. You'd complain if you were swimming in olive oil. I'm not! Now, now, no backchat. Just enjoying dinner. Did you catch any of the rugby earlier? Nah, I was on my Xbox. Robbie was on too. Robbie, always on that Xbox. You'll turn square-eyed, you will. Did you see anything of the score though? Ireland won, obviously. "Obviously," he says. Like it was a foregone conclusion. They had to fight for it, you know. That scrum was something else. I only saw the bit where Mum got a headache. She was muttering about something going wrong with the Wi-Fi. The Wi-Fi's always going wrong. I swear, it’s possessed. I need to get Dropbox and Flickr properly synced up, haven’t had a chance to sort it all out though. All these photos of Granny… Are we going to visit Granny next week then? We're planning to. Your mum's got that… what’s it called? That parenting course on Tuesday? It's a nurture and support thing. Very helpful. Trying to be a good, proactive mum, you know? It sounds boring. It's important. And someone has to do it, obviously. Well, if we go next week, we'll need to sort out a proper time. Should we aim for Saturday? Can I bring Wallies? Wallies? That… that aggressively enthusiastic ginger hamster? He likes Granny. I’m not sure Granny appreciates hamsters, love. Especially ones that… well. He doesn’t bite! He just… nibbles. Alright, alright. Let's not start a debate about rodent visits. We’ll discuss it. So, Saturday for Granny then? Sounds good. Though I’m getting a bit peckish again. Are there any more of those biscuits? They're in the tin. Don't eat them all before we finish our Kievs. Hey! There was a hedgehog in the garden this morning. I saw it! You did? Really? Yeah! It was rooting around under the hedge. Oh, how lovely. Ireland's going wild now, isn’t it? Suddenly everything’s a wildlife documentary. Don't be sarcastic. A hedgehog is a good sign. Means the garden’s got a decent ecosystem. Should I photograph it and put it on Flickr?

Right, so I think I’ve got most of the veg for this soup. Just need some carrots. Do you want me to pop out? Nah, I can grab them on the way back from work tomorrow. I’m getting a bit behind on my usual market shop too, actually. Oh, good point. You should. I saw Mrs. Davies from number 12 at the market yesterday. She’s selling her home-made buckwheat bread again. Did you want a loaf? Really? Buckwheat bread! That’s brilliant. Yes, definitely. I absolutely love that stuff. It's so much better than shop-bought. Get a couple, will you? I’ll bring it in from work tomorrow, if you prefer. No, no, I'll get them. Less for you to carry. Speaking of carrying, did you sort out the leaving do for Mark? Almost. I’ve booked the pub – The Red Lion. They’ve got that nice little back room we can use. Just need to send out the invites. Sheila from HR said she'd help me get a list of everyone who works with him. So, Friday week, seven o’clock? Sounds perfect. Should we do a collection? He’s already mentioned he’s getting a little something for his wife, Sarah, and they’re going away. Good idea. I’ll put a little notice on the office noticeboard. Something discreet. Right. While we're at it, can you remind Sheila to book the raffle? Mark loves a raffle. Will do. What are you thinking for supper tonight? I’m starving. I was thinking lentil soup. Simple, hearty, and uses up a lot of what's in the fridge. Then maybe some crusty bread to go with it. Sounds lovely. You’ve been on a vintage cups and saucers spree again, haven’t you? I noticed a pile of boxes in the living room earlier. You noticed, did you? I got a few more from eBay last night. A really beautiful set of Royal Albert - the 'Old Country Roses'. They arrived this morning. Royal Albert? Fancy! How much did those set you back? Not too bad, actually. A steal, really. Only £25 for the set of six. You have to be quick on eBay to get the bargains. True. Though you do end up with a lot of things you don’t necessarily need. But they make me happy! And they’re so pretty.

So, you’re  really  sure about this, Uncle Dave? About routing the payments through Cyprus? It sounds... complicated. And risky. Complicated, yes. Risky? Less so than you think, love. It's all about layers, see? Nobody looks twice at a small business transferring funds between EU countries. Keeps things clean, keeps things flowing. But isn’t that… skirting the edge a bit, Dave? I mean, the Inland Revenue? What if they start asking questions? My business is already under enough scrutiny as it is. The Inland Revenue don’t ask questions, love, they just assume everything’s above board. As long as the paperwork is right, as long as the transactions look legitimate… it’s fine. It's about structuring it, see? Like a good building. Strong foundations. You’re talking about money laundering, aren’t you? Don’t use such harsh words, lad. Let's call it... strategic asset management. Helping people manage their resources effectively. Effectively? By hiding them from the government? That sounds a bit dodgy, even for you, Uncle Dave. Dodgy is a strong word, lass. It’s… proactive. And frankly, it’s how a lot of businesses operate these days. You wouldn’t believe the fines some people are racking up in VAT alone. Speaking of fines, how are Liam's driving lessons going? Still getting tickets? Loads. Last week he got a parking fine  and  a speeding ticket. All in the same day. Honestly? He's hopeless behind the wheel. Maybe he should stick to playing Xbox. He needs to learn, though. Running a business requires a certain… independence. Can’t be relying on others to drive you around. Though, honestly, some of my clients could learn a thing or two about independence. Always relying on me to sort their problems out. You're a lifesaver to some, aren't you? You've got a real knack for… untangling things. Though, sometimes I worry about you. All this responsibility. It can’t be easy. It has its moments. Remember that time I had to arrange for those shipments of…  goods … to be redirected through Amsterdam? That was a tricky one. Customs were on high alert. Had to use a contact who owed me a favour. A very big favour. What kind of goods, Uncle Dave? Please don’t tell me… Never you mind, love. Let’s just say it involved a lot of very expensive leather jackets.

Right, so the rain's finally stopped, eh? Didn’t think it’d ever shift. Absolutely lashed down this morning. It did indeed. Drove like a nightmare getting over from Sutton. Visibility was down to nowt. Thought I was going to end up in a ditch! Luckily you didn't, Dad! Glad you made it. So, coffee’s all ready. Anyone want a top-up? Please! I need it after that shift. Absolute madness at the store today. Half the town seemed to want to buy Christmas decorations in October. Honestly, some people. At least you’re prepared though, aren't you, Liv? Trying to be! It’s just…the pressure to hit targets is relentless, you know? Anyway, what's everyone been up to? Sarah, how’s the work going? It's alright, you know. Busy, as always. Got that grant proposal to finish by the end of the week. Hoping it’ll come through. Fingers crossed for you! Anything exciting planned for when you get it? Just a little breather, to be honest. Maybe a spa day. Desperately need one. And you, Chloe? Still loving being a primary school teacher? Absolutely! The kids are brilliant. Little Thomas finally managed to spell ‘cat’ correctly today. I nearly cried with joy! See, that's what it’s all about. Making a difference. Good on you, love. Aw, that's lovely! I miss kids sometimes, having to deal with demanding customers all day. It’s a different kind of challenge. Speaking of challenges, has anyone heard anything about that sign language class I was looking at? Yeah, the community centre one. It’s booked solid, apparently. Loads of interest. I looked into it too, Mum. There’s another one at the library, starting next month. Smaller group, seems less intense. I can send you the details. Oh, that would be brilliant, love! I’d really like to learn a bit. It could be useful, you never know. You'd be amazing! You’re always picking up new things. We’re all very proud of you, love. Moving on to more pressing matters… Any news on the baby front? Little Leo’s been surprisingly good this week! Slept through the night on Monday! Oh, fantastic! Nearly a miracle, isn't it? We  have  to see him soon! It’s been ages. How's your partner doing, Chloe? He’s exhausted but happy, mostly.

Honestly, another day, another mountain of linguistic data. I feel like I’m drowning in corpora. Tell me about it! My manuscript pile is threatening to topple over. I swear, if one more author submits a piece riddled with passive voice… You're preaching to the choir. I’ve spent half my morning arguing with an author about the Oxford comma. It's a hill I will die on. Oxford comma is  essential . Seriously. I’m Swedish-Chilean, so I’ve seen things. Trust me, linguistic ambiguity is the enemy. Absolutely! It's just the principles of clarity and precision… it’s my bread and butter, you know? But sometimes you wish people just… communicated. Clearly. Easy for you to say, you're the Language Research Coordinator. You  get  to dissect the nuances. We’re stuck fixing the aftermath! Still, it's fascinating, isn’t it? How language evolves, shifts, adopts. I was reading this article about Malaysian English… the influences are incredible. Oh, yes! The creolisation aspect is particularly interesting. It’s a living, breathing thing, always adapting. I’ve been looking into loanwords from Hokkien... fascinating how they've integrated and adapted into colloquial speech. My grandma in Sweden used to say that language is like a river. Always flowing, always changing course. She’d tell these wonderful folk tales where words held literal magic. Sounds lovely. I’m surrounded by dry legal contracts. My life lacks magic. Speaking of things that change... has anyone else noticed the new intern, Leo? He seems a bit lost. Leo? Ah, yes, the History grad. I did a quick onboarding session with him. He's bright, just a bit… overwhelmed. He keeps staring at the photocopier. Like it's some kind of alien device. Poor thing. We all felt that way at the start. Remember when I tried to staple a manuscript backwards? Don't remind me. I thought I was going to have to explain the entire concept of a stapler to you! We should probably have a proper team lunch sometime, to let his settle in. Something outside of the Printing House. I'm in! Anything but another sandwich from the café. My tastebuds are staging a revolt. Definitely! Maybe somewhere with a bit of atmosphere, somewhere we don’t have to whisper about Oxford commas. Sounds amazing. I know this little Italian place just off Mill Road... their pasta is divine.

Right, so Gumtree's been a bit dead for the marshals, innit? No one's biting. Aye, it's a weird one. I posted like, five times yesterday. Just changed the wording a bit each time. Still nothing. Proper quiet. Maybe they think it’s a con. "Volunteer to stand in the rain for free, waving flags for a load of lads going to Mongolia." Doesn't exactly scream ‘trustworthy opportunity’ does it? True, true. Maybe we need to put more emphasis on the charity tie-in. Throw in a picture of the little Mongolian kids we're helping, pull at the heartstrings a bit. Yeah, good shout. I’ll grab some of those photos from the website. Speaking of which, did you sort the visa application stuff? Almost. Got the forms filled out, but I keep getting tripped up on the bloody passport photos. What’s wrong with 'em? They're rubbish, mate. Honestly. I went to that new photo booth in town – the one with the fancy lighting – and it just ate my face. Looked like a right alien. You’d be hard to recognise. Tell me about it! So I'm thinking of just going to Boots and getting the standard headshot. Less chance of looking like an ET. Yeah, Boots is probably safer. And make sure you get it printed on the right paper – that shiny photo paper, yeah? Otherwise, it won't scan. Right. Shiny paper. Got it. What about donations? Are they trickling in? Slow. Really slow. We need a proper push. I was thinking maybe a bake sale outside Greggs? Get some of my mum's lemon drizzle – proper good stuff. Greggs might kick us out, though. Remember what happened with Liam and the hot dog stand? Don't remind me. Right. Plan B. We hit up the local pubs. Put a collection tin on the bar, rattle a few buckets. I’ll make some little signs. "Mongolia or Bust! Help us help them!" Something like that. Good! Get the banter going. And I’ll message my nan – she always donates to something. She probably thinks we’re saving orphaned penguins or something. Probably. Okay, so photo booth sorted, visa stuff progressing, donations needing a boost… Anything else pressing? Oh yeah! Mine's expired. Passport. I forgot to check. No way! Yeah. Renewed it online, but it'll take ages to come. Are we actually going to  get  to Mongolia?

So, what did you think of the party on Saturday then, love? Did you have a good time? Aye, it were alright. A bit loud, mind. A bit loud? Your grandad wasn't exactly quiet either, was he? He was telling that story about the sheep again, wasn't he? Yeah, the one where he chased it with a rake for three miles. I’ve heard it about a million times. He does love that story. Auntie Carol kept winding him up, didn't she? Asking him if he ever caught it. She did. And Uncle Derek was trying to show everyone his magic tricks. Oh, Derek and his magic! Those weren't very impressive, were they? He needs some new routines. Did you have a chat with your cousin, Liam? Just a bit. He was mostly talking about his band. Said they’ve got a gig on Friday. Oh, really? Where are they playing? At the pub in York. The one near the station. Right. I'll have to try and pop in and see them sometime. Were there enough sandwiches? I tried to make sure there was plenty. Aye, loads. Proper stuffed myself, I did. Grandma’s sausage rolls are always the best, though, aren't they? They are, aren’t they? She’s got a knack for those. Did you help her with them at all? Nah, I was busy trying to escape from Auntie Susan’s endless questions about university applications. Oh, Susan. She means well, doesn’t she? Just wants you to be successful. She’s been thinking about your future ever since you were knee-high to a grasshopper. Tell me about it. I told her I was still looking at colleges. Didn't want to commit to anything yet. That's sensible. Don't rush into anything. It’s your life, love. Did you manage to have a dance with your mum? Yeah, a couple. It were alright. Good. She does love a good dance. She seemed happy with how things were going, didn’t she? It means a lot to her, you celebrating your grandad and grandma’s anniversary. Aye, she seemed alright. She kept saying it was a good turnout. It was, wasn't it? Family coming from all over. Nearly fifty of us. Your grandad and grandma were chuffed to bits, I reckon. It was a lovely party, all things considered.

Dad, have you got any pens? I’ve run out. Let me see… yeah, found a couple in the glove box. Here you go, love. Thanks. Could you check I’ve got my water bottle too? It's roasting in here already. Yep, seems alright. You remember to drink plenty, especially when we’re down in Cornwall. It’s gonna be even hotter. I know, right? I'm already dreaming of the beach. Do you think we’ll actually get any time to relax or will it just be unpacking and cleaning? We’ll make time, don't worry. I’m trying to be organised this time, unlike last year. Remember all that chaos with the washing machine?  Laughs  Oh god, yes! How did a washing machine almost derail our entire holiday to the Lake District? Don't ask! Anyway, I’ve already checked reviews on that little bistro in St Ives. They do a really good seafood platter. Ooh, that sounds amazing. Can we get some liquorice allsorts for the journey though? I’m craving something sweet. You know, like medicine… but tasty.  Chuckles  You’re a strange one. Alright, liquorice it is. We could stop at Holland and Barrett. They’ve got loads, and those freeze-dried raspberries are pretty good too. Yeah! Maybe we can pick up a few things for Mum too. She was saying she’s running low on her IBS stuff. Right. Speaking of which, I need to remind myself to book that appointment for my knee. It’s been playing up something fierce lately. Are you still thinking about moving? You mention it all the time. It's tempting. A little cottage in the countryside, maybe near Devon. Bit smaller than this place. Less to clean, you know? Less space for all your old DVDs though! Remember Jurassic Park? We used to watch that on repeat. I do! Good times. Actually, I saw a documentary the other day about those Egyptian pyramids. Incredible how they built them without all this modern technology. Makes you wonder what they knew. I know! And look at the Northern Lights. It must be so amazing to see them in Norway. They’re practically magical. Absolutely. I’ve always wanted to go. Have you been thinking about uni applications? A bit. I’m thinking languages, maybe. Hungarian sounds fascinating. Such a tricky language to learn though. It is.

Right, so you’re absolutely sure this is the best way to handle it, David? It feels a bit… hasty. Hasty? No, I think it's the most sensible, Eleanor. We've been over this a dozen times. The solicitor said engaging a mediator now, before things escalate, is the best course of action. Less stressful for everyone involved. Stressful or not, David, ensuring ANON’s wishes are paramount. You're not rushing this because it’s convenient for you, are you? Mother, I’m not. Of course, ANON’s wishes are the priority. I’m simply trying to be practical. Prolonging this will only make things more difficult. Practical's good, lad. Can't be moping around worrying about it. Best to just get the job done proper, eh? Like fitting a good frame around a picture. Keeps things steady. David's right in principle, Gwyn. But I'm concerned about the emotional toll this will take on… well, everyone. Especially ANON. She's been so fragile lately. That's precisely why mediation is crucial, Eleanor. A neutral party can help facilitate a calmer conversation, prevent accusations… Conversation? David, these are complex matters. Money, property, long-standing friendships… It wouldn't be a simple chat over the garden fence. Aye, it'll be a right tangle of threads, that'll be. Like trying to untie a fisherman’s knot blindfolded. Exactly! And what if the mediator can’t help? What if it just… stirs things up? We’ll cross that bridge when we come to it, Eleanor. We have to at least  try  a peaceful resolution. The alternative – a drawn-out court battle – would be devastating. Though a solicitor's fees would hardly be devastating to some, I imagine. Look, I've booked the initial consultation for next week. It’s just a preliminary meeting to assess whether mediation is viable. We can cancel if it doesn’t feel right. Alright. A preliminary meeting. But if it's not working, we pull out immediately. Promise? Promise. Mother? Just make sure ANON is comfortable with the whole process. That's all I ask. Don't let her be bullied into anything. Aye, look after the lass. She’s a good sort. Wouldn't want to see her gettin’ upset over all this. Best thing is to just keep things simple and fair, innit? Like a well-made dovetail joint. Solid and dependable.

Right, operation Mother’s Day is a go. Any initial thoughts, team? Can we have cake? A really, really big cake! And sprinkles! Lots and lots of sprinkles! Absolutely, both of you. Cake and sprinkles, noted. But we need a plan. Grandma’s coming over, right? Yep! She likes flowers. And cuddles! She likes big cuddles! Of course, cuddles are essential. Okay, so flowers and cuddles are on the list. I was thinking we could do something a bit different this year. Instead of just cards and presents… What else? I was thinking, weather permitting, we could go to Forest School? Remember how much Grandma liked it last time? With the sticks! And the mud! And the… bugs! Yes, all of that. We could build her a little fairy house, maybe? Or collect some stones and paint them. Something creative. Like painting rocks? I can paint a flower! A really, really good one! I can paint a monster! A grumpy monster! Wonderful! We'll have a variety of art then. Now, Grandma also mentioned she doesn't really like roses. Apparently, they remind her of… … “a load of hot air” apparently! Hot air? What's that mean? It means she thinks they're a bit silly, sweetie. It’s an idiom, a funny way of saying something. Is it like when Dad says “break a leg”? Exactly! Like that. Don’t want to wish Grandma “a load of hot air”, do we? No! We’ll get her sunflowers! And a blue one! Like the sky! Sunflowers are perfect! Okay, so let's recap. Cake, sprinkles, flowers , cuddles, Forest School, fairy house/rock painting. Anything else? Can I make her a card? With glitter! Lots and lots of glitter! Of course you can! The more glitter, the better. Just… maybe not  too  much on the table. Remember what happened last time? It looked like it was snowing glitter! It certainly did! Right then, operation Mother’s Day: glitter permitting, is officially underway. Let's go make a list. And then… cake. Should we start on the cake? Yes! Please! Yes, please, Mummy! Pink sprinkles! Pink sprinkles it is. Let’s get organising! Right then, so it looks like it’s gonna rain this afternoon so the forest school is out! I'll get the art supplies out instead! Right then who’s got the glitter? I have got the glitter! All the glitter!

Honestly, I just don't know how she's coping. Seeing Mum like that… it’s just… draining. I know, love. It's heartbreaking. She’s always been the strong one, hasn't she? The one you could always rely on. Absolutely. Remember when Dad… when he was ill? She was a rock. Now… now she just looks… fragile. And the way she keeps trying to downplay things. “Oh, it’s just a bit of a cough,” she said. A bit of a cough that’s turned out to be stage three. They always do, don’t they? Minimise everything. It's like they think it's a weakness, admitting they're struggling. It is a worry, though. She's so resistant to help. Keeps saying she's fine, doesn't want to be a burden. Says she'll manage. She won’t manage on her own, though, will she? We need to push a little more. Have you spoken to Sarah and Mark about it? I did, briefly. Sarah’s too busy with the kids, Mark’s got that massive project at work. They both feel helpless, too, which I get, but it just leaves me feeling like I'm carrying everything. Well, you  are  carrying a lot. But we’re here for you, you know that. Can I pop over tomorrow and keep you company? Just a couple of hours? We could go through some of those letters she’s been accumulating. That would be lovely, actually. She's getting so behind. The bills, the letters from the hospital… it's overwhelming. I’m trying to sort things, but with the proofreading work, I’m struggling to find the time. Don’t beat yourself up about it. You’re juggling a lot already. And remember what your therapist said about setting boundaries? You can’t pour from an empty cup, love. I know, I know. It’s just… I feel guilty. Guilty for even  thinking  about my own needs when Mum’s going through this. Honestly, guilt is a useless emotion in situations like this. You need to look after yourself so you  can  look after her. It's not selfish, it's practical. That’s what Sarah keeps saying. She mentioned getting me a voucher for a massage… Actually, that does sound rather nice. Do it! You deserve it. And tell her to book one for herself too.

Right, so I’ve been looking at the seminar schedule for next term. It’s brutal. Like, really brutal. Three seminars a week, plus my prep time... I'm going to be living on coffee and instant noodles. Sounds about right for a postgraduate. At least you're actually teaching, though. My timetable looks like a jigsaw puzzle from hell. Trying to fit everything in around my volunteering… It’s not ideal. Yeah, it’s definitely a step up from undergrad. I mean, research on top of teaching… Have you had any luck with finding a decent vegetarian cookbook yet? I'm officially sick of beans on toast. I did find one at the charity shop last week, loads of Indian recipes actually. Should be good, lots of vegetables and spices. Want to try making something tonight? I was thinking maybe a vegetable korma? Absolutely! That sounds amazing. Although, supermarket shopping is going to be a nightmare. Did you see the price of avocados last week? Highway robbery! Don't even get me started! We need to find some cheaper alternatives. Maybe butternut squash? It has a similar texture. Good shout. Seriously though, I’m starting to think about looking into funding for my next stage of research. The tuition fees are going to be a killer. Yeah, it’s scary. Have you looked into those Korean government scholarships again? I know you said it was a long shot, but… I know, right? I've been glancing at them. The cultural aspect is fascinating - the role of honorifics and politeness markers in Korean conversation is something I'd love to explore more deeply.
