And it would be incredible to actually  be  in South Korea, experiencing the language and culture firsthand. You’d love it. I remember you saying something about the Chuseok harvest festival – that would be amazing to witness. Definitely. I've been reading a bit about the gender dynamics there too. Apparently, there are still quite different expectations and roles between men and women… fascinating, but a bit unsettling. It's always interesting comparing cultures, isn't it? It makes you think about your own assumptions. Remember that article we read about the linguistic relativity hypothesis? Oh yeah, the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis. The idea that language shapes thought. I always thought it was a bit too deterministic, but... Exactly! But it does raise interesting questions. Actually, speaking of language, Professor Davies was going on about Chomsky's Universal Grammar again today.

Speaker_1 : Right, who ordered the pepperoni and mushroom? Because that’s  clearly  me. Speaker_2 : Aye, you were sniffin' around the pizza box like a bairn at a sweet shop. Honestly, Liv, you're mental. Speaker_3 : Stop bein’ mean, Chloe. It's good pizza, innit? I reckon this could actually beat Dominos. Speaker_4 : Don't get ahead of yourself, Maisie. It’s pizza. It's  always  good. Okay, so, serious question - has anyone actually started their physics work? Because mine is just…staring at me. Mocking me even. Oh god, don't remind me. I swear, Professor Davies is actively trying to make us fail. I'm starting to think I should’ve just stayed with History. Speaking of staying with something, did you see Charlie Simpson was back with the boys? Like, seriously back? No way! Busted reunion? Is that allowed anymore? Proper throwback! Remember screaming the lyrics to 'Yearning' in primary school? I had a sports kit top on and everything, ironically. Oh my god, I  totally  do! I’m pretty sure I tackled someone while trying to sing. It was a mess. Anyway, back to physics. I’m having a mental block. I’m pretty sure maths is designed to confuse me. That’s because you’re thinking too much, Liv. Just… do it! Like in Cloud Atlas. Everything’s connected somehow. Woah, deep, Chloe. Right, I’m forgetting we're supposed to be enjoying pizza and not having an existential crisis. What did everyone think of The Big Fat Quiz last night? Maisie absolutely smashed it! She knew  everything . Even random facts about…well, I don’t even know  what . You were on fire! I was useless. Completely blanked on who directed City of Bones. It was mortal. It was like, if you don’t know that, are you even a film person? Speaking of forgetting things, anyone else remember Sophie's Secret Santa last year? The scented candles that smelled like old socks? Oh god, yes! Absolute disaster! She looked so embarrassed. And then she had to pretend like she loved it! Classic. Have you guys ever played Heads Up? We should. Yes! Let's do it after. Maybe we can get some flavoured vodka going. Raspberry? Woah, hold your horses. Assessments are looming. Focus, people! Has anyone heard anything about the flooding in Lancaster? Is it still bad? Apparently. They’re saying it’s affecting the bus routes again.

Honestly, the amount of times people try to define "like" in a corpus… it's wild. You’d think it’d be simple, yeah? Just a little word. Tell me about it. Everything’s complicated, isn't it? Especially language. I deal with stress calculations for bridges, and  that's  straightforward compared to the nuances of filler words. Exactly! And the layers! It can be a discourse marker, a hedge, an intensifier…depending on the context. One research project I’m working on, we’re mapping its emotional weight. Apparently, there are subtle shifts in intonation that completely change its meaning. Emotional weight of "like?" That's brilliant. So, a casual "like, what are you doing?" versus a pleading "Like,  please  don't tell Mum?" Precisely! And then you get into regional variations. Everyone uses "like" differently. I'm sure your lot down south have their own horrifying interpretations of it. Hey! We're quite refined down here. Though, I did hear someone use it seven times in a single sentence the other day. It was… unsettling. Sounded like a broken record. Seven! My god. We had someone emailing me once, convinced “like” was a verb. They wanted to know if you could "like" a sentence. No, you can’t “like” a sentence! That’s incredible. Did you manage to convince them otherwise? Eventually, yeah. It took a very long email explaining grammatical function. It’s just… sometimes I feel like I’m fighting a losing battle against the English language. That’s a bit dramatic, isn't it? But I get it. Engineering has its challenges too – trying to account for every possible weather condition, for example – but at least bridges generally behave as expected. True. At least bridges don't randomly shift their meaning and confuse linguists. Do you ever miss the north? Sometimes. I miss the accents, definitely. And proper chips. Not these thin, greasy things they call chips down here. Oh, you’re preaching to the choir. You need a proper chip shop vinegar soak. It's a fundamental human right up north. Absolutely. Maybe we should plan a weekend trip back? We could hit up that new exhibition at the Baltic. They're showing photography focused on industrial landscapes. That sounds brilliant! And then a load of chips. Definitely a load of chips. You thinking about telling your company about the possible promotion? I'm dreading it.

This rain, eh? Don't stop, does it? No, it really doesn’t. Drizzling all morning. Makes you want to just stay indoors, doesn't it? It's awful. Makes the garden look so dreary. Hope it clears up for the weekend, though. We need some sun, definitely. I’ve been trying to get out for a run, but it's just not ideal. Are you feeling alright, ANON? You seemed a little quiet earlier. Just a bit stiff in the joints, love. Getting on, you know? Damp weather doesn’t help. The doctor said it’s arthritis setting in. Oh, dear, that’s not good. Are you taking anything for it? Just the paracetamol, mostly. Doesn’t do a lot, mind. Still aches something shocking. My dad’s the same. He says every joint complains when it rains. It’s a common thing, apparently. Electrolytes in the air reacting with something in the joints… or some nonsense like that. So they say. Want another biscuit? Please. They are rather nice! Yes, thank you. Speaking of… did you see Norwich played awful yesterday? Proper shambles. Absolutely dreadful. Honestly, I'm starting to worry about them this season. Puts a downer on a Sunday, doesn’t it? Well, at least it gave us something to complain about. It's always the same, isn't it? That it is. It's all gloom and doom these days. Remember when they used to win every week? Seems a lifetime ago. Though, to be fair, I don’t think I’ve ever known a season where Norwich were consistently brilliant. True. My brother’s gone completely off football, says it’s all just money these days. He's not wrong, mind. Used to be about the love of the game. Everything’s about money now. Even my grandson’s obsessed with that new phone. Wants the latest one. Costs a fortune! They do! My niece just got a new tablet. It can do practically everything. Sometimes I wonder if we’re all becoming too reliant on these gadgets. Don't get me started! I swear, I'm spending more time trying to fix my mum's printer than I am grading essays. Oh, technology. Always a headache, isn’t it? Give me a good book any day. Hear, hear! At least books don’t need charging. A fair point. Still, it's good to stay connected, isn't it?

Right, spill! What's been going on? It feels like ages since we all last properly chatted. Tell me about it! Life has been a whirlwind. Work’s been crazy, but in a good way, you know? Massive targets met, so I'm chuffed. How's the admin life treating you, Elodie? Still surrounded by spreadsheets? You have  no  idea. But I'm enjoying it, honestly. It’s surprisingly fulfilling being organized, and I’m learning loads. But enough about me, what about you two? Phoebe, still creating gorgeous things? And Chloe, any exciting art projects on the go? Yeah, things are good! I've been doing a lot of freelance work lately, which is brilliant. Just finished a really cool branding project for a new yoga studio. It was super creative, a lot of hand-drawn elements – I loved it. Me too! I'm working on a series of illustrations for a children's book, which is proper fun. It’s nice to be doing something a bit different. Oh, and I'm seeing Liam, remember him from uni? Liam! Wow, really? The one with the… questionable taste in music? He’s evolved, I swear! He's actually really lovely, and we get on so well. We went to that new Italian place last week, it was amazing. Ooh, where? We need recommendations! I’m always up for Italian! Okay, shifting gears slightly... Did you hear about Sophie and Mark? No! What happened? They’re engaged! Can you believe it? After all this time! Oh my god, that’s amazing! Where did he propose? Apparently, on a beach in Santorini. Very romantic, very Instagrammable. That’s so lovely! Wonder if they've set a date yet? Are they thinking big and extravagant, or small and intimate? I’m betting they'll go all out. Sophie's always loved a bit of glamour. We  have  to go dress shopping with her! That’ll be so much fun! Absolutely! We definitely need to schedule something. We should all go out for dinner while we’re at it. I'm in! How about next Saturday? We could try that new tapas place everyone's been raving about. Sounds perfect! What about boys for you two? Anyone new on the scene? Don’t even ask! My dating life is a complete disaster zone. Guys either ghost me, or they’re just… not worth the effort.

Now, this mobile phone business...it’s a right mystery to me, it is. Never could get the hang of it. Martha tried to show me how to send a picture the other day. Ended up calling her three times by accident. Oh, dear. They are a bit fiddly, aren't they, Arthur? I still prefer a good old-fashioned postcard. Something you can stick on the fridge. All this digital stuff... disappears into the ether, doesn’t it? You know, it’s really quite clever actually. The way they can connect you to anyone, anywhere. I use it to keep in touch with my daughter, she's over in Australia now. Sends me all sorts of photos. Australia, eh? Fancy that. Remember when young David was always talking about wanting to go to Australia? Oh, yes! Always had his head in the clouds, that one. Didn’t he try to train a pony for the Grand National once? Oh, don't remind me! That little grey thing, Daisy, tripping all over herself at the first hurdle. A sight to behold, it was. Took weeks to get the mud out of the fields. Remember Mrs. Higgins’s horses too? She bred some champion ones, didn’t she? Used to come to our school fetes and let the kids ride them. Oh, yes! She was a lovely woman. Always had a smile and a Werther's Original for you. My grandchildren adored her. Speaking of grandchildren, little Emily's started playing chess. Chess, that’s a good game. My dad used to beat me at it every time. He always had a trick or two up his sleeve. It’s a brilliant game for their brains. Encourages logic and strategy. Though, I did spend a very frustrating half hour last week trying to explain castling to my nephew. He just didn't get it. Things are a bit tight at the moment, aren’t they? Pension barely covers the bills. Heating's gone up again. Tell me about it. It's the same here. Can't even afford a proper Christmas this year. Just a small tree and some tinsel. Gets you down a bit, doesn’t it? It does. Though, I suppose we've seen worse times. Remember back in the eighties? Everything was so uncertain. Oh, don’t remind me! The miners’ strike…and the queues at the shops. A dreadful time for everyone.

It’s so lovely to finally catch you, David! It feels like ages since we last properly chatted. It has, hasn't it, Eleanor? Life just seems to slip away, doesn’t it? Wonderful to see you, dear. And you're looking well. Thank you! So good to see you looking so chipper, too. Come in, come in. I’ve just put the kettle on. Earl Grey alright? Earl Grey is perfect, thank you. You always did make a good cup of tea. Much better than my Martha can manage, bless her heart. She burns the water most of the time! I’m sure she has other talents! So, what have you both been up to lately? Been doing much travelling? I know you used to love a good holiday. Well, we’ve had a bit of a slower pace these last few years, you know, getting on a bit. Martha’s knees aren’t what they used to be. But we did manage a little trip to the Lake District last spring. Absolutely stunning, it was. Oh, I’ve always wanted to go! It sounds idyllic. I'm teaching a new class of Year 8s this term, which is already proving rather energetic. Trying to get them excited about French idioms… it’s a challenge! French, eh? Always thought it was a beautiful language. My sister, Patricia, she was quite fluent, actually. Used to live in Paris for a while. Worked in a little bookstore near the Sorbonne. That sounds delightful! Do you still dabble in your model railways at all? I remember you were rather proud of your layout. Oh yes, still going strong! Built a new section, actually. A little bit of rural Devon, complete with a miniature cream tea shop. It’s quite something, if I may say so myself. Keeps me busy, you see. Better than sitting around doing nothing. That's wonderful! Always admired your dedication to it. I’m trying to take up pottery, you know, for a bit of a creative outlet, but it’s… messy. Very messy indeed. Pottery, eh? Good for the hands. Gets you using different muscles. My father was a carpenter, you know. Could build anything with his hands. Real craftsman. That’s lovely. So, any big plans for the weekend? Anything exciting lined up? Actually, yes. My grandson, young Thomas, he’s coming round for Sunday lunch. He’s started learning the clarinet now.

Honestly, Valentine’s Day was a bit of a letdown, wasn’t it? Like, everyone made such a huge deal of it. Tell me about it! My mum was having a right go, asking if I'd got a card, you know. Like I  need  a card to prove I’m loved. Exactly! And then all the restaurants massively inflate their prices. We ended up getting pizza from that new place down the road. Oh, did you try “Papa Tony’s”? I did last week. It was pretty good, actually. Way better than Domino’s. No, we went to “Pizza Paradise.” It was decent, but definitely overpriced for what it was, yeah? I mean £25 for a large pepperoni? Ridiculous. Mad, innit? I reckon they just know people are desperate to splash out. What did you guys do the rest of the weekend though, apart from pizza? Went to the cinema on Saturday. Saw 'Dune: Part Two'. Honestly, it was brilliant! The visuals were insane. Oh, I’ve heard good things! I'm still trying to convince Liam to go with me. He's being a right grumpy about it, though. Says it’s “too long and sci-fi-ey." Proper Midlands grump. Liam's always like that, isn’t he? You should just drag him along! It's worth it. What’s he been up to then? Still struggling with his essay? Yeah, it's a nightmare. He’s stuck on the introduction. I’ve read it like five times and I still can’t work out what he’s trying to say. It's just…sentences. Oh dear. Maybe he needs a break. You should take him shopping or something. Distract him from the academic doom. That’s a good idea actually. We were meant to go to Birmingham on Sunday, but he said he was too busy. Proper selfish. Birmingham’s good for shopping, though! Loads of new shops have opened up. Have you checked out that new vintage store in the Custard Factory? No! Is it good? I'm always on the lookout for a bargain. My accent was practically giving me away there the other day; the shop assistant kept trying to get me to buy things on sale! You're not that noticeable with your accent, love. I barely noticed it. That’s easy for you to say, you grew up in London! Everyone here comments on it.

This Dan Dan noodles is genuinely incredible. I’m going to need a serious appetite to finish this. Honestly, yeah. I went a bit mad with the spice level, didn't I? My face is already tingling. A little, but it's good! You know, reading that article about the government's new housing initiative… it’s all just… massively performative. Ugh, don't even get me started. It’s just throwing a few crumbs to everyone and patting themselves on the back. They keep using phrases like “levelling up” without actually addressing the core issues. Exactly! And the way they frame it - owning a home is a  right  now, suddenly? After decades of deliberately creating a market where it's totally unaffordable for young people? It’s almost insulting. My cousin’s still living with his parents in Harrow – he's 27, a software developer, earning decent money, and he  still  can't save enough for a deposit. It's just… impossible. I know! It's the same with my friends. They’re all bouncing around rentals, constantly worried about rent increases or landlords selling up. I was looking at some new developments near Canary Wharf… the prices are obscene. Obscene is the perfect word. They’re building these luxury apartments that no one can actually afford, and then claiming it’s solving the housing crisis. It's purely capitalist, isn’t it? Just feeding the property speculators. Totally. It makes you think, like, does anyone actually  benefit  from this system, beyond a very small percentage of people? And it’s layered with all this… I don’t even know how to say it without sounding dramatic, but the racial undertones are just so obvious sometimes. The areas where affordable housing is actually built are often systematically overlooked for investment, leaving those communities even further behind. My mum keeps saying… What does she say? She says it's a deliberate strategy. Designed to keep certain communities marginalized and dependent. It sounds harsh but… I’m starting to see it. It's no surprise there’s a rise in racial tension. People are desperate, feeling forgotten, and it's all being fueled by this unequal system. Have you seen that piece by Fatima Manji in  The Guardian ? Yeah, the one on gentrification in Brixton? Brilliant. She connects it so directly to the wealth disparity and the manipulation of narratives. It’s infuriating.

So, what did you think of the nursery? Little Leo seemed pretty happy when I picked him up. Honestly, I'm a wreck, love. Absolutely a wreck. Leaving him there this morning... I had to bite my tongue to stop myself from turning around and grabbing him back. I know, Mum, but he was laughing and playing with the other kids. He seemed to be having a right giggle. You’ve got to remember, it’s good for him to socialise. I know, I know. It’s just… he’s been with me full time for nearly two years. It's a big change. I keep thinking, ‘Is he eating okay? Is he settling? Does he miss me?’ He’s got lovely staff there, remember? They’ve all got qualifications, they know what they’re doing. And you’re going back to work, aren't you? You need to get back into something. I do. I just feel guilty, you know? Like I’m abandoning him. It’s ridiculous, I know. I keep looking at jobs, but nothing’s really jumping out. Do you think I should go for something part-time to start? Yeah, definitely. Something part-time would ease you back in. Maybe something around here so you can get to nursery easily. What about that customer service job at the garden centre? You were looking at that. I was, wasn’t I? It’s a bit…but it's a start, isn't it? Right, food. I’ve made that pasta you like. Remember when you were little and you used to cover yourself in tomato sauce? Oh God, Mum! Don't remind me! I was a nightmare. You’d be scrubbing it off my face for ages. You were! And that's why I put extra relish on the table. So you'd have somewhere else to cover yourself. You are wicked! So, holiday plans? Are we still thinking Mallorca next summer? Definitely. Leo’s getting bigger every day. He needs a bit of sun and sand, and frankly, so do I. Although I’m terrified he’s going to spend the whole time trying to eat the sand. Probably. We'll need to invest in a good sun hat and some factor 50. Right, what about weaning? He is still on pouches mostly isn't he. Yes, mostly. He ate some mashed sweet potato the other day without throwing it all over the floor.

Honestly, the day was just… hectic. I’m still processing it all. Tell us. What happened? You looked a bit pale when you walked in. It was the police. They wanted a statement. About the… incident at the gallery. Oh, wow. The one with the… the sculpture? Yes. Apparently, someone tripped and damaged it. A rather valuable piece, apparently. Luckily, no one was seriously hurt, but I was the closest person, so they wanted my account. That's awful. Do you think they suspect anyone? I honestly don’t know. They were just gathering information. It felt very… procedural. The frustrating thing is, it was all so quick. One minute I was admiring the piece, the next there was a crash. Well, at least you weren’t involved directly. Just an unfortunate witness. Do they want another statement later? They said they might, but just to contact them if they need anything else. It’s just… unnerving, being involved with the police like that. I can imagine. Do you want to talk about it more? Not really, not right now. I just need to eat and relax. Speaking of which, this lasagne is amazing, Liam! Thanks, Mum. Glad you like it. So, apart from my drama, anyone else have anything eventful to report? Just the usual battles with EE. My phone bill is ridiculous this month. They’ve added some ridiculous premium service I didn't authorise. That's so annoying. They do that on purpose, don’t they? It feels like it! I’m on the phone to them tomorrow, ready for a fight. I’ve compiled all the evidence. Good luck with that! Let us know how it goes. Right, my week is looking fairly quiet. Trying to sort out the staffing rota at the store – always a challenge. Oh, you know how it is. I’ve got a meeting with investors on Wednesday, which should be interesting. Trying to secure more funding for the new app. Good luck with that. Is it looking promising? Potentially, yes. The feedback has been positive, but you never know with these things. So, what are we all doing this weekend? Any plans? I was thinking of finally getting around to clearing out the attic. Dreadful task, but it needs doing. Oh, don’t say that! You’ll find a treasure trove of forgotten gems! More likely a treasure trove of dust and broken toys, I suspect.

So, how’s married life treating you? Settling in okay with Sarah? Yeah, it’s… good. Really good, actually. A bit different, obviously. She’s quite… organised. Sounds familiar. My sister’s the same. You’ll learn to love the organised life. Maybe! I’m still trying to find my feet a bit. Speaking of feet, she made me clear out the shed the other day. Absolute jungle in there. A wedding present, perhaps? Getting you used to hard work? Probably! I was complaining about it, but she said something about needing space for a potting bench. Not complaining now. So, what have  you  been up to? Still lecturing the world in English? Yep, still battling with prepositions and present perfect. It’s a never-ending story. I just finished a series on Roman history, actually. Really got into it. Roman history? Seriously? Like gladiators and stuff? Exactly! We looked at Spartacus, of course. It's incredible, the sheer scale of the revolts, the brutality of it all. And then, the early deaths… Makes you think, doesn’t it? Yeah, definitely. Less complaining about clearing a shed when you think about that. I saw ‘Spartacus’ years ago, proper epic. You know, liked the music too. All those big drums. Right! Reminds me of some of that Greek music, actually. Speaking of which, I made some spanakopita the other day. Remember how we used to love that stuff? Oh man, yes! Your mum’s recipe, right? Still got it? Of course. It’s practically sacred. I'd love you to come over for proper tea and spanakopita next week – Sarah might need some lessons in Greek cuisine. Sounds lethal! Need to get some chickpeas and… Do you still have that mortar and pestle? Yeah, gathering dust on the shelf, to be honest. I should dust it off. We could make some proper harissa. Perfect! Got loads of herbs and spices now, since Sarah got into her own little herb garden. Trying to be all eco-friendly and stuff. That's great! Speaking of eco-friendly, I found this amazing shop in China Town the other day. They have all these nuts and seeds, dried fruits... ridiculous selection. Got some goji berries, never tried those before. Goji berries? So posh. Are they good with chickpeas? I don’t know yet! Trying them in a smoothie. And I got a little jade pendant. A souvenir, I suppose.

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. This week has been brutal. Tell me about it! That English test was a nightmare. I swear, Mrs. Davies was trying to trick us. Seriously! All those obscure Victorian poets. Who even  reads  that stuff? My head’s still spinning with Tennyson and… and… what was his name? Browning, I think? Ugh. I spent the whole test staring at the ceiling trying to remember something, anything, about his life. Me too! I think I accidentally wrote about squirrels for one of the questions… I panicked. Squirrels? That's amazing! I wrote about pizza. I just couldn't think. Did you finish all the questions, at least? Barely. Ran out of time on the last one. I just wrote, “This poem is… interesting.” and handed it in. Classic! At least you tried. How was Art then? Mr. Jacobson was being weird again, wasn’t he? Oh my god, yes! He spent the entire lesson talking about the symbolism of bananas. Bananas, Chloe! Who cares about banana symbolism? I know! He’s so random. I think he just enjoys confusing us. I'm worried about the project, though. The abstract sculpture. Me too! I have absolutely no idea what I'm doing. I’m thinking of just gluing random things together and hoping for the best. That’s actually not a bad idea. Less thinking, more… sticking. Speaking of which, are you going to wind band rehearsal on Saturday? Definitely. I’m finally getting the hang of that clarinet solo. It’s still tricky, but not as awful as it was before. Are you playing the flute again? Yeah, I’m trying to. Mrs. Peterson says I need to project more. It’s hard when all I can think about is my English test. I get it. So, did you hear about what happened with Liam and Sophie? No! What? Don’t tell me he… He apparently tripped over his own feet in front of the whole school during rugby practice. And landed right in a puddle. No way! Oh my god, that’s hilarious! Was he okay? Apparently, yeah. Just completely soaked. He looked mortified, though. Everyone was trying not to laugh. Serves him right for showing off. So, French lessons… still a disaster zone? They are. Madame Dubois is relentless. She expects us to be fluent after, like, three months. It’s impossible!

Lovely to see ya, Maureen! And Liam, good to see you too – look a bit peaky, lad, are you alright? Aye, Brenda, it’s brilliant to see you too! Him? He’s always peaky, isn't he? Thinks he's a rugby player, but spends half his time glued to a computer screen. I was researching something, Mam. Can’t you ever let me do anything? And I’m fine, thanks. Just… tired. History coursework is killing me. History, is it? What are ya studying now? The Tudors again? No, the First World War. It's depressing. All the statistics... mind boggling. Don’t mention statistics! Makes me think about the cost of living crisis. Did you see that article in The Northern Echo about the energy prices? Aye, appalling, Maureen. Appalling. Makes you wonder how folks are coping. I'm not convinced my pension will even cover my heating bill this winter. You've got a good pension, Gran. More than most. Besides, you could always knit more jumpers. Always the practical one, aren't you, Liam? Me mam used to say, “Brenda, a good jumper can save a fortune” Speaking of saving fortunes, have you been following the football, Brenda? Newcastle are flying! Flyin'! I nearly lost my voice on Saturday shoutin’ at the telly! Absolutely brilliant. The new manager's done wonders, hasn’t he? He’s alright. Though I think the whole “Toon Army” branding is a bit much. All those flags... it feels a bit manufactured, doesn’t it? Manufactured? It’s passion, Liam! Pure and simple. A bit of Geordie pride. Remember the days when we'd all be down the Leazes End, singing our hearts out? Oh, the Leazes End...  that  was something. Used to get a right singin’ voice after a full day of teachin’. You'd be hoarse for a week! You lot were mad. Honestly. All chanting and scarves and… Honestly, it probably contributed to the decline of the British coal industry. All that shouting. You're a card, you are! Honestly, the youth of today... No appreciation for a bit of proper atmosphere. So Maureen, did you manage to sort out that issue with your computer? Still struggling with the new software? Honestly, Brenda, I’m at my wit’s end. I keep trying, but it’s like it’s actively fighting against me. I was trying to book a doctor’s appointment online the other day... Ended up ordering a new set of garden gnomes instead.

Right, everyone, help yourselves. Bit of everything for everyone, I hope. Lovely, lovely. Looks a right treat, Sarah. You always do well with the chicken. Never dry. Always does, dear. Always. Takes a gift, you know, keeping it moist. I’ve never managed it myself. Always ends up like cardboard. It smells amazing. Though, Mum, maybe go a bit easier on the potatoes. You know we’re all trying to… you know. Trying to what? Starve? Don't be daft, Michael. A bit of potato never hurt anyone. Besides, you all have good genes. That's what everyone says, Mum. But a bit of moderation never hurts either. I was reading an article the other day about the obesity crisis, and… Oh, here we go. Another doom and gloom article. You lecturers are all the same, Sarah. Always telling us something we already know. It’s not just lecturers, Dad. It’s a serious issue. Look at little Leo down the road… hasn’t left his house in six months. He’s probably just playing video games, dear. They do engross you. Remember when your father used to spend hours tinkering with his Morris Minor. That was different! That was keeping something running! This is just… sitting around. And a lot of it is processed food. You can't blame people, the clever devils marketing all that rubbish. Well, Dad’s got a point there. The advertising is relentless. And food allergies are just getting worse, aren’t they? Poor Emily’s got another reaction to something. Yeah, she's convinced it's the new almond butter we bought. Doctor says it could be anything. Getting harder and harder to figure out what she  can  eat. Speaking of doctors and hospitals… how’s your knee, Roger? Last I heard you were still hobbling around. It's alright. Slow recovery, you know. That surgery last year. They said no complications, but it's still stiff. Got to keep the exercises up. It must be frustrating. The waiting lists are ridiculous these days. My colleague’s mum’s been waiting six months for a hip replacement. It's the funding, isn't it? Always the funding. It’s a disgrace. Should be prioritised. So, are we doing a jigsaw after dinner? I bought that new one from the charity shop. It’s a picture of Norwich Cathedral. Sounds lovely, Mum. Though I’m not sure Michael will be keen.

Right, so I was wrestling with Moodle again today. Honestly, it feels like a sentient being actively trying to make my life difficult. Tell me about it! I had a student emailing me asking why their submission wasn't showing up, and naturally, it was a Moodle glitch. Spent a good twenty minutes debugging that one. Same! I was trying to create a quiz using the new question bank feature, and it just... refused to save. Kept giving me this vague error message. Had to resort to the old method, which is clunky and takes twice as long. Ugh, the old method. I hate it. Do you think we should push for training on the new features? I feel like half the staff are just stumbling around, trying to figure it out as they go. I've mentioned it to Janice in IT, but I don't think it's a priority for them. They're dealing with the server migration and all that. Plus, convincing the department to allocate budget for something like that is always a battle. It's frustrating, isn’t it? Especially when we’re trying to modernise our teaching and these tools are supposed to make it easier. Instead, they just add another layer of complexity. Exactly! And the way the discussion forums are structured… it's just a black hole of unanswered questions and off-topic ramblings. Honestly, I'd rather have handwritten essays. Don’t say that! The Dean would have a fit. But I get your point. I tried setting up a guided discussion with specific prompts, and it just ended up with everyone posting GIFs of cats. See! Sentient being. It  knows  what will distract people. Speaking of distracting, did you manage to get that new software installed for the media studies students? Nearly. It’s finally downloaded, but it's refusing to recognise my graphics card. Spent a good hour troubleshooting that earlier. It’s listing some ancient driver version… I think I need to dig into the settings tonight. Oh, that sounds cheerful. Those media studies students are going to be a nightmare if they can't render their projects properly. Maybe I’ll offer to come over and have a look later, if you’re still struggling. That would be amazing, actually. Thanks. Maybe pizza and frustrated sighs? Definitely pizza and frustrated sighs. And probably a very strong cup of tea.

Honestly, I feel like I’ve been existing in a perpetual state of jetlag. Everything feels slightly…off. Tell me about it. I'm running on fumes and coffee. The flight back was brutal. Little Leo wasn't exactly a picture of tranquility. He was, wasn't he? Luckily, Elsie slept most of the way, which was a minor miracle. But now, both of them are just... off. Teething, maybe? Probably teething. Or just adjusting to being back in their own beds. Did you manage to get any sleep on the plane? A couple of hours, scattered across various positions that probably looked quite ridiculous. I woke up convinced I was attempting to do yoga in the aisle. Sounds about right. Right, so let's actually try and organise something for this weekend. That local production of 'A Midsummer Night's Dream' – we really should go, shouldn't we? Absolutely. It’ll be lovely to get out of the house, even just for a couple of hours. Remind me who's directing it? Emily Carter, isn't it? She did a fantastic job with ‘The Tempest’ last year. I think this one will be really good. I’m keen. It’s been ages since we’ve seen anything decent. The problem is, childcare… I’ve already tentatively spoken to Sarah. She said she'd be happy to come over on Saturday evening and look after them. Really? That’s brilliant! You’re a star. Thank you. No worries. She loves them. Are we thinking dinner before or after? I was thinking a quick bite somewhere near the theatre. Let’s do before. Something simple. Maybe that new Italian place on High Street? Their pasta is supposed to be amazing. Good shout. I’ll book a table then. What time do you think? The show starts at seven-thirty, right? Yes, seven-thirty. So maybe six o'clock for dinner? That gives us a little cushion in case Elsie decides to launch into a major meltdown. Smart move. Right, booking confirmed. Six o'clock at Bella Notte. Anything else we need to sort? Just… a serious need for copious amounts of caffeine. And maybe a long, uninterrupted nap. Oh, and to remember to unpack! That suitcase has been lurking in the hallway since we got home. Priorities, darling. Caffeine first. Naps second. Unpacking… well, that can wait until Monday. Let's focus on getting through today, and maybe catching a glimpse of the sun.

So, have you heard from your sister’s family recently? Last I knew they were still having issues with getting the paperwork sorted for Zara’s visa. Yes, just yesterday. It's still a nightmare. Apparently, the processing times in Baghdad are… well, they're glacial. They’re dealing with a backlog, compounded by everything else. They're saying it could be another six months at least. Six months! Little Layla is missing her mum terribly. That's awful. Six months is a long time. You’d think with your brother-in-law’s connections… Connections don’t seem to matter much these days, do they? You’d think they'd prioritise family reunification, but bureaucracy… it moves regardless of human need. And the politics, of course, always swirling around. It's all tangled up with the oil, isn’t it? It always is. Though, you know, I was reading an article the other day about Libya… the instability there, the influence of groups like Wahabi… it’s just frightening, isn't it? How easily things can unravel. Oh, Libya. A complicated situation. It always was, even before Gaddafi. And now… well, it’s just a playground for various actors. Everyone’s got their own agenda, vying for control of the oil streams. It’s the root of so much conflict, isn't it? Poverty, extremism… it all stems from those black gold rivers. Exactly. It's heartbreaking really. Speaking of heartache, are your friends in Erbil managing okay? I remember they were worried about the economic situation there. They’re doing alright, relatively. The KRG is stable-ish, at least compared to some other parts of the region, but inflation is hitting hard. Everything’s more expensive. My friend Ranya’s husband, he's a teacher, he’s struggling. Teachers’ salaries haven’t kept pace. Young people are getting so disillusioned. It's a recurring theme, isn't it? Everywhere you look, young people feel abandoned by the system. It's hard to watch. I'm seeing it here too, with my students. So much apathy, so much cynicism. It’s the future, though, isn't it? We need to inspire them. Encourage them to be active, engaged citizens. Difficult when the deck is stacked against them. It is. Are you and Sarah still thinking about moving house? I remember you saying you wanted something with a bit more space.

That lamb was absolutely divine, wasn’t it? Honestly, the best I’ve made in ages. It was brilliant, love. Really, really good. You’ve perfected the roasting time. It was indeed. Proper Sunday dinner fare. Though I do miss a good Yorkshire pudding, you know. You never did make those properly, dear. Oh, stop it! They were fine. And honestly, having the TV in the dining room isn't the worst thing. We actually got to see the end of that nature documentary while we were eating. I thought it was a bit strange at first, but it works okay. Much better than it was before when the TV was in the lounge and we all missed the football. Well, times change, don't they? When I was a headmistress, the television was practically banned from the staff room. Distraction, you see. You always were a stickler for rules, weren't you? Thankfully, we’re a little more relaxed now. I've got some of that Scottish tablet you like, Mum, would you like a piece? Oh, don't mind if I do! That’s the only tablet worth eating. Not that sugary nonsense you find elsewhere. True, it’s a proper treat. Thinking about treats... we were talking about that cruise, were we not? Yes, we were! I've been looking at some itineraries. The Mediterranean ones sound lovely, but so does Scandinavia. Scandinavia eh? Bit chilly for a holiday. I reckon we should stick to somewhere warmer. The Caribbean, maybe? The Caribbean! Honestly, at my age, I'd rather not fly for twelve hours. I’d rather a smaller ship, a bit closer to home. Maybe the Norwegian fjords? Beautiful scenery. We could look into that. I've been trying to get back into some sort of workout routine, you know? Just a bit of yoga or Pilates. The doctor's been nagging me. You're always working out! I'm still struggling to find the motivation. I think a cruise might be the ideal way to no workout. Lie by a pool and order cocktails. I used to be quite the swimmer, you know. Back in my day, we had proper swimming lessons. Not like this splashing about you see now. Speaking of splashing about, how's Mrs. Peterson's dog doing? I saw her walking him the other day. Oh, Buster? Still bouncing around like a lunatic.

Right, so, who's taking the bins out tonight? Not me, I’m knackered from college. Liam, you were moaning about the smell yesterday. Aye, well, I'm not exactly leaping at the chance, am I? Been all day filling out job applications, getting nowhere. You’ll find something, Liam. Don't get disheartened. He always says that. Doesn’t make it any easier, does it? Thanks, Jamie. Really cheering me up. Just keeping it real, mate. So, Elodie, how’s uni going? Still loving the Graphic Design? Yeah, it’s amazing! We're doing a project on typography, which is surprisingly cool. Loads of technical stuff, but it's really creative too. Sounds fancy. Still got your head around all that German terminology though? Most of it. Some of it’s a nightmare, especially when it comes to the history of fonts. My brain just… shorts out. Remember back in sixth form, when you used to try and teach me German? "Der, die, das…" And you’d just stare blankly! Still can't say "Apfelstrudel" properly. You're still saying "Apple Strudel" instead of "Apfelstrudel," aren't you? It sounds the same! Okay, okay, settle down. So, anyone fancy ordering a pizza? I’m starving. Yes, please! I’m absolutely wrecked. What about Mom and Dad? Are they still coming round later? Aye, they said they’d be here around seven. Mom’s making that weird casserole again. The one with the unexpected pineapple? The very one. Don’t ask. Pineapple in a casserole… Peak Mum. You know she means well. It’s just… adventurous, let's say. Adventurous is a polite word for it. Remember that Christmas she tried to make a trifle with frozen chips? Speaker_1 & Oh my god, I’d completely forgotten! It was a disaster. The dog wouldn't even eat it. Says it all, really. Still, at least they’re putting in the effort. Trying to be supportive. So, you still living down with your folks, Jamie? Yeah, don’t get me started on my little brother and his constant gaming. It’s driving me up the wall. Living with your family can be rough, can't it? At least you have good company now. Yeah. Rest of us aren’t so bad. Now, pizza? What toppings? Pepperoni and mushroom for me, definitely. Anything spicy! I'm good with a Hawaiian. Don't judge me.

Right, so I need to get these fairy cakes baked for tomorrow’s lesson. Do you reckon six per child is enough? Ten! Ten fairy cakes! Six is boring! Ten's way better! Ten! Ten is a  lot  of fairy cakes, isn't it? I'll probably end up eating half of them myself. But okay, ten it is. Right, do you two want to help me stir? Yes! Can I put the sprinkles on? Me too! I want blue sprinkles! Okay, okay, sprinkles duty is yours. But be careful, don't put them all in your mouth! I won't! I will! Just a few! You’re incorrigible. So, the lesson… I’m going to use the fairy cakes to talk about fractions. Think they’ll understand? It’s a tricky one. Yes! Fairy fractions! Can we play Tomodachi Life after school? Maybe. If you’ve been really good and we didn’t end up with too much pink sprinkle on your faces. Speaking of, did you see that book I found in Morrisons yesterday? The one about dragons? The one with the sparkly cover? Yes! It looked perfect for story time. Did you get it? I did! It’s on the bookshelf. Although, I was thinking I might need to look for another copy of "The Gruffalo" too. It’s getting a bit battered. The Gruffalo’s the best! I like the mouse! He's clever! He is clever. Right, whisking time! And we’re forgetting a very important thing… What? What? Your half-birthdays! We haven’t celebrated them yet! Half-birthday cake! With candles! Lots of candles! Okay, okay. After the fairy cakes for the lesson, we’ll have a little half-birthday celebration. I’ll make something special. Yay! Can we have chocolate? Probably, if you’re good helpers with these fairy cakes. Now, stir those batter! And remember: no sprinkle-eating! I’m serious! Okay! But just a tiny one! Oh, you two. You are going to be the death of me! But I wouldn’t trade it for anything. Now, focus, bakers! We have a lesson to prepare for! And half-birthdays to celebrate! Right then, let’s get baking. Sprinkle! Me too! Sprinkle! Right, careful now… Mmm! Mmm! Don’t eat the mixture! I’m just testing it! You know, for quality control! You’re a little rascal. Good! Can I put the sprinkles in now?

Honestly, I’m still fuming about that car ad. The one popping up everywhere. The electric SUV? The one that specifically targets people who like vintage photography? Exactly! It’s creepy. Like, how do they even  know ? I haven’t looked at a car website in months. Just been scrolling through Instagram looking at old film cameras and suddenly, boom, there it is. It’s the Facebook algorithm at work, love. It’s collecting everything. Every like, every comment, every picture. It builds a profile of you before you even realise it has. I know, I know. It's just... aggressive. And slightly insulting, suggesting I need a new, expensive car because I appreciate artistry. It’s like they’re assuming all vintage photographers are wealthy and middle-aged. Or just exploiting a niche. They know people who like film photography are often quite particular. They’ll go for something stylish, something that  looks  good. And they’ve got you pegged. Wanting something aesthetically pleasing to match your aesthetic. It’s clever but... disconcerting. I tried blocking them already, you know. They’ll find another angle. They always do. Speaking of the internet, did you see that article about the AI-generated art pieces selling for ridiculous amounts? Vaguely. Something about an auction? It felt… wrong, somehow. It is a bit, isn't it? Someone creates an algorithm, feeds it a load of data, and suddenly it’s producing “art” that’s worth thousands. What does that even  mean  for actual artists who put years of work into honing their craft? It devalues the process, doesn't it? The hours, the dedication, the learning. It’s just…a click. Exactly. Though, on the other hand, I saw an interesting thread on Facebook - someone was using AI to restore old photos. Bringing back faded images, repairing tears… bringing family memories back to life.  That  felt a little more justifiable. Oh, that’s lovely! See? It's not all bad. It’s just…the line between helpful tool and exploitative replacement is getting blurred. Definitely. It’s all getting a bit dizzying, isn’t it? Maybe we should stick to looking at actual film cameras. Less algorithm, more… tangible beauty. I like the sound of that. Another cider, then? To a world with fewer targeted car ads and more slightly dusty film stock? Absolutely. To that. And escaping the Facebook vortex, at least for the rest of the afternoon.

Right, pause it there, yeah? Just before the big… you know, the giant strawberry. It's getting a bit much, isn't it? It's massive! He’s got to climb it! He  has  to climb it. Absolutely ludicrous, the whole thing. But… strangely compelling, innit? I like the bit where they’re all having dinner at the dinner table. With the food falling from the sky. Yeah, that’s well done. It’s got a bit of a commentary on consumerism, hasn’t it? All that food, just… raining down. Nobody really appreciating it. It looks yummy! I’d eat all that. You would, wouldn’t you? You've got a better appetite than I do, that’s for sure. I had a sandwich for lunch today and felt full afterwards, and I worked all day. What did you do at work today? Honestly, the usual drama. We've got this new display campaign on, pushing summer clothing, and Mrs. Davies – you know, the manager – she’s decided the mannequins need to be posing dramatically. Like,  really  dramatically. Spent half the day trying to get a sequined dress to stay on one of them. Sounds silly. It was. And then Barry, from menswear, kept complaining about how the positioning made the clothes look smaller. It was chaos. This remote isn't working, is it? No, it's stuck. Can I try? Be my guest, love. You’ve got a better knack for these things than I do. Seriously, what  is  with these remotes? You need a PhD to operate them. Aha! Got it! Brilliant! See? You’re better than Mrs. Davies and Barry put together. Do you think the people in the film… like, do you think they knew the food would turn into monsters? Hmm. That's a good question. Maybe. I think it’s about how we treat the planet, you know? If we keep taking and taking and not looking after it... Like with plastic? Exactly! Like with plastic and everything. That’s what it probably means. It's simple enough for kids to get, though, isn't it? Just a madcap adventure. I think it's about how if you eat too much, it grows really big and makes you explode. That’s a perfectly valid interpretation! See? You’re a proper film critic. It's wild how conversations have changed too, with social media. Everything's so... reactive.

Blimey, it's a bit bleak out there, eh, Paul? Not quite the sunny Mediterranean I'm used to these days. Aye, Finland in January ain't exactly postcard material, is it, Ste? You've landed yourself in a proper snow globe, lad. Still, gets you thinking, doesn't it? About the world. It does, it does. Had a rather interesting lecture today actually, about the impact of political climate on literary movements. Quite cyclical, really. Speaking of which, what do you make of this current situation back home? Feels like we’re in a right mess. Mess is putting it politely, Ste. A proper shambles. Remember New Labour? Thought we were finally getting somewhere, didn’t we? Tony Blair… seemed like he knew what he was doing. There was a certain optimism, wasn’t there? A feeling of proper progression. Though, even then, I had my reservations about the Iraq war. That cast a long shadow, didn't it? A fundamental shift, perhaps. Aye, gutted the country, that did. Promised us all the world, and what did we get? More division, more strife. Now look at it… Proper circus they’ve got going on. It's the general lack of accountability, isn’t it? Nobody seems to take responsibility for anything these days. The endless pointing fingers. What’s your take on the current lot in charge? Don't get me started. All talk, no action. Promises bigger than the Mersey Tunnel, and they can’t even manage the bins. Remember when they said they were going to fix the trains? Still waiting for that miracle, I am. Ah, the trains. A perennial source of frustration. Speaking of transport, how’s the taxi trade treating you these days, Paul? Rough out there? Footing's tough. Petrol's gone through the roof, costs are sky-high. People are moaning about everything, but nobody wants to pay a fair price for a ride. It's all "can you knock a quid off?" You try explaining economics to a customer complaining their coffee's cold. I can imagine. Still, you’re resilient, aren't you? Always have been. You’ve seen more changes than most, haven't you? From Liverpool docks to ferrying tourists around… Aye, seen it all. Heard it all, too. Some of the things you hear in a taxi… you wouldn’t believe. Just the other day, this bloke tried to convince me the moon was made of cheese.

Right, so I was trawling through the BNC recordings last night, classic Sunday evening, and I swear, I heard someone clear their throat  exactly  like my Nan used to. It was uncanny. Oh, you and the BNC! Honestly, you’re obsessed. Though, I can imagine. Nan clears her throat like a foghorn, doesn't she? Exactly! It’s this deep, rattling thing. Anyway, it got me thinking about how much language is tied to memory and place. Makes you feel…distant, somehow. Distant…yes. Sorry, were you following that? A little. Don't worry about it. Speaking of distant, have you seen Anya's LinkedIn? She's basically headhunting for a marketing job in the Maldives. Can you  imagine ? No way! The Maldives? That’s incredible. She’s always wanted to live abroad, hasn’t she? She has. Says she's craving sunshine and…pugs. Apparently, they’re huge in the Maldives. Pugs! Seriously? Who knew? I feel like she’s always moaning about spam on social media though. Is she going to be fine, being so far away from everyone? She's putting on a brave face. But she's visibly nervous. Keeps asking me about visiting London. She should come anytime! We'll hit up that Spanish tapas place we love. Tapas…good. She's terrified of flying, though. Which doesn’t exactly help her Maldivian dreams. I tried to tell her about those new planes with the noise-cancelling technology, but she just went pale. Oh, that’s rough. I'm not a huge fan of flying myself, to be honest. I get a bit jittery. Remember that time we were going to Spain and that turbulence? I thought we were going down. Oh god, yes! You were clinging to the armrests like your life depended on it. Armrests…safe. I was! Anyway, I was reading about whale migration patterns the other day. Apparently, some whales travel thousands of miles, just like Anya considering. It’s amazing, isn’t it? The instinct. It is incredible. Though, I'm not sure I’d trust my instincts to get me to the Maldives. I’d probably end up in Birmingham. Fair point! You’d just wander straight back to Abergavenny. Do you miss it? Sometimes. The scenery’s beautiful. It’s just…small. I need this chaos of London. Chaos…interesting. I get that. It's weird thinking about it though, all these people impulsively deciding to move halfway across the world.

So, you still thinking about that hummingbird tattoo? You were going on about it last week. Absolutely. I've been looking at references. Small, on the wrist, you reckon? Not too… obvious? Wrist’s good. Subtle, but still pretty cool. Not like that weird abstract thing Liam got. Honestly, looked like someone threw paint at him. Oh, don’t remind me. He seemed so proud of it. Anyway, dinner’s almost ready. Chicken tagine tonight, thought we’d try that new recipe. Sounds amazing! You’ve been on a roll with these recipes, Mum. Seriously, you should think about starting a blog. Don’t be silly. I’m far too busy. Though, managing the interns at the publishing house is a full-time job in itself. They seem to think proofreading involves scrolling Instagram. Classic. Are you finally getting around to tackling the bathroom renovation? You mentioned it ages ago. Slowly but surely. Found a fantastic tile supplier in Shoreditch. Bit pricey though. Trying to convince myself it’s an investment. Hello! Smells incredible in here! Sorry I’m late, the Overground was a nightmare. Hey! Come in, come in! We were just about to eat. Mum's made tagine – it smells unreal. Amazing! Right on time. So, Christmas - have you started thinking about it at all? Don't even mention it. It's barely November! But yes, I’ve been looking at flights to see your dad. And trying to avoid all the tat in the shops already. It’s like they start selling Christmas decorations in July these days. Tell me about it. Work is already ramping up for Christmas. The publishers are panicking about hitting targets. So much pressure. What’s the deal this year? Any big releases you’re working on? Yeah, a few. There's this young fantasy author who's really promising, and a biography of… well, you probably won't have heard of him, a fairly niche historical figure. Lots of late nights ahead, I reckon. Oh, stop stressing already! You need to relax. What about your Christmas plans? Any cheeky little getaways? I’m trying to keep it low-key this year. Maybe just a few days in the Cotswolds with a good book and escaping all the madness. You know, recharge the batteries. Sounds perfect. You deserve it. Anything exciting happening with you, Mum? Besides battling the interns and designing bathrooms? Well, I did finally finish reading that manuscript I was telling you about.

So, you said you were thinking of going to Morocco? Tell me everything! I’ve always wanted to go. I know, right? I've been obsessively looking at flights. Found some really cheap ones for October, just after my birthday. Marrakech, mostly. I'd love to do a desert trek though, even just a short one. Ooh, a desert trek! That sounds incredible. Get loads of sun and sand. Are you going with anyone? I’m trying to convince Sarah and Tom. They’re a bit… hesitant. Tom’s worried about the food. You know him, always fixated on finding familiar things. He’d probably try to smuggle a tin of baked beans through customs. Honestly, Moroccan food is amazing! So colourful, so flavourful. I went to that little Lebanese place on the high street the other week, and it was almost exactly like what my aunt used to make. See, there’s no need to worry! You’ll be fine. I'm mostly excited about the souks – all the spices and lanterns and interesting fabrics. I need a new scarf, desperately. All mine are looking rather drab. Speaking of clothes, did you see that Zara sale preview? I'm tempted to get a few bits before everything disappears. I need something autumnal, something cozy. I’ve been really into oranges and browns at the moment. Oh, I saw it! I'm trying to resist, though. My wardrobe is overflowing. It's tempting to buy everything, isn't it? I told myself I was going to focus on capsule wardrobes, but... That’s a good plan in theory, but hard in practice. What do you think of this curry, by the way? I tried a new recipe. More chili than usual. It’s brilliant! Really spicy, exactly how I like it. You’re getting really good at this cooking thing. Remember when you used to burn toast? Oh, don’t remind me! It's definitely improved. I started those Pilates classes, which I think has helped me feel a bit more… energetic in the kitchen. Plus, being able to move properly means I can chop vegetables without nearly slicing my fingers off! Pilates! Good for you! I’ve been meaning to try a yoga class. My back has been killing me lately, probably all the sitting typing. You should! I find it really relaxing, even if I do look like a tangled pretzel half the time.

Honestly, that seminar today was brutal. I felt like I was talking to a wall. Did you have a better turnout? A little better, yeah. Still not stellar, though. Three students actually engaging with the material is a victory in my book these days. I tried a new approach with that Baudrillard reading, you know, engaging with memes… Oh god, you did? How did that go down? I can just picture it. Baudrillard and TikTok... Surprisingly well, actually. They actually debated the idea of simulation – well, some of them did. It was a risk, but I thought it might grab their attention. It’s getting harder to get them to concentrate, isn't it? It is. They're all just… glazed over, half-listening to something else. Perhaps we need to integrate a compulsory nap into the curriculum. Now there's an idea! Though I suspect the union would have something to say about that. Speaking of things that need attention... Have you managed to get those toe nails done yet? You were complaining about them last week. Not yet, no. They're still a disaster. I really should book something. I keep putting it off. It feels so… frivolous when there’s so much marking to do. Frivolous? Self-care isn’t frivolous, darling. It's essential. You’ll end up snapping one if you don’t. You're probably right. Alright, I'll book something. What about Sarah and Ben? Have you heard from them recently? Not for a while. I saw a picture of their little Leo on Facebook - he’s getting so big! Still rocking the dinosaur phase, apparently. Oh, adorable. I must message Sarah. We should try and meet up soon. It feels like ages since we've all been out together. Definitely. We could do that Thai place on Elm Street next week? That sounds lovely. I'll reach out to Sarah and see what she thinks. I bet she’s just swamped at the moment, with Leo and everything. Yeah, probably. It's always something with little ones, isn't it? Still, those dinner parties are the best. Just need to convince Mark to hold back on the political debates this time. Oh, that'll be a challenge. Let's just hope he remembers we're all exhausted from marking essays. Fingers crossed. Shall we grab some takeaway coffee around the corner? My brain needs a boost.

Honestly, I still can't believe what happened with that actor, you know, Daniel… something. Daniel something-Jones. Jones, yeah. The one from that historical drama? It's all over the news, isn't it? Pretty shocking stuff. Shocking is an understatement. Apparently, he's been involved in some, well, let’s just say unsavoury incidents for years, and it’s only just all coming out. It makes you wonder what else we don’t know about these people, doesn’t it? It does. The curated image we have of celebrities… it’s so far removed from reality. It’s almost a performance in itself. Reminds me of that documentary,  Fyre: The Greatest Party That Never Happened.  Total fabrication. Oh, I loved that! The level of delusion was astonishing. Makes you question everything you see online. Which, let's be honest, is pretty much everything. Exactly. It's horrifying, really. Makes you almost long for the days of simpler news. You know, newspaper headlines and that's it. Speaking of simpler times, did you catch that old episode of  Absolutely Fabulous  re-aired the other day? Pure genius. Still so funny. I did! Patsy and Eddy are timeless, aren’t they? My daughter, Chloe, was laughing so much. She’s only fourteen, but she gets it. It’s one of those shows that just gets better with age. Reminds me of having everything on VHS in the 90s, hunting for an episode. Remember doing that? Oh god, yes! Rewinding to find the beginning again. And the video quality... ugh! Though, thinking about Chloe, are you still happy with her school? She seemed a bit…uninspired last time we spoke? It's a mixed bag, really. The teachers are fantastic, absolutely dedicated, but the curriculum is… well, it's a bit rigid. I'm trying to encourage her to pursue some extra-curriculars, maybe the pottery club she mentioned. Pottery's a good one. Gets the creativity flowing. My business partner, Ben, does it to de-stress. He swears by it. It’s ironic, isn’t it? A high-powered company director needing to mold clay. That’s brilliant! You know, sometimes I feel like I need to de-stress by yelling at conjugations. Teaching French can be surprisingly intense. I can imagine! Speaking of intense, my brother's still going on about the moon landing conspiracy. Absolutely convinced it was filmed in a Hollywood studio.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? I’m bored. Now, lass, we’ve only been driving for three hours. Cornwall’s a fair distance, you know. Remember what they say – "a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step." I know, but it’s all just… green. And grey. And sometimes brown. I’ve seen enough fields to last me a lifetime. Look! See that field over there? It's got all those wildflowers. See the blue ones? They’re cornflowers, I think. And those really bright yellow ones, that are buttercups. Makes it a bit more interesting, doesn't it? I guess so. It reminds me a bit of the Wizard of Oz, all the fields of poppies. Except less… vibrant. You always did like that film, didn’t you? I remember taking you to the cinema when you were little, and you insisted on wearing your Dorothy dress. Oh, God, don't remind me. Mum took loads of pictures. I bet she still has them somewhere. Probably buried under a mountain of old school reports! Speaking of which, are you reading anything good at the moment? Sherlock Holmes still capturing your interest? Yeah, I’m trying to get through  The Sign of Four . It's good, but a bit slow sometimes. I wish they’d written it like Lewis Carroll. All the wordplay and nonsense… it’s much more fun. True, but Carroll wasn't exactly known for plot-driven narratives, was he? Still, I remember playing with Morse code with your grandad. He was fascinated by all that communication stuff. Telegraphs, telegrams, even Braille. Really? I didn’t know that. Did he ever teach you? Tried to, but I’m not sure I ever grasped it properly. Took me a while to understand what all the flashing lights meant. Like those wind turbines we passed earlier, and the way the road winds. That reminded me of the Jamaica Inn. The Daphne du Maurier one? Oh yeah, I’ve read that. Really spooky. It is. Gets you thinking about how people communicated back then. No instant texts, no quick emails. A telegram was a big deal. True! Speaking of texts, did you get that message from Chloe about the beach hut? Ah yes, she says it needs a good sweep out before we get there. Apparently, the wind's been blowing sand everywhere. We’re making good time, though.

Right, so I was wrestling with this annotation error all afternoon. It’s a tricky one, turns out the corpus is riddled with regionalisms I hadn't accounted for. Like, apparently, “neb” means something entirely different in Newcastle than it does here in the South West. Neb? Like a fog? I remember the fogs in Manchester, thick as pea soup they were. Couldn’t see your hand in front of your face. Used to walk to the station in complete darkness. That sounds unpleasant, Grandad. Though I’m used to pretty bad fog myself, living down in Dorset. It rolls in off the sea, completely obscures everything. It is a nightmare for the corpus, honestly. The nuances are just… immense. Anyway, enough about my linguistic woes, what have you two been up to? Dad, you were saying you finally got around to sorting out the car? Yeah, the old Volvo needed a bit of a service. Took it to that garage just outside Wincanton, the one with the incredibly friendly mechanic. You know, the one who always offers me a cup of tea and gives me a ridiculously long explanation of what he’s doing. Petrol stations used to be different, you know. Proper little shops. You could get sweets and newspapers and even a bottle of milk. Not just petrol and impulse-buy chocolate now. True! Sometimes I miss those little roadside shops. Remember that one near Stockton-on-Tees, with the unbelievable selection of cheese? You and your cheese! Speaking of which, are we having your famous Sunday roast tonight, Elly? Absolutely! I’m doing lamb, with all the trimmings. I even managed to find some proper Yorkshire puddings, not those soggy, pale things you get in the supermarket. Yorkshire puddings… reminds me of playing marbles with the lads down the street. Cheating, of course. Always cheating. My best mate, Arthur, he’d put his hand on the ground and shift the marbles when nobody was looking. That's classic. I'm terrible at board games, I always get accused of strategic advantage. I’m just trying to  play . You're a menace, Dad. You’re always angling for an advantage. Remember when we were kids and you'd rig Monopoly? It wasn’t rigging! It was… innovative resource management. Right. Anyway, I was thinking, maybe we could go to the cinema next week? They’ve got that new war film on.

Honestly, darling, the train journey was dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. Delays everywhere. I ended up feeling quite travel-sick. Oh, Mum, I’m so sorry to hear that. Were you alright when you got here? You look a bit pale. Jet lag hitting you hard? A bit. It’s that crossing time zones, you know. Takes its toll. But I’m fine now, especially with a proper cup of tea and you here. Did you manage to get those shelf brackets I asked for? Yep, got them. They're in the hall. Also grabbed a new set of light bulbs, the ones you said were a better colour temperature. Trying to get the flat ready, you know? Good lad. Honestly, this moving business is stressful. I've been making lists – endless lists! You wouldn’t believe the amount of stuff I’ve accumulated over the years. Do you remember that hideous ceramic cat your father bought me in Skegness? How could I forget? It was lurking in every corner for decades! You finally got rid of it, though. Eventually. But there's still so much. I found an old photo the other day – remember David from university? The one who tried to be a poet? Vaguely. He was a bit… intense, wasn’t he? Wore a lot of scarves, if I recall correctly. Intensely pretentious! He sent me a poem once, a truly dreadful ode to a sardine. Never could remember his last name. Anyway, it made me think, where are all those people now? Life moves on, doesn't it? It certainly does. How’s Carol doing? I haven’t heard from her in ages. Carol's… well, Carol’s Carol. Still adamant she’s going to be a famous landscape painter, despite never having exhibited anything. Her daughter’s getting married next year, apparently. Big, extravagant affair. Oh, lovely! Will you be going? I’m trying to. It's just… getting around these days isn't as easy as it used to be. My knee's been playing up again. The doctor says it’s arthritis. Nasty business that. Have you been doing those exercises he showed you? Sporadically, darling, sporadically. Easier said than done, bending down to pick things up. Remember that time we were on holiday in Cornwall and I brushed against a weaver fish? Oh my goodness, how could I forget? You were convinced you were going to need stitches!

Honestly, look at that fella's clematis. Proper jungle, isn't it? Could be worse. Could be like your mum's greenhouse, a blooming rainforest. Aye, she goes mad for it, doesn't she? It’s a project, that’s for sure. I'm just trying to keep this spider plant alive. It's a challenge. You’ll get there. Plants are tricky. I’m still mourning my aloe vera…it just went brown and crispy. Oh no! That’s the worst. I read somewhere you're supposed to water them like, twice a year. I’m probably drowning mine. That sounds about right. So, did you see what they’re saying about the A-Level reforms? Absolute madness. I did! They’re basically making it harder just to prove they’re academically rigorous, aren't they? It’s just going to disadvantage students from less privileged backgrounds even more. Exactly! Access to resources, tutoring – it’s all going to become even more of a factor. It’s just perpetuating the cycle. It's awful. My little cousin’s doing Maths next year, and she’s already stressed enough. Doesn't need this on top. Speaking of stressful…did you hear about the petrol crisis? Don’t even get me started! I nearly cried when I saw the queues at the Esso down the road. I had to cancel that trip to London. Insane, isn’t it? Seems like a perfect storm of everything. Labour shortages, Brexit…the lot. It is proper bizarre. I was thinking about that documentary we watched the other week, about how essential workers were treated during the pandemic. It just feels like people are still being… taken for granted. Absolutely. The NHS is still creaking under the pressure. I read somewhere they're delaying non-urgent operations again. It breaks my heart. My friend's sister's been waiting over a year for a hip replacement. It’s not fair. I saw some poor NHS worker on the telly yesterday, looking absolutely burned out. It's not sustainable. Something has to change. But what? It feels like we’re just circling the same arguments. On a slightly less depressing note, I’m thinking of getting a fringe. I saw this girl on TikTok with a really neat, blunted fringe. A fringe? You? Are you sure? You’ve always rocked the longer style. I know, I know!

Honestly, I'm proper skint this month. Between rent and lectures, it's brutal. Tell me about it. I’m dipping into savings just to cover food. Uni's expensive, innit? Seriously! I'm working shifts at the supermarket every weekend, and it’s still barely enough. You two thinking about summer jobs? Definitely. I'm applying for everything, even the ones I'm wildly unqualified for. Gotta get that cash flow moving. I might look into something at the farm back home. Steady work, alright wages. But ugh, Yorkshire in summer… it’s either blazing or pouring. You’re lucky to have that option! My mum says I need to get a proper job, not just “freelance writing and existential dread”. Existential dread is a valuable skillset! Especially for English Lit. True. Though, I'm finding the lectures a bit dry this term. Wish we had a cool professor like in those American movies. Yeah, and one who doesn't spend half the time ranting about the Black Plague. Honestly, it’s all we’ve talked about in history for weeks. Mr. Davies is obsessed. He genuinely thinks it's relevant to modern political discourse. He’s lost the plot, honestly. Though, thinking about it, maybe it is relevant - overpopulation, disease, societal collapse... Woah, heavy. Let's not go there. Anyone fancy a brew? Ooh, yes please. Strong one. I'm in. Right, speaking of heavy things... did anyone hear about that article about intersectional feminism and financial inequality? Vaguely. Something about how women of colour face even more barriers in the workplace? Yeah, it was proper eye-opening. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It does. But it also makes you want to throw your hands up and just live in a cottage somewhere, knitting jumpers and avoiding the patriarchy. Tempting. But who’d pay for the cottage? We’d all chip in! Cottage commune, with a shared veggie patch and a fierce commitment to dismantling capitalism. I'm down for the veggie patch. But dismantling capitalism? That’s a bit ambitious for a Tuesday afternoon. Besides, someone's gotta buy the tea bags. And I'm already broke. Good point. Alright, cottage commune on hold. Tea first. And then maybe we can all just agree to collectively  not  smoke anymore. I’m worried about Sarah starting again. Yeah, she looked stressed last week. Maybe we should check in with her.

It’s just… vast, isn’t it? Sometimes feeling like this - this expanse – makes you think about… well, everything. Even friendships. Don't start, please. I’m already feeling a bit… reflective, if you know what I mean. No, no, don’t misunderstand. It's just... have you ever felt like you needed to gently… phase someone out? Phase out? Like, ghost them? Because honestly, I've done that. Not proud of it, felt incredibly guilty afterwards, but yeah. A few times. Usually when things have genuinely become toxic. Exactly, the toxicity part is important. I’m not talking about a full-blown, screaming-match kind of toxic. More… a gradual drifting apart, but one where you just… don’t feel the same pull anymore. And you know, continuing the friendship feels… draining. I get that. It’s weird, isn’t it? Because you’ve got history. You’ve shared experiences. It feels rude to just… cut ties. Precisely! And I overthink it. Like, am I being a bad friend? Am I overreacting? Should I just try harder? You always do that. Always questioning. Look, friend relationships are like any other, they evolve. People change. Sometimes, you just… grow in different directions. And there’s nothing wrong with that. But how do you  do  it? Without hurting their feelings massively? Without an awkward conversation? I’m thinking about Sarah, specifically. We’ve been friends for ages. But… the last few years, every conversation feels like an obligation. Ugh, Sarah. Right. Okay, so, direct confrontation is rarely the answer, unless it's genuinely necessary. Gradual withdrawal is key. Less contact. Less availability. Short, polite replies. But subtle isn’t really my forte, is it? I tend to be pretty… obvious. That’s true. Try focusing on your own life. Make it  look  like you’re just busy. New hobbies, volunteering, whatever. If she asks, you’re just swamped. And what if she presses? Gets suspicious? That’s when you use the vague excuse. “Things are just a bit hectic right now," or "I'm trying to prioritize my wellbeing.” Things like that. Don't over-explain. The more you explain, the more suspicious she'll be. It feels… manipulative. It’s not about manipulation, it’s about self-preservation. You’re not obligated to maintain a friendship that’s no longer serving you. And honestly? Most people subconsciously pick up on these cues anyway.

This lentil soup is amazing, Grandma. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, you’re just being kind, darling. It’s a very old recipe. My mother used to make it. From Vienna, you know. Proper Austrian lentil soup, not like these pale imitations you get these days. I can taste the difference. It’s got depth. So, how are you feeling? Really feeling? Much better, thank you. The arthritis was playing up a bit last week, but it’s subsided. I’ve been spending my time in the studio, trying to finish that series of watercolours I was telling you about. The ones of the Venetian canals? Are they going well? They’re…developing. It's difficult to capture the light, you know. The way it shimmers on the water. It's a constant battle. I think I’ve finally found a technique that works, though. A little layering with pastel, you see. I'd love to see them. When do you think they'll be ready for an exhibition? Well, I’m hoping to show them at the gallery in Chelsea in the spring. It’s a bit ambitious, but I’m trying. They said they'd be interested, at least. They showed me a new artist last week. Quite good, really. Very abstract, but intriguing. That's fantastic. So, uni's going well? Still enjoying the literature course? It sounds wonderful, all that talk of clever people and clever books. Tell me, what are you reading at the moment? Anything that’s truly gripped you? Actually, I just finished "One Hundred Years of Solitude." It was incredible. So dense, but so beautiful. It’s completely changed the way I think about storytelling. Oh, Marquez! Yes, I’ve read him, of course. A brilliant man. Such a vivid imagination. Do you think you’ll go back to Italy anytime soon? I’d love to. Rome especially. I said I'd go this summer but it just hasn't felt right. Exam stress, and then work. Perhaps next year. Italy is always a good idea. My sister is still living in Florence, you know. You must go and see her. She’d love to see you. I definitely will. I have been meaning to call her actually. I've been so busy I've not had the time. She's a lovely woman, your aunt Maria. She makes the most wonderful pasta.

Bit quiet in here, isn't it? After all that gym talk. Just absorbing the scenery, I think. Poland’s… surprisingly calming. And I'm trying to figure out the best route into Tarnow. Google Maps is being dodgy. Calmness is rarely a feature of my inner monologue these days. Still, nice to have a moment. Remember when you first started teaching? You were so stressed about every tiny detail. I  was  a mess. I felt like I had to be perfect. Every lesson plan, every activity… God, I was exhausting myself. And the kids could tell. They always do. You can’t fake easy, love. Especially not with teenagers. You either have the confidence or you don’t, and you learn it on the job. Exactly. I'm much better at just…rolling with it now. Letting the lesson go where it needs to go. It’s freeing. You know, it’s funny… I often think about how when I was back home, even with my Master’s, I still felt this pressure to prove myself, especially being a woman in teaching. Oh, goodness. Don't even get me started. They call it a ‘female profession’ don’t they? As if that's a compliment. It’s still riddled with subtle - and not so subtle - sexism. It is. I’ve had parents questioning my authority, assuming I’ll be leaving to have kids any minute now. I had one bloke actually say to me, "Are you sure you can handle a class of twenty ten-year-olds, love? Seems a bit much for a girl.” Honestly. The cheek of some people. It’s absurd. The world's convinced we’re delicate flowers, incapable of anything serious. Even something as simple as driving a campervan across Europe evidently.
