Speaking of driving…are you feeling okay to keep going, or should I take over? It’s getting a bit later, and I'm not sure how much further we’ve got. Nah, no. I’m fine. Just thinking. It’s good to get away, isn't it? Just… drive. Gets the cobwebs out. Sometimes I just need to escape all this. Escape's a good word for it. Reckon we should've stopped for something to eat before we did the gym thing today? I'm regretting not grabbing a pierogi. Now you’re talking. Pierogi are essential Polish cuisine. Clearly, my priorities are slightly skewed right now.

This coffee's lovely, Mum. Really good. And these mugs are just perfect, aren't they? Proper hand-thrown feel to them. Aye, they are bonny mugs, lass. Proper weight to 'em. You've got a good eye for things, you always did. Fancy a bit more milk? Please. The weather's been playing proper games this week, hasn't it? Beautiful sunshine one minute, then sudden showers. It is that. Aye. Like someone flickin' a switch. I saw a spider this morning, huge thing, scuttling across the window. Gave me a right fright! Oh, spiders! I hate them. Not brave enough to shoo them out. I just sort of…edge away. How’s the garden looking? Did you manage to deadhead the roses? Aye, I got to ‘em. They were a bit sad-looking, like, needed a bit of a tidy. The lavender's doing well though, smells lovely. Still, there’s always something to do, isn’t there? Never a rest for the wicked gardener. Never! I’ve been trying to get the climbing roses trained up the archway. They’re being terribly stubborn this year. Roses are like that, always having a mind of their own. Remember old Mrs. Featherstone down the road? She had the most magnificent roses, but she’d be out there every day, wrestling them into shape. I do recall! We had that power cut last Tuesday, didn't we? The whole street went dark. Oh, I remember that! Sat in the garden with a candle, watching the birds. A whole flock of starlings, all chattering away. Lovely sight, really. It was rather peaceful, actually. Though I couldn’t cook tea, of course. Ended up with cold sandwiches. You’ll be painting the garden room then, I reckon? I saw you eyeing up the colours the other day. I am. Thinking of a soft grey. Something calming. It's looking a bit drab at the moment. Do you remember Margaret and Arthur? From the WI? Aye, Margaret and Arthur. Lovely couple. Haven't seen 'em in ages. Arthur's not been well, has he? Not great, apparently. Keeps having falls. Poor Arthur. I was thinking about going to that little folk festival in Saltaire next month. Fancy coming? Oh, I don't know about that, lass. My knees aren’t what they used to be. Plus, I nearly took a tumble on the stairs yesterday.

So, have you booked the ferry yet, Granpappy? Aye, lass. Got it sorted. Dover to Calais, leaving the 18th. Nice and early, too. Don't want any queues. That’s brilliant, Dad. Thanks for sorting that. I was getting a bit anxious about it. Are we still going to that campsite near the beach? The one with the slides? Aye, the Camping Municipale in Le Touquet. You loved it last time. You were obsessed with those slides, sweetheart. Spent the whole week on them. They were epic! Can I take Chloe and Maya this time? Well, let me check with their parents, love. It’s a bit far for a day trip, isn’t it? Please, Mum? It would be so much fun. We could build sandcastles and go crabbing. Crabbing’s good fun, that is. Remember that little crab you caught last time, Elsie? Thought it was going to pinch your finger. Oh yeah! It  did  pinch me! It was tiny but strong. You were screaming the house down. Honestly. I was seven! Still, gave us a laugh. Right, so what about your French, Elsie? Are you practicing? I'm trying, Dad. Duolingo every morning. It's slow going though. I learned 'Bonjour' and 'Merci'! See? You're getting there. Little bit of effort goes a long way. Maybe we should get a phrasebook, too. Just to be on the safe side. Don’t need one! I’m fluent.  Bonjour!  You’re a little comedian, you are. What about activities? Are you still wanting to go to the market in Boulogne, Dad? Definitely. Always good for a bit of bargain hunting. And I’m hoping to get a bit of inspiration for some new tunes. That little cafe over looking the harbour... perfect spot. Can we get some Belgian chocolates? The ones with the caramel? Of course, love. We’ll get you a whole box. Are you getting excited now? Yep! France, here I come! 슬라이드! Sliders, not 슬라이드! Sorry, Granpappy. Old habits. Right, well I’ll start making a list of what we need to pack. Sunscreen, definitely. And Elsie, don’t forget your swimsuit! Can I bring my new headphones? Sure darling. You take care of those dear they cost a fortune. I'll make a list, I'll get the suncream in. Wooo! France! Quite right lass. France. All these years it has done me well and I've gone out and seen so many friends still out there.

Okay, so Heath Ledger. Seriously.  10 Things I Hate About You  is just…  chef’s kiss . I know, right?! I was not prepared for how romantic it would be. And Julia Stiles is amazing. Totally. I feel like I need to rewatch all of Heath Ledger's films now. Definitely. So, massively distracted from actual life stuff though, aren't we? Like, school. Ugh, don't remind me. History essay due on Monday. I haven't even started. Seriously? I finished mine on Tuesday! It was actually quite good. I wrote about the suffragettes. See, you're a star! I’m struggling to even  think  about the Tudors right now. It all just seems so… dusty. Maybe if you break it down? Just a little bit each evening? I guess. But I’m so behind on maths too. Mrs. Davies is being particularly brutal this year. Tell me about it! I had to stay after school yesterday just to get her to explain one question to me. Seriously? What was it? Maybe she explained it to you better than she did to me. It was some stupid algebraic equation. Honestly, why do we need to know that? I know, right? Like, when are we ever going to use that in real life? Exactly! I’m going to be a vet, not an accountant. True! Speaking of real life, are we still on for that trip to London next month? Definitely! Mum’s booked the train tickets, and she’s looking at hotels. Oh, brilliant! I'm so excited. Where are we thinking of going? Well, obviously the British Museum. And I really want to see Wicked in the West End. Ooh, Wicked! Yes! And we have to go to that cute vintage shop in Notting Hill. Absolutely! And maybe grab a ridiculously overpriced coffee somewhere. Perfect! It's going to be so good to get away from Cambridge for a bit. I know! And a break from school. We both deserve it. Definitely. Plus, you promised me we’d try that new bubble tea place near Oxford Street. Oh yeah! How could I forget? It's a deal. Bubble tea and London adventures! Best. Trip. Ever. Now, back to trying to understand something a Tudor did… Wish me luck. You got this! And if you're really struggling, send me a message. I’ll try and help. And then we can dream about Heath Ledger some more.

Right then. This chamomile's quite pleasant, isn't it? Less strong than that peppermint you brewed last week, dear. Almost caused a fit, that did. Oh, don’t be silly, Arthur. It was perfectly mild. You're just being dramatic again. Did you see Margaret's post on Facebook? No, what did she post? Well, she's claimed she’s seen a ghost in her shed. A right goosebumps picture it was, all blurry and grey. Margaret and ghosts. Classic. Probably just the shadows from the overgrown ivy. Shadows, aye. That's the modern explanation, isn't it? Never used to be shadows, you know. Used to be fairies and sprites and things. Grandad, you're drifting off again. What was I saying? Oh, right, Facebook. I’ve been trying to scrub my feed of all political nonsense. It just gives me a headache. I know exactly what you mean. My niece, Bethany… she gets into the most dreadful arguments online. All caps and exclamation marks. Wanting to tell everyone what to think. It’s the anonymity, isn’t it? People saying things they’d never say face-to-face. Used to be a neighbour of mine, Ethel, she was like that. Always wanting to tell everyone how to run their lives. She even used to lecture me on how to trim my roses. Roses! I never grew roses. Oh, Ethel. Remember when she tried to convince us all to join that… what was it called? The Divine Pilgrims? The Divine Pilgrims! The cult that wore those awful purple robes and tried to sell you pamphlets about interdimensional beings. I think I remember something about that. My dad used to say they were trouble. Trouble, indeed. I remember little Timothy Henderson getting chicken pox at one of their meetings and Ethel blaming it on the Devil. Oh, heavens. Poor Timothy. He was covered from head to toe. I felt so sorry for his mother. It's funny, isn’t it? How people attach meaning and blame to things. I read an article the other day about OCD. It's not just about handwashing; it's about this overwhelming compulsion to control everything. Yeah, I've read about that. It's pretty debilitating. My colleague, Daniel, he’s got it quite badly. He spends hours checking his work. Checking, aye. Always wanting to be right. My late wife, bless her soul, she was like that.

Right, so dinner’s nearly ready. Who’s feeling hungry? Starving! What’s cooking, Mum? Smells amazing. Something good, I hope! My stomach's been rumbling since lunchtime. Head of Department duties, you know. Always on the go. Just finished up a quick edit. Smells lovely! Are we having roast potatoes? Just finished sanding down some silver. Need to refuel. Roast potatoes would be a dream. Evening, everyone. Looks like a lively gathering as usual. What's on the menu tonight? It’s roast chicken, roast potatoes, carrots, peas… the works. Proper Sunday dinner. Oh, perfect! Remember that time we went to Germany and tried to order roast chicken, and it came out as… something completely different? Don’t remind me! My German is appalling. I think I accidentally asked for a plate of pickled onions! It was hilarious! And the waiter looked so confused. Dad, your accent didn't help. Hey, I was trying my best! It’s a difficult language. All those umlauts! I remember that trip. We were trying to find the autobahn, and ended up completely lost in a tiny village. We were. Your dad kept insisting he knew the way, even though we were driving in circles. Those were the days. Remember that old Ford Cortina? Your father adored that car. Always tinkering with it. Oh god, yes! The one that constantly broke down on the way to school. I spent half my childhood waiting on the side of the road. It was a classic, though. A proper workhorse. Remember the colour? That awful green? Horrible shade of green. But somehow, it was iconic. Like a family heirloom. It was. I do miss it sometimes. Simple times. Though I’m glad we upgraded to something a bit more reliable! Reliable?! We had a brand new Volvo after that Cortina! Luxury. Speaking of the old days… remember young Emily down the road, trying to learn French with that ridiculous accent? Oh my god, yes! She sounded like a cartoon! It was the worst. She practiced in the street, just shouting French phrases at the lampposts. She probably ended up being fluent just from sheer determination. Dinner’s ready! Everyone, grab a plate. Let's reminisce some more after we've eaten. Sounds good to me. Always a pleasure to be home. Agreed. Although, I expect a challenging discussion to arise at some point. This is a family gathering, after all.

Hey! Good to see you, man. Been ages. Didn’t realize Devon was this… green. Yeah, it's perpetually damp. Good to see you too, Liam. Grab a seat. Mum's just put on some soup. Soup sounds amazing. University food wasn't exactly a culinary adventure. So, what have you been up to? Still slinging pans? Yep, still at The Salty Crab. Honestly, it's a bit of a chaotic whirlwind most days, but I’m loving it. Really learning stuff, you know? Proper practical skills. That’s brilliant. I keep reading about how valuable internships are in my uni course, but actually doing the work… that’s a whole different ballgame. Seriously. Watch out for that. You’ll be pulling 14-hour shifts and scrubbing floors before you know it! But the food, man... you get to make proper good food. What about you? Still buried in books? Pretty much. Semester's been mad busy. We’ve got this huge project on contemporary music production - it’s actually pretty interesting. Oh yeah? What bands are you looking into? Loads, but right now I’m obsessed with Dry Cleaning. Their live shows are insane, so raw and energetic. Have you heard them? Dry Cleaning, yeah! I’ve heard a few tracks. Bit quirky, aren’t they? I’m more into heavier stuff, you know? Been listening to a lot of Royal Blood recently. Royal Blood are great! That bass tone… unreal. I saw them live last year, it was mental. What about albums? Anything good come out that you've been spinning? Actually, yeah. Little Simz's new one, 'NO THANK YOU'. Absolutely stunning. Been on repeat all week. The production is phenomenal. Have you checked it out? No, I haven't! I'll have to add it to the list. I just got the new IDLES album, ‘Tangk’, and I’m finding it a bit… divisive, I think. Some of it’s brilliant, some of it feels a bit forced. IDLES are always pushing boundaries, aren’t they? You gotta give them credit for that. So, what's the plan after uni? Got anything lined up? That's the million-dollar question, isn't it? Ideally, I’d love to get into music production somehow. Maybe assist on some studio sessions, build up my portfolio. But the competition is ridiculous. Yeah, it is. But you’re talented, Liam.

Honestly, this place is absolutely buzzing, isn’t it? Can barely hear myself think. Nah, it’s alright, Mum. It's just a bit busy. Loads of people about. Busy is an understatement! Still, needed a coffee. Been running around like a headless chicken all morning. School trip logistics are a nightmare. What’s the plan for today then? You’ve got that meeting at Durham this afternoon, haven’t you? I do. Meeting about the new curriculum – you know how those things are. Endless discussions about outcomes and engagement. It'll be draining. Where are we with the shopping list? Nearly out of milk. Oh yeah, shopping list. I can grab some milk on the way home. And bread. And those weird oat biscuits you like. Bless you, love. You’re a lifesaver. So, any news from the uni? Still thinking about that engineering degree? Aye, yeah. Had another look at the syllabus. Seems pretty good. It’s just…expensive, isn’t it? Everything is these days. We’ll figure it out. Maybe you could look into those bursaries again? Or a part-time job? I’m looking. It's just…hard, innit? Everyone wants experience. How am I supposed to get experience if nobody gives me a chance? I know, it’s frustrating. But you've got that internship lined up for the summer, haven't you? With that company in Newcastle? Yeah, but it’s just…sleeping on a friend’s sofa all summer. It’s not ideal. And what about beds? We need a proper camping setup for that, don’t we? Sleeping bags, proper mattress. We'll sort it all out. Don't you worry. Maybe we should have a look at a loyalty promotion with Cotswold Outdoors, they put on real good deals. What did you think of the Footie last night? The lads played well. Didn’t watch it. Too busy doing homework. Did you see that story about obesity levels in kids? Worrying, that is. Dreadful. It’s a combination of things, isn’t it? Lack of exercise, poor diet. It's just so disheartening. That bloke in the drive-through window, he's got his voice really loud, Mum. Oh, he has, doesn't he? Sorry, I didn't even notice. Needs to tone it down a bit, doesn’t he? Aye, blaring out. Sorry dear, I didn't realise. I wasn’t really paying attention with all the noise… So, tell me more about this engineering course.

Cheers for coming down! It's good to finally see you outside of a Zoom screen, eh? Sussex is... well, it’s Sussex. Bit quiet, but nice. Yeah, brilliant to get out of Brum for a bit, honestly. The rain was proper relentless. Thanks for having me over, the flat’s looking good! You've really made it your own. Cheers, still got a few boxes to unpack, to be honest. Life’s been a bit hectic, you know? Recording that linguistics project took ages. Still doing the recordings then? Last time we spoke, you were wrestling with capturing the nuances of Shakespearean English. Still am! It's fascinating though. I actually recorded a bit on regional accents the other day – your accent’s surprisingly useful for that! You know, the subtle shifts in vowel sounds… Oh, don't start analyzing me, mate! I'm just a bloke from Bronsgrove. Got my head stuck in spreadsheets now, you know, Assurance Analyst. Glamorous, right? Spreadsheets! Sounds…adult. You look well though. So, what's the gossip? Still seeing Sarah? Yeah, Sarah’s doing brilliantly. Actually... she’s pregnant. No way! Seriously? Wow! That's amazing news! When's she due? December. We’re completely terrified, to be honest. Money’s been a bit tight thinking about all that, and the sheer responsibility of it all. I can imagine! We were just talking about money yesterday, actually. Trying to figure out a proper budget, living down here is surprisingly pricey. Tell me about it. Birmingham’s not exactly cheap, but Sussex is another level. How’s the salary treating you? It’s decent, enough for a flat and a few beers. Teaching’s rewarding, though, even if it doesn’t pay the bills like a proper corporate job. I still get a kick out of helping people learn English, especially the Spanish students. They’re so enthusiastic. That's great. We were thinking about a reunion actually, a few of us from uni. Did you hear back from Liam about getting something organised? I think he was trying to sort something out. He said it was tricky getting everyone confirmed, people’s lives get so complicated, don’t they? You know, mortgages, kids… Actually, talking about mortgages, have you and Sarah looked into that yet? We've started poking around, yeah. Joint bank account seems the sensible thing, doesn't it? Splitting the bills, saving for a deposit… it’s all a bit daunting.

Honestly, I still can't quite believe it. Just…gone. Poor David. And Sarah, of course. It’s just…unfair. I know, love. It’s shocking. I still keep expecting to see him pottering about the garden. Such a lovely man. Him and Margaret, you know, they were always so cheerful. They were. It’s just… Margaret's going to be devastated. They were inseparable. They did everything together. The kids...well, they're being strong, bless them, but you can see it. Absolutely. Poor kids. It's a huge thing to process at their ages. Are they alright practically? You know, with the arrangements and all that? Sarah’s managing, mostly. She’s trying to be strong for the boys. She's got Liam – he's handling it pretty well, surprisingly. But Finn… Finn’s struggling a bit. He’s always been closer to David. He keeps asking when Daddy’s coming back. Breaks your heart. It does. My Jake would do the same. I remember when… well, never mind. Anyway, is there anything you can do? Anything at all? I’m happy to help with things, you know. Picking up the boys, meals, whatever. That’s so kind of you, Becka. Honestly, just having someone to talk to is a huge help. I feel like I’m treading water sometimes. It’s just been…a lot. With the business and everything else. You’re doing amazing, Jo. Don't beat yourself up. You’re juggling so much. And don’t forget to look after yourself. Are you still seeing Sarah for those… sessions? Yeah, yeah, I am. It’s… it’s helping a bit. Mostly just having a safe space to let it all out, you know? I haven’t slept properly in weeks. Keep waking up in the middle of the night, just thinking… What if? I understand. Grief does that to you. It throws you around. It’s like being on a rollercoaster you didn't sign up for. Have you talked to the doctor about the sleep thing? I’ve considered it, but… I don't want pills. I'd rather try and sort it out myself, if I can. Honestly, just worried about everything – the boys, Sarah, Margaret… It's relentless. I know. It feels like you’re carrying the weight of the world sometimes. Look, I know you well, Jo. You’re a fiercely independent woman, but you can't do it all.

This is nice, isn’t it? Proper Sunday roast. It is. Though I’m having to fight for the good bit. Mark, stop reaching! It’s the best bit, Dad! I wish I’d had more gravy. More coming right up, love. So, how was tennis this morning? Did you actually manage to beat old Mr. Henderson this time, Tom? No way. He’s still got it. He served an ace right at match point. It was brutal. He's a tricky one, that Henderson. Years of experience. You need to work on your backhand. Perhaps you should join that coaching scheme Sarah’s been telling you about? I don’t know, Dad. It’s a lot of money. It’s an investment, Tom. And you're good at it. Remember that tournament you won last year? Remember that goal I scored yesterday? Proper screamer. Always bringing it back to football, don’t you, Ben? Well, it  was  a good goal! The keeper didn't even move. And how's school going? Exams looming, I presume? They are, yes. A bit stressful. Trying to think about apprenticeships as well, you know? Seeing what’s out there. I’ve been looking. My mate Liam’s doing an apprenticeship with a local garage. He says it’s surprisingly good. That’s a good shout. Practical experience is invaluable. Any interest in that tech stuff you were mentioning the other day, Mark? Investing in a small business? Yeah, there's this startup with an app that helps students manage their time. The guy's looking for investors. I've done some research – seems promising, but it’s a risk, obviously. An app? Sounds boring. Don’t be dismissive, Ben. It's the future! Your dad's got a good head for business, Mark. What do you think, love? It is tempting. The returns could be good, but it's crucial to weigh up the risks. I'm not going to throw all our savings at it, of course. Maybe just a small investment to start with. Remember the referendum, though? Everyone said leaving the EU was a sure thing. Let’s not go there, Tom. Dinner table politics are never a good idea. Can I have some more potatoes, please? Restraining your appetite for weeks so you can stuff your face at Sunday dinner, eh? Classic. Honestly, you’re all a bunch of characters.

This train's surprisingly busy for a Tuesday, isn’t it? I thought midweek travel would be quieter. Yeah, it is a bit of a squeeze. Are you excited for the Lancaster visit? It’s ages since you've seen your Auntie Carol. I know, it is! It's good to see her. And Uncle David, of course. It feels like forever. I’m mostly looking forward to getting some fresh air though. Are we thinking of popping over to the coast afterwards? Maybe Morecambe? Definitely. I've heard the sunsets are amazing from there. Though, apparently, the cockles are a bit of a disaster now. Did you see that article about the algal bloom? Oh no! Really? That's awful. I was looking forward to trying some. Guess we'll stick to fish and chips then. Proper chippy chips – I’m craving them already. Exactly! Lancaster has some good ones, I’ve heard. So, any news on your dissertation? You sounded stressed last time we spoke. Still…a work in progress, let’s just say. I’m finally refining the methodology, but the literature review feels endless. All this jargon… sometimes I wonder if I’ll ever be finished. I totally get it. Mine was the same. Trying to convince yourself that the ‘theoretical framework’ is actually  useful  and not just a pile of academic nonsense. Precisely! Are you any closer to deciding on your Master’s? Any particular universities you’re leaning towards? I've been looking at York and Sheffield. Sheffield has a really good linguistics department, apparently. But York’s campus is just beautiful. What about you? Still thinking Cambridge? I’m applying to Cambridge, but I'd also like to look at UCL. Always loved London, plus the research opportunities there are incredible. It’s all so overwhelming, isn't it? Thinking about the next stage. It is, but exciting too. Have you thought about what you actually  want  to do after? Career-wise, I mean. I’m leaning towards project management within a research setting. Something that uses my skills but also feels…meaningful. What about you? Still interested in working with vulnerable populations? Yeah, definitely. That's why I chose mental health nursing, you know? It’s tough, but it's incredibly rewarding. My mum’s been worried about me though, with all the pressure on the NHS. Oh, is she? It’s understandable.

Honestly, I'm still gutted Arctic Monkeys cancelled their gig. Proper bummer. Tell me about it! I managed to get tickets ages ago, been looking forward to it for months. What were you planning on wearing? Haha, you know. Something vaguely cool. Probably my vintage band tee, jeans, Converse. The usual. You? I was going for a full on 90s throwback. Grunge vibes. Flannel shirt, ripped jeans, the works. Would have looked proper mental. Would have been brilliant! Remember Liam's Halloween costume last year? He went as Kurt Cobain and nearly tripped over his own feet. Oh god, yeah! The poor thing. He spent half the night sprawled on the floor. Did you see Sarah’s Insta story from that festival last weekend? No, what? What happened? Don't leave me hanging! She was proper dancing with some random guy, covered in glitter. Looked like she was having the time of her life. I didn’t recognise him. No way! Sarah? Dancing? Glitter? That's not her usually. She's usually over in a corner chatting about… something very serious. Exactly! It was bizarre. I wonder who he was. Maybe a new boyfriend? Maybe! Or maybe she just decided to let loose and have some fun. Good for her, honestly. What are you doing this weekend, anyway? Aside from mourning the loss of the Arctic Monkeys, obviously. I'm thinking of finally getting round to finishing that Warhammer model I started ages ago. The one I showed you, the Space Marine? Oh yeah! The one that looks like he’s about to go into battle. It’s pretty impressive, if I remember right. Yeah, it is. Just need to paint the details. It’s surprisingly therapeutic, actually. You should try it sometime. Nah, I'm happy sticking to painting my nails. Less fiddly. I'm trying out this new holographic polish, it's insane. Holographic, eh? Bit flashy for my taste, but each to their own. Speaking of flashy, did you hear about Mark getting a new motorbike? No! Seriously? He's gone full biker now? I always thought he was more of a… a cardigan and comfy slippers kind of guy. Apparently, he's been saving up for ages. Reckons it’s his midlife crisis. Mark? A midlife crisis? That’s hilarious! He's only just turned twenty-four! He needs to calm down. Tell him yourself! I’m not saying anything.

Right, so I’m placing a research station in Atlanta. Gotta get a foothold there, right? Definitely. Atlanta's crucial. But leave a couple of cards in Chicago, too. We need to be able to fight off outbreaks over there. I’m going to focus on building immunity in Asia, seems like that's where the outbreaks are spiralling. You lot can deal with the Americas. I’m thinking yellow tiles. Easy for you to say, Mat. You're metres away from the medicine supply! I’m stuck here in Africa trying to coordinate everything. Sounds like the NHS during winter, doesn’t it, boyo? Chaos! Tell me about it. Remember that time at the hospital when… never mind. Not relevant. Are you lot sure you know what you’re doing? I’m just here for the biscuits and the moral support, really. We’re doing fine, Gwyn! Relax! We've got a strategy, sort of. Yeah, it's a strategy born of panic mostly, but it’s a strategy nonetheless! Panic is a good motivator. Speaking of motivating, anyone want more tea? I’ll pop the kettle on. I'm worried about Europe. They’re getting hit hard. We need to send someone, anyone, to boost their defenses. Ethan, you're closest. I'm already stretched thin handling the outbreaks in South America! I can barely keep my head above water as it is! Remember that time we were playing Monopoly and you got so frustrated, Olwen, you flipped the board? Dad, please don't bring that up. That was a dark day for family game nights. It was legendary! You were furious! You were throwing properties everywhere, weren’t you? Ended up with Brighton in the fish pond. Mid-game snack break! Right, refocus, people! We're on the brink of a global pandemic! And apparently, gluten-free biscuits are palatable this time. Progress! Okay, okay! Ethan, I need you to head to Europe. I’ll prioritize the research in Africa and see if I can get someone over to South America. Rhys, you’re on Asia lookout. Looks like I'm fighting a two-front war. Brilliant. Anyone got a spare outbreak card they can just... not  use? Always the optimist, aren't you, girl. You know, this is remarkably like council meetings, isn’t it? All arguing and squabbling, and nobody really knows what they’re doing.

Right, so, World Book Day is next week, isn't it? What are you two dressing up as? I'm going to be Little Red Riding Hood! With a big basket! I’m… a dinosaur! A T-Rex! Roar! A T-Rex! Fantastic! That's brilliant, darling. You’ll need a really big tail then. And what about a hat? Mummy, can I have a cape? A sparkly one! We’ll see, sweetheart. Let’s get through the dinosaurs first! We were also thinking of getting you a little book for your birthday, weren't we? Birthday! Yes, your birthday is just around the corner. We need to start thinking about what to do. I was thinking maybe a picnic in the garden, weather permitting, of course. Ooh! And a bouncy castle! A bouncy castle might be a  little  ambitious, darling. But we can see. What about a CBeebies pantomime? They’re doing one at the theatre in Cambridge, didn’t I tell you? Oh yes. It’s got Bluey and Bingo! Do you remember we watched that special episode with the shadow puppets? Yes! And Bluey said, "For real life?" And it was so funny! For real life! See? You remember! Remember what Grandma always says, ‘A child’s memory is like a sieve.’ But sometimes they remember the best bits, don’t they? Mummy, can we watch something on CBeebies now? Please? Always asking for the telly, aren’t you? Alright, alright. But just one episode. What do you want to watch? Storytime? Dino Dana! Dino Dana it is then. Though I still think you’d look rather good as a Very Hungry Caterpillar… No! Red Riding Hood! Alright, alright. You’re both set on your characters. And I need to look at something for Mother's Day. We need to send Grandma a card. Mummy, what's Mother’s Day? It's a day when we say thank you to all the lovely mums! And we give them flowers, and cards, and hugs. You’re the best mummy ever! Oh, you are sweethearts. Now, Dino Dana it is. And later we’ll read some stories and maybe plan some more birthday surprises. Let’s get comfy. Who wants a biscuit? Me! Me too! A chocolate one! Alright you two, settle down! Let's enjoy the show. Happy watching! Oh, this is nice. Just a peaceful afternoon with my little monsters.

This lentil soup is genuinely banging, you know. You’ve outdone yourself, Chloe. Thanks, Ben! Just fancied something comforting, thought it would be nice with this awful weather we're having. Still raining, isn't it? Absolutely pouring! Good thing we’re all tucked in, isn't it? I swear, it's non-stop drizzle. I almost wore my wellies this morning. Seriously. Ms. Wellies over here. You’re being dramatic, Sarah. Hey, it's London! Anything could happen! So, Ben, how’s the big engineering project going? Still wrestling with those hydraulics? Yeah, still a headache. The client keeps changing their mind about the specifications. It’s like herding cats, honestly. Keeps me on my toes though, I suppose. Sounds stressful. You should come away somewhere sunny when you get a chance. Get some proper relaxation. I know, I know. I've been looking at flights to Barcelona. Just need to clear this hurdle first. What about you, Chloe? Still loving the journalism world? It’s chaotic as ever, but good. Just finished a piece on that new eco-housing development. Surprisingly interesting, actually. Environmentally friendly housing, huh? Trying to convince yourself that the planet can be saved, are we? Something like that. It’s depressing sometimes, you know? All the doom and gloom. Tell me about it. I saw a thing online the other day about… I can't even remember what it was. Something about rising sea levels. Gave me the shivers. Oh, don't go there! I'm trying to enjoy my lentil soup! Speaking of, Chloe, have you had any luck with that dating app you were talking about? Oh god, don’t even ask. It’s a minefield. Met a guy last week who spent the entire lunch talking about his cryptocurrency portfolio. Classic. Honestly! What is it with men and their investments? It’s not captivating conversation. Tell me about it. And then there was the one who thought I was an influencer. Kept asking me to promote his… beard oil. No way! Oh, Chloe! You have the worst luck. Maybe you should just stick to meeting people the old-fashioned way. Like what? Stumbling into them at a library? Because that's about as likely as it raining sunshine. I don't know – maybe a pottery class? Or a hiking group? Something active, something with genuine interests. That's a good shout, Ben.

Right, so that was quite a discussion about "Pride and Prejudice," wasn’t it? I'm still trying to wrap my head around Mr. Darcy's initial demeanour. He was just so… standoffish. Absolutely, wasn't he? Though, I always felt it was more about his awkwardness than actual arrogance. A bit like Uncle Barry, really. All stiff upper lip and complicated tax returns. Remember those early attempts at build-a-bear. He used to meticulously plan every eyebrow on those little bears. Oh, God, yes! I remember Barry trying to build a Paddington bear and getting so frustrated when the fur wouldn't fluff up right! He was practically shouting at a teddy bear. It sounds about right. It's funny, isn't it, how some people just get so fixated on details like that? It reminds me of my dad trying to build Lego. He just couldn't follow the instructions - ended up with a wonky spaceship and a lot of frustration. My dad used to get like that with flat-pack furniture. He’d start determinedly, then end up muttering about Scandinavian design being a conspiracy. And always missing a screw. Speaking of childhood... I’ve just realised I was speaking practically all morning in dialect. Honestly, wasn't there, Em? I’d be surprised if you weren't. I know! It's ingrained, isn't it? I try and not in meetings, obviously, but the moment I'm relaxing with family...  'Y'know what I mean?'  It just comes out. My kids tease me about it constantly. That’s brilliant, isn’t it? You realize how much of your identity is wrapped up in language. I feel a bit guilty, actually. I’ve always tried to keep my Lincolnshire accent quite neutral, particularly at work. It’s probably made me sound a bit… bland. I think it's a tricky balance, isn't it? It’s good to be professional, but there's something lovely about embracing your roots. I think my Essex accent is probably more subtle. It comes out when I'm stressed, or when I'm talking to people from Essex. It’s kind of a safety mechanism, I guess. Definitely. Like a comfort blanket. What have you been up to at work, Sarah? Anything exciting happening in the world of accounts? It's been surprisingly busy. The new regulations are a nightmare, honestly. So much paperwork.

Right then, settle in, settle in! We've got loads to tell you about the Lake District. Honestly, it was just… stunning. Stunning is right, love. Best holiday we’ve had in ages. Didn't realise how much we needed to get away. That sounds amazing! So, where did you stay? Was it in one of those cute little villages? We were in Grasmere, actually. Proper postcard stuff. All stone cottages and little fellside paths. Brenda, you remember that Lakeland biscuit tin you had? It looked exactly like it. Oh yeah, the one with the sheep on it. And the smell! That whole village smelled like those biscuits, honestly. Must have been lovely. Did you do much walking? Oh, loads! We tackled Catbells. Bit of a climb, but the view from the top… wow. Just incredible. Took some photos, you’ll see. Though Peter kept getting in the way. I  wasn’t ! I was admiring the scenery. Right, Dad. Admiring the scenery while standing directly in front of Mum's photo shot. He was practically on the summit, waving his arms around. Scared all the sheep half to death. They were used to it, love. Used to tourists. Now, there was this one particularly cheeky sheep...it nicked my sandwich! No way! Happened exactly like that. Right out of your hand! He just looked at you, chewed, and then wandered off. Proper entitled, that sheep was. That’s brilliant. Did you see any other wildlife? We saw a red squirrel! Proper little flash of red darting through the trees. Peter almost tripped over a badger set trying to get a closer look. It was dark by then. He didn’t see it. Thank goodness. He'd have had a heart attack. This all sounds incredible. What about food? Did you eat anywhere particularly good? Oh, loads of good places. Had some excellent fish and chips by a lake. And a massive pot of tea. Brendan, you know how I love a good cuppa. The best! And we went to this little farm shop. Got some proper, proper jams and chutneys. You'll all be getting some when you come round. Awesome! Anything else particularly memorable? Well, we did get caught in a downpour one day. Absolutely torrential. We ended up huddled under a bus shelter, looking like drowned rats. And Peter was complaining the whole time. "It's raining, it’s cold, I’m hungry…" Honestly!

Morning, all. Anyone else feeling like they need a jolt after that Bollywood movie night? Morning! Definitely. My head’s still buzzing with all the colours and music. You alright, Liam? You look a bit…dazed. Morning! Liam, you look like you wrestled a tiger. Did you actually fall asleep face-down on the sofa again? Almost. I think a rogue cushion attacked me. Anyway, has anyone seen the news? Absolute chaos. Apparently, that MP’s embroiled in some massive scandal. Oh gosh, not again. The tabloids are going wild, I imagine. I saw a headline flash up while I was looking at recipes. Something about… offshore accounts? Standard stuff, really. Just another politician with their fingers in the pie. I'm trying to ignore it; it's depressing. Is that shakshuka you're making, Chloe? Smells amazing. Yeah, thought we could all use something vibrant this morning. Plenty of paprika and smoked paprika. Liam, you want some? Please. I need all the vibrancy I can get. This week at work has been brutal. We're trying to retrofit this old factory – the engineering challenges are insane. The original structural calculations were just… optimistic, to say the least. Optimistic? That sounds like code for utterly wrong. Exactly. It's a nightmare navigating the planning regulations, too. It's like they deliberately make it difficult. Tell me about it! Learning a language has often felt easier, sometimes. Seriously, Liam, you should start a blog about your engineering adventures. "The Adventures of a Structural Saviour." I think I’ll stick to spreadsheets, thanks. Less dramatic. What about you, Zara? Still buried in the world of words? Always. I'm chasing a lead on a piece about the impact of social media on local news outlets. It’s grim. Everyone’s glued to their phones, and local journalism is suffering badly. It’s a vicious cycle, isn’t it? No one reads the paper, so they lose funding, so they have to cut staff, so the reporting gets even worse… Precisely. I was supposed to be interviewing a former editor this afternoon. Said he started his career for a pittance and worked his way up, but can't imagine anyone doing that now. Money's just so tight these days. Remember when we were students? Ramen noodles and cheap wine were a luxury. Now it’s just… constant financial pressure. Don’t remind me.

Honestly, I don’t know how people drove before satnavs. I’d be hopelessly lost. Like, genuinely circling a roundabout for hours lost. Tell me about it! Remember that time we went to the Lake District and the satnav took us down a single-track lane? More like a sheep track! I thought we were going to get stuck for good. Aye, that's the thing about those gadgets. They don’t always know best, do they? Best to use yer common sense, lad. Easier said than done when you’re trusting a robotic voice telling you to turn right into a ditch! Google Maps is a bit better, I think. Yeah, Google Maps is alright, but it drains your phone battery like you wouldn’t believe. True. I just use my phone’s standard map thing. It's basic, but it does the job. Standard map’s good. Gets you back to basics. Me, I’ve always preferred a decent road atlas. You learn the geography that way. You're showing your age, Reg! So, how are the kids doing? Did you hear back from Mike about that apprenticeship? Yeah, he got it! He’s starting next month with that engineering firm. Really chuffed. Told you he would! He’s a good lad, my little brother. That’s brilliant news! Proper well done to him. Engineering’s a good trade. Solid work. That's fantastic! What about Sarah? Still thinking about going out to Saudi Arabia? She’s still on the fence. The pay is amazing, obviously, but she's worried about the culture difference. She’d be alright. She’s pretty adaptable. She'll have to be. But a bit of adventure never hurt anyone. Could be a good experience for her. Definitely. Though, I'd miss her loads if she went. We all would. It's just, the opportunity is...well, it’s massive. Still, she can always come back. It's not a life sentence. Exactly. And if she doesn’t like it, she can always bolt. That’s the beauty of it. Speaking of big changes, how's the decorating going? Have you finished the living room yet? Almost! Just need to put up the shelves. It’s been a nightmare though, trying to find someone to do the plastering. Yeah, everyone’s been booked up. You should have asked Liam, he knows a bloke. Liam?

Incredible, aren’t they? The sheer variety in Stockholm is just… staggering. Reminds me a little of Kew, but with a distinctly Scandinavian feel. It is lovely. Although, I must admit, my allergies are acting up a bit. I’ve already sneezed, I don’t know, a dozen times. Did you remember to pack my antihistamines, Mark? Of course, love. Right here. Though, honestly, you should really look into that allergy testing. Might be able to narrow down the culprits. You both sound like you’re gearing up for a medical conference rather than enjoying a beautiful day! I'm feeling fine, actually. Though I’m noticing my skin’s looking a bit dull. Stockholm air, I suppose. Dull skin? Have you been using that new serum I sent you? The one with the, what was it? Hyaluronic acid and… Honestly, Sarah, it smelled a bit… fishy. I haven't opened it. Fishy?! It's ocean-derived! It’s supposed to be amazing for hydration. You’re missing out! Ladies, ladies. Maybe a cup of tea would calm everyone down. I spotted a little café just over there, nestled amongst those rhododendrons. That sounds perfect. Hydration without the… aquatic aroma. Speaking of hydration, Mark, are you finally drinking enough water? You were complaining about a headache yesterday. I'm trying! It's just so easy to forget when you're busy. New Zealand taught me the importance of constant hydration – always a water bottle in your hand. The climate demands it. This Swedish air feels drier than Wellington, to be honest. You'd think surrounded by all this greenery, it'd be humid. But no, it’s surprisingly crisp. Did you know that some of these plants have incredible medicinal properties? I was reading about one – Arnica, I think it was – used for bruising and muscle aches. I’m always intrigued by that kind of thing. It’s amazing how much healing power plants possess. You know, I had a terrible backache after that presentation last week. Arnica cream might do the trick. Actually, I’ve been dabbling in herbal teas myself. Trying to cut back on caffeine. My sleep hasn't been great. You really should. And are you still doing those intense power walks? You need some real relaxation in there, Mark. You’re running yourself ragged. It’s the business, Sarah. Always something. I was thinking of hiring an assistant.

Honestly, Mum, it's just so frustrating! The voice recognition on my phone is useless. It keeps interpreting “right” as “flight.” Like, how? Well, dear, you do have a bit of a… distinctive accent. Gillingham, isn't it? More of a sing-song than some. It’s not  that  bad, Grandad! Everyone from around here sounds the same. It’s just… a Kentish lilt, isn't it? It's lovely, Poppy. Don’t tease her. It's a proper South East accent. I remember when I moved to Harlow, people thought I was trying to be posh! Posh. As if anyone round here's posh. Can we not, Kevin? I’m already stressed enough. I had a meeting with the solicitor today about Liam... Oh, dear. Still going on, is it? Thought you two were patching things up. We  try . But he’s dug his heels in about seeing Finn. He insists he’s “unfit” because of… you know. Oh, Mark. Always so dramatic. He needs to think about Finn’s feelings, not just his own. ‘Dramatic’ is one word for it. Stubborn, more like. Exactly! He keeps saying he’ll get it sorted, but it's been six months! Finn just wants to see his dad. It breaks my heart. Your mother always told me, children need their fathers. Even difficult ones. Easy for you to say, Grandad! You had a perfect dad, who never touched a drop. Don’t you go comparing him to your Liam, dear. Everyone makes mistakes. He does have a point, love. You need to be strong for Finn. What did the solicitor say? She said we can push for supervised visits, but it’ll be a long and expensive legal battle. I just don't know… it’s exhausting. Sometimes I wish I could just… escape. Escape where? Somewhere with better voice recognition? Very funny, Kev. Somewhere where I don’t have to worry about court dates and Liam’s latest meltdown. Somewhere I can just… breathe. Remember when we used to go cycling down by the Stour? Oh, yes! You and your brother, racing each other. You always cheated, didn't you, darling? I did  not ! It was just… strategic positioning! Strategic positioning. Right. Those were good times, weren't they? Simpler times. They were. I miss that simplicity. Dad used to make the most fantastic Sunday roasts. He did, didn’t he?

Right, cheeseboard's ready. Who wants a bit of cheddar? I’ve grated some proper mature stuff this time – not that pre-grated rubbish. Yeah, please. Cheddar's good with olives. Are there olives? Yep, got a selection. Kalamata, green ones, the lot. You boys hungry? I made that baked Alaska, remember? Bit ridiculous, I know, but it felt appropriate. Baked Alaska? Seriously? That's… intense. I know! It was a challenge. Getting the meringue just right… Anyway, how’s school? Anything exciting happening? Not really. History's pretty dull at the moment. We're doing Victorian factories. Oh, fascinating, actually! Think about the social impact… the working conditions… it’s appalling in many ways, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s like, loads of kids working in factories. Exactly. It's a reminder, isn’t it, about how far we’ve come. Though, sometimes I wonder… Wonder what? Just… looking at recruitment at work, it's still shocking sometimes how blatant the discrimination can be. Ageism, you know? People thinking I’m past it, just because I’m not twenty-something anymore. That's not fair. No, it isn't. And even subtle things… people talking down to you, assuming you can't understand the latest tech. It's infuriating. Reminds me of something my gran used to say about… Mum, can we talk about Halloween? Are we still doing that big party? Of course! It’s going to be massive. I’m already thinking about decorations. Are you helping me with the spooky playlist? I can do that. I've been listening to loads of weird stuff. What about… that film?  Suspiria ? That's a bit intense for a party, isn't it? Although… I do love Goblin… Remember when we saw that at the Electric Cinema? Ages ago. Yeah, you scared me half to death. I was just trying to set the mood! It's funny the things you remember, isn't it? This whole thing about Halloween… it reminds me of when you were little, dressed as a tiny werewolf. You absolutely hated it. I did not! You did! You cried the whole way to Mrs. Henderson’s house. She gave you a massive bagful of sweets, though. It was worth it. Mum! Don’t tell people that. Oh, come on. It’s a goldmine of embarrassing memories. You know, it makes you think about things… like the age of consent.

That’s a rather lovely marmalade you’ve got here, Bethan. Tangy. Proper Yorkshire marmalade, isn't it? It is! My mum sent over a batch. Thought you'd appreciate a bit of home, being so far from West Yorkshire. How was the flight over? Did you manage to sleep on the plane? Dreadfully. You know how it is. Turbulences makes me quite agitated. The one near Newfoundland was particularly… enthusiastic. But New York was glorious. Absolutely glorious. The scale of everything! I’m still buzzing from it, really. I can imagine. You were planning on doing loads of museums, weren't you? The Met, MoMA… Everything. And a Broadway show, of course. Wicked. It was brilliant. Though, I did spend half the show worrying about my phone battery. Social media consumption is a terrible habit, isn't it? I felt guilty taking pictures of everything. Like I was just ticking off boxes. We all do it. It's the way of the world now. Did you post loads of pictures on Instagram? Just a few. Mostly food, if I’m honest. Those bagels are worth documenting. And the cheesecake…oh, the cheesecake! Still dreaming about it, I am. But tell me, how’s the flying lessons going? You were so excited about them last time we spoke. They’re brilliant! I had a lesson on Tuesday. Managed a gentle loop-the-loop. Felt utterly ridiculous, of course, but exhilarating too. It's rather humbling, realising how much trust you're putting in that machine and the instructor. Good on you! You always were brave. Remember living in Japan? You zip-lining across gorges without a second thought. I’d have been petrified. Well, you were busy perfecting your origami skills, weren’t you? It’s all about perspective. What are your plans for today then? I was thinking we could potter around Mumbles, maybe go for a walk along the beach. The refuse collectors are out today so it'll be a bit chaotic, but it’ll be easier to get a parking spot. That sounds lovely. A nice, gentle stroll would do me good. And maybe a visit to that little bookshop near the pier? I need to grab some new reading material. I’m desperately behind on my literature. I have been meaning to start rereading Mrs Dalloway but I haven’t got round to it. Perfect. We could pop in.

Right, ‘Quixotic’! Double word score, corner. Take that, Liam. Beginner’s luck, really. You just got lucky with those letters. Seriously, how did you even  spell  that? Give him a break, Liam. It’s a good word. And it fits perfectly. Reminds me of that Don Quixote book we had to read last year for Lit Crit. Lit Crit was brutal. All that dense theory. I’m still trying to unpack some of it. Tell me about it. I nearly dropped out after that Derrida module. Anyway, gotta capitalize on this win, right? What can I make… ‘Zap’? No, that’s not a word. You know you always try to sneak in dodgy words, Finn. It  should  be a word, Chloe! It's a sound! Like, a laser beam zap! You're hopeless. Look, I’m going for ‘Conundrum’. Triple word, and it clears a load of high-scoring letters. Clever. Tactics, man. You’re always playing the long game. Gotta be, otherwise, you end up with practically nothing left. Like last week, when you tried to spell ‘Palimpsest’ with only two letters and a blank. Hey! It was a valiant effort. Plus, did you know the word "palimpsest" is interesting? It comes from Greek, meaning "again scraped". Because originally, they’d scrape the old writing off parchment to reuse it. Weird, huh? That  is  interesting! Like a linguistic archaeological dig. Makes you think about how language evolves, doesn’t it? It’s kinda like rearranging tiles in Scrabble, really. You’re constantly creating new meanings. Right, deep thoughts while trying to rack up points. Okay, my turn. I got a ‘J’… this is going to be tricky. “Jewel”? Easy points. Nah, too predictable. Actually, I'm thinking about using it with "Jolt" and getting a triple letter score. It requires a bit of rearranging though. You're thinking too hard! Just play something. Oh, speaking of books, have you guys seen that new Julia Donaldson one? The illustrations are gorgeous. My little cousin absolutely loves it. Donaldson’s always a winner, isn’t she? Remember how obsessed my sister was with The Gruffalo when she was little. She used to dress up as it! It was terrifying. My sister was obsessed with whatever Harry Potter book was current. Still is, actually. Re-reads them every year. Nostalgia, I guess. Classic. Thinking about it, A-Levels were the peak of nostalgia for me.

Right then, Doris, you’ve been quiet this morning. Everything alright? Oh, just pondering, Arthur. Pondering the state of things, you know. The world’s a strange place these days. Always has been, love. Always has been. Just gets stranger with age, doesn’t it? Seems like yesterday I was chasing pigeons in Costessey, now I’m… well, I’m here. Here, have a cuppa. Strong, just like you like it. Did you see anything interesting in the paper this morning? The crossword proving difficult again? Aye, had a go at it. Got a few in, but that cryptic stuff... it’s beyond me now. Seems like they make 'em harder deliberately. Found an article about that new bridge they’re building just outside Norwich, though. That’s a considerable piece of engineering. Oh, is that right? I read about that too. Heavens, the traffic they’re going to cause while it's being constructed. It’ll be chaos. Remember when they built the A47 bypass? Took years. Years and years. Couldn’t get anywhere without going miles around. Things move slower these days, though, don't they? Everything seems to take longer. That's a funny thing to say. I feel things are speeding up all the time, what with the children's technology and all. It's just so fast-paced that sometimes it can rather dizzy you. That technology... I can’t make head nor tail of it. Just a load of flashing lights and confusing buttons. Always loved a good book, though. Something solid to hold onto. You always did. Remember those comics you used to read? The ones with the cowboys and Indians? Aye, I do. Spent hours reading those. Good times. Simple times. Everything seemed easier then, didn’t it? It did, Doris. It certainly did. It did. Now where was I...ah yes, the bridge. A lot of concrete, that’s for sure. A lot of concrete. Well, you have your tea and I'll go bake some scones. It's a nice day today and fresh scones in the garden seems like the ideal way to spend the rest of a day. Sounds lovely Doris, very lovely indeed. Have the cream ready. Don't skimp on the cream. Never do. Never do. Would you like a biscuit with your tea? Yes, please. A digestive will be nice. Thank you, Doris. Thank you very much.

That was absolutely superb, Anon. Honestly, the best roast I’ve had in years. You've really outdone yourself. Oh, thank you, Dad. Really glad you enjoyed it. It was a bit of a challenge sourcing everything locally, but it was worth it, I think. Absolutely delicious, dear. That rosemary really sang through. And the vegetables were cooked perfectly. You know I'm a stickler for a properly roasted carrot. You always were! Though, really, everything was spot on. What was in the gravy? It had a lovely depth of flavour. Just the usual – chicken stock, red wine, a bit of Worcestershire sauce, and a secret ingredient… a teaspoon of Marmite. Marmite? In gravy? You're having a laugh surely. I’m serious! It adds a real umami richness. Tried it? Well, I’ll be. Can’t say I can taste it exactly, but it  is  good. Clever you. It is rather ingenious, actually. I might have to steal that trick. Though, I think my husband would have a heart attack if he found Marmite anywhere near the gravy. He’s very traditional, you know. Every family has their Marmite moments! Speaking of which, I was reading in the local paper this morning that the new station is  finally  opening. No! Really? After all those years of delays? I thought they’d given up. Honestly, it’s a miracle. Remember when they said it would be ready in 2018? I do! It’s going to be a game-changer for the village, though. No more relying on the buses. Good for them. Means I can get to Exeter a bit easier and I've been promising myself I'd try that new fitness centre on the outskirts. They've got a swimming pool and everything… it’s just getting  into  the pool that’s the problem these days. I know what you mean. I've been using this new app, 'Move More Devon'. It's actually quite motivating. It sets small goals and tracks your progress. Oh, that sounds interesting. I've been trying to be more active, but it’s hard to find the time with everything on my plate. Teaching is rather relentless. Yeah, it's designed to fit into busy schedules, even just 10 minutes a day makes a difference. They even have walking routes mapped out. Well, I might give it a try. Anything to keep these old joints moving.

Honestly, that film was dreadful. Utterly dreadful. Didn’t you think? Nah, I quite liked it. The visuals were good, at least. Bit predictable though, yeah. Predictable? It was aggressively derivative! Like, it took cues from five different superhero franchises and just smashed them together. And the plot… don't even get me started. Come on, it’s popcorn entertainment. You can’t expect Shakespeare. Exactly! Which reminds me, did you see that Shakespeare thing on BBC Four last week? Hamlet with Cush Jumbo? I missed it! Was it good? I’ve been buried in coursework, as usual. Seminars have gone mental this term. Dr. Davies is grilling us every week. It was brilliant! Really fresh take on it. Punchy, modern…Jumbo absolutely killed it. Definitely worth catching the repeat. You should check it out. Will do. Speaking of coursework, I'm absolutely dreading this essay on Brexit and the EU single market. It's like trying to follow a squirrel on espresso. Tell me about it. Politics is a minefield these days anyway, let alone trying to write an analytical essay about it. Everyone’s got an opinion already. Exactly! And every opinion is shouted the loudest. Trying to find a nuanced argument is like nailing jelly to a wall. Fancy a game of FIFA later? Need to vent some frustration. Always! I’m smashing everyone at the moment. Domination, pure and simple. You’re going down, mate. Oh, I’ll show you. I've been practicing my free kicks. And I’ve got a new strategy: just spam Rashford down the wing. It works every time. That’s cheating! It’s effective. Anyway, seriously, you heard about Mark's stag weekend? He’s booked paintballing in Snowdonia. No way! Snowdonia? That’s brutal. He’s got some masochistic tendencies, doesn't he? Apparently, he's always wanted to get shot at by his mates in the Welsh mountains. Genius, I reckon. Sounds less like a celebration and more like an endurance test. Imagine the photos... We’re gonna have to get it all on video. Speaking of photos, did you ever hear back about that job interview you did at the gaming company? No, not a peep. Which is annoying. I thought it went well. Seemed really enthusiastic about my portfolio. They'll be dragging their feet. Big companies are always slow. Keep your chin up. You’ll land something.

Oh my god, Beth! It’s so good to see you! You look amazing. You too, Liv! Seriously, it feels like ages. Last time was, what, Oxford ball season? Yeah, feels like a lifetime ago! How are you? Seriously, tell me everything. What’s been going on? Loads, honestly. Work’s been… intense. Pearson's decided to throw everything at me this quarter. Massive campaign launch for their textbooks, you know? Stressful, but good. How’s the project coordination going? Still swirling around in a vortex of spreadsheets? Pretty much. It’s alright though, I like the variety. Currently coordinating a new sustainability initiative for a construction company – surprisingly interesting actually. And the team’s really good. That sounds cool. Sustainable construction is a huge thing right now. So, spill. How's Mark doing? Still around? Oh, Mark. No. It’s over. Officially, properly over. Oh no! What happened? Don’t tell me he got arrested or something ridiculous like he sometimes threatened to do. No, nothing dramatic. Just… we grew apart, I guess. He wanted to move to Bristol, I couldn’t leave London. You know how I feel about London. Plus, he was getting increasingly… into sourdough, if you know what I mean. Like, obsessively into it. Sourdough obsession? That  is  a bit much. You dodged a bullet there, Liv. Seriously. I think so. It just felt… suffocating. Anyway, what about you? Anyone new on the scene? There’s a guy, yeah. His name’s Finn. Works in finance. Pretty dull, honestly, but lovely. And he actually does the washing up when I’m at his flat, so that’s a massive win. Washing up? You’re a lucky woman! My last guy would leave the dishes piled up for a week. It was a biohazard. See? You definitely made the right call with Mark. Speaking of families, how are your parents? Still volunteering at the animal shelter? Yeah! Mum’s actually fostering a tiny kitten right now. It's the cutest thing ever. Dad’s still battling squirrels in the garden. He's convinced they're plotting against him. Classic Dad. Mine are being… well, parents. Nagging me about settling down, getting a mortgage, the usual. You know how they are. Oh god, I do. My aunt’s already started showing me pictures of her neighbour’s newly engaged grandson. It’s relentless. I know! And then they ask, “So, are you going to…?”

Right, kettle’s on. Fancy a builder's brew or something a bit fancier? Builder's is perfect, thanks. Been a long day sifting through data, you know? My brain feels like mush. Tell me about it. Trying to wrangle these qualitative responses is a nightmare. Give me numbers any day. How's the thesis coming along then? Still wrestling with the existential dread of it all? Pretty much. I've hit a bit of a wall, to be honest. All the theoretical stuff is solid, it’s just… getting it to  say  something concrete. That’s the worst part, isn’t it? When it all feels like hot air. Want a biscuit with that? I got those ginger ones you like. Yes, please! You’re a lifesaver. These ginger biscuits are brilliant. Seriously, where do you find them? M&S, usually. I stock up whenever I'm in town. Speaking of stocking up, I saw your mum online, she’s going mad for orchids again. Oh god, is she? She's taken up indoor gardening with a vengeance. Apparently, the one she’s trying to coax back to life at the moment is a particularly fussy Dendrobium. A Dendro-what? Sounds fancy. Honestly, your mum, she's a force of nature. Remember when she tried to grow pumpkins in that tiny patch of garden? Oh yeah! They were the size of golf balls! She was so cross when they didn't grow properly. Said the soil wasn't 'vibrant enough'. Vibrant enough! Only your mum! Mine would have given up after a week. She's more of a ‘stick some daffodils in a pot’ kind of gardener. She's always had a flair for the dramatic, hasn’t she? Reminds me, she sent me a recipe for a lemon and rosemary cake. Apparently, it’s the ‘key to healing all emotional wounds.’ Only your mum would prescribe cake for emotional trauma. I'll have to try that. Sounds delicious. Are you feeling emotionally wounded at the moment? A little bit. The thesis, you know? The usual. And the pressure of having to impress my supervisor… Don’t let him get to you. You're brilliant, you know that. Just keep plugging away. And bake a cake. Seriously, it might actually work. Worth a shot, I suppose. Thanks, love. It's good to just… talk, you know? It’s easy to get stuck in the head.

Morning, Rhys. Dreadful weather we’re having, isn’t it? Damp chills you to the bone. Morning, Kamal. Aye, it’s a dreich one alright. Wouldn’t be surprised if we get a bit of sleet later. Proper Welsh weather, this. How was your weekend, then? Quiet. Very quiet. Did a bit of gardening - which was a complete wash, really. The tomatoes are looking worse for wear. Seems the slugs have been having a field day. Had to rescue a few. You know how it is. Aye, I do. Spent most of mine wrestling with bindweed in the vegetable patch. A never-ending battle, that is. Did you see young Cole Morgan, the striker for Cardiff? His son was playing in the youth team game on Saturday. Apparently, the lad's got a decent shot on him. No, I missed that. Football isn't really my thing, you know. Though I do follow a bit of snooker. Watching O'Sullivan is always a treat - even if he does have moments of... frustration. Incredible talent, though. Aye, he is. A gift, really. Though sometimes you wonder what’s going on in that head of his. Speaking of frustrating things, have you started marking those essays yet? The ones on post-structuralism? Don't remind me. I've tackled about a third. Some of them are… ambitious, let’s say. One student has apparently decided that Derrida's work is essentially a recipe for soufflé. Good gracious! Well, at least they’re thinking outside the box. Mine are mostly repeating things they read on Wikipedia. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if they even bother reading the core texts. It's getting increasingly difficult, isn't it? I was reading an article the other day about the changing requirements for entry into the police force and the armed forces. They’re looking for more than just physical strength and aptitude now. Analytical skills, critical thinking… things we’re supposed to be teaching them, aren’t we? Absolutely. Seems like a whole different skillset now. My nephew’s thinking about joining the army, you know. Wants to be a signaller. He's a bright lad, but he's slightly intimidated by all the psychometric testing they make you do. Oh, yes. They’ve really ramped that up, haven’t they? It's all about risk assessment and psychological stability now. Less about bravery, more about controlled response.

Right, so, the Christening venue… I’ve looked at The Old Church again, and they've actually got availability on the 18th of November. What do you think, Liam? November already? Wow, time's flying. The Old Church is lovely, though. Really traditional, right? Is it still pricey? A bit, yeah. But they've got a wedding offer on at the moment, which brings it down a fair bit. It’s got that nice little garden too, weather permitting, for the kids to run around. Run around! Exactly! And it’s close to the village hall, so we could do the party there afterward, ease the catering a bit. That sounds sensible. Better than trying to squeeze everyone into your house again, eh? Remember last Christmas? Don't remind me! I was practically living on the sofa for a week. So, November 18th? Potential go-ahead for The Old Church and the village hall for afterwards? Sounds good. Can you send me the quote? I need to check my student budget, you know. Ramen noodles are a luxury these days. Absolutely, will do. Now, birthdays. Little Poppy’s going to be four next month, practically a big girl. Any thoughts on a party? Four! Where has the time gone? She's barely out of nappies. What does she want? Still obsessed with unicorns? Very much so. She’s been sketching them everywhere, it's quite sweet. I was thinking maybe a little unicorn-themed party at the park? We could get one of those bouncy castles. Ooh, yes! Perfect for letting off some steam. You'll need a whole army of referees to keep the peace, though. Probably! I was also considering inviting some of her nursery friends. But I don't want it to get too massive. Keep it manageable and fun. Who else is involved in the planning? Dad hiding behind the newspaper as usual? He’s doing the cake, actually! Claims he's perfected his chocolate fudge recipe. Don’t hold your breath. Oh God. The last one was practically concrete! It was… robust, let’s say. But he’s persistent. He says his secret ingredient is extra dark chocolate. Cake! Yes, sweetheart, cake! So, park party for Poppy, hopefully at the Old Church for the Christening, cake from Dad… Do you think we’re missing anything? It’s all a bit overwhelming. Relax! You’re doing great.

Right, so, weekend plans then? Anyone fancy a potter around Lichfield Cathedral? It’s surprisingly clear after all that rain we had. Nah, I’m working Saturday. Crazy busy with stocktaking. Honestly, the weekend always flies by, doesn’t it? Fly like a birdie! A birdie! Yes, it does, sweetheart. Go on, have a biscuit. Sunday though, I’m free. Maybe we could finally look at those Christmas decorations down the loft? Mum, you said you wanted to sort them. Oh, yes, I did. And goodness, I've a feeling the cat's made a home up there. Honestly, that thing thinks it owns the place. Remember that time it brought a live mouse into the kitchen? Oh god, yes! Dad nearly fainted. He did! Poor love. Though he pretends he’s a hardened man, doesn’t he? Squeak! Little one’s got a vivid imagination. So, New York… have you been looking at flights, love? Yeah, I’ve had a quick peek. They’re eye-wateringly expensive, aren’t they? Especially for October half-term. We’re going to have to start saving properly now. We are. I was looking at some apartments on Airbnb. Nothing fancy, just somewhere central and safe. Remember how we got lost for hours in Venice? Don’t remind me! I was convinced we’d be sleeping rough. That little alleyway with the grumpy Italian man who screamed at us… He just didn’t like tourists! He probably just wanted a quiet evening. Still, we found that amazing gelato place afterwards, didn’t we? Totally worth the panic. True. Gelato always makes everything better. Though, honestly, I’m still scarring from my wedding day. Remember Auntie Brenda spilling red wine all down my dress? Oh, I do! You were incandescent! But look, you managed to salvage it, and those photos are hilarious now. Wedding! Pretty! Yes, sweetheart. Very pretty. Listen, darling, do you want to put on your wellies and go and play in the garden? It's stopped raining now, and the puddles will be lovely. Yeah, good idea. Keep her entertained while I check the prices for Brooklyn hotels. Right you do that love. And don't get too stressed. New York will be fantastic, and we'll all have a brilliant time. It's going to be a proper adventure. Just like our honeymoon, but hopefully with fewer wardrobe malfunctions! Here's hoping.

Right, so basically, this is the outline I've got for the thesis. It's… a lot. Yeah, it looks it. Don't worry, I've been there. What's the core argument you're trying to make? Just give me the elevator pitch version. Okay, right. So, I'm arguing that the shifting landscape of post-industrial heritage in Lancashire is inextricably linked to the evolving notions of regional identity. It’s about more than just old mills and factories. Okay, that’s… pretty dense. In a good way. Go on. So, like, the initial focus was on preserving these sites as a testament to the industrial past, right? A kind of nostalgic celebration of Lancashire’s contribution to the Industrial Revolution. But now, there's a growing awareness of the social and environmental costs. The communities that were built around these industries suffered massively. Right, the flip side of the coin. Exactly. So, I'm looking at how that's reflected in the current repurposing of these spaces – turning mills into apartments, factories into creative hubs – and how that impacts the way people in Lancashire define themselves. Is it still a place of proud industrial heritage, or is it something else now? Sounds fascinating. What kind of sources are you using? Loads, thankfully. There’s a surprising amount of local council archives around heritage site management, that's been really useful. I’ve been digging through newspaper articles from the 70s and 80s too, looking for the social commentary around the closures. And I'm doing some oral history interviews with people who lived and worked in these areas at the time. Oral histories are gold. You’ll get stuff you’d never find in a document. What about academic stuff? Yeah, I've surveyed the relevant literature on post-industrial landscapes, heritage studies, and regional identity. Pretty standard stuff, really. This section is just a literature review. Painful, but necessary. I remember those. So, what's next on the agenda? Are you doing fieldwork? Yeah, I’ve got a few site visits lined up next week. Visiting some of the key heritage sites and taking photos, just observing how they’re used and presented now. Plus, the interviews, obviously. I've got three scheduled so far. Sounds good. And you've got a chapter outline, so you know where you're headed. Yeah, but trying to actually  write  the thing is… well.

Morning, everyone. Bit of a weird night, actually. Oh yeah? What happened? I had the strangest dream. I was giving a presentation… to a room full of cats. And they were all judging me. Really judgy cats. Silly! Did the cats have hats? No hats, sweetheart. Just… scornful stares. And one of them kept batting at my notes. Me had a dream about trains… choo choo! Sounds exciting, darling. So, judgy cats, huh? What were you presenting about? Prospect Research – oddly enough. It felt very important in the dream. Like the fate of all the catnip in the world depended on it. Typical you, even in your dreams you’re working. I dreamt I was on a beach, turquoise water, white sand... just bliss. Beach! Me wants beach! We should get back to Cornwall soon, then. Little ones need some sand between their toes. Definitely. Though truthfully, both of them would probably just try and eat the sand. Tasty sand. Right, well, enough about dreams. Did you see those lottery numbers last night? Don’t even start! I bought a ticket, obviously. What are the odds of winning? Slim to none, I reckon. It's always good to dream, though, isn’t it? Imagine - no more Prospect Research, a little cottage by the sea, and… a dog. Oh, a dog? You’re still on about that. I am! I need a Labrador. Big, daft, happy Labrador, bouncing around the garden. Doggy! Fetch! A Labrador would be a lot of work, you know. Walks, feeding, vet bills… I'm willing to commit. Think of the cuddles! And someone to chase the squirrels away. You’d probably end up teaching it to do your spreadsheets. That’s not entirely out of the question. But seriously, imagine… a dog. And a lottery win. Little cottage, beach, Labrador... that's the dream. It’s a nice dream. Let's just stick to dreaming for now, eh? Less stressful. Fancy some toast? Toast! Please! Me too! With jam! Coming right up! First, coffee. Then toast. Then… world domination via lottery winnings and furry companions. Just kidding. Mostly. Don't you dare. Now, about that toast...what kind do you want, darling? Blueberries or raspberries? Blueberries! Raspberries! " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " " "H.H..

Honestly, I can’t believe you’re driving so fast! My ribs feel like they're protesting. Sorry, sorry! It was just a straight bit of road. Are you sure you’re okay? I mean, really okay? Yeah, fine. Just…ow. Don’t need to point out how badly I managed that fall, do you? No, of course not. Though, landing on your elbow wasn’t exactly graceful. Did you at least get it checked out? A&E was a nightmare. Packed tighter than a tin of sardines. Spent two hours in the waiting room. Two hours?! What did they say? They poked and prodded and x-rayed it. Said it’s just a bad sprain, thankfully. No break. Gave me a colourful bandage and a leaflet on wrist exercises. A colourful bandage? They always give the best bandages. Bright pink, usually. Bright orange, actually. Like a traffic cone. So subtle. Still. At least it's not broken. You’re lucky. I remember when I fell off my bike as a kid – broke my collarbone. Absolute agony. Oh, poor you. I’ve had worse scrapes, though. Remember when I tried to climb the fence at the park and ended up hanging halfway, yelling for help? How could I forget? You looked like a very distressed, slightly panicked squirrel. I did not! I was being adventurous! Anyway, this is much worse. I can barely move my arm. And I have that meeting on Monday. Right, the presentation. That’s not ideal. Look, can I drive slower for a bit? And maybe we can stop at Boots and get you an ice pack? An ice pack would be brilliant, actually. And a strong cup of tea. And maybe a miracle. A miracle’s a bit much to ask. But ice and tea, I can definitely manage. Are you sure you didn’t try to impress anyone with your acrobatic skills? Very funny. It was a rogue paving stone. Seriously, tripping hazards everywhere these days. It’s the council’s fault, honestly. Of course it is. Always is. Well, focus on your tea and ice pack. We'll figure out the presentation later. Just don't try any more acrobatic feats, alright? No promises. But definitely no fence climbing. Not for a while, anyway. Thanks, love. That actually sounds really good. Ice and tea. Sorted. You got it. Where's Boots then? I hope this is what you were looking for!

Terrible business, isn’t it? This situation in Ukraine. Just dreadful. Makes you wonder what’s coming next, doesn't it? Absolutely appalling. Can’t believe it's 2024 and something like this is still happening. I was reading about it earlier, and the scale of the humanitarian crisis... it's just heartbreaking. It is. And the rhetoric coming out of Moscow… Well, it's frightening, frankly. Are you keeping an eye on the markets? This sort of instability never helps. Yes, a little. I’m trying not to get too anxious about it, mind you. The business is stable enough that it can weather a bit of turbulence. Not like some of the smaller shops in the Lanes struggling after the pandemic, you know. True, you've always been fairly resilient. Smart investments. So, tell me about this idea you mentioned last week. The little coffee cart? Right, yes. I’ve been doing some serious thinking, Matthew. I reckon there’s a real gap near the Marina. Lots of walkers, cyclists… nowhere decent to grab a proper coffee and a pastry. Not just a chain, you know? Something a bit… niche. Niche. Right. And you’ve already looked into permits and so on? That's always the tricky part in Brighton, isn’t it? I've had a preliminary chat with the council. Surprisingly straightforward, so far. They’re keen on encouraging small businesses. The main challenge is the initial outlay, but I’ve got a decent chunk of savings, and the bank seems reasonably receptive. Excellent. What sort of coffee are you thinking? Something beyond the usual Starbucks fare? Absolutely. Fair trade, obviously. And I was thinking about roasting my own beans, small batch. Maybe some interesting blends. Ethiopian, Colombian… even a little experiment with some Kenyan. Sounds ambitious. And a significant investment in equipment. It is. But I think it’s worth it. I’ve been doing some market research - talking to people down at the Marina. There’s real demand for it. And I'm quite excited about it, to be honest. It’s something different to do.
