Retirement’s proving a bit… dull. I can imagine. You've always been one for keeping busy. Remember when you were organising those charity events in Hove? Oh, don't remind me! That was a nightmare. Trying to get the council to close off the High Street... a bureaucratic warzone.

This pub's got a really odd vibe, doesn’t it? Bit… fortress-y. Like being inside a giant brick hat. True, the décor’s certainly… unique. But the beer's decent, and it's nice to be out. Where are we at with dinner, by the way? Still thinking Thai? I’m leaning towards Thai, yeah. Or maybe Indian? I'm craving something spicy. Are you feeling it? Definitely spicy. I had a dreary day at the office. Need something to kick it out of me. Did you finish that last episode of Happy Valley? Oh my god, yes! Absolutely brilliant. The ending… so bleak, but so well done. She was incredible. Catherine Cawood is just phenomenal, isn't she? Properly gripping stuff. Reminds me a bit of university days, all those gritty crime novels we used to devour. Definitely. Remember debating Dostoevsky in that freezing lecture hall? I practically had frostbite. Oh god, yes! And Professor Davies' eccentric explanations of symbolism. You could practically smell the tweed. Speaking of eccentricities, do you think they’ve tried to make this pub look old on purpose? All the exposed brickwork and those weird portraits... Maybe? It's certainly got a deliberate, if slightly odd, aesthetic. Look at that awful velvet wallpaper. Did they purposefully choose the worst pattern they could find? Possibly! Oh, and I’m freezing. I should have worn a thicker coat. It's rather draughty in here. Here, have my scarf. Are you still listening to that indie band I recommended? The Echoing Caves? Actually, yes! They’re really good. Bit melancholic, but proper good. Reminds me of that cat we had at uni, Winston. Always hiding under the radiator. Winston! Oh, I'd forgotten about him. He was such a grumpy thing. Always swiping at you if you got too close. Absolutely. A tiny, furry tyrant. I wonder what happened to him? No idea, I bet he's ruling a household somewhere, still judging everyone's life choices. Right, Thai or Indian then? Let’s decide, so we can actually get a table somewhere. Thai, definitely. And maybe a spicy green curry? And we’ll need to sort out a warmer coat for me tomorrow. This Woolwich wind is something else! Sorted. Thai it is. And don’t worry, I'll give you a hug to warm you up. It’s not as effective as a proper coat, but it's something!

So, you’re actually heading back to Skye then? Soon? Aye, next week. Got a clear few days carved out. Hoping for a bit o' decent weather for once. It’s been dreich down here, hasn't it? Dreich doesn't even cover it, brother. Felt like living inside a damp flannel for the last few weeks. Honestly, I was starting to grow moss. You and me both. I need to get back to the mountains. The light’s been terrible for photography. Everything's just grey. You know, I was thinking about that shot you got last summer, up near the Old Man of Storr. That one with the mist swirling around it? Ah, that was a lucky one. Right place, right time. Caught it just as the sun started to break through. Incredible. I've been trying to recreate that kind of vibe, but… nothing. My photos look like rainy postcards. It’s more than luck too, you know. You’ve got to be patient. Hunt for the right light, the right mood. And know the place like the back o’ your hand. Aye, that’s what I’m missing, I think. I’ve been heading up Arthur’s Seat, trying to get something similar, but it’s just not the same. Arthur’s Seat's great for a bit o' exercise, but it’s not Skye, is it? The scale's all wrong. You need the big landscapes, the vastness. It's different altogether. I hear you. Thinking about maybe taking a proper trip up one day. Haven’t been back to Skye in years. You should. Seriously. Get yourself a good waterproof jacket, a pair of sturdy boots, and a camera with a decent zoom. Sounds like an investment. But a good one, I reckon. What are you hoping to capture this time around? Got any particular spots in mind? There's a little cove north of Portree... Talisker Bay, I think it’s called. Stunning at sunset, when the light hits the black sand just right. Hoping to get some long exposure shots with the waves rolling in. Sounds...magical. Aye, it can be. The problem is, chasing that magic is what takes up most of your time. Hours spent waiting for the cloud to shift. Patience, huh? You’re preaching to the choir. Well, somebody has to. Tell you what, send a few of your Arthur’s Seat attempts over.

Right then, so let's have a good natter. What's the plan for this week then, love? Anything exciting happening? Not hugely exciting, Mum. Just the usual primary school mayhem really. Ofsted are looming, you know. That’s stressing me out a bit. Oh, love, don’t let them stress you. You’re a brilliant teacher, you know that. They’re just looking for a reason to find fault. Just be yourself, and show them what you do. Easy for you to say. You never had Ofsted hanging over your head! It's just... a lot. And then there's little Leo, of course. Of course! How's the nursery search going? Did you manage to have a proper look at that place near the park? The one you mentioned last week? I did! It was… nice. Really bright and colourful, which is good. But the staff seemed a bit… distracted, you know? And the outdoor area was a bit small. I want him to have space to run around and explore. I'm not sure it's right for him. Mmm, I see. You've got to trust your gut on this one, love. He’s already such a little character, he deserves the best possible start. Have you looked at St. Michael's? I know it’s a bit more expensive, but the reputation’s excellent. I’ve added it to the list. It's just... a lot of money! And everything’s so expensive these days, isn't it? Tell me about it! Though I’ve got that voucher for Boots. I was going to get some more nappies, but you could have it for Leo’s clothes. It’s got a good few quid on it. Oh, Mum, you're the best! Really? That would be amazing. Thank you. Don't mention it, love. What about your sister? Has she sorted out the weekend visit with your dad yet? She’s trying. They’re having one of their little… disagreements. Apparently, he’s being difficult about where they should go. It’s always something with them, isn't it? Oh, yes. The usual. Family, eh? Still, they’ll sort it. They always do. Are you watching that new drama on Tuesday nights? "The Gilded Cage"? It’s really good! I’m hooked on it! The costumes are gorgeous, and the plot is so twisty. I've heard good things!

This is absolutely brilliant, honestly. You’ve outdone yourself, Anon. Seriously. Glad you like it, Liv! It's just something I whipped up. Could’ve been worse, right? It's good. Really good. Proper pasta. Not like that stuff you get at… you know… Don’t even go there, Dan. Remember that Bolognese incident? Don’t remind me. It was like ketchup on spaghetti. Truly traumatic. I’ll stick to my own cooking then. So, Liv, anything exciting happening at work? Still battling the seemingly endless flow of spreadsheets? You have no idea. This conference next month is driving me mad. The keynote speaker cancelled last minute, the AV guy’s on holiday… it’s just one thing after another. Typical. Oh no! That’s awful. What are you going to do? I’m scrambling. Trying to find a replacement speaker, praying the AV setup doesn't spontaneously combust... it’s a mess. Want a drink? Yeah, cheers. What are you having? Just water for me, thanks. I’ve got a massive gym session tomorrow. Trying to be good. Good for you! I could do with a gym session. I've barely seen daylight this week. You need to relax, Liv. Seriously. When was the last time you actually did something fun? Fun? Is that even a word anymore? I think I used it somewhere in a PowerPoint presentation. Don’t be like that! We could go out next weekend. Movie? Dinner? Something? I don’t know… I feel like I’m permanently behind on everything. Just one night. Promise you’ll just relax and switch off. Okay, okay, you’ve twisted my arm. But you're buying. Deal! So, what about you, Chloe? How's the production control life treating you? Still wrestling with supply chains? It’s… interesting. My boss is being a bit of a nightmare at the moment. Constantly breathing down my neck, questioning every decision. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Ugh, I hate that. Micromanaging drives me insane. Tell me about it. And he keeps giving me this look, like I’m going to mess everything up. Sounds like he wants to take your place. Maybe! It’s just… I’m starting to wonder if it’s worth it. All the stress, the early mornings… You’re brilliant at what you do, Chloe. Don’t let him get you down. Maybe you need to have a proper chat with him, lay it all out.

Right then, who wants tea? I’ve just put the kettle on. Oh lovely, Arthur. I’ll have a cup, please. Milk and no sugar, as always. Yes please, Maureen. A good strong cuppa would be just the ticket. Milk and one sugar for me, if you don't mind. Thank you, Arthur. I’d love a cup. Just a splash of milk, dear. Coming right up. Always a pleasure to make a proper pot of tea, you know. Not like that instant stuff some people drink. Don’t you start, Arthur! Some of us haven't the time for faffing about with teapots and bags. Faffing about? It's called appreciating the finer things, Brenda! You youngsters wouldn't understand. Now, now, let's not have a debate about tea, shall we? It’s a simple pleasure. Like a nice biscuit with it, though. Any biscuits, Arthur? Got a tin of digestives and some ginger snaps. Take your pick. Digestives for me, please, Arthur. Always a classic. Ginger snaps sound rather nice actually. A little bit of spice to warm you up. There you go. Always something for everyone. Sometimes I think it's the little things, isn’t it? A good cup of tea, a biscuit… keeps you going. Absolutely, Arthur. It’s the simple things. Reminds me of when I was a lad, coming home from school, mum would always have a cup ready. My mother used to make the best scones. Served with clotted cream and jam. Nothing quite like it. Oh, scones! Don’t get me started. You need a proper baking tin, though. Not one of those flimsy things. You and your baking, Brenda. Always particular, aren’t you? Here’s your tea. Careful, it's hot. Thank you, dear. Lovely. Really hit the spot. Delicious, Arthur. Thank you. Wonderful, thank you. Just what I needed. Glad you all like it. Now, who wants another biscuit? I haven’t even started on the stories yet! Don’t you start telling those rambling tales, Arthur! You'll be here all night. Just a few, Brenda. Just a few. They're always a good laugh, aren’t they? Looking forward to them. Yes please! Right then! Where to begin... let me see... it all started with Mrs. Higgins and a rogue goose... Oh, not that story again! It's a classic! A classic, I tell you! Let the man tell his story, Brenda!

Right, I think that’s everyone served. Bit of a feast tonight, isn’t it? Absolutely! You've outdone yourself, Anon. This lamb is incredible. Seriously, where did you get it? From that new farm shop on the edge of town. They do fantastic meat. A bit pricey, admittedly. Worth it! Proper flavour. Beats the supermarket stuff any day. Though, I still maintain a decent roast can be done with supermarket lamb. It’s all about the technique. Of course, you’d say that, David. The culinary guru. Speaking of technique, Mark’s got a driving lesson tomorrow, hasn't he? Yeah, with Liam. Feeling a bit nervous, to be honest. I keep picturing myself reversing into a lamppost. You’ll be fine. Liam's a good instructor, proper patient. Remember that time I nearly took out a parking meter in London? Nearly gave the instructor a heart attack. Oh, David, don’t remind me! Was that the one where you blamed the meter for jumping out in front of you? It  did  jump! Alright, maybe a slight exaggeration… Honestly! But seriously, Mark, don't worry about it too much. Just focus. And no drinking beforehand, obviously. Obviously! I wouldn't dream of it. It’s just...the thought of the test. You'll pass, love. You’re a smart driver. And speaking of tests, Sarah’s still fuming about the CRB check they’re making her do for volunteering at the animal shelter. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? All that paperwork and the expense. Seems excessive for just cuddling kittens. It is a pain. London's got it even worse, with all the extra layers of bureaucracy. You'd think ensuring the safety of kittens was a lower priority than dealing with protest permits. Don't even mention protests. Saw some stuff on the news about that demonstration in central London. Got quite heated, apparently. My aunt Meg was talking about that, said they were protesting about circumcision. Honestly, people will protest about anything these days. True. Though, bearing in mind the history of London and its various opinions, probably not that unexpected. Changing the subject completely – anyone been to that new gallery down in Norwich? The one showcasing local artists? I went last week. Quite good actually. A bit… abstract for my taste in some cases, but some really interesting pieces. That landscape painter – quite evocative. I like landscapes.

God, it’s good to be back. Everything smells… normal. Not like chlorine and factor 50. Welcome back! You look… tanned. And exhausted. How was it? Honestly? A mix. The beach was incredible, the sun was amazing. But massively overstimulating. My brain feels like it’s been through a washing machine. Tell me everything! Did you finally manage to properly switch off? Tried to. Difficult with Mum constantly checking in. She rang three times a day, asking if I’d applied sun cream or if I was eating enough. Classic Mum. Did Dad say anything? He just rolled his eyes and said "Don't encourage her.” Progress, I suppose. But seriously, I feel like I need a week just to recover from the holiday. You deserve it. I tried to keep the house ticking over, but... well, you know. Don't worry about it. What did you have for dinner? Smells good. Just did a really easy pasta thing. Loads of veggies. I was too knackered to be adventurous. So, spill. Any dramas? Met any cute lifeguards? No lifeguards, sadly. Although there was this one guy who worked at the beach bar… pretty cute. But I was trying to be all responsible and not get involved in anything. Wise move. There's plenty of time for cute bar staff when you're  not  feeling stressed. How’s Liam? Still working overtime? Yeah, apparently he’s being headhunted for a new position. More money, longer hours. The usual. Sounds exhausting. You’ll have to drag him out for a proper night out soon. Speaking of, I saw Chloe and Finn the other day. Finn’s been teaching Chloe how to play squash. Apparently, she's terrible. Oh, that’s brilliant! She’d probably throw the ball at his face. Something like that. They were both laughing their heads off. Oh, and Sarah's leaving her job. Apparently, the boss is a nightmare. Really? That's such a shame for her. That place was draining her. Yeah, she needed to get out. I'm thinking we should all get together next week. Dinner at that new Italian place? That sounds perfect. I’m already looking forward to it. Did you manage to sort out the leak in the bathroom? Nearly! The plumber came but said something about needing a special part. Coming back tomorrow, hopefully. It’s just a constant drip, drip, drip.

Did you hear back from Sarah about the Macmillan nurse? Not yet, no. I left her a message this morning. She sounded… pretty rough on the phone last time, poor thing. Yeah, she did. I’m really worried about her, you know? It’s just… a lot. It is. But she's being so brave. She says she's focusing on the small things, enjoying the sunshine when there is any. That’s good, isn’t it? Trying to compartmentalize. Still… the chemo’s really taken its toll, hasn’t it? It has. And the scan results… I’m just praying they haven’t detected anything new. Me too. I’m going to pop over next week, just to take her some meals and do a bit of tidying up. Anything I can do. That's really lovely, love. She'll appreciate that. I was just thinking, maybe we should coordinate so we’re not both hovering at once? Good point. I’ll wait for Sarah to get back to me about what days would work best. Right, house situation… Oh yes. Still nothing concrete on the planning permission? Not yet. I got an automated email saying they're still reviewing the application. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? The Sanderson’s are putting their place on the market, though. Really? The cottage on the green? That's lovely. Yes, the one we were talking about last month. Apparently, they’re downsizing. It’s going on with Humphrey & Finch next week. Humphrey & Finch, right. Expensive as always. I wonder if they’ve got any more planning inconsistencies? That’s what I was thinking. Their extensions always push the boundary, don’t they? I'm almost scared to look, incase it's just a pipe dream. It would be perfect though, wouldn't it? That garden alone… and so close to the village. It is. But getting planning permission for any kind of extension would be a nightmare. Given the history of this place, you know. Mrs. Fitzwilliam still brings it up every time we see her! Oh, bless her. Honestly, you'd think the drama of that pergola happened yesterday. It feels like it sometimes. Still, we've got to try. If the Sanderson's place is available... Let's not get ahead of ourselves. Let's wait and see what the planning department says about our initial design. And check if that cottage even falls within our budget!

Honestly, the instant coffee in the kitchen. It's genuinely offensive. Like, who buys that stuff? It tastes like burnt socks. Tell me about it! And they don't even put any milk in the fridge. Just those weird long life cartons that taste vaguely of plastic. It's a crime against coffee, really. Right? And the noise! I swear some of these students think they’re living in a nightclub. Bangs and shouting until three in the morning. I used to get a decent lie-in, you know? Now, it's just a constant bombardment. Oh, the noise is bad. But it's the passive-aggressive notes they leave. Like, “Please be considerate of other residents.” Like, yeah, thanks, Captain Obvious. As if a strongly worded note is going to stop them from playing their music at full volume. I hate those notes. They're always so sanctimonious. You'd think they’d just knock on the door and have a chat, wouldn’t you? But no, a note. Exactly! And the way they leave the communal areas. Honestly, it’s like a student bomb went off sometimes. Crumbs everywhere, dirty dishes piled up… Don’t even start me on the dishes. I spent twenty minutes scrubbing a baked bean tin off a plate the other day. Twenty minutes! I’ve got better things to do. Seriously! And those motivational posters in the common room. “Reach for the stars!” “Believe in yourself!” It’s just… so cheesy. I want to rip them down. I know, right? Like, we're all trying to keep these students safe and sound, and they’re being bombarded with cheesy inspirational quotes. The irony is killing me. And the pile of recycling? It’s overflowing constantly. You can’t even get near the bins. It smells awful, too. Oh, the smell! It’s a permanent fixture. Cardboard and old pizza boxes radiating their pungent aroma. It’s a biohazard, truly. I think my least favourite thing though… has to be the endless scrolling on TikTok at all hours. You can hear them through the walls. Just constant tapping and giggling. You're not wrong. It's strangely irritating, isn’t it? It’s just… relentless. Makes you want to move out. Tell me about it. I'm yearning for silence and a clean kitchen. Maybe I'll invest in some earplugs. And a hazmat suit for the bins.

Honestly, it’s mad how many English faces you see in Belgium, isn’t it? We were in Antwerp yesterday, and I swear half the people were speaking English. It’s just the package tours, love. They flock to it. Always have done. Remember when we went to Spain back in… well, a good while ago? Every other café seemed to be filled with Croydon accents. Oh, I remember! And the football shirts! It was a sight to behold. Though, Antwerp was lovely, wasn’t it? Bit busier than I expected. The traffic getting in was a nightmare. It was! We spent nearly an hour crawling along. I almost wished I’d learned a bit of Dutch just to shout at the other cars. Don't you dare! Wouldn't do you any good. They’d just look at you like you were daft. Best stick to English rhyming, that's a language everyone understands. Like what, Dad? Well, "fat cat," "hat rat," you know the sort of thing. Gets a laugh every time. Oh, Dad. Seriously though, I’m trying to learn a bit of French now, for uni. It’s surprisingly hard. It is. I always wanted to learn Spanish, but the grammar... it’s just too much. Remember when we used to go to Herne Bay for shopping? That was easier than learning Spanish! Oh my god, yes! Remember that awful little department store? It always smelled of mothballs and disappointment. And you’d always try and convince me that the hideous Christmas decorations were "charming”. They were! Still are! I love a good Christmas market. We should go to one in Germany this year. Oh, I’d love that! Though I need to be careful with my feet. They've been playing up a bit lately. We can take it easy then and just enjoy the atmosphere. Have you heard from Liam? His birthday’s coming up. He called yesterday. Says he’s got a puppy. A little Jack Russell. Oh, how lovely! Bless him. It’s nice to hear he’s happy. It is. It's been such a difficult few years, with Aunt Susan... it's good to see the family doing alright. They're a tough bunch, alright. Remember raising those boys? You were a whirlwind, Carol! Don't remind me! All the school plays, the football matches… it was exhausting, but worth it.

So, did you see what happened with the equality vote? It was mental. Mental is right! Honestly, I couldn't believe it. How could they vote against it? It’s 2024! I know! Everyone at school was going crazy about it. Liam was proper fuming, said it was like going back to the dark ages. Your Liam, always with the dramatic pronouncements. Still, he’s got a point. Did you vote? Nah, I’m too young, remember. But my mum and dad did. Mum was practically shouting at the TV when they announced the result. Your mum definitely would have. She's got principles, your mum. I voted, of course. It’s just… frustrating, you know? To think we’re still having this conversation in Ireland. It's a bit mad isn't it, especially when you consider how much stuff has changed. Like, my nan, she wouldn't even believe how much things have moved on. Your nan? She probably thinks women shouldn't even have the vote! Just kidding. Sort of. Haha! She’s a bit traditional, yeah. She still thinks marriage is the way to go, you know. Like, you have to get married before you can move in together. Oh, bless her. My mum’s the same, ironically. Always going on about the importance of marriage, while simultaneously embarrassing me every chance she gets. How so? Last week, I was talking to a rather nice gentleman at the park, you know, while Poppy was playing. And my mum just… walked over and started asking him if he was married and if he had grandchildren. In front of  me ! Oh no! That's brutal! Brutal is an understatement. I wanted the earth to swallow me whole. Poppy just looked at me and started giggling. Mortifying. That’s gold! My mum's always doing stuff like that. Like, she bought me a "World's Best Son" mug for my birthday last year. Oh, that’s a classic embarrassing-mum move. I know! And she keeps threatening to get one for Dad too. He’ll be mortified. It's my birthday next month. Are you gonna get me anything? Of course, silly! Have you got any ideas? Hmm... I don't know. Maybe some new trainers? Or a new game? I’m trying to save up for that new football game, you know. Right, well we’ll see what we can do.

Right then, you’ve got that new set of lathe tools, haven’t you, Margaret? Fancy bits of kit, they are. Better than the ones I used to have, that’s for sure. Yes, dear. David managed to get a good deal on them, actually. Said they were top of the line, apparently. Do you think they'll be any difference? You were quite the whiz with a lathe yourself. Oh, I was alright. Managed to turn out a few respectable bowls, I did. Though nowadays my hands aren’t what they used to be. Arthritis, you know. Still, good to see you two keeping busy. David restoring that old Singer sewing machine, and you with those posh tools… all a bit much for me, really. It’s good to have hobbies, Arthur. Keeps the mind sharp. Margaret's been doing a marvelous job with that bird table. Quite the craftsman. Don’t be silly, David. It’s just a bit of wood and some glue. Speaking of wood, this chicken is a bit dry, isn’t it? Needs more gravy. Margaret, you always made a cracking gravy. I’ll make some more after lunch. It was a bit of a rush this morning. Did you hear about what happened down the road? Little Timmy Henderson’s hamster… Don’t tell me… Oh, for goodness sake, Margaret! Must you? Let’s not. Well, it's terrible, Arthur. Apparently, his little sister, bless her heart, put the hamster in the microwave. Just for a few seconds, she said, to warm it up. In the microwave! Good heavens. The poor little thing. Was it… Margaret, really! Arthur doesn't need to hear that. It’s dreadful enough as it is. Kids these days, eh? No sense. I know, it’s shocking. The police were called, you know. Apparently, the mother is distraught. I feel awful for her, you know. Well, it's a tragedy. A real tragedy. You can't just put a hamster in a microwave, can you? What was she thinking? She wasn't  thinking , Arthur. That's the point. Little monsters, some of them. Still, they’re young, right? They learn. It does make you think, though, doesn’t it? About how quickly things can go wrong. It certainly does. Reminds me of the time my cousin Horace… well, another story for another day. It involved a potato and a very unfortunate incident with a drainpipe… Oh, not another one of Horace’s tales, Arthur.

Honestly, I was reading about this mirror-writing thing online. Apparently, it’s not as rare as people think. Someone managed to write an entire novel backwards, and then read it in a mirror! Really? That’s quite something. How on earth would you even start? It sounds like a nightmare. More effort than doing my accounts, definitely. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? Reminds me of Leonardo da Vinci. He wrote like that, you know. Probably to keep his secrets safe. Exactly! But this was a modern person. I wonder if it’s a sign of some sort of… neurological quirk? Probably just a very dedicated eccentric. Speaking of finances, did you see the news about those banks considering charging for holding people's money? Don't even start! Can you imagine? We're already drowning in debt as it is. It's outrageous. It's a slippery slope. They’ll be charging us just to breathe next! Back in my day, you earned a decent wage for a decent job. Now… Tell me about it. House prices alone are enough to bankrupt a generation. Remember when you could buy a semi-detached for the price of a small flat now? It's madness. We're lucky we bought when we did. Though, that mortgage still looms... Marriage and mortgages, two wonderful and expensive burdens. All part of life, dear. Speaking of burdens, have you seen that story about the cat who got stuck in a Christmas tree? It was on the news this morning. Oh, the ginger one? The poor thing! It was hanging upside down like a furry ornament. Cats. Always getting themselves into scrapes. It’s their nature. Just like politicians. Don’t even get me started on American politics! It's all so dramatic. It feels like a reality show sometimes. All that shouting and posturing. It’s distracting from the real issues, that’s what it is. Much prefer my cryptic crossword. Keeps the brain ticking. Anyone fancy a go after dinner? I'm no good at those. You always beat me. It's not fair. I can barely work my television remote some times. Technology is the bane of my existence. That’s because you never update your software! I’ll have a look at it for you later. Now, about that plastic bag charge… do you think it's made any difference? I still see people struggling with overflowing bags at the supermarket.

Honestly, you two are glued to those screens. Not a single book has been opened all afternoon. But Mum, Ninjago is amazing! Lloyd just got a new dragon! Yeah! And I built a whole new village in Minecraft! It's got a secret underwater base. A secret underwater base, really? And that's more important than reading a story? Well, yeah! It's interactive. I can  build  the story. I understand that’s engaging, but reading helps your imagination too, you know. It lets you visualise… But in Minecraft,  I  visualise! I make it all myself! Look! See? It's got a waterfall and everything! It's very impressive, darling. Truly. But sometimes, just  thinking  something up, without the blocks and the dragons... that's a different kind of strength. But the Ninjago sets are so cool. I’m saving up for the new Temple of Airjin. It's got a rotating tower and a snake army! A snake army... right. And what about this Lego Ninjago book I bought? The one with all the backstories? Ugh, that’s boring. Real Ninjago is playing with the Lego. I know, I know. It’s hard to compete with flashing lights and exploding buildings. What’s the most impressive thing you’ve built in your Minecraft world, Adrian? I made a roller coaster that goes through a volcano. It's so fast. And it goes underwater too! A rollercoaster through a volcano and underwater? That  is  impressive. Still, just for a little while, could you put them away? We could build a Lego castle together – a  real  one, out of bricks. But Mum, I’m in the middle of a quest! Kai got captured and I need to rescue him! Kai can wait five minutes. Five minutes to build a castle with your mum. Please? Can I still play it later? Of course you can. Just five minutes. Let's see if we can build a better castle than the one in Ninjago! Fine. But Kai's still waiting. Where’s the grey bricks? Need lots of grey for walls! There they are, darling. Let's get building. Do you want me to start the foundations? It’s very important to get the foundations right. You know, like in Minecraft...but real. Hmmm. Maybe we can make it have a secret room too. Like in my Minecraft world. Now you're talking. A secret room it is!

Right then, coffees all ready! Let’s all settle in. How was the drive for you two? It was alright, Mum. A bit drizzly but nothing too bad. The M6 was surprisingly quiet. Yeah, fairly smooth journey. Though I nearly got stuck behind a tractor for about ten minutes, which was a laugh. Proper countryside moment, you know? Oh, those are the best! Did you both manage to get your bearings alright? Lichfield can be a bit confusing if you’re not used to it. We're fine, Mum. Emma navigated brilliantly. It’s a lovely little place though, nicer than I remember. Definitely a nicer vibe than Manchester, that’s for sure. A bit more…serene. So, tell us everything about the holiday. You seemed really relaxed in your photos. Oh, it was lovely! Absolutely lovely. Cornwall, remember? The Cornish coastline is just breathtaking. We did loads of walking, mostly along the coastal paths - plenty of fresh sea air. And the fish and chips! Remember those, Em? They were unreal. So fresh. Yes! The fish practically jumped onto the plate. What was your favourite part, Mum? Honestly, it was just the peace. Waking up to the sound of the sea every morning, having breakfasts on the little balcony…it was bliss. There’s a little cove down near Penzance, Mousehole, that was particularly beautiful. We spent an afternoon just paddling and collecting sea glass. You even managed to get a tan! I was rather jealous, as usual. A faint tan! Don’t get carried away. Honestly, Middleton was amazing too, we had some delicious food, a truly lovely experience. So, what are we doing today then? Are we going into Lichfield city centre for a wander? I’ve heard they have a really good vintage shop. Ooh, yes! Let’s do that. And maybe grab a cheeky ice cream. It  is  still summer, technically. I thought we could go to the Cathedral first. It’s always worth a visit, even if you've been before. And then maybe lunch, and after that, the vintage shop sounds lovely. Perfect. Maybe if the weather's good afterwards we could go for a walk in Stowe Pool? I’d love to see the swans. That's a wonderful idea. Anything you need, just let me know. Are you two hungry yet? I made a Victoria sponge this morning, still warm from the oven.

Right, who’s got the ham and cheese? I’m starving. Here, yeah. Massive one. Did you see Mr. Davies’ face when Liam tripped over his feet in assembly? Proper mortified! He looked like he wanted the floor to swallow him whole. Honestly, Liam's a disaster sometimes. He is, isn't he? But it’s hilarious. Anyway, Ms. Patel said we need to start thinking about prefect nominations. Seriously? Already? Who do you reckon’s going to go for it? Definitely Chloe and Daniel. Chloe’s been sucking up to all the teachers for weeks now. Yeah, she’s been practically hanging around Ms. Johnson’s office. Total brown-noser. Think Liam would even bother? Nah, he’d just fall over trying to give his speech. Remember when he tried to do that presentation on the Tudors? Don't remind me. He kept getting the names wrong and got confused between Henry VIII and Elizabeth I. Classic Liam. So, playing Uno after this? I’m feeling lucky. Yeah, but you’re cheating again, aren’t you? You always hide the reverse cards. Me? Never! It's a strategic advantage. Besides, did you see what's happening in Ukraine? It's mental. Don't start, Finn. We're trying to have a relaxing lunch. It's depressing enough as it is. I just...it's worrying, isn't it? Like, how close are we to…you know? My mum was saying it’s all because of Putin. She's always going on about how Russia is expanding again, like in the old days. My dad says it’s all down to NATO pushing eastward. It’s complicated. It is. Anyway, back to more important things…did you guys see the new episode of “Cosmic Crusaders”? Dude! The space battle was insane! Did you see when Captain Nebula used the… Okay, okay, no spoilers for people who haven’t seen it yet! By the way, did you hear Zara and Aisha had a row in the toilets? Apparently, it was about who gets to sit next to Raja in history. Raja's such a prize. Everyone fancies him. He's alright, I guess. Heard he got a scholarship application looked over by his uncle, who is apparently a general in the army. Seriously? That’s sneaky. Are all his relatives military? Probably. Slough’s full of them, isn’t it? My cousin’s dad was in the Navy.

Ugh, Mr. Harrison is  still  marking our momentum questions. Seriously, it's been like, a week. I know, right? He's so slow. Remember last year when he marked those essays for, like, three months? Don't remind me! I blocked that out. At least he's not as bad as Mrs. Davies, though. She just stares at you when you ask a question. Oh god, yeah. It's like, “Don’t bother me with your tiny human queries!” Exactly! And our form tutor, Miss Evans, is being weird. She keeps making these random announcements like, "Remember to smile!" Seriously? What’s with that? Is she trying to win some positivity award? I think so. It's so forced. Remember that time she tried to get us all to do a "gratitude circle" after a particularly chaotic assembly? Oh my gosh, I’d forgotten! Emily nearly exploded with laughter. Me too! It was epic. Anyway, did you finish reading  To Kill a Mockingbird  for English? Mostly. It’s a bit heavy, isn’t it? I keep getting distracted. I watched  17 Again  last night and now I just want to pretend I’m in high school again, skipping lectures and eating pizza. That sounds pretty good, actually. I’ve been meaning to watch that. Is it any good? It's cheesy, but in a good way. Really funny. And Matthew Perry is just brilliant. Right. I’ll add it to my list. What about Sophie and Chloe? Are they still being weird about the new boy, Finn? Oh, definitely. They’re like a pack of wolves, circling him in the lunch queue. Chloe actually tripped over her own feet trying to get closer to him. Classic Chloe. Remember last week when she spilled her smoothie all over Mrs. Peterson? Oh, the horror! Mrs. Peterson looked like she was about to have a stroke. Poor thing. Speaking of English lessons, Mr. Bell says we might have to do some creative writing now. Ugh, really? I can’t be bothered. That’s so much harder than analysing a poem. I know! I'm terrible at making things up. I always end up with awkward descriptions of vegetables. You and your vegetable descriptions! Maybe we should write a story about a smoothie-wielding girl who falls for a mysterious new boy? Hmm, that’s not bad. But we need a really dramatic plot twist.

So, Transylvania, seriously? You’re actually going? Yeah! It's been a dream for ages. Vlad the Impaler, spooky castles, forests... I’m proper buzzing for it. You're mental! But I'm jealous. Seriously, that sounds amazing. More amazing than, like, a week in Bournemouth, anyway. Bournemouth’s not exactly a thrilling destination, is it? Gotta say, Transylvania’s a bit more… adventurous. Exactly! I've booked a little place in Sighisoara. Apparently, it's where Vlad was born. You're going to find yourself haunted, I'm telling you. I hope so! A  friendly  haunting. What are you guys doing for the summer, anyway? Besides, you know, being sensible. Sensible is my middle name. I'm mostly staying here, running the café. Might have a few trips to the coast, but nothing wild. How about you, Liam? Still working, mainly. Some shifts at the pub, trying to save up for… something. Not sure what yet. Maybe a ridiculously expensive espresso machine. Sounds fair dinkum, mate. You gotta treat yourself. Proper good, that. What’s “fair dinkum?” Is that like… genuine? Yeah, deadset. Genuine, true blue. Like, "that’s fair dinkum good coffee.” You know? Oh, right! I've heard you say that before. It's cute, in a bizarre way. Hey! It’s just how we talk. You London lot are all about your slang too. True, true. Heard about Chloe and Ben? Apparently, they broke up. Dramatic stuff. No way! I thought they were solid. What happened? Apparently, a girl from his football team. Total cliché. Awful stuff. Those things always are. Listen, I'm booked to do a private party next weekend. Anyone free to come along? It’s a fancy dress thing - 80s. I might be able to swing it. Fancy dress… hmm. Should I go as a questionable patron of a vintage coffee shop? Perfect! I’m in, definitely. I'll go as Madonna. I'll think about it. Got to check the café schedule first. But 80s, eh? That'll be fun. I’ve been thinking about laser eye surgery actually. Have any of you looked into that? No, way too risky for me. I’m happy with my specs, thanks. Yeah, I’ve had a look. Seems pretty pricey, doesn’t it? Lots of hoops to jump through. I'll stick with my contacts for now. Scary though, isn’t it?

Right, so, the playlist for Saturday’s party... what are we thinking? Definitely need some Dua Lipa, don’t we? Dua! Dancing! Trampolines! Yes, trampolines, darling, but we need music for before the trampolines, too. Something a bit… moodier. Think Mumford and Sons, maybe? Mumford? Like... bears? Not  like  bears, sweetie. It's a band. They make lovely music. But we need some bangers later, don’t we? For when everyone’s properly let loose. Bangs! Loud bangs! Be careful now, remember what we talked about – no shouting or…  words . No bad words, Mummy! Exactly! Now, about the photos... I was thinking a little Alice in Wonderland theme for our family photos, you two. Wouldn't that be fun? Alice! Big hats! Rabbit hole! Yes! A rabbit hole! And you can be the Queen of Hearts, darling. And you, my little knight. Though, you might need a slightly less muddy outfit for that after your go on the obstacle course yesterday, didn't you? It was  amazing ! So muddy! I jumped over the tires and everything! He was slippy! Slippy indeed. We’ll need to give you a good scrub before the photoshoot. What are you both having for lunch? I was thinking pasta. Pasta! With cheese! And tomato sauce! Pizza! Like at the party! We can’t have pizza every day, sweethearts, but pasta it is. I'll put it on. Speaking of the party, I need to sort out some more fairy lights. And maybe some more of those little aerial hoop things – remember how much you loved those last time? Aerial hoop! Spinning! Mummy, can I do a flip? Well, maybe if you’re very careful and I’m there to spot you. But first, let’s eat some lunch. And then we'll figure out how many pink roses we need for Alice’s garden. Right? Pink! Lots of pink! And mud! A little mud for the Queen. Alright, alright, a  little  mud for the Queen. But no real mud in the photos, please! Now, who wants to help Mummy chop some tomatoes? And remember… no bad words! Absolutely no bad words. Even for the Queen. Speaker_2 & 3: No! Good, that’s my little angels. Now let’s get chopping! Fairy lights… roses… pasta… obstacle course cleanup… this is going to be a busy weekend. And I still need to book the photographer for those family photos.

Speaker_1 : Right then, who’s having another slice? This pizza's better than Betty used to make, bless her. Speaker_3 : Don't be saying that, Arthur! Betty's pizzas were legendary. This is good, mind, but legendary is a different category. Speaker_2 : David, you’re just being picky. It’s lovely. And look at this roulade, Freelancer, it's gorgeous! Did you make it? Speaker_4 : Yeah, I helped a bit. It’s for celebrating, isn’t it? Speaker_5 : Definitely celebrating! Emily got her results today! There you go, good girl. What did you get, love? Four A’s and a B, Grandad! Going to Cambridge! Cambridge! Fantastic, Emily! Well done! That’s brilliant news. What are you going to study? English Literature. Oh, fantastic! Reading all day! Sounds like heaven. Can you tweet a picture of the pizza? It looks amazing! Chloe! I’m not tweeting a picture of my pizza! Typical teenage behaviour. Always on their phones. Back in my day, we celebrated with a cup of tea and a biscuit. No tweeting. Though I never quite understood Twitter anyway. What’s the point? It's just people showing off, Arthur. Posting pictures of their lunch and things. Don’t get started. It’s not just for showing off, Grandad. Sometimes it’s about sharing things, like news, or supporting people. She’s got a point, Arthur. It’s a way to keep in touch. Remember when Emily was practicing driving? I saw her tweet a photo of her nail-biting attempt at a parallel park. Dad! Don’t remind me! I nearly gave up right there and then. And didn't your mother go to Parents' Evening last week? Oh, that was a performance from Sarah, your headteacher! Don't even mention her. She gave me the full pressure-point speech again about homework and extra lessons. Said I needed to push Emily more. Speaker_4 : Tell her, Dad! I’m already stressed! Remember when young Tom fell out of the tree trying to get the cat down? Broke his arm, he did. That was a memorable day. And then there was the time your cousin Trevor tried to build that shed… ended up collapsing on top of him. Oh, the shed! I'd nearly forgotten that one. He was under that pile of wood for ages before we found him. Oh my God! Did he get hurt? I'm hungry.

Right, so I was reading this article about animal communication the other day... it was fascinating. Apparently, prairie dogs have incredibly complex alarm calls, differentiating between the size, speed and even the colour of potential predators. Really? That's incredible. Dad, you'd be interested in this. You know, you always said the birds in the garden were telling you something. Hmm. Well, they’re probably telling me to get rid of that blasted squirrel that keeps stealing the berries. Though I’m not sure they're using alarm calls. More like a constant chattering. They probably are! It's probably a very complex dialect. I mean, think about it – linguistics isn't just about human language, is it? Exactly! And the article mentioned ongoing research looking into dolphin whistles… Apparently, each dolphin has a unique signature whistle. Right. Right. Pointless. Anyway, my move. You're in check, Sarah. Honestly, Dad, you’re relentless. Always bringing me back to the chess. Did you record that documentary about Winston Churchill this morning? Yes, watched about half of it. Too long. Far too long. Though, he was a force, wasn’t he? Definitely. A complicated force, though. I’m reading a bit about Scottish independence at the moment, and you can’t avoid Churchill popping up in the arguments. It’s always Churchill, isn't it? Everything goes back to Churchill. Speaking of things that are complicated, did you ever find a good solution for those bookmarks you were complaining about? Still using receipts, thank you very much. Practical. Practical and aesthetically jarring. You know, I saw this lovely Japanese paper clip bookmark – I’d be happy to send you some nice ones from Korea. They have some stunning designs. I can show you after this game. Korea, eh? Bit far for a bookmark, isn't it? Although… I did hear they have some excellent tea. Everything in Korea is excellent. It's a fascinating country. Though, I worry about people getting deported… I read a case the other day. Horrible. Gets you thinking. Don’t get all political on me during a game of chess, Sarah. Move your rook. Fine, fine. But you can’t deny it’s important. What are you having for lunch later? I was thinking beans on toast. Simple, satisfying. Beans on toast sounds good. I might try and pop out for some decent coffee afterwards. The stuff in the house is… questionable.

This pierogi are genuinely amazing, aren’t they? I could eat a plateful. They’re proper good! Definitely better than the ones I had in Krakow. So, how are the students shaping up? Still got the boy who thinks 'very' is an adjective to end all adjectives? Oh, absolutely. He’s still going strong. And using “very” to describe everything from the weather to his grandma. Bless him. It’s a challenge, but you know, that's what makes it interesting. What about your lot? Are they assimilating well? Yeah, pretty good, actually. A few of them are struggling with the grammar, as you’d expect, but they’re all really keen. One of them’s obsessed with Netflix, though – keeps trying to incorporate American slang into his essays. Oh, dear. That’s a tricky one. Tell him to stick to the textbook! Though, speaking of financial woes… have you had any luck with that horrifying student loan situation? Don't even mention it! It's like this endless black hole. I'm paying peanuts back each month and it barely makes a dent. Makes you question the whole system, doesn’t it? Especially when you’re over here working abroad for less than you’d be earning back home. Absolutely. And the pension situation… don’t even get me started. It’s a mess. I’m perpetually terrified I’ll be living on lentils and Polish vodka in my old age. Tell me about it. Trying to think about retirement is just… depressing. Right, so, are we thinking Tarnów back to Krakow, or should we loop around to that slightly bigger town, Nowe Brzesko? Hmmm, Brzesko has a decent supermarket, doesn’t it? And I need to chase up that MOT for the car. Apparently, they’re very strict here. Don’t want to get pulled over. True. Less hassle driving through Brzesko then. And I need to stock up on some decent coffee before heading back. This stuff is... passable. Passable is putting it mildly! It’s like drinking muddy water sometimes. Did you see that article about the consent workshops they’re doing in schools back home? No, what about it? Apparently, they’re quite radical, teaching kids about boundaries and what constitutes consent, even at primary school level. It's controversial, of course. Some people think it’s going too far. I think it’s brilliant, to be honest.

So, Human Sciences, yeah? Still thinking that's the one? Yeah, pretty much. It's just… a lot, isn't it? Like, how much reading are we actually talking? Apparently loads. But you're good at that kind of thing. I'd drown in all the social theory. Maths is your brain, man. I’d be lost. True, but I'm kind of worried it’ll be too much theory and not enough actual... stuff. Like, I like the idea of understanding how people tick, but will I really learn anything practical? I don’t know. I keep hearing it’s really interdisciplinary. You could end up doing some pretty interesting projects, apparently. Yeah, but what if I hate it? Like, what if I realize halfway through first year that it’s completely not for me? Well, you can switch, can't you? Or just grind it out. You always grind it out. I guess so. What about you? Still holding out for Maths? Yeah, definitely. Always wanted to do something with stats, you know? Maybe data analysis or something. Less theory, more numbers. Perfect. Sounds good. So, are you going to try and get into Cambridge then? Honestly, I'm terrified. It's a long shot, isn't it? But I figure, why not try? Yeah, go for it! You’ve got the grades, you’ve got the potential. Don't sell yourself short. Easy for you to say. You’re practically guaranteed a place. Don't be ridiculous. It’s still tough. Right, speaking of tough, fancy a beer? Seriously? We're supposed to be studying! Relax. It's Friday. We deserve it. What are you thinking? Lager? Something stronger? Maybe just a cider. Don't want to end up embarrassingly drunk in front of potential uni professors. Fair enough. I’m having a pint of Guinness. Need to build up my resilience for those massive lectures. You're something else. So, rugby this weekend? Are you still playing? Yeah, big match against Harrow on Saturday. Gonna be brutal. You coming down to watch? Probably. Need to see if I can get a lift. It’s a trek from Slough. I'll sort you out a ride. Don’t worry about it. Just be there. After the match, we could grab some food. That Italian place down the road is decent. Sounds good. I’m starving already. You thinking of cooking anything anytime soon?

So, Dad, you were saying you didn’t agree with this new windfall tax? No, I don’t. Not at all, Sarah. It's just… shortsighted, is what it is. They’re trying to grab a quick win, you see, but it's only going to discourage investment. But surely, if these energy companies are making record profits… isn't it fair to take a little bit? Fair? Well, that's a sticky word, isn’t it? It’s easy to say 'fair' when you’re not the one facing the consequences. Look, they’ve already invested heavily in renewable energy, haven't they? They're moving away from oil and gas. This tax just makes it harder to finance that transition. I suppose so. It just feels like they’re exploiting the situation. People are really struggling with their energy bills. Precisely. But taxing existing profits doesn't magically lower bills. It just shifts the burden somewhere else. It’ll be consumers paying in the long run, mark my words. The government needs to look at long-term solutions, not these knee-jerk reactions. Like what? What do you think they should be doing? Incentivising energy efficiency, for a start. Insulation grants, making it easier for people to switch to renewables. And a proper review of the energy market. Monopolies aren’t good for anyone. It’s a complicated mess, isn't it? All intertwined. It is. Trust me, I've spent a lifetime wrestling with tax laws and financial regulations. It’s never as simple as it seems on the news. They love to simplify things, don't they? Makes for better headlines. They do. So, do you think it’ll actually change anything? The windfall tax, I mean? No, I don't. It'll generate some revenue, certainly. But it won't solve the underlying problems and could even make things worse. They'll be burdened with the headache of auditing and allocating the revenue, all while the underlying problems remain… it’s just a sticking plaster on a broken leg. You always were a pessimist, Dad. I'm a realist, Sarah. A realist. There’s a difference. Look at the corporation tax changes – another mess. They were reducing it, then raising it again… what signal does that send to businesses trying to plan for the future? So, you think the government's just making it up as they go along?

Honestly, Mum, the meeting was a disaster. Absolute carnage. Oh no, really? What happened? You sounded alright when you rang earlier. I was trying to be! But Mr. Davies just kept interrupting. He steamrolled over my entire plan for the Henderson project. Said it wasn't "bold" enough. Oh, Davies. He’s always been a bit… much, hasn’t he? Remember when he tried to get Ms. Thornton fired for letting the students wear trainers on "Dress Down Day"? Don't remind me! But this was actual professional sabotage. He then proceeded to present  his  plan - which was basically the same as mine but with, like, a flashy PowerPoint and a made-up acronym. Oh, the cheek! Did anyone else speak up for you? Sarah did, bless her. She said my initial proposal was "sensible and well-researched”, which is Sarah’s way of saying boring, but it was nice to have someone backing me. Good for Sarah. You know, David had a similar situation back at the factory, years ago. Clive, the manager, kept taking credit for his ideas. David was so frustrated, he just walked away and found a better job. Sometimes, that’s the best course of action. I wish I had the guts to just walk! But then the Henderson project would be a mess and I’d look bad. It's that whole career ladder thing. It is a dreadful thing. You know your Auntie Maureen, the one who runs the bric-a-brac stall? She always says, “A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.” Sensible woman, that Maureen. You and your Auntie Maureen. So, how was your week? Anything exciting? Any drama with the exam results yet? Oh, you know. Mr. Peterson nearly had a meltdown over a missing mark on a History paper. Apparently, it was the difference between a C and a D. Can you imagine the pressure these kids are under these days? Absolutely ridiculous. I can. My friend Liam’s stressing about his A-Levels. He’s convinced he’s going to fail maths. Maths! Honestly, why do they insist on making it so complicated? Back in my day, it was just sums and fractions. Simpler times. Tell me about it. Anyway, I'm thinking of going for a drink with Chloe and Maya tonight. Fancy joining us? Oh, I'd love to, darling, but I've promised to help Mrs. Higgins with her garden.

Right then, who’s fancying a game of Scrabble? I’ve got the board out. Ooh, yeah! Sounds good, Dad. Are we having wine with it? Definitely wine. I’m proper parched. What did you get, Sarah? Anything decent? Just a sauvignon blanc, nothing fancy. I’ve been trying to find a good reasonably priced one, you know? All this wine goes down a treat though. I’ve got a decent Rioja chilling, lad. You’ll appreciate that. Better than that fizzy stuff you are drinking usually. Hey! That's not fair. I like Prosecco sometimes. It's light and refreshing. He's just teasing, Liam. Seriously though, Dad, did you ever hear back from Auntie Brenda about that old photo album? I was asking about it last week. Aye, she rang. Said she’d found it tucked away in the attic. Sent a few pictures to me, you won’t believe how young we all looked. Proper little nippers. Oh, cool! Can I see them? I’ll show you later. You’d be laughing, though. Look at me in that one, wearing a flat cap. Don’t know why I ever thought that looked good. You always had a thing for flat caps! Anyway, I was thinking, should we all try to get together with Chloe and Mark next weekend? It’s been ages. Yeah, definitely. I could do with seeing them. I've been swamped with this new project at work, it’s a nightmare. All deadlines and no breathing space. That’s modern life, isn’t it? Always rushing about. I remember when things were a bit quieter. Always loved this place used to have time for birds and nature. So, Scrabble then? Liam, you’re going first. Don't be playing silly games and just using the high-scoring letters. No promises! But seriously, Sarah, any luck with those job applications? It's a bit of a slog to be honest. I’ve sent out about fifteen in the last few weeks, and heard nothing back. Thinking about maybe updating my CV. They’re all like that now, lass. Competition's fierce. You've got to stand out. Maybe try those agencies down in Newcastle. I could have a look at your CV if you like? Mine's been through a few eyes with work, maybe I can offer a fresh perspective. That would be amazing, Liam, thank you.

Honestly, the marking pile is ridiculous this week. I swear, they’re deliberately trying to sabotage me. Half of them seem to think ‘their’ and ‘there’ are interchangeable - it’s infuriating! I hear you. I had a whole essay filled with “your” instead of "you're." It’s like they haven't even glanced at the grammar rules. You’d think after Year 10… Exactly! They’ve had years of it drilled into them. Though, to be fair, some of them are struggling with things outside of school too. One lad's parents barely speak English, so it’s tough for him to get support at home. That's true. It's never a simple case, is it? Still, doesn’t excuse the ‘their/there’ situation! So, how was the conference in Bristol? Did you pick up any brilliant new teaching strategies? Oh, don't even  start  me on the conference. It was just…a lot. All very ‘buzzwordy’ and nothing particularly practical. We spent an hour discussing ‘learner-centered pedagogy’ when I just wanted to know how to deal with the kids who spend the entire lesson scrolling through TikTok. I know exactly what you mean. Remember that conference in Exeter last year? “Differentiated learning environments utilising transformative assessment practices”? Honestly, I walked away feeling more confused than when I went in. Precisely! And the keynote speaker? Dreadful. Kept talking about ‘synergy’ and ‘thinking outside the box.’ It was like a bad business seminar, not a teaching conference. Mine was equally underwhelming. A woman who’d apparently written a book on ‘mindfulness in the classroom’ spent the entire presentation promoting  her  book. Very subtle, that. Ugh, the self-promotion! Always a classic. Did you at least manage to sneak away for a nice dinner somewhere? Bristol's got some decent restaurants, right? I did! Found a lovely little Italian place just off the harbour. That was the highlight, honestly. Needed a good plate of pasta after all that motivational jargon. See, that’s what conferences should be about. Good food and a bit of a break from the madness. Did you meet any interesting people? A few. There was one teacher from a school in Devon, just outside Tavistock – seems like she’s doing some really innovative work with creative writing. We exchanged numbers, might be good to collaborate on something. That’s brilliant! It’s always good to connect with other teachers.

Right, so are we still on for that detour to the viewpoint? It’ll add maybe half an hour to the journey, but apparently, the views are incredible. Yeah, definitely. I saw a photo online – it looked stunning. Just… remind me, is it before or after Jasło? I’ve got my maps app going, but sometimes it gets a bit dodgy in these parts. After Jasło, yes. It's just past the big industrial estate. The GPS will probably lead you right there, but there’s a tiny little turning, so keep an eye out. It’s signposted, but… vaguely. Right, got it. You know, I’ve been trying to get back into a proper exercise routine. Poland isn’t exactly conducive to long walks, what with the roads and everything. Tell me about it. I'm desperately trying to tone up before… well, before the photo album gets made, I suppose. Being cooped up in a campervan isn't doing wonders for my thighs. I know the feeling! I was thinking about maybe doing some yoga in the mornings, when we wake up. We could use the space outside, if the weather’s decent. That’s a really good idea. I’ve got my mat in the back. I've been trying to read more, too. Finished that Cormac McCarthy novel you lent me. Bleak, but brilliant. ‘The Road’? Yeah, absolutely brutal, but stayed with me for days. I’m halfway through ‘Piranesi’ at the moment. It's completely different – very dreamlike. Have you heard of it? No, I haven't. What’s it about? It's hard to explain, really. It's about this guy who lives in a series of interconnected halls filled with tides and statues... very atmospheric. You might like it, actually. Bit weird, but fascinating. Sounds perfect, then. I'm always up for weird. Speaking of things that are fascinating… that woman we passed back in Tarnow, driving that ridiculous pink Fiat. What  was  she doing? I know! It was like a sugary explosion on wheels. Probably heading to some festival, I reckon. Polish people do love their festivals. True. It made me think about volunteering actually. After this trip, I’m thinking of looking into something. Maybe with animals? Or… I don't know, anything really. Just something to give me a bit more… purpose. That’s brilliant! It’s good to have something to aim for.

So, I was reading about the Vikings the other night, you know, for a bit of a change. Absolutely fascinating creatures, weren’t they? Not just pillaging and raiding - apparently, they were quite skilled navigators. Used the stars for guidance, you know. Amazing considering how rudimentary their technology must have been. That  is  fascinating, isn’t it? I mean, thinking about how far back people have travelled, given what we know now. It puts everything into perspective, doesn't it? This little life of ours… Exactly! And then you start thinking about things like… are we going to live forever? I’ve been reading up on gerontology, you know, the science of ageing. Apparently, telomeres, those little caps on the ends of our chromosomes, are key. They shorten every time a cell divides. Oh, right. I’ve heard something about that. So, like, when they get too short, that's… bad? Accelerates ageing? Precisely. Scientists are trying to find ways to lengthen them, you know, maybe even reverse the process. It's all a bit mad, but some research suggests we could significantly extend life expectancy. Some are even talking about immortality… not literally, of course, but pushing it far beyond what we’re used to. Immortality. That’s a bit much, isn't it? I’m happy just managing to get through this week with [toddler’s name] and all his demands! Honestly, sometimes I feel like everything’s shifting and moving too fast. I know, I know. It’s relentless. But think about that for a moment. We’re talking about potentially living to 150, 200, even more. Imagine the things you could see, do, learn... It's a scary thought, actually. More time to see people you love disappear. More time to worry. More time for… everything to go wrong. I understand. But there's risk in everything, isn't there? Even in staying where you are. Speaking of which, I was thinking… we should actually  do  something about this entire "living a life" business. I was thinking about that weekend kayaking trip we talked about? Kayaking? Where? The coast’s awfully rough this time of year. We could go to the Lee. It’s calmer there, sheltered. Just a few days, get away from it all. No Wi-Fi, fresh air, on the water… What do you say? Hmm… It  does  sound nice. But [toddler’s name] ...

This coffee's really good, actually. Much better than that instant stuff Dad usually makes. It is, isn't it? I’m glad you like it. I finally got around to fixing the coffee maker. It was driving me mad, all those grounds everywhere. Aye, it was a mess. You've done a good job, love. So, where did you get that coffee from? The little shop in town? Yeah, the one on the High Street. They do a decent selection. I saw loads of vouchers for it too, actually. Might be worth stocking up. I saw a really cute high chair online yesterday. For the baby. It's like a little wooden chair with a detachable tray. Oh, really? Where from? We need to start looking properly. Liam keeps saying he wants to get one before the end of the month. It was from that website, "Little Sprouts" or something. They have loads of lovely baby stuff, but it’s a bit pricey. We'll have to watch the money, won't we? This holiday’s already costing a bit. Those fish and chips last night... Don't start, Dad! It was a treat. Besides, we're having a quiet day today. Just going for a walk along the front. Remember that referendum? Everyone’s still moaning about it. Don't even go there. I’m trying to have a nice cup of coffee in peace. It’s the least I deserve after all the gardening I’ve been doing. The chickens are laying well, aren't they? Got a dozen eggs this morning. Yes, they are. You should bring some over for supper. Oh, and I was thinking about those sunglasses I saw at Primark. Should I get them? They were only five pounds. Five pounds? Go for it! It's not like you need to worry about your budget, are you? I’m saving up for that new plant pot I liked. What plant did you want. One of those really long trailing plants. I saw some lovely fruit trees at the garden centre yesterday. Little plum and apple trees. Would be nice to have in the garden, wouldn't it? That would be lovely, Dad. Maybe when we've got a bit more space. It is nice that Uncle David and Auntie Sarah got married again. They seem really happy together. It's nice to see them settled.

Honestly, the neighbours have been at it again. Banging around at all hours. It's driving me mad. Which ones? The ones with the yappy dog? Yes, them. I swear, they're deliberately doing it when I’m trying to sleep. I considered popping over, but then I thought, what's the point? It’ll just end in an argument. Mum, you're too nice. You should just tell them to quieten down. Easier said than done, love. Anyway, how’s work going? Are you still flat out with those campaigns? Yeah, it's manic. I’m trying to get everything tied up before the Christmas rush, but honestly, it’s like trying to herd cats. The client wants the moon on a stick, you know? Tell me about it. I had a patient the other day who was convinced she needed a full-body scrub with lemon juice because she read it on the internet. Oh my god! You've got some stories, haven't you? So many. Speaking of Christmas, are you still thinking of putting up the tree on the 1st of December? Definitely. It’s not Christmas until the tree's up and twinkling, is it? Although, I was thinking of getting one of those pre-lit ones this year. Less hassle. Oh, don’t you dare! It’s not the same. The smell of pine needles is essential. Plus, we both enjoy untangling those lights. It's our little tradition. Okay, okay, you’ve convinced me. Traditional tree it is. Although, I might treat myself to a new set of nail polishes. My nails are looking dreadful. You should! You deserve it. You've been working so hard. Speaking of treating yourself, how are things with Tom? Good! We're going to that German Christmas market in London next week. It’ll be so festive. Oh, how lovely! I always wanted to go to one of those. You know, I was reading about German Christmas traditions the other day… apparently, the Christmas tree tradition actually started in Germany. Really? I didn’t know that. Yeah, and the little wooden nutcrackers – those are from German folklore too. It's fascinating, really. Maybe when you've got some time, you could write a little blog post about it. You know, for your photography website. Hmm, that's an idea. I've been meaning to update it. My birthday’s coming up soon, too.

Right, so, verdict? What do you reckon of the flat? It’s… really nice! Honestly, it's so much bigger than I expected from the pictures. And the light is amazing. Glad you think so. It needs a bit of personality injecting, though, doesn't it? Feels a little… sterile. Definitely. We need blankets, cushions, photos… all the cosy bits. What about a rug for the living room? The floorboards are a bit chilly. Good shout. I was thinking about that. I’ve drafted a list actually, of things we need to get. We're going to need to hit up Ikea, I think. Oh god, a full Ikea run. The horror. But yes, necessary evil. What’s top of the list? Definitely need to sort the internet out first. I emailed the provider this morning, hopefully, it can be connected tomorrow. No internet, no life, basically. Tell me about it! What about food? I’m starving. We've got some bread and cheese, but that’s about it. I was thinking we could do a really simple pasta thing tonight. I saw some amazing looking courgettes at the market the other day – they were huge and bright yellow. Ooh, yes! Zucchini pasta sounds good. Do we have any pesto? I’m suddenly craving pesto. I  think  we have a jar lurking somewhere. I’ll check. We need to figure out the rubbish collection schedule too, eh? Don't want to be accidentally chucking things in the wrong bin. No, that would be disastrous. And what about… do you smell that? Smell what? Like… smoke. It's quite faint, but it's there. Yeah, I think I do. It’s probably just someone nearby having a barbecue. Or… Or what? Or the people in the nursery next door. They light fires in their garden sometimes. It can get a bit thick. A nursery? Next door? Really? Yep. Little wooden building, full of screaming kids. It's… an experience. That’s… a lot. Still, at least it'll be entertaining. Speaking of entertaining, have you sorted out the banking stuff? Changing addresses and all that. Not yet. It's on the to-do list, just below ‘buy a rug’ and ‘confront the nursery with their smoking habits’. Priorities! I can help with that later. Should we put on some music? Get this place feeling a little less… empty? Absolutely. Let’s get some tunes going.

Oh my gosh, Priya! It’s so good to see you! It feels like ages. Honestly, it has! Peterborough is… well, it's something, isn't it? But it’s great to finally catch up. This place looks nice, though. Bills is always a safe bet, right? Good food, decent cocktails. Have you been before? Nope, first time. It smells delicious already. So, how are things? Last time we spoke, you were drowning in spreadsheets as a Project Coordinator? Don't even get me started! It's...intense. But good, actually, really rewarding. We just launched a new initiative, which is a massive win. How’s the graduate placement going? You were off to… where was it again? Birmingham, wasn’t it? Yeah, Birmingham. It's been a whirlwind. Totally different from uni. Much more real-world stuff, you know? A bit overwhelming at times, but I'm learning loads. It's with that marketing agency, 'Phoenix Creative'. So far so good, though. Phoenix Creative! Fancy! That sounds really exciting. Are you enjoying the city? Birmingham's surprisingly cool. Loads of little independent coffee shops, and the Balti Triangle is incredible. Seriously, you need to visit. I’ll drag you there sometime. I'm holding you to that! It sounds amazing. My parents are finally thinking about a holiday – they're talking about doing the Balti Triangle! I'm trying to convince them to go to Greece though. Remember that disastrous holiday to Spain we took back in 2010? Oh my god, the ants in the hotel room! And your dad trying to order paella with a mouthful of soup! Seriously, best memories. Don’t remind me. But my dad still insists it was a wonderful trip. He's… well, he's my dad. So, how are your parents doing? Have you seen them recently? They're good, yeah. Mum's been experimenting with new curries again - she’s got a massive cookbook collection! Dad’s finally retired, so he's enjoying chasing the grandkids around. It's chaotic, but lovely. That's so nice! I need to call my mum, she's been feeling a bit down lately. Things are a bit… much at home with my brother, you know? He's still single and complaining about everything. Oh, blimey. Classic brother. Do you think you’ll be staying in Peterborough long-term? Honestly, I don’t know. I love the job, but the city itself… it’s not exactly brimming with excitement, is it?

Honestly, this pint is doing wonders for my brain after that meeting. Felt like I was arguing with a brick wall. Tell me about it. Supervision meetings are the bane of my existence. Mine was just…a monologue about his theories. Barely a question asked to me. Sounds about right. At least you get a free pint afterwards. Mine was just a sigh and a request for more data. Cambridge never stops needing more data, does it? No it doesn't. Still, nice to escape the university bubble for a bit, eh? This pub's got a good vibe. It does. Makes a change from the slightly-too-trendy places around here. And it's good to actually hear a decent accent, too. I miss the North East, you know? I can imagine. You always light up when someone mentions it. You should visit more often. I know, I know. It's just…life gets in the way. Work, the flat, you know. And honestly, flights up to Newcastle from London are extortionate. True. What's your research into at the moment, anyway? Still chasing those elusive research grants? Always chasing. Currently battling over whether to focus on consumer behaviour or social media’s impact on local identities. North East stuff, obvs. Always going back to the North. Figures. Always interested in where people are from, aren't you? I’m still trying to wrestle my data into some semblance of order. It's throwing everything it can at me. It's tempting to just set it on fire. Sounds stressful. You look knackered. Right, fashion. Distract us. What did you think of that exhibition at the Fitzwilliam last week? The one with all the vintage stuff? Oh, the textiles one? It was surprisingly good! Loads of amazing designs, but honestly, some of those hats were… something else. Right? I saw one that looked like a giant cabbage. Someone clearly had a lot of time on their hands. I wish I’d worn something a bit more… stylish. I feel a bit drab in this jumper. Don't be silly. It's comfy. You always look good. Anyway, speaking of style… I finally got hold of those Arctic Monkeys t-shirts you were talking about. No way! Which ones? The “Whatever People Say I Am, That’s What I’m Not” era or later? The original! Got the black one with the band logo.

Alright, Grandma, you still watching that news? Seems like all doom and gloom these days. Aye, lad. It's a sorry state of affairs, isn't it? Always has been, really, but seems to be getting worse. This Prime Minister… what a mess. My teacher, Mr. Davies, was saying in school, about how everything’s gone massively expensive. My mum's stressing about the gas bill something awful. Oh, I know all about that. Gas bill used to be a pittance, you know. Back in my day, you could heat the whole house for tuppence and a smile. Tuppence? Seriously? What’s a tuppence, even? It’s an old penny, love. Two ha'pennies made a penny, a penny made a shilling, and twelve shillings made a pound. Makes your head spin, doesn't it? Different world back then. People had values. Earned their keep. Well, it certainly sounds different. Anyway, Mr. Davies said this new tax thing isn’t helping anyone, especially not people whose wages are stuck. Tax, tax, tax. They’re all at it, aren’t they? Promise you the world, then stick their hand in your pocket the moment they get in. Always the same. Remember that Wilson fella? Promised to squeeze the orange for everyone. Squeezed it right dry, he did. Wilson? Was he a prime minister? Aye, in the sixties. Labour, he was. Good intentions, but ended up giving everyone a right headache. Had three-day week, remember that. Didn’t like that one bit. Couldn’t get me new coat finished on time. Right, well this bloke now? What’s he doing wrong? Too much borrowing, lad. That’s what. Spending money we don’t have. Like giving a child a full bag of sweets and expecting them not to fall and stain the carpet. It's gonna come back to bite us. Yeah, Mum said something about that. Says it’s going to affect my future, getting a job and all. Well, you're a smart lad, Ethan. You'll be alright. Just keep your wits about you, don't trust anyone in a suit, and learn a trade. Something solid. Not all this computer fiddling. Though, I suppose that's your generation's way. I’m thinking about coding, actually. My friend Liam’s doing it, says it’s good money. Coding, eh? Never heard of it. Fancy that. All these newfangled things.

Right, everyone settled? Dinner’s ready. And Liam, for goodness sake, put your elbows off the table. It’s a habit you need to break, son. But it's comfier, Dad. Don't let him get away with it, Sean. Manners matter, even when it's just family. Aye, manners are important. Taught my wee ones that well enough, I did. Though they still try to sneak a second helping when I’m not looking. You always did have a knack for spotting those extra portions, Mum. Everything smells lovely, Siobhan. Thanks, Sean. I tried a new recipe. Shepherd’s Pie with a rosemary crust. Rosemary crust? Sounds good! Rosemary's lovely. Reminds me of the gardens back in Glasgow, full of herbs and flowers. Of course, you didn’t have the sunshine we’ve been getting here. We’re very lucky with the weather, Mum. Did you see that blood moon last night? It was incredible! Yeah! It was so red. I tried to take a picture but it didn’t come out very well. Honestly, Liam, you and your phone! Put it away for five minutes and just appreciate it. Blood moon eh? It's an ill omen, some folks say. Oh, come on Mum, don't start with the superstitions. It's just a natural phenomenon. Sean's right. It’s beautiful, isn't it? Perfect for a clear night here in Cork. We should take the kids to Fitzgerald’s Park tomorrow. Yeah! Can we, Dad? Please? Absolutely. We’ll pack a picnic. Liam, you can try and get a decent picture this time and I'll make sure you're not wearing that ratty hoodie. Dad! That’s a lovely idea, Siobhan. It’ll do the grandchildren good to be out in the fresh air. You’re a good lass, minding them. It's not easy, you know, with little ones. Thanks, Mum. It's tiring, but worth it. Actually, Mum, I was wondering…would you be free to do a few afternoons next week? I've got a couple of appointments and could really do with a hand with Thomas. That would be fantastic, Mum. A real lifesaver. Aye, I’d be happy to. Thomas is a wee rascal, but I enjoy his company. Keeps an old lady on her toes. Granny, will you teach me how to build a proper Lego spaceship? Now that’s a skill I can impart!

So, what did you make of the Scottish result? Quite a thing, wasn’t it? Absolutely remarkable. I still can't quite believe they didn't go for independence. Though, I suppose it was close enough. A bit of a nervous few days for everyone, eh? Indeed. My daughter, Sarah, was glued to the news. She’s got a couple of friends up there, you know. Very relieved, she was. Though, she did say it’s not the end of the conversation, is it? More of a pause, she thinks. Probably right. Politicians will be scrambling to make good on promises now, won’t they? Speaking of scrambling, I had a rather peculiar job interview the other day. Oh, really? For yourself? No, for someone I know. A young chap just out of university. Property management firm. Honestly, the interviewer was… unusual. Kept asking questions entirely unrelated to the job. Like, “If you were a vegetable, what would you be and why?” Good heavens! That's a bit out there, isn't it? Reminds me of some of the more eccentric characters I used to encounter in my teaching days. Exactly! And then he quizzed him about his favourite colour and whether he believed in aliens. The poor fellow looked completely bewildered. I'd be!
