You'd think they’d want to see demonstrable skills, experience… something relevant! What did your friend think? He was having second thoughts immediately. I told him to walk away if he felt uncomfortable. Plenty of other companies would appreciate his qualifications. I had a colleague once, similar sort. Showed up for an interview in shorts and a Hawaiian shirt. Didn’t last long. People don’t always think things through, do they? So, how's your daughter doing? Last I heard she was looking at moving down to London. Yes, she’s still considering it. Has a couple of interviews lined up, one with a marketing agency. Seems hopeful. It’s a big step, of course. Leaving Brighton. It is. But she’s a bright girl. She’ll do well. It’s just… leaving family, you know? Absolutely. Though, we'll visit. Frequent visits. And it's nice that she’s pursuing her ambitions. It's good to see ambition in young people. These days many are just... content. I agree. It’s important to strive for something. So, how's business? Still bustling down at the shop?

Right, so, Luton's coming up on the left. Anyone want a break? My back’s starting to protest this long drive. Yes, please! My legs are getting a bit numb. A quick coffee would be lovely. Count me in. My stomach’s starting to rumble. Think I skipped breakfast in the rush to leave. Alright then, five minutes at the services. Aaron, you navigate us onward. Ann, you decide if we aim for Greggs or somewhere more… respectable. Respectable? Dad, really? It’s a service station. And I’m navigating, not Google Maps. It’s a modern skill, you know. Sassy, aren't we? Don't be rude to your father, Aaron. So, about this move... any thoughts on where we'll put the cat tower? The cat tower? Seriously, Dad? That thing is the size of a small apartment. It keeps Mittens happy! And she’ll be missing this place, you know. Changing houses is stressful for everyone. Even feline overlords. She’ll be fine. As long as there are sunbeams to nap in and places to scratch. Speaking of which, I was thinking of getting one of those automatic feeders. Oh, those are brilliant. I saw one on TV that dispenses treats too! Treat-dispensing cat gadgets. My life is becoming increasingly ridiculous. Ridiculously good, I hope! Speaking of ridiculous, did you see that article about the man who ate 77 sausages in ten minutes? New world record apparently. Oh, goodness! That's just disgusting. Imagine the indigestion. Think he’ll be ordering a takeaway later though, won't he? I bet he’s regretting it now. It’s probably made a massive dent in his pension plan. Speaking of which, I need to look into that. My tuition fees are still hanging over me like a terrible cloud. Don't worry yourself about that yet, son. Things will sort themselves out. Plenty of time to sweat the small stuff. You're trying to sound wise, David. Just admit you're avoiding talking about the packing. Alright, alright, you got me. It's a mammoth task. I've been trying to sort through those old computers. Found a ZX Spectrum from the eighties! Oh wow! I used to have one of those. Remember Pac-Man? You guys are speaking a different language. It’s like ancient history. I’m more of a PlayStation man myself. You’ll appreciate the novelty of it, dear.

Right, grandad, are you sure you’re alright with me driving like this? It's a bit bumpy, innit. Aye, lass, I'm fine. Been on worse roads than this in me day. Back when they were building the motorway up to Manchester, roads were a disgrace. Absolutely disgraceful, they were. Were you driving then, Grandad? Oh, aye. Had a Morris Minor. Bright red it was. Nothing like these fancy motors you’ve got. Reliable, though. Wouldn't let you down. This one's reliable enough, mostly. Just a bit…agricultural around the edges at the moment. Did you see that sheep back there, Liam? Briefly. Looked like it was giving us the eye. Aye, they do that. Bold as brass, sheep are. Used to see ‘em wandering along the main road back home, causing chaos. One time, a whole flock blocked the road. Took the farmer an hour to round ‘em all up. We drove past a farm with loads of alpacas earlier. They were proper staring at us. Bit creepy, really. Alpacas are quite striking, aren't they? They look like fluffy llamas. Llamas. Fancy name for a glorified donkey, that. Alpacas, though… always struck me as a bit standoffish. Proper posh farm animals. They were definitely giving us the side-eye. I think they were judging my car. They probably were. It could use a wash. Don’t remind me. I’ll get around to it. Are you comfortable, Grandad? Want me to pull over? No, lass, I’m alright. Just keep moving. These country lanes are a bit tighter than I’m used to, mind. Never had to navigate roads like this in my Morris Minor. Mostly just city streets and motorways. It’s a lovely drive, though. The scenery's really nice. It is. Makes you appreciate getting out of the city a bit. Although I do miss a good coffee shop. Coffee shops. What nonsense. A good cup of tea and a biscuit does the trick. That's all you need. You’re a man of simple pleasures, Grandad. Right you both. Let’s just hope we don’t see any more wandering livestock. I'm not keen on a close encounter with a cow today. Heard tell of a farmer who kept goats. They used to jump on the roofs of cars. No way! Seriously? Aye, seriously. Naughty goats, they were. Naughty as anything.

Right then, everyone dig in! I made that roasted vegetable tart you all like, and Michael, you promised to bring your famous potato salad. Smells amazing, Bridget! And you remembered my nut allergy with the tart, thank you. Yes, potato salad is here, ready to be devoured. Michael, you’ve massively outdone yourself today. Always a pleasure to feed a hungry family. Though, honestly, I think you’re more discerning critics than any restaurant. Bridget, that tart looks fantastic. Don’t be silly, Michael. It’s a simple recipe, really. I find myself trying out more things now I've retired. Keeps the brain ticking, you know. Though I’m still trying to convince the choir to let me lead a session on mathematical musical ratios. They’re not entirely convinced it’s relevant! Mathematical musical ratios? That’s brilliant, Aunt Bridget! You’re incorrigible. How’s the choir going otherwise? Are you finally nailing that high note in ‘Amazing Grace’? Not quite, dear. Still a work in progress! But the director seems pleased overall. It's lovely to be surrounded by music again. And socialising, of course. It's important to stay active and meet people. Though, someone should teach young people the importance of punctuality! That grandson of yours was nearly half an hour late tonight. Tell me about it! Honestly, he thinks time is some sort of elastic concept. I keep telling him it's important for respect, for everyone's time… It doesn’t sink in. I had to keep chasing his messages. Typical boy. They all think they’re entitled to run on their own clock. When I was a lad, if you were late, you faced the music! Teachers used to be much stricter. Mr. Davies, my maths teacher, would have had you cleaning the blackboard for a week! Oh, those days are gone. They’re so focused on sensitivity these days. Though, I did once have a student who’d deliberately arrive late every Tuesday. Drove me mad. Turned out his mother worked two jobs and he was responsible for looking after his younger sister until she got home from school. Suddenly lateness didn't seem quite so… annoying. That’s a good point. Perspective is everything. Speaking of families, have you guys thought about that charitable foundation idea we talked about? Yes, I have. I’ve been reading up on various models, and something focused on supporting local schools seems sensible.

Right, so parent’s evening. I’ve got quite a lot to tell you both about school. Abigail, your teacher – Mrs. Davies – seems a little worried about your maths. Maths is hard! I know it can be, sweetheart, but you’re capable of so much. She said you seem to switch off a bit when they’re doing times tables. Are you daydreaming? Sometimes. Are you daydreaming about princesses and unicorns? Sometimes. Princesses are silly! Jackson, be nice. Abigail likes princesses. Anyway, Mrs. Davies suggested we get some little games for you to practice at home. Like those times table cards. I don't want cards! You don’t have to play with cards. We can make it into a game. Like a treasure hunt, and the treasure is knowing your times tables. Can I be the pirate? You can certainly be the pirate, matey! And Jackson, your teacher said you’re doing really well with your reading and writing. He’s really enjoying learning about… what was it? Knights and castles? Yeah! And dragons! Dragons, of course. He was worried about your concentration a little bit. He said you get easily distracted. By dinosaurs! Dinosaurs! Yes, absolutely. We’ll try and keep the dinosaurs to story time then, won't we? Right, food's ready. Shepherd's pie tonight. Yummy! Is it got lamb in it? Yes, darling, it has. Do you remember what Mr. Henderson said about World Book Day? You have to dress up! Exactly! You’re going as Hermione Granger, aren’t you? Yes! And I'm bringing in my wand. I’m going as a T-Rex! Brilliant! And we’re going to the circus next Saturday, aren’t we? Wow! With the trapeze and the lions? And the clowns! I hope you're ready for some clowning around. We need to sort out after-school club. I'm not sure Sarah can do Tuesdays, can she? I want to go to the adventure playground! Later! After school club first. Oh, and Uncle David sent a funny message. He asked, “What does cooked human flesh smell like?”  Giggles uncontrollably   Laughs hysterically  I know! Honestly, he’s a card. Don’t repeat that, you two. That’s just very silly. Eat your shepherd’s pie! It's delicious. And Abigail, let’s tackle those maths games this weekend, okay? A little pirate treasure hunt might just do the trick.

Right so, Oisin's turning five, eh? Big lad. We need to sort this birthday party out. Any thoughts on what he'd actually  want  this year? Last year was just chaos with the bouncy castle. Honestly, he keeps saying he wants to be a pirate. A full-blown, eye-patch and parrot pirate. Aye, a wee pirate, is he? Well, that's a grand theme. Are you thinking of a proper party or just a few pals over? I was thinking a few pals over, maybe a treasure hunt? Keep them occupied, you know? Less running wild in the house. I like the treasure hunt idea. We could hide the sweets and toys around the garden. Or maybe even inside, if the weather's not playing ball. Treasure! See! He's already on board, isn't he? He definitely is. Your sister’s kids are working in that curtain shop now, aren't they? Could they make us some pirate flags or something? A bit of a favour. They are! Liam and Saoirse. They seem to be enjoying it, actually. Liam’s got a real eye for colour, which is handy. I’ll ask them. They might do it for free, being family. Aye, family’s always good for a bit of a favour. My niece in Glasgow helps me out with my knitting – a grand girl, she is. Now, are you going to that rugby match on Saturday? Thinking about it. Bit pricey but I’d love to take Oisin. He's mad for the rugby, mimicking all the players. The way he says 'ruck' is just hilarious. It is! He goes, "Ruuuuuuck!" like he's trying to break something. Wee terror, is he? Reminds me of my grandson. Now, I was treasurer of the local garage association for years, you know. Keeping track of all that money – a right faff it was! I can imagine! Speaking of money, have you seen what they’re doing with the tax on rented houses now? Absolutely bonkers. Tell me about it. It's squeezing everyone. I saw a charity calling today, someone trying to get me to donate. Always when I'm eating my dinner! Aye, those calls can be persistent. I got one yesterday asking for donations to a dolphin sanctuary! Glasgow’s a fair way from the sea, mind you. Exactly! They clearly don’t do their research. Right, back to Oisin's party.

Right, so I was thinking, you’ve got to beat this one, alright? It's brutal. Alright, alright. Lay it on me. Prepared to be humbled. Okay. "Palindrome palindrome palindrome palindrome" using only words with three letters. You're having a laugh, aren’t you? That’s… that's genuinely evil. Seriously? Three-letter words only? That’s… intensely constricting. Can you actually  do  it? I spent a good hour on it! It’s got to be a palindrome. It’s got to only be three-letter words. And it has to make  some  sense. "Bob did nod." Is that the best you've got? Can’t see a way to stretch that out. That's not even remotely close! Bob did nod is  not  a palindrome palindrome. It's just...a sentence. Okay, okay. Let’s tackle this strategically. What are the most useful three-letter words for building palindromes? "Dad," "Mum," "Pop"… utterly useless. Think about verbs too. "Run," "See," "Eat"… still nothing. I was thinking about ‘eye’ and ‘wow’ but you need a lot more than that. There’s a reason it took me so long. Right, let’s brainstorm. Okay, start with something in the middle. Something that could be mirrored both ways, like … "dog"? "Dog god" doesn’t quite work, does it. Too abrupt. Okay, let's look at nouns then, things you can repeat. "Red red." Better. But not a sentence. Hmm. "Sis is." That’s a starting point, right? “Sis is sis?” Still needs…a lot. What about using a couple different lists and just combining them. Like one side of the palindrome is related to animals and the other to food? That's not the point! It’s a single wordplay sentence. Right, you’re right. It’s got to feel cohesive. Okay, look, maybe it's impossible. I’m seriously doubting it’s solvable. You've rigged the game, haven’t you? Maybe. Little bit. But I genuinely thought it could be done. It’s infuriatingly difficult. So, you’re not going to give us the answer then? Nope. It’s your turn to set one. Something slightly less sadistic. Please. Alright, alright. Let me have a think… Okay, this one's a bit different. It's a riddle, but you have to answer it using only words found in the title of a single film. Any film. Ooh, that’s clever!

Oh my god, look at this picture! Remember this from when we went to Creamfields? You look like a drowned rat! That's because I  was  a drowned rat! It was pouring, wasn’t it? And you were moaning about your shoes the entire time. They were expensive shoes! And I did not moan, I just...stated facts. It was impractical footwear for a muddy field. Right. Stating facts. Anyway, look at Liam’s face. He looks terrified. He does! He looks like he’s seen a ghost. What was he so scared of? Probably just the amount of people. He wasn't exactly a crowd person back then. You know, remember how he nearly fainted when he tripped over someone? Oh god, yes! And you just kept walking, didn't you? Left him sprawling on the ground. Hey, I didn’t leave him! I yelled, “You alright?” and then carried on to get a pint. Priorities, you know. Speaking of priorities, did you manage to nap today? I was shattered after that seminar. I’m convinced I spent more time nodding off than actually listening. Honestly, I'm the same. I had a solid hour on the sofa this afternoon. Best thing ever. Needed that recharge. What’s on at the Academy next week? Fancy going? I saw something about The Lumineers. Remember how obsessed we were with them in uni? Oh my god, yeah! We used to listen to them on repeat in the halls. Head of the halls wasn't too pleased, I recall. He wasn’t, was he? Probably thought we were torturing him. Have you heard from Chloe and Tom lately? Not properly. Chloe sent me a quick text saying they were in Barcelona. Picture of some ridiculously good-looking paella. I’m proper jealous. Ooh, I bet. We should go somewhere like that soon. Proper getaway. Definitely. Although, knowing us, we’d probably spend the entire time arguing over which tapas to order. That’s probably true. Honestly, we're a nightmare together sometimes. But a good nightmare, right? Always. Hey, is that your Mum heading over here? Yeah, looks like it. She always pops in for a chat. Should we order another round? She’ll be wanting tea and biscuits, knowing her. Sounds like a plan. I'm ready for another laugh, and probably another look at that ridiculous picture of you. You look terrible!

Right, so let’s run through this planning application one last time. I’m feeling a bit twitchy about it, to be honest. Twitchy how? It’s a straightforward objection, really. Overdevelopment for the area, impact on local green space… all fairly standard. I know, I know. It's just… Mrs. Davies from number 12 cornered me in the supermarket yesterday with a sob story about how the new flats will block out the sun to her prize-winning roses. It’s almost impossible to be taken seriously. Welcome to community consultation. But we need to be. They’re proposing something that’s clearly out of scale. Look at the density, the height… it doesn’t fit. Exactly. And I’ve tried to make that clear in the submission. I just need to make sure the structure is watertight. Are we happy with the order of the points? I put the environmental impact first, then the traffic assessment… I think that’s a good call. Environmental impact is always a strong opener. It sets the tone. And you've backed it up with the recent ecological survey, haven't you? That’s key. Yes, I’ve included the full report as an appendix. I also highlighted the impact on the local bat population – they’re particularly sensitive. Good. They’ll have to at least address that. What about the traffic concerns? Did you mention the likely increase in congestion on Elm Street? Absolutely. I’ve outlined the current peak hour traffic flow and then projected an increase based on the proposed number of residents. The County Council’s own figures support it. I’ve included those as well. Perfect. The most important thing is to present it as logical, well-researched, and reasonable. Avoid hyperbole and emotive language. We're not trying to win a popularity contest, we’re presenting a considered objection. Right. No “this will ruin our neighbourhood” statements. More like “this is not aligned with the local development plan and will negatively impact…”. Exactly. And remember to concisely summarise the key points at the end. Reiterate your core concerns and the specific recommendations you’d like the committee to consider. I think I've done that. Should I add anything about the increased strain on local services – schools, doctors…? It’s a valid point, but I think it’s a bit tangential. The main concerns are planning-related.

Ugh, I’m beat. This day has been…a lot. What have you been up to? Same! Honestly, a complete whirlwind. Three particularly challenging patients today, the usual. Grabbed some dinner though - ordered a takeaway. Thai, you want some? Yes, please! I’m starving. What did you get? Pad Thai and a green curry. A little spicy, but good. So, anything exciting happen in Project Coordinator land? Not exciting, just relentlessly tedious. Meetings about meetings, spreadsheets that never end… I swear, if I have to look at another Gantt chart, I’m going to scream. I feel that. Feel like I spend half my day explaining why people need to breathe and eat. Anyway, did you hear about Sarah and Mark from sixth form? No! What? Spill the tea! I haven't seen them since that disastrous school play. Apparently, they’re getting married! Can you believe it? Remember how they were obsessed with each other back then? Thought it was a phase. Honestly, I thought it was just Mark being…Mark. He always had a thing for the dramatic. What's she like now? Last I saw, she was sporting massive crimped hair and a Spice Girls phase. She’s totally changed! Apparently, she's a lawyer now, really successful and super sophisticated. He’s still…Mark. Still obsessed with rugby and apparently, trying to grow a beard. Oh, bless him. It'll probably look like a patchy caterpillar. Remember that time he tried to copy Brad Pitt in Fight Club? The bowl cut was questionable, to say the least. Don't remind me! And speaking of questionable… have you noticed Mrs. Henderson's new curtains? They’re bright orange. Bright  orange . No way! I haven’t been over that side of the house yet. How is that even a thing? Does she not have a mirror? Apparently, she thinks it complements the terracotta tiles she put in the garden. Honestly, the woman has no taste. I’m half expecting her to start wearing orange too. Don’t give her any ideas! Right, so what are we doing this weekend? Any plans? I was thinking about that coastal walk we talked about – the one near Brighton? It’s supposed to be gorgeous. Ooh, yes! Perfect. We could stop somewhere for fish and chips afterwards. Absolutely. Oh! I also wanted to check out that new film with Florence Pugh,  Little Women .

Right, this is ridiculous. Who actually  makes  these healthy cakes? It looks like cardboard. It’s advertising, Liam. They're not trying to make you eat it, they’re trying to make you  want  to eat it. Glossy pictures, upbeat music… it’s all carefully calculated. Calculated to make me feel bad about my chocolate bar habit, more like. Speaking of which, fancy a cuppa and a biccie? I’m going to sneak into the kitchen while this person pretends to bake a quinoa delight. Sounds good. You know, I was thinking about that article I read the other day, about the increase in shoplifting in the area. It's a bit worrying, isn’t it? Yeah, proper dodgy. My nan says it’s because of the cost of living. Folks struggling, desperate. Definitely a factor. Though, I read that a lot of it is organised crime groups, targeting high-value items. You know, like luxury goods, mobile phones… Aye, probably. So, what's the plan for the week then? You got anything exciting on? Apart from battling criminals, of course. Not really. I've got a couple of placement shifts booked. Thinking of hitting up a car boot sale on Saturday, though. Need to clear out some old stuff. You fancy a look? Reckon I could be persuaded. Might find some retro gaming stuff. You know I'm always on the lookout for an old Playstation. You and your retro games! Remember that time you spent three hours at that one car boot, searching for a specific game cartridge? Don't remind me! My mum was fuming. She thought I’d lost the plot. Still worth it for  Final Doom , though. You're a lost cause. Seriously though, I was thinking we could try meal prepping this week. Save some money, eat healthier... Meal prepping? Sounds like a chore. I’d rather just order a takeaway. Don't be like that. It doesn’t have to be boring! I saw a recipe for a chicken and veggie stir-fry that looked pretty good. Plus, remember what we were saying about NLP? We could use some tools to, like, reprogram ourselves to enjoy healthy eating! NLP? You're trying to use brainwashing techniques on me to get me to eat broccoli? Not brainwashing. Just… influencing our subconscious. It works, honestly! I read about it in… well, it’s a long story.

So, anyone else obsessed with the Shazam app? I swear, I’ve identified like, fifteen songs in the last week. Shazam? It's alright. I use Google Lens more, you know, for identifying plants and dodgy art in antique shops. Much more practical. Google Lens is amazing, isn't it? Identifies my nephew’s Lego sets instantly. Saves me a fortune on guessing what to buy him for Christmas. I find it freaky. Like, the phone's just  listening  all the time. Bit Big Brother-y, isn’t it? Yorkshire folk don't trust listening devices. It’s in our nature. I’m more of a Spotify Discover Weekly girl myself. Reliable tunes. True, but nothing beats the thrill of finally figuring out what that one song is you’ve been hearing everywhere. Remember that awful jingle for the holiday park? Shazam saved me. Holiday parks… speaking of horrors, did anyone see that documentary about reality TV production? Brutal.  Loaded: The Real Cost of Reality TV ? Yeah, grim stuff. Totally changes how you view those manufactured dramas. It makes you question the ethics of it all. Speaking of things questioning ethics, I'm still furious about the way the BBC handled that local news story last week. Oh, you mean the one about the library funding cuts? A complete whitewash, wasn’t it? I wrote a pretty scathing piece about it for the online magazine. Did you? Good on you. Need more investigative journalism. It's depressing to scroll through news these days. All just clickbait and outrage. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? Tabloidisation of everything. Makes you long for the days of proper, in-depth reporting. You know what I miss? Those thick Sunday supplements. Remember those? Like a literary feast. Absolutely. Although, I wouldn't trust half of what they printed. Still… a proper paper felt substantial. I actually like the shorter, more digestible online articles. I don't have time to wade through paragraphs of stuff. Fair point. Though I do get distracted scrolling. It’s a rabbit hole, isn’t it? Tell me about it. I was researching radio dramas for a new project and ended up watching cat videos for an hour. Don't we all? Hey, has anyone been to that new ramen place on Broad Street? I've heard good things. The one with the queue around the block? Yeah, I went with Amelia last week.

It’s lovely to see you all. I’m so glad you could make it. Let’s have another glass of this Sauvignon Blanc, shall we? Absolutely, Penelope. This is delightful. It’s ages since we’ve all been together like this. Reminds me of those reunions back in the day, doesn't it? Though, thankfully, no dodgy cheese and wine anymore. Indeed. It’s remarkable really, isn’t it? How we all ended up gravitating toward this patch of countryside. I remember coming down here in '67, fresh out of Manchester. Looking for a lecturing position… And I was here, shortly after, nervously interviewing for a dental position. The practice was in a right state, I can tell you. Dust thicker than fog, equipment that looked like it belonged in a museum. You were brave, Arthur! I was interviewing down the road at the secondary school. Remember, Penelope, looking for a teaching post? This area was practically bursting with vacancies back then. It certainly was. Though finding somewhere to live was another matter altogether. Landlords were vultures, wanting a fortune for damp and crumbling terraces. I ended up renting a tiny room above a bakery. The smell of bread every morning was lovely, of course, but the pigeons… oh, the pigeons! I practically lived in a bedsit myself. Shared a bathroom with three other blokes. One of them used to play the tuba. All through the night. Goodness, the sound! I was luckier, really. My wife, Eleanor, was quite clever at spotting a bargain. We managed to snap up a little cottage needing a considerable amount of work. Renovation was a nightmare, naturally. Tell me about it! I bought a place needing completely re-wiring, re-plumbing and a new roof. I swore I’d never pick up a hammer again, but I did. And I’ve been doing it ever since. It’s cheaper than paying someone! Speaking of picking up hammers… Arthur, tell us again about that postgraduate trip to Athens. It’s a classic! Oh, that. Right. So, we were all sent to Athens to do a refresher course in prosthetic work, you see. Bright young dental students, full of ambition. And the first day we arrived… the military took over. Full-blown dictatorship. Good heavens! You weren’t worried? Worried? We were bewildered! The hotel staff were terrified, the streets were filled with soldiers… we were trying to master crown and bridge techniques while the country was experiencing a coup!

Do, do sit down, Daphne. Lovely to have you. Milk and biscuits? I’ve got some rather good ginger snaps. Thank you, Marion, that's so kind. Ginger snaps sound wonderful, yes please. It’s such a charming house, filled with so much character. You’ve really made it your own. Oh, I’ve had years to clutter it up! It was my gallery for so long. Though, well, the internet rather took over, didn’t it? Pity, really. I miss the buzz of having people browse. I imagine it must have been lovely. A gallery, dealing in antiques... that sounds a fascinating life. A world away from my own, really. Speech and language therapy isn't exactly brimming with glamour! Oh, I wouldn't say that! Helping people find their voice, communicate... that’s a profound gift. What drew you to that field initially? My grandmother, actually. She had a severe stammer, and I remember feeling so helpless as a child, watching her struggle. It sparked something in me, a real desire to help others overcome those challenges. What about you? How did you end up as an artist and then an antique dealer? Well, my father was a gardener. A rather grumpy one, to be honest, but he had the most exquisite eye for colour and form. He used to say I inherited it, I suppose. I was always sketching and painting, even as a little girl. Went to art school, of course, then fell into dealing after a rather disastrous exhibition. Oh, dear! Utterly disastrous! Nobody bought a thing, darling. Well, almost nobody. A lovely old gentleman did buy a rather peculiar still life of pears. He said it reminded him of his late wife. Made me laugh, actually. So I started buying and selling, bits and pieces. It just grew from there. Somerset has wonderful hidden treasures, you know. Did you have a good childhood, Daphne? Growing up in Australia must have been quite different to Somerset. Very different indeed. Sydney was… bright, warm, energetic. I remember the smell of frangipani flowers everywhere. My father was a civil servant, very proper. My mother was a wonderful storyteller. We’d sit on the veranda at night, listening to her tales of her childhood in England, during the war. She used to paint too, though she never considered herself an artist like you. War stories... my mother used to recount those as well.

Right, so I reckon this butternut squash’s seen better days, yeah? It’s rock solid. Tell me about it. You need to really hack at this one. Want me to get started? Yeah, please. I'm tackling the onions. Smell’s already making my eyes water, isn't it? Always does. You’re thinking of getting that sleeve tattoo finished, then? Yeah, eventually. Thinking a geometric pattern. Something a bit…clean. Not all skulls and stuff. You still hate tattoos, don't you? I don’t  hate  them. I just think it’s a bit permanent, isn't it? Especially when you're still figuring things out. Fair enough. But it’s just a bit of me, you know? And I've been thinking about it for ages. Right. Well, as long as you don’t regret it, that's all that matters. So, risotto tonight then? We've got enough veg for a decent one. Yep, risotto it is. Should we ask Liv to come over? She's been sounding a bit down lately. Good idea. I'll give her a shout. She was worried about the Christmas market going belly-up, wasn’t she? Yeah. Apparently, a big competitor opened right next door. Sucks, doesn’t it? Being a small business owner. Right, she's on her way. Says she’s bringing gingerbread cookies! Excellent! That’s already making me feel Christmassy. That’ll be her! Hey Liv! Come in, come in! Hey guys! Smells amazing in here already. Thanks for having me. No worries! Gingerbreads, you say? Yep! Fresh from the oven. They're testers for some new Christmas decorations I’m thinking of selling at the café. Little gingerbread men with candy canes, you know? That’s adorable! Really cute. Thanks! I’m hoping they'll be a hit. Things have been a bit tight this year. The competition's been fierce, especially with those chain coffee shops all decked out already. Yeah, it’s tough out there. Are you going to do a Christmas Eve open evening? Trying to! But staffing is tricky. I need to find someone who's reliable. You guys wouldn't know anyone, would you? Preferably someone who likes tea and Christmas carols. I might! My cousin’s daughter, Chloe, is looking for a bit of extra work. She’s really sweet and loves a good mince pie. Seriously? That would be amazing!

So, thinking about it, Cambridge was really rather lovely, wasn’t it? A proper bubble. Yeah, it was. Bit too…quiet sometimes, though. Miss the buzz of London a bit. It's a different pace, isn’t it? Good for concentrating, though, I’d imagine. How's the thesis coming along? Still wrestling with that Victorian novelist? Yeah, still wrestling. It’s…dense. More dense than I initially thought. I'm probably about a third of the way through writing it. Well, that’s good progress. Don’t beat yourself up about it. It’s a massive undertaking. And you’re doing brilliantly. Have you thought about a celebratory dinner when you hand it in? Definitely. Something fancy. Maybe that place in Soho we always liked. Yes! Absolutely. So, after handing in the thesis, any grand plans? Are you thinking of job hunting immediately or taking a bit of a breather? I’m leaning towards a breather, to be honest. A few weeks, maybe. Travel a bit? I was looking at flights to Barcelona. Barcelona! Lovely. You deserve a break. Though, you know, it’s a competitive market out there. Don't leave it too long if you want something good. Have you considered that publishing internship you mentioned? Yeah, I’ve applied. Haven't heard back yet. It’s likely that Oxford would be a better shout wouldn’t it? It might be. Oxford’s a clever city, very different from London. You would thrive there, I think. It's so serious. Do you like serious? I do, actually. Sometimes London can be a bit…frivolous, you know? All flash and no substance. Exactly! But you need to think about living arrangements. Oxford’s ridiculously expensive. Although, I wouldn’t put you off. We can help with that, of course. Thanks, Mum. That's really good to know. I've been looking at places online, but it's just… overwhelming. Shared houses mostly, which is fine, but I’d love to have a place of my own eventually. Of course you would. It will happen. It just takes time. Have you thought about buying somewhere in London in the future? We could help you get on the ladder. That's the dream, isn’t it? But the prices! It’s insane. I swear, a shoebox in Zone 5 costs more than a mansion in…well, somewhere more sensible. Don't I know it.

Excuse me, do you happen to know where the seminar room for the Archaeology panel is? Oh, definitely! It’s just down this corridor, third door on the left. Are you here for Alumni Day too? Yes, I am! It’s lovely to see so many people back. I’m Eleanor, by the way. Language Research Co-ordinator. Hi Eleanor, I’m Chloe. I’m a Research Administrator in the linguistics department. It's nice to meet you. This is my first Alumni Day, actually. Really? Well, welcome! It's a good one. I’m particularly keen to hear the Archaeology panel - I find the history of language incredibly tied to its physical origins. Me too! I’ve always been fascinated by ancient cultures. Do you have a particular area of interest in that regard? Well, currently I'm doing a project analyzing the development of regional dialects in the East Anglian area. It's horrifying the number of words that have vanished just in the last century. Interesting conversation, ladies. Archaeology and linguistics are far more entwined than most people realize. Oh, hello! We were just discussing that. Are you here for Alumni Day too, sir? Indeed I am. Professor Alistair Finch, from the History department. I used to lecture here. These hallowed halls have seen a great many changes over the years, you know. It’s wonderful to meet you, Professor Finch. I think my supervisor occasionally mentions your lectures. Well, I hope he mentions them positively! I specialized in Arab culture and its connections to early European history – a surprisingly rich interplay of languages, trade, and scholarship. You realize, of course, how crucial Arabic was in the transmission of knowledge during the medieval period? Absolutely! We often overlook that. So much classical learning was preserved and expanded upon by Arab scholars. It’s remarkable. Are you still involved in any excavations or field work? Ah, sadly not as much as I'd like. I did spend a good few years in the Middle East, excavating a small, lost village near Palmyra. The pottery shards alone told a fascinating story of trade and cultural exchange. I often joked with my team that we were chasing ghosts of conversations. That sounds incredible! Was it difficult to get funding for projects like that? Always! Archaeology, particularly in less-visited regions, faces constant funding challenges. But the insights you gain... well, that’s invaluable.

Honestly, the amount of time I spent staring at screens today… lecture, readings, then trying to unwind by scrolling. It’s ridiculous. Tell me about it! I’m covered in flour and feeling like my brain’s turned to dough. Trying to come up with new flavour combinations is exhausting sometimes. Did you see that video of the guy making a cake shaped like a pug? It’s gone viral. Oh, I saw that! Absolutely bonkers. My café was packed today, everyone wanting to film themselves trying to recreate it. It’s crazy how quickly things blow up online. Do you reckon it’s all just luck, or is there a formula to a good viral video? There's an element of luck, definitely. But timing’s key, and understanding the algorithm. It's the same with photography and film - you can have the most technically brilliant shot, but if nobody sees it…it's a waste. Though, I've got to say, the pug cake was genuinely good. Nicely executed. It just feels like everyone's chasing views these days. My mate Liam is convinced he's going to be famous on TikTok. He's doing these… really obscure historical reenactments. Like what? Like, the Battle of Hastings, but he’s wearing a ripped hoodie and using a skateboard as a shield. It’s… something. But I don’t know if it’s going to launch him to stardom. Bless him. It’s that whole pressure, isn't it? To be constantly creating content, to be noticed. I worry about these young kids, honestly. And the education system just doesn’t seem to cater to it. My cousin's struggling with dyslexia at uni, and the support is just… insufficient. You're right about that. It's almost as if they expect everyone to learn the same way, at the same pace. Class plays a huge part in that too, doesn't it? Those with more resources can get extra tutoring or support, leaving others behind. That's so true. I’ve seen it in the café, parents trying to push their kids into specific paths, the ones they think will lead to ‘success’. Sometimes I wonder if they ever stop to ask what the kids  want . My parents are definitely pushing me towards law. The whole ‘stable career’ thing. But I’m thinking about doing a film course. They don't get it.

Honestly, this week has been relentless. The student feedback on the new module… it was a bit rough, wasn't it? Yeah, I saw that. They’re always honest, aren’t they? Brutally so. You’ll smooth it out, though. You always do. It's just... makes you question everything, you know? And then Sarah called, complaining about her knee. Again. The physio's booked her in for another round of whatever expensive treatment it is. Poor love. That’s been dragging on forever. It’s just the NHS seemingly incapable of dealing with anything beyond a broken leg these days. Exactly! And it's ironic, isn't it? We're both lecturing on the importance of public services, and our family is constantly battling to access them. The usual hypocrisy. What did you think about the Prime Minister’s speech yesterday? All that talk about fiscal responsibility... while splashing out on yet another vanity project. Don't even get me started. It’s all smoke and mirrors. They’re desperately trying to distract from the cost-of-living crisis, aren’t they? I'm worried about the students, honestly. Some of them are really struggling. Same here. I’ve had a couple mention needing to take on extra shifts just to afford rent. It's grim. Have you looked at our investments lately? I feel like we should be doing something more proactive. I’ve been meaning to. Things felt a bit shaky last time I checked. Are you thinking about diversifying? Possibly. I was reading about ethical investing - companies committed to sustainability and fair wages. Might be a good long-term move, both financially and ethically. That sounds promising. But honestly, I just want to put my feet up and watch some mindless TV. Did you catch that new detective series on Sunday? The one with… The one you said was a complete waste of time? Well, I was wrong! It was surprisingly good. Actually quite gripping. It’s nice to switch off completely, you know? Forget about student feedback, aching knees, and political disasters for a while. Absolutely. Speaking of switching off, I was thinking we could have that weekend away we talked about. Just you and me. Somewhere quiet. No lectures, no physios, no government pronouncements. That sounds absolutely perfect. Where were you thinking? Somewhere with a nice pub, maybe? Exactly. Somewhere with a roaring fire and a pint of proper ale.

This lentil soup is absolutely divine, isn’t it? Honestly, I think it's the best I’ve ever made. It is lovely, Mum. Really warming. Perfect for a chilly day like this. Though, honestly, watching the weather forecast is a bit depressing isn’t it? All grey for the next week. Grey’s good. Means the birds’ll be sticking around the garden. Spotted a nuthatch this morning, a proper beauty. Oh, did you, John? I must try and look out for one. They’re so quick, aren't they? I saw a badger rummaging around the other night, which was quite a surprise. A badger! Wow. Did you get a picture? Sadly no, dear. It was far too dark. I nearly woke up the neighbours just gaping at it from the window! Used to see them regularly when I was a lad in Lincolnshire. They were just part of the landscape. Now they’re rarities. Speaking of the landscape… I was just reading about that expedition to Mars, the one with the rover. Absolutely fascinating. All about the soil chemistry and searching for signs of… well, you know. Life? Oh, isn't it just wonderful what they can do these days? Science has come so far. Remember when we thought going to the moon was the pinnacle? Now it’s Mars! Though, I do worry about the budget… all that money spent on space when there are people struggling here. It's a necessary investment, Margaret. Humanity needs to look to the future. And it's created so many industries and jobs. Look at the technology that’s come out of it! Totally. And all the incredible images they send back - it's beautiful to look at, even if it's desolate. Have you seen that new film, 'Arrival'? Really clever science fiction. No, I haven't. I struggle with science fiction. Bit too… abstract. I prefer a good historical drama, something with period costumes and stately homes. You and your dramas, Margaret! Give me a good old football match any day. Did you see the game on Saturday? Dreadful performance. Honestly, Dad, you complain about them every week! But yes, it wasn’t brilliant. I’m more interested in the Women’s Super League to be honest. Far more exciting football. Oh, you’re right. I watched a bit of that on the telly last week. Rather good. So, David's birthday is next month, isn’t it?

So, how was the Lego today, Finn? Did you finish building that spaceship? Nearly, Dad. I’m just adding the wings now. It’s really complicated, you know. Like, the instructions are in a million different steps. Sounds impressive. You’ve got a lot of patience, Finn. Unlike some people I know. A little spark of creativity is all it takes, Sarah. Are you having fun with Rory? He’s been obsessed with the teddy bear today. He keeps dragging it around, making it 'walk'. It’s very endearing, but exhausting! Rory’s got a new favourite, hasn’t he? The one with the floppy ears. Oh, yes! Bartholomew. He’s been calling it ‘Bar-bar-roo’ all afternoon. Bless him. Rory, say ‘Bartholomew’! “Bar…bar…” He’s getting there. So, what else did you guys do today? Besides chasing after a walking teddy bear. We tried to get out for a walk in the park, but it was a bit chilly, so we didn't stay long. Rory was more interested in examining a puddle than actually walking, anyway. Ah, the classic toddler fascination. Puddles are miniature worlds to them, aren’t they? Did he try and eat it? Not this time! I managed to distract him with a leaf. Though I’m pretty sure he was eyeing up a slug at one point. Eugh! That’s gross. I’m glad I’m not a toddler. Slugs are the worst. They're not bad cooked, y’know. Just joking, Finn. Don’t tell your mother I put that in your head. What did you two have for lunch and dinner? Lunch was a disaster. He refused everything except a single carrot stick and a pile of crumbs. Dinner… well, it was marginally better. Some mashed potato seemed to go down. He’s a fussy eater then? A champion fussy eater. It's a daily battle. I'm starting to think I’ll be living on toast for the foreseeable future. That's the story of parenthood. Little victories. Did you manage to get any work done today, Sarah? A little bit. Tried to sort through some emails, but Rory insisted on ‘helping’ by repeatedly deleting my drafts. He likes the delete button very much. Sounds about right. My little sister does the same thing with Mum's phone. It’s hilarious, but infuriating. Well, at least he's keeping you entertained.

Right then, who’s bringing the sprouts this year? Don’t want a repeat of last year's sprout catastrophe. Oh, Arthur! You and your sprouts. I’ll do them, dear. I've perfected my butter and nutmeg method. Can’t go wrong. Butter and nutmeg, eh? Bold choice, Brenda. I’m taking the parsnips this year. Got a lovely honey-glazed recipe. Parsnips? Seriously, Dad? Yeah, they're a bit boring. Can’t we have, like, roast sweet potatoes with maple syrup? Sweet potatoes at Christmas? Good heavens! Where do you youngsters get these ideas? Real Christmas dinner needs sprouts, parsnips, and proper roast potatoes. Now, now, Arthur, be nice. Let the girls have their sweet potatoes. Variety is the spice of life, isn’t it? Besides, it's a long drive back for you, love. You need something to look forward to. How was the journey? Dreadful, Brenda, absolutely dreadful. That lorry driver cut me up on the A11. Nearly had a heart attack, I did! That’s the way of the A11, isn't it? Complete mayhem. Did you get the car serviced before you set off, Arthur? Yes, yes, I did. Young Kevin at the garage, he’s a good lad. Sorted it all out. New oil, filters everything. Cost a fortune, mind you. Ooh, speaking of fortunes, Leo finally asked me to go to that art exhibition in Norwich next Saturday. Oh, that’s lovely, darling! Which one is it? The modern one with all the blobby paintings? Yeah! He said he wanted to discuss Jackson Pollock with me. Sounds… intense. Pollock? Bit pretentious, isn't it? He's not pretentious! He’s just... enthusiastic. He knows loads about horses too. Horses? What's a boy who likes Pollock know about horses? He rides! He's got a horse called Sparky. Sparky! That's a wonderfully silly horse name. Sparky is a good name. Well, I'm glad you’re all enjoying yourselves young’uns. I’m just saying, a lad who appreciates modern art and rides horses? Sounds like he's trying a bit too hard, if you ask me. It’s like one of those jokes the lads tell. Know what I mean. You’re just jealous you don’t know anything about Pollock, Arthur. I know perfectly well what I like, and it doesn’t involve splattering paint on a canvas. Give me a nice landscape any day.

Right, so I’ve got the lasagne bubbling away nicely. Anyone want a glass of wine while we chat? Yes please! White, if you’ve got it. Feeling a bit… celebratory. Celebratory? What’s all this then? It's almost my birthday! Just a week away. Oh, massively! Happy almost birthday, sweetheart. We need to sort out a present then. Any ideas? Honestly? Just a nice dinner out somewhere. Somewhere a little fancy. I’ve been working so hard, really need to unwind. Fancy, eh? We’ll see what we can do. Your mum’s got a few ideas, I’m sure. She’s always got ideas. Oh, she does. She's been buzzing around asking what you want for weeks now. I know! Poor Mum. I'm terrible at deciding. Well, you’ve got a week. What about work? Is it still crazy busy? It’s alright, actually. A bit quieter than usual. The new campaign is launched, so I’m doing a bit of tweaking and making sure everything’s running smoothly. Found a really weird phrase the other day though - marketing copy about "synergistic growth opportunities". Honestly, I had to Google it. Sounds dreadful. All those corporate buzzwords. I'm glad I’m away from that now. Head of Department was stressful enough! Tell me about it. Nursing is stressful in a completely different way, though. Today was manic. Elderly lady kept insisting her parrot was giving her stock tips. Seriously? Dead serious! Said the parrot was very astute with investments. Had to gently explain that parrots don’t really understand the stock market. Oh, that’s brilliant. Sounds like a sitcom. You should write that down! "The Parrot Investor" – could be a hit. Maybe I should. It’s certainly more entertaining than some of the things I deal with. So, any exciting weekend plans? Besides a fancy dinner, of course. Not really, no. Might go for a walk in the woods with the dog. Just need some fresh air, I think. It’s been such a long week. Honestly, Sarah, have you seen that new show on Netflix? The one with all the… Don’t tell me, another true crime documentary. No! No, it's a comedy about a group of friends trying to open a bakery. It’s hilarious. You’d love it. I’ll add it to my list. Between work and everything else, my watchlist is miles long.

It’s beastly cold in here, isn't it? Not like Norfolk weather, this. Damp. Proper damp. Well, you know what they say about England, Alec. It’s always damp somewhere! Though, I do agree, the heating is struggling a bit today. Barry hasn’t quite got it sorted, has he? Barry’s got other things on his mind, dear. He's been up to his elbows in paperwork all week with the renovations at the shop. It’s a nightmare, that planning permission. Tell me about it! Dealing with the council is like wrestling an octopus. They just keep shifting and refusing to let go. Renovations, you say? What are you doing to the shop, David? Oh, just freshening it up a bit. Putting in a new display window. Modernizing the whole thing. Trying to appeal to a younger crowd, you know? Though, I’m not sure I entirely understand their tastes these days. All that… Big Brother. Honestly, what a waste of time! Don't get me started on Big Brother! Such dreadful television. All that shouting and drama. I prefer a nice documentary about dogs, myself. Now, dogs... that’s a conversation I could get behind. My granddaughter's got a gorgeous Labrador. Absolutely delightful. Gentle as a lamb. Always loved a good dog. Had a terrier when I was a lad. Best friend anyone could ask for. Loyal. Speaking of loyalty, did you hear what happened with the Wilkinsons? Apparently, Mrs. Wilkinson has rather a fondness for the gardener… Oh, dear. That’s just dreadful, isn't it? Such a respectable family. Imagine the scandal. It's always the respectable ones, isn't it? Though, I suppose everyone's got their secrets. Remember that awful business with the vicar and the choir mistress? Heavens! That was years and years ago. The talk of the village, it was. Though I always thought they were a rather peculiar pair. It’s all rather titillating, isn't it? Even though we all frown upon it. Well, it certainly keeps things interesting. Barry was saying the other day he saw Mrs. Hatfield at the church bazaar, looking rather down in the dumps. Apparently, her son is having some financial difficulties. Life’s tough on everyone, isn't it? Speaking of bazaars, are any of you going to the village hall on Saturday? They’re trying to raise money for the new roof.

Right, nearly ready! Smells amazing, doesn't it? Reckon this will feed us for days. It does, seriously. You’re a legend, honestly. Much better than my attempts at Italian. Last time I tried carbonara, it was basically scrambled egg with pasta. A disaster. Oh, bless you. Everyone has a cooking fail. At least you tried! So, have you heard anything new about your nan? Yeah, she’s actually been pretty good this week. Went to that pottery class she signed up for, apparently she made a little gnome. She's thrilled, thinks it's going to be a Christmas decoration already. Oh, that's lovely! She always was crafty, wasn't she? Remember that giant knitted cat she made for me when I was about ten? How could I forget? It was terrifying! Like a fluffy, four-legged monster. It took up half my bed. It did a bit. So, what else is happening? Did you end up seeing "Barbie" with Liam? We did! It was way funnier than I expected. Properly ridiculous. Ryan Gosling was brilliant, obviously. And Margot Robbie looked incredible. Honestly, I'm still humming the songs. I’ve been meaning to see it, but things have been mad busy here. This conference in October is gonna be hectic. I’ve got speaker confirmations to chase up, venue layout to finalise… it's endless! It sounds it. You’re always so organised though. Makes me wish I was better at planning. I’m just constantly reacting to things at work. Production's a nightmare sometimes. Delays and shortages everywhere. Tell me about it. Stressful, isn’t it? Although, I wouldn’t trade it. I do genuinely like my job. It’s rewarding when everything comes together, you know? Definitely. And they're offering that extra training course now at work… the one in lean manufacturing? I'm thinking about signing up. Oh, really? That sounds good! Good for your career, isn't it? Yeah, plus it might actually make my job a bit less… chaotic. Less fire-fighting, more problem-solving. Reckon it’ll do the trick. Right, dinner’s ready! Lasagne and a film night – perfect Sunday, wouldn’t you say? Absolutely perfect! What are we watching? I was thinking maybe something lighthearted. Need something to take my mind off work. I’ve got "Paddington 2" lined up. Can’t go wrong with a bit of marmalade-loving bear, can you?

So, what do you reckon, lad? About all this Scottish independence business? Seems like it's really heating up, doesn't it? Yeah, it's everywhere. Everyone at school's talking about it. Some of my mates reckon they should be independent, some don't. It's a bit confusing, to be honest. Aye, it’s a big decision, isn’t it? A proper fork in the road for the whole country. What’s confusing you particularly? Well, like, what would even  happen  if they voted yes? Would we still be able to travel freely? Would England be, like, a different country? Good questions, love. Well, if they voted yes, Scotland would become a separate nation, a completely independent country. That would mean new borders basically, although they've said they'd want to maintain close ties with the rest of the UK. Travel would likely change, require passports possibly, at least initially. England would definitely be a different country, in that it would lose Scotland. So, like, would the pound still be the currency? Would they have their own money? That’s one of the really complicated bits. They'd have to decide that. They could choose to keep the pound - a shared currency, essentially - but it's complicated and has implications for both economies. Or they could create their own currency, which would be a whole new set of challenges. What about the military? Would they have their own army and stuff? Aye, they’d need to build up their own defence forces, or enter into some sort of agreement with other countries. It’s a massive undertaking. And what about things like healthcare and education - how would those be funded and run differently? It sounds like a lot of hassle. Don’t they share resources now? Like, does England benefit from Scotland, or vice versa? Well, that's another key debate, isn’t it? There's arguments both ways. Some say England subsidises Scotland, but others say Scotland contributes a lot through things like North Sea oil and tourism. It's all a bit murky, to be honest. My Dad says he thinks it’s a bad idea because it’ll destabilise everything. Your Dad's got a point. It  could  be destabilising. But others argue it’s a chance for Scotland to shape its own future, to control its own laws and policies. There's a lot of passion on both sides.

Right, look at ‘im! Honestly, this fella’s trousers are tighter than me nan’s bloomers! Aye, he’s a right state, innit? Look at ‘im tryin’ to look all tough with that face. Like, who even does that? Blimey, he  is  something else, isn't he? It's the way he says ‘yeah’ – like ‘ya’. It's so weird. I know! It’s driving me mad! Yorkshire folk don't say ‘ya’ like that! It’s a proper… mish-mash. I’m trying to figure out why he's even on there. He looks like he’s got a solid job, decent house... What’s the drama? Apparently, the girl claims he’s got loads of kids he doesn’t support. Oh, classic Jeremy Kyle, then. More kids than he can shake a stick at. So typical. It's so depressing though, isn't it? Watching all this stuff. Makes you think. I’ve started noticing how much people drop letters out when they talk. Like ‘haven’t’ becomes ‘haven’. Elision! That’s what it’s called, right? Learn it in linguistics. Yeah, like, “He’s gonna” rather than “He is going to.” I do it all the time without even realizing it. I do too! And my mum’s always going on at me about it. “Speak properly, lass!” she says. My dad’s the same. He’ll be shoutin’ at the telly, “Stop sayin’ ‘goin’, say ‘going’!” He gets right riled up. It’s funny though, isn't it? Like, you’re aware of it in your head, but it comes out naturally. You’re thinking “I should say ‘is’,” but you just say “’s.” Exactly! Plus, you hear people from other places doing it, and it sounds completely different. Someone from London dropping letters sounds so weird. Yeah! Like, if they started saying "Was ya goin'?" I'd be mortified. Oh my god, imagine! Look at ‘im now! He’s started crying! Honestly, this is prime Jeremy Kyle material. Aye, he's right blubberin' now, poor thing. Bet he’s exaggeratin' everything, though. I wonder what the lie detector will say, honestly. Bet it’ll say he’s lyin' through his teeth. All these folk are con artists. I still reckon his trousers are the most shocking thing about all this though. They’re crimped! Crimped!      Right, I need a cuppa. All this drama is stressin' me out.H.,H..

Honestly, this ref is having a nightmare. Every call’s going against them. He is a bit dodgy, isn't he? But they're still holding their own, aren't they? Solid defensive work. Solid, yeah, but they’re missing chances up front. You’d think with the talent they’ve got… It’s early days yet. Plenty of time to turn it around. Relax. You're winding yourself up. Easy for you to say. You're not from the North East. You don’t understand the pain of near misses and dramatic collapses. I’ve lived through Birmingham City, love. I know a thing or two about heartbreak. Fair point. Still...that lad, Henderson, he's looking a bit off today. He's just a bit rusty, hasn’t had much game time lately. He’ll find his feet. What are you knitting at the moment anyway? Last time I saw you, you were halfway through that ridiculously complicated scarf. Oh, the scarf’s on hold. I’ve started on booties. For...well, for a friend. Booties? Expecting a little one then, are we? Sneaky. I thought you said you weren't thinking about it. I’m not! It's a friend's. A very good friend. They're struggling to come up with names. I was just thinking, what would you go for? Boy or girl? Hmm. Boy...maybe Arthur? Classic, solid, you know? Girl… Eleanor? I like the vintage feel. Arthur's nice. Eleanor’s a bit too posh for them, I think. They’re more of a… a Liam and Sophie kind of couple. Right, yeah. Something a bit more down-to-earth. What about Finn? For a boy? Seems popular at the moment. Finn's alright. It’s just...everything feels so overdone now, doesn't it? Everyone’s got a Noah or an Oliver. True. Remember when we were kids and everyone was called Jordan? That was awful. Oh god, yes! Awful. Penalty! Oh, no! No, no, no… Steady on. It’s not over yet. Just breathe. Look, remember the Olympics? That diving competition last year? They were down by a ridiculous amount going into the last dive, and they pulled it out of the bag. That was amazing, yeah. Different though. This is football. Anything can happen, but… Exactly! Anything  can  happen. Just watch. See? They're rallying. Look at that pass! Alright, alright.

Right, so Bee Movie. What did you both think? Honestly? I liked the bit where Barry does the dance! The honey! He made so much honey! Yes, he did! A  lot  of honey. It seems a bit…much, doesn’t it? I mean, using all that honey to pay off all the bees... It was funny, Mummy. It was big. It was. Big. Okay. Now, have you two been thinking about…kings and queens? Granny told us about King Arthur! She did? And what did Granny say about King Arthur? He had a sword! And a bird! A bird, yes! A falcon. Very regal. And what do  you  think about kings and queens? I want to be a princess! I want a castle! Me too! And a crown! With sparkly bits! Sparkly bits are very important. But you know, some people think we shouldn’t have kings and queens at all. They think we should be a Republic. What’s a Republic? It’s where everyone elects their leaders. Like the President in America. No crowns, no castles, just…people. But then who would have the cool hats? Hmm, good point. Good point. Then maybe you could be Prime Minister instead? Can I have a crown  and  be Prime Minister? We’ll see about that. Now, did you know you can actually  pay  to go inside Buckingham Palace sometimes? Really? Yes! It’s like a really fancy house museum. Full of old paintings and furniture. Though, a bit silly, isn’t it? Paying to see a house that doesn't really get used. Granny used to say it was silly, she hated the idea of charging people to look at it. Granny liked Royal fruits! Remember? Oh, yes! Granny and her Royal Gala apples. She wouldn't let anyone else have them. She used to peel them for us. That’s right. Speaking of Granny, do you ever think about her old house in Bury St Edmunds? The one with the big garden? I remember the swing! And the squirrels! So many squirrels! She used to grow the best raspberries there. Better than anything you can buy in the shops. We need to remember to take vitamins, like Granny did. To stay healthy and strong. Should we take vitamins  and  be Royalty? Absolutely. Now, we're going to see diving at the Olympic Stadium on Saturday. Are you excited? Yes! We have to be really quiet though, okay?

Honestly, I'm quite knackered after all that clearing out. You wouldn’t believe what I found lurking at the back of the airing cupboard - a box full of my old school reports. Dreadful things. Oh, you always were a bit of a worrier, weren't you, Margaret? I bet they’re full of ‘could do better’ and ‘lacks application.’ Precisely! And my mother's handwriting... like a spider on amphetamines. It’s a wonder anyone could decipher it. Did you find anything worth selling? Like, retro video games or something? Don't get your hopes up, lad. Your grandma mostly keeps floral china and moth-eaten blankets. Right. Shame. Speaking of selling, Carol’s organising that auction for the church hall, isn't she? All those old hymn books and dodgy floral arrangements. Yes, a rather eccentric affair, apparently. She says she’s got a specialist coming in to appraise some of the silver. I hope he’s reputable. Carol’s trusting soul. She’s always been good at organising things. Remember that village fete she single-handedly put on back in '98? The bouncy castle barely stayed upright. And the cake sale was a disaster! Mrs. Featherstone's Victoria sponge collapsed in the heat. Speaking of disasters, did you hear about Liam’s cousin’s stag do in Thirsk? Apparently, it didn't go well. Oh dear. What happened? Apparently, there was a rogue alpaca. A rogue alpaca? You’re pulling my leg. Seriously! It wandered onto the course during the golf and caused chaos. They had to call animal control. Only in Yorkshire. Goodness me. Now, has anyone seen the news about those NHS waiting lists? It's absolutely scandalous. My cousin's been waiting six months for a knee operation. Horrendous. We need a complete overhaul of the system, honestly. Far too bureaucratic. When I was a girl, you could see the doctor whenever you needed to. It's the same everywhere, isn’t it? It’s a disgrace. Trying to book an appointment online is a nightmare. I spent half an hour just yesterday. My mam’s just got a smart watch thing. She says it tracks her sleep and stuff. Is that any good? Technology, eh? Honestly, it's all going too fast. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the remote control for the telly. Don't even mention it, dear.

Right, so I’ve been thinking about the Walker. Should we go this weekend? There's that new exhibition on Victorian photography. Ooh, yeah! That sounds right up our street. But… parking. Seriously, the parking around the Walker is a nightmare. We'd have to factor in at least half an hour just to find a spot. True. Maybe we could get the bus? A bit slower, but less stressful. Plus, we could grab a coffee on the way back. That’s actually a really good idea. Okay, bus it is then. Let me check their opening hours. What about work this week? Are you buried in marking again? Worse, actually. A parent turned up yesterday, absolutely fuming because I gave their kid a C in English. Said I was sabotaging his future. You know the type. Oh, Liam, that’s ridiculous! You can’t please everyone, especially when it comes to kids and grades. Did you tell them just to calm down? Eventually, yeah. Had to involve the Head of Department, the whole nine yards. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I need a degree in conflict resolution as much as I need one in English Lit. Speaking of things needing degrees... How's the Masters interview prep going? It's… stressful, to be honest. I booked that mock interview with Professor Davies, and he absolutely ripped me to shreds. Said my answers were too vague, my research wasn’t focused enough… Oh, come on! Davies is just having a phase. He's always like that to everyone. You'll ace it, I know you will. You're brilliant, remember? You practically memorized all the key theorists. I know, but the financial side of it all is still playing on my mind. We need to figure out the loans thing proper. Any movement on that front? I’ve been looking into it. Student Finance England reckons we’re eligible for a decent amount, but it’s still gonna be tight. We need to start reigning in the spending a bit. No more impulse buys from that overpriced shop on Bold Street. Okay, okay, you're right. I’ve been eyeing up a really cute knitted cat toy for Mrs. Higgins, though. She'd love it. Mrs. Higgins can wait! Speaking of spending, have you thought any more about starting to look at places to move? That flat's getting a bit cramped.

Honestly, I'm still recovering from last night. That rave was  insane . Like, my feet are actually throbbing. Seriously? Where was it? I’ve been meaning to get out more. It was at that new place, “Cosmic Bloom”, down by the docks. The DJ, Kai Zenith, was incredible. You know, proper deep house, not just that surface-level stuff everyone’s playing. Kai Zenith? Never heard of him. I’m more into, like, indie pop, you know? Pale Waves, Still Woozy… Yeah, I get that. But trust me, the vibe was just… different. You should check him out on Insta. His handle's @KaiZenithSounds. Will do. Speaking of Instagram, did you see what Leo posted? He finally got that sleeve tattoo he’s been talking about for ages. No way! Let me see...  Scrolls through her phone  Oh my god, it's amazing! That dragon looks so cool. I’m tempted to finally get something myself, maybe a little constellation behind my ear. Do it! Little constellation is cute. Remember how obsessed we were with Disney as kids? We should get matching little Tinkerbell tattoos. Oh my god, you’re ridiculous. Though… that  is  a good idea. Maybe not Tinkerbell though, a little shooting star, perhaps? Yeah, definitely shooting star. So, what are you doing this weekend? Any plans? Not really, I was thinking of just collapsing after last night. Maybe binge-watching ‘Euphoria’ again, that Zendaya is just…  chef’s kiss . What about you? I was thinking about hitting up “The Bean Scene” - that new cafe near the library. Their pistachio latte is apparently  divine.  And then maybe catch a football match on Sunday? Ooh, The Bean Scene. Been meaning to try that. But football? You know I'm a terrible fan. I get so stressed. It'll be fun! My brother's bringing us some pizza afterwards. Proper loaded with pepperoni and jalapenos. Okay, pizza you’ve sold me. Though I might need a serious nap first. Uni’s been wiping me out this week. That essay on Victorian social reform… ugh. Tell me about it! I’m drowning in research for my animation project. Trying to recreate a classic Disney short, but in stop-motion. It's so time-consuming. Wow, that sounds intense. Are you using claymation or…? It’s paper cut-outs actually. Gives it a really cool, vintage feel. What about your family? Are they still nagging you about finding a “nice, stable” boyfriend?

Mum, have you seen this new Pokémon card? It’s a holographic Charizard! Oh, wow! Let me see. That  is  pretty cool. Are you trading it with anyone? Nah, I'm keeping it. It's gonna go straight into my binder. I’m trying to collect all the shadow Pokémon. Ba! Ba! Oisin wants to see the Pokémon too, doesn't he? He loves Pokémon. Yeah. He keeps saying “Pika Pika!” all the time. It’s kinda cute. It is. You know, we should Skype Grandma and Grandpa tomorrow, they’d love to see your Charizard. And Oisin too, of course. Yeah, good idea. Maybe we can show them my new guitar chords too? I'm getting the hang of "Smoke on the Water." That’s brilliant! You’ve been practicing really hard. You’ll be a rockstar in no time. Oisin, do you wanna hear your big brother play guitar? Da! Da! Can we go out for Ramen next week? I’m really craving it. We absolutely can! We’ll plan it. Maybe Saturday? We could get ice cream afterwards too, you've been working so hard. Yes! Ice cream! What flavour do you want, Mum? Ooh, maybe strawberry. It's been ages. Let Oisin have vanilla, he always loves vanilla. He’s got ice cream all over his face already. He does, doesn’t he? You know, you need to get some new clothes, you're growing like a weed! I don’t need new clothes. I’m fine with what I’ve got. Well, you  are  trying to squeeze into those skinny jeans again. They're getting a little tight, aren't they? They're not! They’re fine! It’s the style, Mum. Everyone wears skinny jeans. I know, I know. Just saying. Maybe something a bit looser would be more comfortable. And put some slippers on! Your toes are blue! Fine. But only because you're telling me. That's my boy. Now, tell me more about these shadow Pokémon. What makes them so special? Well… they’re like, super rare. And they’re really powerful. They appeared after the Champion league was running... Oisin! Sleepy! Oh, look at that, Oisin’s getting tired. Time for a little snuggle and maybe a story, eh? . Yeah, soon. We'll make sure he gets that before we go to Rammen. Right. I’m going to carry on playing my game.

Honestly, this cupboard is a disaster. I’ve been putting it off for weeks. It's just overflowing with…stuff. Mostly old photographs, I think, and things I can't quite bear to throw away. Tell me about it! Mine’s much the same. It's a bit sentimental, isn’t it? Holding onto things. Terribly sentimental. I found a box of old school reports the other day. Honestly, makes you wonder why I ever thought I was clever. Oh, we were both perfectly capable! I’m sure. Did you find any of those old toys lurking in there? I nearly unearthed my collection of ceramic thimbles the other day. Goodness, those were a phase. No thimbles for me, thankfully. But I did find something! Remember our gardening set? The little wooden one with the tiny trowel and watering can? Oh,  yes ! The one Mum insisted we played with even though we just used it to dig holes in the carpet. Remember how she’d sigh dramatically and tell us we’d be responsible for the carpet when we were old enough to understand responsibility? Vividly! And we’d just look at each other and giggle. It was fantastic. We weren't going to understand responsibility for a  long  time. No, we weren't! Though, looking at this cupboard, I’m not sure we ever really did. Did you find the Bako set? Goodness, I’d almost forgotten about that! Yes, tucked away at the very back. All those colourful blocks… It was brilliant, wasn’t it? We spent hours building elaborate castles and spaceships, and all sorts of ridiculous things. I remember one time we tried to build a replica of the Eiffel Tower. It was an absolute disaster. It truly was. It collapsed within five minutes. Dad took a photo of it though. Said it was a masterpiece of modern engineering, in its own unique way. He always did encourage our… creative endeavours. It’s so strange, isn't it, how things appear when you’re starting to clear out? It's no just clearing debris, you’re unearthing memories. Exactly. It’s almost overwhelming. It makes the tidying even harder. I just want to sit and reminisce for hours. I completely understand. And then you feel guilty for not actually tidying. It’s a vicious cycle! Still, it’s a lovely day outside. Bit grey, but at least it's not raining.

Honestly, the mosquitoes were dreadful today. I’m already itching everywhere. I thought summer was supposed to be better than this. Tell me about it. I was slapping myself the whole walk. Did you manage to get any pictures of Leo in the park? He seemed relatively happy, despite the buzzing harassment. A few! He mostly just stared at the ducks, which I’m taking as a win. He didn’t try to eat any grass, at least. Did you spot that near-miss traffic incident on the way over? Absolute chaos on Trumpington Road. Oh, really? I was too busy battling the mosquitoes to pay attention to the road. What happened? Some idiot pulled out from a side street without looking. Horns were blaring, people were swerving… it was a bit stressful, especially with Leo in the pram. Ugh, classic. I was thinking about that Arctic Monkeys gig last week. The traffic getting  out  of Cambridge was horrific. Took us nearly an hour to get home. I know! It was brilliant though, wasn’t it? Alex Turner's voice sounded incredible. Absolutely. Worth the traffic nightmare, definitely. I’m still humming some of the tunes. Have you looked at tickets for that Florence + the Machine concert next month? I have! They're selling fast, though. I’ll have a proper look tonight. Need to check Leo’s schedule first, of course. He’s starting to have a mind of his own about nap times. That’s the joy of parenting, isn't it? Suddenly every decision revolves around a tiny human's sleep pattern. Remember when we used to spontaneously go out for drinks? Vaguely! It feels like a lifetime ago. Still, listening to music loud with a baby nearby doesn’t quite have the same appeal, does it? No, but watching him wiggle and smile when he hears something he likes… that’s pretty special. Like when he started gurgling along to the piano music this morning. Ah, yes! He totally bobbed his head. He’s got rhythm, that boy. Maybe we’ll have a little prodigy on our hands. Let’s not get ahead of ourselves. First, let’s just focus on surviving the mosquitoes and the traffic. And maybe snagging those Florence tickets. Agreed. Right, shall we head back? I think he's starting to get a bit restless. Plus, I’m definitely needing a cup of tea after that mosquito assault.

Honestly, the recruitment agencies are driving me mad. I applied for, like, five jobs today and haven't even heard back from most of them. It’s just a black hole. Yeah, I know the feeling. It's brutal out there. At least you're putting yourself out there, though. That’s the main thing. Easy for you to say, Mr. Professional Golfer with a steady income! I'm just sitting here refreshing my emails every five minutes. Did you get much practice in today? Yeah, a pretty solid session at the driving range. Felt a bit… off though, to be honest. My swing just wasn’t clicking. You know how it is? Ugh, totally. Sometimes you just lose it. Must be frustrating though, especially when you're competing. I had a mini-crisis this morning trying to write a cover letter. I just couldn't seem to get the words right, sounded completely robotic. You should read it to me later, maybe a fresh pair of eyes will help. Did you end up watching that new spooky show on Netflix last night? The one I sent you? Oh! "The Haunting of Blackwood Manor"? Yeah! It was actually really good, spooky without being too cheesy. Definitely gave me a few nightmares though. I kept waking up worried there were ghosts in the bedroom. Seriously? You're scared of ghosts now? After all those late nights studying at uni, you're terrified of a bit of fiction? Hey! It’s the atmosphere, okay? The old house, the flickering lights… it just got to me. I had to pee like five times last night. Blame the show. Five times? That’s dedication to being scared! How about we go out for a proper treat tomorrow evening? We could hit up that new theatre – the one doing “A Midsummer Night’s Dream.” Ooh, yes! That sounds lovely. Something a bit different. I could really use a distraction from all this job hunting. What about food afterwards? I'm craving something seriously indulgent. We could try that new tapas place in Manchester. I heard they do incredible paella. Manchester? That's a bit of a trek, isn’t it? I was thinking maybe something a bit closer to home. We’ve got that Indian restaurant we both like. Yeah, that's a good shout. We could just pop there. It’s been a while. Are you sleeping okay otherwise?

"The wheels on the bus go round and round! Round and round! Round and round!" That’s quite the rendition, isn't it, love? He’s really committed to that song. He is! He’s been going on about buses all day. Wants to go on a “big bus!” Where did you even learn that word, Finn? Cloud bus! Big cloud! He thinks clouds are buses, doesn't he? That's adorable. It is, isn’t it? Right, so, dinner's almost ready. Sheena, is everything alright in the kitchen? Smells fantastic, by the way. Yeah, nearly done. Just finishing off the potatoes. Finn's been “helping” which mainly involves scattering flour everywhere. The joys of toddler assistance. Still, at least he's engaged. Reminds me of when I was little, used to get into everything. Mum used to despair! You were a handful, apparently. I remember! Hey! I was just energetic. Alright, alright, settle down you two. Finn, are you going to eat your broccoli, or are we having another battle? No! Broccoli! Come on, a couple of bites. Then you can go back to your cloud buses. I've got a film ready for after dinner. Do you want to watch it? What is it? That new Pixar one, 'Elemental'. It looks good. Finn seemed pretty interested in the trailer when I showed him. Sounds perfect. Finn, 'Elemental'? Do you want to see a film about fire and water? Fire! Water! Right, well, I'll go and get the drinks then. Anything you guys fancy? Just a pint of Guinness for me please. Thanks. I'll have a glass of red. Easy peasy! Coming right up. Just need to dodge the flour bombs. Finn, leave the flour alone, please! Cloud flour! He truly is a little rascal. But we wouldn't trade him for the world. Right, Finn, show us how the bus goes again! Let's hear those wheels! "The wheels on the bus go round and round..." Oh, my ears!
