It’s a beautiful chaos, isn’t it? A beautiful chaos. Just needs a bit less flour. Definitely needs less flour. And maybe a soundproof room for when he starts rapping. Let’s not tempt fate! We’ll stick to the wheels on the bus for now. Alright Finn let's see you show us your favourite colour! What colour is the bus? ....blue! You're a genius!

Morning, love. Did you see that? Honestly, Harry was practically sleeping in his pants last night. I did! I peeked. Cheeky monkey. Said he was ‘embracing the holiday vibe.’ The man’s got a point, though, it  is  lovely and warm. Daddy silly! He is a bit silly, isn’t he, Maisie? Daddy likes to be comfy. Hungry! Alright, alright, little man. Breakfast in a bit. Did you get much sleep, Liam? You seemed a bit restless. Not terribly, no. Kept thinking about… you know. The extension. Oh, here we go. Don’t tell me you’ve been sketching again while I was marking those essays. Just a few… rough ideas. Nothing serious. But imagine, a proper study, you know? Somewhere quiet where I can actually concentrate without Maisie and Archie trying to build a fort around my head. A valid point. And a decent playroom for them! No more building forts with my lesson plans. Exactly! We could get those bi-fold doors, letting in tons of light. Think about it – French doors, overlooking the garden… a little deck… Oh, you're dreaming big now. Bi-fold doors are  expensive . I know, I know. But it would really add value, wouldn't it? And we’ve got that inheritance to think about… Don’t start spending it before we’ve even had a proper conversation with Aunt Margaret. She’ll want a say, you know she will. Always loved this place. Garden! Can go play in garden? In a bit, sweetheart. After breakfast. Daddy and Mummy need to talk about… architect plans. Play now! Not yet, mate. Not yet. Imagine though, a proper games room... a little pool table… Honestly, Liam, you’re worse than the kids! Pool table? In Suffolk? You’ll have the neighbours talking. They’ll think we’re mad. They already do, darling. They know we sleep in our pants. True. Although, you really  did  go a bit far last night. Seriously, just boxer shorts? Comfort is key, Sarah! Comfort is key. Now, about those extension plans… Let’s get some pancakes going first. The kids are demanding. And then, the serious planning begins. Pancakes! Pancakes! Alright, alright, everyone calm down. Pancakes it is. Liam, you’re on the washing up. You have to earn those extension plans. Deal. But I'm putting the pool table in first. Just you wait. You'll be loving it.

This coffee is…adequate. Not quite the robust Italian blend I’m accustomed to, you know? Ah, you’re always dreaming of Italy, David. Tredegar coffee will never quite measure up, will it? Though, I must say, it’s a welcome break from that dreadful instant stuff they’ve started serving in the staff room. Dreadful is the right word, Gareth. It tastes like…well, like disappointment. Speaking of which, I’m still waiting to hear back about that funding application for the comparative linguistics project. Oh, the one on the evolution of Celtic loanwords in Arabic? Sounds fascinating, David. Any word from the Arts and Humanities Research Council? Nothing yet. Radio silence. It's frustrating, you know? Months of work, piles of data...and it all hinges on a grant decision. Makes you question the whole endeavour sometimes. Tell me about it! I’m battling with the same thing for my project on the sociolinguistics of Welsh dialect variation. They seem to think postgraduates can do all this research for peanuts these days. Precisely. And don't even get me started on the house renovations. I’ve decided to finally tackle the bathroom. Oh, that’s brave. DIY, eh? You're a professor of linguistics, not a builder! I know, I know. But the quotes from those builders were outrageous. Anyway, I’ve stripped out the old suite – a hideous avocado green monstrosity from the 70s. I’m trying to find some authentic Italian tiles, you see. Something to evoke the Amalfi coast... You and your Italy! My wife's gone mad for decorating too – trying to create this "rustic farmhouse" look. Resulting in a lot of distressed wood and beige. Far too beige for my liking. Beige is the enemy. Speaking of enemies, I had a terrible experience with Wessex Water the other day. Leaking pipe, they promised to be there within 24 hours. Turned out to be nearly 48! Wessex Water… oh, don’t even start. They’re a nightmare. You’d think with all the rain we’ve had, they’d be better equipped! Reminds me, did you see that article about the upgrades at the Large Hadron Collider? Yes, remarkable, truly. The advances in particle physics are astounding. It makes you wonder what secrets the universe is still holding. Absolutely. Though personally, I’m more concerned about the increasing cost of electricity to power the thing.

Right, operation Lego sort is a go! Okay, big box or small box first? Big box! Big box has the best bits! He agrees! See, even Arthur thinks the big box is the best. Right, who wants to find all the red bricks? Me! Me! I found one! Excellent work, Elsie! Now, Daddy, can you hunt for the yellow ones? We need to build a… a spaceship! A spaceship! Pew pew! Pew pew! Exactly! Pew pew! Arthur’s doing a fantastic impression. Okay, spaceship comes after we’ve sorted everything. Do you remember what we talked about last night, Elsie? About what happened in Harry Potter? When Harry fought the big snake! And Professor McGonagall turned into a cat! That’s right! Brilliant. What did you think of Barty Crouch Junior? He tricked everyone! He was bad! He certainly was. Right, Lego for a bit, then we can talk about The Simpsons. Do you guys know who my favourite character is? Homer! That’s a very popular choice! Arthur, who's your favourite? Turtles! Turtles! Of course! Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles are always a winner. Maybe we can watch one after we finish sorting the Lego? Can we go to the cinema to see a turtle movie? Please? We’ll see, Elsie. First, we finish the Lego, then we talk about Granny’s house. Daddy’s been saying something about new flooring, hasn’t he? Gran’s house is old! Everything needs fixing! It is a bit, darling. But Granny loves it. Speaking of fixing and sorting… Are you two craving some of that Easter chocolate yet? Chocolate! Chocolate! Alright, alright! One little square each. But then it’s back to the Lego! We need to find all the blue ones before you eat all the chocolate. It's like a treasure hunt. Building a spaceship  and  finding hidden treasure. What's better than that? Lego! And turtles! And chocolate! You're a good girl. Both of you. Now let's get back to it! This spaceship won’t build itself. And please, try not to eat  all  the chocolate. Save some for me! Okay, Mummy. But just one more piece... maybe... Elsie! Okay, okay, just one more. But then operation Lego continues! That’s it! The best team ever. Now let's see if we can find… a purple brick! A purple brick would be amazing! Where are all the purple bricks hiding?!

Oh my god, you're back! Look at you, you look so tanned! And relaxed. Hey! It's so good to be back, honestly. I feel like I've been away for ages, but also like it was just yesterday. How was everything here? Did the flat survive without me? Everything's fine, don't worry. It was a bit quiet, admittedly. I kept accidentally buying enough food for three people. Seriously, the fridge was overflowing. And Liam kept coming round to watch the football. Liam, bless him. Did he actually win any? He’s always so optimistic, even when they're getting absolutely thrashed. No, not really. A couple of draws, mostly losses. He made a huge deal about one draw though, insisted on ordering pizza and celebrating like they’d won the league. Classic Liam. So, tell me everything. Where did you go? Holiday details, ASAP! Okay, okay! We went to Crete, remember? Honestly, it was amazing. The water was incredible, the food… oh, the food! I think I ate my weight in gyros and souvlaki. Gyros are the best. Did you do any exploring? Besides sunbathing and stuffing your face, of course. We did! We went on a boat trip to some tiny islands, did some snorkelling, hiked up a mountain… it was exhausting, but in the best way possible. And I finally managed to learn a few basic Greek phrases. "Yasas" and "Efharisto" were the highlights. That’s fab! Did you see any cute guys? Don't tell me you went the whole time without at least  one  flirt. Right, you’re bringing up my past, aren't you? There was one… a waiter, actually. Very charming, very flirtatious. But nothing serious, thankfully. It was nice to just… relax and not think about anything. Smart move. So, work hasn't been too chaotic while you've been away? Honestly, I’m dreading going back. Sarah called a couple of times sounding absolutely frantic. Apparently, the Johnson account is a complete mess. I'm going to be knee-deep in spreadsheets for weeks. Oh, no! That sounds horrible. Well, at least you're back now, and you can dive straight in. What about you? How was your yoga retreat? Did you achieve inner peace? It was… interesting. Mostly a lot of downward-facing dogs and chanting. Some of the other people were  very  intense. One woman spent the entire time talking about crystals.

Right then, love, tea's brewed. Grandma and Grandpa settled in nicely? Yeah, they’re watching Bargain Hunt. Grandpa was shouting at the telly, says he could've bought those ceramics for half the price. He always says that, doesn't he? Thinks he’s a millionaire, that man. I did, didn’t I? Should have bid a bit lower. Those people are daft. You always were a shrewd one, Dad. Now, about the heating. It’s a bit nippy in here, isn’t it? Yeah, a bit. Should I put it up a degree? Aye, do that. And I’ve ordered those new lightbulbs you wanted, Ethan. Should be here tomorrow. Brilliant, thanks. They're the ones that last ages, right? Less changing. The very ones. Saves a fortune in the long run. Your Grandma keeps forgetting to turn the lights off, though. I do not! I’m very careful. Just sometimes…well, you know. Memory’s not what it was. She leaves 'em on in the bathroom, then wonders why the bill's high. You're getting away with it today, Mum! Ethan, you'll have to keep an eye on her, will you? Just a gentle reminder. No problem. I’ll be around a lot this weekend anyway, helping with the garden. That'd be lovely. The weeds are taking over, as usual. Honestly, they grow faster than I can pull 'em out. It’s like they’re mocking me. Why don’t scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything! Good one, Elsie! Always did have a good sense of humor. Oh, Grandma. Oh, that’s a classic! Your Grandpa’s still got all his jokes, hasn’t he? Aye, got a few crackers left yet. Though sometimes they come out a bit muddled. Like the other day, I was telling someone about a duck... Oh, here we go... ...and I ended up talking about a hedgehog. Completely lost the plot, I did. Heard that one already! It’s the age, love. The age. You'll get there eventually. So, Grandma, are you comfortable? Need any blankets? I'm reet pet, love. Don't fuss. Just bring me another biscuit. And a bit more tea. Strong this time, mind. You tidying your room before you come back tomorrow lad? It’s a state. Yeah, Grandpa, I'll try. It's… a work in progress. That’s my grandson.

Right, so we’re watching Peter Pan tonight, yeah? Are you both excited? Yes! Tinkerbell! Yes! Tinkerbell’s brilliant. Do you remember we talked about Great Ormond Street Hospital the other day, darling? Mmm-hmm. The ones with the fairies. Exactly! Well, Tinkerbell is a fairy, and they’re helping poorly children at the hospital. It’s really amazing. Remember we said we could maybe do something to help them? Yeah! We could give them glitter! Glitter might not be the best thing for the children’s rooms, sweetheart. But the idea is lovely, isn’t it? We’ll think of something grown-up we can do. Can I be Captain Hook? Oh, you want to be Captain Hook? He’s a bit naughty, isn’t he? He steals Peter Pan’s treasure. He has a hook! I want a hook! I know you do, darling. We might have to make you a pretend one. Captain Hook’s always trying to catch Peter Pan. And Peter Pan never grows up! That's the magic of Neverland. Why doesn't he grow up? Well, he stays in Neverland, remember? It’s a magical place where you can fly and there are fairies and mermaids and all sorts of amazing things. You never have to be a grown-up. And Tinkerbell sprinkles pixie dust! She does! She sprinkles pixie dust to help Peter Pan fly. Have you seen the Tinkerbell films? The ones where she has her own adventures? Yeah! She fights the wolves! You’ve got a good memory! She’s very brave, isn’t she? Sometimes she gets into trouble, but she always finds a way to sort things out. It’s like being a real-life fairy. Is it better than Pan? They're both good! They’re different. Pan is about Peter and Wendy and the Lost Boys, and Tinkerbell films are all about Tinkerbell and her friends. It's about being good, and brave, and protecting the forest and the fairies in it. Can we watch both? Well, maybe another night. Tonight, we're having an adventure with Peter Pan and Captain Hook. Are you ready to fly to Neverland? Speaker_2 & Yes! Right then pop corn? . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . H.HH.H.

Right, so we’re really heading out now then. Just need to make sure Mum's got everything she needs. Water, snacks… you know the drill. The drill. Always the drill with you girls. Honestly, you treat me like a toddler sometimes. Don't be daft, Dad. You forget your inhaler half the time. It's just practical. And Mum’s tired after that early start. Fair enough, fair enough. Though I can still manage to pack my own bag, thank you very much. Still feels odd, really, leaving you both here. Bit quiet, the house will be. Don't worry, you've got loads of books to plough through, haven’t you? And remember to actually get some proper sleep this week. No more midnight news watching. I’ll try. Though I do enjoy a bit of the six o’clock news, don't I? Keeps me informed. Informed of what? All the things that are going wrong in the world? Honestly, Dad, peace and quiet is good for you. It’ll do you good to recharge. Remember when we used to live near Taunton? That drive felt even longer than this one. All those winding country roads… felt like we’d never get to school on time. Oh god, those were the days! Being stuck behind tractors forever. And remember that tiny cottage near Bovey Tracey? The one with the overgrown garden? Fond memories. Though the garden  was  a bit of a jungle, wasn't it? Took you both forever to tame it. We had some lovely summers there, though. So much space for running around. Now look at us, crammed into a car on our way to say goodbye. Well, we’re all going to be together for Christmas, aren't we? And we need to start planning a proper house-warming party for you. Now that you’re settled in the new place and I've got the garden sorted. A house-warming party sounds lovely, actually. A bit of a gathering. I’ve got a few old colleagues I could invite. Excellent. We’ll start planning it properly when I’m back. What are you thinking of doing while you're away? Anything exciting planned? Just relaxing. Catching up on some reading. Might try to have a proper routine. Actually get to bed before midnight. You know, the simple things. It’s a shame we can’t stay longer, but you’ve got that meeting on Monday, haven't you?

Dreadfully dusty, isn’t it? All this restoration work. Makes a body ache, it does. Aye, it does that. Proper hard graft, this. You waiting long? Not particularly. Just popped in to enquire about the ME event next year. I heard it’s being held here again. Oh, the Model Engineering Society event? Yes, that's right. Been coming here for years now. Bit of a tradition it’s become. Wonderful. I'm rather keen to attend. I'm hoping there’ll be a significant focus on women’s involvement this year, too. I’ve noticed in the past, it's been… rather male-dominated. Well, you’re spot on there. Historically, it’s always been a bit of a boys’ club, hasn’t it? But they’re trying to rectify that, I understand. They’ve got a new committee, seem keen to be more inclusive. Good. So important. I spent most of my life battling that sort of thing, you know. Running a gallery, dealing with antiques... you’d be surprised how casually patronising people can be. It was a constant fight for equal footing. I can imagine. My late wife, Elsie, she was a primary school teacher over in Birmingham. Always fighting for the kids, you know? Wanted every child to have a proper start, especially with their nursery education. She believed it was the foundation for everything. Absolutely. Early years are critical. It's astounding how many people still don't realize that. Though I do firmly believe there has to be a gentler approach these days. You know, a more holistic view? I’ve recently taken up Swedish massage... surprisingly revitalizing. Good for the body  and  the mind. Swedish massage, eh? Never tried it myself. Elsie used to get terrible aches in her back from standing all day with the children. We tried everything, you know? Chiropractors, osteopaths… eventually she ended up volunteering at the local hospice. Oh, dear. That's… that’s brave of her. She said it gave her a sense of peace. Helping those who needed it most. Funny thing is, it was often more beneficial for her than it was for the residents, I think. It kept her going through some tough times. She herself had a bit of a scare a few years back, you know. Oh, I'm so sorry to hear that. It's a cruel world. One must cling to whatever brings comfort.

Right, so I was looking at flights again, and EasyJet have a really good deal to Seville in October. Like, surprisingly good. Seville, lovely! Haven't been there in years. Remember that little tapas place we found near the cathedral? Absolutely divine. I’ve been reading up on it, seems beautiful. Warm enough to still be pleasant, but not boiling like it would be in July or August. October is ideal. Are you thinking of a package, or will you book separately? I always find the separate thing a bit of a faff. I was leaning towards booking separately. Gives us more flexibility, you know? We could stay in a nice little Airbnb instead of a hotel. Airbnb can be a gamble, though. Read the reviews very carefully, darling. Watch out for those with only a few, or a lot of vague ones. Definitely. I'm being really meticulous this time. I found one near the Santa Cruz quarter, it's got a little balcony and a lovely courtyard... Oh, a balcony! Perfect for sipping something refreshing. What’s the budget like for accommodation? Don't want you breaking the bank. Remember that disaster in Rome? Oh god, don’t remind me about the cockroach. This is going to be different, I promise. I'm aiming for around £70-£80 a night. Is that reasonable for Seville? That sounds perfectly sensible, actually. Seville's not as crazy expensive as some places. Have you looked at transport within the city? Is it walkable, or do you need to consider buses and trams? It seems very walkable. Lots of articles recommending walking tours, anyway. I was thinking we could take a day trip or two, maybe to Cordoba? Or Cadiz, even. Cadiz would be wonderful! But Cordoba’s closer, less travel time. And the Mezquita is absolutely spectacular, you really must see it. Book tickets in advance, though, it gets very busy. Okay, good tip. I’ll add that to the list. I'm starting to feel a bit overwhelmed with the planning, to be honest. It  is  a lot, dear. But it’s exciting, isn’t it? Break it down into manageable chunks. Flights, accommodation, attractions, food... just little bits at a time. That's good advice. I'm just worried about missing something. And finding somewhere good to eat. Seville is a foodie paradise! Just wander around Santa Cruz, you’ll find tapas bars on every corner.

Alright, so I was looking at my bank statement, and there’s a charge from… "Cricket Wireless" for £37.50. Any idea what that is? Cricket Wireless? Nah, doesn’t ring a bell. Thought you were all about Virgin Mobile these days. Why would you be on Cricket? Exactly! That's what I’m thinking. I haven’t signed up for anything new, and I definitely wouldn’t be using a US provider. It's throwing me. Could be a scam. Could be. Check your phone, see if there are any unfamiliar apps installed. Sometimes they sneak in unnoticed. Happened to my cousin last year – ended up with a subscription he didn't even know about. Good shout. Yeah, I’ll have a look. Speaking of phones, did you catch the Man U game last night? Absolute disaster. Tell me about it! Typical. Waste of a Saturday. Rashford’s been off form for weeks. They need to sort something out quickly. Agreed. Rashford’s just not looking sharp. I reckon they should give Elanga a run in the team. He’s got pace, at least. Elanga’s a decent shout. Raw, though. Needs experience. Speaking of experience... work’s been mad busy lately, as always. They’re pushing the new sales targets again. Oh yeah? What’s the target this time? Seems like every month there’s a new, ridiculous figure. This one’s pretty ambitious. Got to increase sales of the premium packages by 15% this quarter. It’s gonna be a stretch, that’s for sure. Good luck with that. Sounds stressful. How’s your dad doing? Haven’t spoken to him in a while. He’s good, yeah. Bit stiff in the mornings, as usual, but otherwise he’s alright. He says he saw your mum at the supermarket the other day. Said she was asking about you. Oh, tell her I said hi! I’ll give her a call later. I'm heading back to Uni in the week, so it will be good to catch up. It's going by so fast. You'll be back before you know it. Just need to try and stay out of trouble, yeah? No promises. Always an adventure, isn’t it? Let me just check this phone.Definitely something dodgy going on here. This Cricket Wireless thing is driving me mad. Right. Let me know how you get on with it.

You know, I was trying to Skype with young David earlier, but the connection was dreadful. Kept cutting out. Nearly gave me a migraine, it did. Oh dear. He’s got a good computer, hasn’t he? Must be the signal. We had trouble with it last week, remember? With your granddaughter. Broadband’s a fickle beast, isn’t it? Prices keep going up too. Remember when you could get a decent deal? Aye, remember. Everything's gone up. Even the price of a globes. Fancy that, eh? Used to be a fiver or so, now they’re costing a fortune. You’re obsessed with globes, Arthur. Remember when you were showing me that one you got from that antique shop in Norwich? With the old empires marked out. Fascinating, that was. Makes you think about things, doesn’t it? Used to love traveling, you know. Holidaying in Yorkshire. Used to stay in youth hostels. Clean as a whistle they were, back then. My lads did some school project on Yorkshire once. They had to build a model of Fountains Abbey. Took over the kitchen table for a week. Absolute chaos. Oh, school projects. Don't get me started. My little ones were always doing them. One time, they had to build a model of the London underground system! With little trains and everything. Nearly bankrupted me, all the cardboard and glue. London, eh? Always found it a bit overwhelming, myself. Too many people rushing about. Give me the countryside any day. Got to get the garden sorted this spring, though. The weeds are taking over. You should send me some cuttings, Arthur. My wife’s got a real green thumb. She's always building things from scratch. Speaking of building, how are you getting on with your knee? Still bothering you? Don't remind me. Awful, it is. Bad leg’s playing up something fierce today. Keeps me stuck indoors. You need to keep moving, Arthur. Even a short walk around the garden will do you good. She's right Arthur. Remember how happy you always were when you were out pottering about. Aye, happy. It's just… aches something terrible. Still, can't grumble too much. At least I've got good company. Absolutely. Speaking of company, did you see that documentary on television last night about the badger sett near Evesham? No, I missed it. Was it any good?

Right, so EasyJet's being a nightmare, as usual. I keep refreshing and the prices keep creeping up. Tell me about it! I've been trying to book ours for ages. Are you looking at flights for the weekend after next? Yeah, Friday evening to Sunday. It's for Sarah's birthday, remember? Blackpool, big night out. Oh yeah! Totally forgot about that. I'm so useless sometimes. Okay, let me have a quick look… Right, flight’s £85 each, including the baggage. Is that alright with you? Oof, a bit pricey, isn’t it? I was hoping for a bit less. Let me just check Skyscanner… Nope, same price everywhere. I suppose it's peak time, innit? Exactly. You can’t win. Shall I just book them then? I can ping you the details. Yeah, go for it. You're much better at this than I am, I always end up getting confused. What about you? Any drama sorting your flights? Nah, mine were surprisingly okay. Got them last week for about £60 each. Seriously lucky, I think. Wow, you absolute star! I’m proper jealous. Don’t be! Just be grateful I’m doing the booking for you. Right, done! Sent you the confirmation. Have a look and let me know. Just checking… yeah, looks good. Cheers, babe! You’re a lifesaver. So, dinner was lovely, wasn't it? That pasta was banging. It was! Honestly, I’m stuffed. Think I need to lie down for a bit. Fancy putting something on the TV? Yeah, definitely. What are you in the mood for? Something mindless? I’m not really concentrating tonight after all that flight-booking stress. Perfect. Let's put on that awful reality show we both secretly love. You know, the one with the rich people renovating houses? [Laughing] Oh god, yes! Bring on the marble countertops and faux pas! Honestly, it’s so bad, it's brilliant. Totally. Though I do get proper stressed watching them argue about budgets... reminds me too much of real life. Tell me about it. Keeps me up at night, thinking about the mortgage and everything. Wish I'd just gone for a smaller place. Don’t say that! It's a beautiful house. Loads of space for us . And you love it really. I do, I do. Just having a moment of financial panic, that’s all. Blackpool’s not helping, is it?

Right then, let’s have a look at these statements. Seems a bit steep, doesn't it? Milk’s two-fifty a pint now. Two-fifty! When I was a lad… It is ridiculous, Dad. Honestly, everything’s gone up. Even the supermarket’s own brand stuff. You're telling me! I went to Aldi the other day and even their cheap biscuits were pricey. They're all making a killing, aren't they? That they are. And the council tax… don't get me started. Seems like every year it climbs a bit higher. I’m thinking of moving somewhere smaller, less council tax. Where would you go, Dad? You'd miss all your friends here. And me, obviously. You’ll always have a place in my heart, love. But I just feel like I'm throwing money away these days. Paying for services I don't even use. Tell me about it. I had another nightmare with the police yesterday. Some kid causing trouble down the street. Didn’t do much, just shouting really, but they had sirens blaring, lights flashing… absolute chaos. Oh no, really? Yes. And the officer was just… dismissive. Like I was bothering him. No apology for the disruption. The whole justice system's gone to pot, I tell you. It’s all politics, that's what it is. Promise the world, deliver nothing. And everything costs more. Got a letter from Barclays the other day, telling me about some new ‘fees’ they’re introducing. Honestly, it’s daylight robbery. What kind of fees? Just for having an account, apparently. Unless you use it a certain amount each month. It's crazy. I was thinking of moving to a credit union. Good idea. They’re usually much fairer. I’ve got a couple of friends who swear by them. I might look into that too. These mobile phone providers are the same. One year they're offering deals, the next they’re charging you through the nose for something you didn't even know you were signing up for. You're right about that. My bill's been ridiculous lately. Gotta call them again, I suppose. Another hour on hold, listening to that dreadful music. It's always the same, isn't it? They train them not to actually  help  you. Just to keep you on the line for as long as possible. It's appalling.

Right, so we’re doing this ‘favourites’ thing then? Honestly, it feels a bit weird listing everything but alright. I’ll go first. Favourite food... honestly? A really good boerewors roll. Proper South African one, with the chakalaka. Takes me right back home. A boerewors roll? You’re proper random, aren’t you, Chloe? Alright, my turn. Favourite food has to be parmo. No contest. You lot have probably never had one. A parmo? What’s a parmo? Is that a Northern thing? Oh, you're missing out, Aisling! It’s this breaded chicken or pork escalope, covered in cheese and tomato sauce. It's  amazing . Proper comfort food. Sounds heavy! My favourite food is probably… a really good Sunday roast. Proper Yorkshire puddings, loads of gravy, all the trimmings. Makes me feel like I’m home. Sunday roast is good, but you can't beat a good plate of chips, can you? Like, thick-cut chips, loads of salt and vinegar. Simple pleasures, ya know? Chips are good, but a proper boerewors roll... it’s got that spice, and the bread is always toasted perfectly... it just hits different. Anyway, favourite animal. Definitely a honey badger. Don’t mess with a honey badger. A honey badger?! You’re mental. Mine’s a Labrador. Classic, I know, but they’re just the loveliest, goofiest dogs. Always happy to see you. I love a fluffy cat. Like a Persian. All long and floofy. So soft. A Welsh corgi, definitely. They’re just so… enthusiastic. And short! They look like little loafs. I’m gonna go with a squirrel. They’re cheeky little things, always getting into mischief. I used to watch them bury nuts in my garden when I was little. Okay, okay. Favourite holiday destination? South Africa, obviously! But specifically the Garden Route. Gorgeous scenery, beaches… just…  sigh . Cornwall. Definitely. I love the coast, the beaches, the pasties! Greece. Any of the Greek islands. The sun, the sea, the food… brilliant. Snowdonia. Always. It's just… breathtaking. The mountains, the lakes… it’s home. Majorca. Went there last summer and it was unreal. Beautiful beaches, good nightlife… already planning on going back next year. Right, well that was… interesting. Didn’t realise we all had such varied tastes! Aye, it’s good to know we’re all a bit bonkers in our own way though, isn't it? Definitely makes for a good flat.

Honestly, thinking about being old is just…weird. Like, imagining myself knitting and complaining about the weather. You’d probably be knitting incredibly elaborate, colourful jumpers, though. Not beige cardigans. Maybe! But the thought of not being able to, you know, climb a hill, or dance, or even just…do things. It’s massively depressing. I know, right? It feels so far off though. Like it’s something that happens to  other  people. But then Gran’s only, what, 78? And she’s starting to…slow down. Exactly. It’s hitting home a bit more. So, has the essay been a nightmare? I’m still staring at a blank page about abstract expressionism. How am I supposed to eloquently describe splodges of paint? Tell me about it! Mine's on the impact of video games on modern art. I'm seriously questioning my life choices. Professor Davies just loves to throw curveballs. Video games and art! That's actually kind of brilliant though. Like, think about the level of detail and precision in some games now. It's practically digital sculpture. Yeah, that’s what I’m trying to argue. The world-building alone - it's a form of visual storytelling. And the colour palettes, the composition…it's all there. I’m using Breath of the Wild as a main example; the landscapes are stunning. Ooh, good choice! Very aesthetically pleasing. You should talk about the use of colour theory too, how they use it to convey mood and atmosphere. Good shout! I’ll add that in. Maybe I should just start describing Skyrim and all the dragons… Now you're talking! Although, you might lose some academic credibility. Probably. But it’d be more engaging, wouldn't it? It's all about finding ways to make it interesting. What about you? Any breakthroughs with the splodges? Not really. I’m thinking about how Pollock said he was channelling some sort of primal energy, but it just seems like he was flinging paint around. It does a bit, doesn't it? But maybe that’s the point. That it’s raw, unfiltered emotion. Like, he's reacting to something, not thinking about it. Hmm. Maybe. I should probably read some more about it. Ugh, wishing I'd paid more attention in art history. We all do. Speaking of wanting to be a teenager again, are you still obsessed with Animal Crossing?

Honestly, I’m starving. This day has been brutal. Tell me about it. I’ve had a full-on day with Mrs. Davies, you wouldn’t believe. She was convinced the nurses were plotting against her knitting circle. Seriously? Knitters are a powerful force, you know. Can’t afford to make enemies. What are we even having for dinner? Smells delicious. It’s that lentil thing we found that recipe for. Remember? Apparently, it’s super healthy and filling. Oh right! The one from that ridiculous food blog? I'm dubious, but I'll trust you. Did you manage to get the chorizo? Yep! Found some at the little Spanish deli downtown. It smelled amazing. Think it’ll add a nice kick. Good thinking. I'm seriously lacking in spice in my life. Did you hear back from Liam about Saturday? Nope, radio silence. Honestly, I'm starting to suspect he's just stringing me along. Oh no! Don't let him do that. You deserve better than breadcrumbs, especially after that awful date last week. I know, right? He spent the entire evening talking about his stamp collection. A stamp collection, Elara! I felt like I was on a bizarre wildlife documentary. Oh my god, that’s awful! Did he at least offer to show you his prized Penny Black? Don't remind me. He practically wept over it. I was just picturing myself running for the hills. Definitely a red flag. Seriously, if he's more enthusiastic about stamps than you, it’s time to move on. You're way too awesome for a stamp enthusiast. You’re just saying that because you’re my best friend. Maybe. But also because it’s objectively true. Speaking of awesomeness, did you manage to sort out Sophie's birthday? Almost! I was thinking karaoke next weekend? There's that place near the station, "Off Key." It's got terrible lighting, but the cocktails are decent. Karaoke! That's brilliant! I'm totally in. We need to rope in Mark, he's got that dodgy rendition of Bohemian Rhapsody down pat. Perfect! I’ll send him a message then. Also, I’m planning on trying that new yoga class on Tuesday evening, fancy joining me? It’s supposed to be really relaxing. Ooh, tempting. My body is practically screaming for some relaxation. Let me see what’s on. I might have that report deadline looming, though.

Right then, let’s tackle this speaker consent form first. Seems a bit excessive, doesn't it? Recording a seminar – I mean, it's good to have the material available, but… It does feel a little formal, doesn't it, Margaret? But the university legal team are being particularly stringent these days, aren't they? Best to just get it signed and out of the way. I've drafted it with all the required caveats, ensuring participants are made fully aware it’s being recorded and for what purpose. Aye, I've had to use it for a couple of my postgraduate workshops lately. Bit of a faff, but better safe than sorry, I reckon. I’ll send it round now – everyone just sign where indicated, please. Right. Moving on. So, the seminar structure… I was thinking a broad overview of the challenges of cross-cultural communication in the first half, then delve into specific regional nuances in the second. What do you reckon, Deborah? Sounds sensible, Margaret. I was wondering, though, if we could incorporate some practical role-playing exercises? Maybe a simulated negotiation scenario? Something to really engage the students. I like that idea, Deborah. It’s always more memorable than just lecturing at them. I’ve got a few case studies I could adapt – some fairly classic intercultural gaffes, you know. The one about the American negotiator and the Japanese business deal is always a good laugh, albeit a cautionary one. Oh, the one with the gift-giving faux pas? Yes, that's a cracking example. We could do a quick recap of Hofstede's cultural dimensions first, just to give them a framework for understanding. Aye, and perhaps touch on Trompenaars’ dimensions as well. Variety’s the spice of life, isn’t it? Keep ‘em on their toes. I’ve got some data on communication styles in Southeast Asia that might be interesting to showcase as well. Good thinking. We don't want to just focus on the US versus Europe, do we? It’s international business  communication , after all. We need to cover a decent spread of regions. Perhaps a brief section on nonverbal communication as well? Gestures and body language vary so much. Definitely. I was planning on incorporating some visuals - some infographics illustrating the differences. I’ve found a few decent ones online, though we have to be careful about copyright, naturally. I can dig through the academic databases – there’s usually a wealth of research on that sort of thing.

Honestly, that seminar was dreadful. I’m not sure half of them were even listening. You’re kidding. Which one? The ones on post-structuralism, right? Always a minefield. The very one. And you could see it on their faces – glazed over, desperately trying to look engaged. One of them was actively knitting, for goodness sake. Knitting? Seriously? That’s a new level of passive resistance. I know! I tried to steer it back to something relevant, you know, connect it to contemporary art, but crickets. Absolute crickets. I might need a stiff drink. You deserve one. How’s the marking coming along? Is that the mountain of essays still looming? It’s… well, it's a smaller mountain now. I finally finished the introductory ones. Some of them were… creative, let's say. One student wrote their entire essay in rhyming couplets. No! Really? About what? Something about the impact of Dada on modern societal norms. It was… confusing, to say the least. And very, very long. Oh, bless them. Some people just think more is always better. Speaking of mountains, any further developments on the house front? Did you call the surveyor again? I did. Apparently, the subsidence issue isn’t as bad as initially thought, but still needs some attention. He estimates it’ll be another two to three thousand just to stabilise the foundations. Two to three thousand? Ugh. That's a rather significant dent in our savings. It is. I’m starting to wonder if we’re just throwing good money after bad. Maybe we should just forget the whole thing. Don’t say that. We’ve loved this place from the moment we saw it. It’s got character, and a garden, and it's relatively close to town. We just need a slightly more realistic appraisal of the costs involved. But the garden is overgrown, the roof leaks, and now we have subsidence issues. It feels like every time we fix one thing, two more things break. Look, it’s an old house. It’s going to require ongoing maintenance. Every house does. We knew that going in. And besides, think of the potential! Imagine when you’ve finally got that vegetable patch flourishing. You're always so optimistic. Someone has to be. Come on, let's grab some dumplings from that little place on Elm Street. My treat. Consider it a preventative measure against the stresses of academia and dodgy foundations.

This lentil soup is actually really good, isn't it? I was worried it'd be bland. Yeah, it is. You've really nailed it. Though, honestly, I still don’t know how you manage to cook so much so often. I feel guilty if I heat up leftovers. It’s just habit, I suppose. And I hate wasting food. Remember Grandma's house? The sheer volume of food she used to make, and then the slightly panicked rush to get rid of it all at the end of the week? Oh god, yeah. Mountains of stew, enough for an army. And she’d be like, ‘You  have  to take some home, darling, or it'll go to waste!’ She genuinely freaked out about waste. Total food guilt. It's interesting, isn’t it? We’re so much more aware of it now – the plastic bag charge, the whole food waste scandal. Definitely. I still feel a pang of guilt when I chuck a limp carrot in the bin. You know, it’s funny, I was reading an article about modular farming – like farms inside shipping containers, in the middle of cities. Urban farming? That’s clever. Imagine, fresh lettuce grown practically on your doorstep. Exactly! They’re talking about using robotics too. Automated planting, harvesting… it's getting a bit dystopian, isn’t it? Like, what happens to all the farmworkers? It’s the same argument with pretty much every wave of industrialization. Jobs lost, jobs created… it’s a constant shuffle. Thinking about careers, actually. I was talking to a student the other day, really bright, wanted to be an engineer, but felt steered towards law because everyone said it was more ‘secure’. That’s ridiculous. Good engineers are always in demand. It's just – some industries feel a bit 'closed off,' doesn't it? Like, you need to know someone, or go to the right school. Absolutely. It's so frustrating when you see potential stifled. I tried to tell her about work experience opportunities at my old uni. Maybe she could try to get something lined up. Good idea. Do you think they still offer those? It feels like those kinds of things are fading away. I think so. Although, it’s getting harder to get companies to release people for it. Everyone is so pressed for time. What's your workplace like now? Still incredibly stressful?

Right, so the initial results from the study are… interesting. Very interesting. Interesting how? Interesting in a 'we need to throw everything out and start again' kind of way, or interesting in a 'this could actually be useful’ kind of way? More the latter, I think. There’s a definite correlation between… well, it's complicated. Basically, people who perceive their social support to be lower, even if it objectively isn't, are reporting higher levels of chronic stress. So, perception is key as always, isn't it? That’s the psychology bit, I suppose. Remind me, are you using the Dunbar number as a baseline for social circles? I am. It's proving surprisingly robust. The interesting bit is the mediating variable – it seems to centre around feelings of validation. People who feel like their experiences and feelings are validated, even by a small group, seem to be buffering the stress. That makes sense, doesn’t it? We all need to feel seen. Anything useful for practice? Sounds like my clients could all benefit from a bit more validation. Potentially. It strengthens the argument for encouraging more mindful communication and active listening. It’s about creating space for people to truly feel heard, not just... responded to. Right. Speaking of being heard, Mum called. Again. Oh, dear. What was it this time? The garden gnomes? Worse. She's decided the cat is judging her. Seriously. Apparently, Mr. Snuggles gives her “a look” when she’s reading romance novels. The cat has sophisticated taste, then. You tried explaining that cats are just being cats? Of course. I used all my therapeutic skills, the empathetic listening, the validation… nothing. She's convinced he’s sending her messages. You need to gently redirect and focus on something else. Distraction is key with Mum. Have you told her about the village fete? I’ve mentioned it. She’s worried about the jam. Apparently, no one appreciates her Seville orange marmalade anymore. Tell her it’s a niche market. Explain the complexity of the peel. Remind her it takes hours. You're good at this. Should be doing Mum's therapy. Don’t tempt me. I’ve got enough on my plate with these stubbornly non-linear research findings. How was your day, by the way? Assessment Manager must be stressful. Pretty standard. One particularly challenging case involving a student with significant learning difficulties and a very unhelpful school.

Just can’t seem to shake this feeling, can I? Like a lead weight in me chest. Been like this for weeks now. Now, Arthur, don't you start on that again. You know we’re all here for you. What’s brought it on today? The weather’s been a bit gloomy, hasn't it? Aye, proper miserable. Couldn't be further from that sunshine we had last week. You were saying it reminded you of the beaches in Norfolk, weren't you, Arthur? It did. It truly did. The sand…the smell of the sea…used to go there every summer with me mam and dad. Felt…free. Now…now it just feels a million miles away. This house… it’s just walls closing in on me, you know? You know you could always look at going somewhere smaller, Arthur. Somewhere closer to the sea, even. It would be a big change, I know, but… Don't see the point, Doris. Wouldn’t have anyone here. All me friends are…well, they’re gone. And this place...it’s full of memories, good and bad. Can’t just uproot that. Look, mate, I get it. It’s tough. But you're letting it swallow you whole. You can't let the past dictate your present. You've got to focus on what you can do, right now. Easy for you to say, Tom. You've got your family, your teaching… a purpose. I’m just…sitting here. Nonsense, Arthur. You’ve got us! We’re your family. And there’s plenty you  can  do. Remember that volunteering thing you were looking at, down at the wildlife sanctuary? Helping with the baby blue tits and all? Aye, that did sound nice. Little fledglings needing help. Exactly! Something to get you out, something to focus on. And it’s good work, Arthur. Really good work. You've always had a way with animals. And think about it; it’s a lovely place. Open spaces, fresh air, birdsong…it’s a world away from these four walls. I keep thinking about the bills, Doris. They just keep piling up. The council tax… the heating… it’s a worry, even with my pension. It just…adds to the whole weight of things. Money's tight for everyone, Arthur. Don't you beat yourself up about it. Have you looked at that charity they mentioned on the telly the other day?

Honestly, I’ve been obsessed with this serum lately. You absolutely have to try it. Oh really? What is it? You know I'm always looking for something new, my skin is just… blah right now. It’s a Vitamin C serum from The Ordinary. The big orange one. I know everyone goes on about them, but it's actually delivered massively for me. My skin feels so much brighter, and I think the fine lines are even lessened a little. The Ordinary, yeah? I’ve seen those everywhere. So cheap too, isn’t it? Are you sure it’s any good then? Sometimes I think you get what you pay for, you know? I was the same at first! But genuinely, it's brilliant. Don't let the price put you off. It’s just concentrated ingredients. I put it on after my cleanser, before my moisturiser. It tingles a little bit, which I read was normal. Tingling? Good or bad tingling? Good tingling! Like a wake-up call for your skin. Not nasty burning, just a bit of a buzz. Do you use a moisturiser at night? Yeah, I’ve been using this Nivea cream for ages. It’s nothing fancy, but it’s reliable, and doesn’t break me out. Good! You need something to seal it in. Anyway, aside from my new skincare obsession, how are things with… you know, Sarah? Have you heard from her lately? Not properly. Sent a few messages, but she's just so busy with the new job. I feel like we’re drifting a bit, which is a shame. Remember when we used to spend every weekend shopping? Oh my god, remember Debenhams? We practically lived there! We’d spend hours trying on ridiculous outfits. And then end up with nothing! It was such a waste of time, but a good waste of time. You should come with me next weekend, we could actually get something useful this time. I’d love to! I need some new jeans. All mine have gone baggy. And I want to get my nails done, I'm thinking a nice dark red. You still going to that salon on the High Street? Yeah, still going there. Chloe’s amazing – she always knows exactly what colour will suit me. You should book an appointment, they're getting busy. I will. I've been wishing I had longer nails lately.

Right, so, they’ve finally sorted out the parking down by the Tate. Proper nightmare it was last week, yeah? Had to walk all the way from the Albert Dock. Tell me about it. Nearly gave up going altogether. Proper dodgy too, all those wardens hanging around. Reckon they’re making a killing. Definitely. So, how was today with the kids? Anything mental happened? You don't even want to know. Little Liam threw a plate of spaghetti at his dinner lady. Full on assault. Had to mediate a dispute between two lads over a Pokemon card. It’s relentless, mate. Absolutely relentless. Sounds like a Tuesday. My lesson went alright though. The kids are finally starting to get their heads around Shakespeare. Bit of a miracle if you ask me. You’re a saint, you are. Teaching teenagers Shakespeare? I’d rather wrestle a badger. It's not  that  bad. Though, you won’t believe, Sarah and Mark are going all out for their wedding. Apparently, they’re aiming for a Tudor theme. A Tudor theme? Seriously? What is that, like dressing everyone in ruffs and farthingales? Pretty much. She was showing me some pictures online. It's gonna cost them a fortune. I reckon they're going to be skint for a year afterwards. Probably should have saved up a bit for a deposit, eh? Speaking of which, you still thinking about moving? Yeah, I am. Looking at places in the suburbs. Little garden, somewhere that doesn't sound like a motorway. Smart move. Less noise, less hassle. Though, getting out of this city can be a nightmare during rush hour. I know! But it's got to be better than being right in the centre. What about you? Still thinking about that Masters interview? Yeah, got it next week. Proper nervous, though. It’s a big commitment, time-wise and money-wise. You’ll be brilliant. You’ve got the experience, you've got the passion… Just don’t mention the spaghetti incident. Very funny. Seriously though, the fees are mad, aren’t they? I’m pretty much eating beans on toast for the rest of the year if I get in. It’s mad. Makes you think, doesn’t it? All this pressure to get qualified and then you're drowning in debt. Tells you a lot about modern society, eh. Anyway, Christmas is coming up.

Honestly, I'm just completely baffled by the whole situation with Mark and his ex. It's like she’s deliberately trying to wind him up. Is she? Or is she just… being an ex? I mean, exes do tend to do that, don't they? Especially when kids are involved. But this is beyond, isn't it? Last week she turned up at his son’s football match, unannounced, and started offering coaching tips. Coaching tips! To a six-year-old! Oh, wow. That’s pretty bold. Poor Mark. It must be so awkward. How’s Leo taking it? He’s trying to be all stoic, the classic dad reaction. "It’s fine, I’m fine,” but I can see it’s getting to him. He keeps saying he wants Leo to have a stable, supportive environment and this just... undermines it. Absolutely. It’s so important for the kids. But you know, it's tricky, isn't it? He’s trying to build a life with me, and I completely support him, but navigating these post-relationship dynamics is just exhausting. It is. And I hate feeling like I’m wading into something already so fraught. I don't want to criticize her, he’s Leo’s mum, but the behavior... it’s just disruptive, you know? I feel like I need a manual on how to handle this kind of thing. There isn't a manual! Honestly, just try and focus on Leo and Mark, creating the best possible space for them. You can't control what she does. I know, I know. It’s just frustrating. I feel a bit guilty even bringing it up, like I'm complaining about something trivial. People have bigger problems. Don't be ridiculous. It’s affecting him, and that’s important. And you’re a good friend, supporting him. What about therapy? Have you suggested that to him? He hasn't. He's always been a bit resistant to that sort of thing. Says he's "not the therapy type." Men and therapy… a classic battle. He’ll come around eventually. It might just help him figure out how to deal with her constructively. It's not about solving the problem; it's about him having the tools to manage it. Yeah, you're right. Maybe I'll gently suggest it again. I just want him to be happy. It’s hard seeing him stressed.

Honestly, have you seen ‘The Traitors’ final? I was absolutely fuming. Claudia wasn’t playing strategically at all – she was just reacting! It was awful. You're always so intense about these reality shows, aren't you? I thought she did alright. Bit predictable, maybe, but alright. Besides, I was too busy trying to figure out what everyone was pinning on Pinterest. Apparently, chunky knit blankets are still a thing? Who knew? Don’t remind me! My mum keeps sending me links to those things. Says they're “so cosy.” I’m more into minimalist vibes, you know? Sleek, modern… less grandma’s living room. Fair enough. Though those chunky blankets  are  kinda tempting, especially with this Cambridge damp. Speaking of tempting, you want another pint? My treat. Yeah, please! I deserve it after that ‘Traitors’ heartbreak. What are you having? Same again. You know I'm not one for straying from a good bitter. It's a comfort thing, I think. PhD research will do that to you. Tell me about it. Remember when you were obsessed with re-creating those elaborate cakes you saw on Pinterest? Ended up with a kitchen covered in fondant and a very sad looking Victoria Sponge. Don’t remind me! My supervisor nearly had a heart attack. Said I was prioritizing dessert-making over my dissertation. He wasn’t wrong. Well, you needed a break. Speaking of breaks, are we all still doing the birthday thing for Liam next month? I found this amazing little vintage shop in Norwich – they’ve got a load of old vinyl albums he’d love. Yeah, definitely. Liam’s getting old, we gotta celebrate him somehow. Vintage vinyl’s a good shout. Any chance you could pick me up something cheesy too? Like, genuinely awful 80s pop? Absolutely. I'll try and find something truly embarrassing. You and your questionable taste. Hey! I appreciate a good power ballad. Anyway, so, Pinterest aside… anyone heard from Sarah recently? She hasn’t posted anything on Instagram in ages. I messaged her last week. She's over in Amsterdam at some conference. Said she was drowning in academic jargon, but having a good time nonetheless. Good for her. Amsterdam’s fantastic. Maybe we should all plan a trip sometime. That would be brilliant. We could try and recreate those Scandinavian hygge interiors we saw on Pinterest... you know, minimalist, chunky blankets… maybe with a slightly less grandmotherly aesthetic.

Right, so this one's got good reviews, says it casts a lovely warm light. What do you think of this brass finish, though? A bit much? Hmm, brass is a bit…loud, isn't it? Especially with the wallpaper we've got. Let’s see if they’ve got a nickel option. Ah, there you go, nickel. Much better. Yeah, that’s more our vibe. Bit more understated. Are we going for a three-light or five-light fitting in the dining room, do you reckon? Five feels a bit grand, doesn't it? For the size of the room. Three will be plenty. And this nickel one definitely wins. Right, add that to the basket. Okay, let’s move onto the house hunting then. How’s Rightmove treating us? Not brilliantly, to be honest. Everything either needs a complete renovation or is ridiculously overpriced. Look at this one in Harpenden. Four bedrooms, decent garden… but the kitchen? It’s practically from the seventies. Oh dear. The avocado green. Classic. Let’s have a virtual tour, though. Just to see the layout. Okay, not bad. The living room is a nice size. And the garden  is  pretty. Yeah, the garden’s a selling point. Kids would love the space. But £750,000 for a house that needs a kitchen and bathroom doing? Seriously? Agreed. It's more like a project than a home. Right, next one. Oh, this one's in St Albans. A bit further out, but… wow. Look at the kitchen! Wow, that is stunning. Granite worktops, integrated appliances… but the photos are a little dark, aren't they? It's hard to see the rest of the house. Let’s have a closer look at the bedrooms. Okay, Master bedroom looks… small. Bit cramped. And the ensuite is tiny. But the other bedrooms are decent sizes. The garden's not massive, but it's manageable. And it’s listed at… £900,000! Nearly £150,000 more than the avocado-green disaster in Harpenden! I know! It's madness. But the kitchen is  beautiful . Maybe we could compromise? A smaller garden, smaller bedrooms, but a fantastic kitchen to start with? That's tempting. It would save us a huge amount of work in the long run. But is it worth the extra money? Maybe we need to broaden our search. Let's look at a few in Radlett then.

Honestly, I'm beyond exhausted. That shift was… something else. Tell me about it. What happened this time? Don't tell me Mrs. Peterson decided to redecorate with her bedpan again? No, thankfully. Though, that’s always a possibility. This time, it was young Liam. You know, the one with the dementia who thinks he’s a fireman? Oh yeah, the one who keeps trying to put out fires with the water jug? Exactly! He decided the Christmas decorations we put up early are a hazard and needed extinguishing. It took nearly an hour to convince him he wasn’t fighting a real blaze. Bless him. Dementia’s a cruel thing, isn't it? You ever think about doing a bit of extra training on that sort of thing, Sarah? I have, actually. There's a course on understanding dementia and behavioural issues coming up next month. It’s just… another cost, isn’t it? And the time… You should definitely do it though. Makes a real difference, knowing how to approach people. I’ve noticed it so much working with Mr. Davies, with his anxiety. Just talking to him about his favourite football team, you know? Calms him right down. You’re right, you’re right. It’s just… I'm thinking about applying for that senior nurse role at St. Michael's. But the training would help my application, wouldn’t it? It absolutely would. St. Michael's is a good shout. Better pay, less crazy patients, maybe? Hoping! Although, there are never any guarantees with patients, are there? How’s your mum doing, by the way, Lucy? Heard she was feeling a bit poorly last week. She’s much better now, thanks. Just a nasty bug, thankfully nothing serious. She's driving me mad though, constantly asking if I've applied for any other jobs. Mothers are like that, aren't they? Constant nagging about the jobs! Tell me about it! I’ve applied for a few, but nothing’s come through yet. I saw an advert for a live-in carer position, sounded alright, long hours though. Live-in? That’s intense. Are you ready for that? Honestly, I don't know. It's tempting, the money's good, but it would be lonely. Plus, Mitchell would miss me like crazy. It would. But you need to think about what’s right for  you , Lucy. Don’t compromise your happiness for a job.

This sourdough's pretty good, isn’t it? Didn’t realize you were such a rye fan. It's lovely. Found a little bakery in town, just popped in on the way over. They do a mean Chelsea bun too, if you're interested later. Tempting, very tempting. Though I've been reading about this new research on sleep, and apparently carbs before bed are a major no-no. Oh, really? What's it saying? I need all the sleep help I can get these days. Marking those essays takes it out of you. Apparently, it messes with your cortisol levels. Makes it harder to wind down. They’re suggesting protein and healthy fats, like avocado. Ridiculous, isn’t it? Denying yourself a decent bit of bread. Well, that’s just the kind of depressing thing scientists love to find out, isn't it? Always taking the joy out of things. Remember that camping trip we did in the Lake District? Oh god, yes. The one where we got hopelessly lost. Hopelessly is an understatement. We spent three hours wandering around in circles, arguing about which direction was North. You were convinced Google Maps had betrayed us. It was deliberately misleading me! It was a conspiracy! Trying to force us to embrace the wilderness. Honestly, I'd followed those instructions perfectly. Perfectly into a bog, perhaps. We ended up having to ask a farmer for directions, who looked at us like we were utterly mad. He was very polite, though. Offered us tea. He did. Strong, milky tea and some rock-hard biscuits. But bless him, he steered us straight back to the main road. It reminded me of that time I got lost in York. Oh, the York debacle. I swear, York is designed to mislead tourists. Every street looks exactly the same. Trying to find that little museum with the Roman mosaics? I could have walked around in circles for a week. And you insisted on navigating, despite me offering to use Waze. I'm perfectly capable of navigating! I just... overconfidently misinterpreted a map. That's putting it mildly. Speaking of navigation, saw a fascinating article about a pilot the other day – Captain Davies, apparently. Utterly brilliant. Landed his plane in a hurricane, apparently. A hurricane? Goodness. Apparently, the wind sheer was incredible. But he compensated, adjusted everything perfectly. They’re saying it was one of the most impressive maneuvers they’ve ever seen.

Honestly, Barnaby’s been eating me out of house and home. I swear he's gained weight. Barnaby, the hamster? Seriously? You’re having a crisis over a hamster gaining weight? It's not  just  a hamster, Chloe. He’s my fluffy little companion! And he's clearly got a thing for sunflower seeds. I've cut back, but he just stares at me with those big, beady eyes. It's guilt-tripping, I swear. Aye, they're clever little buggers, aren’t they? My gran had a hamster once, called Reginald. He used to hoard bedding in his cheeks like it was gold. Reginald! That’s brilliant. Mine, Pip, just sleeps all day. Total introvert. See, Barnaby's active! He's on his wheel, he's burrowing, he’s plotting ways to steal my grapes. Well, maybe he's just... maturing. Hamsters go through phases, right? Remember when I got that pet stick insect, Cecil? He molted like, six times in a month. A nightmare to keep track of. Cecil the stick insect? You’re making that up. I swear I'm not! He was tiny and green and utterly fascinating. Don’t judge me, I was ten. Right, stick insects. Moving on… Did anyone see that meme about gingers and sunshine the other day? Oh, here we go. No, seriously, it was hilarious. It was like, a ginger person trying to sneak into the shade under a single leaf. Aye, the internet’s obsession with gingers is just bizarre. Like, we’re people, aren’t we? It's just a bit of fun, Maisie. No need to get all serious. It's a bit insensitive, Chloe. Remember when people used to call me “Carrot Top”? Didn’t appreciate that. Sorry, Beth. It’s just… stereotypical. Although, I do think gingers are disproportionately good at sports. Noticed that. You've clearly been observing something, Hannah. Probably just a coincidence! Speaking of coincidences, did anyone see Sarah at the library the other day? She looked completely different. Really? How so? I don’t know, just... brighter. Different haircut. I almost didn’t recognize her. Maybe she's had a makeover! Going through a whole new vibe. Or maybe she finally decided to stop wearing those grey jumpers she lives in. Probably both. Anyway, back to Barnaby. I’m thinking of putting him on a diet of just lettuce and cucumber. Restrict the sunflower seeds.

Right, so I’m declaring Australia. Feels pretty safe, doesn’t it? And I’m reinforcing Indonesia. Anyone contesting that? Contesting? Mate, I’m laughing at you! Australia? You're gonna be swallowed whole. I'm going for North Africa, though. Solid base, reliable income. Honestly, you two are so predictable. I’m taking Asia. All of it. Massive points potential there. Asia? Really, Mum? You’re going for the high-risk, high-reward strategy? Are you sure? Don’t patronise me, darling. I know a thing or two about strategy. Besides, you’re a bit too comfortable in Australia, Ben. It’ll be easy pickings for someone. Speaking of easy pickings, did you see that documentary about Genghis Khan? Brutal, wasn’t he? Proper conqueror. Right, let’s try and stay on topic, yeah? It’s my turn to roll. I'm feeling lucky. Oh, come on! Two! That’s rubbish! Language, Benjamin! Your language is dreadful. And take your glasses off your nose, you’re going to break them again. Honestly, you’re like a child. He's got the energy of a child, bless him. All this thinking! Remember when we were young, eh, Barbara? We wouldn't have been bothering with Risk. We’d have been out... well, you know. Let’s not get into that. Honestly, John. And pass the chocolate, please. This board is making me peckish. Right, so I'm attacking Indonesia with three troops. What do you say, Mum? Fine, fine. Roll. But don’t expect a win. You’ll lose. Yes! Three! Take out all but one. Ha! Beginner's luck. Anyone remember that awful version of Risk they had a few years ago? The one with all the extra rules? Absolute mess. You mean the 'Global Domination' version? Ugh, don’t even mention it. My dad bought it – wasted money. We ended up just playing regular Risk. It's just like when Aaron had that video game obsession. Remember, he was convinced he needed a new update for it. Kept complaining it wasn't working properly. Of course, it was just him. Kids. Always needing the latest thing. Still, Aaron's got a good head on his shoulders. A steady lad, your Aaron. He is. Though, you know, I worry sometimes. About... well, about the future, I suppose. Having kids, responsibility…it’s all a bit daunting. Don't start, Benjamin.

Honestly, I’m having a full-blown crisis. A crisis? What now? Did you run out of oat milk again? Worse. Uni. Everything. I'm starting to think I made a monumental mistake coming here. Lancaster? Seriously? It's pretty good, isn't it? And you love marine biology! I  did  love marine biology. But lectures are… intense. And everyone else seems to  know  things. Like, they’ve already mastered obscure Latin names for tiny little sea creatures, and I’m still struggling to remember phytoplankton from zooplankton. Right, classic imposter syndrome. Happens to the best of us. Remember when I thought everyone at Fresher's knew the lyrics to every Arctic Monkeys song? Turns out, I was the only one belting out "I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor" at 3 AM. Okay, that was pretty mortifying. But this feels bigger than a questionable dance move. What about your course then? All this talk of astrophysics... are you absolutely sure that’s what you want? Honestly? I'm having my doubts too. My mum keeps saying I should do something "stable," like teaching. You know, a proper job. My dad wants me to be a marine park trainer. He reckons I should be swimming with dolphins and everything. It sounds idyllic, but like, the reality is probably cleaning dolphin poop, isn't it? Yeah, probably less Jacques Cousteau, more... bucket duty. What about that internship you applied for at the Cornish Marine Conservation project? Isn’t that a better route? It is! But what if I’m not good enough? What if I mess it all up? Stop it. You're brilliant. You practically breathe saltwater and know every shipwreck in Cornwall. You'll be amazing. Besides, even if you screw up, so what? Everyone does at some point. Easy for you to say, you've got a genius IQ and can apparently recite the entire periodic table. Exaggerating slightly! But seriously, don’t let the worry consume you. We're both young, we've got time to figure things out. Actually, speaking of the future... Have you seen pictures of that actor, Tom Hopper’s, baby? He looks adorable! Oh my god, yes! Is it a boy or a girl? Boy! Apparently, they've named him Dominic. How cute is that? Maybe we'll have little babies running around and trying to understand marine biology and astrophysics one day.

So, the project’s properly mental, innit? Like, doing a presentation on global poverty? What are we even meant to  do  with that? Tell people to give money, I guess? It’s obvious. Miss Patel’s probably looking for a nuanced answer, though. Something about cyclical poverty and systemic issues, yeah? Cyclical…what? Sounds massively boring. I was thinking about showing a clip from that documentary about the slums in Mumbai. Ms. Davies said that's a good idea. Yeah, but then it’s just depressing. Everyone’ll switch off after five minutes. We need something that shows… hope, maybe? Like, initiatives that are actually working. Easier said than done. Everything feels so… overwhelming, doesn't it? Like, how can one person even make a difference? Especially when you see what Bezos is pulling in. Don't even get me started. He’s literally sending himself into space while families are choosing between heating and eating. It’s ridiculous. It’s mad greed, isn’t it? Like, hoarding all the wealth while everyone else struggles. Reminds me of Lex Luthor, honestly. Always plotting to control everything. Speaking of comics, did you see the new Superman issue? Nah, I've been stuck on X-Men. They’re doing the ‘mutant nation’ thing again, which is predictable, but still good. Makes you think, though, doesn’t it? About what it would be like to be an outsider. Yeah, in a weird way, it does. It's like... some people are just born with a bigger stack of cards, you know? And others are stuck with nothing. Exactly! It’s not fair, is it? It’s not about individual effort. Like, my cousin, he works proper hard at the warehouse, right? Still can’t afford a proper holiday. My dad says it’s all down to personal responsibility. Pull yourself up by your bootstraps and all that. But what if you don’t  have  any boots? Classic dad logic. He'll be moaning about politicians later, though, won't he? Saying no one’s doing anything about it. Yeah, he's been on one about Starmer. Says he’s as bad as Sunak. Honestly, politics’ just a mess, isn't it? Don't even know who to vote for anymore. It's confusing. Remember Mr. Hawthorne trying to explain Brexit? My head was spinning for a week. Yeah, it was like a puzzle with a million pieces and half of them were missing.

Honestly, darling, the recording was absolute chaos. I thought I’d be all calm and collected, you know, delivering my little historical insights… but the cat decided to yowl during the most crucial part, and then the washing machine started up. Oh, Mum! That sounds disastrous. Did they use it? They managed, bless their hearts. They did a bit of editing, patched it together. It’s not perfect, but it’s out there. It's meant to be a podcast on Tudor embroidery, can you believe it. Tudor embroidery? That’s… specific. But I’m sure it's fascinating! How are your joints holding up after all that? I can only imagine sitting upright for hours. Not great, I have to admit. The physio's been helpful, but oh, these knees! They’re protesting something fierce. I keep telling myself it's worth it, but some days… I know what you mean. I've been thinking about trying some Pilates or something, just to loosen up a bit. Do you think it would help? Pilates is wonderful for strengthening the core, and that does help with the joints. Just take it slowly, darling. Don't overdo it. You need to listen to your body. Speaking of bodies... have you put on any weight? A bit, I think. It’s just been… hard to motivate myself to do anything. Eating’s become a bit of a comfort thing, you know? I understand, sweetheart. It's easy to slip into those patterns. I've been experimenting with that new low-carb diet. It’s mostly fine, but I miss a decent slice of cake terribly. The neighbour has been baking loads. It’s torture! Mrs. Henderson, always showing off. Mrs. Henderson! She's always been a bit like that, hasn’t she? Reminds me of that dreadful Miss Gable from school. Exactly! And she keeps offering me slices of Victoria sponge. Says she made it especially for me. Temptation! Absolutely vile Victoria sponge though, far too much jam. You’re cracking me up. What are you going to do? Raid her flowerbeds out of spite? Oh, I wish! Though she's got such beautiful roses, it’d be a shame. I might just have to distract myself with a vigorous session of Tudor embroidery. That occupies the brain, at least. So, you’ve been busy then. Anything else been happening? Anyone interesting? Don’t even start, darling.

Right, I think that's the pasta cooked. You reckon it needs a bit longer, Liv? Nah, looks perfect to me. Just give it a stir, make sure nothing’s sticking. Smells lovely, honestly. What did you put in the sauce? It's got a really good aroma. Just a bit of everything, really. Some roasted peppers, mushrooms, garlic...My nan’s recipe, basically. She always said the trick was good quality tinned tomatoes and a generous glug of red wine. Sounds amazing. My cooking skills peak at boiling an egg, to be honest. I'm lucky you brought this feast. Don't be daft. It's a simple pasta dish. You could totally make it. It's just chopping veg and simmering. Easier said than done when I'm trying to juggle a million things at work. This production line is driving me round the bend, honestly. Constant deadlines, changing specifications… it’s relentless. Tell me about it. My conference next month is giving me nightmares. The keynote speaker pulled out last week, and finding a replacement who fits the budget  and  isn't completely boring is proving impossible. Oh no! That’s awful. Have you looked at any TED Talks speakers? Some of them are brilliant. I have. Found a few interesting ones, but their fees are astronomical. I’m on a tight budget, remember. It’s all champagne tastes on a beer budget. Right, yeah. Well, at least we've got good food to take our minds off it. Pass me some of that garlic bread, will you? Coming right up. So, what are we watching tonight? I was thinking that new rom-com everyone's talking about. Oh, is it any good? I’ve seen mixed reviews. Apparently, it’s cheesy as anything, but in a really comforting way. Like a big hug in a film. I like the sound of that. After the week I’ve had, I need a big hug. Although… I did catch a glimpse of that new documentary about deep-sea creatures. It looked pretty mind-blowing. Deep-sea creatures? You'd pick those over a rom-com? You're something else, Liv. Hey, I appreciate a bit of natural wonder. Plus, think of all the weird and amazing things they've probably never even documented. It's fascinating. Alright, alright, you’ve convinced me. Deep-sea creatures it is. Although, if it gets too scary, we’re switching to the rom-com, yeah?

Okay, so seriously, has anyone actually seen "Dune: Part Two"? Like, properly seen it? Yeah! I went on Saturday. It was incredible! The visuals were just… wow. Aye, I saw it last week. It was brilliant, wasn't it? Bit long, though. Long? I kept dozing off. You dozed off? Seriously, Elsie? It’s "Dune"! I was tired. History essay due Monday. Fair enough. But it was a good bit of dosing, right? At least you weren’t missing anything  important . That's what I’m worried about! I’m tempted to go, but I don't know if I have the attention span for a three-hour sci-fi epic. Honestly, it flies by. Once you get into the rhythm, it’s just… immersive. The sound design alone is worth the price of admission. It is, yeah. The sound definitely adds to the epic feel. Did anyone catch the bit with the sandworms breaking through the surface? Proper gave me goosebumps. Oh, that was class! And Zendaya looked amazing. Can we talk about something else now? Like, is anyone else starving? Elsie's always starving. It’s a superpower. So, ignoring Elsie’s perpetual hunger… what was your favourite part? Apart from Zendaya looking amazing, Chloe. Hmm, tough one. I loved Paul’s transformation, the way Timothée Chalamet portrays it. The weight of his responsibility... I loved the battle scenes! So well choreographed. And the costumes were stunning. Every single detail. I thought the ending was pretty powerful, setting up for the next one. Bit bleak, though. Bleak is definitely a word for it. I keep hearing people saying the books are even darker. They are. Much denser, too. Lots of political maneuvering and spice-induced visions. Spice? Like, cinnamon? No, Elsie! Not cinnamon. It’s a fictional drug in the film. It’s what gives the Fremen their abilities! It’s basically the fuel of the universe. Very important for space travel. Aye, crucial for everything. It keeps the whole thing ticking over. Okay, okay, I get it. So, is it worth the three hours, then? Do I brave the cinema? Absolutely! Seriously, you won't regret it. Go for it, you’ll love it. And then we can all discuss every single detail afterwards. Just make sure Elsie’s had a proper dinner beforehand, so she doesn’t faint during the sandworm scenes. I'm getting a snack now.

Oh my god, I need a cup of tea. Paris was… a lot. Welcome back, darling! You look exhausted. Everything alright? And what are those, they smell divine. Paris, eh? Instagram’s gonna be exploding with your photos. Did you manage to see the Mona Lisa without being trampled? Trampled is a good word. Honestly, the crowds were insane. And my ankle… oh, my ankle. Your ankle? What happened? You didn’t tell me you had a dodgy ankle! I didn’t notice until halfway through Saturday. I think someone bumped into me rushing to see the Eiffel Tower, and I just… twisted it. It’s fine, mostly. Just throbbing a bit. Did you go to a pharmacy? Got something for the swelling? Nah, I just hobbled around like a wounded duck for the rest of the trip. Parisian charm fades quickly when you’re limping. The pastries were the only saving grace. Seriously, these are incredible. What are you cooking, Mum? It’s just a lentil soup. Thought you’d be hungry after all that walking, even if it was slightly painful walking! How was the hotel? Fancy? Pretty swanky, actually. Right near the Louvre. But the shower was the size of a shoebox. Seriously. You could barely turn around. Classic Paris! Tiny showers, huge pastries. It's the law. Exactly! And also, Sarah bailed on us last minute. What? Sarah? Why? She said her cat went into labour. Apparently, it's a very dramatic feline. Oh, Sarah. Always an excuse. I know! Left us hanging! We ended up having to navigate the metro with a dodgy map and my dodgy ankle. It was chaotic. I nearly missed my flight. Oh, darling, that sounds dreadful. I’m glad you’re back safe and sound. Though I do feel bad about Sarah. Cats are family, you know. I get it! But seriously, I was so stressed. And the French waiters, they're just… something else. Eye rolls and sighs everywhere. You’re exaggerating! I went to Paris last year, the waiters were perfectly charming. You always say that! You're a natural diplomat, Chloe. I don’t have your patience. One guy practically threw my croissant at me. You’re just being dramatic. Now, sit down, have some soup, and tell me everything. Did you get any good pictures? And did you buy any perfume? Okay, okay. Soup sounds amazing right now.

Hey Chloe! Fancy seeing you here before the linguistics seminar. Didn’t realize you were heading this way. Hey Ben!
