Yeah, just grabbing a coffee before - you know, the usual pre-seminar caffeine injection. How's it going? Still buried under a mountain of BNC data? You have no idea. I'm trying to trace the evolution of passive voice usage in journalistic articles from the 80s. It’s fascinating, actually, but also…a lot. What are you working on this week? Ugh, mostly dealing with the fallout of last weekend’s sales in the store. It’s a supervisor’s life, isn’t it? But hey, payday's on Friday, so that’s something to look forward to. Thinking of treating myself to tickets for Hamilton - have you seen it? No, not yet! I keep meaning to. My sister went last year and raved about it. I’m more of a theatre kind of guy, myself – proper Shakespeare, you know. Remember that production of  A Midsummer Night’s Dream  we saw at the Fringe last summer? Oh gosh, yes! That was brilliant. So different from anything we'd seen before. Speaking of different, I was trying to help my little brother with his TEFL assignment. He’s practically fluent in Malaysian dialect now. It’s incredible. Seriously? That’s amazing. My last undergrad degree was actually in creative writing, remember? I’ve been trying to get back into novel writing but finding the time is tricky. Got a plot idea, just need to wrestle it into shape. What about you, still working on that short story collection? I did for a while, but I ended up shelving it. The characters started arguing with me. It’s terrifying! How’s your referencing going for the thesis? You were looking a little stressed last week. Still a nightmare. I’ve got a mountain of MLA and APA to sort. I'm considering just handing in the paper saying "Here's the research, figure it out yourselves." It’s all consuming with thesis writing and tuition fees and student loans. I’m thinking about a holiday next year - Greece, maybe? Oh, Greece sounds amazing! My sister's getting married there next summer. Massive wedding. Thinking about getting my hair done before, long overdue! Speaking of family, you still seeing Liam? How’s the whole…situation going? It’s…complicated. We haven't been seeing each other, not really.

Right, so first things first, you’ve got to rinse the rice. Really well. Like, until the water runs clear almost. See? Like that. Why? Because otherwise it’ll be all starchy and gluggy, right? No one wants gluggy rice. It needs to be fluffy. Like…like clouds, almost. Clouds aren’t exactly fluffy, are they? They're just…big. Okay, fair point. Like…puffy pillows, then. Puffy pillows of rice. There you go. Now, into the pan. How much water do I need? Right, now this is important. For a cup of rice… twice the amount of water. So two cups. Roughly. Watch me. See? You don’t need to be exact, honestly. Two cups. Right. Okay, pop it on a medium heat. Don’t crank it up high, or it’ll just boil over and make a mess. And then… don't touch it. Leave it. Leave it? For how long? About 18-20 minutes. Keep an eye on it though. You’ll see little bubbles starting, and then it’ll quieten down. When it’s quiet, it's probably done. But, you can lift the lid and poke it with a fork just to be sure. And then what? Then, turn the heat off. And crucially… don’t stir it! Just leave it covered for another five minutes. It needs to steam. That's what makes it fluffy. So, just rinsing, water, heat, wait, don’t stir. Got it. Exactly! Now, while that’s doing its thing, let's get the curry going. We can use those vouchers we got, right? Yeah, for that Indian place. But I don’t really like anything too spicy. Okay, okay. We’ll get something mild, then. I'm thinking…butter chicken? It’s always a winner. And loads of naan bread to soak up the sauce. Sounds good! Now look, remember what happened last week with the meat? Don’t leave it out on the counter for ages, okay? It’s best to cook it straight away or put it in the fridge. Honestly, you can smell when it’s going off. Yeah, it smelled a bit funny. Exactly! And remember when we were talking about those documentaries about food? All that salt and fat… It’s scary, isn’t it? Are jalapenos bad for you? Well, they’re spicy, right? So, they're good for giving you a bit of a kick.

This’ll be another week of beans on toast, then. Don’t be like that, Liam. Mum’s put in a right effort. And it's better than nothing. Aye, I know, I know. Just... feeling a bit down, that's all. Another rejection letter today. "Highly competitive field…" blaa blaa blaa. Don't let it get to you, Liam. You’ve got a degree, you’re smart. Something’ll turn up. Did you apply for that assistant role down at the library again? Aye, did. Didn't even get an interview. They said they've gone with someone who has "relevant experience." What relevant experience does a philosophy degree give you, eh? Thinking about stuff? Proper deep thoughts, Liam. Exactly! Deep, useless thoughts, that's what. It's just, you’re so focused on work. What about that coding course you were looking at? Nah, can't afford it. Not even with Mum's help. Every penny's going on bills, isn't it? True. Mum’s struggling too, isn’t she? I'm worried about her, actually. The care home bills... Don’t go there, Sarah. Let’s just enjoy dinner. Speaking of which, it's actually really good, Mum! Thanks. Even the peas. See? Someone appreciates it. What did you get up to at college today, Elodie? Anything interesting? Miss Thompson grilled us on Romantic poetry again. Honestly, I'm half convinced she just likes hearing herself talk. You should’ve told her! I wanted to, but… you know. Teachers. Remember Mrs. Grimshaw back in school? The geography one? She used to fall asleep during her own lessons. Oh my god, yes! I totally forgot about that. She'd be snoring away, and we’d be passing notes. Bless her. It was a tough time for her, wasn't it? She lost her husband around then. Aye, poor woman. School was never the same. Did you see that new series on Netflix, “The Ridge?” Oh, yeah! I'm hooked! The acting’s brilliant, and the scenery is gorgeous. I started it, but it's a bit intense for me, to be honest. Too many dodgy characters. My friend, Chloe, said it's the new "Line of Duty!" "Line of Duty" was brilliant though. Proper gripping. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Just like my philosophy degree… . Don't start again, Liam! How’s Carl doing? Did you hear back from him about that gig?

This shepherd's pie is really good, by the way. Proper comfort food. Aye, it is reet good, isn't it? Glad you like it. Mum always made the best. Could eat this every night, honestly. Proper hearty. So, you said you were dealing with a bit of a nightmare at work? With the conference? Oh, you have no idea. It's the caterers. Absolutely useless. They promised me Yorkshire puddings for the Yorkshire-themed evening and they’ve sent over… mini quiches. Mini quiches! Yorkshire puddings and mini quiches are not a match made in heaven, are they? Exactly! It’s supposed to be a celebration of Yorkshire. It’s like serving Haggis at a Burns Night supper! You know? Absolutely. That’s a massive faux pas. What are you going to do now? I’m trying to sort it. I’ve called them, had a right barney with them. They’re trying to say it’s “supply chain issues.” Supply chain issues for Yorkshire puddings? Seriously? They’re having a laugh, aren’t they? Do you have any other caterers you could quickly get in? That’s what I’m looking at. Problem is, the conference is tomorrow. Everything’s booked, everyone’s arriving. Changing things last minute is a nightmare. Business life. Never dull, eh? No, it's definitely not. Although sometimes I wish it was. I’m thinking of having a real proper proper go at that yoga studio. The one down the road. Oh, really? The one you mentioned a few weeks ago? You should! Get some of that stress out. I know, I know. I’ve been putting it off. Just feel like I don't have the time, but then I realise I do. I just make excuses. We all do. I spent most of my time last week trying to teach myself to juggle. You? Juggling? Yeah! I thought it’d be a good way to pass the time. Let's just say I'm sticking to watching telly for now. Dropped one on my foot. Oh, you poor thing! See, that is a good reason to avoid juggling though. Maybe yoga's less likely to cause injury. Definitely less likely. You need to move your body a bit though, don't you? Sitting at a desk all day… I know, I know. It's just been the last few weeks have been manic.

Right, so, dishes. Who’s on it? I'll do it. No, let me do it, mate. You two clear the table, yeah? Fine. Thanks, love. So, what did you two get up to today? Anything exciting? Played tennis. Did you? Good for you! How was it? It was alright. Jamie was showing off again. He’s got a good serve, haven't you? Yeah, but he’s got no control. Flapping all over the place. Not as good as me, though. Oh, shut up. Oh, leave him be. It sounds like you both had a good time. You know, I was reading something interesting online today... about Hitler. Here we go. No, honestly! It was about how his moustache was initially a political statement, and then just… stayed. Can you imagine having that much facial hair just because? It looks daft. My mate Ben’s grown a beard. He looks like a Viking. Does he now? Instagram’s full of beards these days, isn't it? It is. Though I don’t understand why anyone would want to look like a lumberjack. Liam’s posting loads of pictures of his girlfriend. Is he? Good for him. About time, I thought. She seems lovely. Does she like tennis as well? Nah, she’s into… dance or something. TikTok stuff. Don’t be mean. I’m not being mean! It’s just… different. Well, everyone’s different. As long as he’s happy. Speaking of TikTok, are you two still glued to your phones? It’s not glued! We only look at it for like, five minutes. Five minutes turns into an hour, you know. You need to do other things. Read a book, play tennis… Or clear the dishes! Honestly, Dad, you’re such a nag. Someone's got to be. Just remember, the real world isn't on Instagram. There's a whole load of other stuff. Exactly. And remember, if anyone’s being unkind online, you tell us, okay? You don't have to deal with it yourself. Yeah, okay, Mom. Yeah, alright. Can we watch something now though? Anything? Sure, let's see. What would you like to watch? Don't put on something stupid, please. No promises. I wanna watch that new action movie. We’ll see. Let’s finish clearing up first. Then we can sort out a film. Okay? Speaker_2 and Okay. You two getting started on those dishes then?

Right, so we need to sort out the sofa before Christmas definitely. I’m thinking maybe DFS? They’ve got those two-for-one deals on again. Yeah, that's probably the best bet. Mum's been saying she wants a new one for ages, hasn't she, Nan? She has, love, she has. That old one’s seen better days. Though I’ll miss the dents, mind. Me and your Grandad used to sit on it for hours, watching the telly. Everything's got a story behind it, hasn’t it? Speaking of stories, did you hear about anon's friend, Sarah? Her whole family's been poorly. No! What's happened? Flu, apparently. The whole lot. Mum, dad, even the little ones. Poor Sarah’s run off her feet. Oh dear. That's awful. You know, it reminds me of when your Uncle Barry got that awful bug. Remember, love? He was laid up for weeks. I was little then, Nan. Vaguely. Yeah, it was a bad ‘un. Anyway, we need to think about getting rid of that old armchair. It's taking up far too much space. We could take it to the tip. Can we? I thought they charged for big stuff now. They do, but it’s cheaper than renting a skip. And we should probably clear out some of those unwanted presents while we're at it, don't you think? All that Christmas tat. Don't you dare throw away that ceramic robin! Your Grandad bought that for me! Mum, you haven’t looked at that robin in fifteen years! It’s been gathering dust in the attic. Speaking of family, what’s happening with Emily? Has she found a place yet? Not really. She’s still looking. It's so difficult to find anything decent at a reasonable price. Especially with all that new building going on. All these new houses... They could do with some green spaces. It’s just concrete everywhere. Honestly, I hate when people wash your clothes. Like, who does that?! Tell me about it! It’s just… weird. Why would you need to clean someone else's socks? Your great-aunt Mabel used to do that. She had a swear box, though. If you said a bad word, she'd make you put a penny in it. Wow! It’s just… what did she do with all the money?

Right, so I was thinking, Friday night, we could definitely do that new Italian place, you know, the one near the theatre? Oh, yes! I've heard good things. But darling, you look absolutely shattered. Are you okay? Seriously, you're paler than usual. Just a bit stressed with work, Mum. It’s… a lot right now. Apparently, they're looking at redundancies in my department. Which is ridiculous. Oh, love, no! That’s awful. Who would be silly enough to let you go? You’re brilliant at what you do. Honestly, companies are mad. Are they really considering it? It’s just talk at the moment, but they’ve had a meeting. They're 'restructuring' apparently, which is never a good sign. It’s making me a nervous wreck, honestly. Well, don't you worry. You’re talented, you’re resourceful, and you’ve always been resilient. You’ll land on your feet, you always do. Anyway, let's not dwell on that. What about this weekend? Grandad’s doing okay, isn’t he? Yeah, he's a bit better. Still a bit grumpy about the cricket, naturally. He moaned for a good hour about the bowling. Of course he did! Honestly, he’s addicted to that sport. Did you see he’s been trying to eat healthier? Apparently, he's swapped biscuits for apples! Can you believe it? An apple? Seriously? That’s barely a change. I’m trying to get to the gym more, actually. Sarah’s been dragging me along, and it’s actually… kind of good. Good for you, darling. You need to look after yourself. All that work, you’re burning the candle at both ends. Remember what the doctor said about your blood pressure. I know, I know. I’m just so busy. Speaking of which, did you ever get around to looking at those plans for the extension? I did! I had a chat with Mr. Davies last week. He's got some fantastic ideas, really maximizing the space. Though, the quote… well, it's rather hefty. Yeah, I figured. Still, it’ll be so worth it in the end, won't it? More room for everyone to visit. Absolutely. Although, I'm not sure I need a bigger kitchen. My cooking tends to involve a lot of burnt offerings already! Mum! You’re a wonderful cook! ...Most of the time. Have you been to that charity shop in Cambridge yet?

So, what are we doing tomorrow then? Like, actually doing? Not just… sitting. Right, well, Finn here has decided my legs are the most exciting thing in the world. Just a minute… okay. Tomorrow. Well, we could go swimming. Swimming’s good. But it’s gonna be packed, isn’t it? Like, every kid and their mum. It probably will be. Or… we could try and get some of those jobs done around the house I keep moaning about. Seriously? Like dusting and… stuff? Okay, okay, bad idea. Sorry. Perhaps we could go see if Liam and Chloe are about? They’re probably bored too. Yeah, that'd be good. They said they were thinking about building a den in Liam’s garden. A den sounds fun. Should we pack some snacks? Finn will need constant refuelling. Definitely. And maybe a ball or something? To throw about? Yes, and I saw a new episode of Mick on telly today. About the ducks. He was trying to teach them Japanese! Japanese ducks? What? I know, it's ridiculous! Stick with Mick is getting weirder every week. I can’t understand half of what he says anyway. It’s all so fast. I always miss bits. Exactly. It’s very… frenetic. Right, are we building a den, playing with a ball, and potentially encountering Japanese waterfowl? Sounds… a plan. Although, I need to practice my guitar a bit before anyone hears me. Oh, good point. You've been neglecting it. We could do that in the afternoon, if the den-building doesn't take all day. Yeah, I want to learn that song everyone’s playing, you know, the one with the… the strumming bit? The one that sounds like… seagulls? Yeah! That’s it. Okay, seagulls and den-building and maybe a little Japanese duck action. Sounds like a surprisingly full day for a summer holiday. It does, actually. You thinking of letting me get away with a day of  just  gaming? Don’t push it! Now, help me coax this little man away from my trousers, will you? He thinks they’re a climbing frame. He’s gonna pull my jeans! Quick! Right, operation den-building planning commences! First, snacks. Always snacks. Right! I’ll go find the crisps. Thanks. And watch out for Finn – he’s on a shoelace-eating mission. Noted. Shoelace patrol initiated. This is going to be a long summer holiday.

Right, this scene’s mental, isn't it? Proper Tarantino. Yeah, it's good. But I'm struggling to concentrate, honestly. My gums are throbbing. Your gums? What’s up? Dentist appointment disaster? You’ve no idea. Just got back. Had to get a filling. Absolute nightmare. The dentist kept going on about my teeth being “a right state.” Charming, innit? Sounds like a classic. At least you got it sorted though. Did he at least offer you a Werther's Original? Standard dentist procedure, surely. No Werther's! Just a lecture on flossing. Like I don’t know I should be flossing! I was thinking of just storming out and leaving my chart, you know? You would! You’d be shouting “I’m a Scouser, not a dental hygiene enthusiast!” Exactly! Though my accent probably confused him even more. He kept nodding slowly like he was trying to decipher a foreign language. He probably thought you were speaking Martian. Listen, you need some comfort food after that ordeal. Fancy ordering some chips? Gravy, mushy peas, the works? Now you’re talking. Proper comfort. What about that cinema trip we talked about? Wanted to see that new Wes Anderson film. Yeah, definitely. Maybe Saturday? I was thinking of heading to that gig at The Kazimier too. The band, The Cosmic Prawns, are playing. Heard they’re decent. Cosmic Prawns? Seriously? What kind of name is that? Don't knock it 'til you've heard 'em! Apparently, they're proper quirky. Anyway, holiday plans still on for Spain then? Trying to book flights soon? Trying to! Every time I look, the prices keep going up. It’s ridiculous. Maybe we should just escape Liverpool for a few days somewhere closer. Cornwall maybe? Cornwall would be cracking. Could cycle around, borrow some of those Citibikes. You know, get some fresh air. Proper breeze, yeah. Though I’d probably end up falling in the sea. I'm not exactly known for my graceful cycling. You’d be a sight to behold! Speaking of sights... I've started a new short story. It's about a man who communicates with pigeons. Pigeons?  Communicates ? You’re losing it, mate. I know, it’s a bit bonkers. But I’m trying to explore the idea of finding connection in unexpected places. Plus, there's a detective involved. Right. A pigeon-whispering detective. Now  that's  something I'd read.

So, tell me everything! How’s the new job going, love? Really going? It’s… a lot, Mum. Honestly. But good! The kids are lovely, really lovely. A bit boisterous, but you can't complain, can you? No, not at all. Little bundles of energy. Are you settling in okay with the staff? That can make or break it, can’t it? They’re alright. A bit of a mixed bag, to be honest. One or two who seem a bit… resistant to new ideas, but the Headteacher’s brilliant. Really supportive. That’s brilliant news, darling. And are you getting used to the, you know… the classroom management? The whole thing? It’s the behaviour that's the biggest challenge, I think. You read all the theory at uni, but actually dealing with a class of six-year-olds who  think  it’s hilarious to throw glitter everywhere? That's a different ball game. Oh, I can imagine! Glitter is the devil’s work, isn’t it? Well, at least you’re having a laugh, eh? Speaking of things that are a bit chaotic, have you seen the state of my Easter cakes? Absolute disasters. No way, let me see! Are they going to be edible, at least? That's the million-pound question! I tried a new recipe, thought I’d be all fancy. Clearly, I’m not fancy baker material. Little Leo was trying to ‘help’ too. It was carnage. Oh, he’s a handful, isn’t he? Still, a little chaos is good for the soul. So, about the Christening… Are we thinking next month? That’s what I was hoping we could firm up. I've spoken to your Auntie Carol, she confirmed she and Uncle David can make it. What about you and James? We’re definitely in. James is really keen. We’re just trying to work out if we can manage bringing Olivia. It’s a long day out for her, and she's been a bit fussy lately. Don't worry about that too much. We have the garden, she can run about. And I’ll keep her entertained. It’ll be lovely to have everyone together, won't it? It will. I’m really looking forward to it. I've already started thinking about decorations and food. Should we do a buffet or a sit-down meal? Buffet's always easier, isn’t it?

It’s so lovely to finally see you, Sarah! It feels like ages. This house is gorgeous by the way, really cosy. Oh, darling, it's wonderful to see you too, Chloe! Yes, I'm quite pleased with it, it's a bit bigger than my flat in London, you know, needed a bit more space. Come in, come in. Tea? Coffee? Tea would be lovely, thank you. So, what have you been up to? Last time we spoke, you were just starting to settle in, weren't you? Oh, it’s been a whirlwind! The move itself was chaos, naturally. And adapting to Birmingham… it’s very different from London, isn't it? Friendlier, I think, though the accent takes some getting used to still. I can imagine! I occasionally venture up to see my sister in Manchester, and that's a whole other world. So, how’s the teaching going? Still thriving at the grammar school? It’s… challenging. The kids are lovely, really, but the workload! Honestly, Chloe, it’s relentless. Ofsted's breathing down your neck constantly. They’re really pushing for this new curriculum too, which is just… a lot. What about you? Still loving the French and Spanish? Absolutely! They’re a joy to teach, the students are really engaged. Though, I’m considering looking for something new, maybe a bit less… intensive. I've been looking into some online tutoring, flexible hours and all that. That sounds tempting, doesn't it? Less pressure. You know, my niece, Emily, she's doing really well. Got into Cambridge, can you believe it? Oh, wow, that’s brilliant! So proud of her. What's she studying? Biochemistry. Absolutely fascinated by it, she always was a clever girl. Brings a whole new meaning to Christmas dinner, doesn't it? Explaining all the molecular structures! I can imagine! Though, honestly, my family’s Christmas dinner conversations usually revolve around whether Auntie Brenda remembered to buy the cranberry sauce  again . Oh, Brenda! Some things never change. Speaking of families, how are your parents? Still battling the garden? They are! Mum’s convinced she’s going to win the Village Flower Competition this year. She’s become obsessed with hydrangeas. It's pretty ridiculous actually. Dad keeps trying to build her some ridiculous contraption to water them automatically. Sounds like them! You know, I've been thinking a bit about starting a little side business, actually.

This is incredible, honestly. Yours is always the best. Seriously, your great-grandmother's recipe? Yeah, it is. Though I've tweaked it a bit over the years, obviously. More walnuts this year, I think. More cinnamon. You need that warmth, you know, for Passover. It  is  exceptional, darling. The consistency is perfect. Not too gluey, not too crumbly. It’s got that… je ne sais quoi. "Je ne sais quoi" at a Passover Seder. Classic Mum. Well, it has! It's the balance. And the apples… Granny Smiths, naturally. Granny Smiths are key. You know, Liam was asking me the other day about the whole Seder plate thing. All the symbolic food. Oh really? What did you tell him? Well, I tried to explain the matzah, you know, the unleavened bread, representing the haste of the Exodus… …and the burning desire to get away from Pharaoh’s awful bread! Oh, Adam, you and your jokes. But it’s true, the matzah does symbolize the lack of time. And the maror – the horseradish – represents the bitterness of slavery. It  is  quite bitter, isn’t it? I always think someone should invent a slightly less intense version. It's a bit much for some people. Maybe a balsamic reduction? Sweeten it a bit? Absolutely not! That would be sacrilege! It has to be properly bitter. It’s part of the experience. Speaking of experiences, I’m thinking of finally doing that Jewish food tour of Italy next year. Italy? Seriously? Which part? Rome, mainly. There’s a surprisingly rich Jewish history there. And of course, the food! I’ve heard the fried artichokes are divine. Oh my gosh, yes! And the carciofi alla giudia… you have to try them. We talked about going with you! I'm definitely in for that! We need to start planning. Maybe spring of '25? Before everyone's dates get too crazy. Sounds amazing. Actually, I was looking at flights to New York the other day… thinking about finally visiting that Katz's Delicatessen. Katz's! Of course! You must go. Do you know the story of how they came up with the name? No, tell me! It’s quite a tale... involved a particularly grumpy customer and a very unfortunate incident with a potato… Mum, maybe later? We're getting to the Afikoman hunt, and Liam’s already eyeing up the chocolates. Yeah, we don’t want to keep him waiting!

Right, so, who's ready to absolutely demolish "The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo"? I'm still reeling from it. Oh, honestly, Sarah, I’m still having trouble processing. It was just…a lot, wasn't it? Proper page-turner though, couldn’t put it down, even when I should have been prepping for tomorrow's budget meeting. Totally agree! I was up way too late last night. I think I finished it around 2 am. I kept thinking, "Just one more chapter…" and then bam, Evelyn’s whole life unfolded. Did anyone else find the ending completely devastating? Devastating is putting it mildly! And the whole unreliable narrator thing! Clever, clever writing. I’m gutted it's finished, though. What shall we read next? Ooh, I was thinking something lighter after that emotional rollercoaster. Something cosy. Perhaps a Dorothy Sayers? Dorothy Sayers? Bit heavy for me after that, I think. Maybe something by Kate Morton? I loved "The Forgotten Garden." Atmospheric and a bit spooky. Kate Morton is always a good shout. Though, I'm feeling a bit…knitting-inspired this month. Has anyone read any books  about  knitting? Seems silly, I know. I’ve just finished a giant chunky cardigan - pure catharsis after that book! Knitting, eh? You know, my grandmother used to knit these incredible Argyle jumpers. She even had patterns for little matching ones for us grandkids. Such a shame those skills are disappearing. I tried to learn once, but I'm absolutely hopeless. I ended up with a tangled mess and a very frustrated cat. My mum's a crochet whiz. She makes the most amazing blankets and throws. I’m trying to pick it up but I'm hopeless at keeping the tension right. Always ending up with wonky edges. Wonky edges have character! Honestly, embrace the imperfections. It’s part of the charm. Speaking of charm, have you all seen "Succession"? Oh, "Succession"! Absolutely brilliant. The writing, the acting... It's just so deliciously cynical. Although, I do occasionally shout at the telly. It's terribly stressful watching them all be awful to each other! I'm hooked! I love how they manage to make morally questionable people so compelling. Plus, that soundtrack is incredible. I’ve been listening to it on Spotify non-stop. Actually, talking of listening, does anyone actually  read  books anymore, or are you all e-readers now? Oh, I'm staunchly old-school.

Right, so, the big question – how do I even  turn this thing on?  It’s just… black. Ah, yes. A common predicament with new technology. See that tiny button on the right side? Press and hold it for a few seconds. Should vibrate and the Nokia logo should pop up. Yep, vibrate! Logo! Okay, progress. Who knew something so simple could be so daunting? It’s the Finnish minimalism, love. Nokia prides itself on it. Less is more, you know? Though I do miss the days of a satisfyingly chunky charger port. These USB-C things are a pain. Tell me about it. I’m already dreading accidentally leaving it somewhere. Right, now it's asking for a language… obviously English, yeah? Absolutely. And then you'll be prompted to set up your Google account. Or a Nokia account, if you’re feeling particularly adventurous. Google, definitely. Is it easy to transfer all my stuff from my old phone? I’ve got loads of photos and… well, everything, really. It should be. They have a handy little Google Drive backup system. Just make sure your old phone is connected to Wi-Fi and you follow the prompts. They’ll walk you through it. Honestly, it's much easier than it used to be. Remember when you had to root around with cables and computer software? Oh god, don't remind me! My dad used to think he was a computer genius trying to do that. A lot of frustration and very little success. Sounds about right. Now, let’s see, do you want me to help you with the Wi-Fi connection? This pub's Wi-Fi is… questionable, to say the least. Please! I’m utterly clueless. I’ve got the password, but it’s not connecting. Right. Let me just… Okay, it’s being a bit temperamental, but I think I’ve got it. Try it now? Yes! It’s working! Thank you. You’re a lifesaver. I feel like I've conquered a small mountain. Don’t mention it. This is what older brothers are for, isn't it? Though, I’m still baffled as to why you chose a Nokia after being so loyal to Apple for so long. I know, right? It was a bit impulsive, I confess. But I just… liked the design, I guess. And the slightly ridiculous idea of having a super-robust, practically indestructible phone while travelling around Finland.

So, what’s your favourite animal then, love? Apart from Finn, of course. Hmm, that’s a tough one. Probably a Red Panda. They’re so fluffy. Red Pandas are brilliant, aren't they? Proper little chaps. Where do you learn all these cool animal facts? YouTube, mostly. Did you know they're actually more closely related to raccoons than pandas? No! Really? You're full of knowledge. Finn, do you know what a Red Panda is? He likes the dogs better, I think. You know, like Malamooches. Oh, those big fluffy dogs! Those are proper characters, aren't they? Remember when we saw that one in Bristol, pulling a little kid on a scooter? Yeah! It was massive. Bigger than me, almost. My cat, Jasper, would be terrified. Jasper's a brave little thing, really. He’d probably hiss at a Malamooche. Probably. Anyway, about Liam’s birthday… what are we doing? His party’s this weekend, remember? Yes, already! It’s flying by. I was thinking maybe board games, and we could set up a little gymnastics area in the garden, if the weather’s good. Yeah, good idea! He loves gymnastics. Maybe we can get him that new balancing beam he wanted? We can look. It's a bit pricey, though. I was thinking of getting him a present for his friend, Emily, too. Something she’d like as well. What about those little puzzles? She likes those. That’s a good shout. We’ll have to pop into the shops later. Speaking of shops, we need to think about holidays. Are we thinking of going back to England this year? I really want to see Grandma again and Granpa. And maybe go to that Japanese film festival in Bristol. They’re showing all my favourites. I’d love that. We just need to figure out the timings and who can look after Finn. He’s getting so big and independent! He is! He can almost say ‘Red Panda’ now. Honestly, he's a little genius. He’s become obsessed with my iPad recently. Keeps trying to swipe it. He’ll be using a laptop before you know it! We have to get him some kind of educational apps. Absolutely. We want to keep him entertained, but not just stuck on screens all the time. How about we try and find him some of those big, chunky children’s books?

Honestly though, I reckon Christmas at home’s always gonna be the best, innit? Like, no matter what. I get that, yeah. But growing up, Christmas was always massive in Manila. Like,  massive . The decorations start going up in September. Seriously. September! Good heavens. That seems a bit…much. A bit excessive, dear. We put ours up the week before Christmas, like any sane person. Aye, that’s proper. My Nan’d have a right fit if we put them up early. She’d be like "Christmas isn't 'til the 25th, lass!" So, Filipino Christmas, the decorations were everywhere – all the lights, the stars, the parols… you know, the star lanterns? It’s all very colourful. And the food! Oh my god, the food. What sort of food? Everything! Lechon – that’s a roasted pig, a big one. Pancit – which is like a noodle dish. And heaps of rice. It's a feast. And my grandma would always make this specific fruit salad, super sweet and…a lot. Sounds rather decadent. We had a traditional Boxing Day lunch - turkey, of course, sprouts, potatoes, the works. Sprout’s are the worst, honestly. My mum tries every year to make them nice with bacon or something, but they’re still sprouts. My grandma in Manila would say Brussels sprouts were so weird. She couldn't understand the appeal. Well, they’re an acquired taste, dear, that’s for sure. I quite like them. With a little butter, mind you. I remember one Christmas, your mum, bless her, tried to make a Christmas pudding. It nearly set the kitchen on fire. Oh god, I’d forgotten about that! I was little, and I was trying to stir it, and the brandy went everywhere. It was chaos. See? Christmas is always a bit chaotic, no matter where you are. It’s the family, the traditions... even the dodgy sprouts and near-kitchen fires. My Christmases were always lovely, quiet affairs. My husband and I would visit my parents, have a nice dinner, and then sit by the fire and read. Very understated. Simple pleasures, eh? I remember one year trying to convince my children that Father Christmas only came if you left out a carrot for his reindeer. Took them ages to understand. My little cousin still believes, bless him. He leaves out a  mountain  of carrots. And cookies. Clearly, Father Christmas likes a good treat.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Sarah. You’ve outdone yourself. It’s lovely, isn’t it? Better than that awful stuff we had at the pub last week. Absolutely delicious, darling. And a welcome change from all that frozen rubbish I often end up eating when I'm wrestling with a deadline. So, David, how's the admin world treating you? Still surrounded by spreadsheets and disgruntled forms? Pretty much, yes. Though we’ve got a new software system being rolled out – supposedly it’ll make things easier. I'm not holding my breath. It'll probably create a whole new breed of disgruntled forms. The eternal promise of technology, isn't it? Streamlining things…and then only adding layers of complexity. Tell me about it. As a transcriber, I’m constantly battling glitches in audio recordings. You’d think with modern technology, the sound quality would be pristine! It's a struggle, isn't it? Anything involving tech seems designed to frustrate you. Speaking of frustrating, have you both seen "Grey Shadows" on BBC? The new detective series? Oh, yes! I’ve been devouring it. Proper twisty, isn’t it? I can’t work out who the villain is. I'm a few episodes behind, but enjoying it so far. Nice change from all the Nordic Noir stuff that’s been everywhere. Precisely! Something a bit more…British, you know? Rain-soaked streets and proper impenetrable accents. I know! Sarah, are you still reading that Agatha Christie collection? Actually, I just finished it. Went down a right hole in one. Wonderous! You should invest in a Kindle, darling. Then you can carry a whole library with you. I’ve got one. It’s brilliant for holidays. Though, I still love the feel of a real book in my hands. I'm on the fence. Part of me loves the idea of having thousands of books at my fingertips. The other part worries about losing the feel of actual paper. You get used to it. And the backlighting is a godsend for late-night reading. True. Are we still on for that lunch with Emily and Mark next week? Yes, definitely. Saturday, wasn’t it? Yes, Saturday. Emily's been wanting to catch up for ages. She's been swamped with that new project. Right. I'll remind Mark. He’s terrible at keeping track of dates. He is, isn't he?

Right then, Doris, love, you’ve got that awful colour in your face again. Been fretting, haven’t you? Oh, Arthur, don't fuss. It's just the heat. And a little bit of worrying, yes, I suppose. About Michael. Michael? Still struggling with the business, is he? Told him he needed to diversify years ago. Stick to antiques, that’s what I always said. Solid investment. Solid investment, that’s right. Rubbish these newfangled gadgets and online businesses. Give me a good Chippendale any day. He's trying a new online shop, though. On Etsy, he says. Apparently, it's quite the thing. Etsy, eh? Sounds a bit…frivolous, doesn't it? Like selling beaded bracelets and scented candles. Is he selling proper antiques on there? Proper antiques, eh? Doubt it. Likely selling reproduction bits and bobs he’s picked up at a car boot sale. He’s selling some of his vintage maps, actually. And a few small porcelain figures. He's hoping to reach a wider audience. A wider audience of what? People who don’t know the difference between a genuine Hepplewhite and a mass-produced imitation? That's the truth of it, isn’t it, Charles? He's trying, Arthur. He's put a lot of effort into it. Good photography, descriptions… It's a gamble, I know, but he needs to do something. Gamble, that’s a polite word for it. Look, Doris, I’ve always said it - you need to be ruthless. Tell him to focus on what he's good at. High-quality pieces, reputable dealers, that's where the money is. Not chasing after fleeting online trends. That’s right. Stick to your strengths. A bit of common sense, and a good eye. Can't go wrong with that. I know, I know. It's just… it’s hard to be ruthless with your own son. He gets so disheartened. Disheartened? Tell him to get a backbone! This isn't a hobby, Doris, it's a business. He needs to prove himself, not wallow in self-pity. Now, Charles, don't be too hard on the lad. He's young. He’ll learn. But what if he doesn’t? What if he loses everything? Then he dusts himself off and starts again. That's the way of the world, Doris. Tough lessons, but necessary ones. Now, fancy a cuppa? All this talk of business is making me quite peckish.

Right, so tentatively, The Old Bridge Hotel for Saturday? Seems central enough for everyone. And they do decent cocktails. Yeah, that sounds good to me. Much better than trying to find somewhere in the city centre itself. Parking's a nightmare. Sounds perfect! Good location, good drinks, sorted. Should we put a little poll out on Slack to confirm? Just in case anyone’s got a serious aversion to the Old Bridge. Aye, a poll’s a good shout. Makes it feel properly organised. I can do that, easy. Sounds lovely, everyone! I’m so glad we’re doing something. This project has been...intense. I'm looking forward to decompressing! It  has  been. The sheer volume of data… Honestly. You know, on the way in, I nearly ran over a little beetle. Right on the pavement. Oh no! Did you manage to save it? Yeah, thankfully. I swerved just in time. It was a little green one, quite shiny. I scooped it up and put it in a flowerbed. Felt a bit ridiculous, really, but couldn’t just leave it there. Bless you! That’s proper kind. We need more beetles and good people. Aw, that’s lovely. Sometimes the little things make a big difference, don't they? Like, noticing a beetle instead of just rushing past. Absolutely. Reminds me of my grandmother. She used to rescue all sorts of creatures – earthworms, snails… you name it. She claimed they were important for the ecosystem. She was a bit eccentric, but she had a point. My nan was like that too! Always freeing trapped bees and stuff. Made me a bit terrified of insects as a kid, but I appreciate it now. Aye, me mam was always saving birds with broken wings. It was a full-time job sometimes. It's nice to have that connection, isn't it? To caring for something small and vulnerable. Anyway, back to the party. Has anyone thought about a theme? I was thinking maybe something vaguely linguistic? "Lost in Translation" or something fun? Ooh, I like that! We could all dress as words or something. Honestly? I'd be happy just getting dressed up and having a laugh. No need to overthink it. Just good people, good food, and a few drinks. I'm with Grace. Keep it simple, keep it fun. Although, I do have a rather fabulous interpretation of "onomatopoeia" in sequins if anyone's keen.

Ugh, I can't believe it’s already Monday. The weekend went by way too fast. Tell me about it! I feel like I just got settled in. Did you finish that history project? Nearly. I got the main bit done, but I still need to write the conclusion and make the presentation slides. It's due on Friday, isn’t it? Yeah, Mrs. Davies really wants it to be polished. I’m a bit behind on mine, actually. I started researching, but then got distracted by TikTok. Classic. I know the feeling. My mum kept nagging me to do something productive instead of watching YouTube. My dad's the same. He keeps going on about “time management” and “prioritising.” Like, I know! Seriously! It’s so annoying when they treat you like you’re completely incapable. So, what's today's torture? Maths or English? Maths, unfortunately. Mr. Harrison is grilling us on quadratic equations. I'm going to fail. Absolutely fail. Oh god, those are the worst. I think I vaguely remember them... vaguely. Did you do the homework? Half of it. I got stuck on question four. It involved, like, a word problem about sheep and a field. It made no sense. Oh, those are the worst! They purposefully make them confusing, I swear. Did you ask anyone for help? No, I panicked and just closed the book. I'll try and figure it out later, I suppose. What about you? Anything exciting in English? We’re starting  Macbeth  this week. I’m kind of excited actually. I’ve heard it's really good. Oh yeah! That's the one with all the witches, right? Yeah! And lots of blood. But apparently, it’s really clever, with all the symbolism and stuff. Sounds intense. I’m still traumatized from  Romeo and Juliet . All that teenage angst. Yeah, that was a bit much. Speaking of intense, did you hear about what happened with Liam and Chloe? No! What? Spill! Apparently, they had a massive row in the cafeteria at lunch on Friday. Everyone was talking about it. No way! What were they arguing about? Something about a stolen hoodie, I think. It got pretty loud, apparently. Mrs. Davies had to step in. Wow! Drama. High school is just so ridiculous sometimes. Seriously! I can’t wait to be done with it all. What are you thinking of doing after A-levels anyway?

This risotto is absolutely gorgeous, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Aye, well your dad always said I made a mean risotto. Used to be his Friday night treat, you know. It really is good. Seriously, I could eat a whole bowl of this. Much better than that reheated lasagne we had last week, no offense, Mum. None taken, love. That was a bit of a disaster wasn’t it? The cheese went all rubbery. Had to chuck most of it. You always say it’s fine to waste a bit, but it feels so wrong. We should really try harder to use up everything. I know, I know. Just a habit, lass. Now, tell me about this new project you're working on at the office. You were looking a bit stressed last time we spoke. It's the Henderson account, remember? They're being  impossible . They want everything yesterday, and the brief keeps changing. I'm spending all my time just chasing them for clarification. It's draining. Sounds awful. Are you able to push back at all, or are you just having to bend to their will? I tried, honestly. My boss said, "Just keep the client happy, it’s a big account”. Which is code for "Your sanity doesn’t matter." Men. All of them. Always prioritizing the bottom line over the people doing the work. Mum, really? You sound like Gran sometimes. Well, I've seen a thing or two in my time, lad. They wouldn’t keep me on for 20 years if I didn’t speak my mind, would they? Anyway, is your dad home yet? I brought him those pasties he likes from Greggs. Not yet, he’s got that late meeting. He keeps saying he's going to put his foot down and try and delegate more, but...you know Dad. He just takes on everything himself. Aye, stubborn as an ox, that man. Hasn't changed a bit since you were a toddler, demanding he read you that same story over and over. Do you remember, Nicola, how you'd cry if he stopped halfway through "The Gruffalo"? Oh God, you’re pulling out the old stories now? Yes! I was such a drama queen. Were there any other good stories he used to read? Loads! He used to make up his own little ones about a mischievous badger who stole all the custard creams.

Honestly, Sarah, it's been a mad few weeks. Just absolutely mad. Tell me about it, love. You sound stressed. Come on, sit down, I’ve made a pot of tea. Earl Grey, your favourite, right? Oh, you shouldn't have. Yes, please, Earl Grey would be lovely. Thank you. It’s just… everything at once, you know? The operation went fine, thankfully. No complications. That's brilliant, love! Really relieved to hear that. When were you back at work? Last week, eased back in. But then Liam’s been… well, Liam's been Liam. Oh dear. Detention again? What was it this time? Skateboarding on school grounds! Honestly, the school's lost the plot. A warning would have sufficed, but straight to detention. And the school's got like, cameras everywhere. Makes you feel a bit like you’re living in a goldfish bowl. Kids, eh? Always pushing the boundaries. My own Jake got detention last term for something ridiculous with a pigeon. A pigeon? Seriously? Seriously! He was trying to teach it to fetch. Honestly, the things they think of. Still, it was a good story, wasn’t it? It is, actually. It's better than stories about skateboarding! But seriously, I’m worried about him. He seems… distant. Not really talking. Teenagers, right? They like to have their secrets. Have you spoken to his teachers? I have, but they just say he’s “fine,” which isn’t very helpful, is it? And Emily’s been getting on my nerves, too - constantly complaining about her friends. It's exhausting. They’re always complaining about their friends! It’s what they do. Just gotta ride it out. But you need to look after yourself first, love. That operation must have taken a lot out of you. It did. And my back hasn't been right since… it’s just a sort of ache. I should probably get that looked at. You absolutely should. Don't you dare put yourself last. Have you been to see your specialist since the operation? Yes, last week. All clear, apparently. But the ache's still there. Right. Listen, I'm popping down to see Carol next week. You fancy coming along? We could all go for lunch. That would be lovely, actually. I haven't seen Carol in ages. It would be a nice change of pace. Good. Sorted then. Now, about your work... you mentioned planning work?

Honestly, I’m knackered. This shift last night was mental. Oh yeah? What was it like? Saturday nights at The Salty Dog are always a bit wild, aren’t they? Wild doesn't even cover it. Proper mayhem. We had a stag do, a hen do, and a football team all converging at once. The queue was out the door for hours. My feet are killing me. Ouch. Are you on the bar all night? Yeah, until half two. Luckily, Liam was on door duty so he kept some of the… more enthusiastic… people in check. But still, constant orders, spilled drinks, people asking for ridiculous cocktails. You wouldn't believe some of the things they wanted. Like what? Don't tell me another one wants a "unicorn sparkle potion." Worse! This guy wanted a Mojito but with pineapple and, and… beetroot? Beetroot?! Seriously? I’m not joking. I had to politely explain that wasn’t really a thing. The bar manager nearly had a fit though. So many wasted ingredients. That's crazy. So, is it worth it, though? The money must be decent on a Saturday. The money’s okay, yeah. Tips were alright too, thankfully. But it's exhausting. I swear, I’m going to need a week of just lying down to recover. It's good practice for handling difficult people, I guess, prepping me for life. I suppose so! Sounds like a long way from studying Shakespeare, though. Tell me about it. Sometimes I feel like I’m living two completely different lives. One where I’m analyzing sonnets, and the other where I’m wiping up spilled beer. Well, at least you're earning while you’re studying. My student loan isn't exactly covering everything these days. True. Though honestly, after last night, I’m half tempted to just live off tips and become a professional bartender. Don’t say that! Your English degree is too valuable to waste. Besides, who would I complain to about awful essays if you weren’t around? Fair point. Now, have you managed to find anything on the Romantic poets yet? I’m properly stuck on Wordsworth. Honestly, it's all just fields and daffodils to me. I've got a few notes. Let's go find a table, and I’ll explain. But first, promise me you’ll lie down later. You look like you could fall asleep standing up.

Right, so anyone got big holiday plans kicking off soon? I’m itching to get away, feeling a bit burnt out. Oh, you know me, always planning! We're off to Cornwall next week. Little cottage by the sea, proper relaxing. Hoping for sunshine, but prepared for rain, as always. Cornwall, lovely! Salt air, proper fresh. I’m off to County Clare myself, in a few weeks. Back to the old country, you know? County Clare! Wonderful. My wife and I are doing the Scottish Highlands this summer. Wild camping, really hoping we don’t encounter any midges. Heard they're brutal this year. Wild camping? Brave man! I'd need a five-star hotel after a day of that. Though, those views must be incredible. Ooh, Scotland! My cousin went last year and said the scenery was breathtaking. Although she did come back covered in bites. She's convinced a wee bit of midge just moved in under her skin. Aye, they're a feathery wee nuisance, those midges. But the beauty of Clare, you're surrounded by the sea, the cliffs... it just washes away all your troubles. That’s the idea, isn’t it? To get properly away from it all. Though, I do worry about the toilet situation with wild camping. Let's just say I’m bringing a lot of loo roll. You’re a legend, David! I’m doing a mini-break to the Lake District. Just sticking to B&Bs, thank you very much. A proper cuppa and a biscuit is essential. The Lake District’s gorgeous! Used to go there as a kid. Remember those sticky toffee pudding things they sold everywhere? Heaven. Ah, sticky toffee pudding. You can't beat it. Reminds me of my granny’s. She used to put a little bit of Irish whiskey in hers. Gave it a wee kick! Now  that’s  a travel tip I can get behind. Whiskey in the pudding. Brilliant! I might need to steal that one. Don’t tell my B&B owner that! They’d have a fit. It's just a little bit for flavour! Don’t tell them. Keeps you warm in those damp Scottish hills too. Aye, a wee drop of something warm keeps the chill out of your bones. It’s the Irish way. Well, I'm off to research the best midge repellent. And maybe a recipe for whiskey-infused sticky toffee pudding.

Oh, come on! That was a definite foul! Referee’s blind, honestly. Blind or just doesn't want to give them anything, Rach. It's Newcastle, they're always going to be scrutinized a bit more. Scrutinized? They're getting robbed! Honestly, you’d think with all the cameras now, they’d see it. They see it. They just don't  call  it. It's a different thing. Happens all the time. Easy for you to say, you're not from the North East, aren’t you? You've never had to deal with this level of injustice. Alright, alright. I’m just observing. Though, let's be honest, even Birmingham get some questionable calls. Birmingham. You’re comparing Birmingham to the mighty Magpies? Don’t be daft. Hey, we’ve had our moments! Remember that dodgy penalty against Villa years ago? Okay, that was bad, I’ll give you that. But it’s not the same. This is practically a conspiracy. Dramatic as ever, Rach. So, hungry? I was thinking maybe we could order something. Dying. But nothing too fancy. After all that stress, I need comfort food. Exactly. Pizza? Burgers? What’s your poison? Burgers. Definitely burgers. Double patty, bacon, all the works. And chips. Loads of chips. Right, let me just have a look at what’s nearby. Any particular place you're craving? Not really. As long as they do decent burgers, I’m happy. Oh! And onion rings. Don't forget the onion rings. Onion rings it is. You know, for someone doing serious research, you have remarkably simple tastes in food. It's called prioritizing, Liam. My brain needs fuel. And a good win would be a bonus. Come on, Newcastle! Don’t let me down! Honestly, this ref… Alright, alright. I'm ordering. And I'm not getting you extra onion rings. You'll complain you're too full for dessert. Dessert? Liam! It’s Newcastle versus… well, anyone. Dessert is a luxury we can’t afford right now. Focus! Focus! You’re impossible. But I love it. One burger, one pizza, extra chips,  some  onion rings, coming right up. And wish Newcastle the best from me. Just… try not to throw the remote at the TV if they lose. No promises. No promises at all. That's my girl. Oh! Free kick! Here we go. This could be it! This could  really  be it!

Right then, Grandma, this flat's looking lovely as always. Mum, you’ve done a brilliant job tidying up. Oh, it's nothing, love. Just keeping busy. You're looking well, Michael. That suit’s smart. It is nice, isn’t it? Though a bit too much dusting for me this morning. My knees aren't what they used to be. Fancy a biscuit, Michael? Ginger or shortbread? Shortbread, please, Mum. Thanks. Grandma, how are you feeling today? Alright, alright. Bit stiff this morning, the rheumatics, you know. The rain doesn't help, nothing but rain lately. Remember when we used to have proper summers? I can barely imagine that! It's been drizzling non-stop for weeks. You know, I was watching that new film, ‘Dune: Part Two’ last night. Absolutely incredible. You’d probably like the visuals, Grandma. ‘Dune’? What's it about? All these new films… too much noise and explosions for me. Give me a good old Carry On film any day. Now  those  were funny. Oh, Grandma, you and your Carry Ons! I think there's a documentary on them on Channel 5 tonight, actually. I’ll have to record it for you then, Grandma. Speaking of recording things, I'm trying to sort out those photos from your birthday last month. I’ve digitised them all now, Mum, do you want me to back them up to a cloud drive or something? Oh, that would be brilliant, love. My hard drive's getting full. You're a lifesaver. You always were clever, Michael. Always fiddling with things. Used to take apart all my dolls when you were a little lad. Guilty as charged! I was always building things. Remember that pedal bike I built from scraps when I was about eight? It was hideous, but I was so proud of it. Oh, I remember that! You nearly squashed Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses riding it down the street. She was furious, she was. Thought you were trying to wreck her garden. I wasn't trying to! It just didn't steer particularly well! Still, got me a ride around the block. Speaking of bikes, Mum, did you ever get around to replacing that old shopping bike you mentioned last week? Not yet, love. Been looking at a few online, but nothing quite right. I don’t want anything too fancy, just something sturdy I can use to get to the shops and back.

Right, pancakes finished! Did you both enjoy them? No. Good! Just good? Not yummy? Leo, you've got maple syrup all over your chin. It is yummy. Rosie, why didn't you eat yours? They had chocolate chips. They were too…flappy. Flappy? Pancakes don't usually get described as flappy. She means floppy, Mummy. Like when you’re playing with playdough. Oh, floppy! Right. Well, we’ve got a busy day ahead. School assembly this afternoon – remember you need to be quiet, Rosie. Miss Davies is talking about… well, I’m not entirely sure what she's talking about, but it’s important. Is it about dinosaurs? Possibly! Maybe. We’re going to the Science Museum next weekend, remember? That's  definitely  about dinosaurs. I got the tickets booked. Can we see the rocket thing? Yes! The Saturn V rocket. It’s enormous. Okay, teeth now. Both of you. And proper scrubbing, especially after all those pancakes. But I don’t want to. Yes, you do. And Leo, no rinsing too quickly! I can hear you through the bathroom door. After that we'll read a Green Knowe story. Green Knowe! The one with the ghost? Yes, the one with the ghost. It's rather lovely, actually. Makes me think of growing up – my Gran used to read those to me. Remember when we talked about children at school who don’t always have enough to eat? Yes. It makes you think, doesn't it? Some kids go home and don't even get a proper dinner. It’s so unfair. Leo, please finish your pancake. Even just a few more bites. It's not fair to waste food either. But Rosie didn't eat hers. That’s different, darling. You need to eat properly so you can grow big and strong. And remember Hannah from class? The one who's always so quiet? We’re collecting for her family this week. Is she hungry? Maybe. Sometimes people are hungry in different ways. Sometimes not having enough food makes people sad and worried. We need to help. Maybe we could draw some pictures for her? Can we go to the beach next weekend instead of the Science Museum? We’ll see. It depends on the weather. And Paris is still on the cards for next year, right? You both really want to go? Yes! Eiffel Tower! Lots of planes! And…and croissants!

This noodles are unbelievably good. Seriously, best Chinese I’ve had in ages. Yeah, this is a good choice. Glad we didn't get that dodgy place again. Remember last time? Oh god, don't remind me. The chicken was practically rubber. I’m still scarred. You're being dramatic, Chloe. It wasn’t  that  bad. Easy for you to say, Ethan. You ate three plates of it. So, has anyone heard anything more about Sarah’s grandma's funeral? Just that it’s next Friday. Apparently, there’s going to be a ridiculous amount of people. Her family is huge. Yeah, Hannah said something about needing to coordinate carpools. Anyone fancy giving her a ring? I can, yeah. I’ll do it later. Anything interesting happening in the news besides, you know, everything awful? Apparently, there's a cricket scandal. Something about match fixing. Honestly, I don’t really follow it that closely. Oh, that’s grim. Remember when we were kids and we used to pretend we were Bob the Builder and build Lego houses? God, yes! You were always the foreman, weren’t you, Ben? Organizing everyone and bossing us around. Someone had to keep things running smoothly! Ethan mostly just knocked over towers. Hey! I was a demolition expert. A very important role. You were the chaos agent. Speaking of important roles, I saw a trailer for that new film – the one with Anya Taylor-Joy.  Furiosa ? Yeah, it looks pretty intense. Should we maybe go see it next week? Sounds good to me. Unless you guys are all tied up with the funeral stuff. I'm free. It'd be a nice change from soil reports and nutrient deficiencies. Right. So, film next week? Maybe after we’ve all helped Sarah out with the funeral arrangements? Definitely. And maybe we can finally tackle cleaning the living room. It’s starting to resemble a student flat. Oh, here we go. Blaming me again. I was the only one who actually vacuumed last month. That was one month, Ben. And you barely touched the corners. Guys, come on. Let’s just enjoy the noodles. It’s a good food, good company kind of night. You’re right, you’re right. More noodles for me then! Anyone want some of my spring rolls? Always! Pass them over. Speaking of good things, I got a new article published today. Bit niche, but apparently, there's a lot of buzz around it within the agricultural community.

So, you were telling me about Mrs. Higgins next door when you were a girl, Mum? The one who kept pigeons? Oh, Mrs. Higgins. A character she was. Kept those pigeons in the loft, you know. More pigeons than people in the street, practically. And every morning, the noise… cooing and flapping. Drove my poor mother mad! You could hear it all the way down the street, couldn’t you? I remember visiting your house as a child, and the constant pigeon noises…it was quite something. It was! But she was a good woman, really. Always had a smile and a cup of tea for everyone. Even when those pigeons made a mess of everything. She used to say, "They bring good luck, you know." Though I never saw any good luck coming from pigeon droppings! It’s funny how people stick in your memory, isn't it? Even the eccentric ones. I'm taking part in a really interesting psychological experiment at the moment, actually. It's all about how memory works and how we filter certain experiences. They’re trying to see what triggers vivid recall. Oh really? What sort of thing are they doing? Well, they show you short videos and ask you to remember details later. It's fascinating. It makes you realise how much we  don't  remember. Reminds me of my sister, Elsie. Terrible memory. Couldn’t remember what she had for breakfast, let alone anything from years ago. But she could remember the exact price of a loaf of bread in 1952! Classic! Speaking of modern things, have you seen those driverless cars they’re testing? Bit unsettling, aren't they? They are! I did a piece on them at school actually. The safety implications are huge, and the ethical questions… who’s responsible if something goes wrong? Blimey. I remember when flying was a luxury. Now everyone’s jetting off somewhere. Makes you wonder about air safety, doesn’t it? Though, statistically, it's still safer than driving. Absolutely. You know, I was at the supermarket the other day and they have that ‘Scan as You Go’ thing now. It’s so efficient, but I missed the chat with the cashier. It feels a bit… impersonal. I know what you mean. I much prefer the human interaction. Though, it’s tempting when you’re rushing. Anyone want a cake? They’re Mum’s recipe – always a favourite.

Right, who wants to help Mummy make decorations for Chinese New Year? We need lots of red and gold! Me! Me! I wanna draw a dragon! A big, sparkly dragon! I wanna draw a rocket! To go to space! Okay, both of you. We can have a dragon  and  a rocket. But the New Year is all about dragons, isn’t it? They bring good luck. Do rockets bring good luck? Well, they take you to the planets! And space has lots of mysteries. We could learn about the planets later, tonight okay? Which one’s the biggest? Is it Mars? No, Mars is red and quite small compared to Jupiter! Jupiter is gigantic – you could fit over a thousand Earths inside it! Wow! Can we draw Jupiter too? We could. But first, let's focus on the lovely dragon. Do you want to use glitter, sweetheart? Yes! Lots and lots! And you can draw your rocket blasting off! Maybe into a galaxy of stars. Can it have a little man waving? Of course it can have a little man waving. What's he waving  at ? At me! Very important. Now, while we're decorating, who's hungry? I was thinking we could order some Chinese food to celebrate later. Noodles! I want noodles! And sweet and sour pork! I want spring rolls! The crunchy ones! You both got it. Right, dragon scales...do you want to use these little star stickers as dragon scales? Yeah! And can I wear my princess dress? It’s sparkly too. Absolutely. Speaking of sparkly and princesses, did you enjoy Barbie and the Great Adventure at school today? Yeah! I said I was Romy! And I got to save Princess Chelsea! I was no. And what about your piano lesson? Did you practice your scales? Kinda. Kinda? You know practising is important. Mrs. Davies says you're doing really well. And your drum lessons - are you getting any better at keeping the beat? Yes! I can do a really good BOOM! That’s progress! And don't forget about your aerial hoop class next week! Are you excited? Yeah! I want to do a cartwheel! You’ll be doing cartwheels in no time, darling. Just keep practicing. Now, red or gold glitter first? Dragon or rocket? Decisions, decisions! Dragon! Dragon first! And then Mars! Can we draw Mars after the rocket? Absolutely. Mars it is!

This place is actually really chilled, right? I was expecting somewhere packed with tourists. Yeah, it’s a good find. Bit pricey, though. Air BnB’s been a nightmare to navigate – directions were basically non-existent. We ended up wandering around for an hour. Tell me about it! My last Air BnB in Barcelona was miles from anything. Ended up using taxis everywhere. Not ideal when you're on a budget. Yeah, Rome’s got that vibe – you can wander for ages and still feel lost. It’s part of the charm, I reckon. Definitely. So, tonight - dinner? What are we thinking? I’m open to anything, really. As long as it's not pizza again. I've had enough pizza to last a lifetime. I was thinking somewhere authentic, you know? Not a tourist trap. Somewhere with proper Roman food. My Nonna would disapprove if we went to a place with picture menus. My mate Jake's got some recommendations. He spent a year here a few years back. Says there’s a great little trattoria near the Pantheon. Pantheon! Sounds amazing. Let’s look it up. Anyone else’s family going crazy back home, wanting updates? Mum’s already sent five texts. Mostly asking if I’m eating enough and if I’ve seen any handsome Italians. Standard. Mine's the same! My little brother keeps asking if I’ve bought him back any Roman souvenirs. Probably wants a miniature Colosseum. My mum’s got that “concerned but proud” vibe going. Keeps asking if I’m making friends and if the coffee’s good. Priorities, you know? Speaking of accents, you sound proper Aussie, mate. Been here long? Just landed yesterday morning. Still trying to adjust to the time difference. How about you both? You’ve been here a week, right? Yeah, a week. Getting used to the chaos gradually. Rome's mad, but in a good way. It's beautiful, though. Yesterday I learned a few basic phrases in Italian. "Ciao" and "Grazie" are pretty useful. Yeah, try to avoid just saying "hello" and "thank you" – they’ll know you’re tourists immediately. True that. Learn to say "un altro birra, per favore” – much more effective. Noted. So, Jake’s trattoria it is, then? Do we book a table? Yeah, let’s do it. And anyone got recommendations for gelato places? Because that’s equally important. I heard one near the Trevi Fountain is supposed to be incredible... although probably swamped with tourists.

Ugh, I’m so stressed about this hen do. It's just… a lot. What's the stress about, Elodie? It's supposed to be fun! I know, I know! But organising something for ten people, with everyone’s dietary needs and budget… it's exhausting. And I’ve got Claire saying she only wants to do pottery, and Sarah wants a cocktail masterclass, and then there’s Jen who just wants a spa day. Sounds like a recipe for disaster. Maybe compromise? Pottery one day, cocktails the next? That's what I'm trying to do! But seemingly everyone has very strong opinions. I saw a gorgeous craft workshop near York, but I don't know if it's worth the travel. York’s lovely! And it would be a nice change of scenery. Though, travel  does  add to the cost. What's the budget looking like for everyone? That’s the other sticking point. I’m trying to keep it reasonable, but then I get tempted by all these fancy experiences. Want to go axe throwing? £50 a person! No thank you! Axe throwing at a hen do? That's a bit intense! Definitely too intense. Remember that time we tried to do a murder mystery at uni and it completely fell apart? Don’t remind me! It was a disaster! Everyone accused each other of cheating. Exactly! I don't want a disaster. I just want everyone to have a good time and I’m currently feeling like I’m failing already! You're not failing. It’s normal to feel overwhelmed. Maybe you need to delegate? Ask Ali and Rosie to take over some of the planning? I considered it, but I’m scared they’ll put their own spin on it and it won’t be what the bride wants. That's fair. But a little help wouldn’t hurt, surely? Maybe Rosie could look at accommodation options? She’s brilliant at finding deals. And Ali’s amazing at finding quirky activities. She'd definitely come up with something fun. I suppose you’re right. I’m just so used to doing everything myself. What are you two up to anyway? Besides judging my hen do struggles. I'm finally getting around to baking that lemon drizzle cake I mentioned. It's for my mum's birthday. Ooh, exciting! Is it the super-zesty one?

Right, so, the chicken's nearly cooked then? Smells pretty good actually. Bit too much paprika, maybe? Nah, it's fine. It needs the paprika, trust me. You wouldn’t want bland chicken. You’re fussing about it already. Fussing? I’m just observing! You practically coated the thing in it. I’m still feeling a bit rough too, you know, from that flu. Yeah, you looked properly peaked last week. Still got a little bit of a rasp, haven't you? Bet it’s still lingering. Probably. It felt like a proper knock-out though, didn't it? Couldn't even get out of bed. Mum was hovering all the time, which was... well, you know Mum. Always fussing. Did she bring you that dodgy soup again? Please don't remind me. That butternut squash thing. Tasted like baby food. Classic Mum. So, you thinking about booking those flights to Barcelona finally? Yeah, I’ve been looking. Hotels are surprisingly pricey though, aren’t they? Found one near the Las Ramblas… looked decent enough, but it’s £150 a night. Blimey, that  is  steep. Maybe look a bit further out? There's loads of Airbnbs now, you know. Can get a really nice apartment for less, probably with a kitchen to cook in. Yeah, good point. Trying to balance saving money with, like, being somewhere walkable. Don’t fancy spending all day on public transport. Remember that awful hotel in Prague? Oh god, don't even go there. That place was… questionable. Sticky carpets, threadbare towels… And the breakfast? Cornflakes swimming in something that vaguely resembled milk. Right? I think I had croissants for every meal just to avoid it. Anyway, Barcelona. You need a break, and sunshine. Are you still craving that paella? Desperately. Absolutely desperate. Actually, speaking of paella, I saw a recipe online the other day… could actually try and make one. Seriously? You? Cooking? Hey! I have potential. Might need your supervision, though. You’re the marginally more experienced chef in this household. Alright, alright. I'll keep an eye on you. Don’t burn the kitchen down while I’m trying to make the rice. Did you get the saffron? It's essential for a proper paella. Think so. It’s somewhere… in the cupboard. I'll have a root around later. Right, how’s the chicken looking? Should I crank the heat up a bit?

Right, let’s have a proper look at this then. We need a shopping list, definitely. What are we missing for this week? Well, the usual really, don't we? Milk, bread... I seem to have run out of teabags. And those little biscuits you like. The ones with the chocolate chips. Oh, yes, those are essential. And apples. I want some nice crisp apples. And something for supper, I fancy a fish pie. Good idea. Shall I write these down? I’m getting a bit forgetful these days. Please do. And write ‘birthday cards’ on there too. We need to order some. And I'm still stuck on what age to put on them. Should we just put 'sixty'? It feels… awkward, doesn't it? A bit. Perhaps we should just put "Over 60" in a fancy font. Or, even better, don’t put an age at all. Just a nice message. Mrs. Higgins at school used to do that. Mrs. Higgins… she had the most wonderful art and craft projects, didn’t she? Remember making those little paper animals? The ones with the googly eyes? Oh goodness, yes! And the felt boards. I’ve still got a few of those felt shapes somewhere, tucked away. Though I can’t remember what we used them for exactly. We used them for storytelling mostly. And those awful hockey boots we had to wear for PE. They always smelled so dreadful! They did, didn't they! I remember my toes were always squished. Though I did enjoy the PE lessons. I was quite good at netball. What did you want to study at university then? I was absolutely determined to do sound recording. I was fascinated by the technical side of music. Remember how we used to record birdsong on those old cassette recorders? You always had a knack for capturing things. I always thought I’d end up teaching social history. I was fascinated by how everyday lives changed. It's astonishing, really, looking back at how much has changed in the last thirty years. Especially with computers. Remember those massive mainframe things they had at the university? Oh, yes! They filled entire rooms! And the noise they made! We’re talking reel-to-reel tape, punch cards… completely different from what we have now. I’ve been talking to the computing museum down the road. They're collecting old computers.

So, the neighbours seem lovely, don’t they? Really welcoming. They are, aren't they? Mrs. Trevorrow brought over a victoria sponge the other day. A  proper  one, too, not one of those shop-bought things. Oh, that’s lovely! You've landed yourself in a good spot then. Much better than that flat in Southend. It is. It really is. The quiet... you can actually  hear  the birds. Can’t do that in Southend, not with the constant rumble of the traffic and trains. Though I do miss the sea sometimes, I must admit. Well, you're not  that  far from the coast now. Easy enough to pop over to Bude for a day trip. Have you joined that walking group yet? I know you were thinking about it. I've looked them up, yes. They seem very keen. Lots of enthusiastic rambling. A bit intimidating, to be honest! Don't be silly. You’ll fit right in. It's mostly local people, wants to share their knowledge of the area. Want to show you where the best bluebells are. Exactly! And it’s a good way to meet people, isn’t it? Beyond Mrs. Trevorrow and her sponge. True, true. I’m still getting used to driving on these country lanes too. They’re so narrow! Nearly clipped a hedge the other day. Oh, everything’s narrower in Devon. Trust me, you'll get used to it. You'll be confidently navigating those lanes in no time. Did you get that quote for the fence yet? I did. It's a bit higher than I was hoping, but needs must. The dog’s already trying to escape into Mrs. Pengelly's prize-winning dahlias. Oh, he is, is he? He’ll be the terror of the village before you know it. He already is! He ambushed the postman yesterday. Little scamp. You'll need to teach him some manners then. Although, no harm done, I'm sure. What are you thinking of planting in the garden? Anything specific? Well, I'd love to get a vegetable patch going – tomatoes, lettuce, that sort of thing. But I haven't really got a clue. They say the soil's good here. I can give you some tips! My mum's a whiz with a vegetable patch. She practically feeds the whole street during the summer. And we  must  try the pub down the road.

Ugh, this is ridiculous. Another rejection email. Let me guess, another retail job? They're all asking for experience, aren't they? It's a vicious cycle. Tell me about it. “Proven customer service skills, previous experience in a fast-paced environment…” I've never even  been  in a fast-paced environment. My life is a gentle, meandering stream of disappointment. Don’t be dramatic. You've got a degree. That’s gotta count for something. A degree in philosophy that nobody wants. I should’ve done something practical like plumbing, honestly. At least you'd be able to fix the leaky tap in the bathroom. Mum's been on at you for weeks about that. Yeah, yeah. Right. Speaking of Mum, did you see that dress she ordered online? The one from Wish? Oh yeah! The purple sparkly one? She sent me a picture. It looks… interesting. Interesting is one word for it. It looked like a gutted disco ball. And she ordered two! Two! What’s she going to do with two sequined purple dresses? I have no idea. Probably try to wear them to bingo night and blind everyone. She’d look great, honestly. Although, seriously, Wish? The quality must be appalling. Appalling is an understatement. I ordered some headphones from them last year. They broke after three days. Three days! And their customer service is non-existent. Online shopping is a lottery, isn't it? Sometimes you get a bargain, sometimes you get a pile of rubbish. I’m trying to resist ordering anything else until I’ve saved up a bit more. Uni’s expensive enough as it is. You should. I’m trying to resist too, but… Amazon’s got deals on everything. Tempting. Have you seen that new documentary on Netflix? The one about the algorithms? It's kind of scary how they get you. No, I haven't. Sounds depressing. I try to avoid anything that reminds me how powerless I am in the face of technology. It’s not all doom and gloom! It explains how they decide what ads to show you. It's pretty fascinating. Plus, they've got that new series with that actor you like… Oh really? Which actor? You know, Liam Gallagher's brother? The one who was in… Matt Smith? Yeah! Okay, maybe I’ll check it out. Anything to distract me from the brutal reality of job searching.

So, this sofa…it’s remarkably comfortable, actually. Far nicer than what I had back in Southend. It really is. And it fits the room perfectly, doesn't it? You've done a brilliant job getting everything in here, honestly. It feels like a home already. Absolutely, dear. You've managed to make it look so cosy, even with minimal furniture. That coffee table’s a lovely touch too. Did you say you found it at that antique place in Bude? I did indeed. Hidden away in the corner. I’m really hoping that old Aga will give us some reliable heating this winter, though. It looks the part, but I’m slightly nervous about it. Is it all sorted with the electrician? He seemed confident when he did his assessment. Yes, he was. Said it just needed a bit of a service. Should be reliable now. Though, you know, these things... They always have a quirk, don't they? My washing machine is twenty years old. Still going strong, but makes the most awful racket. Sounds like a herd of elephants stampeding in the utility room. Oh, I know the feeling! My car’s nearly fifteen years old and I swear it has a personality of its own. It rattles, it groans, but it gets me from A to B. Speaking of getting from A to B, are you thinking of going for that coastal walk tomorrow? The weather forecast looks gorgeous. Oh, goodness yes! I've been looking forward to it all week. I've packed my walking boots and a flask of tea. Are you two joining us? Definitely! It’ll be a nice change from marking essays, that’s for sure. Any particular route in mind, Anon? I was thinking we could head towards Hartland Quay. It’s a bit of a trek, but the views are spectacular. And then maybe stop for lunch at that little pub in Clovelly – The Red Lion. Clovelly!
