Oh, that’s lovely. But watch out for those steep steps… my knees aren't what they used to be. We’ll take it easy, don't worry. Plenty of stops along the way. Though, I might need to get my bicycle serviced before the weekend. The chain’s been sounding a bit iffy lately. Oh, I have an idea! Have you seen those Virgin Experience Days? They do bike servicing. Might be a nice treat.

Right, that was…surprisingly pleasant. Didn’t think I’d be able to relax enough to actually  enjoy  a roast after the week I’ve had. You say relax, I say you spent half the meal talking about participant recruitment rates for your study. Guilty as charged. It’s just…frustrating. I need to get this pilot study running properly, and the response rate is abysmal. Well, health psychology can’t be the most exciting thing to tick in an online survey, can it? You’re asking people about their anxieties and coping mechanisms. I know, I know. I’ve tried everything. Different wording, incentives, assuring anonymity… nothing seems to work. My supervisor’s hinting that I need to rethink my methodology. Oh, don’t let him get you down. It's just the teething problems. Remember when you were agonising over controlling for socioeconomic status in your PhD? You worked that out. Remind me again how much sleep I lost over that. But this feels different. This is a critical part of the funding application. Okay, right. Deep breaths. Maybe… have you tried different recruitment channels? Online forums, community groups…? Yeah, I’ve dabbled, but it’s just…noise. Loads of people clicking without actually engaging. Hmm. Maybe target very specific groups? There are those online support forums for people with chronic illnesses. Perhaps tailor your recruitment to them? It'd be directly relevant. That’s… actually not a bad idea. More targeted. Less general spamming. I hadn’t thought of it like that. See? You're a brilliant researcher, you just need to think a bit outside the box. Speaking of boxes, how's your mum doing with sorting through Dad's things? It’s…tough. She’s trying to be strong, but it’s clearly getting to her. She called earlier, practically in tears about finding his old toolbox. Said it brought back so many memories of him fixing things around the house. Oh, darling. That's heartbreaking. Is she managing okay with everything? She's doing her best. I've offered to go up next weekend and help her sort through the rest. I just don’t know where to start. There's  so  much stuff. We'll go with you. Both of us. It’s not something she should do alone. And we can split it up. I’m pretty ruthless when it comes to decluttering. You always were.

Right, I think that’s everyone seated. Dinner's ready! Smells lovely, doesn't it? It does! Thanks, Mum. This smells amazing, seriously. Is that the lamb you were talking about? It is. Slow-roasted, just how you like it. Your dad managed to find a really good butcher’s just down the road. He always does. Showing off a bit, as usual. Had to tell him he couldn’t spend  all  the pension on lamb! Oi, don’t be like that, Terry! A man’s gotta enjoy himself, innit? Good lamb’s worth spending on. Besides, I'm cleared to do some extra work next week – so that'll bring some money in. Good for you, David. Always good to have a bit extra. Finances have been a bit tight for everyone lately, haven't they? Tell me about it. Between hospital parking and everything else… It's ridiculous. Oh god, hospital parking. The bane of nurses' lives. Is the hospital still trying to implement that new language requirement? Yes, terribly. Apparently, they’re pushing for everyone to be practically fluent in at least three languages. As if we don't have enough on our plates! Absurd. Where are they going to find nurses that speak three languages? It wouldn't happen in my day! They think it’ll improve patient care, apparently. But I reckon it would just cause more stress. I’m struggling enough to keep up with my training and learn all the new protocols! Learning French on top of it… You’d be brilliant at it, though, Auntie Susan. You always loved French at school. Remember you used to teach us all the weird phrases? Oh, goodness. I do try. Although my husband keeps correcting my grammar. He’s got such a good ear for it. Funny how he’s terrible at remembering birthdays, but a French grammar whiz! Men, eh? Never understand the important things. Speaking of important things, does anyone remember that awful German holiday we went on when we were kids? The one where it rained solid for two weeks? Oh god, don’t remind me! We were all miserable. And your dad kept trying to convince us it was ‘character building.’ He did! Said we'd look back on it fondly. As if! He’s a legend, that one. He’s just like my auntie who was the most left-handed person I ever met.

Grandad, you were telling us about that trip to Italy, weren’t you? Before I started rambling on about this new tagging system for the corpus… Aye, Italy. Lovely place. Went with your Auntie Elsie, bless her, back in '68. Just after I retired from BT. Foreign travel wasn’t exactly common back then, you know. It must have been quite the adventure. What was the first place you went to? Venice, of course. Had to be Venice. Picturesque. Gondolas everywhere, though they were a bit expensive for us. Elsie haggled fiercely, she did. Nearly caused a riot! Elsie always was a force of nature. She was. Wouldn’t take a penny less than she thought something was worth. Remember that time she tried to bargain for a cushion in Scarborough? I think I've heard that story, Anon. Something about a seagull and a very stubborn shopkeeper? You have a good memory. Anyway, Grandad, Venice… what else did you see? Did you get to try any good food? Oh, the food! Wonderful. We had this one pasta dish... I can’t remember the name of it now… it was creamy, with mushrooms and… oh, I can almost taste it. Elsie loved it. She always said Italian food was the only thing that could tempt her away from a good Lancashire hotpot. I’m a big fan of a good risotto myself. Have you ever tried acorn risotto, Anon? It's surprisingly good. No, I haven’t. It sounds... adventurous. I’m more of a pizza girl myself. Although, I did have this incredible carbonara in Rome last year. Rich as you like. Rome, eh? You went to Rome? Did you go to the Colosseum? Absolutely. Took loads of photos. It was amazing to think all the history that happened there. I’ve always wanted to go to Rome. Elsie and I talked about it for years, but it never happened. Budget always got us, I suppose. And then… well, then life took over. It's never too late, Grandad! There are some great deals to be had if you look. Maybe if you fancy a trip, we could help you plan it? That’s kind of you, lad. But I'm old now. My travelling days are behind me. I’m quite happy reminiscing about the ones I  did  have, you know? Besides, who'd look after Elsie’s prize-winning geraniums?

Right, so I was thinking about the Semiotics module... that bit on Barthes. Do you reckon we push the Saussure connection a bit more this year? I felt last time the students just glazed over. Hmm, yeah, you're probably right. I think they need a bit more grounding, a tangible example. Maybe we could use that advert campaign, the one for the green tea? It’s got some really interesting signifier/signified relationships. Oh, brilliant! That’s much better than the Dior perfume ad we were considering. Too abstract. Green tea feels relatable, doesn't it? Plus, the colour psychology is pretty blatant. Exactly. And we could tie it into the discussion of cultural context, the whole idea of East meets West. It's visually striking, and easy to deconstruct. Absolutely. Okay, I'll rework the slides then. I was also thinking, should we incorporate more of the Chinese perspective on semiotics? I read a really interesting article… About? Professor Lai's work on  gui , the concept of ‘spirit’ and how it applies to visual symbolism in traditional art. It's fascinating. Might be a bit niche, but… I think it’s worth a shot. It’s important to show them there's more than just Western interpretations. But we need to make sure we present it sensitively, explain the cultural nuances properly. Agreed. I'll add a section on it, with a few translated excerpts. What about the practical element? Last year’s film analysis felt a bit underwhelming. I know, didn't it? We need something with more bite. I was thinking maybe Hayao Miyazaki’s  Spirited Away . The symbolism is just bursting out of it. Oh, perfect! That’s a brilliant choice. Visually stunning, complex themes… it's basically a semiotic playground. Exactly! And most of them will have seen it anyway. Okay, so  Spirited Away  it is. Right, speaking of stunning visuals… I’m starving. How’s the mapo tofu coming along? It's simmering away nicely actually. I added a little extra chilli oil. Hoping to brave it tonight. Brave it? You’re a fire-breather! I thought you enjoyed it. Well, enjoyed is a strong word. Survived, perhaps. Are you watching that new Korean drama everyone's talking about?  Kingdom ? Yeah, got to two episodes so far. Pretty gripping, isn't it? The cinematography is incredible. And the zombies... cleverly integrated into the political intrigue.

This coffee's a bit weak today, isn't it? I think I need to descalcify the machine again. Honestly, it's a constant battle. It’s fine, Mum. Maybe you’re just not as awake yet. I'll have another cup, though. How are things going with getting quotes for the move? Oh, it’s appalling. Absolutely appalling. I’ve had two so far, and they’re both…well, astronomical. One wanted nearly seven thousand pounds just to move everything! Seven thousand! Seven thousand? Blimey. For what, a mansion? No! A three-bedroom bungalow! And then they wanted another thousand to store some of the furniture while we sort out the new place. It’s extortionate, I tell you. You could look at self-storage too, Mum. It might be a bit cheaper. There's that Safestore place in Penrith. I looked at that, love. They’re not much better, really. And then you've got the hassle of hiring a van and doing it yourself. My back wouldn’t thank me for that. You should get a few more quotes, though. Don't settle on the first two. There's always someone willing to undercut. I know, I know. It’s just…it’s all so stressful. And on top of everything else, have you been listening to the news? This whole Labour leadership thing is a mess. It is a bit chaotic, isn’t it? I was hoping for a bit more unity. It's all about the factions, isn't it? Everyone vying for power. The idealism has gone right out of politics. Remember when people actually believed they could make a difference? Oh, I do. When I was younger, I was convinced we could change the world. I joined the Young Socialists, you know. Handed out leaflets…thought we were going to usher in a socialist utopia. A socialist utopia! I know, I know! It’s naive now, looking back. But I genuinely believed it then. It's always been that way, hasn't it? People have grand ideas, but the reality is always a bit…murkier. The oil industry was like that too, you know. All this talk of energy security and independence…behind the scenes, it’s all about profits. I guess every sector has its downsides. So, about this move… are you thinking about selling some of the furniture, then? To save on storage costs?

So, I was thinking about what you said earlier about needing pseudonyms for uni… I'm feeling really Rhys. Like, just Rhys. No surname drama. Rhys! That’s so… understated for you, Leo. But I dig it. I'm sticking with Juniper though, feels right, you know? People in the bakery know me as June, it’s manageable. I’m still Hazel. It suits me. Seriously though, speaking of names...did you guys know the River Lea runs right through East London? It’s wild. Crikey, no way! I've just been wandering around, taking in the sights. Didn't realize there was a river even  here . More like a canal, right? Yeah, canals mostly. Remember that boat trip Liam dragged us on last summer? Absolute disaster. Oh god, that was awful. We ended up stuck in that little lock for ages. And then someone started explaining the kosher laws about fish... Don't remind me. It felt like a religious lecture on a canal boat. Not exactly the vibe. Want some more pasta? Seriously, this is amazing. Yeah, this is grouse. Thanks, Maya. Best carbonara I've had in ages, even better than back home. Though, I reckon a bit more chilli flakes wouldn't go amiss. Need a better condiment game, eh? I completely agree! And a proper squeeze of lemon wouldn’t kill anyone. Honestly, some Italian restaurants in London are criminal when it comes to final flourishes. Speaking of criminal… I tried heating up leftovers in the microwave last night and nearly burned the flat down. Leo! Seriously? What were you doing? Just reheating pasta. It somehow exploded. Literally exploded. Tomato sauce everywhere. Sounds like a scene from a sitcom. Microwaves, man. They’re dangerous. Give me a proper oven any day. You're telling me! They’re terrible for delicate baking too. I swear my sourdough starter judges me when I even  look  at a microwave. True. I stick to the Aga. It’s slower, but the results are always worth it. So, anyone thinking of hitting up a club tonight? There’s that new place, 'Pulse', in Shoreditch... apparently good music. Pulse? I've heard of it. Not sure. I'm still recovering from that near-microwave explosion. I’m up for it. As long as it’s not too ridiculously crowded. I don’t want to lose anyone in a sea of sweaty limbs.

Honestly, Tinder's a nightmare right now. It’s just…blurry pictures of lads in gyms or holding fish. Like, is that supposed to impress me? Tell me about it! I swiped right on one the other day, thinking he was, you know, vaguely decent, and then his bio was literally just, "Gym. Grub. Gains." I nearly spat out my coffee. Oh my god, that’s awful! It’s the same with everyone in Derby, honestly. Pictures of them flexing in the mirror. Where’s the personality? It’s mental. I keep seeing the same faces popping up, too. It’s like a revolving door of beige blokes. I saw a guy the other day who’d just photoshopped himself onto a picture of a boat. Like, he was standing awkwardly next to a captain. What was  that  about? Oh god, don't even. I had one who kept sending me messages about horses. Like, I mentioned I liked countryside walks  once ! Now I’m apparently a professional equestrian. The commitment! It’s relentless. I’m starting to feel anxious just looking at the app. Same. I deleted it for a week, and felt so much better. Then I reinstall it, convinced ‘this time will be different’. Spoiler alert: it never is. Maybe we should all just give up and commit to a life of cats and Netflix? Tempting. Seriously tempting. It would be less stressful than trying to decipher a gym selfie. Speaking of stressful… how’s it going with Liam and the housemates? Are they still leaving dirty dishes piled up in the sink? Ugh, don’t even get me started. It's a biohazard zone in there. I swear, I’m going to start charging them a cleaning fee. He says he’ll put them in the dishwasher… eventually. Classic bloke move. “I'll do it later.” Later never comes. Has anyone seen Chloe lately? She disappeared after that lecture on Victorian poetry. I think she said she was going to the library. Probably hiding from reality. She needs a Tinder break too, honestly. The girl’s a magnet for drama. Honestly, uni life is chaotic, isn't it? Between lectures, coursework, and dodging dodgy Tinder profiles... Tell me about it. I’m drowning in essays. I need a serious dose of chocolate and a nap. You know what we need? We need to go out tonight. Get some fresh air, forget about lads and assignments, and just have a laugh.

Honestly, the way they're going on about benefits now… it’s a disgrace. Absolutely disgraceful. Aye, it is that. Seems like everyone’s after a handout these days. Back in my day... Back in  your  day, Arthur, you could buy a loaf of bread for tuppence! Things were different. Well, aye, they were. Hard work was the name of the game. Nobody expected anything for nothing. Now… Exactly. They’re talking about cutting Universal Credit again. As if people aren’t struggling enough as it is. And the cost of living, don’t even get me started. It's dreadful, isn't it? I was just reading about the energy prices going up again. How are pensioners supposed to cope? Especially with the winter coming. They should get them down. Simple as that. Put a cap on it. Where's the sense in it all. That’s what I keep saying, but it’s all greed, isn’t it? The energy companies laughing all the way to the bank while people freeze. And Parliament… don’t even get me started on Parliament. All squabbling and pointing fingers. Nothing gets done. It's a joke, the whole lot of them. No sense of decency. And this new Prime Minister... I’m not convinced, I really am. He’s a bit posh, isn't he? Always sounding like he’s reading from a script. He seems alright. A bit stiff, maybe, but I'm willing to give him a chance. We need someone stable. Stable? After what we’ve been through? We need someone who understands ordinary people. Someone who’s been through the mill. He went to Eton, didn't he? Eton. Always a bad sign. Well, plenty of clever people go to Eton. It’s not always a bad thing. Cleverness doesn’t equate to common sense, Doris. Believe me, I worked with some very clever people who couldn’t tie their own shoelaces. That’s right! Educated, but useless. So, what are you both watching on the telly these days? Anything good? I've been enjoying that new police drama, "The Shadow Syndicate." Quite gripping. I still like my Antiques Roadshow. Always a bit of a surprise what they find. Oh, Antiques Roadshow is lovely! I also enjoy that gardening programme, "Gardeners’ World." Monty Don is a gem. I can’t stand those gardening programmes. Too much greenery. Give me a good crime thriller any day.

That lentil shepherd’s pie was lovely, really. Didn’t think it would be quite so good with the sweet potato topping. Glad you enjoyed it. Bit more effort than the usual pasta, eh? Working late tonight wasn't helping the dinner plan, though. Needed something quick. No, it was perfect. Just what I needed after that… debacle at the garden club today. Oh? What happened at the garden club? Don’t tell me Mrs. Higgins had another hissy fit about the rose pruning. Worse, actually. Apparently, Bernard’s prize-winning marrows have been… assaulted. Assaulted? You mean like… stolen? Not stolen. Massively nibbled. They reckon it was a badger. A very determined badger. A badger with a penchant for marrows. Honestly. Bernard will be incandescent. He is. He’s already drafting a strongly worded letter to the local council about badger control. Let him. He enjoys a good rant. How was your day otherwise? Did you manage to finish that report for the council? Almost. I got bogged down in the third section. The funding implications are just a nightmare. They want everything for nothing, as usual. They always do. Did you try the ‘justification’ approach again? The one where you show them precisely why cutting that resource would be detrimental? I did, but they just gave me that blank stare. Like I was speaking Martian. I think I'm going to have to pull out all the stops and appeal to their common sense. Wish me luck. You’ll need it. What about the kids? How were they? Liam’s still glued to that new series on Netflix, ‘Galactic Gladiators’. Any excuse to be on his Xbox, isn't there? Sounds… stimulating. And Chloe? Chloe’s being Chloe. Spent the afternoon trying to convince me that she  needs  a neon pink keyboard. Says it’s essential for her coding projects. Essential. Right. Well, a pink keyboard isn't exactly going to break the bank, is it? Perhaps a compromise is in order? I’m thinking. Might threaten to hide the Xbox if she doesn’t at least acknowledge the potential benefit of a black one. Harsh. Very harsh. Did you see anything good on the telly tonight? We missed it. I was wrestling with the council report and you were saving the world, one donation at a time. Somebody has to pay for Liam’s Galactic Gladiators habit. Seriously though, I’m hoping that charity auction goes well.

Honestly, this weather is dreadful. I’m glad you’re not flying in today, it’s pouring down. Absolutely relentless. Aye, it’s been chucking it down back home too. Proper Lancashire weather. Makes you want to curl up with a cup of tea, doesn't it? It absolutely does. Though I'm not sure curling up with a cup of tea is going to cure this wretched cough of mine. It’s been dragging on for weeks. Oh no, how awful. You should really see someone. Have you got any appointments with the doctor? Tried, darling. The Polish healthcare system... well, let's just say it’s a bit of a process. It’s why I’m just soldiering on with honey and lemon. Fair enough. You look a bit peaky, to be honest. Terrible timing with the funeral. I know, isn't it? Mum would have hated me being so far away, but… well, it’s just how it is, I suppose. At least I’m going back. It will be good to see everyone, even if it's under sad circumstances. It will. And it’s a chance to recharge, isn’t it? Get some proper comfort food and northern banter. Exactly! Though I do miss the simple things. Honestly, just having a proper Sunday roast… I’d kill for a proper Sunday roast. I know what you mean. I ended up making one last weekend, just for myself. Trying to recreate my mum’s recipe. It was… passable. Not quite as good, mind. They never are. Anyway, did you see what Emily posted on Instagram? That picture of her and Liam in Barcelona? Oh yeah! They look like they’re having the time of their lives. Wonder when they’re going to get around to settling down somewhere. I wouldn’t rush them. I've been thinking a lot about settling down myself lately. About where I actually  belong,  you know? Funny how being so far from home makes you consider it more. It does, doesn't it? I keep having these thoughts about moving back to Bury, but then… I don’t know. Do I really want to go back to that routine? It feels like so long ago since I left. Honestly, it does. Sometimes, I feel like I haven't really lived since I left Cambridge. This... life... it’s just… existing, I guess.

This Earl Grey is genuinely lovely, you know? I didn't expect a pub to do a decent cuppa. It is good! Way better than the instant stuff I usually resort to at uni. Speaking of which, how's the copywriting going? Still battling rogue commas and existential dread? You know it. Actually, things are pretty hectic at the moment. A big client just landed, needing a bunch of social media copy and some website rewrites. It’s exciting, but also a lot. I’m fuelled entirely by caffeine and sheer willpower. Sounds intense! Is it fun, though? Like, are you actually enjoying the work? Mostly. There are definitely days when I question every life choice, but yeah, when you nail a piece of copy that  really  resonates? It's brilliant. Especially when the client is happy. Makes all the commas worth it. What about you? Still juggling uni and the survey programming? Yep, the eternal balancing act. The programming is actually pretty good, surprisingly. It’s really analytical and I’m finding I quite enjoy the logical problem-solving. Better than essay writing, that’s for sure. Always good to find something you enjoy! Are you still seeing Daniel? We are! He’s… good. It's complicated, you know? He’s busy with his med school stuff, and I’m swamped. We’re trying to make it work. It sounds tough. Just remember to look after yourself, yeah? Don’t let things fall by the wayside. I know, I know. Easier said than done. I’ve got that birthday dinner to plan for Mum next month, too. Feeling a bit overwhelmed already. Any brilliant restaurant ideas? Somewhere a little bit special. Ooh, have you been to that Italian place near Covent Garden? “Bella Notte.” It’s always packed, but the food's incredible. Really authentic. I’ve heard of it! Maybe we should check it out. Are you hungry? We could grab some crisps or something. They've got a decent selection here. Actually, yeah! A packet of prawn cocktail sounds amazing right now. And maybe a little chocolate biscuit. It’s been a long day. Sorted. Prawn cocktail and chocolate biscuits it is. You deserve it. You've been working so hard. You too! These essays can't write themselves.Definitely should check out "Bella Notte” for mom’s birthday! Definitely! I'll book it soon! Do you want a biscuit?

Honestly, I was so startled awake this morning! Cade practically launched himself onto my face. I just wanted cuddles! I was dreaming about dinosaurs. Big ones. Dinosaurs, huh? Well, hopefully they weren't roaring in your ears too much. Did you both sleep okay, apart from the dinosaur attack? Yeah, it was good. Ms. Eleanor sung me to sleep. Oh, good. That’s lovely. Right, so plans for today… Helena’s got that Neon Moon thing in the afternoon, right? Yes! I like the music very nice dress. You look all lovely. We should leave around three, give you both time to get ready. Cade, are you still excited about the circus skills workshop? Yeah! Juggling. Juggling, that’s the one. And tightrope walking, maybe? Although I think that might be a bit ambitious for you. I can do it! We’ll see. Want some breakfast? What are you fancying? Pancakes! Porridge. Okay, porridge for you, pancakes for you. Trying to convince you both to eat something healthy. But pancakes are healthy. They absolutely are not! Right, let’s get this breakfast sorted then. Have you heard Cade, your auntie Sarah is learning some Australian phrases? What phrases? Apparently, she’s trying to learn how to say "G’day” and “No worries.” G’day! Yes, G'day. Sounds silly, doesn't it? No worries. Exactly! See? You’re already an expert. Right, before Helena comes back, we need to sort out the living room. It looks like a bomb's hit it. I made a fort! I can see that! A very impressive fort. Just tidy it up a little bit, okay? We want the living room to be nice for Neon Moon. She's excited about sharing that. Can I put the dinosaur in the fort? Absolutely. The dinosaur can definitely have a place in the fort. Now, pancakes or porridge? Which are you choosing first? Pancakes! Porridge first. Dinosaurs need energy. Dinosaurs definitely do need energy. Alright then, let's get fueling up! And Cadet, try not to launch yourself at me again this morning, okay? Okay Mummy. . Hope this fits the prompt well! Let me know if you'd like any adjustments. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .H.H..

Honestly, I can’t believe the latest developments with that energy bill proposal. It’s utter chaos. Do you think they’ll actually push it through, David? Ach, who knows, Eleanor? Westminster’s a kettle of fish these days, isn't it? You never know what’ll boil over. It’s all just posturing, most of it, I reckon. A lot of smoke and mirrors. The real work happens behind closed doors, as always. It feels pretty serious to me, Dad. Loads of people I know are really worried about how they’ll pay their bills this winter. And the MPs seem to be arguing about everything except actually, you know,  helping  people. Exactly, Rhys! It's infuriating. They’re so caught up in their own petty squabbles they've forgotten who they're supposed to represent. Remember when your great-grandfather used to rant about the miners' strikes? Same energy, different issue. Aye, I remember. Old Dai would have a right go at the Tories even back then. Said they were playing games with people's livelihoods. Fierce man, your great-grandfather. Had a fire in his belly, he did. Reminded me a bit of… well, me, when I was younger. You and fiery arguments. A potent combination, David. But he wasn’t wrong, was he? The way politicians treat ordinary people… it can feel so disconnected. Speaking of which, your Aunt Bronwen was telling me the other day she's thinking of starting a petition… something about local services being cut. Wow, that’s cool. What services? Oh, you know Bronwen. Probably the library or the swimming pool. Always fighting the good fight, that one. Comes from a long line of strong women, that family. Your great-great-grandmother, Megan, she was a real force. Ran the village shop single-handedly after your great-grandfather… well, after he went to work in the mines. Absolutely. And she was apparently legendary for her headstrong nature. Remember Aunty Meriel saying how she once stood up to the landlord and ended up getting the rent reduced? Really? She did? Aye, she did. A clever woman with a sharp wit. You have her in you, Rhys, you know. You just need to find your voice. Driving’s alright so far. Traffic's surprisingly light. Good. Because I'm starting to feel a bit twitchy about this political stuff. It’s exhausting, isn’t it?

Right, so, the dragons… where were we with the dragons? Finn, did you want to tell me what happened next? The dragon… he got stuck! He got stuck? Where did he get stuck, love? In a… a big hole! A muddy hole! And he tried to get out, but he couldn't! That’s brilliant! You're both so imaginative. So, the dragon got stuck in a muddy hole. What did he do then? He… he called for help! He called for help! Good thinking. And who did he call? Princess Poppy! Princess Poppy came to rescue the dragon? That's wonderful! You know, stories are a bit like that too, aren't they? They often have characters who call for help when they're in trouble. Like Helen Moss stories? Exactly like Helen Moss stories! Remember how in  The Grumpy Knight , he needed help sorting out his grumpy mood? Yes. With the rainbow. That’s right! The rainbow helped him. It’s the same idea. Sometimes, in stories, characters need a little bit of help to solve their problems. Sometimes they have to be brave, too, like the dragon. Even though he was stuck, he still called for help instead of just panicking. Did Princess Poppy pull him out? That’s a clever question! Let's decide together. How  should  Princess Poppy help him? Should she pull him out with a rope? No! She should… she should sing a song! A happy song! A happy song to make the mud loosen? That's a fantastic idea! You’re both so creative. See, that’s how stories grow. It’s all about trying different things and seeing what works best. Are we going to go to the Linton Book Festival? We are! Remember? We booked our tickets ages ago. We can go and hear authors telling stories, and maybe even meet some of them! Will they tell Helen Moss stories? I don't know yet, darling, but it would be amazing if they did, wouldn’t it? Maybe we can ask! But for now, let's finish our dragon's story. So, Princess Poppy sang a happy song, and the mud… …Was all wobbly! Absolutely! The mud was all wobbly, and the dragon popped right out! All shiny and clean! The end! What do you think? Speaker_3 & 2: The end! Wonderful. Now, who wants some biscuits? And then maybe we can draw pictures of our dragon?

Right, so I’m thinking lentil shepherd’s pie tonight. Bit healthier than last time. Sounds good! Definitely need more greens in our lives. I feel like I’m surviving on instant noodles and anxieties. Anxieties are a food group, Elara. Don’t deny yourself. Very funny, Rhys. Seriously though, I’ve been thinking about going vegetarian properly. Really? Like, committed vegan? Not quite vegan yet. I mean, I  get  the arguments. Animal cruelty, the whole environmental impact…but cheese. And bacon. I’m not ready to say goodbye to bacon. Fair enough. But have you looked into the cultured meat side of things? The shmeat? Oh, you mean lab-grown meat? It’s wild. Progress is being made, apparently. I read something about it being closer than we think. I’ve seen a bit about it. It just feels… weird, doesn’t it? Like, Frankenstein’s monster in a petri dish. I know, but think about it - no more factory farming, no more slaughterhouses...it could be a massive step towards a more ethical and sustainable food system. It’s still reliant on technology, though, isn’t it? Requires massive amounts of energy to run those labs. Is it  really  that much better? Good point. Still, I'm trying to cut down. I did get some Vitamin B12 supplements, though. You know, just in case I have a final bacon wobble. Smart move. I'm taking a multivitamin too. The pharmacist was saying everyone needs more Vitamin D, especially in London. Gloomy city, you know? I’m just thinking about how fundamentally messed up it is, even with the abattoirs. You’ve got these animals, bred to be as big as possible, pumped full of hormones, then effectively tortured before…you know. Hunting is even worse, though. At least with abattoirs, there’s  some  attempt to make it quick…although I’m sure the reality is often far from it. Hunting is just… a sport. Pure vanity. People pretending they're some kind of primal hunter-gatherer. It's disgusting. Like, you can just buy meat. Exactly! It’s just another form of oppression, really, isn't it? Domination over another living being. Makes you think about humans oppressing humans too, you know? Whoa, deep thoughts over lentils. Is this the calm before a rant, Rhys? Maybe. It's just been on my mind. Speaking of rants, have you seen the latest Curb Your Enthusiasm?

Right, who’s doing the washing up tonight then? It’s a mountain. And honestly, this new washing machine is a nightmare. It’s taking twice as long as the old one. Always the same, isn't it? The new ones are never as good. I swear, they make them deliberately inefficient. Your daughter did mention something about it the other day, didn’t she? Something about sensor issues? Yeah, Dad. It keeps saying it needs to re-wash things even when they're perfectly clean. It's bizarre. I think it’s a fault, really. I’ll have a word with the repair guy, I suppose. Although, the amount of stuff we go through… it’s ridiculous. We need to throw some things away. I’ve been eyeing up that box of Christmas decorations in the loft for weeks. Seriously, nobody uses those reindeer antlers anymore. Leave the reindeer antlers! Your niece, Bethany, she adores them. Insists on wearing them every Christmas morning. You remember, the year she tripped over the Christmas tree wearing them? Oh, goodness, yes! She nearly took the whole tree down with her! Such a little menace, that girl. Speaking of menace, has anyone seen the cat? I swore I heard him yowling earlier. Probably after his dinner. He’s been particularly demanding lately. Remember when Grandma got him those fancy salmon treats? He wouldn’t touch anything else for a week. Oh, that’s right! She spoiled him rotten. Honestly, sometimes I think the cat has more expensive taste than we do. Speaking of expensive, are we doing anything special for New Year’s Eve this year? Sarah’s been asking about it. I was thinking a quiet night in, maybe watch some old movies? After all the Christmas chaos, a bit of peace and quiet would be welcome. That sounds… a bit boring, Dad. We could have a party! Invite some friends. We could even have a theme – 80s or something. Oh, heavens, no. I'm not coordinating an 80s party. My knees wouldn’t cope with the dancing! But maybe a smaller gathering. Just close friends, a nice dinner, and a bit of fizz. Fizz it is. Though, speaking of fizz, I saw an article online the other day about how Italians have completely different words for bubbles in prosecco and champagne. Apparently, it's all about the size and texture. Wow, really?

Right, so, who's got the butterfly forks? I distinctly remember putting them away after Aunt Susan's birthday. They’re in the drawer, Mum. The one you always look in first. Honestly! Why do you always say that? I'm organised! Just because I make sure everything has a specific place… Can we just eat, please? I'm starving. Alright, alright. Two minutes silence for Remembrance Day. We should honour that, even though it's not the 11th. It felt…appropriate, today. Yeah, it was pretty quiet in school. Everyone just stood there. A bit awkward, actually. It was sad. For all those people. It is. And it’s not just about the past, you know. It's a reminder that conflict continues. Have you both been following what’s happening in Russia? It's horrifying, isn’t it? A bit. My history teacher's been going on about it. It's complicated, apparently. It's not complicated! They're invading people’s homes. It’s far more complex than that, darling, but you're absolutely right, at its core, it's an act of aggression. And the misinformation…it's everywhere. Speaking of complicated, whose birthday is next week? I need to start thinking about presents. Grandpa’s. Fifty-five, right? Is it his big one? No, sixty. Big one. Sixty! Can you believe it? He's still going strong. I was telling him the other day how I remember him teaching us to fish when we were little - he'd stand there laughing as we tangled the line. I remember that! He always let me use his favourite rod, even though I kept dropping it in the water. He always bought us the biggest ice creams ever too. Mr. Whippy with everything on. Those were good times. I should get him something… practical. He doesn’t really want anything flashy. Maybe a new fly-fishing kit? Or a really good pair of wellies. He’s always complaining about his. Good ideas! I’ll have a look online. It feels ridiculous, doesn't it, when you think about all the horrible things that are happening in the world to be thinking about wellies. So, you’re definitely getting him something practical then? No butterfly forks? Absolutely no butterfly forks for Grandpa. He hates that sort of thing. Are you both finished? I’ll clear up. Nearly. Another chip, please.

Right, so Cornwall it is then? Are we all agreed? Cornwall! Yes! Can we see the sea? Pirates! Can we see pirates? Maybe not actual pirates, darling, but we’ll definitely see the sea. Big waves! We can build sandcastles and look for shells. And ice cream! Can I have a big ice cream? Of course you can, sweetheart. As much ice cream as you like. Though, remember we need to be careful because your tummy isn’t happy with chocolate, is it? No. Makes me rumble. Rumble! Exactly. So maybe strawberry or vanilla this time, eh? Okay. Strawberry sounds good. Can we go to Adventure Island too? Adventure Island? When we're in Cornwall, sweetie? There isn’t an Adventure Island in Cornwall. But... there’s Adventure Island books! We read them! Remember? Knight’s adventure! Yes, I remember. Those are brilliant stories, aren’t they? But those are stories we read  before  we go on holiday. Real adventures happen in real places. Cornwall is a real adventure - exploring caves, rock pooling… Caves! Dark! Don’t worry, love, we’ll have torches! We'll be like proper explorers. We should probably book somewhere soon, shouldn’t we? Somewhere with a good view. A view  of  the sea! Absolutely. I was thinking about that little cottage near Padstow, remember? The one with the garden? Garden! Bugs! Maybe a few bugs, but lots of flowers too. And space for running around. I’ve been meaning to look at some V&A exhibitions before we go too…perhaps one on landscapes? Would you two be interested? Is there ice cream at the V&A? I’m not sure, darling. But we can look! It'll be a bit quieter than the beach. Quiet? Boring! It won't be boring! It'll be full of beautiful things. It'll inspire us for when we build our sandcastles. Speaking of which, I've got a huge pile of exam marking to get through this week. Need to finish that before we can truly relax and dream of Cornwall. You work too much, Mummy. I do, don't I? But then we get to go on lovely holidays! Now, who wants a banana? And we’ll have a look at those cottages online, shall we? Let’s find the one with the best sea view. Sea! Banana! Yes! Okay, you two, settle down and let’s have a look…and then we can plan all the pirate adventures you want.

Man, Mr. Davies is brutal today, wasn't he? Seriously! Like, double the homework in history. What’s his problem? I think he's just annoyed about that thing that happened in the science lab last week. Did you hear about Liam? Yeah, exploding the baking soda volcano. Classic Liam, though. Always gotta push it too far. Exactly! But Mr. Davies was pretty cross. Ms. Patel said he wasn’t impressed. Nah, well he deserves it. He's being dramatic. Anyway, did you finish that English coursework? I'm stuck on the analysis part. Nearly. I just need to add a paragraph about symbolism. It's a pain, isn't it? This whole thing’s a pain. Tell me about it. I’d rather be out biking. Did you see the new BMX track they're building down near Salt Hill Park? No way! Seriously? I need to go there. My bike's been gathering dust. Should we go this weekend? Yeah, definitely. Unless Zara's party is still on. Oh yeah, Zara’s party. Do you think it’ll be any good? Last one was a bit lame, remember? I heard it's gonna be at her aunt's place this time. Apparently, better music. Plus, Chloe’s going to be there. Chloe? Oh, well that makes it worthwhile then. Speaking of which, did you see her talking to those prefects during break? Yeah, something about a complaint, I think. Something about Ethan being a menace in the corridor? He  is  a menace. Always shoving people. Remember when he knocked over Mr. Henderson’s coffee? Oh man, priceless! But the look on Mr. Henderson’s face... Worth it, though, right? Definitely. Anyway, my throat’s itching a bit. Probably just allergies. It flares up this time of year. Yeah, loads of people at school are complaining about it. Remember when you had that allergic reaction to the peanuts in the canteen last year? Don't remind me! I swelled up like a balloon. They had to call my mum. So embarrassing. It was pretty funny, though, in retrospect. Don't tell anyone I said that. Actually, what did Mrs. Davies say about you being on the school council? She said she’d think about it. So, don’t hold your breath. She's a bit of a stickler for rules, isn’t she? Definitely. Well, whatever. At least we don’t have to go back tomorrow.

Honestly, this road is mental. I’m surprised we haven’t had to slam on. It's like a slalom course out here. It is a bit rough, isn’t it? Could do with some resurfacing. Though, at least it's not the M6. Remember that stretch near Rugby? Absolute nightmare. Don’t remind me. I swear, my suspension was still vibrating a week later. You'd think with your fancy engineering job, you’d be designing smoother roads. If only. I mostly deal with bridges, really. Not a lot of road surface work in that. Though, materials science is something I dabble in… there’s a lot of interesting research into self-healing asphalt now. Self-healing? Seriously? Now  that's  something worth engineering. Imagine, potholes just… disappearing. Exactly. It's still in the relatively early stages, but the potential is huge. Less disruption, less maintenance… Sounds amazing. Speaking of disruption, did you catch any of the cricket yesterday? That rain was a killer. A bit. Just the highlights, really. Bit disappointing to see the game cut short like that. Bazball’s always a bit of a gamble against conditions like that, isn’t it? Definitely. They tried to be too aggressive. Still, it's exciting to watch, even when they lose. Makes you wish you'd paid attention more in PE, eh? Well, you always preferred the bikes, didn’t you? Remember that time you nearly took out Mrs. Henderson's prize-winning petunias? Don't! That was mortifying! I swear, she looked like she was going to have a heart attack. I offered to pay for them, but she just shook her head and muttered something about "reckless youth." She was always a bit fierce, wasn't she? Still, you were pretty good on that old Raleigh blazer. You could outpace me any day. That's because you were always fiddling with your gears! I just pedaled. Simple and effective. Sometimes the best way is the easiest. True enough. You know, I’ve been thinking of getting a proper touring bike. Something sturdy, that can handle some rough terrain. Any recommendations? Oh, absolutely. You should check out the Ridgebacks. Solid as a rock, reliable, and they’ve got pretty good customer service. I've heard good things. Ridgebacks, got it. I’ll have a look online. Maybe we could go for a ride together sometime, once I’ve got one sorted?

Right, so I’ve got the app open. Any preferences? We’re ordering Chinese tonight, yeah? Yeah! Definitely. I'm starving. What are you thinking? Usual suspects? Ooh, yes! But maybe we could try something a  little  different this time? I’m getting a bit bored of the same old sweet and sour. Good point. Okay, let's have a proper look then. They’ve got loads on here. Kung Pao Chicken? Yeah, I like that. Solid choice. I’m really craving something a bit spicy, though. They do a Sichuan Mapo Tofu that looks amazing. Not the  usual  Chinese menu fare. Mapo Tofu… never tried it. What is it? Basically, it's tofu in a fiery, savoury sauce with ground pork. It's seriously good. Proper, proper flavour. Sounds intense. I’m not sure I’m brave enough after that curry I had last week... still regretting that. You ordered Vindaloo! You  knew  what you were doing. Okay, let's do the Kung Pao Chicken then? And maybe the Mapo Tofu for you, Jess? Perfect! And some egg fried rice. Obviously. And I’ll go for a portion of those crispy chilli beef thingies. Always a winner. Right. Noodles or rice? Rice for me, definitely. Noodles always clump up. I’m having rice too, actually. Seems more appropriate with the tofu. Okay. What about starters? Spring rolls? Yeah, spring rolls are good. But let’s get some those little pork dumplings too, the ones with the dipping sauce. Oh, YES! Those are incredible. Worth every penny. Right, dumplings and spring rolls. And… … they've got those giant prawn crackers. Those are always fun to share. Oh yeah! Gotta have the prawn crackers. Adding those to the basket. This is making me so hungry I could eat a horse. Nearly there... Just need to check if they’re doing any deals. Oh, they’ve got a set menu with a main, side, and starter for £25. Actually, that’s a pretty good deal. Let’s do that! Saves us having to think too much. Yeah, sounds easy. What does the set menu include? It’s Kung Pao Chicken, egg fried rice, spring rolls, and…a random selection of vegetables. Random selection of vegetables? What does that even  mean ? I have no idea. Possibly broccoli. Possibly soggy beans. Who knows? Don't worry, the rest looks good enough to compensate.

So, the new initiative at the uni... it's quite ambitious, really. They want us to incorporate more real-world scenarios into the curriculum. Apparently, it's supposed to make the students more employable. Sounds good in theory, doesn’t it? What does that actually  mean , though? More case studies, I imagine? Precisely. I’ve been trying to think of ways to bring Shakespeare into it. It's trickier than you'd think to make Hamlet relevant to a graduate job hunt. Tell me about it. Trying to explain to a patient why understanding iambic pentameter might help them cope with arthritis is… a challenge. The NHS has enough on its plate without requiring a side of Elizabethan verse. Exactly! And you’re on the front line. You hear it all, I imagine. Things are getting tougher there, aren't they? Tough doesn't even cover it. Staff shortages are horrendous. We’re relying on agency nurses constantly, and the workload… Honestly, I came home the other day and just collapsed on the sofa. Couldn't move for an hour. So, what about you? Any drama amongst the academics? Oh, a little bit. There’s a disagreement about the funding for the new translation project. Apparently, someone thinks it’s a waste of money. Honestly, the politics are just as bad, if not worse, than in the NHS, ironically. I can believe that. I read that article about the medical staff in Helsinki, their morale is really bottoming out. Amazing country, Finland though, isn't it? I’ve always wanted to go. It is. My sister went last year. Said the scenery was incredible, and the people were wonderfully polite. I've been meaning to visit but...well, you know. Work. Always work! Speaking of which, I need to vent for a moment. You wouldn't believe what’s been happening next door. Oh? Do tell. I need a distraction from university bureaucracy. This new family moved in – lovely looking couple, seemed really nice. But their teenager… the noise! It's constant. Bass booming through the walls, shouting, motorbikes at all hours. It’s driving me mad. That's awful! The noise levels around here can be a nightmare, can’t they? It's relentless. I tried to have a quiet word with them the other day, but the mum just shrugged and said something about 'letting him be a teenager'.

Dreadful rain we’re having, isn’t it, Arthur? Proper biblical stuff. Aye, lad, biblical. Remember ‘62? Now that was rain. Flooded the docks proper. Couldn't get a cat out o’ Liverpool. I’ve only heard stories about that, of course. Being here relatively… recently. Though I’ve seen my share of storms in Salzkotten. Nothing quite like this, though. This seems relentless. Relentless is right. Speaking of relentless, have you seen what they’re doing with welfare now? Cutbacks everywhere. Yes, I’ve read about the changes. A rather difficult situation for many, I imagine. It's disheartening to see people struggling. Difficult is an understatement. Used to be, people could rely on something. Now… well, a lot of folks are desperate. Seen a few younger lads hanging around, looking lost. Reminds me a bit of myself back in the day, if you know what I mean. Before me mum passed. I can appreciate that. Speaking of which, how’s your daughter, Mary? Last I heard she was doing well in Manchester? Mary’s alright. Works in a bakery, bless her. Long hours, though, and not much money. She sends the grand kids over most weekends. Keeps an old man like me going. You wouldn’t believe those little scallywags though, they're full of mischief. Nearly turned the place upside down last week with bubble solution. Sounds lovely. I’m glad to hear it. I’ve noticed an increase in police presence around here lately. Increased patrols, at least. Aye, they’re cracking down on the chaps sniffing about. Don’t want no trouble on our doorstep. Heard they caught a lad last Tuesday, trying to nick a van. Proper mess. It’s worrying. There's always a tension with immigration, isn’t there? People come here looking for a better life, and understandably so, but they need to integrate, to respect the rules. It’s a complicated thing, lad. Always has been. My dad, he worked down the docks with Irish lads back in the day. Hard graft, but they all got on. Different now, though. Too much… noise. Noise? Aye. Political noise. Everyone shouting, no one listening. Makes it hard to see what’s right and what’s wrong. Speaking of noise, you know that joke about the German tourist and the Scouse taxi driver…? I think I’m ready for a joke, Arthur. Please, enlighten me.

Okay, here's a conversation based on the provided context. I've aimed for a natural feel, keeping in mind the diverse backgrounds and occupations of the speakers.   Location:   Cambridge University Press Printing House, lunch break in the staff canteen.   Speakers:       Chloe :   From Sunderland, Corpus Administrator, Northeast dialect.     Eleanor :   From Aylesbury, Language Research Co-ordinator, Eastern English accent.     Maisie :   From Lincoln, Language Research Administrator. Standard English.     Ava :   From Pennsylvania , Senior ELT Research Manager. American-influenced accent.     Grace :   From Leeds, Publishing. Northern accent.        Ava:   …and honestly, the data from the Canadian corpus was just  wild . They use "okay" as an adverb! Like, "That was okay-ly good." Can you even imagine?   Chloe:   Nah, radgie! That's mental. Like, you'd get a right look if you said that back home. “Okay-ly good?” Who even  thinks  that?   Eleanor:   It’s fascinating though, isn't it? How language just… adapts. I was reading an article this morning about the resurgence of older vocabulary in online gaming communities – like “huzzah” and phrases like that.   Maisie:   It’s a reflection of identity, I think. People are consciously choosing to use language to signal belonging. It’s the same with slang, isn't it?   Grace:   Totally. I’m seeing so much creative slang popping up in author submissions. It’s a constant challenge to figure out how to represent it authentically without completely alienating a wider readership. People are always pushing to use language in new and interesting ways.   Chloe:   Aye, it's all right. But sometimes I think folks are just trying to be clever for the sake of it. Like, my mam keeps using these American phrases she gets from the telly. Drives me round the bend.   Eleanor:   My grandmother does that too! It’s the ultimate sign of aspiration, isn't it? Using a language perceived as "cooler" or "more sophisticated."   Ava:   I can relate to that. People here are constantly correcting my pronunciation – as if I can just  switch  my accent! Honestly, it's exhausting sometimes.   Maisie:   Don't let them get to you, Ava. Your accent adds character. It's part of what makes you, well,  you.    Grace:   Plus, you have a fascinating perspective on the way ELT materials are perceived across different cultures.   Chloe:   Speaking of different cultures… has anyone ever tried to explain the word “tea” to an American? It’s just… impossible.   Eleanor:   You’re very right. I attempted to once, and I ended up having to describe it as “a beverage...associated with a social ritual...involving biscuits.”

…and then the subtitles were completely wrong! Like, the actor was clearly saying one thing, and the subtitle said something entirely different. It was hilarious, but also incredibly frustrating. Oh, that’s classic. It's one of my biggest pet hates. You really lose the nuance, don't you? Especially with Italian films. They're so expressive, and then you've got these clunky translations… Exactly! It’s not just the literal translation, it’s the  feel  of the language. I’m trying to learn Italian, you know, really properly this time. Oh, that's brilliant! Still struggling with the subjunctive, I bet. Don't even get me started on the subjunctive! It's a minefield. I’m trying to just focus on conversational Italian at the moment. My tutor says immersion is the key. Right approach, I think. Though "immersion" in London is a bit… limited. Tell me about it. I did try to hang out in a little Italian café near Russell Square last week, but I mostly just ordered cappuccino and felt self-conscious. Sounds about right. I remember trying to order a beer in German once. My pronunciation was so bad, the waiter just looked at me like I was speaking Martian. Oh, I know that feeling! Remember that trip to Spain when we kept accidentally ordering snails instead of sausages? Don’t remind me! I’m still traumatised by those snails. The texture… ugh. Though, I have to say, the culture was amazing, that trip to Seville. The passion, the music... it’s something else, isn’t it? Absolutely. It’s funny, isn’t it, how differently people express themselves? I was reading an article about Japanese business culture the other day, and how indirect they are with feedback. It’s all about harmony and saving face. Yeah, I've come across that. It clashes a bit with the bluntness of British communication, doesn't it? Especially in academia… it can be brutal. Remember Professor Davies’ feedback last year? Don't. Just don't. I'm still recovering. It's why I'm considering teaching abroad actually. Somewhere a bit more… gentle. Maybe Italy? Now there’s a thought. You could be teaching Italian to bewildered tourists. Or to eager PhD students who are struggling with the subjunctive. You'd be a legend! We should grab coffee next week and you can tell me all about the current state of your Italian learning.

Right then, so the plumber’s coming on Thursday afternoon. Does that suit everyone? Thursday’s alright, yeah. Got football training, but that’s after. Thursday's fine with me, love. As long as he fixes that dripping tap, I'll be happy. Drove me mad last night, it did. Drip, drip, drip… kept me awake half the night. Everything drips these days. Doesn’t used to be like that in our day. Things were built to last. That’s what everyone says, Dad. Though I reckon a lot of that's just nostalgia. Nan, did you see that video of the cat playing the piano? It was hilarious! A cat playing the piano? Don't be daft. Cats play with balls of wool, not pianos. No, honestly! It was like, pressing the keys with its paws. Look, I’ll show you later. Speaking of silly things, I found a biscuit in the sofa cushions this morning. Honestly, who leaves biscuits in the sofa? Probably me. Always sneaking a biscuit when your mum isn’t looking. Dad! You’re supposed to be watching your sugar. A little biscuit never hurt anyone. Keeps the old ticker going, it does. You'll be needing a new ticker soon at the rate you’re going. Gran, remember that time you told me about the parrot that used to swear? Oh, Percy! Yes, indeed. Your grandfather got that bird from a sailor, you know. And it learned some choice phrases. The neighbours used to complain something dreadful. I can imagine! Granddad never did know what to do with it. I tried to teach it to say 'Good morning', but it just kept squawking "Blast and bother!" That’s brilliant! Did Granddad ever get it to stop swearing? No dear, never. He eventually had to put it in a different room, just to save everyone's ears. Right, well, the dryer’s gone on again. I think I need to have a word with that repair man too. Always breaking down. Can I get a lemon with tea later, Mum? Of course, love. Nan, Dad, would you like a biscuit? I've got ginger ones today. Ginger ones? Don't mind if I do. As long as they’re not too gingery! I’ll have one, love. And a cup of strong tea to go with it. Then I can tell another story about Percy the parrot.

Look at this one! Remember Sarah’s stag do? That was… a lot. A lot is an understatement. Did you see the sheer terror in the photographer’s eyes? He clearly regretted taking the job. He did! And poor Liam, dressed as a giant banana. He looked genuinely miserable. Though, I have to admit, the inflatable dinosaur was a stroke of genius. Absolutely. Best stag do ever. Are you going to put these on the photo album or just keep them on the phone? I was thinking album. It feels a bit special, doesn’t it? A record of all our ridiculous friends. Definitely. We should get those prints sorted, the ones from our trip to Yunnan. They're just sitting on the computer. You're right. I keep meaning to. It’s just… life, isn't it? So much to do, so little time. True. But those photos deserve to be seen. Remember that little tea house we found, tucked away in the mountains? The view was incredible. Oh, yes! And the tea was… acquired taste, let’s say. But the people were so lovely. I’m still trying to remember the name of that village. I think it was Shangri-La. Or something close to it. Very picturesque. I miss those winding roads. I miss driving through the countryside. Me too. It’s a bit different driving here, isn’t it? All the scooters and the… intensity of the traffic. Exactly. A lot less relaxed. I miss just being able to pull over and take a photo of a field of wildflowers without worrying about getting run over. You and your wildflowers! What about that group chat from Mark and Chloe? Have you seen all the pictures of their new house? No! Let me see… Wow, it’s beautiful. They’ve done an amazing job with it. Proper renovation project, that. They've really gone to town. I'm surprised they managed it with a baby on the way. They’re a good team, those two. I wonder if we’ll be over for Christmas? I hope so. It would be wonderful to see everyone. And to actually be  in  England, you know? Feel the cold. Don't miss the rain too much. Oh, I’ll miss the rain. It’s comforting, somehow. Reminds me of home. Let's get those photos printed then, shall we? It’ll be like a little piece of home, right here.

Honestly, last night was  wild . I’m still recovering. Tell me about it! My head is pounding. Did you see Liam try to do that TikTok dance? It was a disaster. Oh my god, yes! He looked like a flailing octopus. I recorded it, you know. No way! You better send it. My mum would love to see it. She thinks he’s trying way too hard these days. I will, definitely. Although, you know, he might kill me if he sees it. Did you manage to avoid spilling anything on yourself this time? Barely! I think I only lost one sneaker to a rogue splash of cider. Progress, right? How was Sarah? She seemed pretty quiet last week. She was still hungover from that pre-drinks on Thursday, I think. Kept complaining about her feet hurting. She needs to invest in some proper shoes for going out. Seriously! They’re practically torture devices. I’m sticking to trainers from now on, even if it’s not the most glamorous look. Speaking of, did you see Chloe’s Insta story this morning? The one where she’s posing in front of that fake marble wall? Yeah, it's a bit much, isn’t it? She’s trying  so  hard to be an influencer. I know! Like, we’re still in sixth form, love. It’s a bit cringe. My nan sent me the story and she was like, "Are you trying to be a model, sweetheart?" Oh no! That’s brutal. What did you say? Just told her I was being silly. Honestly, I’m more concerned about getting through Economics than becoming an Insta-star. Same! Mr. Davies is going to be the death of me. I need to start revising properly. Have you started looking at unis again? I’m starting to panic. A little bit. I’m thinking about Leeds, maybe? They’ve got a good photography course. Mum’s still pushing me towards Nottingham though. Oh yeah? Why's that? Apparently, it's got "better job prospects." Typical mum. Though, remember when she tried to convince me to be a vet? Don't remind me. My dad threatened to move out if she kept pushing that. So, dogs or cats on the topic of pets today? I saw a puppy on Instagram that nearly made me cry. Definitely dogs. They’re just more… fun. Less judgmental. Have you seen Buster since Christmas?

Right, so we need to nail down the details for Nan’s visit next week. Do you think she’d prefer the two-bedroom or the little cottage? Hmm, the cottage is charming, but two-bedroom's probably easier for her, isn't it? Less stairs, closer to the bathroom. And, you know, somewhere to put all her…things. Definitely the two-bedroom. She always complains about the cottage being draughty. Agreed. I’ll book the taxi from Penrith station. I’m thinking Thursday? Would that work for you both? Thursday’s perfect. I can get the groceries on Wednesday afternoon. We should get those frozen peas she likes best, yeah? Yes, definitely. And the ready-made mash. Can’t go wrong with the ready-made mash. I was just thinking, she'll want to watch the football on Saturday. Will she be up for it? Nan loves Saturday football. Always has. She’ll be glued to the telly, yelling at the ref. So, what's on? Is there a decent game? Liverpool’s playing Chelsea, apparently. Big match. Going to be a good one. I'm having a little trial of the latest Fifa game. Pretty realistic. Oh, you and the football. You’ll be at it all day long! Don't you think it's a bit much to spend all day on a game? It’s relaxing, Mary! It's my downtime. And it's gotten surprisingly advanced. The tactics are really nuanced. You’d be surprised. Speaking of nuanced, I was reading an article the other day about culpability in automated decision-making. It was fascinating – and terrifying. Culpability? What are you on about now, Lizzie? Basically, if a self-driving car crashes, who’s responsible? The manufacturer? The owner? The programmer of the AI? It's a right can of worms. Sounds like a head ache. Let the computer take the blame. Simple. It’s not that simple, John! There are ethical implications… Oh, good heavens. Let's not get bogged down in ethics with peas and chips! Nan’s the priority. Are we forgetting anything? Her medication needs, her slippers… Slippers! Yes, definitely slippers. And a few magazines. She likes those gardening ones. And a comfy chair by the TV for watching Liverpool. Don't want her straining her neck. Right. Well, it sounds like we’ve got everything sorted then. Hopefully, she’ll enjoy her visit.

Right, well, that's been lovely, hasn’t it? Bit manic, maybe, but lovely. It has! It’s been ages since we all got together like this. Thanks for coming, both of you. Don't mention it, dear. Always a pleasure to relax, especially when there's lovely cake. And that Earl Grey was excellent. It was a nice change from the hospital, honestly. Thanks for having us. The flat's looking lovely, by the way. Glad you think so. Still a work in progress really. Did you manage to find parking okay, Mum? A nightmare, as always in Sussex. Ended up a good ten minutes walk. Should've used the SAT NAV, should've known better. Remember when Dad tried to set up voice recognition software on his phone? Utter chaos. Oh, don't remind me. 'Open the phone,' he'd say, and it would start playing opera. Honestly, you couldn’t make it up. It's unbelievable. He still can’t work out how to send a text message properly. How was the journey for you, Grandpa? Fine, fine. A bit slow on the A27, as always. They really need to do something about that. Another bin strike looming too, I hear. Apparently, the council’s using some dreadful water - barely filtered. It's true. It's amazing the difference in water quality between companies. You can taste it, can’t you? Especially when you're making tea. It's all about the fluoridation, isn't it? Makes your teeth strong, but tastes awful. I’ve been trying to convince myself to get a water filter. Maybe I should. I was thinking of doing a bit of DIY later, actually. Just to fix that loose shelf in the living room. Be careful! Remember my laptop? One minute I'm online, the next it's a very expensive paperweight. Noted! I’ll be extra careful. Anyway, any plans for the week ahead? Well, work, of course. It's always work. My sister's popping round on Thursday, so I’m looking forward to that. I'm going to try and get out to the park tomorrow. The weather's been surprisingly nice. I'm thinking of finally tackling that pile of magazines I’ve been accumulating. It's a mountain! And I really need to get my contact lenses refilled. It’s been wonderful catching up. It’s a shame you’re having to leave already.

Right, let’s see… Manchester United lost. Of course they did. Absolute shambles. Yeah, saw that. City won comfortably though. It's a bit bleak for a Monday morning, innit? Though, you know, it's not Monday for me. It’s… Wednesday. Feels massively disorienting still. It does. All this sunshine isn’t helping the SAD, you know. Makes me miss the properly grey skies of Cambridge, oddly enough. You’re a proper Yorkshire lass now, aren’t you? Embracing the gloom. This coffee is decent though, isn't it? Not bad at all for Tarnow. It's lovely. Much better than that awful place we tried last week. Speaking of decent, did you ever hear back from that student, Tomasz? The one struggling with the phrasal verbs? Oh, yeah! Just got a message. He sent me a little thank you, said he finally  gets  prefix verbs now. Apparently, he’s been practicing with his grandma - she's a keen gardener. Bless him! They do work so hard. It’s just... the State Exams looming. It's always stressful feeling responsible for getting them through it all. They look to you, you know? Tell me about it. I spent half an hour last night thinking about how best to explain the present perfect continuous. It's such a tricky one! I considered having them work on a farm for a week, to really understand the “having been doing” aspect. Now there’s an idea! Polish farms, fresh air, English lessons… could be a niche market. Though, I’d rather be walking the dogs, to be honest. Saw a proper Jack Russell this morning, little ball of fire. Reminded me of old Winston. You miss him, don’t you? I think about him too. Speaking of things I miss… the BBC News. This Polish TV is just… relentless. It’s all politics, all the time. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? The media preys on the negativity. I’ve been trying to counteract it by reading more. Just finished a lovely biography of Sylvia Plath. Ooh, quite dark, that. I'm re-reading ‘Pride and Prejudice’. Comfort reading, you know? Something familiar. I saw a robin in the park this morning too! Proper British. That’s a good sign. So, you managed to get some shopping done, then? Do you need me to send you anything? It’s always cheaper in England.

Right, so this should feed all of us, shouldn't it? Loads of pesto, loads of cherry tomatoes… fancy a glass of wine while it’s cooking? Yeah, definitely. Red or white? I'm leaning towards red, feels more…dinner-y. Red sounds good! I've got some fairly decent Pinot Grigio too if anyone prefers white, but I reckon red with this will be better. So, Liv, how was the conference this week? You sounded stressed on the phone. Ugh, don’t even get me started. It was the biggest one I’ve organised yet, and everything that could go wrong, pretty much did. The keynote speaker’s slides corrupted, the catering company lost half the order, and some delegate’s luggage got accidentally shipped to Birmingham. Birmingham! Seriously?! That’s insane. How did you sort that out? Chaos. Pure, unadulterated chaos. Lots of panicked phone calls, a frantically re-written programme, and a lot of apologising. My boss was…understanding, mostly. He did say I handled it well under pressure though. Want a drink? You look like you need it. Absolutely. Pressure’s the name of the game, isn't it? My production line went completely bonkers on Tuesday. One machine broke down, triggering a domino effect across the whole system. Had to work until nine just to get things back on track. That sounds awful. At least you're good at sorting things out, right? Me, I've been chipping away at this wall all week. Turns out it’s got a load of dodgy wiring behind it. A wall? Seriously? That sounds… adventurous. Yeah, well, helping my mate out. He’s renovating his flat. It’s mostly just boring, to be honest. Lots of dust and concrete. Though I did manage to knock a couple of bricks out accidentally. Felt a bit like a kid. You probably did. So, anything exciting happening in your dating life, Tom? Still seeing anyone? Nah, nothing serious. There's this girl I met at the pub a couple of weeks ago. Seems alright. We're going for a walk in the botanical gardens on Sunday. Botanical gardens! That’s nice. Don’t get your hopes up, though. Botanical gardens are a classic first date for a reason – it’s low-pressure. I know, I know. Trying to keep expectations low. What about you, Liv? You mentioned someone on the phone... something about a rugby player?

This space is lovely, isn't it? I always forget how big Gordon Square is. All those lime trees really do give it a certain… elegance. It is, yeah. Remember that terrible paving work they did last year? It's much better now. Proper surfaces. Absolutely. More walkable. Speaking of walkable, did you see that little boy trying to catch a pigeon just now? He was  determined . Ha! Yeah, quite a chase. Reminds me of trying to wrangle some of my Chinese students in the classroom sometimes. So focused on learning phrases, they'd totally miss everything else going on. Tell me about it. I’m starting to realize how much nuances are lost in translation when you’re teaching TEFL. Especially to students from China. It’s a huge challenge. The way they filter information... you have to be incredibly careful with the vocabulary you use. Remember, I told you about the family from Shanghai I was chatting to last week? Vaguely, yeah. About their trip to Paris and wanting to visit… Versailles, wasn’t it? Right. Well, they were fascinated by the pandas at the zoo. They kept asking about bears in general, you know, about where you can see them in China. It's just... such a different perspective on wildlife. Compared to the ‘watching badgers in Devon' enthusiasm we have. Absolutely. Though, I must say, driving through Devon last summer was picturesque, if agonizingly slow. Trying to navigate those tiny country lanes... Don't remind me! Getting to the Isle of Wight that way was an ordeal. Salt practically corroded my car. And food! All that salt in everything they eat over there… You’re telling me! It's wild. Anyway, I was talking to Amelia the other day, you know, the one who’s doing her PhD in Beijing. She was saying the teaching conditions are intense. Always are, aren’t they? What about your own supervision? Is Professor Davies finally getting back to you with that chapter feedback? Oh, it’s a nightmare! He's apparently in a conference in Tibet. Tibet! I texted him, you know, jokingly asked if he'd seen any yetis. Very funny. You need to be more assertive with him. I know, I know. I'm trying. I'm thinking about having a stern chat. Maybe with a coconut cake as a peace offering. And a decent coffee. Not this watery stuff they serve here.

Right, so are you absolutely sure you’ve got the postcode? I don’t want to end up in Middlesborough again. Last time was a nightmare. Yeah, relaxed. I’ve triple-checked. It’s right here on the email. SG14 2PX. Harpenden. SG… right, vaguely rings a bell. So, Emma says she'll be ready to grab the box when we get there. Are you feeling okay to lug it back to the flat? It’s got all those old tapes in it. Yeah, no worries. I can manage. My back's feeling a bit stiff from that site visit earlier, but I’m fine. More worried about you dealing with a rogue box of archaic recording tech. Don't you mock my job, mister engineer. These tapes are a vital part of linguistic research! They’re voices of the past, you know. Capturing fading dialects. Right, the keepers of the North East’s vocal heritage. I’m bowing down. Seriously though, is there anything else we need to pick up? Hmm. Just a few more batteries for the playback machine, if we can find them. The ones I had are completely knackered. It’d be a right faff if it died halfway through listening to a particularly fascinating Geordie anecdote. We’ll keep an eye out. There’s usually a decent little shop in Harpenden, isn't there? It wouldn't be right driving all this way and not getting a coffee either. Definitely. I'm craving a flat white something fierce. I’ve got that awful feeling I’ll be marking essays for hours tonight anyway, so I need to properly fuel up beforehand. Professor Davies is being particularly pedantic about the referencing style this term. Always is. So, what's the plan after we drop off the tapes? Are you heading straight back, or are you fancying a little wander around Harpenden? It’s got a quite nice high street. Erm, I was thinking of just heading back actually. I need to sort through my emails… it’s just built up and up over the last few days and I really need to tackle it. Plus Nana's ringing later to say she needs an update on what's going on. Right, sensible. Guess it’s grab and go then? Exactly. Unless you have any strong objections to being my designated errand boy for the afternoon. Don't be daft.

Right, so, has anyone else got a sore throat or is it just me feeling like I've swallowed gravel? Nah, I’m alright. Bit of a sniffle yesterday, but that's gone. You catching something, Rach? Poor you. Sounds awful. I had a terrible throat a couple of weeks back – felt like someone was scraping it with sandpaper. Paracetamol didn’t even touch it. Tell me about it! I tried paracetamol this morning, and it did nowt. I’m hoping it's just a cold and not… you know. What, flu? Don't jinx it. Definitely looks like a cold. You should try honey and lemon, Rach. My nan swears by it. I’ll give it a go. Though, admit it, I’m more of a lukewarm Ribena girl, myself. Ribena? Seriously? You southern types are something else. Honey and lemon’s the proper remedy. Gets right in there. Says the lad who eats chips for every meal. Hey! They’re nutritious! Got carbs. He’s got a point, actually. Speaking of, how's things with Liam, Rach? Heard you were a bit down about it last week. Oh, don’t even go there. It’s… complicated. He’s been distant. Like, properly distant. Doesn't text, doesn't call... Ouch. That's rough. What did he say? Nothing. That’s the thing. Radio silence. I tried to talk to him about it on Sunday, but he just brushed me off, said he was ‘busy’. Busy doing what, exactly? Avoiding me? Maybe he's genuinely busy. Work pressures, family stuff… You know? I know, I know. Part of me wants to believe that. But the other part of me thinks he’s met someone else. Don’t jump to conclusions. Has he changed his routine drastically? He's been going to the gym more. Which he used to do, but now he's doing it every single evening. And he's suddenly really into… protein shakes. Protein shakes, eh? Sounds suspicious. I know! It's like he’s trying to compensate for something. Look, if you’re really worried, you could just ask him. Straight up. No beating around the bush. I know, but what if he says something awful? I don’t think I could handle it. Sometimes you have to face the music, Rach. It’s better to know the truth than live in limbo, right? I suppose you’re right.

Ugh, I need a strong cup of tea. This day has been… something. Tell me about it. Long shift? You have no idea. It’s just… the new client is a nightmare. Honestly, they want everything done yesterday, micromanage every single thing, and then complain when it’s not exactly to their vision, even when it is! Sounds familiar. Some people just don't understand the concept of project management. What’s Sarah saying about it? Sarah’s trying to keep the peace, bless her. But even she was looking stressed this afternoon. I think she’s got her hands full with the legal team too, apparently they’re being particularly difficult about the contract. The legal team are  always  difficult. How’s Mark doing? Still trying to convince everyone he’s a guru? Oh, absolutely. He was going on and on today about “synergy” and “leveraging opportunity”. I swear, he's read a self-help book. Classic Mark. Anyway, how are you? Anything exciting happening outside of work-induced stress? Not really. Still reeling a bit from… you know. Liam? Are you okay? You haven't said much about it lately. I'm… fine. Honestly. It's just… awkward, isn’t it? Seeing him around because of mutual friends. It’s definitely awkward. But you're strong, you’ll navigate it. Are you talking to anyone about it? I talked to Chloe last week. It helped a bit to vent. She’s been through worse, you know? Chloe's a good friend to have. Right, speaking of friends, are you free next Saturday? We should actually  do  something. Like, something fun. Not commiserating over tea. I think I can manage that. What did you have in mind? I was thinking maybe that new cocktail bar in Shoreditch? The one everyone's been raving about. Ooh, actually, that does sound good. It's been ages since we’ve done anything properly fun! Exactly! And maybe we can finally convince Emily to ditch that awful boyfriend of hers. Don’t tempt me. Last time I tried, she just got defensive. She needs to see what she’s putting up with. Well, maybe we just need to subtly plant the seed. Operation 'Emily's Happiness' starts next Saturday. I’m in. Right, tea. Strong tea. And then maybe I’ll attempt to de-stress by looking at adorable cat videos. Essential for mental wellbeing.

Right, so, the big question is, are dragons good or bad? Good! They breathe fire and they… they sparkle! Sparkle, yes, dragons can sparkle.
