But sometimes they hoard treasure and… well, breathe fire  at  people. So, are they always good? Bad! They eat knights! My knight got eaten! Oh dear. Well, that wasn’t very nice, was it? But sometimes knights are a bit grumpy and bullies, and the dragons are just protecting their homes. See, maybe the dragon wasn't  bad , just… misunderstood. Like in the story about the grumpy giant? He wasn't really grumpy, he was sad because he lost his teddy bear! Exactly! See, you've got it. Sometimes what  looks  bad isn't. Like trolls, for example. Everyone thinks trolls are horrible, right? They live under bridges and try to trick you. They have big noses! They do have big noses. But what if they're just lonely? What if they’re under the bridge because it's the only place they have? Maybe they need a friend! That's a brilliant idea! Maybe they need someone to bring them cake. Sometimes being misunderstood just means people haven’t been kind. Like the stories about goblins too. People say they steal things, but what if they’re just trying to collect shiny things because their houses are bare? So, goblins and dragons and giants and trolls… they’re all just a bit… sad? A bit sad, maybe. Or just trying to survive. That’s what legends are about, really. They're about helping us understand that things aren't always what they seem. Even the scariest monsters might just need a hug. Can we draw a picture of a sparkly dragon giving a sad troll cake? Absolutely! That's a wonderful idea. Let's get the crayons. And maybe we'll tell the troll a story about a brave knight who learned to be kind, too. Can I be the knight? You can be the bravest, kindest knight in the whole wide world. Now, who wants juice? I think our legends have worked up a thirst! Me! Me! Juice! Please! Coming right up. And then… back to the drawing board! Because there are a  lot  of misunderstood creatures out there. Should we read something a bit different after, though? Maybe not all creatures are sad or misunderstood. Sometimes they are just outright bad. Like the wolf?

So, the film trip went well then, did it? How was it for her? It was brilliant, actually! She came home buzzing. They filmed at that old mill just outside the village – you know, the one that's been derelict for ages. Proper atmospheric. It was spooky! But fun. Spooky, eh? Did you get some good footage? Apparently so. They were all directing each other and doing camera work. Little Maisie was a natural, she insisted on being the boom operator. That's fantastic. I’m glad she enjoyed it. Is her leg still a bit sore after all that running around? A little bit. She’s been limping slightly. I've given her some ibuprofen and told her to take it easy. Likely just a bit of a strain. Poor thing. You should get her to rest it properly. I’m going to try and squeeze in a gym session later. Need to shake off this stiffness. Good for you! Are you going to hit the treadmill? Probably. It’s a bit boring, but it’s the best way to get the miles in, isn't it? I hate running outdoors in this weather. Tell me about it. It’s not exactly warm enough at night, is it? Freezing actually. Wrapping up like the arctic expedition. Exactly! That’s why the treadmill is so appealing – controlled environment, inside, with heating. Plus, I can watch something mind-numbing while I do it. What are you watching at the moment? Just some awful reality show. Don’t judge! It's a distraction. Anything good on telly? Not really, no. We’ve been trying to get Maisie into something a bit more educational. She's obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. T-Rex! Of course she is. Well, I’m going to quickly sort out a spreadsheet before I head off to the gym. Need to chase up some invoices. Sounds thrilling! It is! Speaking of thrills… did you buy those doughnuts I asked you to? Of course! They’re in the fridge. Chocolate frosted with sprinkles. Your favourite. You’re the best. I’m going to need the sugar rush after all that spreadsheet work and the treadmill torture. Doughnuts! You two stay out of them until after dinner! They’re a treat for later. Right, I’m going to put the kettle on. Fancy a cup of tea? Please. And maybe  one  doughnut… just to tide me over. .

This risotto's rather good, isn’t it? Much better than that last place we tried. It is, yes. Definitely a step up. Though I still think Luigi's has the edge on their garlic bread. Luigi's garlic bread  is  exceptional. Right, so, did you see anything about that Green Party candidate in the paper this morning? Apparently, they’re trying to push for more pedestrianised zones downtown. Vaguely. I skimmed it. Brighton could probably do with more pedestrian areas, to be honest. Though it’ll kill the taxi trade, won’t it? Probably. Everything has a cost, doesn't it? Speaking of costs, how's the antique business doing? Still struggling to find decent stock? Oh, you know. The usual. Boot sales are increasingly barren. Everyone’s on eBay now, it seems. Hard to compete with those prices. Though, I did get a rather nice Victorian tea caddy last week. Managed to snag it for a tenner. A tenner! You’re doing alright then. I’m still not convinced my nephew’s going to find a decent job. He’s been applying everywhere. Says it’s a complete jungle out there. It is, isn't it? I feel for the young ones. They’ve got the weight of the world on their shoulders, and frankly, the job market’s dreadful. What’s he trying to do? Digital marketing. Seems to be the buzzword of the decade. But everyone and their dog is doing digital marketing. He's got the qualifications, the enthusiasm… just can't seem to land anything permanent. Persistent is key, I always say. Though it’s hard when you’re constantly getting rejected. Reminds me of when I first started out in business. Went to dozens of banks, trying to get a loan. Was turned down flat every time. It’s all about connections, isn’t it? Who you know. Not what you know. Sadly, often true. Speaking of relationships... how's your daughter doing? Still seeing that chap with the dreadful beard? Oh, you know Sarah. She’s a whirlwind. They're still together, yes. Though she says he's been attempting to "grow out" the beard. Apparently, it's an ongoing negotiation. An ongoing negotiation! Good heavens. Some things are better left un-negotiated, I always say. My sister’s been complaining about her hip again. Oh dear. Is she seeing the specialist? Yes, next week.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that article about the rising cost of orchids. It's ridiculous. Like, a decent Phalaenopsis is nearly fifty quid now. Fifty quid! For a flower? That's…excessive. What’s happened to the market? Apparently, supply chain issues and a surge in popularity. Everyone’s got a houseplant these days, aren't they? It's the new status symbol. Better than a designer handbag, apparently. Well, you can’t exactly eat an orchid. I’m still hoping to find a good price on some succulents. Something that won’t need constant watering, you know? I’m busy enough with the PhD, the last thing I need is a finicky plant. I hear you. Mine thrive on neglect, which is perfect for a workaholic like me. Speaking of work, did you see the latest projections on the funding cuts? It's awful. Don't even get me started. They’re just slashing everything. It’s political greed, plain and simple. And the way they’re trying to deflect blame onto…well, everyone but themselves. It’s infuriating. I know! And the constant comparisons to Donald Trump? Honestly, the cognitive dissonance is astounding. How people can see any parallels is beyond me. It’s just a tactic, isn't it? Distraction. Anything to avoid taking responsibility. Did you see that he’s… I’m not even going to repeat it. It’s too absurd even to dignify with attention. No, thankfully. I try to limit my exposure. It’s bad for the mental health. What are you thinking of getting for your mum’s birthday? I’m completely stumped. Right? She’s impossible to buy for. She's got everything she needs. I was thinking maybe a pastry from that little bakery on Mill Road? Remember that place we went to last year? The ones with the proper Cornish pasties. Oh, yes! Those were amazing. Seriously the best pasty I've ever had. I think that’s a brilliant idea! Something tasty and indulgent. Exactly. Plus, it supports a local business. You know, trying to do my bit for the local economy. It's not as flashy as an orchid, but it’s a lot more practical. Definitely. It feels more…thoughtful, somehow. Although, you know what would  really  be thoughtful? Helping me sort out my finances. This student loan is killing me. Oh, you and your finances!

It’s lovely to be back here, isn’t it? Feels… calmer than London. Definitely. A good reset button. Needed that after the week we've had. Three tutorials back-to-back on Tuesday… brutal. Tell me about it. That documentary film student kept interrupting with existential questions about the meaning of the cut. Seriously. Classic Film Studies. Did you manage to steer him back on track? Eventually. I just had to gently remind him we were discussing camera angles, not the universe. Although, thinking about it, camera angles  are  a pretty good metaphor for perspective… You're going deep now. Speaking of perspective, did you see that documentary about the killer whales off the coast of Scotland? Oh, the one with the injured one? Yes! Absolutely heartbreaking. The way they were caring for it… it just reinforces how intelligent and complex they are. It's devastating what we do to their habitats. It was. Reminded me of that article about the rise in aggressive behaviour on TV. Apparently, studies link exposure to violence with increased aggression in viewers. Ugh, don’t remind me. Another thing that makes me feel horrible about letting the news on in the background. Although, ironically, sometimes the news feels pretty violent even without that… True. It’s all so relentless. Saw something the other day about people squatting in abandoned buildings. Seems a rather desperate situation all round. It is. There’s a lot of sadness there. Remember when we were kids, and all we wanted was a Blue Peter badge? Seems so innocent now. Absolutely. I loved those badges! Spent hours crafting for the competitions. Never won one, though. My papier-mâché volcano was a disaster. Mine always ended up looking like melting blobs. My mum was always trying to help, smoothing everything out… It’s funny, isn’t it? How something so simple can hold such power. A little piece of plastic could make your whole week. It’s a symbol of creativity and effort, I think. And a little bit of adventure. It's nice to think about such uncomplicated things, especially when you’re wading through essays and film theory. Exactly. Reckon we should open another bottle? This view from the window and a good chat is exactly what we needed. Definitely. And maybe we can try to recreate that Blue Peter volcano next time we’re back… just for old times’ sake.

Right then. This photographer chap has sent over some photos of the hostel. Blimey, it’s a right state, isn’t it? Young lads, mostly. Not all angels, you know. Oh dear. That dining room looks like a bomb site. Honestly, dear, how do you manage? All that…energy. Well, someone's got to do it. Bit of a lifeline for some, it is. And you get used to the noise. Though young Colin did nearly set the laundry room on fire last week with a hairspray can. Colin, eh? Typical. Running a hostel must be exhausting. Not the kind of job you can just switch off from. Tell you what, it is. But the other day, I had a young lad, a builder, come up to me and thanked me for a hot meal and a bed. Said it made all the difference. That’s what keeps you going, that is. Reminds you it’s worth it. That's lovely, dear. Very heartwarming. David's cousin, Patricia, is in Addenbrooke’s, you know. Dreadful pneumonia. Poor girl. Oh, that’s awful. Give her my best. I’ve known Patricia since she was a little thing. Always a bright one. Terrible, that. My sister’s husband had pneumonia last year too. Took him weeks to recover. Speaking of recovery, have you seen the price of petrol lately? Absolutely scandalous. My old Ford Fiesta is drinking like a sailor. Fiesta? You're a lucky man. I’ve still got my Morris. Nearly forty years old now. Wouldn’t trade it for anything. Keeps me busy, tinkering with it. You know, reminds me of me father. He was a brilliant mechanic. Always loved taking things apart and putting them back together. Your father had that little shop on Norwich Road, didn’t he? The hardware store? Always bustling, that place. That's right. Worked his fingers to the bone, he did. Mum ran the sweet shop next door. Hardworking pair, they were. Never complained. Never had much, but they always made do. My parents had a chip shop in Birmingham. Long hours, seven days a week. But they were proud of what they had, you know? Built it from nothing. It’s amazing what people can achieve with hard work. Actually, reminds me of those engineering marvels they were building in the 1930s. Massive bridges, incredible structures... That's it exactly. Ingenious, those engineers.

So, you were saying about the recruitment side of things? It’s fascinating, really, how different your world must have been from mine. Dealing with…people, directly all the time. I spend most of my days with essays. Yeah, it was a different beast entirely. Less…structured, I guess, than academia. You're constantly reacting, persuading, selling, battling egos. I miss the hustle sometimes, honestly, the feeling of closing a deal. I can imagine. Though I think the constant rejection must have been wearing. Did you find it…difficult? Dealing with people’s expectations, their hopes riding on you finding them the perfect job? It could be. Definitely had to build up a thick skin. Lots of people don’t understand that recruitment isn’t just about finding  them  a job, it’s about finding the  right  job for the company too. And often those two things don't align. Makes sense. So, a good sales pitch, then? For both sides? Absolutely. It was all about incentives and presenting the best possible version of both the candidate and the role. A bit like selling a student’s work, in a way, I suppose? Just… with higher stakes. A rather apt comparison, actually. Speaking of “selling” and presenting... I’ve been grading those essays from the lecturer training course, the one on academic literacy. And… well, it’s been a bit eye-opening, to say the least. Oh yeah? How so? I’ve heard rumblings about the course being a bit uneven. Uneven is putting it mildly. Some have genuinely impressive critical thinking, solid understanding of academic conventions… but others… it's like they haven't truly grasped the basics. Sentence structure, argumentation - it’s all over the place. That's surprising, isn't it? Lecturers, supposed experts in their fields. You’d think they'd have a handle on written communication. Exactly. And what's most concerning is the confidence some of them have. They submit these pieces riddled with grammatical errors and… questionable logic… and then defend them assertively during feedback. It's a real challenge to navigate. Right. You've got people who are genuinely trying and struggling, and then you’ve got the ones who just… don’t get it. Precisely. I had one who insisted their passive voice was a stylistic choice. A  stylistic choice ! I nearly choked on my tea. Oh my god. That’s… incredible.

Honestly, this Victorian literature is a  nightmare . Like, why are all these people so gloomy? Tell me about it. I'm trying to decipher Chaucer. Sounds like someone gargling pebbles. Hi! Sorry to interrupt, but is this seat taken? Everything else seems rammed. Hi! No, go ahead. Nope, all yours. I'm Aisha, by the way. I'm Chloe. Nice to meet you! Is this all Victorian gloom here, then? Sounds intense. You have no idea. I'm Liam, battling Middle English. Feels like a personal challenge. Sales assistant when I'm not wrestling with literature, so a lot of deciphering things already, I guess! Hi! I'm Priya. And I'm trying to understand post-structuralism. So,  that’s  a different kind of torture. Post-structuralism! You’re brave. I’m Aisha, and I'm studying English Lit, which apparently means I'm destined to be permanently melancholy. I’m from Bradford, so I’m used to a bit of rain and bleakness, I suppose. Chloe: Oh, Bradford! I've heard it's got a really cool music scene. I'm from Bolton, so I’m used to… well, Bolton. It's… Bolton. Liam: Bolton’s not bad! Used to go there for gigs sometimes. Actually, I tried to write a poem once, about a pigeon. It was truly awful. A pigeon poem? Now I  have  to hear about this. Liam: No, no, don’t. It rhymed ‘pigeon’ with ‘midge’ and it was terrible. Absolutely terrible. I think I deleted it… for the good of humanity. Chloe: You're a poet at heart, Liam! Aisha: You know, I tried to learn the ukulele once. It ended in tears. I’m just not musically gifted, apparently. Priya: Ukulele, huh? That’s cute! I’m more into coding. Trying to build a little app, but it's currently refusing to cooperate. It’s like arguing with a very stubborn robot. Chloe: A coding app! That’s amazing! I don’t know anything about that. I mostly just stick to trying to write convincingly terrible student essays. Liam: Tell me about it! I'm pretty sure my tutor thinks I'm deliberately trying to confuse him. Maybe we should all pool our talents. You could write terrible poems about stubborn robots. Aisha: And I'll provide the melancholy soundtrack. Chloe: Perfect! We could form a student support group... for those of us who are spectacularly failing at being adults.

This risotto's actually really good, you know. You’ve absolutely smashed it. Thanks! It's a new recipe I tried, thought I’d give it a go. Glad you like it. So, you were saying about your cousin… in the army? Aye, Liam. He’s just finished his training, actually. He’s posted out to… erm… somewhere in Germany, I think. Can’t really say exactly where. Bit weird speaking to him now, you know? All military jargon and stuff. Yeah, I can imagine. Seems a world away from Doncaster, doesn’t it? My uncle was in the RAF for a bit, but he left pretty quickly. Not really his cup of tea. Nah, not for everyone. It’s a big commitment, innit? Makes you think. Anyway, what have you been up to? Still obsessed with those vintage magazines? Always! I found this amazing one the other day, a 1960s Vogue. The fashion was incredible, just so bold and colourful. You’d love it. I'll bring it over next time. Ooh, sounds brilliant! I’m always gutted I didn't get into vintage fashion more. I just liked trainers and stuff when I was a teenager. It’s never too late! What about films? Seen anything good recently? Not really. I’ve been putting off seeing Oppenheimer. It looks intense, you know? Like, three hours of heavy thinking. It is, but it's brilliant! The cinematography is stunning. Seriously, you should make an effort. It's worth it. Alright, alright, you’ve convinced me. Maybe next weekend then? We can grab some pizza after and complain about existential dread. Haha, deal! Speaking of complaining, my computer is driving me insane. Keeps freezing up at the most inconvenient times. I think it needs a serious clean up. Oh god, that’s the worst! Are you backing up your stuff regularly? Attempting to. It’s a total nightmare to navigate sometimes. I’m thinking about just getting a new one, honestly. A new one? That's a big expense. Maybe get a professional to look at it first? Often it's just a few simple things. My dad’s surprisingly good with computers now, he’s been watching loads of YouTube videos. Maybe. I'm just dreading the hassle. Ugh. Are you free on Saturday then? We could look at that charity shop, you said? I need a new scarf. Aye, Saturday’s perfect.

Honestly, the ref was dreadful tonight. Utterly dreadful. Tell me about it! Every call was against us. Felt like they were actively trying to lose. At least we still won, right? Even with that… questionable officiating. True, true. Small victories, I guess. So, speaking of questionable, have you both heard anything about Liam? Liam? From uni? Vaguely. What’s up? Apparently, he's started dating Chloe. Chloe Davies. Chloe Davies? The one who was obsessed with… I can’t even remember what she was obsessed with. Fashion. Seriously obsessed. And seemingly, Liam is now equally obsessed. She’s infested his Instagram. Oh, that's rough. He seemed pretty happy on his own. Did he mention anything about it? Nope. Just posted a picture of them in matching puffer jackets. The horrors. It's horrifying! Puffer jackets! That  is  a red flag. Maybe he's genuinely smitten. You never know. I’m just… wary. He’s always been so independent. And she seems a bit… overwhelming. I said to my mum “mum, he’s been brainwashed!”. She looked at me like I was mental, though. Mums always do. Anyway, what about politics? Did you see that article about the latest funding cuts? Don’t even get me started. It's ridiculous. They're slashing funding to everything, then complaining about the state of the country. Classic. And the casual racism just keeps creeping in, doesn’t it? It’s so insidious. People think it’s ‘just a joke’ and then act surprised when someone’s offended. It’s exhausting to constantly explain why something is harmful. It’s all so performative. Like, ‘Oh, I’m so concerned about social justice’ but then they retweet something completely problematic. Exactly! It's all virtue signalling. I saw my aunt the other day, posting about supporting a charity, and then she was complaining about immigrants taking "our" jobs. I hate that. It’s just… hypocrisy. Gets my blood boiling. Speaking of things boiling my blood… Aunt Fiona’s coming to visit next weekend. From London. Oh god. Fiona. Don't remind me. So much unsolicited advice. And constant questions about my love life. It's like she thinks I’m still 16. You know she always asks why I haven’t settled down and had kids. Classic Fiona. I just want to hide under the sofa. Anyone free for a movie night to de-stress?

This flat's lovely, really it is. Much nicer than I imagined. All bright and airy. Yes, it's a good size, isn’t it? And so close to everything. Could you manage with the stairs, dear? Perfectly fine, Dad. We’re on the second floor, but the lift's working, mostly. "Mostly" being the operative word. It has a mind of its own. Everything does these days. Though I’m not sure about this… stuff hanging everywhere. Are these… spices? Yeah, a few. I got a bit carried away at Borough Market. Got some amazing garam masala, the smell's incredible. Must be careful with those, dear. Some of them are terribly strong. Remember your Auntie Brenda and that vindaloo? Oh god, she was sweating for a week! Speaking of remembering, did you ever get around to fixing that draught under the kitchen window? Still feels a bit chilly in there. It's on the list, Dad. Window cleaning's a bit of a nightmare, to be honest. Can't find a reliable company. We could always have a go ourselves. I’ve got some lovely cloths, practically unused. They’re a new thing. Little accessories, you know. Mum, you’ve got a cloth for every day of the week! And a colour to match every surface. Reminds me of your mother, your Auntie Elsie. She was obsessed with polishing. Everything gleamed in her house. Had a whole shelf dedicated to pot scourers and furniture polish. Sounds intense. Anyway, how was the journey down? Did you get stuck in traffic? A bit, but nothing too bad. We stopped for a cream tea in Guildford. Such lovely scones. You pronounce ‘scone’ differently than I do. It's 'skone' definitely. That's a silly argument! It’s 'skown' like 'gone'. It’s a classic debate. Honestly, does it really matter? Speaking of food, you two keeping an eye on your cholesterol? I read an article the other day about centenarians – apparently, they all eat ridiculous amounts of butter. Oh dear. I do love butter. And I'm not fond of lentils. Doctor’s always going on about lentils. Doctor’s always going on about something. Had a friend down the pub, Bernard, had a nasty bout of diverticulitis. Horrible thing. Don’t even start! We're trying to relax. Tell us, are you seeing your sister much these days? Not as much as I’d like.

Honestly, the amount of data coming through the corpus today has been  mad . Like, absolutely bonkers. I’ve been chasing after annotation errors for hours. Sounds… intense. I’m used to chasing after structural integrity, not semantic ones, though. Different kind of headache, I guess. Right? It's all headache, innit? Though today's particularly… abstract. It's all about nuanced language use online, and how people are being sarcastic without actually using the usual markers. It’s a nightmare for the algorithms. So, people are… deliberately being obtuse online? Pretty much! It’s a modern skill, apparently. Makes me feel ancient. How's the bridge project going, by the way? Still wrestling with subsidence? It’s… ongoing. We had a bit of a setback with the rainfall last week. The ground's been saturated like you wouldn't believe. Cambridge weather, eh? Supposed to be all quaint and charming, but it just drenches you. Aye, typical. The rain hasn't let up much in Sunderland either. Makes you appreciate a good cuppa, doesn't it? Speaking of which, I need a slice of that carrot cake. Go for it. Thinking about it, I was reading an article online about the housing market the other day. Honestly, it's insane here. I was looking at a tiny flat - barely big enough to swing a cat – for like, £700,000! Seriously? That's ridiculous! Even back home, prices are climbing, but  that … That’s daylight robbery, that is. I can’t imagine saving for a house these days. It's a generational thing, isn’t it? My parents are always going on about how they bought their house for a pittance. They don’t get it. Nah, they really don’t. Remember Nana saying she got her semi-detached for the same price as a parking space now? Exactly! It's depressing, though. Makes you think about… well, about the future, doesn't it? Tell me about it. I’ve been trying to get into a bit of a healthy cooking kick, trying to counteract all the stress, but it's such a faff. I attempted a lentil shepherd's pie the other night. Disaster. The lentils were basically soup. Oh dear. Lentils are tricky. Need to be cooked  just  right. My mum’s German, so I've been raised with a ridiculously serious approach to cooking. Everything has to be precise.

Right, so, coffee's on. Who wants milk and sugar? Just a dash of milk for me, thanks, Sarah. How was your shift? You looked knackered when you picked me up. Don't even ask, Chloe. Absolute chaos. We were short-staffed again, and poor Mr. Henderson decided to have a complete meltdown about his dinner. Honestly, sometimes I wonder… Oh, Mr. Henderson. He’s a character, isn't he? Remember when he thought I was his daughter, Emily? Yeah! And he kept calling you "Emily dear" for a week. It was hilarious. Hilarious for you two, maybe! For me, it’s just another Thursday. Anyway, what's been happening with you two? Imogen, how’s the job going? Still enjoying the accounts? It's alright, you know, steady. Busy, especially with the new ad campaign. Got to write copy for dog food, which is...an experience. Dog food? Really? That sounds… interesting. It is! Trying to make kibble sound appealing is harder than you’d think. Speaking of things that are interesting, how are things with Mum? She mentioned wanting to redecorate the bathroom again. Oh, she’s on one. Wants a grey and teal theme. Apparently, it’s “very on trend”. I told her to hold off until after Christmas, but she’s already ordered the paint. Classic Mum. Never a dull moment. I had to speak to Dr. Davies about my back again yesterday, it’s just getting worse with the hours I work. Oh, Sarah, I’m so sorry. You really need to look after yourself more. Are they going to adjust your medication? They’re talking about physiotherapy, but honestly, I’d rather just curl up in a ball and sleep for a week. What about you, Lucy? Anything exciting going on? The new agency still good? It’s okay. The work is… well, it's work. We had a patient the other day who kept insisting he was a Tibetan monk. It took a good hour to convince him that he was actually in a care home in Kent. Oh, Lucy! You have the stories. It’s just… you see so much. Some days are really tough. But then you have days like today, chatting with you all over coffee... Absolutely. We need more days like this. Are we thinking about that craft fair in December? Mum's already started making Christmas decorations. Oh, the Christmas decorations!
